issue.description:
## Scope

Integrate the error parser into ProcessWrapper (throw exceptions on non-zero exit codes), and write comprehensive integration tests covering the full subprocess lifecycle: successful execution, cancellation, and all error conditions.

## Why this matters

This is the final integration step that ties ProcessWrapper and exception handling together. After this, SDK methods can simply call \`ProcessWrapper.StartAsync()\` and get either results or typed exceptions. Comprehensive tests ensure the subsystem is reliable before higher-level SDK methods are built on top.

## Implementation guidance

- Modify \`ProcessWrapper.StartAsync\` and \`Start\`:
  - After \`process.WaitForExit()\`, check exit code
  - If exit code != 0, call \`ErrorParser.ParseError(stderr, exitCode)\`
  - Throw the returned exception (wrap with "pdftract failed: {ex.Message}" if needed)
  - Return \`ProcessResult\` only on exit code 0
- Create comprehensive integration tests in \`tests/Pdftract.Tests/Process/ProcessWrapperIntegrationTests.cs\`:
  - Test successful execution (exit code 0, stdout contains JSON)
  - Test cancellation during execution:
    - Start with \`CancellationTokenSource\`
    - Cancel after short delay
    - Verify \`OperationCanceledException\` or process killed
  - Test each error condition:
    - Mock/fixture for each error code type
    - Verify correct exception type is thrown
    - Verify exception message contains useful details
  - Test process tree cleanup:
    - Spawn a process that spawns a child
    - Kill parent and verify child also dies
  - Test concurrent process spawns (if applicable)
- Add performance/stress tests:
  - Verify no file handle leaks (run many processes in a loop)
  - Verify memory doesn't grow unbounded

## Acceptance criteria

- ProcessWrapper throws on non-zero exit code
- ErrorParser.ParseError is called with stderr JSON and exit code
- Thrown exception matches the error code type
- Successful execution (exit 0) returns ProcessResult without throwing
- Integration tests verify successful execution
- Integration tests verify cancellation kills process tree
- Integration tests verify each error code throws correct exception type
- Integration tests verify exception messages are useful
- Integration tests verify no resource leaks (file handles, processes)
- All tests pass with \`dotnet test\`

## References

- Parent bead: bf-4ej9sq
- Plan section: SDK Architecture / The Ten SDKs, line 3476
- Depends on: Child bead 3 (exception hierarchy and error mapping)
issue.title: .NET SDK: Integrate error parsing into ProcessWrapper and add comprehensive tests

issue.description:
## Scope
Add the validation gate that prevents bead close if rust-verify fails. Wire the end-to-end flow: create branch → submit workflow → poll → gate close.

## Why this matters
This enforces validate-before-close. A bead cannot close unless its code changes pass fmt/clippy/tests, preventing broken code from entering the tree.

## Implementation guidance
In NEEDLE worker close logic (where beads are marked closed):
- Add validation step before  is called
- New function 
- Flow:
  1. Call create_wip_branch() → get branch_ref
  2. Call submit_rust_verify(repo, branch_ref, bead_id) → get workflow_name
  3. Call poll_rust_verify(workflow_name, timeout) → get result
  4. If result.exit_code == 0: allow close to proceed
  5. If result.exit_code != 0: block close, return error with logs

Modify worker close flow:
- Before calling bf.close(), call verify_before_close()
- If verify fails, surface logs to agent and do NOT close bead
- Agent can retry after fixing issues

## Critical considerations
- Must NOT close bead if verification fails
- Logs must be surfaced to agent (not swallowed)
- Worker name should be deterministic per agent (e.g., claude-code-glm-4.7)
- Handle case where worker has no code changes (should still run verify against HEAD?)
- Idempotent: can retry after fixing issues

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] verify_before_close() calls the full 3-step flow
- [ ] Bead close is BLOCKED on verify failure
- [ ] Logs are surfaced to agent on failure
- [ ] Bead close proceeds only on exit_code == 0
- [ ] Integration test: mock failure verifies block, mock pass verifies allow
- [ ] Worker logic updated to call verify before close

## References
Plan: validate-before-close lifecycle, bead close flow
issue.title: Integrate verify gate into bead close lifecycle

issue.close_reason: Fix already implemented in commit 44ce09e0. decrypt_ue_or_oe now correctly uses raw AES-256-CBC block decryption without PKCS7 unpadding or .expect(). The function decrypts the 32-byte /UE//OE block with NoPadding and returns the full 32-byte key. Regression test test_decrypt_ue_or_oe_no_padding_roundtrip_no_panic verifies the fix works without panicking. Test passes (exit code 0), code compiles successfully. ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA: PASS - decrypt_ue_or_oe uses NoPadding, no panic, test validates correct credential authentication works.
issue.description: crates/pdftract-core/src/encryption/aes_256.rs:216-238, fn decrypt_ue_or_oe. Per PDF 2.0 Algorithm 8/2.A (and this function's own doc comment: 'AES-256-CBC with all-zero IV and no padding. The input is exactly 32 bytes'), the 32-byte /UE or /OE ciphertext must be decrypted with AES-256-CBC and NO padding to recover the file encryption key. Instead the code calls decrypt_padded_mut::<Pkcs7>(...).expect('AES-256 decryption failed'). A raw 32-byte file key is not PKCS7-padded, so Pkcs7 unpadding returns Err(UnpadError) for essentially every real key (unless the last plaintext byte happens to be a valid pad length), and the .expect() then PANICS. This is reached from derive_file_key_user/derive_file_key_owner (aes_256.rs:166,207) AFTER the credential hash validates (line 157-166), so opening a V5/R6 AES-256 encrypted PDF with the correct (or empty) credential crashes the library. This also violates plan.md's explicit invariant: 'no panic! in library code' / 'All parse errors are recoverable'. Note aes_128.rs:122 and aes_256.rs:391 (decrypt_stream) correctly use map_err(...)? for genuinely PKCS7-padded stream/string data; only decrypt_ue_or_oe is wrong. ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA: (1) decrypt_ue_or_oe no longer uses Pkcs7 unpadding or .expect(); it decrypts the 32-byte /UE//OE block with AES-256-CBC NoPadding (raw block decrypt) and returns the full 32 bytes. (2) A test opens a V5/R6 AES-256 encrypted fixture (e.g. tools/generate_encrypted_pdf_fixtures.rs output) with the correct/empty credential and asserts derive_file_key_user returns FileKeyResult::Success WITHOUT panicking, and the recovered key decrypts a stream to expected plaintext.
issue.title: AES-256 (V5/R6) file-key recovery uses Pkcs7 unpadding and panics via expect(), breaking decryption of correctly-authenticated PDFs

## Scope

Implement the method bodies to call through to the subprocess engine, replacing stubs with real invocations.

## Why this matters

The contract methods are the public API. They must delegate to the subprocess engine to perform actual work. This wires the SDK interface to the implementation.

## Implementation guidance

For each of the 9 methods, implement the method body to:

1. Build subprocess command from parameters
2. Convert options to CLI flags (use option structs from Child 4)
3. Invoke subprocess via subprocess engine
4. Parse subprocess output (JSON or text)
5. Return typed result (convert JSON to Go structs from Child 1)
6. Handle errors via error handling system

Method-specific behavior:
- **Extract/ExtractText/ExtractMarkdown**: Run `pdftract extract` with flags, return Document or string
- **ExtractStream**: Run `pdftract extract`, spawn goroutine to stream PageResults over channel
- **Search**: Run `pdftract search`, stream MatchResults over channel
- **GetMetadata**: Run `pdftract metadata`, parse JSON to Metadata struct
- **Hash**: Run `pdftract hash`, parse JSON to Fingerprint struct
- **Classify**: Run `pdftract classify`, parse JSON to Classification struct
- **VerifyReceipt**: Run `pdftract verify-receipt`, return bool

## Critical considerations

- Streaming methods spawn goroutines that feed channels (close channel when done)
- Context cancellation must propagate to subprocess (kill subprocess if ctx canceled)
- All subprocess calls use timeout from context
- Channels are buffered (size 16) to avoid blocking
- Error handling uses error system from Child 3 dependency

## Acceptance criteria

- All 9 methods have full implementations (not stubs)

issue.description:
Two code paths report encryption status as a hardcoded literal false even though the crate has a working encryption detector (detect_encryption in the encryption submodule, exercised by fixtures under the encrypted fixtures directory).

Sites:
- crates/pdftract-core/src/sdk.rs:225 -> get_metadata() returns PdfMetadata with is_encrypted set to a literal false, comment 'TODO: detect encryption from catalog'. The public SDK metadata API therefore reports every encrypted PDF as unencrypted.
- crates/pdftract-core/src/document.rs:281 -> build_fingerprint_input() sets CatalogFlags is_encrypted to a literal false, comment 'TODO: detect encryption'. The Phase 1.7 structural fingerprint catalog flags never reflect encryption, so an encrypted PDF and an otherwise-identical unencrypted one are indistinguishable on this flag.

Both are wrong (not merely incomplete): the value is a constant, not derived from the trailer Encrypt entry that the detector already parses.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
1. get_metadata in sdk.rs, run on an existing encrypted PDF fixture from the repo, returns is_encrypted == true, and still returns false for an unencrypted fixture.
2. Neither sdk.rs nor document.rs contains a hardcoded is_encrypted false literal; the value is computed from document Encrypt presence. Verify by grep showing no such literal remains in those two files, plus a passing test asserting item 1.
issue.title: is_encrypted hardcoded false in get_metadata and structural fingerprint despite working encryption detector

issue.description:
Seal the Forgejo token value using kubeseal against the iad-ci cluster.

## Scope
Use kubeseal CLI to encrypt the Forgejo token into a sealed value that can be safely committed to git.

## Why this matters
SealedSecrets allow us to store secrets in git without exposing the raw values. The sealed form can only be decrypted by the SealedSecret controller in iad-ci.

## Implementation guidance
1. Use kubeseal with iad-ci kubeconfig:
   ```bash
   kubectl --kubeconfig=/home/coding/.kube/iad-ci.kubeconfig create secret generic forgejo-ci-token --dry-run=client --from-literal=token=<TOKEN_VALUE> -n argo-workflows -o yaml | kubeseal --kubeconfig=/home/coding/.kube/iad-ci.kubeconfig --format yaml > /tmp/forgejo-ci-token-sealed.yaml
   ```
2. Extract the encryptedData.token value
3. Update the SealedSecret manifest with the sealed value
4. Clean up temporary files

## Critical considerations
- Use the iad-ci kubeconfig directly (not proxy) - kubeseal needs write access to fetch cert
- Clean up any temporary files containing raw token
- Verify the sealed value is base64-encoded and properly formatted
- Never commit the raw token

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Token is sealed using kubeseal against iad-ci
- [ ] Sealed value is added to the SealedSecret manifest
- [ ] No raw token exists on disk or in git
- [ ] Manifest is ready for application

## References
- Parent bead: bf-5ig30
- Dependent on: bf-5u0rre (manifest must exist first)

**Parent:** bf-5v0bgu
**Depends on:** bf-4rezab

**Scope:**
Once the content stream bytes are resolved, execute the drawing commands using RasterizerContext to produce an actual glyph bitmap instead of the placeholder.

**Why this matters:**
The placeholder bitmap (16x16 black square) provides no shape information for font fingerprinting. Actual content stream execution renders the real glyph shapes.

**Implementation guidance:**
1. Create RasterizerContext::new(font) to get a rendering context with proper font metrics
2. Call `ctx.execute_content_stream(&stream_bytes)` to run the PDF drawing commands
3. Replace the placeholder code (lines 598-603) with returning the actual bitmap: `Some(*ctx.bitmap.as_bytes())`
4. Handle execution errors - if execute_content_stream fails, return None

**Critical considerations:**
- Content stream execution may fail - handle errors gracefully and return None
- RasterizerContext must properly implement all PDF drawing ops used in Type3 glyphs (moveto, lineto, curveto, stroke, fill, etc.)
- Bitmap size is fixed at 32x32 (1024 bytes) - the context should handle scaling/clipping
- Verify the bitmap coordinate system matches PDF conventions (origin at bottom-left for Type3)

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Content stream bytes are executed through RasterizerContext
- Non-placeholder bitmap is returned for glyphs with resolved streams
- Error handling returns None rather than crashing on malformed content streams
- Code compiles and RasterizerContext invocation is correct
- Unit test with mock stream bytes verifies bitmap is produced

**References:**
- crates/pdftract-core/src/font/type3_rasterizer.rs:594-595 - where execute_content_stream should be called
- crates/pdftract-core/src/font/type3_rasterizer.rs:597-607 - placeholder code to replace
- crates/pdftract-core/src/font/type3_rasterizer.rs:200-550 - RasterizerContext implementation
issue.title: Execute content stream and render glyph bitmap

issue.description:
## Scope
Make the existing fixture-discovery `Result` functions callable from sibling integration tests. Today they are `pub(crate)` inside the `tests/fixture_discovery.rs` test binary, but each `tests/*.rs` file compiles as a *separate* binary — crate-private items are invisible to siblings. Establish a shared helper surface so the discovery function is genuinely reusable. This is the concrete blocker behind bf-29u9w's "callable from integration tests" criterion.

## Context
`bf-1ryi2` already implemented `discover_all_fixture_infos_result()` and the parameterized `discover_fixture_infos_result_in(root)` worker in `crates/pdftract-cli/tests/fixture_discovery.rs` (both `pub(crate)`), plus `FixtureInfo` and `FixtureDiscoveryError`. The reusable entry point exists; only the cross-binary visibility boundary is unresolved.

## Implementation
1. Decide the reuse mechanism: a `tests/common/mod.rs` (or `tests/common/fixture_discovery.rs`) shared module included via `mod common;` from each consuming test, OR hoist the helpers into a small test-support crate. Prefer the lowest-friction option matching existing repo conventions.
2. Adjust visibility (`pub` within the shared module) so consuming integration tests can call `discover_all_fixture_infos_result()`.
3. Add one call from a *second* integration test binary to prove cross-binary reuse works.
4. Keep symlink-safety (`ancestor_is_symlink`) intact.

## Acceptance criteria
- `discover_all_fixture_infos_result()` (or equivalent) is callable from at least one integration test *other than* `fixture_discovery.rs`.
- Reuse mechanism is documented with a short comment explaining why direct `use` across `tests/*.rs` files does not work.
- `cargo test -p pdftract-cli --no-run` compiles cleanly.

## References
- Parent: bf-29u9w
- Depends on: bf-1ryi2 (closed) — original FixtureInfo + result-fn implementation
issue.title: Expose reusable fixture discovery API across integration test binaries

issue.description:
## Scope
Implement cycle detection to prevent infinite loops when PDF references form cycles.

## Why This Matters
PDF structures can contain circular references (A references B, B references A). Without cycle detection, this causes stack overflow.

## Implementation Guidance
1. Add a depth parameter or visited set to track recursion depth
2. Detect when we're in a reference cycle (same object appearing again in chain)
3. Return a sensible default classification when cycle is detected
4. Set reasonable recursion depth limit (e.g., 10-20 levels)

## Acceptance Criteria
1. detect_char_proc_type tracks recursion depth or visited references
2. Returns early when cycle is detected or depth limit exceeded
3. No stack overflow on circular reference structures
4. Unit tests cover cycle scenarios
5. All existing tests still pass

## References
- Parent bead: bf-5vlv4i
- Plan: lines 3851-3890 (PDF object type detection)
- Prerequisite: bf-5feruy must be complete
issue.notes: Task already complete - cycle detection already fully implemented in detect_char_proc_type_with_context_impl. Verified implementation: (1) Cycle detection via visited HashSet (2) Depth limiting with MAX_CHAR_PROC_DEPTH=20 (3) Proper check ordering (depth before cycle before dereference) (4) Returns 'circular-reference' and 'depth-limit-exceeded' CharProcType variants. Test coverage verified: 7 comprehensive tests covering circular refs, depth limits, boundary cases, and normal chains. All tests compile and pass. No code changes needed.
issue.title: Add reference cycle detection and protection

## Scope
Create `docs/operations/prometheus-rules.yaml` with Prometheus alerting rules for `pdftract serve` deployments. Required by plan Monitoring section (~line 3832).

## Required alert rules
1. `PdftractExtractionLatencyHigh` — p99 > 2× the 150ms target for > 5 minutes

issue.description:
## Scope

Define the Rust types for Profile YAML deserialization using serde_yaml. Profile struct has: name, description, priority (i32), match (MatchExpr), extraction (ExtractionProfile), fields (BTreeMap<String, FieldExtractor>). MatchExpr is a boolean tree with all/any/none combinators and 11 predicate kinds (TextContains, TextMatches, HeadingMatches, HasCurrencyPattern, HasSignatureField, Structural, etc.). ExtractionProfile overrides specific ExtractionOptions fields (reading_order, table_detection, readability_threshold, include_invisible, include_headers_footers, force_ocr, min_block_chars). FieldExtractor has localizers (near, region, pick) and extractor (regex, parse).

## Why this matters

The Profile type is the foundation for all profile work. Without proper serde types, we can't load YAML from disk, can't validate profiles, and can't implement the match/field evaluators. This must come first.

## Implementation guidance

- Add serde_yaml = "0.9" to pdftract-core/Cargo.toml (behind profiles feature flag)
- Profile struct in src/profile/mod.rs with serde Deserialize
- MatchExpr enum: All(Vec<MatchExpr>), Any(Vec<MatchExpr>), None(Vec<MatchExpr>), TextContains(StringOrArray), TextMatches(String), HeadingMatches(String), HasCurrencyPattern(bool), HasSignatureField(bool), Structural(StructuralPredicate)
- StructuralPredicate: PageCount {min,max}, HasTable(bool), HasFormField(bool), HasMath(bool), HeadingDepth {min,max}, FontDiversity {min,max}
- ExtractionProfile: reading_order, table_detection, readability_threshold, include_invisible, include_headers_footers, force_ocr, min_block_chars
- FieldExtractor: near (Option<Vec<String>>), region (Option<RegionSpec>), pick (Option<PickStrategy>), regex (Option<Regex>), parse (Option<ParseType>)
- RegionSpec enum: TopQuarter, BottomQuarter, LeftHalf, RightHalf, Top(u8), Bottom(u8), Bbox([f32;4])
- PickStrategy enum: LargestFont, SmallestFont, NearestBelow, NearestRight, First, Last
- ParseType enum: Decimal, Date, Int, Bool
- StringOrArray newtype wrapper that accepts both string and array of strings
- Validation: reject YAML with top-level keys matching PROFILE_SECRETS_FORBIDDEN pattern
- Unit tests for deserialization of valid and invalid YAML

## Critical considerations

- Serde_yaml error messages should be user-friendly; consider custom error types
- PROFILE_SECRETS_FORBIDDEN check happens during deserialization, not after
- Regex compilation should happen at load time, not at match time
- Profile priority is i32 (allows negative priorities)

## Acceptance criteria

- Profile type deserializes valid YAML correctly
- Invalid YAML produces clear error messages with line numbers
- PROFILE_SECRETS_FORBIDDEN keys cause deserialization to fail with clear error
- Unit tests cover all match predicate variants
- Unit tests cover all field DSL variants
- Cargo check passes with profiles feature

## References

- Plan 7.10 lines 2912-3070
- Profile YAML example at lines 2914-2961
- Match DSL table at lines 2963-2980
- Extraction tuning keys at lines 2982-2992
- Field DSL at lines 2994-3006
issue.title: 7.10.1: Profile YAML schema and serde types (Profile struct, Match DSL, Extraction tuning, Field DSL)

## Scope

When a profile matches, its extraction block should override specific ExtractionOptions fields. Extraction tuning keys: reading_order, table_detection, readability_threshold, include_invisible, include_headers_footers, force_ocr, min_block_chars. Apply overrides to default ExtractionOptions to produce profile-specific options.

## Why this matters

Different document types benefit from different extraction strategies. Invoices need line_dominant reading order. Slide decks need struct_tree reading order. Scientific papers need xy_cut for column detection. Extraction tuning lets profiles optimize for their document type.

## Implementation guidance

- apply_extraction_profile(base: ExtractionOptions, profile: &ExtractionProfile) -> ExtractionOptions
- Each key in ExtractionProfile maps to an ExtractionOptions field
- reading_order: Override if Some, else use base value
- table_detection: Override if Some, else use base value
- readability_threshold: Override if Some, else use base value
- include_invisible: Override if Some, else use base value
- include_headers_footers: Override if Some, else use base value
- force_ocr: Override if Some, else use base value
- min_block_chars: Override if Some, else use base value
- ExtractionProfile uses Option<T> for each field to allow partial overrides
- Unit tests for each override field
- Integration test: invoice profile sets reading_order to line_dominant

## Critical considerations

- Profiles only override what they specify; unspecified fields keep base values
- ExtractionOptions must support all tuning keys from the plan
- Reading order enum must include all profile values (xy_cut, docstrum, line_dominant, struct_tree)
- Table detection enum must include all profile values (default, strict_borders, borderless_only, off)
- Forward compatibility: unknown extraction keys produce warnings but don't fail

## Acceptance criteria

- apply_extraction_profile overrides specified fields
- Unspecified fields retain base values
- Invoice profile sets reading_order = line_dominant
- Scientific paper profile sets reading_order = xy_cut
- Slide deck profile sets reading_order = struct_tree
- Unit tests cover all override fields
- Integration test shows profile-specific extraction

## Scope
Define the 7 type classes required by the SDK contract: Document, Page, Span, Block, Match, Fingerprint, Classification. These should be language-native Python classes (preferably `@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)`), NOT raw dicts.

## Why this matters
The SDK contract requires typed objects, not dicts. Callers need `document.pages` not `document["pages"]`. Type definitions enable IDE autocomplete, mypy checking, and better documentation.

## Implementation guidance
Create type classes in `crates/pdftract-py/python/pdftract/types.py`:
- Use `@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)` for immutability and performance
- Define these classes:
  - `Document`: `pages: List[Page]`, `metadata: Metadata`, etc.
  - `Page`: `width: int`, `height: int`, `blocks: List[Block]`, `spans: List[Span]`
  - `Span`: `text: str`, `font: Optional[str]`, `size: float`, `bbox: Tuple[int, int, int, int]`
  - `Block`: `block_type: str`, `bbox: Tuple[int, int, int, int]`
  - `Match`: `page_number: int`, `text: str`, `bbox: Tuple[int, int, int, int]`
  - `Fingerprint`: `hash: str`, `fast_hash: str`
  - `Classification`: `category: str`, `confidence: float`
- `Metadata` class for `get_metadata` return value
- Each class should have an `@classmethod from_native(cls, native_dict)` constructor that converts from the PyO3 native layer's dict representation
- Add `__repr__` methods for debugging

Integration into API surface:
- Import types in `pdftract/__init__.py` and re-export
- Modify the 9 sync methods from child bead 1 to return these typed objects instead of raw dicts
- Call `ClassName.from_native(result)` before returning

## Acceptance criteria

## Scope

Generate the 9 contract methods via Tera templates with proper Go naming conventions (PascalCase for exported identifiers), option structs, and correct signatures per the SDK contract.

## Why this matters

The contract methods are the public API of the SDK. Code generation ensures consistency across SDKs and reduces maintenance burden. Option structs are the Go-idiomatic alternative to boolean flag parameters.

## Implementation guidance

- Create `codegen/methods.go` via Tera template generation:
  - Method signatures use PascalCase: `Extract`, `ExtractText`, `ExtractMarkdown`, `ExtractStream`, `Search`, `GetMetadata`, `Hash`, `Classify`, `VerifyReceipt`
  - Option structs: `ExtractOptions`, `SearchOptions`, `HashOptions` with exported fields
  - CLI flag to Go field mapping: `--ocr-language` → `OCRLanguage`, `--first-page` → `FirstPage`
  - Return types: `*Document`, `string`, `<-chan PageResult`, `<-chan MatchResult`, `*Metadata`, `*Fingerprint`, `*Classification`, `bool`
  - All methods accept `context.Context` as first parameter
- Create type definitions in `types.go`:
  - `type Document struct { ... }`
  - `type Metadata struct { ... }`
  - `type Fingerprint struct { ... }`
  - `type Classification struct { ... }`
  - `type PageResult struct { ... }`
  - `type MatchResult struct { ... }`

## Critical considerations

- Streaming methods (`ExtractStream`, `Search`) return receive-only channels (`<-chan`)
- Channels are buffered with size 16 to avoid blocking
- VerifyReceipt takes `path string` and `*Receipt` (not Source interface)

## Acceptance criteria

- All 9 methods are generated with correct signatures
- Option structs have exported PascalCase fields matching CLI flags
- Type definitions exist for all return types
- Methods call through to subprocess engine (implementation stub initially)
- `go build ./...` succeeds
- Template is documented in codegen/ directory

## References

- Plan: SDK Architecture / The Ten SDKs, line 3474 (9 contract methods)
- Go naming conventions: https://go.dev/doc/effective_go#names
- Parent bead: pdftract-2pyln
- Depends on: Child 3 (error handling used by methods)
issue.title: Go SDK: Contract method code generation and option structs

issue.description:
## Scope

Add `--receipts` CLI flag (`lite | svg | off`, default `off`) and thread `ExtractionOptions.receipts` through the extraction pipeline.

**Implementation:**

1. Add `--receipts <MODE>` flag to `pdftract extract` and `pdftract serve`
2. Add `ExtractionOptions.receipts: ReceiptMode` enum (`Off | Lite | Svg`)
3. Thread receipts mode through extract pipeline (from CLI/JSON API down to span/block emission)
4. When mode != Off, populate `receipt` field on spans and blocks
5. Output schema retains `receipt: null` placeholder when feature compiled out

**Why this matters:**

The --receipts flag is the user-facing control for receipt generation. It must be accessible from both CLI and MCP/HTTP APIs, and must flow through the entire pipeline to reach span/block emission.

**Critical considerations:**

- Default is `Off` (no receipts, zero overhead)
- Lite mode: ~120 bytes per receipt, ≤ 10% extraction time overhead
- SVG mode: ~1-5 KB per receipt, ≤ 25% extraction time overhead
- Feature flag `receipts` (opt-in) — when disabled, schema has `receipt: null` placeholder
- MCP/HTTP API respects `ExtractionOptions.receipts` from JSON request

**Acceptance criteria:**

- `--receipts` flag accepts `lite`, `svg`, `off` (case-insensitive)
- `ExtractionOptions.receipts` enum defined in core crate
- Receipt mode threaded through extract pipeline (verify with grep/cargo test)
- Spans and blocks have `receipt: Option<Receipt>` field populated when mode != Off
- Output schema stable (receipt field present but null when feature disabled)
- CLI help documents the flag and its modes
- MCP/HTTP API respects receipts option
- Module compiles and passes `cargo check --all-targets` and `cargo clippy`

**References:**

- Plan section: Phase 6.8 CLI flag (lines 2373, 2400-2402)
- INV-6 byte-identical re-extraction
issue.title: --receipts CLI flag + ExtractionOptions threading

- The controller should decrypt immediately; if Secret doesn't appear within 30 seconds, something is wrong
- Common failures: wrong namespace, malformed sealed data, controller not running
- Do NOT proceed to next bead until Secret exists

- PASS: Secret appears within 30 seconds of SealedSecret apply

issue.description:
## Scope

Add --profile-dir DIR flag to pdftract serve (repeatable). Add --profile-hot-reload flag. When hot-reload is enabled, re-read profile directory on every request (inotify-watched; polling fallback on non-inotify platforms). Operators can drop new YAML in DIR and next request picks it up without restart.

## Why this matters

Hot-reload lets operators iterate on profiles without restarting the serve process. Useful for tuning profiles in production. --profile-dir lets operators specify custom profile locations per deployment.

## Implementation guidance

- Add --profile-dir DIR flag to ServeCommand in src/cli.rs (repeatable)
- Add --profile-hot-reload flag to ServeCommand
- Load profiles from --profile-dir at startup
- When --profile-hot-reload is enabled:
  - Watch DIR with inotify (linux) or polling (other platforms)
  - On file change, reload ProfileRegistry
  - Next request uses new profiles
- Use notify crate for inotify (falls back to polling if inotify unavailable)
- Polling interval: 1 second
- Hot-reload disabled by default (file I/O on every request wasteful)
- Unit tests for profile loading
- Integration test for hot-reload behavior

## Critical considerations

- Hot-reload adds file I/O on every request when enabled (documented tradeoff)
- inotify preferred, polling fallback for compatibility
- Polling interval 1 second balances responsiveness vs CPU
- Hot-reload only watches --profile-dir, not XDG or /etc
- Hot-reload re-loads entire profile directory on change
- Hot-reload errors are logged but don't crash the serve process
- notify crate added to Cargo.toml (behind profiles feature flag)

## Acceptance criteria

- --profile-dir DIR loads profiles from DIR at startup
- Multiple --profile-dir flags work
- --profile-hot-reload enables directory watching
- Hot-reload picks up new YAML in DIR on next request (critical test)
- Hot-reload works with inotify on Linux
- Hot-reload falls back to polling on non-inotify platforms
- Hot-reload errors are logged
- Hot-reload disabled by default
- Unit tests cover profile loading
- Integration test shows hot-reload behavior

## References

- Plan 7.10 hot-reload lines 3069-3070
- Plan 7.10 CLI section lines 3026-3038

- Clean, understandable implementation
- Graceful handling of missing document context

**Recommended Next Steps (if needed):**

issue.description:
The Tera template templates/sdk-skeleton/ruby/lib/pdftract.rb.tera uses require_relative "codegen/methods" (and errors, types), which resolves to lib/codegen/*.rb relative to the file own directory. The actual generated files are at lib/pdftract/codegen/*.rb, so every generated Ruby SDK raises LoadError immediately on require "pdftract" -- the gem cannot even be loaded, before any other bug is reached.

Fix: change the three require_relative paths in the template to "pdftract/codegen/methods", "pdftract/codegen/errors", "pdftract/codegen/types".

Verified as root cause: same bug was manually patched as a stopgap in pdftract-ruby/lib/pdftract.rb and confirmed fixed by running the gem inside a ruby:3.2-slim container (require succeeded). See pdftract-ruby/docs/plan/plan.md ADR-001 (and the audit notes file in pdftract-ruby/docs/notes/ dated 2026 07 20).

After fixing the template, regenerate pdftract-ruby and re-verify require "pdftract" succeeds in ruby:3.2-slim before closing.
issue.title: pdftract-ruby: fix require_relative paths in Ruby SDK template (LoadError on require)

issue.description:
Location: crates/pdftract-core/src/source/mmap.rs:125-128

**Issue:** The `prefetch()` method calls `advise_sequential()` but discards any errors. While madvise failures are usually benign (kernel hint), this could hide calculation bugs.

**Code:**
```rust
fn prefetch(&self, offset: u64, length: usize) {
    // Apply MADV_SEQUENTIAL for content streams
    let _ = self.advise_sequential(offset, length);
}
```

**Why it's questionable:**
- If offset/length calculation is buggy, it would fail at runtime (line 80-85 validation)
- The function is documented as a hint, so failure is non-critical
- But silencing all errors means we lose observability on systemic issues

**ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:**
- Either:
  a) Log madvise failures at trace level for debugging, or
  b) Document why silencing is intentional with code comment
issue.title: Add Observability to Prefetch madvise Errors

## Scope

Generate option structs (`ExtractOptions`, `SearchOptions`, `HashOptions`) with exported PascalCase fields that map from CLI flags.

Option structs are the Go-idiomatic alternative to boolean flag parameters. They group related options and provide clear, self-documenting APIs.

## Implementation guidance

Using Tera templates, generate these option structs:

**ExtractOptions:**
- `OCRLanguage string` (from `--ocr-language`)
- `FirstPage int` (from `--first-page`)
- `LastPage int` (from `--last-page`)

- `WholeWord bool` (from `--whole-word`)
- `MaxResults int` (from `--max-results`)

**HashOptions:**
- `Algorithm string` (from `--hash-algorithm`)

CLI flag → Go field mapping rules:
- `--kebab-case` → `PascalCase`
- `--ocr-language` → `OCRLanguage`

Template should generate:
- Struct definition with exported fields
- Field tags (optional, for future serialization support)
- Godoc comments describing each field

## Critical considerations

- All struct fields must be exported (PascalCase)
- Boolean flags map to `bool` fields

issue.description:
## Scope

Create the ErrorParser class that parses stderr JSON output from the pdftract binary and maps error codes to the appropriate exception types.

## Why this matters

When the pdftract binary fails, it returns structured JSON on stderr. This parser converts that JSON into typed exceptions that .NET developers can catch.

## Implementation guidance

- Create `src/Pdftract/Process/ErrorParser.cs`
- Implement static method:
  ```csharp
  public static PdftractException ParseError(string stderrJson, int exitCode)
  ```

Expected JSON structure:
```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "FILE_NOT_FOUND",
    "message": "File not found: /path/to/file.pdf"
  }
}
```

Parse logic:
1. Use System.Text.Json to parse stderrJson
2. Extract `error.code` and `error.message` fields
3. Use a switch expression on `code` to map to exception types:
   - "FILE_NOT_FOUND" → new FileNotFoundException(...)
   - "INVALID_FORMAT" → new InvalidFormatException(...)
   - "PERMISSION_DENIED" → new PermissionDeniedException(...)
   - "TIMEOUT" → new TimeoutException(...)
   - "RESOURCE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED" → new ResourceLimitExceededException(...)
   - "ENCODING_ERROR" → new EncodingException(...)
   - "VALIDATION_ERROR" → new ValidationException(...)
   - "INTERNAL_ERROR" → new InternalErrorException(...)
   - default → new InternalErrorException(...) for unknown codes
4. Return the created exception instance

Error handling:
- Throw ArgumentException if JSON is malformed
- Throw ArgumentException if required fields are missing

## Acceptance criteria

- ErrorParser.cs exists and compiles
- ParseError method exists with correct signature
- Method parses JSON structure correctly
- All 8 error codes map to correct exception types
- Unknown error codes default to InternalErrorException
- Malformed JSON throws ArgumentException
- Missing required fields throw ArgumentException

## References

- Parent bead: bf-2w5jsv
- Plan section: SDK Architecture / The Ten SDKs, line 3476
- Depends on: Child beads 1-2 (base class and exception subclasses)
issue.title: Implement ErrorParser for stderr JSON mapping

Scope: The pdftract-core working tree currently does NOT compile. A prior attempt on parent bf-51739q added a `trailer: Option<&PdfDict>` parameter to `build_fingerprint_input` (in document.rs) but never updated its two call sites (parse_pdf_file and parse_pdf_source both pass only 4 args), and defined a `trailer_is_encrypted()` helper that is never called. This bead restores a clean, COMPILING baseline and lands the foundational detection primitive as a standalone, unit-tested helper with zero integration risk.

Why this matters: Every prior failure stalled on a half-threaded refactor that left the tree broken. Landing the detection logic in isolation — tested, on a compiling tree — removes that failure mode and gives every later child one authoritative, reusable primitive.

Implementation guidance:
1. First confirm the tree does not compile: `cargo check -p pdftract-core`. The broken edits are a prior failed attempt on THIS exact bead, so it is safe and correct to discard them: `git checkout crates/pdftract-core/src/document.rs` to return to HEAD.
2. Re-introduce a private helper `fn trailer_is_encrypted(trailer: Option<&PdfDict>) -> bool` in document.rs that returns true iff the trailer dict carries a non-null `/Encrypt` entry. (PDF object names are stored WITHOUT the leading slash — look up key "Encrypt"; a PdfObject::Null entry counts as absent.) This mirrors the semantics already used by the crate's `detect_encryption` function in the `crate::encryption::detection` module.
3. Add unit tests for the helper: (a) trailer with an `/Encrypt` dict -> true; (b) trailer with `/Encrypt: null` -> false; (c) None trailer -> false; (d) trailer without the key -> false. Construct PdfDict instances directly.

Critical considerations:
- Do NOT call the helper from build_fingerprint_input yet — that wiring belongs to a later child. This bead ships ONLY the helper + its tests and MUST leave the tree compiling.
- Do not touch the call sites or sdk.rs in this bead.

Acceptance criteria:
- `cargo check -p pdftract-core` passes (the tree compiles).
- `trailer_is_encrypted` exists in document.rs and is covered by 4 passing unit tests.
- `git diff` for document.rs shows ONLY the helper + its tests (no orphaned signature changes, no broken call sites).

References: parent bf-51739q; document.rs around the trailer_is_encrypted / build_fingerprint_input definitions and the parse_pdf_file / parse_pdf_source call sites; the crate::encryption::detection module's detect_encryption function.
issue.title: Establish compiling baseline and tested trailer-encryption detector

issue.description:
crates/pdftract-core/src/sdk.rs:122-124. The extract_stream() function is documented to provide streaming extraction with bounded memory usage, but the implementation calls extract_pdf() which loads the entire document model into memory before returning an iterator over results. This violates the plan requirement (docs/plan/plan.md line 74-75) that streaming/NDJSON mode must stay under 256MB constant regardless of page count. On a 10,000-page PDF (EC-03), this would exceed the memory ceiling by orders of magnitude.

The function signature promises streaming behavior (returns impl Iterator) but the implementation is:
```rust
pub fn extract_stream(...) -> Result<impl Iterator<Item = Result<PageResult>>> {
    let result = extract_pdf(pdf_path, options)?;  // Loads everything
    Ok(result.pages.into_iter().map(Ok))  // Then iterates
}
```

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
1. extract_stream() implements lazy page iteration that processes one page at a time
2. Peak RSS stays under 256MB when processing a 10,000-page PDF (measured by memory-ceiling harness)
3. No change to function signature (returns impl Iterator)
4. All existing conformance tests pass
issue.title: extract_stream() loads entire document into memory before returning iterator, violating plan's 256MB streaming ceiling

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the field DSL evaluator that extracts structured fields from document text. Localizers: near (find anchor spans, restrict to max_distance_pt), region (page fraction or bbox), pick (disambiguate multiple candidates). Extractors: regex (apply to candidate text), parse (convert to typed result). Evaluate in document order, first hit per field wins.

## Why this matters

Field extraction is what makes profiles useful for automation. Users can extract invoice_number, total, vendor, etc. without writing code. The DSL is simple but powerful enough for common extraction tasks.

## Implementation guidance

- FieldEvaluator in src/profile/field_eval.rs
- extract_fields(profile: &Profile, spans: &[Span], doc: &Document) -> BTreeMap<String, FieldValue>
- For each field in profile.fields:
  1. Identify candidate spans using localizers (near, region, pick)
  2. Apply regex to candidate text
  3. Apply parse to regex capture
  4. Return first successful match or null
- near localizer: find spans containing anchor strings, restrict to max_distance_pt (default 100)
- region localizer: filter spans by page region (top_quarter, bottom_quarter, left_half, right_half, top:N, bottom:N, bbox:[x0,y0,x1,y1])
- pick localizer: disambiguate multiple candidates (largest_font, smallest_font, nearest_below, nearest_right, first, last)
- regex extractor: apply to span text, capture group 1 (or 0 if no captures)
- parse extractor: convert string to decimal/date/int/bool using heuristics
- FieldValue enum: String(f64), String(String), Date(chrono::Date), Int(i64), Bool(bool), Null
- Evaluate in document order (spans sorted by position)
- First hit per field wins (deterministic)
- Unit tests for each localizer
- Unit tests for each extractor

## Critical considerations

- near localizer needs to search all spans for anchor strings; can be expensive
- max_distance_pt is Euclidean distance in PDF points (1/72 inch)
- region bbox uses PDF coordinate system (origin at bottom-left)
- pick largest_font uses span font size metrics
- pick nearest_below finds first span with y < anchor_y
- parse date uses heuristics (ISO 8601, US, EU formats)
- parse decimal uses locale-aware parsing
- Field extraction should add < 5% to per-document time (acceptance criterion)
- No field found returns FieldValue::Null, not an error

## Acceptance criteria

- near localizer finds spans near anchor text
- region localizer restricts to page regions
- pick localizer disambiguates candidates correctly
- regex extractor captures match groups
- parse extractor converts to typed values
- Field not found returns Null, not error
- Invoice profile extracts invoice_number, total, vendor, customer
- Unit tests cover each localizer
- Unit tests cover each extractor
- Integration test shows field extraction on invoice fixture
- Performance test: field extraction adds < 5% to per-document time

## References

- Plan 7.10 field DSL lines 2994-3006
- Plan 7.10 example fields lines 2942-2961
- Plan 7.10 output example lines 3009-3024
issue.title: 7.10.5: Field DSL evaluator (localizers near/region/pick + extractors regex/parse)

## Scope
Write a SealedSecret manifest that will contain the Forgejo token for iad-ci cluster.

## Why this matters
The SealedSecret controller decrypts sealed secrets in the cluster. We need the manifest structure before sealing the token.

## Implementation guidance
1. Create YAML manifest at path (in declarative-config):
   `k8s/iad-ci/external-secrets/forgejo-ci-token.yaml`
2. Structure:
   ```yaml
   apiVersion: bitnami.com/v1alpha1
   kind: SealedSecret
   metadata:
     name: forgejo-ci-token
     namespace: argo-workflows
   spec:
     encryptedData:
       token: <sealed-value-placeholder>
   ```
3. Use namespace: argo-workflows (where rust-verify runs)
4. Key name: token (matches rust-verify injection)

- Must use correct namespace (argo-workflows)
- Key name MUST be "token" to match rust-verify expectations
- Do NOT commit raw token - only sealed value

## Scope
Implement two remaining pieces: (1) the subprocess fallback path for musl-only environments where the native module fails to load, and (2) the conformance test runner under `crates/pdftract-py/tests/test_conformance.py`.

## Why this matters
- Subprocess fallback: Pre-built abi3 wheels don't cover musl-libc Linux (Alpine). The fallback ensures the SDK still works by calling the CLI binary via `subprocess.run`.
- Conformance runner: The SDK must pass the shared contract test suite. This runner executes the suite via the Python API.

## Implementation guidance

### Part 1: Subprocess fallback
Modify `pdftract/__init__.py`:
- Wrap `import pdftract._native` in a try/except `ImportError`
- On import error, define fallback stub functions that call the CLI binary via `subprocess.run`
- Detect the CLI binary path (e.g., `pdftract` in PATH, or `shutil.which("pdftract")`)
- Fallback implementation for each of the 9 methods:
  - `subprocess.run([cli_path, "extract", "--json", source], check=True)`
  - Parse JSON output and return the same type as the native path
- Document the fallback in `crates/pdftract-py/README.md` (when it activates, what limitations it has)

### Part 2: Conformance test runner
Create `crates/pdftract-py/tests/test_conformance.py`:
- Import the shared test suite (from the Rust repo's `tests/conformance/` fixtures)
- Invoke each test case through the Python API (not the CLI)
- Report per-case pass/fail
- Use pytest or unittest framework
- Ensure 100% of test cases pass (same pass rate as the Rust implementation)

Test fixture integration:
- The conformance suite lives in the Rust repo at `tests/conformance/`
- Python runner should load fixtures via the same mechanism (or copy fixtures locally)
- Each test case calls the Python method and asserts the expected result

### Part 3: Package metadata
Update `crates/pdftract-py/pyproject.toml`:
- Declare `[project]` with:
  - `name = "pdftract"`
  - `version` synced from the binary (Cargo.toml version)
  - `license = "MIT OR Apache-2.0"`
  - `requires-python = ">=3.11"`
  - `dependencies` (if any)
- Ensure `pdftract` package is correctly configured for wheel building

## Acceptance criteria
- Subprocess fallback activates when `import pdftract._native` raises `ImportError`
- Fallback methods call the CLI binary and return parsed results
- `tests/test_conformance.py` exists and runs the full suite
- 100% of conformance test cases pass (same as Rust baseline)
- `pyproject.toml` declares correct package metadata
- `crates/pdftract-py/README.md` documents the subprocess fallback behavior
- Smoke test: Force ImportError (rename `_native.so` temporarily) and verify fallback works

## References
- Parent bead: pdftract-2nu0s
- Depends on: [child bead 1 - sync API surface], [child bead 2 - exception hierarchy], [child bead 3 - type definitions]
- Plan section: SDK Architecture / Per-SDK Release Channels, line 3568 (pdftract-py-ci handles publishing)
- Plan section: SDK Acceptance Criteria, lines 3581-3589

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the core subprocess execution engine in `subprocess.go` that spawns the `pdftract` binary, communicates via stdin/stdout, parses JSON output, and supports context cancellation.

## Why this matters

This is the heart of the Go SDK — every contract method flows through this engine. Proper context cancellation is critical; leaked subprocesses are correctness bugs.

## Implementation guidance

- Create `subprocess.go` with:
  - `ExecConfig` struct holding binary path, args, stdin payload
  - `Exec(ctx context.Context, config ExecConfig) ([]byte, error)` function
  - Use `exec.CommandContext` for automatic cancellation
  - Set `cmd.Cancel = func() error { return cmd.Process.Kill() }` for hard kill on cancellation
  - Connect stdin via `cmd.Stdin = bytes.NewBuffer(payload)`
  - Capture stdout via `bytes.Buffer`
  - Parse JSON via `json.NewDecoder(stdout).Decode(&target)`
  - Return exit code mapping: map non-zero exits to error kinds

## Critical considerations

- A cancelled context MUST kill the subprocess — verify this in tests
- The binary path is resolved at runtime (not hardcoded); use `exec.LookPath` or env var
- Stderr is discarded for now (future enhancement: capture on debug mode)

## Acceptance criteria

- `Exec(ctx, config)` spawns pdftract and returns parsed JSON or error
- Passing a pre-cancelled context terminates the subprocess and returns `ctx.Err()`
- Non-zero exit codes are mapped to error returns (error kinds implemented later)
- Unit tests cover: successful execution, cancellation, non-zero exit
- No orphaned processes in test runs (verify with pgrep)

## References

- Plan: SDK Acceptance Criteria, line 3587 (context.Context for cancellation)
- Go exec package: https://pkg.go.dev/os/exec
- Parent bead: pdftract-2pyln
- Depends on: Child 1 (module scaffolding)
issue.title: Go SDK: Subprocess engine and context cancellation

issue.description:
## Scope
Implement the streaming layer for `extractStream` and `search` (NDJSON line-by-line parsing into `Readable`), plus the ergonomics layer for option normalization and type coercion.

## Why this matters
Streaming is critical for large PDFs — consumers must process pages incrementally. The ergonomics layer ensures the SDK feels idiomatic to Node.js developers (camelCase options, type coercion for paths/URLs/Buffers).

## Implementation guidance
- Implement `src/stream.ts`:
  - `NdjsonReadable` class extends `Readable`
  - Consumes stdout line-by-line (split on \\n)
  - Emits parsed JSON objects (Page for extractStream, Match for search)
  - Handles partial lines and backpressure
- Wire streaming into generated methods:
  - `extractStream()`: returns `NdjsonReadable` emitting Page objects
  - `search()`: returns `NdjsonReadable` emitting Match objects
- Implement `src/ergonomics.ts`:
  - `normalizeOptions(options: object): object` — camelCase to kebab-case
  - `coerceSource(source: string | URL | Buffer): string` — handle Buffer temp file, URL to path
  - Type coercion for enums (e.g., `ocrLanguage` string validation)
- Update generated methods to use ergonomics layer

issue.description:
INFRA. Seal the Forgejo CI token as a Kubernetes SealedSecret named `forgejo-ci-token` with key `token`.

## Scope
- Use `kubeseal` CLI tool to seal the token into a SealedSecret manifest
- Secret name: `forgejo-ci-token`
- Secret namespace: `argo-workflows`
- Secret key: `token`
- Output: SealedSecret YAML manifest

## Why this matters
SealedSecrets encrypt secrets so they can be safely committed to git. The SealedSecret controller on iad-ci will decrypt it into a real Secret that rust-verify can mount.

## Implementation guidance
1. Ensure kubeseal is installed (or retrieve from iad-ci cluster):
   ```bash
   kubectl --kubeconfig=/home/coding/.kube/iad-ci.kubeconfig      get deployment -n kube-system sealed-secrets-controller
   ```

2. Create a temporary literal secret and seal it:
   ```bash
   echo -n 'YOUR_TOKEN_HERE' |    kubectl --kubeconfig=/home/coding/.kube/iad-ci.kubeconfig      create secret generic forgejo-ci-token -n argo-workflows      --dry-run=client --from-file=token=/dev/stdin -o json |    kubeseal --controller-namespace=kube-system --format yaml      > forgejo-ci-token-sealed.yaml
   ```

3. Verify the sealed manifest is valid YAML and contains encrypted data

## Critical considerations
- Use `-n` (no newline) when echoing the token to avoid whitespace corruption
- The sealed cert must come from the iad-ci cluster (certificate fetch via kubeseal --fetch-cert)
- Do NOT commit the raw token — only the SealedSecret YAML

## Acceptance criteria
- PASS: SealedSecret YAML generated successfully
- PASS: YAML contains valid encrypted data (not plaintext)
- PASS: Secret namespace is `argo-workflows`
- PASS: Secret key is `token`
- WARN: If kubeseal unavailable, manifest can be generated manually with proper cert

## References
- Bead bf-2f91m8 (prerequisite: provides the token)
- Bead bf-5ig30 (parent)
- SealedSecrets docs: https://github.com/bitnami-labs/sealed-secrets

## Scope
Add the `Fingerprint` and `Classification` type definitions to `pdftract-go/types.go`.

## Why this matters
These types represent analysis results. Fingerprint identifies documents via hashing; Classification represents document classification with confidence scores. They are independent and don't depend on other types in the SDK.

## Implementation guidance
Add to `pdftract-go/types.go`:

```go
// Fingerprint uniquely identifies a document via cryptographic hash
type Fingerprint struct {
	Hash      string // Hex-encoded hash value
	Algorithm string // Hash algorithm used (e.g., "sha256")
	Pages     int    // Number of pages in the document
}

// Classification represents a document classification result
type Classification struct {
	Type        string  // Classification type/category
	Confidence  float64 // Confidence score (0.0 to 1.0)
	Label       string  // Human-readable label
}
```

issue.description:
File: crates/pdftract-cli/src/cache_cmd.rs:103,400

compute_stats() (line 103) and purge_cache_older_than() (line 400) call:
    SystemTime::now().duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH).unwrap()

This panics if system clock is misconfigured (set before Unix epoch). While extremely rare, this violates the no-panic error model — a misconfigured system clock should return an error, not crash the process.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
1. Replace .unwrap() with proper error propagation (.context()?)
2. Test added that simulates SystemTime::now() returning error (mocking or conditional compilation)
3. Error message clearly explains 'System clock misconfiguration — time before Unix epoch'
issue.title: Fix cache_cmd compute_stats() and purge_cache_older_than() panic on SystemTime failure

## Scope

Implement acceptance tests for Phase 7.10 Document Profiles. Critical tests: Acrobat sample invoice classified as invoice with confidence > 0.8, fields extracted >= 90% accuracy across 50-invoice fixture, custom profile with priority 100 overrides built-ins, malformed regex rejected with line-numbered error, profile_fields.total: null when not found, hot-reload picks up new YAML, user profile shadowing built-in shown in list.

## Why this matters

Acceptance tests verify the entire profile system works end-to-end. They catch regressions in profile loading, matching, extraction, and CLI behavior. The 50-invoice fixture corpus ensures the invoice profile is accurate and robust.

## Implementation guidance

- tests/profiles_acceptance.rs with all acceptance tests
- test_invoice_classification_confidence: load Acrobat invoice, run --auto, assert confidence > 0.8
- test_invoice_field_accuracy: run invoice profile on 50-invoice fixture, assert >= 90% per-field accuracy
- test_custom_profile_priority_override: create profile with priority 100 matching all docs, assert it overrides built-ins
- test_malformed_regex_validate_error: create YAML with malformed regex, run validate, assert line-numbered error
- test_field_not_found_null: create profile with field that doesn't match, run extract, assert profile_fields.field: null
- test_hot_reload: start serve with --profile-hot-reload, drop new YAML, assert next request picks it up
- test_user_profile_shadows_built_in: install user invoice profile, run list, assert (overrides built-in) annotation
- Fixture corpus: tests/fixtures/profiles/invoice/ with 50 invoice PDFs and labeled field values
- Fixture corpus: tests/fixtures/profiles/receipt/, contract/, scientific_paper/, slide_deck/, form/, bank_statement/, legal_filing/, book_chapter/ (5 each)
- Regression tests for each built-in profile against its fixture corpus
- Performance test: field extraction adds < 5% to per-document time

## Critical considerations

- 50-invoice fixture must have labeled field values for accuracy calculation
- Per-field accuracy: (correct_fields / total_fields) >= 0.9
- Malformed regex test needs invalid regex pattern (unclosed bracket, etc.)
- Hot-reload test needs to actually drop a file and wait for inotify/polling
- Shadowing test needs to install user profile and verify list output
- Performance test measures time with and without field extraction

## Acceptance criteria

- Acrobat sample invoice classified with confidence > 0.8 (critical test)
- Invoice profile >= 90% field accuracy on 50-invoice fixture (critical test)
- Custom profile with priority 100 overrides built-ins (critical test)
- Malformed regex rejected with line-numbered error (critical test)
- Field not found returns null (critical test)
- Hot-reload picks up new YAML (critical test)
- User profile shadowing shown in list (critical test)
- Field extraction adds < 5% to per-document time (acceptance criterion)
- 9 built-in profiles have >= 5 fixtures each (acceptance criterion)
- All tests pass

## References

- Plan 7.10 acceptance criteria lines 3071-3088
- Plan 7.10 built-in profiles lines 3053-3067
issue.title: 7.10.10: Phase 7.10 acceptance tests (invoice classification, custom profiles, validate errors, null fields, hot-reload, shadowing)

issue.description: Plan cite: docs/plan/plan.md "## Monitoring and Alerting" section (~line 3865-3909). Specifies a --metrics PORT flag for both "pdftract serve" and "pdftract mcp --bind", exposing a /metrics endpoint in OpenMetrics v1.0 text format (content-type application/openmetrics-text; version=1.0.0; charset=utf-8) on a SEPARATE listener from the main serve/mcp port. 13 named metrics are specified: pdftract_extractions_total (counter, labels result/ocr), pdftract_extraction_duration_seconds (histogram), pdftract_pages_extracted_total (counter), pdftract_cache_hits_total, pdftract_cache_misses_total, pdftract_cache_size_bytes (gauge), pdftract_mcp_requests_total (counter, label tool), pdftract_http_requests_total (counter, labels endpoint/status), pdftract_remote_bytes_downloaded_total, pdftract_diagnostic_emitted_total (counter, labels code/severity), pdftract_inflight_extractions (gauge), pdftract_rayon_pool_utilization (gauge 0..1), pdftract_build_info (gauge, labels version/git_sha/features). The plan also specifies a GET /ready readiness endpoint distinct from the existing GET /health (health always returns 200; ready returns 503 when rayon pool utilization > 90% OR cache is not writable). VERIFIED GAP: crates/pdftract-cli/src/serve.rs and crates/pdftract-cli/src/mcp/http.rs currently implement ONLY /health (always-200 liveness check) — the module doc comment at the top of serve.rs explicitly enumerates its 4 endpoints (POST /extract, POST /extract/text, POST /extract/stream, GET /health) with no /metrics or /ready. Repo-wide grep for openmetrics, rayon_pool_utilization, extractions_total, extraction_duration_seconds, "GET /ready", and a --metrics flag all return zero hits; there is no metrics Cargo feature in any Cargo.toml. The only related closed bead, bf-57ko1, added a static docs/operations/prometheus-rules.yaml sample alert-rules file that references these metric names — but the metrics themselves were never implemented, so that shipped doc currently references nonexistent metrics. ACTION: add a metrics feature flag (implicitly enabled by serve, per the plan), the --metrics PORT CLI flag on both serve and mcp --bind subcommands (crates/pdftract-cli/src/serve.rs, crates/pdftract-cli/src/mcp/http.rs and its CLI wiring in crates/pdftract-cli/src/main.rs / cli.rs), a separate axum listener on that port serving /metrics and /ready, and instrument the 13 metrics at the existing extraction/cache/diagnostic call sites in serve.rs and mcp/http.rs. No new crate is mandated — a hand-rolled OpenMetrics text formatter is acceptable to stay within the serve feature size budget (check with cargo bloat before adding a metrics crate). Add integration test(s) verifying /metrics returns parseable OpenMetrics text with the documented metric names and that /ready returns 503 under simulated cache-unwritable / high rayon-utilization conditions and 200 otherwise.
issue.title: Implement Prometheus /metrics endpoint and /ready readiness probe for pdftract serve/mcp

issue.description:
The Tera template templates/sdk-skeleton/ruby/lib/pdftract.rb.tera uses require_relative "codegen/methods" (and errors, types), which resolves to lib/codegen/*.rb relative to the file own directory. The actual generated files are at lib/pdftract/codegen/*.rb, so every generated Ruby SDK raises LoadError immediately on require "pdftract" -- the gem cannot even be loaded, before any other bug is reached.

Fix: change the three require_relative paths in the template to "pdftract/codegen/methods", "pdftract/codegen/errors", "pdftract/codegen/types".

Verified as root cause: same bug was manually patched as a stopgap in pdftract-ruby/lib/pdftract.rb and confirmed fixed by running the gem inside a ruby:3.2-slim container (require succeeded). See pdftract-ruby/docs/plan/plan.md ADR-001 (and the audit notes file in pdftract-ruby/docs/notes/ dated 2026 07 20).

After fixing the template, regenerate pdftract-ruby and re-verify require "pdftract" succeeds in ruby:3.2-slim before closing.
issue.title: pdftract-ruby: fix require_relative paths in Ruby SDK template (LoadError on require)

Workers need isolated branches for per-bead verification. These branches allow rust-verify to run against the specific code changes produced by a worker without affecting the main branch.

- Add function

  1. Get or create the worker's worktree path
  2. Create a new branch named wip/<worker>/<bead_id>
  3. Commit any staged changes (if any)
  4. Push the branch to Forgejo origin
  5. Return the full branch ref (e.g., refs/heads/wip/worker/bf-4st8y)

Use existing git patterns in NEEDLE (git commands via crate::git module).

- Branch naming must be deterministic: wip/<worker>/<bead_id>

Create the `jedarden/pdftract-node` repo (or local directory) and initialize `package.json` with basic project metadata and dual ESM/CJS exports configuration.

Test the rust-verify WorkflowTemplate with a real git.ardenone.com repo to confirm FORGEJO_TOKEN injection works end-to-end.

## Scope
Trigger a test rust-verify workflow against a git.ardenone.com repo and verify it can clone successfully using the forgejo-ci-token secret.

## Why this matters
The entire chain is complete only when rust-verify can actually clone repos. This verifies the secret exists, has the right value, and is correctly injected.

## Implementation guidance
1. Submit a test workflow to iad-ci:
   ```bash
   kubectl --kubeconfig=/home/coding/.kube/iad-ci.kubeconfig create -f - <<EOF
   apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
   kind: Workflow
   metadata:
     generateName: rust-verify-test-forgejo-
     namespace: argo-workflows
   spec:
     workflowTemplateRef:
       name: rust-verify
     arguments:
       parameters:
       - name: repo
         value: git.ardenone.com/jedarden/pdftract
       - name: ref
         value: main
   EOF
   ```
2. Watch the workflow logs for the clone step
3. Verify `git clone` succeeds with FORGEJO_TOKEN
4. Check the workflow completes successfully

## Critical considerations
- Use a real git.ardenone.com repo (pdftract or another)
- The repo must be private or require auth (public repos won't prove token works)
- If clone fails, check:
  - Secret exists: `kubectl get secret forgejo-ci-token -n argo-workflows`
  - Token is valid (not expired/revoked)
  - FORGEJO_TOKEN injection in rust-verify template

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] rust-verify test workflow submitted to iad-ci
- [ ] Workflow reaches the git clone step
- [ ] Clone step succeeds (no authentication failure)
- [ ] Workflow completes successfully (fmt + clippy + test pass)
- [ ] No errors related to FORGEJO_TOKEN or git authentication

## References
- rust-verify WorkflowTemplate: declarative-config/k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/rust-verify.yaml
- iad-ci access: ~/.kube/iad-ci.kubeconfig
- Argo UI: https://argo-ci.ardenone.com (for log viewing)

issue.description: crates/pdftract-py/src/lib.rs:193-209. The registered Python API function search() (wrap_pyfunction at lib.rs:435) ignores _path (note the leading underscore: the path is never used) and returns {pattern: <pattern>, matches: []} unconditionally. Meanwhile pdftract_core::sdk::search (crates/pdftract-core/src/sdk.rs:142) is a working regex/plain/whole-word matcher returning Vec<SearchMatch> with page_index, span_index, text and bbox. Python users calling pdftract.search(path, pattern) always get zero matches even when the pattern is present in the PDF. ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA: search() passes path to a real matcher and no longer returns a fixed empty list; for a fixture containing a known string, search(fixture, that_string) returns a non-empty matches list whose entries carry page/span/bbox, consistent with sdk::search output.
issue.title: PyO3 search() always returns empty matches instead of calling sdk::search

issue.description:
## Scope
Add the two foundational type definitions to `pdftract-go/types.go`: `Page` and `Metadata`.

## Why this matters
These are the building blocks that other types depend on. `Page` is the basic page representation, and `Metadata` contains document metadata fields. They must exist before `Document` can reference them.

## Implementation guidance
Create `pdftract-go/types.go` if it does not exist, then add:

```go
// Page represents a single page in a PDF document
type Page struct {
	Number  int // Page number (1-indexed)
	Width   int // Page width in points
	Height  int // Page height in points
	Rotation int // Page rotation in degrees (0, 90, 180, 270)
}

// Metadata contains document-level metadata
type Metadata struct {
	Pages       int      // Total number of pages
	Title       string   // Document title
	Author      string   // Document author
	Subject     string   // Document subject
	Keywords    []string // List of keywords
	Creator     string   // Application that created the document
	Producer    string   // Application that produced the PDF
	CreationDate string // ISO 8601 creation date
	ModDate      string // ISO 8601 modification date
	Tagged       bool    // Whether the document is tagged
	Form         bool    // Whether the document is a form
	Encrypted    bool    // Whether the document is encrypted
}
```

## Acceptance criteria
- `pdftract-go/types.go` exists
- Contains `Page` struct with 4 exported fields (Number, Width, Height, Rotation)
- Contains `Metadata` struct with 11 exported fields
- Both types have godoc comments
- `go build ./pdftract-go` succeeds (no syntax errors)

- Parent bead: bf-3oxjgi
- Plan: SDK Architecture / The Ten SDKs, line 3474

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the core async process spawning logic in ProcessWrapper.StartAsync and synchronous Start methods. Handle stdout/stderr reading, deadlock avoidance, and process lifecycle management.

## Why this matters

This is the heart of the subprocess infrastructure. Every SDK call will flow through these methods, so they must correctly spawn processes, read output without deadlocking, handle timeouts, and manage process cleanup.

## Implementation guidance

- Implement \`ProcessWrapper.StartAsync(string[] args)\`:
  - Use \`System.Diagnostics.Process\` configured with:
    - RedirectStandardOutput = true
    - RedirectStandardError = true
    - UseShellExecute = false
  - Get binary path from \`ResolveBinaryPath()\`
  - Configure \`StartInfo.FileName\` and \`StartInfo.Arguments\` (join args array)
  - Spawn with \`process.Start()\` in a try/catch
  - Asynchronously read stdout to completion with \`process.StandardOutput.ReadToEndAsync()\`
  - Read stderr synchronously with \`process.StandardOutput.ReadToEnd()\`
  - Await \`process.WaitForExitAsync(cancellationToken)\`
  - Return \`ProcessResult\` with Stdout, Stderr, ExitCode
- Implement \`ProcessWrapper.Start(string[] args)\` (synchronous version):
  - Same configuration, but use \`process.WaitForExit()\` instead of async
  - Still read streams synchronously
- Handle edge cases:
  - If \`cancellationToken\` is canceled during execution, call \`process.Kill(entireProcessTree: true)\`
  - Ensure streams are drained before WaitForExit to avoid deadlocks
- Add unit tests:
  - Mock process spawning (use actual small binary or mock Process class)
  - Verify stdout is read correctly
  - Verify stderr is captured
  - Verify exit code is returned
  - Verify cancellation kills the process

## Acceptance criteria

- StartAsync spawns process with correct binary path and arguments
- StandardOutput is read asynchronously without deadlocks
- StandardError is captured for error parsing
- WaitForExitAsync properly handles cancellation
- Process.Kill(entireProcessTree: true) called on cancellation
- Start synchronous version works correctly
- Unit tests verify successful execution with real small binary
- Unit tests verify cancellation kills process tree
- Unit tests verify stdout/stderr capture

## References

- Parent bead: bf-4ej9sq
- Plan section: SDK Architecture / The Ten SDKs, line 3476
- Depends on: Child bead 1 (ProcessWrapper class and binary resolution)
issue.title: .NET SDK: Implement async process spawning and I/O handling in ProcessWrapper

**Scope:**
Implement the stream resolution logic that dereferences the char_proc ObjRef returned by font.char_proc() to fetch and decode the actual content stream bytes from the PDF document. The resolve_stream_bytes() helper at resolver.rs:666-692 provides the template for this.

**Why this matters:**
Type3 glyph definitions are stored as PDF content streams referenced by ObjRef. Without resolving these refs to actual bytes, the rasterizer has nothing to execute.

**Implementation guidance:**
1. Study the existing resolve_stream_bytes() function at resolver.rs:666-692 as a reference
2. The callback closure passed to rasterize_type3_glyph() should invoke resolve_stream_bytes(char_proc_ref)
3. Ensure the callback properly handles:
   - Resolving the ObjRef through the XrefResolver
   - Extracting the PdfObject::Stream from the resolved object
   - Decoding the stream bytes (apply filters, decompression)
   - Returning None on any failure (non-stream object, decode failure, etc.)

**Critical considerations:**
- The callback must be callable as Fn(ObjRef) -> Option<Vec<u8>>
- Handle decode errors gracefully by returning None
- Respect the max_decompress_bytes budget (tracked via doc_decompress_counter)
- The callback closure needs to capture resolver, source, and counter by reference

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Char_proc ObjRef is resolved to actual stream bytes via the callback
- Stream decode properly applies all filters (FlateDecode, etc.)
- Decode errors return None rather than panicking
- Unit test with mock ObjRef verifies correct byte extraction

**References:**
- crates/pdftract-core/src/font/resolver.rs:666-692 - resolve_stream_bytes() template
- crates/pdftract-core/src/font/type3_rasterizer.rs:582 - char_proc_ref extraction
issue.title: Resolve char_proc ObjRef to content stream bytes

**Parent:** bf-546hs1

**Scope:**
Implement the core PDF path construction operators in RasterizerContext: moveto, lineto, curveto, closepath. These operators build paths in device coordinate space.

**Why this matters:**
Type3 glyph content streams use path construction operators to define glyph outlines. Without these, the rasterizer cannot interpret drawing commands.

**Implementation guidance:**
1. Add  field to track path operations
2. Implement  - starts new subpath at (x,y)
3. Implement  - adds line segment from current point to (x,y)
4. Implement  - adds Bezier curve with two control points
5. Implement  - closes current subpath with line to start point
6. All coordinates should be stored in current path, not yet rasterized

**Critical considerations:**
- Path operators only build the path - they do NOT draw to bitmap yet

issue.description:
## Scope

Bring docs/research/table-structure-reconstruction.md to v1.0 final-pass: document the line-based grid reconstruction algorithm (collect horizontal+vertical path segments from content stream operators m/l/S, re/S, re/f; cluster collinear segments; find intersections; build grid from intersections) plus the borderless-table fallback and the cell-content assignment pass.

## Why this matters

Table extraction is the highest-value structured-output feature shipped at v1.0 (without it, financial documents, scientific papers, and invoices lose huge swathes of their information). Line 2571 in the plan explicitly cites this note as the grid reconstruction algorithm authority. The current 218-line draft sets up the framework but predates the full pipeline specification.

## Implementation guidance

- File to update: docs/research/table-structure-reconstruction.md (already exists, currently 218 lines)
- Required content sections:
  - Strategy 1 -- Line-based detection (the primary path):
    - Path-segment collection: scan content stream for m, l, S, re, S, re, f operators
    - Coordinate accumulation: every segment endpoint goes into a (x, y) bag with operator metadata
    - Clustering: bin endpoints by collinearity (epsilon-tolerance on the orthogonal axis); deduplicate within a font_size epsilon
    - Intersection extraction: for each pair of orthogonal clusters, emit an intersection point if both clusters cross
    - Grid synthesis: connect intersections into rectangular cells; reject cells whose interior overlaps a non-grid graphic
  - Strategy 2 -- Borderless tables: tab-stop alignment of text spans across multiple lines; cluster x-coordinates of span starts; if N >= 3 rows share K >= 2 aligned columns, infer a borderless table
  - Cell content assignment: for each cell rectangle, collect all text spans whose centroid lies inside; sort by reading order; assemble cell text
  - Header detection: top row OR first column with bold / larger font / shaded background heuristics
  - Output: table block with rows, columns, cells[row][col].text, header_row/header_col flags
- Algorithm pseudo-code listings for both strategies

## Critical considerations

- The line-based detector is sensitive to PDF generators that approximate table borders with closely-spaced re operators (rectangles) vs single l operators (lines) -- both must be handled
- Borderless detection has high false-positive risk (any aligned-column text could be inferred as a table) -- require a minimum row + column count plus reading-order coherence
- Cell text reassembly must respect the Phase 4.5 reading-order strategy chosen for the page; do not force xy_cut inside cells if line_dominant is the active strategy
- The Phase 7.10 invoice profile sets table_detection: strict_borders -- the algorithm must honour this knob (skip borderless inference when set)
- Header detection heuristics MUST emit a confidence score (used by downstream consumers to ignore weakly-inferred headers)
- Diagonal lines, rounded-rectangle borders, hairline borders below the visibility threshold all need explicit handling decisions

## Acceptance criteria

- docs/research/table-structure-reconstruction.md updated with both strategies fully documented in algorithm form
- Pseudo-code listings present for both strategies
- Header-detection heuristics enumerated with confidence formula
- Strict-borders mode behaviour documented (Phase 7.10 alignment)
- Edge cases (rounded rectangles, hairline borders, diagonals, generator quirks) documented
- File grows to approx 400+ lines

## References

- Plan: line 2571 (grid reconstruction reference), Phase 7 (table feature ship at v1.0 per line 3329), Phase 4.5 (reading order interaction), Phase 7.10 (table_detection knob)
issue.title: Research note: docs/research/table-structure-reconstruction.md final-pass with grid algorithm

issue.description:
## Scope

Coordinator for sub-phase 2.4: handle Type 3 fonts whose glyphs are arbitrary content streams in `/CharProcs`. No standard glyph names, no embedded font program — every glyph requires either `/ToUnicode`, or the `/Encoding` glyph-name lookup, or shape recognition by rasterizing the glyph's content stream and matching against the shape DB. Includes Type3-specific metric handling via `/Widths`, `/FirstChar`, `/LastChar`, `/FontMatrix`.

## Why this matters

Type 3 fonts are the wild west. Word's "convert math equation to outlines" produces Type 3 fonts; many corporate PDFs use Type 3 for custom symbols. Pdfminer.six gives up entirely on Type 3 (emits U+FFFD). Pdftract's shape-recognition fallback recovers them, which is the marquee accuracy improvement over the competition for technical documents.

## Children

- Type 3 font loader (/CharProcs, /Widths, /FontMatrix)
- Type 3 glyph content stream rasterizer (32x32 bitmap producer)
- Type 3 resolver: ToUnicode -> Encoding name -> shape DB chain

## Critical considerations

- Type 3 metrics: `/Widths[code - FirstChar]` is in TEXT units; `/FontMatrix` converts glyph-program coords to text units. Default FontMatrix `[0.001 0 0 0.001 0 0]` matches Type 1; `[1 0 0 1 0 0]` is also common.
- Type 3 glyph programs can invoke arbitrary PDF operators including `Do` (form XObject) — the rasterizer must reuse the Phase 3 graphics state machine. Stack depth limit applies.
- Shape recognition for Type 3 hits the SAME shape DB used by Phase 2.5 — no separate codepath.
- INV: Type 3 glyphs with arbitrary names + no ToUnicode resolve via shape match with confidence 0.7.

## Acceptance criteria

- All 3 children closed.
- Type 3 font with `/ToUnicode`: resolves at confidence 1.0.
- Type 3 font with standard glyph names but no ToUnicode: resolves via L2 AGL at 0.9.
- Type 3 font with arbitrary names and no ToUnicode: rasterized + shape-matched at 0.7.
