issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the `libpdftract` shared library: a fourth workspace member (`crates/pdftract-libpdftract`) with `crate-type = ["cdylib"]` exposing the 9 contract methods as `extern "C"` functions. Generate the `pdftract.h` header via cbindgen. The API returns owned JSON strings the caller frees with `pdftract_free()`; the library is reentrant and thread-safe. Distribute via GitHub Release (binary `.so`/`.dylib`/`.dll` + `.h` + `.pc` pkg-config file) plus a Homebrew formula PR (auto-opened) plus a vcpkg port PR (manual reviewer involvement).

## Why this matters

C/C++ is the lingua franca for FFI; libpdftract is the bridge that any language without a dedicated SDK (R, Erlang, Common Lisp, Tcl, niche or future languages) can call via its own FFI mechanism. cbindgen-generated headers eliminate the manual header-synchronisation burden. The owned-string return + caller-frees pattern is the standard C-FFI convention; thread-safety and reentrancy mean concurrent calls Just Work.

## Implementation guidance

- Crate: `crates/pdftract-libpdftract/` (fourth workspace member; update `[workspace]` members list in root Cargo.toml)
- Cargo.toml declares `crate-type = ["cdylib", "staticlib"]` (both shared and static for downstream flexibility)
- Public API: every function is `pub extern "C"` and uses C-compatible types (`*const c_char`, `*mut c_char`, `usize`, `i32`)
- Method signatures (representative):
  ```c
  // Returns JSON string; caller MUST free with pdftract_free()
  char* pdftract_extract(const char* source, const char* options_json);
  char* pdftract_extract_text(const char* source, const char* options_json);
  char* pdftract_extract_markdown(const char* source, const char* options_json);
  // Streaming returns an opaque handle; pdftract_stream_next yields one Page JSON at a time
  void* pdftract_extract_stream_open(const char* source, const char* options_json);
  char* pdftract_stream_next(void* handle);  // returns NULL when stream ends
  void pdftract_stream_close(void* handle);
  char* pdftract_search(const char* source, const char* pattern, const char* options_json);
  char* pdftract_get_metadata(const char* source, const char* options_json);
  char* pdftract_hash(const char* source, const char* options_json);
  char* pdftract_classify(const char* source);
  int32_t pdftract_verify_receipt(const char* path, const char* receipt_json);  // 0 = invalid, 1 = valid
  // Free a string returned by any of the above
  void pdftract_free(char* ptr);
  // Last error retrieval (thread-local)
  const char* pdftract_last_error(void);
  // ABI version
  uint32_t pdftract_abi_version(void);
  ```
- cbindgen config (`crates/pdftract-libpdftract/cbindgen.toml`):
  - `language = "C"`
  - `include_guard = "PDFTRACT_H"`
  - `pragma_once = true`
  - `cpp_compat = true` (generates `extern "C"` wrappers for C++ users)
  - `documentation = true` (cbindgen renders doc comments)
- Generated header file: `crates/pdftract-libpdftract/include/pdftract.h` (regenerated by `cargo build --features cbindgen`)
- pkg-config file: `crates/pdftract-libpdftract/pdftract.pc.in` (templated with version + install prefix); installed alongside the library
- Distribution: GitHub Release attachments named `libpdftract-vX.Y.Z-<triple>.tar.gz` containing `lib/libpdftract.so`, `include/pdftract.h`, `lib/pkgconfig/pdftract.pc`, both LICENSE files
- Homebrew formula: auto-PR against `homebrew-core` or a `jedarden/homebrew-tap` repo (the tap is the lower-friction path)
- vcpkg port: manual PR against `microsoft/vcpkg`

## Critical considerations

- Memory ownership rules: every string returned by `pdftract_*` is HEAP-ALLOCATED and the caller MUST call `pdftract_free()`; using `free()` directly is undefined behavior because the Rust allocator may differ from the C runtime allocator
- Thread safety: the library MUST be reentrant and thread-safe; achieve this by avoiding global mutable state (or guarding it with Mutex) and using `thread_local!` for last-error storage
- Error handling: C has no exceptions; errors are signalled by returning NULL and the caller retrieves the message via `pdftract_last_error()` (thread-local)
- ABI versioning: `pdftract_abi_version()` returns a u32 (MAJOR << 16 | MINOR << 8 | PATCH) so consumers can verify the loaded library matches their compiled header
- The cdylib MUST NOT pull in glibc-only deps that break musl static linking; verify with `ldd libpdftract.so` (musl build should show only ld-musl)
- cbindgen is invoked at build time via a build script (`build.rs`); the regenerated header is committed to git for downstream consumers who do not run cbindgen
- The C-FFI SDK is hand-maintained and is NOT a generator target (per plan: "The C/libpdftract binding is hand-maintained (cbindgen output + a cdylib Cargo target)")
- Multi-platform distribution: 5 triples × 1 (no feature variants for the FFI SDK) = 5 archives; Windows `.dll` + Linux `.so` + macOS `.dylib`
- Conformance runner: `tests/conformance.c` is a small standalone executable that exercises the C ABI directly; build with the system C compiler against the freshly-built libpdftract

## Acceptance criteria

- The fourth workspace member `pdftract-libpdftract` exists with cdylib + staticlib targets
- `cargo build -p pdftract-libpdftract --release` produces `libpdftract.so` (and `.dylib`/`.dll` on respective hosts)
- `crates/pdftract-libpdftract/include/pdftract.h` exists and is regenerated by build
- A trivial C program linking against `-lpdftract -I.../include` and calling `pdftract_extract_text` succeeds
- The library is thread-safe (verified by running `tests/conformance.c` with `-fsanitize=thread`)
- All 9 contract methods exposed as `pdftract_*` C functions
- `pdftract_free()` correctly frees strings without leaks (verified with valgrind)
- A Homebrew formula PR opens automatically against jedarden/homebrew-tap on release
- A vcpkg port PR template exists for manual submission to microsoft/vcpkg

## References

- Plan section: SDK Architecture / The Ten SDKs, line 3477 (C/C++ native FFI via libpdftract cdylib + cbindgen header + extern "C" API + reentrant + thread-safe)
- Plan section: SDK Architecture / Per-SDK Release Channels, line 3574 (GitHub Release + Homebrew formula + vcpkg port)
- Plan section: SDK Architecture / Code Generation, line 3553 (C binding hand-maintained)
- cbindgen docs: https://github.com/mozilla/cbindgen
- Sibling: pdftract-libpdftract-build Argo workflow (next bead)

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement pdftract serve --port PORT. Endpoints POST /extract (JSON), POST /extract/text (text/plain), POST /extract/stream (NDJSON), GET /health. Multipart/form-data uploads with optional form-field options. Concurrent request handling via axum + tokio; rayon for within-document parallelism; rayon-to-tokio bridge via spawn_blocking. Custom RequestBodyLimit JSON rejection. No built-in auth (per plan: deploy behind reverse proxy).

## Why this matters

HTTP serve mode makes pdftract usable as a microservice. The endpoints map directly onto the 3 output modes (full JSON, plain text, streaming NDJSON). Concurrency model is non-trivial: tokio handles per-request concurrency; rayon handles per-document page parallelism; spawn_blocking bridges the async/sync boundary. Getting this wrong wastes CPU or deadlocks.

## Implementation guidance

- Crate: axum, tokio, tower-http, multer (multipart parsing)
- Feature flag: serve (adds ~2 MB binary; axum + tokio not in default build)
- Pre-built release pdftract:serve Docker image is compiled with --features ocr,serve
- Endpoint handlers:
  - POST /extract -> multipart -> ExtractionOptions -> spawn_blocking(extract) -> JSON Response
  - POST /extract/text -> spawn_blocking(extract_text) -> text/plain Response
  - POST /extract/stream -> NDJSON stream Response via futures::stream::unfold + rayon producer
  - GET /health -> {"status":"ok","version":"x.y.z"} immediately
- Multipart parsing via multer; required file field "file"; optional fields map to ExtractionOptions kwargs (ocr, ocr_language, etc.)
- Request size limit: default 256 MB, configurable via --max-upload-mb
- RequestBodyLimit custom JSON rejection: convert tower-http default text/plain 413 to {"error":"REQUEST_TOO_LARGE","message":"..."}
- Error JSON body shape: {"error":"CODE","message":"..."}
- Error statuses: 400 (bad request), 413 (too large), 422 (extraction error), 500 (internal)

## Critical considerations

- NO BUILT-IN AUTH per plan (line 2138); deploy behind reverse proxy (nginx, Traefik) with auth
- NO file-path parameters in serve mode — PDF is always multipart upload (eliminates path traversal risk)
- rayon thread pool shared across all requests; per-request spawn_blocking bridges async-to-sync
- Streaming endpoint /extract/stream uses chunked Transfer-Encoding via axum::body::Body::from_stream
- 8 concurrent requests must succeed (critical test); /health 200 OK during load
- /extract/stream Content-Type: application/x-ndjson
- ExtractionOptions form-field defaults match CLI defaults

## Acceptance criteria

- All Phase 6.4 child task beads closed
- curl -F file=@test.pdf http://localhost:8080/extract -> valid JSON response (critical test)
- File over size limit -> HTTP 413 with custom JSON body
- 8 concurrent requests via curl -P 8 succeed
- /health 200 OK even during load
- pdftract serve --features serve compiles; without --features serve the subcommand is absent

## References

- Plan section: Phase 6.4 (lines 2095-2147)
- Security constraints (lines 2136-2139)
- INV-11 binary size (serve adds ~2 MB)

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the byte scanner that begins immediately after the `ID<ws>` token and ends at the EI delimiter. EI is recognized as the byte sequence `0x45 0x49` (capital E, capital I) preceded by a whitespace byte (0x20, 0x09, 0x0A, 0x0D, 0x0C). Returns the raw image bytes (excluding the preceding whitespace and the EI itself) and advances the cursor past EI.

## Why this matters

This is the ONLY place in PDF content stream parsing where the parser deals with raw, non-token-structured bytes that may contain arbitrary byte sequences including 0x45 0x49. The whitespace-preceded rule is the discriminator — without it, naive `find(b"EI")` corrupts the parser state on any image containing those bytes.

## Implementation guidance

- Cursor starts immediately after ID + 1 whitespace byte.
- Scan forward looking for byte sequence `[ws_byte, 0x45, 0x49]` where ws_byte is any of {0x20, 0x09, 0x0A, 0x0D, 0x0C}.
- Also accept end-of-stream as EI delimiter (some malformed PDFs omit EI; bound the image to the rest of the content stream).
- Return `(image_bytes: &[u8], bytes_consumed: usize)` where image_bytes excludes the preceding whitespace and EI; bytes_consumed includes everything from ID end to EI end.
- Performance: this is a tight inner loop; can be SIMD-accelerated with memchr crate for the 'E' byte then verify EI sequence and preceding whitespace.

## Critical considerations

- INV: EI must be preceded by whitespace per spec sec 8.9.7. A bare 0x45 0x49 in image data IS NOT a terminator.
- Image data may contain the pattern `<ws>EI` SPURIOUSLY (e.g., a JBIG2 stream might have such bytes); this is RARE but possible. Acceptable solution: trust the spec's filter+dimensions-determine-length convention OR adopt the whitespace-EI heuristic and accept that malformed images may cause early termination. The plan picks the whitespace heuristic; document as a known limitation.
- For maximum safety, the parser could use the InlineImageHeader's width/height/colorspace/bpc to COMPUTE the expected byte length and skip exactly that many bytes; this is more reliable. v0.1.0 uses the whitespace-EI heuristic for simplicity; track as ADR.
- Empty image (BI ... ID EI immediately): valid; return empty slice.

## Acceptance criteria

- Image `ABCD<ws>EI` returns image_bytes "ABCD".
- Image `ABCDEI<ws>EI` (containing "EI" without preceding whitespace inside) returns image_bytes "ABCDEI" (the inner EI is NOT a terminator because not preceded by ws).
- Image at end-of-stream without EI: returns the remaining bytes, emits INLINE_IMAGE_NO_EI diagnostic.
- Subsequent text operators after EI parse correctly (the EI consumed exactly; cursor at next token).

## References

- Plan section: Phase 3.5 Parsing (line 1596)
- Critical tests: lines 1599-1600

issue.description:
## Scope

Define the public enum `ConfidenceSource { Native, Heuristic, Ocr }` and the mapping function `fn map_confidence_source(unicode_source: UnicodeSource, corrected_in_4_7: bool) -> ConfidenceSource`. The mapping per plan spec:
- `to_unicode` or `agl` -> Native
- `fingerprint` -> Native
- `shape_match` -> Heuristic
- `unknown` (U+FFFD) -> Heuristic
- OCR path (Phase 5.4) -> Ocr
- Phase 4.7 correction applied -> Heuristic (overrides Native)

## Why this matters

ConfidenceSource is the OUTPUT-SCHEMA-EXPOSED confidence categorization that downstream consumers use to filter/highlight low-confidence text. The plan's mapping is a deliberate simplification of the 6-variant UnicodeSource down to 3 categories suitable for non-expert consumers: Native = "extracted directly from PDF", Heuristic = "guessed via algorithm", Ocr = "rasterized and recognized".

## Implementation guidance

- Enum:
  ```rust
  pub enum ConfidenceSource {
      Native,     // serializes as "native"
      Heuristic,  // serializes as "heuristic"
      Ocr,        // serializes as "ocr"
  }
  ```
- Serde derives with rename_all = "lowercase" (or explicit per-variant rename).
- Mapping function lives in `pdftract-core::layout::span`:
  ```rust
  pub fn map_confidence_source(us: UnicodeSource, corrected: bool) -> ConfidenceSource {
      if corrected { return ConfidenceSource::Heuristic; }
      match us {
          UnicodeSource::ToUnicode | UnicodeSource::Agl | UnicodeSource::Fingerprint => ConfidenceSource::Native,
          UnicodeSource::ShapeMatch | UnicodeSource::Unknown => ConfidenceSource::Heuristic,
          UnicodeSource::Ocr => ConfidenceSource::Ocr,
      }
  }
  ```
- The `corrected` parameter: true if any Phase 4.7 correction (ligature repair, hyphenation repair, mojibake detection) was applied to this span.

## Critical considerations

- INV: the mapping is LOSSY (6 -> 3 collapse); the full UnicodeSource is retained on each Glyph for diagnostic use, but the Span carries only the collapsed ConfidenceSource.
- A span built from glyphs with MIXED UnicodeSource: use the WORST-confidence (lowest f32) source mapping. Span.confidence is min; Span.confidence_source is the mapped source of the worst glyph (or Heuristic if any 4.7 correction applied).
- INV: Phase 4.7 correction ALWAYS overrides upward (Native -> Heuristic) — never downward (Ocr -> Heuristic).
- JSON serialization uses lowercase strings ("native", "heuristic", "ocr").

## Acceptance criteria

- Single-glyph span from to_unicode source: confidence_source == Native.
- Single-glyph span from shape_match source: confidence_source == Heuristic.
- Mixed-glyph span (agl + shape_match): confidence_source == Heuristic (worst).
- 4.7 ligature repair applied to all-agl span: confidence_source == Heuristic (correction overrides).
- OCR-produced span: confidence_source == Ocr.
- JSON serialization: lowercase strings.

## References

- Plan section: Phase 4.1 ConfidenceSource enum + mapping (lines 1638-1646)

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the image-source dispatch policy that selects the binarization algorithm per page based on the PDF filter chain (from Phase 1.5 filter inventory):

- DCTDecode (JPEG, typical physical scan) → Sauvola binarization
- FlateDecode (lossless, typical digital origin) → Otsu binarization
- JBIG2Decode → skip binarization (already bitonal)

Module: crates/pdftract-core/src/ocr/preprocessing/dispatch.rs.

## Why this matters

Sauvola is slower but adapts to local lighting (good for scans where one corner is darker than another); Otsu is faster but assumes globally consistent illumination (good for digitally-rendered images). Picking the wrong algorithm produces worse binarization, which produces worse OCR results.

JBIG2 is already binary; binarizing it again would be wasteful and possibly destructive (JBIG2 compression is lossless for bitonal but lossy in subtle ways).

## Implementation guidance

- ImageSource enum (set by 5.3 coordinator from Phase 1.5 filter inventory):
  ```rust
  pub enum ImageSource { PhysicalScan, DigitalOrigin, Jbig2 }
  ```
- Dispatcher function:
  ```rust
  pub fn select_binarizer(src: ImageSource) -> BinarizerKind {
      match src {
          ImageSource::PhysicalScan => BinarizerKind::Sauvola,
          ImageSource::DigitalOrigin => BinarizerKind::Otsu,
          ImageSource::Jbig2 => BinarizerKind::Skip,
      }
  }
  ```
- ImageSource is determined from the filter chain on the image XObject (Phase 1.5):
  - First filter == DCTDecode → PhysicalScan
  - First filter == FlateDecode → DigitalOrigin
  - First filter == JBIG2Decode → Jbig2
  - Other (mixed, exotic) → default to PhysicalScan (conservative; Sauvola is safer for unknown sources)
- Wire into the OCR preprocessing pipeline coordinator (sibling 5.3 bead)

## Critical considerations

- The dispatch is per-image (per Phase 1.5 image XObject), not per-page; a single page may contain multiple images each with different filter chains
- BinarizerKind::Skip means: no binarization step, but contrast normalization (sibling) still runs (unless image is JBIG2, in which case skip both)
- Unknown filter chains default to PhysicalScan to avoid wrongly skipping a recoverable image
- The dispatch decision is logged at TRACE level for debugging OCR quality regressions

## Acceptance criteria

- DCTDecode image → select_binarizer returns Sauvola
- FlateDecode image → Otsu
- JBIG2Decode image → Skip
- Unknown filter chain → PhysicalScan (default)
- Dispatcher is pure (no I/O); easy to unit-test exhaustively
- Wired into the 5.3 preprocessing coordinator

## References

- Plan section: Phase 5.3.2
- Phase 1.5 (filter chain inventory)
- Phase 5.3.3 (Sauvola/Otsu impls; consumed by this dispatcher)
- Coordinator: pdftract-2s0c (parent)
- Sibling: contrast normalization
Labels: dispatch, phase-5, preprocessing

issue.description:
## Scope

Document and enforce the serve-mode security constraints: NO built-in auth (deploy behind reverse proxy); NO file-path parameters (eliminates path traversal); decompression limits surfaced via max_decompress_gb form field + --max-decompress-gb CLI flag; request size limit via --max-upload-mb (default 256 MB). Provide a sample nginx + Traefik config in docs/operations/.

## Why this matters

Without auth, an unprotected pdftract serve on a public port is an open door for resource exhaustion or extraction-as-a-service abuse. The plan is explicit (line 2138) that auth is out of scope; the contract is "deploy behind a proxy". Documenting this clearly + providing sample configs reduces misuse risk.

## Implementation guidance

- No auth middleware in axum router; document the design decision in module rustdoc
- serve --bind validation: WARN if --bind 0.0.0.0:... is used without a doctor-style auth warning printed at startup
- File-path safety: PDF is always received as multipart upload bytes; never accept a path parameter (server never reads from server filesystem on behalf of request)
- max_decompress_gb form field maps to ExtractionOptions.max_decompress_bytes (multiply by 1<<30)
- --max-decompress-gb CLI flag sets the default for the server lifetime; per-request form field overrides
- --max-upload-mb default 256; uses tower-http RequestBodyLimit
- Sample configs:
  - docs/operations/serve-nginx-example.conf (auth_basic + proxy_pass localhost:8080; allowlisted path)
  - docs/operations/serve-traefik-example.yaml (BasicAuth middleware + service backend)
- Update CLI help text to call out the security model

## Critical considerations

- Startup banner: "pdftract serve is starting. NO BUILT-IN AUTH. Deploy behind a reverse proxy for production."
- Path parameter rejection is by design: there is no endpoint that accepts a server-local path; all PDFs come in via multipart
- --max-upload-mb cap-of-cap: hard cap at 4 GiB to prevent integer overflow
- Decompression limit defense against zip-bomb PDFs; documented in 6.4 critical-tests
- Sample configs in docs/operations/ MUST be in the secret-protection allowlist (already covered in config)

## Acceptance criteria

- Startup banner printed clearly on serve start
- Attempted file-path parameter (e.g. GET /extract?path=/etc/passwd) returns 404 (no such endpoint)
- Decompression limit enforced: zip-bomb fixture rejected with code DECOMPRESSION_LIMIT
- Sample configs committed and validated (parseable by their respective tools)
- CLI help reflects the security model

## References

- Security Hardening epic (pdftract-bgj)

issue.description:
## Scope

Curate the open-licensed font corpus from which the shape DB is generated. Provide a `scripts/fetch-shape-corpus.sh` that downloads a curated list of font families from Google Fonts and SIL Open Font License sources, places them in `build/shape-corpus/`, and copies each font's LICENSE text into `build/font-licenses/`. The list of families is committed as `build/shape-corpus-manifest.txt`.

## Why this matters

Without a documented, reproducible corpus, the shape DB cannot be regenerated by anyone but the original author, and the project violates the licensing terms of bundled font shape data. Open-licensed corpus selection IS the source-of-truth for what glyphs the DB can recognize — selecting only Latin fonts means the DB never matches Greek glyphs.

## Implementation guidance

- Manifest format: one font family per line, `family_name url license_short_id`. Example:
  ```
  Liberation Sans https://github.com/liberationfonts/liberation-fonts OFL-1.1
  DejaVu Sans https://github.com/dejavu-fonts/dejavu-fonts SIL-OFL-1.0
  Noto Sans https://github.com/notofonts/notofonts.github.io OFL-1.1
  Source Code Pro https://github.com/adobe-fonts/source-code-pro SIL-OFL-1.1
  ```
- Coverage targets: Latin basic + extended (Liberation Sans, DejaVu Sans, Noto Sans), monospace (Source Code Pro, JetBrains Mono), Greek/Cyrillic (DejaVu Sans, Noto Sans), Symbols (Noto Sans Symbols, STIX Math), Math (STIX Two Math, Latin Modern Math).
- Script: bash with `curl` + `unzip`. Idempotent: skip download if file already present.
- License copying: for each font, look for LICENSE.txt or OFL.txt in the package; copy verbatim to `build/font-licenses/<family>.txt`.
- Commit a list of which Unicode blocks the corpus covers (Latin Basic, Latin-1, Latin Extended A/B, Greek, Cyrillic, General Punctuation, Mathematical Operators, Arrows, etc.).

## Critical considerations

- DO NOT bundle the source font files in git (large binary diff churn). The script downloads on-demand.
- DO commit the LICENSE attribution files even if the fonts themselves are not committed — they document compliance.
- Coverage gaps: if the corpus does not include a Unicode block, L4 recognition for that block will always fail. Track coverage gaps as known limitations.
- License compatibility: OFL allows redistribution of the SHAPE DATA (it's a derivative work of the font outlines); document this analysis in `build/font-licenses/COMPLIANCE.md`.

## Acceptance criteria

- `bash scripts/fetch-shape-corpus.sh` downloads all manifest entries to build/shape-corpus/.
- LICENSE files for each font present in build/font-licenses/.
- `cargo xtask gen-shape-db --fonts build/shape-corpus/` produces a glyph-shapes.json with > 4500 entries.
- COMPLIANCE.md documents the OFL derivative-work analysis.
- Re-running the script is idempotent (no duplicate downloads).

## References

- Plan section: Phase 2.5 Source paragraph (line 1428)

Invalid UTF-8 handled gracefully with U+FFFD substitution. Empty/whitespace-only words skipped. Default confidence 50% when x_wconf missing. issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the HOCR XML parser. Input: HOCR string from TessBaseAPI::get_hocr_text. Output: Vec<HocrWord> where HocrWord = { text: String, bbox_px: [u32; 4], confidence_0_100: u8 }. Uses quick-xml streaming reader (no DOM allocation). Each word becomes one Span downstream in 5.4.4.

## Why this matters

HOCR is Tesseract's only output format that exposes per-word bbox AND per-word confidence. The Span model requires both (INV-7 confidence_source on every Span; bbox always present). The parser also handles HOCR's quirks (multiple title attributes, optional language attributes, escape sequences) deterministically.

## Implementation guidance

- Crate: quick-xml (event-driven, no allocation)
- Walk events; track depth and class attribute
- When entering span with class="ocrx_word": capture text + title attribute
- Parse title attribute: "bbox <x0> <y0> <x1> <y1>; x_wconf <conf>" with regex or manual split
- Each ocrx_word -> HocrWord struct
- Skip ocr_line and ocr_carea (paragraph) levels for now; bbox merging is at the line/paragraph level done in Phase 4.2/4.3, not here
- Multiple-word elements within a single ocrx_word (rare) are flattened with space joins

## Critical considerations

- quick-xml events use Cow<[u8]>; convert text content via str::from_utf8 with error handling (Tesseract sometimes emits invalid UTF-8 in OCR results — wrap in U+FFFD)
- title attribute parsing must tolerate extra fields (e.g. "x_size 12", "x_descenders 3") — parse robustly, ignore unknown
- HOCR coordinate system: top-left origin, pixel units, integer values
- Empty ocrx_word (whitespace-only text) -> skip
- Reproducibility: traverse order must match HOCR document order

## Acceptance criteria

- Parser handles standard Tesseract 5.x HOCR output (capture sample fixture, parse, expect known word list)
- Invalid UTF-8 in OCR result handled gracefully (substituted with U+FFFD, no panic)
- Confidence values 0-100 parsed correctly
- Bbox coordinates parsed as integers (no precision loss)
- 100-page HOCR (~10k words) parses in < 50 ms (microbench)

## References

- Plan section: Phase 5.4 HOCR parsing (lines 1898-1900)
- Tesseract HOCR format docs (https://kba.github.io/hocr-spec)
- quick-xml crate docs

## Scope

Implement pdftract validate FILE.json [--schema PATH] subcommand. Loads JSON, validates against schema, prints errors with JSON paths, exits 1 on failure.

Module: crates/pdftract-cli/src/validate.rs.

## Why this matters

The subcommand lets users validate their own pdftract-output JSON files (or third-party pdftract-compatible outputs) against the schema without running an extraction. Useful for: validating cached results, validating MCP-tool responses captured to disk, validating profile-extracted outputs for testing.

## Implementation guidance

- CLI:
  ```
  pdftract validate FILE.json [--schema PATH]
  ```
- Default --schema is the bundled docs/schema/v1.0/pdftract.schema.json (via include_str!)
- --schema PATH overrides for testing against custom schemas
- FILE may be \"-\" for stdin
- Output: list of validation errors, each line: <json_path> <error_message>
- Exit 0 on valid, 1 on invalid
- Use jsonschema crate (same as test suite sibling)

- Stdin support: FILE = - reads JSON from stdin; useful for piping (e.g. pdftract extract --json /dev/stdout file.pdf | pdftract validate -)
- Pretty-print errors with the JSON path (e.g. /pages/0/spans/3/text instead of /pages.0.spans.3.text)
- Multiple errors: print all; do not stop at the first
- Quiet mode (-q): only exit code; suppress error output (useful for shell pipelines)

- pdftract validate valid.json → exit 0; no output
- pdftract validate invalid.json → exit 1; per-error line on stdout
- pdftract validate - reads from stdin

issue.description:
## Scope

Lex the numeric literal token types from a byte slice:

- `Integer(i64)` — optional `+` / `-` followed by one or more decimal digits
- `Real(f64)` — optional `+` / `-` followed by a decimal-point-containing number (`3.14`, `-.5`, `42.`, `.001`)

Tokens are distinguished by the presence of a `.` character. Implementation produces both as a single state machine that decides Integer vs Real on the first `.` seen.

## Implementation guidance

- Greedy scan: consume `+`/`-` if present (max one), then digits, then optional `.` + more digits
- If a `.` is encountered: token is Real, parse via `f64::from_str` on a `&str` borrowed from the byte slice (PDF numbers are ASCII-only by spec, so unsafe-utf8-conversion is safe)
- If no `.`: token is Integer, parse via `i64::from_str`
- On parse failure (e.g. overflow): emit `STRUCT_INTEGER_OVERFLOW` or `STRUCT_REAL_INVALID`, return `Token::Integer(0)` or `Token::Real(0.0)` with diagnostic
- Reject malformed input: `--5`, `1.2.3`, `1e5` (PDF does NOT support scientific notation per spec 7.3.3), trailing junk
- Boundary detection: stop at whitespace or delimiter; do not consume the delimiter

## Critical considerations

- PDF spec 7.3.3 says real numbers MAY exceed f64 precision but in practice every producer stays within ~10 significant digits. Do not attempt arbitrary-precision; f64 is sufficient
- Integers exceeding `i64::MAX` (rare; typically large /Length values) clamp to `i64::MAX` with `STRUCT_INTEGER_OVERFLOW` diagnostic. Do NOT panic
- Per spec, `-.5` is valid (just `.5` with a leading minus). The state machine must accept "sign then dot then digits"
- `42.` (digits then dot, no fractional part) is valid Real per spec; parse as 42.0
- A bare `+` or `-` with no following digits is NOT a numeric token; emit `STRUCT_INVALID_NUMBER` and return Token::Integer(0)
- PDF spec specifically forbids `e`/`E` scientific notation; if encountered after digits, terminate the number at the `e` boundary (the `e` becomes start of next token, e.g. a name `/e5`)
- Hex digits like `0xFF` are NOT PDF numeric literals; the `x` terminates the number at position 1

## Acceptance criteria

- Critical tests pass (see plan and below):
  - `123` -> `Integer(123)`
  - `-7` -> `Integer(-7)`
  - `3.14` -> `Real(3.14)`
  - `-.5` -> `Real(-0.5)`
  - `42.` -> `Real(42.0)`
  - `.001` -> `Real(0.001)`
  - `+0` -> `Integer(0)`
  - `1e5` -> `Integer(1)` followed by `Name(b"e5")` or whatever comes next (no scientific notation)
  - `99999999999999999999` (overflow) -> `Integer(i64::MAX)` with `STRUCT_INTEGER_OVERFLOW`
  - `--5` -> diagnostic `STRUCT_INVALID_NUMBER`
- proptest property: random byte sequences starting with `+-0123456789.` never panic
- INV-8 maintained (no unwrap/expect)

## References

- Plan section: Phase 1.1 Lexer, line 1029-1031 (Integer, Real types)
- PDF spec 7.3.3 (Numeric Objects)
issue.title: Implement PDF numeric literal lexer (integer + real)

issue.close_reason: Implemented page /Rotate normalization for glyph bboxes. Added normalize_glyph_bboxes_by_rotation() function in content_stream.rs supporting 0/90/180/270 degree rotations with inverse transformation matrices. All 8 acceptance criteria tests pass. Commit: 606e162. Verification note: notes/pdftract-1jlpy.md
issue.description:
## Scope

After all glyph bboxes for a page are computed (post content-stream execution), inspect the page's `/Rotate` entry (0/90/180/270) and apply the inverse rotation to every glyph bbox so that downstream layout phases ALWAYS operate in an un-rotated coordinate system. The page's `width` and `height` in the output schema reflect the rotated dimensions (as the viewer sees them) — both bbox normalization AND output dimensions must be consistent.

## Why this matters

Without normalization, a page rotated 90 degrees has all glyphs at "rotated coordinates" (x and y swapped relative to viewer expectation), which breaks baseline clustering (y-axis assumed vertical), column detection (histogram of x0 assumed horizontal), and reading order (XY-cut assumes vertical = "next line"). Normalizing once after page execution lets the rest of Phase 4 ignore /Rotate entirely.

## Implementation guidance

- Determine page MediaBox + /Rotate from Phase 1.4 page dict.
- Construct inverse rotation matrix:
  - 0: identity (no-op)
  - 90: `[[0, 1, 0], [-1, 0, 0], [page_width, 0, 1]]` — counter-clockwise rotation; new origin at (page_width, 0) in original coords
  - 180: `[[-1, 0, 0], [0, -1, 0], [page_width, page_height, 1]]`
  - 270: `[[0, -1, 0], [1, 0, 0], [0, page_height, 1]]`
- For each glyph, transform all 4 corners of bbox by the matrix, then take the new min/max for the axis-aligned post-rotation bbox.
- Set output page.width / page.height to the rotated dimensions: for 90/270, swap MediaBox width/height; for 0/180, use as-is.
- Apply normalization ONCE per page, at the end of content stream execution, before passing the glyph list to Phase 4.

## Critical considerations

- INV: /Rotate is in degrees, must be a multiple of 90, otherwise emit `INVALID_ROTATE` diagnostic and treat as 0.
- /Rotate is inherited from page tree ancestors if not on the page itself — Phase 1.4 should resolve inheritance; if not, walk parents here.
- Glyph bboxes are min-corner / max-corner (axis-aligned); transforming all 4 corners and re-computing min/max is required (a rotated bbox is no longer axis-aligned).
- All bboxes within the page must use the same rotation — emit a diagnostic if /Rotate changes mid-page (impossible per spec but worth catching).
- INV: after normalization, glyph y-coordinates increase UPWARD (PDF convention) regardless of input rotation. Phase 4 baseline clustering assumes this.

## Acceptance criteria

- /Rotate 0: all bboxes unchanged.
- /Rotate 90: a glyph at original (10, 20) bbox [10,20,20,30] post-normalization is at [20, 10, 30, 20] (90 deg CCW rotation, swapping axes).
- /Rotate 180 + 270 verified similarly.
- Output page.width and page.height match the rotated dimensions (90/270 swap).
- /Rotate 45 (illegal) emits diagnostic and treats as 0.

## References

- Plan section: Phase 3.1 Page rotation paragraph (line 1497)
- Critical test: "Rotated page (Rotate=90): coordinate system rotated before applying algorithm" (line 1740, Phase 4.5)
issue.title: Page /Rotate normalization applied to glyph bboxes after page assembly

All acceptance criteria PASS: [(Hello)250(World)] TJ → W has is_word_boundary=true; [(kern)-10(ing)] TJ → no boundary; [(a)500(b)500(c)] TJ → both b and c carry is_word_boundary; [] TJ → no-op. 13 new tests added. Verification note at notes/pdftract-1kdzu.md
issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the `TJ array` operator: walk an array whose elements alternate strings and numeric kerning adjustments. For each string element, behave like Tj (emit glyphs, advance). For each numeric element, adjust text_matrix by `-n/1000 * font_size * Tz/100` (negative n = tighter, positive = looser). Large positive kerning values (> 0.2 * font_size) inject a SYNTHETIC word boundary on the next glyph (set is_word_boundary=true).

## Why this matters

TJ is how typeset PDFs (LaTeX, InDesign, Word) achieve kerning between letters within a word AND space-equivalent gaps between words. Without recognizing large positive kerns as word boundaries, every "kerned" PDF extracts as run-on text — pdfminer.six famously has this bug.

## Implementation guidance

- Operand: `Object::Array(Vec<Object>)`. Walk linearly.
- Numeric element: compute kern = `-n / 1000.0 * font_size * (horiz_scaling / 100.0)` in text-space units. Apply: `text_matrix = translate(kern, 0) * text_matrix`.
- Boundary trigger: if `n > 0` AND `n / 1000.0 * font_size > 0.2 * font_size` (i.e., `n > 200`), set a `pending_word_boundary` flag. The NEXT glyph emitted carries `is_word_boundary = true`.
- Actually re-read plan: "Large positive values (> 0.2 * font_size) inject word boundaries". The 0.2 * font_size is the THRESHOLD on the kerning amount in text space (not on n). Compute `kern_text_units = n / 1000.0 * font_size`; if `kern_text_units > 0.2 * font_size` (i.e., n > 200 in any font), set boundary. Negative kerns NEVER inject boundaries.
- String element: same as Tj — tokenize bytes, resolve, emit glyphs, advance.
- Non-string/non-numeric elements in TJ array: emit TJ_INVALID_ELEMENT diagnostic and skip.

## Critical considerations

- INV: TJ kern sign convention: NEGATIVE n moves position FORWARD (tighter to next glyph); POSITIVE n moves BACKWARD (which actually inserts space — paradoxical but correct per spec sec 9.4.3 Table 109).
  Wait — re-read spec: positive n = "displaces the next glyph by translation_x = -n/1000 * font_size" — negative translation = right-to-left displacement (visually left in PDF default coords). For LEFT-TO-RIGHT TEXT this means positive n inserts a gap. Verify with a test.
- The boundary threshold is the PLAN'S RULE; spec doesn't define one. Plan says `> 0.2 * font_size` of POSITIVE kern triggers a boundary — implement exactly.
- Boundary flag is consumed by the next glyph emitted; if no further glyph in this TJ, the flag carries to the next text-show operator (until consumed or until BT/ET resets state).
- Multiple boundary triggers in a row (rare): one flag, one boundary on next glyph.

## Acceptance criteria

- `[ (Hello) 250 (World) ] TJ` produces 10 glyphs; the W has is_word_boundary == true (kern of 250 > 200 threshold).
- `[ (kern) -10 (ing) ] TJ` produces 7 glyphs; the i has is_word_boundary == false (negative kern).
- `[ (A) 0 (B) ] TJ` no boundary (zero kern).
- Large kerns repeated: `[ (a) 500 (b) 500 (c) ] TJ` — both b and c carry is_word_boundary.
- Empty array `[] TJ` no-ops.

## References

- Plan section: Phase 3.2 TJ kerning paragraph (line 1536)
- Critical tests: TJ with large positive kerning, negative TJ kern (lines 1556-1557)
issue.title: TJ operator (array with kerning + large-positive synthetic spaces)

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the --header HEADER:VALUE repeatable CLI flag that adds custom HTTP headers to remote source requests (Phase 1.8 HttpRangeSource). Useful for adding API keys, custom auth tokens, or CORS-related headers when fetching PDFs from APIs.

Module: crates/pdftract-cli/src/cli.rs.

## Why this matters

Many institutional PDF hosts (research paper APIs, corporate documents in S3-fronted buckets, JWT-protected services) require custom HTTP headers that are not part of the standard URL syntax. Without --header, users would need to download PDFs separately before piping into pdftract, defeating the streaming-from-URL benefit.

## Implementation guidance

- CLI flag (clap derive):
  ```rust
  #[arg(long, value_name = \"HEADER:VALUE\", action = ArgAction::Append)]
  pub header: Vec<String>,
  ```
- ArgAction::Append makes the flag repeatable
- Parser: split each entry on first colon (NOT first space); whitespace around the colon is trimmed
- Validation: header name must match [A-Za-z0-9-_]+; value any printable bytes; reject CRLF in either part (HTTP header injection protection)
- Pass-through: when the input is an HTTPS URL, wire the headers into the HttpRangeSource constructor; for local files, ignore the headers silently
- Multi-header support: each --header adds to the request; duplicates allowed (some APIs use repeated headers)

## Critical considerations

- HTTP header injection protection: CRLF in either name or value rejected at CLI parse with a clear error (otherwise an attacker controlling part of the value could inject arbitrary HTTP)
- Header name normalization: HTTP headers are case-insensitive; preserve original case for outbound but match case-insensitively internally if comparing
- Standard headers (Host, Content-Length) MUST NOT be settable via --header; the HTTP layer manages those. Emit a clear error if user tries: \"Header 'Host' is managed automatically by pdftract\"
- Authorization header is allowed (this is the primary use case)
- The headers ONLY apply to the initial PDF fetch; if pdftract follows redirects, headers are preserved (matching ureq default behavior)
- Local-file ingest (non-HTTPS URL): --header is silently ignored (no warning); avoids noise when users have generic shell aliases

## Acceptance criteria

- pdftract extract --header X-API-Key:abc https://api.example.com/doc.pdf -> HttpRangeSource sees the X-API-Key header (verified in mock-server test)
- pdftract extract --header X-API-Key:abc --header X-Tenant:xyz -> both headers present
- pdftract extract --header Host:foo -> CLI parse error (managed header)
- pdftract extract --header X-Bad with CRLF in value -> CLI parse error
- pdftract extract --header NoColon -> CLI parse error (no colon)
- Local file extraction with --header -> no error, no header sent (silent ignore)

## References

- Plan section: Phase 1.8 + remote CLI cross-cut
- Coordinator: pdftract-25igv (parent)
- Sibling: --pages flag, URL credential parser
Labels: cli, http, phase-1, remote
issue.title: Header HEADER:VALUE repeatable CLI flag (passes through to HttpRangeSource)

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the 3 marked-content operators: `BMC /Tag` (begin marked content with tag only), `BDC /Tag <<props>>` or `BDC /Tag /PropName` (begin marked content with property dict or property-resource name; may carry /MCID), `EMC` (end marked content, pop top frame). Maintain a `marked_content_stack: Vec<MarkedContentFrame>` on the page executor.

## Why this matters

These operators define the tagging boundaries. Without correct stack management, MCID propagation to glyphs (sibling bead) breaks: outer tags leak into inner scopes or inner tags persist past their EMC.

## Implementation guidance

- `BMC name`: pop Name. Push `MarkedContentFrame { tag: name.clone(), mcid: None }`.
- `BDC name props`: pop Name + dict/name. Resolve props:
  - If props is a Name: look up in ResourceStack::lookup_properties(name); if found and contains /MCID, use it.
  - If props is an inline dict: read /MCID directly.
  - If neither: mcid = None.
  - Push `MarkedContentFrame { tag, mcid }`.
- `EMC`: pop top frame. If stack empty, emit `EMC_WITHOUT_BMC` diagnostic and no-op.
- The stack lives across BT/ET (marked content spans multiple text objects) but is bounded per page (reset between pages).
- Stack depth limit: 64 (mirror gstate); deeper push emits `MARKED_CONTENT_DEPTH_EXCEEDED`.

## Critical considerations

- INV: marked content stack is INDEPENDENT of graphics state stack — q/Q does NOT affect it. (Spec sec 14.5.)
- BDC properties name resolution requires ResourceStack::lookup_properties — page resources have a /Properties subdict for this.
- /MCID values are u32; the spec says "non-negative integer"; widely seen values are 0-10000.
- Some PDFs use /MCID multiple times in the same scope (illegal but seen) — the LAST one wins; emit `MCID_REDEFINED` diagnostic.
- INV: EMC pops exactly one frame; if the matching BMC/BDC had a depth-limit-discarded push, the EMC silently underflows (already discarded the frame).

## Acceptance criteria

- BMC /Span EMC: stack push then pop, balanced.
- BDC /Span <</MCID 42>> EMC: frame with mcid=Some(42) pushed then popped.
- BDC /P /MyProps EMC where /MyProps resolves to dict containing /MCID 7: frame mcid=Some(7).
- BDC /P /UnknownProps EMC: frame mcid=None, diagnostic for unknown prop name.
- EMC without BMC: EMC_WITHOUT_BMC diagnostic, no panic.
- 64 nested BMC: succeeds; 65th emits depth diagnostic and discards.

## References

- Plan section: Phase 3.4 Operators (lines 1582-1583)
issue.title: BMC / BDC / EMC operator parsers + marked-content stack

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the deterministic preprocessing pipeline that converts a raw page raster into a Tesseract-optimized image. Pipeline order: deskew (Hough via pixDeskew, skip < 0.3 deg) -> contrast normalization (histogram stretch) -> binarization (Sauvola for physical scans, Otsu for digital, skip for JBIG2) -> denoising (3x3 median, skip for JBIG2) -> border padding (10 px white).

## Why this matters

Tesseract's accuracy is highly sensitive to input quality. A 2-degree skew alone can raise WER by 3-5%. Uneven lighting (common in physical scans where the binding casts a shadow) causes Otsu thresholding to under-binarize the dark region; Sauvola adapts locally and handles it. Border padding is empirically known to improve Tesseract's edge-of-page recognition. The skip-for-JBIG2 path saves CPU on already-binary inputs.

## Implementation guidance

- Crates: leptonica-plumbing (pixDeskew, Sauvola), image (Otsu, median filter)
- Pipeline entry: fn preprocess(input: GrayImage, image_source: ImageSource) -> GrayImage where ImageSource is { PhysicalScan, DigitalOrigin, Jbig2 }
- Determine ImageSource from Phase 1.5 filter chain on the dominant image XObject (DCTDecode -> PhysicalScan; FlateDecode of a non-binary image -> DigitalOrigin; JBIG2Decode -> Jbig2)
- Skip rules: deskew always runs; contrast/binarize/denoise skipped for Jbig2; border padding always runs
- Each pipeline step is a standalone pub fn so they can be tested in isolation

## Critical considerations

- pixDeskew accepts grayscale input — no pre-binarization for skew detection (refer to plan line 1874)
- Sauvola window size and k parameter: use leptonica defaults (w=15, k=0.34); document if tuned
- Median filter is 3x3, not 5x5 — too aggressive denoising blurs character edges
- Border padding adds 10 px on each side; this is in pixel space, NOT pt space (apply post-render, pre-Tesseract)
- All preprocessing must be deterministic: same input -> bit-identical output (no thread races, no nondeterministic algorithms)
- pixDeskew handles input outside the [-15, +15] degree range by clamping; document this in module rustdoc

## Acceptance criteria

- All 5.3 child task beads closed
- 2-deg skewed scan fixture: deskewed to within 0.1 deg before OCR (critical test)
- Uneven-lighting fixture (shadow from binding): Sauvola produces clean binary; visual inspection passes
- Already-binary JBIG2 fixture: binarization + denoising steps skipped (verified via trace); no quality degradation
- End-to-end: preprocessing pipeline does NOT regress WER on the clean 300-DPI scan fixture

## References

- Plan section: Phase 5.3 (lines 1869-1885)
- leptonica-plumbing crate docs

## Scope

Author and ship the v1.0.0 built-in document profile bundle: nine YAML profiles (invoice, receipt, contract, scientific_paper, slide_deck, form, bank_statement, legal_filing, book_chapter) with at least 5 fixture documents and a regression test per profile, plus the labeled classifier corpus at tests/fixtures/classifier/ (200 documents: 50 invoices, 50 papers, 50 contracts, 50 misc), plus the provenance manifest at tests/fixtures/profiles/PROVENANCE.md and per-profile READMEs at profiles/builtin/<type>/README.md.

## Why this matters

Profiles are the user-facing surface that drives Phase 5.6 document classification and Phase 7.10 profile-aware extraction tuning, including type-specific field extraction (invoice_number, vendor, total, etc. emitted under metadata.profile_fields). The 200-document labeled corpus backs the Phase 5.6 acceptance criterion of >= 90% classification accuracy with per-class precision and recall >= 0.85 and macro-F1 >= 0.88. The 5+ fixtures per profile back the Phase 7.10 acceptance criterion of >= 90% per-field accuracy on the labeled invoice corpus and analogous gates on the other profiles. Without this bundle pdftract --auto is functionally inert.

## Implementation guidance

- Profiles live at profiles/builtin/<name>.yaml; bundled into the binary via include_str! when the profiles feature is enabled
- Each profile follows the YAML schema documented in plan lines 2894-2944: name, description, priority, match (any/all/none combinator tree), extraction (reading_order, table_detection, readability_threshold, include_invisible, etc.), fields (per-field extractors with regex/near/region/pick/parse)
- Match DSL primitives (line 2947-2961): text_contains, text_matches, heading_matches, has_currency_pattern, has_signature_field, structural.{page_count,has_table,has_form_field,has_math,heading_depth,font_diversity}
- Field DSL (line 2976-2987): localizers (near, region, pick) + extractors (regex, parse: decimal/date/int/bool)
- Built-in profile field sets per line 3037-3047 (e.g. invoice extracts invoice_number, vendor, customer, invoice_date, due_date, total, subtotal, tax, line_items)
- Fixtures live at tests/fixtures/profiles/<name>/{fixture-01.pdf,...} with a sibling expected-output.json carrying the canonical metadata.profile_fields per fixture
- Regression test at tests/profiles/test_<name>.rs runs each fixture through extract --profile <name>, asserts metadata.profile_fields exact match against expected-output.json
- Labeled classifier corpus at tests/fixtures/classifier/{invoice,scientific_paper,contract,misc}/*.pdf with a manifest at tests/fixtures/classifier/MANIFEST.tsv mapping path -> expected document_type
- Provenance manifest at tests/fixtures/profiles/PROVENANCE.md: every fixture source MUST be public-domain or open-licensed; no leaked confidential data; license/origin tracked per file
- Per-profile README at profiles/builtin/<name>/README.md describes match criteria summary, fields extracted, known limitations, sample input pointer

## Critical considerations

- Phase 7.10 acceptance: invoice classifier >= 90% per-field accuracy on 50-invoice labeled corpus (line 3054)
- Phase 5.6 acceptance: 200-doc labeled corpus, per-class precision + recall >= 0.85, macro-F1 >= 0.88 (lines 1973, 1988)
- PROVENANCE.md is a security/licensing gate — confidential or proprietary documents in fixtures would be a public disclosure incident (parallel to PROFILE_SECRETS_FORBIDDEN concern)
- Profile YAML loader (per Security epic) rejects top-level password/token/secret/api_key keys; built-in profiles MUST be free of these by design
- Each fixture should exercise at least one rare or adversarial structural feature alongside the common case (e.g. invoice with multi-currency, multi-page invoice, receipt with non-English merchant, contract with embedded signature image, scientific paper with multi-column layout and inline math, slide deck with mixed portrait/landscape pages)
- Classifier reproducibility: same document classified twice must produce identical output bytes (Phase 5.6 reproducibility criterion)
- form profile has no field extractor (only reading_order: line_dominant + surfaces all form_fields from Phase 7.4) — special-cased in the profile YAML

## Acceptance criteria

- All Profile Authoring child task beads closed

issue.description:
## Scope

Author the top-level `pdftract-release-cascade` WorkflowTemplate that runs on a milestone tag push and orchestrates the per-channel publish templates in correct dependency order. This is the single workflow a release engineer launches (or that the GitHub webhook -> Argo Events triggers automatically) to publish a full release.

## Why this matters

Without a cascade workflow, releases require manually launching 6 per-channel workflows in dependency order and remembering to wait for each. The cascade encapsulates the topology: it owns the inter-template dependencies (`pdftract-crates-publish` requires `pdftract-build-binaries` artifacts; `pdftract-docs-build` requires `pdftract-crates-publish` for docs.rs links; `pdftract-github-release` requires all of the above; per-SDK templates fan out after `pdftract-build-binaries`).

## Implementation guidance

- DAG topology:
  ```
  pdftract-build-binaries
  ├── pdftract-py-ci
  ├── pdftract-crates-publish
  │   └── pdftract-docs-build
  ├── pdftract-docker-build
  ├── pdftract-sdk-<lang>-publish  (×8 non-rust SDKs)
  └── pdftract-github-release   (joins on all above)
  ```
- The cascade is invoked by an Argo Events Sensor watching for a `vX.Y.Z` tag push on `jedarden/pdftract`
- Each per-channel step references the per-channel WorkflowTemplate via `workflowTemplateRef`
- Failure isolation: `continueOn: failed` at the per-channel level — a PyPI 5xx does NOT block crates.io or GHCR
- Final summary step posts a Slack/Discord notification (optional) with the published artifact list and any per-channel failures
- The cascade template lives at `k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/pdftract-release-cascade.yaml`
- The Argo Events resource (Sensor + EventSource for the GitHub webhook) lives at `k8s/iad-ci/argo-events/pdftract-tag-trigger.yaml`

## Critical considerations

- ADR-009: cascade orchestration is purely on iad-ci; the GitHub webhook hits Argo Events which signs and forwards the event
- The cascade is RE-RUNNABLE per partial failure: a release engineer can `argo retry` the cascade and only failed per-channel templates re-execute
- A failed `pdftract-github-release` is recoverable by re-running just that one template manually (`argo submit --from workflowtemplate/pdftract-github-release --parameter tag=vX.Y.Z`)
- The dependency on `pdftract-docs-build -> pdftract-crates-publish` is real because docs.rs links resolve only after crates.io publish; do not parallelise these
- The fan-out to per-SDK templates is wide (8+ templates) — set `parallelism: 10` on the cascade to avoid starving the cluster
- A Pre-Release Go/No-Go checklist (see Rollout and Rollback in the plan) gates the manual cascade launch; for automated webhook trigger, the check is enforced by branch protection on the tag-creation PR

## Acceptance criteria

- WorkflowTemplate file lands at the path above in jedarden/declarative-config
- The Argo Events Sensor lands at the path above and is wired to the pdftract repo's tag-push events
- A test cascade submission against a fresh tag executes all per-channel templates in correct order
- A simulated failure of `pdftract-py-ci` does NOT cancel the other per-channel templates
- A cascade re-run after a transient failure only re-executes failed per-channel templates
- The Slack/Discord notification (if configured) reports per-channel status

- Plan section: Pre-Release Go/No-Go (Rollout and Rollback)

issue.description:
## Scope

Define the PdfSource trait abstraction over PDF byte sources. The trait is the API surface that Phase 1.1-1.5 parsers consume: instead of taking &[u8], they take &dyn PdfSource. This is the foundational refactor that touches every parser module's signature.

## Why this matters

PdfSource is the abstraction boundary that lets local files (MmapSource, FileSource) and remote HTTPS PDFs (HttpRangeSource, Phase 1.8) share the same parser code. Without it, the parsers would have to be duplicated or templated, and remote sources would require copying entire PDFs into RAM. With it, the parser stack is source-agnostic.

## Implementation guidance

- Trait definition in crates/pdftract-core/src/source/mod.rs:
  ```rust
  use bytes::Bytes;
  use std::io::{self, Read, Seek};

  pub trait PdfSource: Read + Seek + Send + Sync {
      /// Total length of the source in bytes
      fn len(&self) -> u64;

      /// Read length bytes starting at offset. Returns Bytes for zero-copy slicing.
      /// Bounds: offset + length <= len(); else io::Error
      fn read_range(&self, offset: u64, length: usize) -> io::Result<Bytes>;

      /// Optional hint to the source to pre-fetch a range (no-op for local, override for HTTP)
      fn prefetch(&self, _offset: u64, _length: usize) {}
  }
  ```
- bytes = \"1\" crate for the Bytes type (zero-copy slicing)
- Send + Sync bounds are MANDATORY: rayon page-parallelism in Phase 3+ requires concurrent reads from multiple threads
- Read + Seek supertrait bounds let existing serde-style parsers consume PdfSource via standard adapters
- prefetch default impl is no-op; HttpRangeSource (Phase 1.8) overrides to issue speculative Range requests

## Critical considerations

- Bytes vs &[u8]: Bytes is reference-counted; cheaper to clone than Vec<u8>; supports zero-copy slicing (Bytes::slice)
- io::Result<Bytes> not Result<&[u8]>: a &[u8] would require the source to own the buffer, which conflicts with HttpRangeSource's cache eviction (cached pages can disappear under the consumer)
- Send + Sync rules out RefCell-based caches inside HttpRangeSource; use parking_lot::Mutex (already used by pdftract-core)
- The trait is intentionally object-safe (no generic methods, no Self in return types) so &dyn PdfSource works
- All Phase 1 parsers refactored to take &dyn PdfSource (or &impl PdfSource for monomorphization-friendly inner loops); this is a wide-blast-radius refactor

## Acceptance criteria

- Trait compiles in crates/pdftract-core/src/source/mod.rs
- &dyn PdfSource is object-safe (compiles)
- All Phase 1.1-1.5 parser modules refactored to consume PdfSource
- Trait re-exported from pdftract-core::source::PdfSource
- Documented with examples showing Read+Seek usage and direct read_range usage

## References

- Plan section: Phase 1.8 Remote Source Adapter (trait definition lines)
- Coordinator: pdftract-2cnmr (parent — PdfSource trait + 2 local impls bundle)
- Phase 1.1-1.5 (all parsers consume this trait)
Labels: phase-1, source, trait

## Scope

The Rust SDK is direct crate import (no IPC); `pdftract-core` IS the SDK. This bead delivers the supporting work: (a) an integration test rig under `crates/pdftract-core/tests/conformance.rs` that runs the shared conformance suite directly against the library, (b) docs.rs publishing configuration ensuring `cargo doc` succeeds with all default features and that docs.rs auto-builds documentation on crate publish, (c) examples directory `crates/pdftract-core/examples/` demonstrating the 9 contract methods.

## Why this matters

Rust users do not need a wrapping SDK; they import `pdftract-core` directly. But to honour the SDK contract from Rust, the `pdftract-core` public API MUST expose all 9 methods with the documented signatures and the conformance suite MUST pass against the library directly. docs.rs is the canonical Rust API reference; broken docs.rs builds are a documentation outage. The crates.io publishing pipeline (pdftract-crates-publish, separate bead under Release Engineering) handles publishing — this bead delivers the SDK-side requirements.

## Implementation guidance

- Integration test rig: `crates/pdftract-core/tests/conformance.rs`
  - Loads `tests/sdk-conformance/cases.json` from the workspace root
  - Iterates cases; for each, calls the appropriate `pdftract_core::extract`, `extract_text`, etc.
  - Uses the shared `compare_with_tolerances` helper (or delegates to `pdftract conformance compare` subcommand if implemented)
  - Reports per-case pass/fail; cargo test --test conformance exits non-zero on any failure
- Public API exposure: `pdftract-core` MUST export top-level functions matching the contract:
  - `pdftract_core::extract(source: impl AsSource, options: ExtractOptions) -> Result<Document, PdftractError>`
  - `pdftract_core::extract_text`, `extract_markdown`, `extract_stream`, `search`, `get_metadata`, `hash`, `classify`, `verify_receipt`

  - `rustdoc-args = ["--cfg", "docsrs"]`
  - `targets = ["x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu"]` (docs.rs builds Linux glibc only)
- Examples directory: `crates/pdftract-core/examples/`:
  - `extract.rs` (basic extract)
  - `ocr.rs` (OCR usage)
  - `search.rs` (regex search)
  - `stream.rs` (page-at-a-time streaming)

- README link to docs.rs: `[![docs.rs](https://docs.rs/pdftract-core/badge.svg)](https://docs.rs/pdftract-core)`

## Critical considerations

- The Rust SDK is the FIRST-CLASS reference implementation — every other SDK ultimately delegates to the binary that uses pdftract-core. Contract violations here propagate everywhere
- docs.rs builds use the `default` feature set + any explicitly listed features in `[package.metadata.docs.rs]`; OCR feature is excluded because Tesseract is not installable in the docs.rs build sandbox

issue.description:
## Scope

Use the PDF structure tree as the authoritative reading order for tagged PDFs. Walk /StructTreeRoot depth-first, map each StructElem to a block kind (P/H1-H6/Table/L/LI/Figure/Artifact via /RoleMap when non-standard), assign extracted MCID-tagged content sequences to their owning StructElem via the /ParentTree, and emit blocks in document order. Set reading_order_algorithm = "struct_tree" when the StructTree provides the ordering. Fall back to XY-cut if /MarkInfo /Suspects is true AND StructTree coverage on a given page is < 80% of extracted glyphs.

## Why this matters

Tagged PDFs are the only reliable source of authoritative reading order: heuristic detectors (4.5 XY-cut / docstrum / line_dominant) all approximate the document author's intent, while the StructTree is that intent. Microsoft Word, LaTeX with hyperref, and Adobe InDesign emit StructTree on every export; PDF/A-2a/3a/4a compliance requires it. Without 7.1, pdftract silently downgrades these documents to heuristic ordering, undermining the > 95% reading-order target on multi-column docs. The /ActualText override is the only correct way to extract ligatures, drop-caps, and decorative glyph swaps. /Artifact suppression is the only correct way to strip running headers/footers/page numbers from extracted body text.

## Implementation guidance

- Crates: none beyond Phase 1 PDF parser (catalog/structtree walking is pure object traversal)
- Walk algorithm: depth-first from /StructTreeRoot; at each StructElem, record element type (mapped via /RoleMap if non-standard), /ActualText, /Alt, /Lang (BCP-47)
- MCID-to-StructElem mapping: build via /ParentTree (PDF 1.7 14.7.4.4) - the ParentTree is keyed by structParents page numbers and maps MCID positions to StructElem refs
- Block-kind mapping: P -> paragraph, H/H1..H6 -> heading{level}, Table -> table, L -> list, LI -> list_item, Figure -> figure, Artifact -> suppressed (NOT emitted)
- Coverage check: count distinct MCIDs claimed by StructTree on each page; if < 80% of extracted glyphs on that page AND /MarkInfo /Suspects true, fall back to XY-cut for that page only (per-page granularity)
- reading_order_algorithm field: emit "struct_tree" when StructTree drives ordering; "xy_cut" if any page falls back

## Critical considerations

- /Suspects flag in /MarkInfo means the producing application has flagged this StructTree as unreliable - take it seriously
- /ActualText replaces the visible glyph text (e.g. ligature 'fi' -> ActualText 'fi'); apply BEFORE Unicode mapping
- /Alt is for /Figure only - alternative text for accessibility
- /RoleMap remaps producer-specific element types to standard ones; respect it
- /Artifact MCIDs are excluded from all output (headers/footers/page numbers/decorative rules)
- ParentTree resolution must NOT crash on malformed structParents - skip that page with diagnostic
- coverage threshold of 80% is the agreed cutoff; configurable via ExtractionOptions in future
- StructElem may have /K array containing kids (other StructElems) OR /MCR (MCID refs) OR raw integers (MCIDs) - all three shapes must be handled

## Acceptance criteria

- All Phase 7.1 child task beads closed
- Word-generated tagged PDF: heading levels correctly extracted (H1/H2 map to level 1/2) - critical test from plan
- Tagged PDF with /ActualText on a ligature: ActualText value used, not glyph-decoded text - critical test
- Tagged PDF with /Artifact marked content: artifact glyphs excluded from output - critical test
- PDF with Suspects true: falls back to XY-cut for low-coverage pages, reading_order_algorithm = "xy_cut" - critical test
- CI test fixtures: tagged-word.pdf, tagged-latex.pdf, tagged-actualtext-ligature.pdf, tagged-artifact-header.pdf, tagged-suspects-true.pdf

## References

- Plan section: 7.1 StructTree Exploitation (lines 2543-2564)

- Phase 4.5 reading_order algorithms (heuristic alternatives + reading_order_algorithm field)
- Phase 7.10 profile match predicate structural.has_table benefits from authoritative Table kind
- INV: stable taxonomy of block kinds (no new kinds without schema bump)

## Scope

Implement footnote emission in the Markdown sink. Each footnote_ref span gets a unique numeric ID assigned in document order; emits [^N] in body where the ref appears; emits [^N]: footnote text definitions at end of page (v1.0 decision; end-of-document is a future option).

Module: crates/pdftract-core/src/output/markdown/footnotes.rs.

## Why this matters

Footnotes are the highest-value cross-block annotation in scholarly and legal documents. Without footnote-style emission, footnote text either disappears from output or appears inline (breaks paragraph flow). CommonMark + GFM both support [^N]/[^N]: reference-style footnotes which render correctly in GitHub, GitLab, Obsidian, Notion.

## Implementation guidance

- During Phase 7 (footnote detection), each footnote_ref span carries a footnote_id
- During Markdown emission:
  - For each footnote_ref span: emit [^<footnote_id>]
  - At end of page (per v1.0 decision): emit [^<id>]: <footnote_text>\\n
  - Footnote IDs are unique within the document (use Phase 7 footnote_id directly, not per-page numbering)
- For documents without footnotes: this code path is a no-op
- Pretty formatting: blank line before the [^N]: definition block

## Critical considerations

- v1.0 emits footnote definitions at end of page; end-of-document is deferred (would require buffering all footnotes; tradeoff between proximity and flow)
- Footnote IDs must be stable: re-running extraction on the same PDF produces the same IDs (deterministic, in source order)
- CommonMark spec doesn't include footnotes; GFM (GitHub Flavored Markdown) does; document the dependency on GFM-compatible renderers
- Empty footnote text → emit [^N]: (empty) — placeholder rather than skip (so the reference is at least visible)

Implement detect_line_direction(line_text) -> LineDirection. Walk chars; count L (LTR) vs R/AL (RTL). Return: Ltr if ltr > rtl; Rtl if rtl > ltr; Mixed if tied or both zero.

issue.close_reason: Implemented q/Q stack with depth limit 64 and overflow diagnostics. Changed MAX_GSTATE_DEPTH from 32 to 64 per PDF spec. Added gstate_overflow_logged flag to emit overflow diagnostic only once per page. All acceptance criteria PASS: 64 nested q calls succeed; 64 q + 64 Q restores initial state; Q at depth 0 is no-op with underflow diagnostic; 1000 paired q/Q operations succeed; diagnostic emitted exactly once per page. Commit d3fc0de. Verification note at notes/pdftract-1os1.md.
issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the `q` (push) and `Q` (pop) operators driving a `Vec<GraphicsState>` save stack. Enforce the spec's 64-level depth limit: q at depth 64 emits a `GSTATE_STACK_OVERFLOW` diagnostic, discards the push, and returns Ok (safe failure, not a parse abort). Q at depth 0 emits `GSTATE_STACK_UNDERFLOW` and is a no-op.

## Why this matters

Every text operator implicitly reads the current state; nested forms / repeated transformations rely on q/Q to scope CTM and color changes. Without correct depth limit handling, malicious or malformed PDFs could exhaust memory; without underflow safety they could abort extraction.

## Implementation guidance

- Storage: `Vec<GraphicsState>` of length 0..=64. The CURRENT state is `vec.last()` (not stored separately) — q clones it onto the stack; Q pops.
- Wait — re-read: q is "Save the current graphics state on the stack" then continues to MODIFY a fresh state? No — per spec: q pushes a COPY of current state; current state pointer continues to point to the live top-of-stack. So implementation: `current: GraphicsState` plus `Vec<GraphicsState>` history. q: history.push(current.clone()), depth = history.len(); Q: current = history.pop().unwrap_or(current).
- Depth limit: `const MAX_GSTATE_DEPTH: usize = 64;` `if history.len() >= MAX_GSTATE_DEPTH { emit_diagnostic; return; }`.
- Both operators are O(1) except for the Clone — GraphicsState clones must be cheap (Arc<Font> is the only heap pointer).

## Critical considerations

- The depth limit applies to NESTED saves, not to total q operations across the stream — i.e., a stream with thousands of `q ... Q` pairs is fine if they don't NEST.
- Diagnostic must be emitted ONCE per page, not once per overflow — track a `gstate_overflow_logged: bool` on the executor.
- Q at depth 0 should NOT panic; many PDFs have a stray Q from a botched authoring tool.
- INV: q always followed by EVENTUAL Q (PDFs may be unbalanced — at end-of-stream just discard unpoped states).

issue.description:
## Scope

Detect Optional Content Group (OCG) marked content: BDC with /OC tag where the property dict has /OCG referencing an OCG dict. Look up the OCG's default state in the page-level /OCProperties /D /OFF list (Phase 1.4 catalog data). If the OCG is OFF by default, mark the corresponding marked-content frame as hidden; emitted glyphs inside receive `Glyph.is_hidden = true` (NEW field on Glyph, default false).

## Why this matters

Hidden layers in PDFs typically contain watermarks, draft annotations, commentary, or alternate-language overlays. Phase 4.6 plain-text output filters hidden glyphs by default; the `--include-hidden-layers` flag re-enables them. Without OCG tracking, watermarks and similar always extract.

## Implementation guidance

- Extend Glyph struct (Phase 3.2 sibling) with `pub is_hidden: bool` (default false). Bump struct size by 1 byte (effectively 8 with alignment).
- BDC handler: when tag == "OC" and props dict has /OCG (an indirect-ref to an OCG dict), look up OCG in pre-cached `default_off_ocgs: HashSet<ObjectId>` (built at page-load time from /OCProperties /D /OFF).
- If OCG is in the off-set, mark frame as `is_hidden = true`.
- emit_glyph sets Glyph.is_hidden = true if ANY frame in the marked-content stack is hidden (outer hidden propagates to inner).
- INV: hidden flag is OR'd through nested frames (outer hidden makes all descendants hidden).
- /OCProperties pre-processing happens at page load (Phase 1.4); pass the HashSet to Phase 3 executor.

## Critical considerations

- INV: this is a SOFT filter — glyphs are emitted with the flag; downstream chooses to keep or drop. Do NOT skip emission.
- /OCProperties may also contain /ON and /ORDER lists; for v0.1.0 only /OFF is honored (default-OFF detection).
- Some PDFs reference OCG by indirect ref via the inline dict; resolve to ObjectId.
- OCG support is OPTIONAL per spec; if /OCProperties absent, the off-set is empty (no glyphs marked hidden).
- Cycle-safe: OCG dict references are flat (no recursion), so no cycle concern.

## Acceptance criteria

- BDC /OC <</OCG 12 0 R>> EMC where OCG 12 is in default-OFF: glyphs inside have is_hidden = true.
- BDC /OC <</OCG 12 0 R>> EMC where OCG 12 is NOT in default-OFF: glyphs inside have is_hidden = false.
- Nested OCs, outer hidden: all inner glyphs hidden.
- No /OCProperties on document: no glyphs ever marked hidden.
- /OC BDC without /OCG (malformed): no effect, diagnostic emitted.

## References

- Plan section: Phase 3.4 OCG /OC tag suppression note (line 1579 epic spec)
issue.title: OCG /OC tag tracking + default-OFF detection via /OCProperties

All 6 acceptance criteria PASS: AC1 all-printable > 0.9, AC2 all-U+FFFD < 0.1, AC3 all-whitespace whitespace_score=0, AC4 low confidence scaled, AC5 non-English dict forced 1.0, AC6 ligature split lowers score. issue.description:
## Scope

Implement score_span_readability(span, document_lang) -> f32 in [0.0, 1.0]. Composite: 0.35 * printable_fraction + 0.30 * dict_coverage + 0.15 * whitespace_score + 0.10 * ligature_integrity + 0.10 * confidence_floor. Each signal returns [0.0, 1.0]; weighted sum is readability score. If document_lang is non-English: dict_coverage forced to 1.0 (disabled).

## Why this matters

Composite score is FINAL VERDICT per span — drives BrokenVector escalation, drops below-threshold spans, raises diagnostics. Wrong weights shift which spans get filtered. Plan weights calibrated against test corpus.

## Implementation guidance

- printable_fraction: non-U+FFFD non-control chars / total. > 0.95 good.
- dict_coverage: unicode-segmentation UAX#29 word boundary split; count in 20k phf::Set / total. > 0.60 good. DISABLED if non-English.
- whitespace_score: ratio = whitespace / total. If 0.05 <= ratio <= 0.40 -> 1.0; else 0.0 (binary).
- ligature_integrity: 0 split ligature patterns -> 1.0; else 0.0 (binary). POST-repair state.
- confidence_floor: min(1.0, span.confidence / 0.6). 0.6 confidence -> 1.0.
- Combine: weighted sum, clamp [0.0, 1.0].

## Critical considerations

- INV: weights sum 1.0; const READABILITY_WEIGHTS: [f32; 5] = [0.35, 0.30, 0.15, 0.10, 0.10].
- Word split: unicode-segmentation UAX #29 boundaries.
- Empty span: return 0.0.
- Performance: 1000 spans/page * 100 ns/lookup = 100 us, negligible.

## Acceptance criteria

- All-printable English high coverage: > 0.9.
- All-U+FFFD: < 0.1.
- All-whitespace: < 0.1 (whitespace binary fail).
- Single short low-confidence word: scaled by confidence_floor.
- Non-English doc: dict forced 1.0; score from other signals.
- Ligature-split span: integrity 0 lowers score.

## References

- Plan section: Phase 4.7 Readability scoring table (lines 1765-1773)
issue.title: Span readability composite scoring (5 weighted signals -> [0.0, 1.0])

Define the public ConfidenceSource enum with three variants: Native, Heuristic, Ocr. Serializes as lowercase strings (\"native\", \"heuristic\", \"ocr\") matching the 6.1 JSON schema.

ConfidenceSource is the OUTPUT-SCHEMA-EXPOSED confidence categorization: downstream consumers (dashboards, audit tools, RAG pipelines) filter or highlight low-confidence text using this 3-variant categorical signal. Locking the variant set early prevents schema churn across 6.1 schema versions.

All acceptance criteria PASS: depth limit (64), push/pop balance, underflow handling, MCID propagation, INV-8 no-panic verified.
issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the per-page marked-content stack as Vec<MarkedContentFrame> on the page executor. Bounded depth (64 frames); emits MARKED_CONTENT_DEPTH_EXCEEDED on overflow. Provides push/pop API used by the BMC/BDC/EMC operator parsers (sibling).

## Why this matters

The stack is the data structure underlying marked-content; it's what makes MCID propagation to glyphs work correctly. Bounded depth prevents pathological inputs (deeply-nested BMC without EMC) from OOM-ing.

## Implementation guidance

- Struct:
  ```rust
  pub struct MarkedContentFrame {
      pub tag: Name,
      pub mcid: Option<u32>,
  }

  pub struct MarkedContentStack {
      frames: Vec<MarkedContentFrame>,
  }

  impl MarkedContentStack {
      pub const MAX_DEPTH: usize = 64;
      pub fn new() -> Self { Self { frames: Vec::new() } }
      pub fn push_bmc(&mut self, tag: Name);
      pub fn push_bdc(&mut self, tag: Name, mcid: Option<u32>);
      pub fn pop_emc(&mut self) -> Result<MarkedContentFrame, MarkedContentError>;
      pub fn top(&self) -> Option<&MarkedContentFrame>;
      pub fn top_mcid(&self) -> Option<u32>;
      pub fn depth(&self) -> usize;
  }
  ```
- push_bmc / push_bdc enforce MAX_DEPTH: if depth >= MAX_DEPTH, emit MARKED_CONTENT_DEPTH_EXCEEDED diagnostic and return without pushing
- pop_emc returns Err(EmcUnderflow) when stack is empty; caller's operator parser converts to EMC_WITHOUT_BMC diagnostic
- top_mcid is the convenience used by glyph emission: returns the topmost frame's mcid (None if stack is empty or top frame has no MCID)
- Stack lives across BT/ET boundaries within a page; reset between pages

## Critical considerations

- MAX_DEPTH = 64 mirrors the gstate-stack depth limit (consistent attack-surface bound)
- Stack is independent of gstate stack (q/Q does NOT affect it); document with a code comment
- Don't auto-reset on overflow; just stop pushing. The pop_emc on overflow-pushes will still pop correctly because the discarded pushes never happened
- Some PDFs use /MCID multiple times in the same scope (illegal per spec but seen in the wild); the BDC parser's responsibility is to take the LAST value (sibling bead handles this); the stack just stores whatever it's given
- Per-page reset: page executor calls MarkedContentStack::new() at start of each page

## Acceptance criteria

- push_bmc 64 times → all push; 65th push emits MARKED_CONTENT_DEPTH_EXCEEDED and returns; depth is still 64
- push_bmc N then pop_emc N → empty stack
- pop_emc on empty stack → Err(EmcUnderflow); caller emits EMC_WITHOUT_BMC
- top_mcid returns Some(mcid) when top frame has Some(mcid); None when empty stack
- Unit tests cover push/pop balance, overflow, underflow
- INV-8 (no panic) verified on all stack operations

## References

- Plan section: Phase 3 marked-content stack
- PDF spec section 14.5 (Marked Content)
- Coordinator: pdftract-1l6wn (parent)
- Sibling: BMC/BDC/EMC operator parsers (consumer of this stack)
Labels: data-structure, parser, phase-3
issue.title: Marked-content stack (Vec<MarkedContentFrame> with 64-depth limit)
