issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the 10 MCP tools that the MCP server advertises via tools/list and dispatches on tools/call. Each tool wraps an existing pdftract surface (extraction, search, metadata, hashing, classification, etc.) with a typed argument schema (JSON Schema), structured error mapping (Rust errors → JSON-RPC error codes), and the per-invocation observability hook described in plan section 6.7.

Module: crates/pdftract-cli/src/mcp/tools/ with one file per tool plus a registry that produces the tools/list response.

## Why this matters

Agents discover what pdftract can do via tools/list; the catalog must expose every meaningful pdftract capability with arg schemas precise enough that the agent (and the human writing the agent prompt) can use the tool without reading source. A sparse or vague catalog forces agents to fall back on guessing args or making round-trips; a too-broad catalog (e.g. one mega-tool with 50 args) makes agent tool-selection unreliable.

Splitting extraction into extract / extract_text / extract_markdown reflects the three primary consumer shapes: full-document JSON for downstream processing, plain text for summarization/RAG, Markdown for human display. Specialized tools (get_metadata, hash, classify) are cheap pre-flight calls agents can make before deciding whether to spend the budget on a full extract.

## Tool catalog

| Tool | Description | Required args | Optional args |
|---|---|---|---|
| extract | Full extraction returning the document JSON | path (string) | pages (string e.g. \"1-5,7\"), ocr (bool), formats (string array; multi-output), auto_profile (bool), password (string), receipts (\"off\"|\"lite\"|\"svg\") |
| extract_text | Plain-text extraction | path | pages, ocr, password |
| extract_markdown | Markdown extraction | path | pages, ocr, anchors (bool, default false), password |
| search | Regex search across the file returning matches with page+bbox | path, pattern | case_insensitive, max_matches, password |
| get_metadata | Metadata + outline + fingerprint only (cheap; no full extraction) | path | password |
| get_table | Single table by page index and table index (Phase 7.2) | path, page, table_index | password |
| get_form_fields | AcroForm/XFA field values (Phase 7.4) | path | password |
| get_attachments | Embedded files (Phase 7.5) | path | include_data (bool — base64-encoded bytes when true) |
| hash | Compute structural fingerprint only (Phase 1.7) | path | password |
| classify | Run Phase 5.6 classifier only (no extraction) | path | — |

The path argument accepts local filesystem paths (relative to working dir) and https:// URLs (uses Phase 1.8 remote source adapter when the remote feature is enabled).

## Implementation guidance

- Tool registry: a HashMap<&'static str, Box<dyn Tool>> built at startup; tools/list iterates the registry producing { name, description, inputSchema } entries
- inputSchema for each tool is a JSON Schema fragment derived from the tool's argument struct via the schemars crate (already a dev dep — promote to runtime here under the mcp feature)
- Per-tool dispatch: deserialize args from JSON-RPC params (with -32602 on invalid shape), invoke the corresponding pdftract function, serialize result to JSON
- Error mapping:
  - PdftractError::InvalidPath → -32602 with PATH_INVALID code in data
  - PdftractError::Encryption → -32000 with PDF_ENCRYPTED code (use -32099..-32000 implementation-defined range for pdftract-specific errors)
  - PdftractError::Io → -32000 with IO_ERROR
  - Panic (caught at the tool boundary via std::panic::catch_unwind) → -32603 InternalError + log full backtrace to stderr
- Tools that haven't been implemented yet (get_table, get_form_fields, get_attachments are Phase 7) must still be advertised in the catalog but return -32000 with NOT_YET_IMPLEMENTED code; this lets agents see the full surface while degrading gracefully
- Observability: every tools/call invocation emits one structured stderr log line per plan section 6.7 line 2329: timestamp, tool_name, path (or its SHA-256 hash when --no-log-paths is set), duration_ms, response_size_bytes, error_code (null on success)

## Critical considerations

- Tool descriptions in the catalog must be concise (1-2 sentences) — agents truncate long descriptions when generating their tool-selection prompts
- The path argument accepts both local paths AND https:// URLs; the dispatch logic checks the scheme to route to MmapSource vs HttpRangeSource (Phase 1.8)
- formats array for extract enables multi-output: e.g. [\"json\", \"markdown\"] returns { json: ..., markdown: ... } in the response. Single-format requests return the bare extraction
- receipts arg (\"off\"|\"lite\"|\"svg\") wires into the Phase 6.8 receipts feature; pass through to ExtractionOptions
- The dispatcher must validate tool name against the registry BEFORE deserializing params; unknown tool name → -32601 MethodNotFound (mapped from JSON-RPC's tools/call dispatch)
- get_metadata is intentionally cheap (skips page-level parsing); the implementation must avoid touching content streams — only metadata dict + outline + fingerprint
- include_data on get_attachments materializes binary blobs into the JSON-RPC response (base64-encoded); document the size implications in the tool description
- Password handling: passwords arrive in plain JSON-RPC params over the wire. Reverse-proxy TLS + bearer-token auth are the protection; in the log line, never log the password value
- Path-traversal protection (sibling 6.7.6) wraps every local path arg before dispatch; this bead's dispatch logic calls into the protection layer for any path arg

## Acceptance criteria

- tools/list returns 10 entries with name, description, inputSchema fields
- Each tool's inputSchema validates against draft-07 JSON Schema (lint via jsonschema crate in tests)
- tools/call extract with a 100-page PDF on a tmpdir returns the same DocumentJson shape as pdftract extract --json --output /dev/stdout
- tools/call extract_text returns the same plain text as pdftract extract --text on the same input
- tools/call get_metadata on a 100-page PDF completes in <= 250 ms (cheap path)
- tools/call hash on a 100-page PDF completes in <= 100 ms (fingerprint-only path)
- tools/call get_table on a Phase 7-not-yet-implemented tool returns -32000 with NOT_YET_IMPLEMENTED data field
- tools/call with unknown tool name returns -32601 MethodNotFound
- tools/call extract on encrypted PDF without password returns -32000 with PDF_ENCRYPTED code
- Every tools/call invocation emits exactly one structured log line on stderr
- Plan section 6.7 critical test: \"Tool error on encrypted PDF: JSON-RPC error response with code -32000 and human-readable message\" passes

## References

- Plan section: Phase 6.7 MCP Server Mode (lines 2304-2330)
- MCP spec: tools: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/spec/server/tools
- JSON Schema draft-07 (used for inputSchema)
- Phase 1.7 fingerprint (hash tool)
- Phase 1.8 remote source adapter (https:// URLs)
- Phase 5.6 classifier (classify tool)
- Phase 6.8 receipts (receipts arg on extract)
- Phase 7.2/7.4/7.5 (get_table, get_form_fields, get_attachments — Phase 7 stubs)
- Sibling bead 6.7.6 (path-traversal protection wraps every path arg)
Labels: mcp, phase-6, tools

issue.description:
## Scope

Build the xref-resolver test corpus and the integration test runner:

1. **Curated fixtures** under `tests/xref/fixtures/`:
   - `well_formed_traditional.pdf` — single-revision PDF with traditional xref (5-10 objects, 1 page)
   - `well_formed_stream.pdf` — single-revision PDF with xref stream (PDF 1.5 file)
   - `hybrid_file.pdf` — traditional xref + /XRefStm; one obj overlap to test priority
   - `prev_chain_3_revisions.pdf` — 3 incremental revisions; object 5 modified each time
   - `linearized.pdf` — linearized 50-page PDF with /H hint stream
   - `truncated_after_xref.pdf` — file truncated at the start of xref (forces forward scan)
   - `startxref_off_by_one.pdf` — startxref offset wrong by 1 byte (forces forward scan)
   - `corrupt_xref_entry.pdf` — one xref entry has wrong offset; others valid
   - `circular_prev.pdf` — /Prev forms a cycle (A->B->A)
   - `deep_prev_chain.pdf` — 50 incremental revisions (tests depth limit at 32)

2. **Integration test runner** under `tests/xref/integration.rs`:
   - Walks fixtures, runs `resolve_xref()`, captures resulting XrefSection
   - Compares against sibling `.expected.json` golden file (object map + trailer dict)
   - `BLESS=1` rewrites goldens

3. **Diagnostic assertion helpers**:
   - `assert_diagnostic(diagnostics, code, byte_offset_range)` — checks that a specific diagnostic was emitted with offset in the expected range

## Why this matters

The xref resolver is THE most fragile parser layer because real-world PDFs are wildly inconsistent here. Without a rich fixture corpus, regressions go undetected. The fixtures span: well-formed (baseline), each strategy (1-4), each special case (incremental, linearized), and adversarial (cycle, deep chain).

## Implementation guidance

- Fixture generation: use qpdf, pdftk, and a custom Rust helper `tools/build-xref-fixture` to produce the variants
- The corrupt fixtures should be the SAME base document with surgical byte modifications:
  - truncated_after_xref.pdf: take well_formed_traditional.pdf, truncate at `byte_offset_of_xref - 1`
  - startxref_off_by_one.pdf: take well_formed_traditional.pdf, modify the startxref value by +1
  - corrupt_xref_entry.pdf: take well_formed_traditional.pdf, modify one entry's offset to be invalid
- The deep_prev_chain.pdf fixture: 50 successive `qpdf --add-attachment` commands to create 50 revisions; total file size ~5 MB
- Golden files: `.expected.json` per fixture, holding `{ entries: [...], trailer: {...}, diagnostics: [...] }`
- The test runner is in Rust because the golden comparison needs to handle PdfObject serialization (which is pdftract-specific)
- Property tests on the xref resolver (not just unit tests): random fixture mutations should not panic; add `tests/proptest/xref.rs`

## Critical considerations

issue.description:
## Scope

Extend `crates/pdftract-core/build.rs` to read `build/glyph-shapes.json` and emit two parallel `&'static` arrays sorted by pHash ascending: `SHAPE_TABLE: &'static [(u64, char)]` for hash -> char, and `FREQ_TABLE: &'static [(u64, u32)]` for hash -> frequency rank (same index as SHAPE_TABLE). Generated file written to `OUT_DIR/shape_db.rs` and `include!`'d in `src/font/shape.rs`.

## Why this matters

A compile-time `&'static [(u64, char)]` is the minimum-footprint, fastest-lookup structure for the L4 query. phf::Map cannot help here because the query is approximate (Hamming distance scan), not exact. Sorted-by-pHash enables an optional binary-search shortcut for exact matches before the linear Hamming scan.

## Implementation guidance

- Parse the JSON with `serde_json` (build-time dep is fine).
- Sort by pHash ascending. Validate no duplicate pHash entries (deduplicate at source).
- Emit Rust source:
  ```rust
  pub static SHAPE_TABLE: &[(u64, char)] = &[
      (0x1234..., 'a'),
      (0x1235..., 'b'),
      ...
  ];
  pub static FREQ_TABLE: &[(u64, u32)] = &[ ... ];
  ```
- Use `write!` macro with byte-perfect formatting; do not depend on rustfmt at build time.
- Print `cargo:rerun-if-changed=build/glyph-shapes.json` so cargo re-runs build.rs only when the JSON changes.

## Critical considerations

- INV: SHAPE_TABLE.len() == FREQ_TABLE.len() and entry i has matching pHash key — emit a compile-time assert.
- char escaping: `'a'` for printable, `'\u{1F600}'` for non-printable. Use `format!("{:?}", c)`'s output which produces valid Rust syntax.
- Binary footprint: 5000 entries x 16 bytes (u64 + char + padding) = 80 KB for SHAPE_TABLE, + ~60 KB for FREQ_TABLE = ~140 KB raw. Plus Rust metadata ~< 300 KB total. Within budget.
- If the JSON is missing (fresh checkout without `cargo xtask gen-shape-db`), emit an empty table with a build-warning, not an error — allows cargo build without shape DB.

## Acceptance criteria

- Build succeeds with empty JSON -> SHAPE_TABLE is `&[]`.
- Build succeeds with 100-entry JSON -> SHAPE_TABLE has 100 entries sorted by pHash.
- Re-build without JSON changes does NOT re-execute build.rs glyph generation (verify via build log).
- Duplicate pHash in JSON -> build error with line number.
- Total binary size for SHAPE_TABLE + FREQ_TABLE < 300 KB (cargo bloat verified).

## References

- Plan section: Phase 2.5 Database format (line 1422)

issue.close_reason: Implemented BI/ID inline image header parser with shorthand key expansion, array filter support, ID whitespace validation, and malformed header recovery. All 14 tests pass. Commit 4ac8479. Verification note at notes/pdftract-1sxpa.md.
issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the parser for the inline image header that begins with `BI` and ends with `ID`. Consumes alternating key-value pairs (`/Name Value`); accepts shorthand keys per spec (e.g., `/W` for /Width, `/H` for /Height, `/CS` for /ColorSpace, `/BPC` for /BitsPerComponent, `/F` for /Filter, etc.); collects them into an `InlineImageHeader { width, height, color_space, bits_per_component, filter, decode_parms, ... }` struct.

## Why this matters

The header is the only structured part of an inline image and contains the image's bbox dimensions and filter chain — both needed for ImageXObject record creation (sibling bead). The parser must terminate exactly at ID (the byte 'I' followed by 'D' at token boundary) to hand off correctly to the raw-bytes scanner.

## Implementation guidance

- Stop condition: encountering the token `ID` (case-sensitive, followed by exactly one whitespace byte per spec; the whitespace is consumed by ID, not by the raw-bytes scanner).
- Token loop: read Name; read Value (any direct object - int, real, name, string, array, dict). Allow newlines/comments between pairs.
- Shorthand key expansion table (per ISO 32000-1 Table 92):
  - /W -> /Width
  - /H -> /Height
  - /BPC -> /BitsPerComponent
  - /CS -> /ColorSpace
  - /F -> /Filter
  - /DP -> /DecodeParms
  - /D -> /Decode
  - /IM -> /ImageMask
  - /I -> /Interpolate
  - (Plus a few less common)
- Build the InlineImageHeader struct.

## Critical considerations

- The header is small (usually < 20 entries); parsing speed is not a concern.
- ID is a 2-byte token followed by EXACTLY 1 whitespace byte (LF, CR, or space) per spec — that whitespace is mandatory; if absent, emit `INLINE_IMAGE_ID_WHITESPACE_MISSING` diagnostic and recover by treating any non-token byte as image data.
- Filter chain may be a single name or an array of names.
- Color space may be a name OR an array (for /Indexed, /CalRGB, /ICCBased).
- Unknown key in header: log diagnostic, ignore.

## Acceptance criteria

- `BI /W 10 /H 10 /CS /DeviceGray /BPC 8 /F /ASCIIHexDecode ID ...EI` parses successfully.
- Shorthand expansion: header.width == 10 (from /W).
- Header with array filter `/F [/ASCII85Decode /FlateDecode]` parses.
- ID without trailing whitespace: diagnostic emitted; downstream raw-bytes scanner starts immediately.
- Malformed header (missing value): TOKENIZER_ERROR diagnostic, recover at next /Key.

## References

- Plan section: Phase 3.5 Parsing paragraph (line 1596)
- ISO 32000-1 sec 8.9.7, Table 92
issue.title: BI/ID inline image header parser

## Scope

Author profiles/builtin/book_chapter.yaml per the Phase 7.10 YAML schema, plus at least 5 PDF fixtures at tests/fixtures/profiles/book_chapter/ each with a sibling expected-output.json, plus tests/profiles/test_book_chapter.rs that asserts exact-match of metadata.profile_fields.

## Why this matters

The book_chapter profile ships in v1.0.0 as one of the nine built-ins (line 3048). Books and chapters are a high-volume document type for archival and educational workflows; extracting title, chapter_number, author, sections correctly enables index and search applications. This profile also serves as the catch-all for long-form narrative text that does not match more-specific profiles.

## Implementation guidance

- File: profiles/builtin/book_chapter.yaml
  - name: book_chapter
  - description: "Book chapters, monographs, long-form narrative documents"
  - priority: 5 (lowest among the 9 profiles -- it is the catch-all for narrative text)
  - match: all: [structural.page_count: {min: 5, max: 1000}, structural.heading_depth: {min: 1, max: 5}, any: [text_matches: '^Chapter \d+', heading_matches: '^(Chapter|Part|Section) \d+', structural.font_diversity: {min: 1, max: 4}]]; none: [text_contains: ['Abstract', 'WHEREAS', 'Invoice', 'Account Statement']]
  - extraction: reading_order: line_dominant (book pages flow top-to-bottom); table_detection: default; readability_threshold: 0.6; include_invisible: false; include_headers_footers: false (page numbers and headers are not body content)
  - fields: title (first chapter page; region: top_third; pick: largest_font), chapter_number (first page; near: ['Chapter', 'Part'], regex: '\d+'), author (region: top_quarter; pick: smallest_font or next-largest-after-title), sections (per-heading collection across the chapter; ordered list)
- Fixtures: 5 chapters covering: novel chapter (Gutenberg), academic book chapter, textbook chapter with figures, technical manual chapter, recipe-book chapter

## Critical considerations

- book_chapter is the LOWEST-priority profile so it does not steal matches from more-specific types (invoice, paper, contract, etc.); the priority: 5 setting reflects this
- chapter_number extraction depends on the chapter having a numeric prefix; un-numbered chapters (Prologue, Epilogue, Acknowledgements) fall back to a null value
- sections extraction collects all heading-level-2+ headings; this is a best-effort table-of-contents
- Body text quality matters more for book_chapter than other profiles because consumers actually READ the output -- the readability_threshold: 0.6 keeps low-quality text out
- Multi-chapter PDFs (a whole book in one PDF) are an edge case -- the profile matches the first chapter only at v1.0; document as a known limitation
- Page numbering: books use roman numerals for front-matter (i, ii, iii, ...) then Arabic for body (1, 2, 3, ...); the page_label field in the extraction schema preserves this -- the profile does NOT extract page numbers itself
- Fixtures: at least one should be from Project Gutenberg (PD); at least one academic publisher with CC-BY license; at least one bilingual or non-English-script chapter
- The book_chapter profile also serves as the "miscellaneous narrative text" catch-all -- if a document does not match any other profile but is text-heavy and has paragraph structure, book_chapter wins over unknown

## Acceptance criteria

- profiles/builtin/book_chapter.yaml validates
- 5+ public-domain or open-license fixtures with expected outputs
- tests/profiles/test_book_chapter.rs passes
- Per-field accuracy: >= 90% on the 5-fixture corpus (sections relaxed to >= 80%)
- The book_chapter profile does NOT steal matches from more-specific profiles in the classifier corpus (verify by running the 200-doc corpus and asserting no false-positives)

## References

## Scope

Bring docs/research/opentype-math-and-formula-extraction.md to v1.0 final-pass: document the OpenType MATH table parsing, formula-region detection via math-operator presence, glyph variant resolution (cvt / cvar tables when present), and the emission of formula blocks as kind: paragraph with metadata flags.

## Why this matters

Scientific paper extraction (one of the v1.0 built-in profiles) is materially incomplete without basic formula handling. Line 1709 in the plan ties formula detection to OpenType Math table presence and explicitly cites this note as the algorithm authority. The current 168-line draft establishes the framework. The note also informs the profile classifier signal structural.has_math (line 2958).

## Implementation guidance

- File to update: docs/research/opentype-math-and-formula-extraction.md (already exists, currently 168 lines)
- Required content sections:
  - OpenType MATH table parsing: locate the MATH table in the font; extract MathConstants, MathGlyphInfo, MathVariants, MathKern subtables
  - Formula-region detection: any span using glyphs from a font with a MATH table is formula-candidate; aggregate formula-candidate spans into formula regions by proximity
  - Variant glyph resolution: stretching variants (vertical and horizontal) -- map a stretched glyph (large parenthesis, integral sign) back to its base codepoint plus a stretch hint
  - Inline vs display formula classification: display formulas are centred and offset from surrounding text; inline formulas are mid-paragraph
  - LaTeX-like reconstruction (best-effort, not authoritative): emit a TeX-like string in metadata.formula_tex when a confidence threshold is met; otherwise emit Unicode text only
  - Output: kind: paragraph blocks with metadata.contains_formula: true and (optionally) metadata.formula_tex
- Algorithm pseudo-code
- Validation methodology: arxiv paper fixtures with known equations

## Critical considerations

- The MATH table is OpenType-specific; legacy TeX-encoded PDFs (mathx, msbm, cmsy) need a separate dispatch in the font recognition coordinator (Phase 2.2)
- Variant glyph resolution must NOT emit a different codepoint per variant -- the base codepoint with a stretch hint is the right structure (one logical character per equation symbol)
- LaTeX-like reconstruction is BEST-EFFORT; do not commit to round-trip fidelity at v1.0 -- mark it experimental in the output and gate behind a feature flag if implementation slips
- structural.has_math signal: this note must define exactly what triggers the flag (any glyph from a MATH-table font, OR a confidence threshold of formula spans, OR LaTeX-string pattern in text)
- Scientific paper profile (line 3043) depends on this signal for classification; if has_math is unreliable the profile misclassifies inline-math papers as book_chapter
- Reading order interaction: formula regions are atomic for xy_cut purposes (do not split equations across columns)

## Acceptance criteria

- docs/research/opentype-math-and-formula-extraction.md updated with MATH table parsing detail and formula detection
- Pseudo-code listing for formula-region detection
- Inline vs display classification rules documented
- LaTeX-like reconstruction documented as best-effort with feature-flag guidance
- structural.has_math signal definition documented for profile classifier consumption
- File grows to approx 300+ lines

issue.close_reason: Implemented GIL release with py.allow_threads on extract_py entry point. Added Python multi-threading test to verify parallelism. Code compiles and passes formatting. Commit: 870d707. Verification note: notes/pdftract-1tswa.md. PASS: GIL released during extraction, multi-threading test added, compiles successfully.
issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the GIL-release wrapper around every extraction entry point. py.allow_threads(|| ...) releases the GIL during the blocking Rust extraction call so other Python threads can run. Wrap extract / extract_text / extract_stream (per-yield) consistently and audit other module functions that may block.

## Why this matters

Without GIL release, Python multi-threaded code (Flask handlers, asyncio.to_thread, ThreadPoolExecutor) blocks all other Python work for seconds during extraction. This is critical-test #5 (line 2093): "4 threads each extracting different PDFs simultaneously; no deadlock". Without allow_threads, that test gets 4 sequential extractions.

## Implementation guidance

- Pattern: let result = py.allow_threads(|| { extract_inner(path, opts) })?;
- All blocking operations (PDF I/O, parsing, OCR, output serialization) execute inside allow_threads
- Per-yield in extract_stream: when waiting on Receiver<PageFrame>, release GIL during recv; reacquire for PyDict construction
- Cancellation: while inside allow_threads, Python signal handling (Ctrl+C) is delayed; emit a Diagnostic if extraction takes > N seconds without yielding back
- For shared mutable state inside allow_threads (e.g. progress callback): use Mutex; never touch Python state without re-acquiring GIL via py.with_gil(|py2| ...)

## Critical considerations

- INV: NEVER call Python C-API while GIL is released
- pythonize call to build PyDict MUST happen with GIL held (outside allow_threads or via with_gil)
- Stream iterator __next__: release GIL for recv; reacquire for pythonize
- Rust panic inside allow_threads -> caught by PyO3 + re-raised as PdftractError (not segfault)
- This is the load-bearing test for Python multi-threading users — broken GIL handling silently degrades parallelism

## Acceptance criteria

- Critical test (line 2093): Python ThreadPoolExecutor with 4 workers, each calling pdftract.extract on a distinct PDF -> wallclock time < (4 * single-extract-time) / 2 (proves parallelism)
- pyo3-asyncio integration: pdftract.extract callable from inside asyncio.to_thread without deadlock
- Ctrl+C during long extraction: process exits cleanly within a few seconds (signal handler unblocks)

## References

- Plan section: Phase 6.3 Python GIL handling (line 2080) + critical test 5 (line 2093)
- PyO3 docs on allow_threads
issue.title: 6.3.3: GIL release (py.allow_threads) on all extraction entry points + multi-threading test

issue.description:
## Scope

Add `[package.metadata.binstall]` metadata to `crates/pdftract-cli/Cargo.toml` so that `cargo binstall pdftract` downloads the matching binary archive from the GitHub Release instead of compiling from source. The metadata names the URL template, archive format, and binary path inside the archive.

## Why this matters

Without the metadata, users running `cargo binstall pdftract` fall back to a fresh `cargo install` from source — which on a fresh machine takes 6+ minutes and requires a full Rust toolchain. With the metadata it is a 2-second binary download. This is the lowest-friction install path for non-Rust users discovering the project via the Rust toolchain.

## Implementation guidance

- Add to `crates/pdftract-cli/Cargo.toml`:
  ```toml
  [package.metadata.binstall]
  pkg-url = "{ repo }/releases/download/v{ version }/pdftract-v{ version }-{ target }.{ archive-format }"
  pkg-fmt = "tgz"
  bin-dir = "pdftract-v{ version }-{ target }/{ bin }{ binary-ext }"
  
  [package.metadata.binstall.overrides.x86_64-pc-windows-gnu]
  pkg-fmt = "zip"
  ```
- The `{ target }` placeholder is replaced with the rustc target triple at binstall time; the five supported triples MUST all be present as release assets (see `pdftract-build-binaries` template)
- The `{ archive-format }` resolves to `tar.gz` for the default `tgz` format and `zip` for Windows
- Verify the URL template matches the actual asset names produced by `pdftract-github-release` — naming drift between this metadata and the release asset names is the most common binstall failure mode
- Include this metadata only on `pdftract-cli` (not `pdftract-core` which is a library)

## Critical considerations

- The `{ repo }` placeholder pulls from `package.repository`; if `repository` is wrong or unset, binstall fails with an opaque url-empty error
- Windows uses `.zip` per Unix convention (the binary archive bead must produce `.zip` for `x86_64-pc-windows-gnu`)
- Glibc-built Linux binaries are NOT shipped — only the static-musl pair is published; on a glibc-only host binstall will fall back to `x86_64-unknown-linux-musl` (which is fully self-contained and works fine)
- The `cargo binstall pdftract` UX is documented in the README install instructions block
- Verifying the install path requires: tagged commit, `pdftract-github-release` workflow completes, `cargo install cargo-binstall`, then `cargo binstall pdftract --version X.Y.Z`

## Acceptance criteria

- `crates/pdftract-cli/Cargo.toml` contains `[package.metadata.binstall]` table with the documented `pkg-url`, `pkg-fmt`, `bin-dir`
- The Windows override is present and sets `pkg-fmt = "zip"`
- On a clean machine after a release: `cargo binstall pdftract` downloads the appropriate binary without compiling
- The README install section includes `cargo binstall pdftract` as the recommended Rust-toolchain install path

## References

- Plan section: Release Engineering / Distribution Channels, line 3378 (Cargo binstall index)
- cargo binstall project documentation
- Sibling: pdftract-github-release workflow defines the actual asset URL pattern
issue.title: cargo binstall metadata in pdftract-cli Cargo.toml

issue.close_reason: Implemented resolve_type3() for Type 3 font encoding resolution. L1 (ToUnicode), L2 (AGL), skip L3, L4 (shape recognition). Added ShapeEntry, ShapeMatch, lookup_shape() stub. Fixed overflow in Type3Font::load_widths. 3 tests pass. Shape DB awaits Phase 2.5 build/glyph-shapes.json. Verification note: notes/pdftract-1uj5.md
issue.description:
## Scope

Implement `resolve_type3(font: &Type3Font, char_code: u8) -> ResolvedGlyph` that runs the Type 3-specific fallback chain: (1) try `/ToUnicode` CMap (same Phase 2.2 L1 parser); (2) try `/Encoding` -> glyph name -> AGL via Phase 2.2 L2; (3) rasterize the glyph via the sibling rasterizer bead and look up the pHash in the Phase 2.5 shape DB. Returns the same `ResolvedGlyph` shape used elsewhere, with `unicode_source = "to_unicode" | "agl" | "shape_match"`.

## Why this matters

The Type 3 resolution chain shares L1/L2 with regular fonts but SKIPS L3 (no embedded font program -> no fingerprint hash possible) and uses a Type3-specific rasterizer at L4. Without a dedicated dispatcher, the Phase 2.2 resolver would attempt L3 fingerprinting on Type 3 fonts (which would always return None) and waste time.

## Implementation guidance

- Branch on `font.kind()`: if Type3, dispatch to `resolve_type3`; otherwise dispatch to Phase 2.2 generic resolver.
- L1 logic: reuse the Phase 2.2 ToUnicode CMap parser — Type 3 ToUnicode is structurally identical to other fonts.
- L2 logic: same Phase 2.2 `(encoding + Differences + AGL)` pipeline; the glyph name comes from the Type 3 `/Encoding` (may be arbitrary).
- L4 logic: rasterize via `rasterize_type3_glyph` -> compute pHash via shared pHash function -> call `pdftract-core::font::shape::lookup(phash)`.
- Skip L3 explicitly with a comment `// Type 3 fonts have no embedded program; L3 fingerprinting not applicable`.

## Critical considerations

- Per the plan: "If glyph name is non-standard (arbitrary user name), rasterize the content stream to a 32x32 bitmap and apply shape recognition (Level 4)" — the heuristic for "non-standard" is "AGL lookup returned None". Run L2 first; if L2 returns None for an Arc<str> that was non-empty, escalate to L4.
- Failure case: L1+L2+L4 all miss -> U+FFFD with diagnostic `TYPE3_GLYPH_UNMAPPED`.
- Caching is shared with the Phase 2.2 resolver cache via a polymorphic key; do not maintain a parallel Type 3 cache.

## Acceptance criteria

- Type 3 font with ToUnicode mapping code 0x41 -> 'A': resolves to ('A', "to_unicode", 1.0).
- Type 3 font with standard glyph name `A` via Encoding and no ToUnicode: resolves to ('A', "agl", 0.9).
- Type 3 font with arbitrary name `xglyph123` and no ToUnicode + a rendered shape matching letter 'X' in the shape DB: resolves to ('X', "shape_match", 0.7).
- Type 3 font with arbitrary name + no shape match: ('U+FFFD', "unknown", 0.0) + diagnostic.

## References

- Plan section: Phase 2.4 Pipeline (lines 1402-1406)
- Critical test: "arbitrary glyph names and no ToUnicode: shape recognition fallback, confidence = 0.7" (line 1412)
issue.title: Type 3 resolver: ToUnicode -> Encoding -> shape DB chain

issue.close_reason: Implementation verified and committed (ccd13f1). All 34 tests passing. AC PASS: Latin text strips all zero-width chars; Arabic/Indic preserve ZWNJ/ZWJ; auto-detection working; BOM always stripped. Verification note in notes/pdftract-1vrxg.md (commit 19c1fc2).
issue.description:
## Scope

Implement `normalize_word_breaks(span: &mut Span, script_hint: Option<unicode_script::Script>) -> u32` that strips U+200B (zero-width space), U+FEFF (BOM mid-stream), U+200C (zero-width non-joiner), U+200D (zero-width joiner) UNLESS the span's script_hint requires them: Arabic, Indic scripts (Devanagari, Bengali, Gujarati, etc.), and certain other complex scripts use ZWJ/ZWNJ for legitimate orthographic distinctions. Returns count of stripped codepoints.

## Why this matters

These four characters are zero-width formatting controls. In Latin text they're noise (from copy-paste or poor producers); in Arabic/Indic they're MANDATORY for correct grapheme rendering. Blindly stripping breaks legitimate text; blindly preserving leaves noise. Script-aware filtering is the correct approach.

## Implementation guidance

- Crate: `unicode-script` (if approved; otherwise use unicode_normalization's script lookup) — provides `Script` enum and `char::script(c)` lookup. If not approved, use a simple lookup: characters in Arabic/Hebrew/Devanagari/Bengali/etc. blocks via codepoint range checks (no extra crate).
- For each char in span.text:
  - If c is U+200B or U+FEFF: ALWAYS strip (always noise; they're never used orthographically).
  - If c is U+200C or U+200D: STRIP unless script_hint is in {Arabic, Hebrew, Devanagari, Bengali, Gujarati, Gurmukhi, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam, Thai, Myanmar, Khmer, Lao, Tibetan, ...}.
- Use `String::retain` with closure that knows script_hint.
- Track and return strip count.
- script_hint can be derived from the document's /Lang (Phase 1.4) or from span text's dominant script (call once per page or per span).

## Critical considerations

- INV: U+200B (zero-width space) and U+FEFF (BOM) are NEVER content; safe to always strip from extracted text.
- U+200C (ZWNJ) and U+200D (ZWJ) ARE content in Arabic ("ای" requires ZWNJ between certain characters), Indic ("क्ष" with ZWJ for conjuncts), Persian, Sinhala. Stripping breaks rendering.
- Script detection: from the SPAN's own text — if the span has primarily Arabic chars, script_hint is Arabic. From /Lang the document hint.
- Fallback when script_hint is None: STRIP all 4 (safe default for unknown-script docs; bias toward cleaner Latin output).
- Performance: O(n) per span.

## Acceptance criteria

- "auto\u{200B}mation" (Latin) -> "automation" (1 stripped, U+200B).
- Arabic "ای\u{200C}\u{200D}" with script_hint=Arabic -> unchanged (ZWNJ/ZWJ preserved).

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the `BT` (begin text) and `ET` (end text) operators that bracket every text object in a PDF content stream. BT initializes `text_matrix = identity` and `text_line_matrix = identity`; ET discards both (subsequent text operators have NO valid text matrix until the next BT). Validates BT/ET pairing: BT inside BT emits `BT_NESTED` diagnostic; ET without BT emits `ET_WITHOUT_BT` diagnostic.

## Why this matters

Without correct BT initialization every page accumulates leftover text_matrix state from the previous page's last text object — bbox positions drift catastrophically. ET-without-BT or BT-nested cases come up in malformed PDFs (Apple Preview occasionally emits these); silent recovery prevents extraction abort.

## Implementation guidance

- Track an `in_text_object: bool` on the executor.
- BT: if already true, emit BT_NESTED; reset both matrices to identity; set in_text_object = true; reset the word-boundary recalibration window (alongside Tf reset per Phase 3.2).
- ET: if false, emit ET_WITHOUT_BT and no-op; otherwise set in_text_object = false (the matrices are "invalid" until next BT — implementation choice: leave them at last value or zero — set a sentinel/zero is safer to expose bugs).
- Text-show operators (Tj, TJ, ', ") should check `in_text_object` and skip with `TEXT_SHOW_OUTSIDE_BT` diagnostic if false.
- BT does NOT modify CTM, font, or any color/spacing state — only the two text matrices.

## Critical considerations

- INV: BT pairs always reset to IDENTITY, NOT to whatever Tm was last set. Matrix history outside the BT scope is preserved (it's a state knob, not a stack).
- INV: ET discards text matrices but DOES NOT pop the graphics state — q/Q remain orthogonal.
- Some PDF producers emit `BT ... BT ... ET` (nested) — both inner BTs reset to identity. The diagnostic is informational, not an error.
- Some PDFs (rare) emit text operators between BT pairs that have NO Tf — those operators should no-op rather than crash (font is None).

## Acceptance criteria

- Two consecutive `BT 100 100 Td Tj... ET BT Tj... ET` blocks: the second Tj starts at text_matrix == identity, NOT at (100,100).
- ET without matching BT: emits ET_WITHOUT_BT, does not panic.
- Nested BT (BT...BT...ET): inner BT resets matrices; outer ET balances; second BT in the pair emits BT_NESTED diagnostic.
- Tj outside BT/ET: emits TEXT_SHOW_OUTSIDE_BT and produces no glyphs.

## References

- Plan section: Phase 3.1 BT/ET in operator table (lines 1481-1482)
issue.title: BT/ET text object lifecycle (text matrix reset)

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the `Pdftract` NuGet package as a subprocess-based SDK. Spawn the bundled `pdftract` binary via `System.Diagnostics.Process`, parse JSON output via `System.Text.Json` (NOT Newtonsoft to keep dependency footprint minimal), expose the 9 contract methods as async-first methods returning `Task<T>` / `IAsyncEnumerable<T>`. Repo at `github.com/jedarden/pdftract-dotnet`.

## Why this matters

.NET is the dominant enterprise platform on Windows-heavy workloads and a growing presence on Linux via .NET 8+. Async-first means the SDK plays well with ASP.NET Core request pipelines without thread-pool starvation. Using `System.Text.Json` (built into the framework) instead of Newtonsoft avoids dragging in a 100K+ LOC dependency and a separate version-compatibility surface.

## Implementation guidance

- NuGet package id: `Pdftract` (no scope; package id is title-case per .NET convention)
- Repo: `github.com/jedarden/pdftract-dotnet` (separate repo)
- Target framework: `net8.0` minimum; `net9.0` recommended; document the support matrix
- File layout (generator-driven; see Tera template scaffolding bead):
  - `Pdftract.csproj` declaring `TargetFramework` and NuGet metadata
  - `src/Pdftract.cs` (the main client class)
  - `src/Codegen/Methods.cs` (generated)
  - `src/Codegen/Errors.cs` (generated; 8 exception classes)
  - `src/Models/Document.cs`, `Page.cs`, etc. (record types)
  - `tests/Pdftract.Tests/ConformanceTests.cs` (xUnit)
- Method signatures (.NET, async-first):
  - `public class Pdftract : IDisposable`
  - `Task<Document> ExtractAsync(Source source, ExtractOptions? options = null, CancellationToken ct = default)`
  - `Task<string> ExtractTextAsync(...)`
  - `Task<string> ExtractMarkdownAsync(...)`
  - `IAsyncEnumerable<Page> ExtractStreamAsync(...)`
  - `IAsyncEnumerable<Match> SearchAsync(Source source, string pattern, SearchOptions? options = null, CancellationToken ct = default)`
  - `Task<Metadata> GetMetadataAsync(...)`
  - `Task<Fingerprint> HashAsync(...)`
  - `Task<Classification> ClassifyAsync(Source source, CancellationToken ct = default)`
  - `Task<bool> VerifyReceiptAsync(string path, Receipt receipt, CancellationToken ct = default)`
  - Plus sync variants (Extract, ExtractText, etc.) that internally call `.GetAwaiter().GetResult()` on the async version — discouraged but necessary for legacy code paths
- Option names use PascalCase per C# convention: CLI `--ocr-language` becomes `OcrLanguage`
- Source type: discriminated union via abstract class `Source` with subclasses `PathSource`, `UrlSource`, `BytesSource`; expose factory methods `Source.FromPath(string)`, `Source.FromUri(Uri)`, `Source.FromBytes(byte[])`
- Errors: `public class PdftractException : Exception` is the base; 8 subclasses mirror the contract
- CancellationToken propagates to the subprocess via `Process.Kill(entireProcessTree: true)` on cancellation
- Native AOT compatibility: avoid reflection-only paths; mark types `[JsonSerializable]` for source-generated System.Text.Json contexts

## Critical considerations

- .NET 8+ is the floor; .NET Framework (4.x) is NOT supported (no Span<T>, no IAsyncEnumerable on Framework)
- System.Text.Json deserialization is configured with `PropertyNamingPolicy = JsonNamingPolicy.SnakeCaseLower` to match the binary's snake_case output, but the SDK exposes PascalCase property names per .NET convention
- The async-first design: sync wrappers should emit a SuppressMessage attribute or compiler warning so consumers know they are using the discouraged path
- Native AOT compatibility is a v1.1+ goal but the SDK is designed with AOT in mind from day one (no reflection-based JSON, no LINQ Expression trees)
- The `Pdftract` class implements IDisposable but `ValueTask DisposeAsync()` is also exposed via `IAsyncDisposable` for proper async cleanup
- IAsyncEnumerable for streaming: backed by the binary's NDJSON output; the SDK reads stdin asynchronously and yields parsed items as they arrive

## Acceptance criteria

- The `Pdftract` NuGet package builds with `dotnet pack`
- All 9 contract methods exposed as both async and sync variants
- All 8 exception classes inherit from PdftractException
- Document, Page, etc. exposed as C# records
- `dotnet test` runs the conformance runner and 100% passes
- CancellationToken cancellation terminates the subprocess
- The package supports `net8.0` and `net9.0`

## References

- Plan section: SDK Architecture / The Ten SDKs, line 3476 (.NET subprocess via System.Diagnostics.Process + System.Text.Json; async-first)
- Plan section: SDK Architecture / Per-SDK Release Channels, line 3573 (NuGet)
- Plan section: SDK Acceptance Criteria, line 3587 (async conventions: C# Task<T>)
- Sibling: pdftract-dotnet-publish Argo workflow
- Sibling: SDK contract and conformance suite

## Scope

Implement the three output formats for pdftract doctor:

- Default (TTY): colored human-readable table with check name, status badge (OK/WARN/FAIL with ANSI colors green/yellow/red), and detail string; summary line \"N OK, M WARN, K FAIL\" at the bottom
- Non-TTY default: same content as TTY but plain text (no ANSI escapes)
- --json: single JSON object {\"summary\":{\"ok\":N,\"warn\":M,\"fail\":K},\"checks\":[{\"name\":\"...\",\"status\":\"OK|WARN|FAIL|N/A\",\"detail\":\"...\"},...]}
- --features: list of compile-time features only; no diagnostic checks run

Module: crates/pdftract-cli/src/doctor/output/ with separate human.rs, json.rs, features.rs files.

## Why this matters

doctor's output is the operator's interface; getting it wrong wastes the value of the checks. A wall of text without color hides the FAILs in the middle of OKs; a missing summary forces the operator to scroll. JSON output is consumed by CI smoke tests and monitoring dashboards that need a stable parseable shape.

Different consumers want different output: a human running ./pdftract doctor on the terminal wants color; a CI script wants --json; a Dockerfile that wants to record the feature build at image creation wants --features.

## Implementation guidance

### Human-readable (TTY default)

- Use the colored crate (already in dev-deps; promote to runtime under cli feature gate). Crate is unmaintained but stable; alternatives like console or owo-colors are equivalent — pick whichever has zero new transitive deps
- Format:
  ```
  Check                         Status  Detail
  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  pdftract binary               OK      v1.0.0 git:abc1234 features: ocr,serve,mcp
  tesseract install             OK      v5.3.0
  tesseract languages           WARN    optional langs missing: deu, fra
  leptonica install             FAIL    pkg-config: lept not found
  ulimit -n                     OK      8192
  ...
  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  12 OK, 1 WARN, 1 FAIL
  ```
- ANSI colors: OK=green, WARN=yellow, FAIL=red. Detect TTY via atty crate (already a transitive dep); non-TTY → plain text
- Table column widths: name 30, status 6, detail flex; truncate names > 30 chars with ellipsis
- Summary line at the bottom; if FAIL count > 0, also print to stderr (so CI scripts capturing stdout still see the failures via stderr stream)

### --json

- Output to stdout:
  ```json
  {
    \"summary\": {\"ok\": 12, \"warn\": 1, \"fail\": 1, \"not_applicable\": 0},
    \"checks\": [
      {\"name\": \"pdftract binary\", \"status\": \"OK\", \"detail\": \"v1.0.0 git:abc1234 features: ocr,serve,mcp\"},
      {\"name\": \"tesseract install\", \"status\": \"OK\", \"detail\": \"v5.3.0\"},
      ...
    ]
  }
  ```
- Single newline at the end (no pretty-print by default; --json --pretty if needed in future)
- N/A checks INCLUDED in the JSON (with status=\"N/A\") so consumers see the full set; human output OMITS N/A rows to reduce noise

### --features

- Prints one line per compiled feature: \"ocr\", \"serve\", \"mcp\", ...
- Exit code 0; no diagnostic checks run
- Useful for Dockerfile build records: pdftract doctor --features > /image/build-metadata.txt

## Critical considerations

- The TTY detection (atty) governs color and table-vs-plain decision; --no-color flag overrides
- ANSI escape codes must be stripped from non-TTY output entirely (don't just disable color setting; verify no escape bytes in output)
- JSON output is machine-consumable; do NOT include colors, table separators, or summary in JSON
- Summary line in human output is NOT in --json (the JSON's \"summary\" object replaces it)
- N/A status: in human output, skip the row entirely; in JSON, include with status: \"N/A\" for completeness
- Long detail strings: human output truncates at terminal width minus column overhead; JSON includes full detail
- Test with stripped colors: pdftract doctor | cat → no ANSI bytes; pdftract doctor (interactive) → colors

## Acceptance criteria

- pdftract doctor on a TTY → colored table with summary line at bottom
- pdftract doctor | cat → plain-text table with summary, no ANSI bytes
- pdftract doctor --json → single JSON object that deserializes as { summary, checks: [] }
- pdftract doctor --json | jq '.summary.fail' → integer
- pdftract doctor --features → list of features one per line; exit 0; no checks run
- pdftract doctor --no-color → plain text even in TTY
- 14-check output fits within 80-column terminal width without wrapping (column widths calibrated)
- N/A rows excluded from human output, included in JSON

## References

- Plan section: Phase 6.10 pdftract doctor (lines 2486-2517)
- Sibling 6.10.1 (provides the CheckResult shape consumed here)
- Sibling 6.10.3 (exit codes interact with summary counts)
- atty crate for TTY detection
- colored crate for ANSI
Labels: cli, doctor, output, phase-6

issue.description:
## Scope

Add a `compute-sha256sums` step to `pdftract-github-release` that produces an aggregate `SHA256SUMS` file covering every distributed artifact in one place: 10 binary archives, 5 wheels, 1 sdist, and the CycloneDX SBOM. The file format matches GNU coreutils `sha256sum` output (one line per file: `<sha256>  <filename>`). Verified by users via the single cosign verify-blob command using the companion `SHA256SUMS.sig` file.

## Why this matters

Per-artifact `.sha256` sidecars are tedious to verify (one command per artifact). One aggregate file with one signature is the modern release convention (used by Rust toolchain, Go releases, Kubernetes). The `cosign verify-blob --signature SHA256SUMS.sig SHA256SUMS` UX is one command for all artifacts.

## Implementation guidance

- Compute step (after all artifacts collected, before signing):
  ```bash
  cd release-artifacts
  sha256sum pdftract-v*-*.tar.gz pdftract-v*-*.zip \
            pdftract-*-cp311-abi3-*.whl pdftract-*.tar.gz \
            pdftract-v*.cdx.json \
            > SHA256SUMS
  ```
- Sort by filename for deterministic ordering: `LC_ALL=C sort -k 2 < SHA256SUMS > SHA256SUMS.sorted && mv SHA256SUMS.sorted SHA256SUMS`
- Verify locally before signing: `sha256sum --check SHA256SUMS` (must return 0)
- The `SHA256SUMS` file itself is then signed by the cosign step (separate bead) producing `SHA256SUMS.sig`
- Verification command for users (documented in the README "Verifying releases" section):
  ```bash
  cosign verify-blob \
    --certificate-identity-regexp 'argo-workflows/pdftract-' \
    --certificate-oidc-issuer 'https://iad-ci-oidc.ardenone.com/' \
    --signature SHA256SUMS.sig SHA256SUMS \
    && sha256sum --check SHA256SUMS
  ```

## Critical considerations

- The SHA256SUMS file is part of the artifact verification chain — its content MUST be deterministic; sorting by filename and using `LC_ALL=C` guarantees this
- The file does NOT include `SHA256SUMS.sig` itself or `multiple.intoto.jsonl` (those are signed/verified by other means)
- The file DOES include the SBOM (so the SBOM's integrity is verifiable through the same cosign verify-blob)
- The file does NOT include Docker image manifests (those are signed by cosign sign on the registry, not by blob hash)
- A discrepancy between SHA256SUMS and a downloaded file is a release-integrity incident (P0) — possible causes: corrupted upload, MITM during download, intentional tampering. Response: re-run the cascade and re-verify against the new signature
- Linux/macOS `sha256sum` and `shasum -a 256` produce identical output; Windows users without Git Bash should run `certutil -hashfile FILENAME SHA256` and compare manually (documented in the README)

## Acceptance criteria

- The `pdftract-github-release` workflow includes a `compute-sha256sums` step that produces a deterministically-sorted file
- Two consecutive cascades against the same tag produce byte-identical SHA256SUMS files
- The verification command in the README works for an end-user after downloading SHA256SUMS, SHA256SUMS.sig, and any artifact
- The file is attached to the GitHub Release alongside SHA256SUMS.sig
- A deliberately corrupted downloaded artifact is detected by `sha256sum --check SHA256SUMS`

## References

- Plan section: Release Engineering / Artifact Taxonomy, line 3351 (SHA256SUMS aggregate)
- Plan section: Signing and Provenance, line 3401 (sign-blob of SHA256SUMS)
- Plan section: Release Engineering Acceptance Criteria, line 3442 (one cosign verify-blob umbrella)
- GNU coreutils sha256sum documentation

## Scope

Create the skeleton `pdftract-ci` Argo WorkflowTemplate YAML in `jedarden/declarative-config -> k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/pdftract-ci.yaml`. The template defines the top-level DAG structure that orchestrates all per-target build, test, quality, benchmark, and release steps. This bead establishes only the file's existence, the WorkflowTemplate metadata, the parameter list (commit SHA, ref, repo URL, branch/tag triggers), an exitHandler for status reporting, the imagePullSecrets / serviceAccount wiring, the workflow-level volume claim template for shared cargo target cache, and the empty step skeletons that subsequent Phase 0 beads will fill in.

Once this bead is closed, sibling beads can develop each leg of the DAG in parallel without colliding on the same YAML file (they edit distinct named steps inside the templates: list).

## Why this matters

Phase 0 is foundational — no Phase 1+ work can be code-reviewed or merged until CI is active per ADR-009 and the parent epic's primary objective. The scaffolding bead must land first so other Phase 0 contributors can branch off it without colliding on a single YAML.

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement a schema-version migration tool that takes (schema-version, json) input and applies registered transformations for known v1.0 to v1.x schema-version evolution.

Module: crates/pdftract-schema-migrate/ (new workspace crate) OR xtask migrate-schema subcommand.

## Why this matters

The plan's additive-evolution rules require that minor-version schema changes are additive only (no field removal, no type changes). The migration tool supports the rare necessary transformations (e.g. a field renamed across a minor version with a compat alias). Without it, downstream consumers must hand-write migration logic for each version they support.

## Implementation guidance

- New crate or xtask:
  - crates/pdftract-schema-migrate/ OR
  - xtask/src/bin/migrate_schema.rs
- Public API:
  ```rust
  pub fn migrate(from_version: &str, to_version: &str, json: serde_json::Value) -> Result<serde_json::Value>
  ```
- Migration registry: HashMap<(from, to), Box<dyn MigrationFn>>
- Each registered migration is a pure function from one Value shape to another
- For v1.0 to v1.0: identity (no-op)
- For v1.0 to v1.1+: register specific field renames, default additions, etc.
- CLI subcommand for ad-hoc use: pdftract migrate-schema --from v1.0 --to v1.1 input.json > output.json (or as part of pdftract validate)
- Forward-compat: if no migration is registered for the requested transformation, return an error

## Critical considerations

- v1.0.0 to v1.0.0 is the only currently-needed migration (a no-op); the tool's structure exists for future-proofing
- Adding a v1.0 to v1.1 migration is a separate task triggered when v1.1 schema lands
- BREAKING v1 to v2 migrations are out of scope; v2 requires a full data migration plan
- The migration registry is internal; downstream consumers don't extend it
- Migration tool MUST NOT silently lose data; round-trip tests verify

## Acceptance criteria

- migrate(\"1.0\", \"1.0\", json) returns json unchanged (identity)
- migrate(\"1.0\", \"1.1\", json) errors with \"no migration registered\" until v1.1 lands
- CLI subcommand works: cat input.json | pdftract migrate-schema --from 1.0 --to 1.0 produces identical output
- Unit tests for the registry structure (can register, can lookup, can fail-gracefully on missing)

## References

- Plan section: Phase 6.1.3 + schema evolution rules
- Coordinator: pdftract-2rc4 (parent)
- Sibling: schema generation
Labels: migration, phase-6, schema

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the depth-first walker over /StructTreeRoot. For each StructElem, resolve its element type (Standard, or mapped via the document /RoleMap when the producer uses a non-standard tag), and record /ActualText, /Alt, /Lang. Emit a typed StructElem tree in memory ready for MCID assignment in 7.1.3.

## Why this matters

This is the entry point of the StructTree pipeline; every later sub-task consumes its output. Producer-specific tags (e.g. "Heading1") must be remapped to Standard ("H1") before downstream block-kind mapping; without this, every Word-generated PDF would emit unknown element types.

## Implementation guidance

- Locate /StructTreeRoot via document catalog (/Catalog /StructTreeRoot)
- Walk via /K (kids) array; each entry may be: a child StructElem dict, a /MCR (marked content reference) dict, an integer (raw MCID), or an /OBJR (object reference)
- /RoleMap: a dictionary in /StructTreeRoot mapping producer tag names to standard names; resolve recursively (chains of remaps allowed)
- Build a typed StructElemNode { id, std_type, raw_type, actual_text, alt, lang, kids: Vec<Kid> } where Kid is enum { Element(node), Mcid(u32), ObjRef(ObjRef) }
- Standard structure type set: per PDF 1.7 14.8.4 - Document, Part, Art, Sect, Div, BlockQuote, Caption, TOC, TOCI, Index, NonStruct, Private, P, H, H1..H6, L, LI, Lbl, LBody, Table, TR, TH, TD, THead, TBody, TFoot, Span, Quote, Note, Reference, BibEntry, Code, Link, Annot, Ruby, RB, RT, RP, Warichu, WT, WP, Figure, Formula, Form

## Critical considerations

- /RoleMap may map to another non-standard name; chase chains until a standard name is reached OR a cycle is detected (cycle => emit diagnostic, treat as NonStruct)
- /Lang inherits from ancestor StructElem when absent on a node - tracker required in walker
- /ActualText may be present on intermediate nodes; apply to all descendant content (overrides glyph text within scope)
- Some PDFs put the StructTreeRoot as an array shorthand - tolerate both Dict and Array roots

## Acceptance criteria

## Scope

Implement the TH-06 supply-chain gate as a CI test: enforce Cargo.lock checked-in for binary crates, run cargo audit (severity >= medium blocks), run cargo deny (license + ban enforcement), and verify build/CHECKSUMS.sha256 against the actual build-time data files. The gate runs on every PR and nightly against main.

## Why this matters

TH-06 (line 877) is the supply-chain attack defence. Lines 883-896 codify the policy: Cargo.lock checked in for binary crates, cargo audit + cargo deny in Phase 0 CI on every PR with severity >= medium blocking merge, checksum pin on build/font-fingerprints.json and build/glyph-shapes.json. The test bead operationalizes the policy.

## Implementation guidance

- Files to create / modify:
  - Cargo.lock in pdftract-cli/, pdftract-py/ checked in (per ADR / line 887); .gitignore in pdftract-core/ leaves Cargo.lock untracked
  - deny.toml: license allowlist (MIT, Apache-2.0 with or without LLVM exception, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, ISC, Zlib, Unicode-DFS-2016, MPL-2.0 file-level only); GPL/AGPL/LGPL forbidden in default features; agpl-tools feature MAY surface AGPL-licensed optional code; bans: openssl-sys, native-tls, git2, libgit2-sys; minimum versions: ring >= 0.17.5, rustls >= 0.23
  - audit.toml: (rare; mostly relies on rustsec defaults) -- declare ignored advisories with a written justification per ignore
  - build/CHECKSUMS.sha256: a checked-in file mapping each build-time data file to its SHA-256
  - build.rs in pdftract-core: verify build/font-fingerprints.json and build/glyph-shapes.json checksums against build/CHECKSUMS.sha256; abort with a clear error pointing at the regeneration script on mismatch
  - Argo WorkflowTemplate or step in pdftract-cargo-build: run cargo audit -D warnings; run cargo deny check; verify the build.rs checksum gate via cargo build (which transitively runs build.rs)
  - Nightly cron Argo workflow: same checks against main
- Test cases (executable in a test crate or as a shell script run by CI):
  - cargo audit clean (no medium-or-above advisories on the current dep tree)
  - cargo deny check clean (license, ban, advisory subsets all pass)
  - tampering test: locally mutate one byte of build/font-fingerprints.json, run cargo build, assert build aborts with the documented error message
  - tampering test: same for build/glyph-shapes.json

## Critical considerations

- Cargo.lock for pdftract-core (library) is intentionally untracked so downstream consumers resolve their own deps (line 887) -- a CI test that checks-for-existence of Cargo.lock would WRONGLY flag pdftract-core; the test must be scoped per crate
- License allowlist: GPL/AGPL/LGPL "FORBIDDEN in default features" per line 889; the agpl-tools feature is the escape hatch; deny.toml must reflect both
- Banned crates list: openssl-sys, native-tls, git2, libgit2-sys -- the policy uses rustls instead of native TLS to keep cross-compilation simple
- Duplicate version policy: a duplicated major version produces a WARNING; a duplicated major across direct deps produces an ERROR per line 890
- The build.rs checksum gate is the supply-chain protection for build artifacts -- without it, a CI runner compromise could subtly alter the font fingerprint DB and produce wrong extraction results
- Renovate policy (line 892) is OUT OF SCOPE for this bead (it lives in the repo's renovate.json) but the bead should note that the gate is what catches the slipup if Renovate auto-merges a bad patch
- Quarterly cargo vendor snapshot to ardenone/declarative-config under build-mirrors/pdftract/<quarter>/ -- documented out-of-scope for this bead (it is an operational task, not a code gate)

## Acceptance criteria

- Cargo.lock files present in pdftract-cli/, pdftract-py/
- deny.toml with license allowlist + ban list + min-version requirements committed
- build/CHECKSUMS.sha256 committed and verified by build.rs
- cargo audit + cargo deny green in Phase 0 CI on every PR
- Nightly cron re-runs against main; opens a tracking issue on any new advisory
- Tampering test: mutating a build-time data file aborts the build
- Audit / deny configs explicitly model the forbidden-license + banned-crate policy from lines 889-890

## References

- Plan: line 877 (TH-06 entry), lines 883-896 (Supply Chain Considerations), Phase 0 CI gates
issue.title: TH-06 test: supply-chain gate (Cargo.lock + cargo audit + cargo deny + build/CHECKSUMS.sha256)

## Scope

Build the stream-decoder test corpus and integration tests:

1. **Curated fixtures** under `tests/stream_decoder/fixtures/`:
   - `flate_simple.bin` + `.expected` (raw deflate input + expected output)
   - `flate_png_pred15_all_six.bin` + `.expected` — PNG predictor 15 with all 6 selector values (10-15) appearing in one stream
   - `flate_tiff_pred2.bin` + `.expected` — TIFF predictor 2 on 8-bit RGB
   - `flate_truncated.bin` + `.expected` — mid-stream EOF; expects partial bytes + STREAM_DECODE_ERROR
   - `flate_bomb_3gb.bin` + `.expected` — 1 KB input expanding to 3 GB; expects ~2 GB + STREAM_BOMB
   - `lzw_early_change_0.bin` + `.expected` — qpdf-encoded with /EarlyChange 0
   - `lzw_early_change_1.bin` + `.expected` — default
   - `ascii85_z_shortcut.bin` + `.expected` — `z` shortcut + odd final group
   - `ascii85_terminator.bin` + `.expected` — bare `~>` ending
   - `asciihex_odd_length.bin` + `.expected` — `<48656C6C6>` -> b"Hello"-prefix + padded final byte
   - `runlength_basic.bin` + `.expected` — all three byte-value ranges (literal copy, repeat, EOD)
   - `dct_valid_jpeg.bin` + `.expected` — known JPEG file; expects byte-perfect passthrough + SOI marker check
   - `dct_missing_eoi.bin` + `.expected` — JPEG without EOI; expects passthrough + STREAM_INVALID_JPEG warning
   - `jbig2_passthrough.bin` + `.expected` — minimal JBIG2 file; expects passthrough + OCR_JBIG2_UNSUPPORTED (without full-render feature)
   - `crypt_identity.bin` + `.expected` — input passes through unchanged
   - `filter_array_a85_then_flate.bin` + `.expected` — input is ASCII85-encoded; after a85 decode, bytes are deflate-compressed; expects final decoded text
   - `unknown_filter.bin` + `.expected` — /Filter /SomeFakeFilter; expects STRUCT_UNKNOWN_FILTER + passthrough

2. **proptest harness** in `tests/proptest/stream_decoder.rs`:
   - `prop_filter_pipeline_never_panics`: arbitrary byte inputs to each filter
   - `prop_flate_roundtrip`: random bytes -> zlib-encode -> FlateDecode -> assert equal
   - `prop_a85_roundtrip`: random bytes -> ASCII85-encode -> ASCII85Decode -> assert equal
   - `prop_runlength_roundtrip`: similar
   - `prop_bomb_limit_enforced`: synthetic FlateDecode bombs of varying sizes; assert output capped at max_decompress_bytes

3. **Integration test runner**: walks fixtures, runs filter pipeline, compares against .expected, asserts diagnostics

## Why this matters

Stream decoding is the broadest attack surface in pdftract — every PDF has dozens or hundreds of compressed streams. The plan's Critical tests are non-negotiable; the proptest harness covers the long tail.

## Implementation guidance

- Fixture generation: use qpdf with `--object-streams=disable --decode-level=all` to extract raw stream bytes; or hand-craft via short Python scripts with the `zlib`, `Pillow`, `pdfminer.six` libraries
- The flate_bomb_3gb.bin fixture: zlib has the famous "zlib bomb" trick (RLE-style: 1 KB compresses to GB). Generate via `python -c "import zlib; print(zlib.compress(b'\\0' * (3 * 1024**3)))"` and trim to 1 KB
- The .expected files for binary outputs: store hex-encoded for readability OR as raw binary with a sibling .expected.sha256 hash
- The proptest_flate_roundtrip needs zlib-encode side; use the `flate2::write::ZlibEncoder` from the SAME crate to ensure symmetry
- The proptest budget for stream_decoder: ~5000 cases per property, ~30k total; runtime within Phase 0.5 budget
- Each fixture's .expected file uses a deterministic comparison: byte-equal for outputs, regex-match for diagnostic messages, exact match for diagnostic codes

## Critical considerations

- The flate_bomb_3gb.bin test must complete WITHIN 5 seconds despite the 3 GB expansion; the bomb limit triggers early
- Test all 6 PNG predictor selectors (10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15) in one stream — the plan's critical test requires this combinatorial coverage
- DCTDecode passthrough test asserts byte-EQUALITY, not size-only; any modification to the bytes is a regression
- The crypt_identity fixture verifies the /Identity passthrough path
- The unknown_filter test verifies graceful degradation: unknown filter = passthrough + diagnostic, NOT abort
- Filter array test (ASCII85 then Flate) verifies the orchestrator's iteration order; if the order reverses, the test fails immediately
- proptest_bomb_limit_enforced verifies the bomb limit works for STREAMS at varying sizes (10 MB, 100 MB, 1 GB, 3 GB expanding)
- Performance regression: each fixture's runtime should be < 100 ms (except bomb fixture which is < 5 sec); track via a CI bench step (Phase 0.7's bench-matrix may report stream-decoder benchmarks as a side metric)

## Acceptance criteria

- All 17 fixture files exist with sibling .expected goldens (binary or hash)
- `cargo test -p pdftract-core --features proptest -- stream_decoder` passes
- Each filter exercised by at least one fixture
- Each diagnostic code (STREAM_DECODE_ERROR, STREAM_BOMB, STRUCT_INVALID_*, OCR_*_UNSUPPORTED, ENCRYPTION_UNSUPPORTED) emitted by at least one fixture
- A deliberate regression in any filter (e.g. swapping predictor 11 and 12) is caught by the corresponding fixture
- The flate_bomb_3gb test runs in < 5 sec and produces ~2 GB of output + STREAM_BOMB
- proptest_filter_pipeline_never_panics: 5000 cases per filter per PR

issue.description:
## Scope

Parse the traditional PDF <=1.4 xref table starting from a given byte offset (the value from `startxref`). The table consists of one or more subsections, each prefixed by `obj_start obj_count`, followed by `obj_count` × 20-byte entries.

Format (PDF spec 7.5.4):
```
xref
0 6
0000000003 65535 f 
0000000017 00000 n 
0000000081 00000 n 
0000000000 00007 f 
0000000331 00000 n 
0000000409 00000 n 
trailer
<< /Size 6 /Root 1 0 R >>
startxref
492
%%EOF
```

Each entry is exactly 20 bytes:
- 10 digits: byte offset (for `n` entries) or next-free-object number (for `f` entries)
- 1 space
- 5 digits: generation number
- 1 space
- 1 byte: `n` (in use) or `f` (free)
- 2 bytes: line ending — `\r\n` or ` \n` (spec allows both; some buggy producers use `\n` alone)

## Implementation guidance

- Public API: `parse_traditional_xref(source: &PdfSource, start_offset: u64) -> XrefSection`
- Where `XrefSection { entries: HashMap<ObjRef, XrefEntry>, trailer: PdfDict }`
- And `XrefEntry::InUse { offset: u64, generation: u16 }` or `XrefEntry::Free { next_free: u32, generation: u16 }`
- Read bytes starting from `start_offset`; lex the `xref` keyword
- Loop: read `obj_start obj_count\n`, then read exactly `obj_count * 20` bytes; parse each as one entry
- Continue until the `trailer` keyword (signals end of all subsections)
- After `trailer`, parse the trailer dict via the object parser (Phase 1.2 parse_direct_object)

## Critical considerations

- Critical test from plan: PDF spec mandates ` \n` (space + LF) or `\r\n` (CR + LF) as the 20th-byte line ending. Some non-conformant producers emit `\n` alone, making entries 19 bytes. Detect this by trying both 19-byte and 20-byte stride; if neither works, fall through to forward scan
- The 10-digit offset can encode up to 9,999,999,999 bytes (~10 GB), enough for any real PDF
- Free entries (`f` flag): `next_free` is the object number of the next free object in the linked list, generation is the would-be-generation if the object slot is reused. pdftract IGNORES free entries (they don't add to the resolvable-objects map)
- Subsection boundaries: `0 6` (subsection starting at object 0, with 6 entries), then `100 3` (subsection at object 100, 3 entries). Subsections within ONE xref table do NOT override each other — they're disjoint by spec
- Multi-revision (cross-revision) overrides happen at the `/Prev` chain layer, NOT here
- A malformed line in the middle of a subsection: skip the line, emit STRUCT_INVALID_XREF_ENTRY, continue with the next 20 bytes (or 19 if the previous-line size determined that's the stride)
- The trailer dict's `/Size` field gives the total object count across all sections; can be used as a sanity check
- The very first entry (object 0) MUST be a free entry pointing to the head of the free list (typically `0000000000 65535 f`). Non-conformant files may violate this; emit STRUCT_INVALID_XREF and continue

## Acceptance criteria

- Simple test: well-formed single-subsection xref with 6 entries parsed correctly
- Multi-subsection test: xref with `0 3` then `100 2` produces 5 in-use entries with the right object numbers
- Line-ending variant tests: ` \n` and `\r\n` both work; `\n` alone is detected as 19-byte stride
- Malformed entry test: single bad line skipped, neighbors still parsed
- proptest: random byte sequences fed to parse_traditional_xref never panic
- INV-8 maintained

## References

- Plan section: Phase 1.3 line 1088 (traditional xref); critical test on `\r\n` vs ` \n` variants
- PDF spec 7.5.4 (Cross-Reference Table)
issue.title: Implement traditional xref table parser (20-byte fixed-width entries, multi-subsection merge)

issue.description:
## Scope

Detect and handle encrypted PDFs. The trailer dict's `/Encrypt` ObjRef points at an encryption dictionary that describes:

- `/Filter` — typically `/Standard` (the password-based handler); custom handlers (e.g. Adobe Public Key) are not supported
- `/V` — algorithm version: 1 (RC4 40-bit), 2 (RC4 40-128 bit), 4 (RC4 + AES-128 via crypt filters), 5 (AES-256, PDF 2.0)
- `/R` — revision: 2, 3, 4, 5, 6
- `/KeyLength` — key length in bits (40, 128, 256)
- `/O`, `/U` — owner/user password hashes for password validation
- `/CF`, `/StmF`, `/StrF` — crypt filter definitions and which one to use for streams vs strings (V=4, V=5)
- `/Perms` (V=5) — permissions bits (encrypted)

Password attempt sequence (per plan):
1. Empty string first
2. User-supplied via ExtractionOptions.password
3. On failure: emit ENCRYPTION_UNSUPPORTED, abort

## Implementation guidance

- Cargo features: `decrypt = ["dep:aes", "dep:rc4"]`; default-on per plan
- Crates: `aes` 0.8 (RustCrypto), `rc4` 0.1 (RustCrypto)
- Public API: `detect_encryption(trailer: &PdfDict, resolver: &XrefResolver) -> Option<EncryptionInfo>` + `derive_file_key(enc: &EncryptionInfo, password: &str) -> Option<Vec<u8>>`
- Algorithm per PDF spec 7.6:
  - V=1, R=2: RC4 with 40-bit key derived from password + /O + /P + first16(/ID[0])
  - V=2, R=3: RC4 with up to 128-bit key
  - V=4, R=4: RC4 or AES-128 via crypt filters; /StmF picks which for streams, /StrF for strings
  - V=5, R=5/6: AES-256 with SHA-256 / SHA-384 key derivation (R=6 adds extra hashing rounds for Spectre-style timing-attack resistance)
- Key derivation is THE most fragile part: tiny off-by-one errors produce wrong keys that silently decrypt to garbage. Cross-test against qpdf or pdfium decryption of the same input
- Decryption integration: once file key is derived, every stream content's decompression (Phase 1.5) prepends a decryption pass with the appropriate per-object key (object key = SHA1(file_key + obj_id + gen + salt)[0..16] for V=4; similar for V=5)
- Per-object key derivation: spec 7.6.2; salt is the literal bytes `b"sAlT"` for AES, no salt for RC4
- /Encrypt is GENERALLY a direct dict (not an indirect ref) per spec, but accept both

## Critical considerations

- Critical test from plan EC-04, EC-05, EC-06: RC4, AES-128, AES-256 fixtures all decrypt with user password "test"
- Critical test from plan: encrypted file with empty owner password decrypts successfully — verify the empty-string-first attempt
- Critical test from plan: encrypted file with UNKNOWN handler (e.g. Adobe Public Key Filter) -> ENCRYPTION_UNSUPPORTED, no crash
- Password sources by mode:
  - CLI: --password <PASSWORD>
  - Python: password=None keyword arg
  - HTTP form field: password
- The wrong-password case is detected by comparing the derived /U hash against the stored /U value (per spec algorithm). If mismatch: try owner password; if both fail: ENCRYPTION_UNSUPPORTED + abort
- AES requires PKCS#7 padding on decryption; the trailing padding bytes are NOT part of the decoded content
- AES uses CBC mode with a 16-byte IV PREPENDED to each ciphertext stream; the decryptor must strip the IV before passing to AES-CBC
- The /ID array (PDF spec 14.4) is REQUIRED for encrypted files; missing /ID makes key derivation impossible. Emit ENCRYPTION_UNSUPPORTED with "missing /ID" reason
- INV-8: never panic. Wrong password is a normal error, not a panic
- decrypt feature is default-on — the `cargo bloat` budget (Phase 0.4) must account for aes+rc4 (~80 KB total). If budget pressure: gate decrypt off in future PB

## Acceptance criteria

- EC-04 fixture (RC4-encrypted, user password "test"): decrypts to known plaintext content streams
- EC-05 fixture (AES-128): decrypts
- EC-06 fixture (AES-256, PDF 2.0): decrypts
- Empty-password fixture: decrypts without --password flag
- Wrong-password attempt: ENCRYPTION_UNSUPPORTED diagnostic; exit code 3 (per CLI exit-code spec)
- Unknown-handler fixture: ENCRYPTION_UNSUPPORTED; no crash
- proptest: random byte sequences as /Encrypt dict never panic
- Performance: decryption of 100-page encrypted PDF completes within 10% slowdown vs unencrypted

## References

- Plan section: Phase 1.4 line 1114 (encryption dictionary, RC4/AES-128/256 via aes+rc4 crates, decrypt feature default-on, password attempt sequence)
- EC-04, EC-05, EC-06 (encrypted variants)
- PDF spec 7.6 (Encryption)
- Dependency Matrix: aes, rc4 (decrypt feature)
- ExtractionOptions.password
- INV-8

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the --compare OTHER.pdf flag for pdftract inspect. When provided, the inspector loads both A and B documents into memory, renders both pages side-by-side in the main canvas (page N of A on left, page N of B on right), and adds a "Diff" overlay layer that visually marks blocks/spans that differ between A and B. Used for verifying that extraction-algorithm changes don't regress output.

## Why this matters

When pdftract developers tweak the column-detection heuristic, the reading-order algorithm, or the OCR threshold, they need to SEE which documents change and HOW. Comparison mode is the regression-test visual aid: load the same PDF before and after a change, scroll page-by-page, and spot the differences. This is what unblocks confident iteration on the heuristic-heavy parts of the pipeline (Phase 4.5 reading order, Phase 5 OCR thresholds).

## Implementation guidance

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the `/Prev` chain walker that handles incremental updates. When a PDF is edited by an application (e.g. annotation added), the editor appends a new xref + trailer at the end of the file rather than rewriting the whole document. The new trailer's `/Prev <offset>` points to the PREVIOUS xref's offset. Multiple edits create a chain.

The chain walker:
1. Loads the trailing xref (whatever strategy parses it: traditional / stream / hybrid)
2. If trailer has `/Prev`, recursively loads the previous xref from that offset
3. Merges: for each ObjRef, the entry from the LATER revision (loaded first) wins
4. Continues until a trailer with no `/Prev` (the original/baseline revision)

## Implementation guidance

- Public API: `load_xref_with_prev_chain(source: &PdfSource, start_offset: u64) -> XrefSection`
- Algorithm:
  1. Load xref at `start_offset` (auto-detect traditional vs stream)
  2. If hybrid (has /XRefStm), call hybrid merger
  3. Record trailer's `/Prev` offset if present
  4. Recursively call `load_xref_with_prev_chain(source, prev_offset)`
  5. Merge: start with the result of the recursive call (older revisions), OVERWRITE with the current revision's entries (newer wins)
- Cycle detection: maintain `HashSet<u64>` of visited offsets; if `start_offset` is already in the set, emit STRUCT_CIRCULAR_REF and stop the chain (return only the current revision's xref)
- Depth limit: 32 revisions max; emit STRUCT_DEPTH_EXCEEDED on deeper chains (adversarial input)

## Critical considerations

- Critical test from plan: PDF with /Prev chain of 3 revisions — latest value of each object number wins. Verify the merge semantics: revision 3 (latest) overrides revision 2 overrides revision 1
- The trailer dict returned by the chain MUST be the LATEST revision's trailer (newest /Root, /Info, /ID). Do not merge trailer dicts
- /Prev offset of 0 typically means "no previous revision" but some buggy producers emit 0 as a meaningless value. Treat /Prev <= 0 as absent
- /Prev pointing to an offset > file size: emit STRUCT_INVALID_PREV_OFFSET, ignore the /Prev key, treat as end-of-chain
- /Prev cycle (revision A points to B points to A): cycle detection catches it; chain breaks at the cycle, all revisions visited so far are merged
- Performance: each /Prev load is independent; cannot parallelize trivially because each level requires the trailer of the previous level. Worst case: 32 levels × ~100 ms each = 3.2 sec; acceptable
- Linearized files have /Prev too, but it points within the file (not to a prior version) — the linearization handler treats it specially
- Hybrid files: each revision in the /Prev chain may itself be hybrid; the hybrid merger is invoked at each level before chain-merge

## Acceptance criteria

- Critical test passes: 3-revision chain — object 5 appears in all 3 revisions; the LATEST value is the one in the final map; older two values are not retrievable
- Object 7 added in revision 2, modified in revision 3, freed in revision 4 (4 levels) — final map shows object 7 as free
- Object added in revision 3 only — final map has it
- Trailer of the final map matches the latest revision's trailer (verify /Root pointer)
- /Prev cycle test (A->B->A): STRUCT_CIRCULAR_REF emitted, chain breaks
- Depth-50 chain: STRUCT_DEPTH_EXCEEDED at depth 32, only first 32 revisions merged
- proptest: random /Prev configurations never panic
- INV-8 maintained

## References

- Plan section: Phase 1.3 line 1093 (/Prev chain); critical test on 3-revision override
- PDF spec 7.5.6 (Incremental Updates)
issue.title: Implement incremental update chain handler (/Prev recursive load, override semantics, depth limit)

## Scope

Author profiles/builtin/scientific_paper.yaml per the Phase 7.10 YAML schema, plus at least 5 PDF fixtures at tests/fixtures/profiles/scientific_paper/ each with a sibling expected-output.json, plus tests/profiles/test_scientific_paper.rs that asserts exact-match of metadata.profile_fields.
