The scientific_paper profile ships in v1.0.0 as one of the nine built-ins (line 3042). This is the highest-volume document type for academic-tooling integrations (reference managers, citation tools, summarization workflows); extracting title, authors, abstract, doi, journal, publication_date, references correctly is the user-visible value.

## Implementation guidance

- File: profiles/builtin/scientific_paper.yaml
  - name: scientific_paper
  - description: "Academic papers from arXiv, journals, conference proceedings"
  - priority: 30
  - match: all: [any: [text_contains: ['Abstract', 'References', 'doi:', 'arXiv:', 'Bibliography'], heading_matches: '^(Abstract|Introduction|References|Bibliography)'], structural.has_math: true OR structural.heading_depth: {min: 2}, structural.page_count: {min: 4, max: 50}]
  - extraction: reading_order: xy_cut (handles 2-column layout); readability_threshold: 0.5; include_invisible: false
  - fields: title (region: top_quarter, pick: largest_font), authors (region: top_quarter, pick: nearest_below; after title), abstract (near: ['Abstract'], region: top_half), doi (regex: 'doi[:\.]\s*(10\.\d{4,9}/[\w\-\._;()/:]+)', parse: string), journal (region: top_eighth; pick: first), publication_date (near: ['Published', 'Received', 'Accepted'], parse: date), references (region: bottom_half; structured list extraction from 'References' heading to end)
- Fixtures: 5 papers covering: arXiv (CC-BY), PLOS ONE, IEEE-style 2-column, Nature-style single-column with sidebar, conference proceedings (ACM/IEEE)

## Critical considerations

- 2-column layout is the dominant scientific paper layout -- reading_order: xy_cut MUST handle this; document the failure mode if a paper uses an unusual layout (e.g. 3-column)
- Title extraction via 'pick: largest_font' fails when the title font is the same size as section headings; document the limitation
- DOI regex MUST match the canonical doi.org form (10.NNNN/...) but be tolerant of leading "doi:" / "DOI:" / "https://doi.org/" / "https://dx.doi.org/" prefixes
- Authors extraction is the hardest field -- handles "Lastname, F." vs "Firstname Lastname" vs "F. Lastname" formats; first-pass implementation should capture the verbatim author block and let downstream parsing handle name decomposition
- References extraction is BEST-EFFORT at v1.0; full reference parsing (separating each reference into structured fields) is out of scope -- ship as a single text block
- Math equations and formulas are handled by Phase 7 OpenType Math (cross-reference docs/research/opentype-math-and-formula-extraction.md); the structural.has_math signal must work for this profile to win against book_chapter
- arXiv-specific: paper IDs (arXiv:2401.12345) should be extracted as a separate field if present (consider adding arxiv_id to v1.1)
- Fixture diversity: cover both LaTeX-source PDFs and Word-source PDFs

- profiles/builtin/scientific_paper.yaml validates
- 5+ fixtures with expected outputs
- tests/profiles/test_scientific_paper.rs passes
- Per-field accuracy: >= 90% on the 5-fixture corpus
- The 50-paper subset of the classifier corpus achieves precision/recall >= 0.85

issue.description:
## Scope

Author the `pdftract-build-binaries` WorkflowTemplate at `k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/pdftract-build-binaries.yaml` (in `jedarden/declarative-config`). Triggered by milestone tag (`vX.Y.Z`). Produces 10 binary archives: 5 target triples × 2 feature variants (`default` and `full`). Each archive contains stripped binary, both LICENSE files, README, and CHANGELOG excerpt. Archives are uploaded as Argo artifacts so `pdftract-github-release` can attach them to the GitHub Release.

## Why this matters

This is the per-tag build workhorse. Every binary on every channel (GitHub Release, binstall, Homebrew formula, vcpkg) originates from this template. If it is flaky the entire release cascade is non-deterministic.

## Implementation guidance

- 5 target triples: `x86_64-unknown-linux-musl`, `aarch64-unknown-linux-musl`, `x86_64-apple-darwin`, `aarch64-apple-darwin`, `x86_64-pc-windows-gnu`
- 2 feature variants: `default` and `full`
- Use a 10-item `withItems:` DAG matrix; each item is `{triple, features}`
- Build container: `rustembedded/cross` per triple (same images Phase 0.2 uses); osxcross SDK mounted from ESO `osxcross-sdk` Secret
- Build command: `cross build --release --target {{item.triple}} --features {{item.features}} --locked --frozen`
- Strip with target-appropriate strip (musl-strip, osxcross strip, mingw strip)
- Set `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` from the tag commit so output is reproducible across reruns
- Package layout inside archive:
  ```
  pdftract-vX.Y.Z-<triple>/
  pdftract            (or pdftract.exe on Windows)
  LICENSE-MIT
  LICENSE-APACHE
  README.md
  CHANGELOG.md        (only the section for this version)
  ```
- Archive format: `.tar.gz` for Unix triples, `.zip` for `x86_64-pc-windows-gnu`
- Archive name: `pdftract-vX.Y.Z-<triple>.tar.gz` (default) or `pdftract-full-vX.Y.Z-<triple>.tar.gz` (full features)
- Upload each archive as a named Argo artifact for the downstream `pdftract-github-release` template to consume

## Critical considerations

- ADR-009: this runs on the iad-ci cluster ONLY; never use GitHub Actions
- KU-12: macOS and Windows binaries are BUILT but never RUN in CI; this template delivers build only — runtime validation is the manual smoke runbook
- The 10-build matrix runs in parallel; `continueOn: failed` so one triple failure does not block the other nine artifacts
- All cargo invocations MUST pass `--locked --frozen` (see Cargo.lock policy bead)
- Stripped `x86_64-unknown-linux-musl` binary <= 4 MB (gated by Phase 0.4 cargo bloat; should already pass here)
- The CHANGELOG excerpt extraction is non-trivial: a small script parses `CHANGELOG.md` for the section under `## [X.Y.Z]` heading and writes it as `CHANGELOG.md` inside the archive
- Cross-compile macOS without an Apple-issued SDK requires `osxcross` with a stored SDK tarball in OpenBao -> ESO -> Secret -> volume mount (Secret name `osxcross-sdk` in the argo-workflows namespace)
- Retry on partial output: `argo retry` on the failed matrix items only; do not re-execute green items

## Acceptance criteria

- WorkflowTemplate file lands at the path above in jedarden/declarative-config
- ArgoCD reconciles the template into the argo-workflows namespace on iad-ci
- A test workflow submitted against a sample tag produces 10 archives uploaded as artifacts
- Two consecutive runs against the same tag produce byte-identical archives (reproducibility check)
- A failure in any single triple does NOT cancel the other nine
- Wall-clock <= 12 min for the slowest variant (Apple Darwin aarch64 + full features)

## References

- Plan section: Release Engineering / Argo WorkflowTemplates, line 3389
- Plan section: Artifact Taxonomy, lines 3349-3350 (the 10 binary archives)
- Sibling: pdftract-1bn (Phase 0.2 build matrix establishes the per-triple build steps); this template extends it with the second `full`-features variant and the archive packaging step
- ADR-009 (Argo-only CI), KU-12 (manual macOS/Windows runtime check)
issue.title: Argo WorkflowTemplate: pdftract-build-binaries (10 archives = 5 triples × 2 feature variants)

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the five signal evaluators that feed PageClassifier::classify. Each evaluator is a pure function over a PageContext (Phase 1 content-stream operator inventory + Phase 4 char stats) returning a Signal { name: &'static str, strength: f32, vote: PageClass }. Evaluators run in declared order with short-circuit at strength > 0.95.

## Why this matters

Signals are how classification produces confidence. They are also the locus of reproducibility: every signal must be deterministic for the same input. The Phase 5.1 critical-test fixtures (pure-text PDF, scanned single-page, PDF/A invisible-text, hybrid) are essentially tests on the signal evaluators wired together.

## Implementation guidance

- Evaluator order (short-circuit when strength > 0.95):
  1. text_operator_presence: 0 text ops + has images -> Scanned 0.95
  2. all_tr3_with_full_page_image: every text op has Tr=3 AND a single image XObject covers >= 95% of page area -> BrokenVector 0.99 (definitive)
  3. image_coverage_fraction > 0.85 -> Scanned 0.85
  4. char_validity_rate < 0.4 (4.7 readability score) -> BrokenVector 0.80
  5. char_validity_rate > 0.85 -> Vector 0.90
  6. char_density_ratio < 0.03 chars/in^2 -> Scanned 0.65
- PageContext fields needed (defined in 5.1.1): text_op_count, tr3_op_count, total_op_count, image_xobject_areas, page_area_pt2, char_validity_rate (from 4.7), char_count, char_density_pt2
- Each evaluator is in its own free function and unit-tested in isolation

## Critical considerations

- Cite EC-12 (Tr=3 + full-page-image is a deterministic BrokenVector signal)
- char_validity_rate signal MUST be optional (None if Phase 4.7 has not run on the page yet); evaluator returns None
- image_coverage_fraction must clamp to [0,1] even if image XObjects overlap (use page-area projection)
- All thresholds are constants in a single SIGNALS_CONFIG struct so they are tweakable in one place (and so EC-12 + fixture expectations stay in sync)

## Acceptance criteria

- Unit test each evaluator individually with synthetic PageContext values straddling thresholds
- Integration test: PageClassifier wired with all evaluators classifies the four fixture PDFs correctly with confidence in expected ranges
- Determinism: rerun classifier on same PageContext -> identical Signal vector

## References

- Plan section: Phase 5.1 Signals table (lines 1813-1821)
- EC-12 Tr=3 + full-page-image

issue.description:
## Scope

For each input PDF that has at least one match, write a copy to DIR/<basename>-highlighted.pdf with /Highlight annotations added to each match's page. Highlight annotations use yellow color, /Subtype /Highlight, /QuadPoints derived from the match bbox (4 corner points per quad: bottom-left, bottom-right, top-left, top-right). The original content stream is NOT modified; only the /Annots array is amended. Output is a valid PDF that opens in Acrobat, Preview, Chrome PDF viewer, Firefox, and Safari.

## Why this matters

The annotated-output feature is the single highest-impact differentiator of pdftract grep vs. competitors. Users get a one-click visual answer to "where in this contract is the indemnification clause?" - opening the highlighted PDF reveals the answers immediately. Non-destructive editing (annotations only, content stream intact) ensures the original PDF semantics are preserved exactly.

## Implementation guidance

- Crates: reuse Phase 1 PDF object writer (PDF cross-ref + object emission) - if not present, this task includes building a minimal incremental-update writer
- Strategy: incremental update (PDF 1.7 7.5.6): append a new xref + trailer at end of original file, with updated page objects whose /Annots array gains the new /Highlight refs
- For each match on page P:
  - Annotation dict: { Type: /Annot, Subtype: /Highlight, Rect: [x0,y0,x1,y1] from match.bbox, QuadPoints: [x0,y0, x1,y0, x0,y1, x1,y1] (4 quad corners), C: [1.0, 1.0, 0.0] (yellow RGB), F: 4 (Print flag), CA: 0.4 (opacity), T: "pdftract grep" (author), Contents: match.match_text }
- Group annotations by (input_path, page_index); one write per input file
- Output filename: DIR + "/" + input_basename.replace(".pdf", "-highlighted.pdf"); collisions append "-1", "-2" suffix
- DIR creation: mkdir -p before writing
- Original file unmodified - copy first, then incremental-update the copy (or use incremental write directly to a new file)
- After write, verify the output opens (re-parse via Phase 1 + count /Highlight annots match expected count)
- Performance: highlight write should add < 100 ms per file even with 100 matches

## Critical considerations

- /QuadPoints order: spec says BL, BR, TR, TL but many viewers accept BL, BR, TL, TR - use the spec order: [x0,y0, x1,y0, x1,y1, x0,y1] (BL, BR, TR, TL); each quad is 8 floats
- Multiple matches on same page: emit multiple separate Highlight annotations (one per match) for granularity
- Original content stream untouched - INV
- Incremental update preserves original xref; downstream tools can still recover the original by truncating to original size
- Encrypted PDFs: skip --highlight emission (cannot incrementally update without re-encryption); emit diagnostic
- Output validity: Acrobat, Preview, Chrome, Firefox, Safari all must render the highlights; CI test via headless Chrome screenshot diff
- DIR write race: each worker creates its output independently; no shared writer

## Acceptance criteria

- Critical test (from plan): annotated PDFs round-trip through pdftract extract; highlights render in Chrome's built-in PDF viewer (verified via headless-browser screenshot)
- /Highlight annotation count in output matches MatchEvent count
- Original PDF byte-identical to input (compare bytes of first N bytes of output prefix vs. original)
- Incremental-update structure verified by xref-table inspection
- Encrypted PDFs skipped with diagnostic
- DIR auto-created via mkdir -p
- Output filename collision handled with -1/-2 suffix

## References

- Plan section: 7.8 lines 2725 (--highlight DIR flag), 2747-2751 (annotated output details), 2791 (acceptance criterion)
- PDF 1.7 spec 7.5.6 Incremental Updates, 12.5.6.10 Highlight Annotations
- 7.8.4 (MatchEvent input)
- 7.6 (Annotation read pipeline; complementary)
- INV: --highlight non-destructive

issue.description:
## Scope

Compute a reproducible 256-bit content hash that identifies the SEMANTIC content of a PDF independent of metadata churn, byte ordering, and producer-tool re-saves. The fingerprint is exposed in JSON output (`metadata.pdf_fingerprint`), via the `pdftract hash` CLI subcommand, and is the cache key for Phase 6.9 (content-addressed cache) and the binding identity in Phase 6.8 receipts.

Child beads:
- Fingerprint algorithm implementation (Merkle-style SHA-256 over canonicalized inputs)
- `pdftract hash` CLI subcommand
- Per-page input canonicalization (geometry rounding, resource dict hash, content stream hash)
- Fingerprint reproducibility test corpus (re-saves, linearization toggle, metadata-only edits, content edits)

## Why this matters

The fingerprint is the binding identity in three downstream features:
- Phase 6.8 receipts: when verifying a receipt, the fingerprint of the PDF being verified must match the fingerprint stored in the receipt
- Phase 6.9 cache: cache key for extraction results; identical PDFs (modulo metadata) hit the same cache entry
- `pdftract hash` CLI: users can identify "is this the same PDF I extracted last week, regardless of producer re-save" via a single command

If the fingerprint were sensitive to metadata churn (e.g. /Producer or /CreationDate), the cache hit rate would collapse and receipts would mis-verify across re-saves.

## Critical considerations

Inputs to the hash (Merkle-style, DETERMINISTIC order):
1. Page count (u32, big-endian)
2. Per page in page_index order:
   a. SHA-256 of each decoded content stream (Phase 1.5 output), concatenated in stream-array order
   b. SHA-256 of the resolved resource dict
   c. Page geometry: MediaBox, CropBox, Rotate — canonicalized to 4-decimal-place fixed-point integers (× 10⁴, rounded half-to-even)
3. SHA-256 of the structure tree if is_tagged; the all-zero hash otherwise
4. Catalog feature flag byte: is_encrypted | contains_javascript << 1 | contains_xfa << 2 | ocg_present << 3

Inputs DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED (per ADR-008):
- /Producer, /Creator, /CreationDate, /ModDate, /Author, /Title, /Subject, /Keywords
- /ID array (varies per save even for byte-identical content)
- XMP metadata stream (/Metadata)
- xref byte layout and object number assignment
- Inline whitespace in content streams (lexer-normalized before hashing)

Output format: Lowercase hex SHA-256 prefixed with the algorithm version, e.g. `pdftract-v1:a7f3...` (INV-13).

CLI:
- `pdftract hash FILE.pdf` prints `pdftract-v1:<hex>\n` to stdout
- Exit codes: 0 success, 2 corrupt, 3 encrypted-no-password, 4 cannot read path/URL, 5 network failure mid-extraction, 6 TLS handshake failure

Acceptance criteria (CI-gated):
- Reproducibility: identical input -> byte-identical fingerprint across 100 invocations
- Same PDF re-saved by Acrobat, pdftk, or QPDF: identical fingerprint
- Same PDF with metadata changes only: identical fingerprint
- One paragraph edited: fingerprint differs

## Acceptance criteria (for the sub-phase coordinator)

- All 4 child beads closed
- Algorithm v1 stable and documented in `crates/pdftract-core/src/fingerprint/algorithm.md`
- All 5 Critical tests from plan Section 1.7 pass (Acrobat+pdftk same, CreationDate-only same, glyph-removed differ, 10-invocation identical, linearized vs non-linearized same per KU-7)
- INV-3 (byte-stable across runs) verified by 100-invocation test
- INV-13 (version prefix on every emission) verified by regex match

## References

- Plan section: Phase 1.7 PDF Structural Fingerprint, lines 1182-1219
- ADR-008 (fingerprint excludes /Producer, /CreationDate, XMP, /ID)
- INV-3, INV-13
- KU-7 (linearization toggle test)
- Phase 6.8 (receipts), Phase 6.9 (cache)
issue.title: Phase 1.7: PDF Structural Fingerprint — reproducible 256-bit content hash

## Scope

Create the stub `pdftract-py-ci` Argo WorkflowTemplate YAML at `jedarden/declarative-config -> k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/pdftract-py-ci.yaml`. The template's DAG structure mirrors the eventual wheel-build pipeline (one step per target triple, plus an upload step) but every step is a placeholder `exit 0` script. Phase 6.3 implementation replaces the script bodies with actual maturin invocations.

## Why this matters

The plan explicitly requires the stub template to exist in Phase 0 so that the CI infrastructure is fully provisioned before Phase 1 begins, even though the wheel-build logic isn't ready until Phase 6.3. Without this stub, the eventual Phase 6.3 work would need to also include Argo template provisioning, conflating two distinct deliverables (CI infra vs Python wheel logic). The stub also exercises the declarative-config -> ArgoCD sync path for the second template so any operator issues are surfaced now.

## Implementation guidance

- File location: `k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/pdftract-py-ci.yaml`
- DAG structure (each step is `image: busybox:1.36 command: [sh, -c, "exit 0"]`):
  - `setup` (placeholder for git clone + maturin install)
  - `wheel-linux-x86_64` (placeholder for ghcr.io/rust-cross/manylinux build)
  - `wheel-linux-aarch64` (placeholder)
  - `wheel-darwin-x86_64` (placeholder for osxcross build)
  - `wheel-darwin-aarch64` (placeholder)
  - `wheel-windows-x86_64` (placeholder for cross with mingw build)
  - `publish-pypi` (placeholder for `twine upload --repository pypi`)
- Trigger: same webhook as pdftract-ci but only fires on milestone tags matching `v*.*.*` (NOT every PR — wheel builds are expensive)
- Per-step placeholder must include a comment `# TODO(Phase 6.3): real maturin invocation here` so the stub is unmistakably a stub
- `serviceAccount: argo-workflow`, `imagePullSecrets: [docker-hub]`, `podGC: OnPodCompletion`, semaphore for parallelism limit (4 concurrent wheel builds)
- Top of YAML: header comment block documenting Phase 6.3 ownership

## Critical considerations

- Stub must be syntactically valid and ArgoCD-sync clean; otherwise the iad-ci namespace's app shows Degraded and blocks other Phase 0 deliverables
- Stub must NOT publish anything to PyPI — even an empty wheel — because the PyPI token in `argo-workflows/pypi-token` Secret is live and uploading a 0-byte `pdftract-0.0.0.dev0.whl` would burn a PyPI version number that pdftract may want for the real v0.1.0
- The placeholder `exit 0` is intentional; do NOT use `exit 1` to mark "TODO" — that would mark the workflow Failed and trip the iad-ci app monitor
- Reference Phase 6.3 epic explicitly so the eventual fill-in work is traceable

## Acceptance criteria

- `pdftract-py-ci.yaml` exists in declarative-config and ArgoCD-syncs Healthy
- A manually-submitted workflow from the template completes Succeeded within 60 s (all steps exit 0)
- `argo template lint` passes with no warnings
- Stub clearly identifies itself as a Phase 6.3 placeholder via the header comment and per-step `# TODO(Phase 6.3)` comments
- WorkflowTemplate appears in `kubectl get workflowtemplates -n argo-workflows`

## References

- Plan section: Phase 0, line 1009-1011 (pdftract-py-ci stub requirement)
- Phase 6.3 (Python bindings) — owns the eventual implementation

issue.description:
## Scope

Coordinator for sub-phase 2.5: build the visual-pHash-to-character lookup table that backs Level 4 shape recognition. Includes (a) an offline pipeline that rasterizes ~5000 glyphs from open-source fonts, computes pHash for each, and emits `build/glyph-shapes.json`; (b) a build.rs static emitter that produces a `&'static [(u64, char)]` sorted by pHash; (c) a runtime nearest-neighbor scanner over Hamming distance with a frequency-rank tie-breaker.

## Why this matters

Level 4 shape recognition is what separates pdftract from pdfminer/pypdf on the long tail of broken PDFs. Every "PDF embeds a subset font with no glyph names and no ToUnicode" case routes here, and the difference between U+FFFD and recognized text is the difference between a usable extract and trash. 5000 entries cover Latin/Greek/Cyrillic/symbols at ~99% of real-world glyph frequency.

## Children

- pHash implementation (32x32 DCT, 8x8 AC top-left, median threshold -> u64)
- Offline glyph rendering + pHash pipeline (cargo xtask)
- build.rs emitter for sorted `&'static [(u64, char)]` table
- Runtime nearest-neighbor scanner with Hamming distance + frequency tie-break
- Source corpus selection script (Google Fonts / SIL OFL fonts)

## Critical considerations

- INV: phf::Map cannot be used (nearest-neighbor needs scan); use sorted slice.
- pHash false-positive rate goes up sharply for Hamming threshold > 8; default = 8, configurable.
- Ties broken by Unicode frequency rank stored in a companion `&'static [(u64, u32)]` table (parallel to the main table by pHash).
- Binary footprint target: ~300 KB combined. CI gate via `cargo bloat --release --crates`.
- Linear scan over 5000 entries x 8ns/popcount = ~40 us worst case — well within the per-page budget.

## Acceptance criteria

- All 5 children closed.
- A rasterized lowercase 'a' produces a pHash that matches the 'a' entry in the DB at Hamming distance 0.
- A rasterized italic 'a' matches 'a' in the DB at Hamming distance <= 8.
- A rasterized random doodle pHash returns no match (no entry within Hamming 8).
- Binary footprint < 300 KB for the two tables combined.
- Lookup time < 50 us on a 5000-entry table (criterion benchmark).

## References

- Plan section: Phase 2.5 Glyph Shape Database (lines 1416-1428)
- docs/research/glyph-recognition-and-unicode-recovery.md

issue.description:
## Scope

Author the `pdftract-py-ci` WorkflowTemplate. Produces 5 platform wheels (one per target triple) plus 1 source distribution (sdist) for the `pdftract` PyPI package. Uses `maturin` to build the PyO3 binding from `crates/pdftract-py`. Wheels are `abi3`-tagged (cp311-abi3) for forward compatibility across Python minor versions.

## Why this matters

PyPI is the highest-traffic distribution channel by an order of magnitude. The Python-binding bead (Phase 6.3 in the plan) implements the native module; this template wraps it in the publishing pipeline. abi3 wheels means one wheel per platform serves Python 3.11+ instead of one wheel per (platform × Python minor version) — cutting the matrix by 4x.

## Implementation guidance

- 5 platform wheels: `manylinux_2_28_x86_64`, `manylinux_2_28_aarch64`, `macosx_11_0_x86_64`, `macosx_11_0_arm64`, `win_amd64`
- Build container: `quay.io/pypa/manylinux_2_28_x86_64` for Linux x86_64; `messense/manylinux_2_28-cross:aarch64` for Linux aarch64; `messense/maturin-action` Docker patterns for macOS (osxcross) and Windows (cross-rs)
- Use `maturin build --release --features default --target <triple> --strip --interpreter python3.11 --abi3`
- The wheel naming will be `pdftract-X.Y.Z-cp311-abi3-<platform_tag>.whl`
- sdist built once with `maturin sdist`
- Twine upload step: `twine upload --skip-existing dist/*` using the PyPI token from ESO Secret `pypi-token-pdftract` (synced from OpenBao key `pypi-token-pdftract`)
- Trigger: milestone tag (`vX.Y.Z`); re-runnable but PyPI rejects duplicates so re-runs only upload missing platforms
- All 5 wheel builds run in parallel under a `withItems:` matrix; failure of one platform does NOT block uploads of the four others
- The sdist build runs as a separate DAG node; it requires `pyproject.toml` to declare `build-backend = "maturin"`

## Critical considerations

- ADR-009: NO OIDC trusted-publisher (that is a GitHub Actions exclusive feature). Use PyPI API token, full stop
- The token-rotation runbook lives in `docs/operations/secrets-rotation.md`: rotate every 90 days, update OpenBao, ESO auto-syncs within 60 s
- `manylinux_2_28` is the current PEP 600 manylinux baseline; older PEPs (manylinux2014, manylinux_2_17) are accepted by pip but produce smaller compatibility envelopes — `2_28` is the project's lower bound
- abi3 means the wheel is forward-compatible with Python 3.11, 3.12, 3.13 etc. — one wheel per platform per Python MAJOR; we never have to ship a per-minor-version wheel
- musl wheel target is NOT included in v0.X; on Alpine the user must use the sdist or wait for v1.1+ when `musllinux_1_2` wheels are added
- Pre-release artefacts (`vX.Y.Z-rc.N`) publish to PyPI's pre-release channel — `pip install pdftract` does NOT pick them up; `pip install pdftract==X.Y.Z-rc.N` is required

## Acceptance criteria

- WorkflowTemplate file lands at `k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/pdftract-py-ci.yaml` in `jedarden/declarative-config`
- A test workflow against a sample tag produces 5 wheel artifacts + 1 sdist in Argo
- The `twine upload` step succeeds with the ESO-provided token
- `pip install pdftract` on a clean machine (Linux glibc, macOS, Windows) installs the appropriate platform wheel
- A failed channel publish (e.g. PyPI 5xx) does NOT cancel the other matrix items
- Two consecutive runs of the same tag are idempotent (twine `--skip-existing` returns 0)

## References

- Plan section: Release Engineering / Argo WorkflowTemplates, line 3390
- Plan section: Artifact Taxonomy, lines 3355-3356 (5 wheels + 1 sdist)
- ADR-009 (PyPI must use token auth on iad-ci, not GitHub OIDC trusted publisher)
- Phase 6.3 (the underlying PyO3 binding) provides the cdylib that maturin packages
- maturin docs: https://www.maturin.rs/
issue.title: Argo WorkflowTemplate: pdftract-py-ci (5 wheels + sdist for PyPI)

issue.description:
## Scope

Enforce at CLI parse time that exactly one transport (stdio or HTTP+SSE) is selected for a given pdftract mcp invocation. Two-transport invocation is rejected with a clear error before any I/O happens. Per ADR-006: stdio and HTTP transports cannot coexist in one process because they have opposite stdout discipline (stdio: JSON-RPC sink; HTTP: log channel).

Module: crates/pdftract-cli/src/mcp/cli.rs (or extend the clap derive macros on the existing McpArgs struct).

## Why this matters

Running both transports in a single process would create dual stdout ownership: stdio mode writes JSON-RPC frames to stdout, while HTTP mode emits log lines there. The two streams would interleave, corrupting both the JSON-RPC stream (breaking agent clients) and the log output (breaking observability). The cleanest fix is a hard CLI-parse-time constraint: a single pdftract mcp invocation may specify --stdio XOR --bind ADDR; not both, not neither (default --stdio).

Deferring this check to runtime (e.g. at transport startup) leaves a window where partially-initialized transports race; rejecting at clap parse time is the cleanest contract.

## Implementation guidance

- Use clap's ArgGroup with multiple(false) to enforce that --stdio and --bind are mutually exclusive. The default behavior is --stdio if neither is given.
- McpArgs struct:
  ```rust
  #[derive(Args)]
  #[command(group(ArgGroup::new(\"transport\").required(false).multiple(false).args([\"stdio\", \"bind\"])))]
  pub struct McpArgs {
      #[arg(long)]
      pub stdio: bool,
      #[arg(long, value_name = \"ADDR\")]
      pub bind: Option<SocketAddr>,
      // ... auth_token, root, no_log_paths, etc.
  }
  ```
- Post-parse normalization: if neither --stdio nor --bind set, treat as --stdio = true (default)
- Reject pdftract mcp --stdio --bind 127.0.0.1:8080 at parse time with: \"error: the argument '--stdio' cannot be used with '--bind <ADDR>'\"
- Help text on pdftract mcp --help explicitly notes the mutual exclusivity and the rationale (one sentence)

## Critical considerations

- ADR-006 records the rationale; reference it in the doc comment on McpArgs so future maintainers don't try to relax this
- Don't accept --stdio --bind via env vars either; clap's ArgGroup covers CLI but env-var conflicts must be detected manually if pdftract supports MCP_STDIO=1 or similar
- The default-to-stdio behavior is per plan section 6.7 line 2290: \"if neither is given, --stdio is the default\"
- The clap error format is standard (exit code 2); no special handling needed

## Acceptance criteria

- pdftract mcp → launches in stdio mode (default)
- pdftract mcp --stdio → launches in stdio mode
- pdftract mcp --bind 127.0.0.1:8080 → launches in HTTP+SSE mode
- pdftract mcp --stdio --bind 127.0.0.1:8080 → exits 2 with clap conflict error mentioning both flags
- pdftract mcp --help shows both flags grouped under \"Transport (mutually exclusive)\" with a brief explanatory note
- Unit test that constructs the McpArgs Command via clap derive and asserts the ArgGroup conflict on dual-transport invocation

## References

- Plan section: Phase 6.7 MCP Server Mode (lines 2286-2349, especially 2290 and 2331)
- ADR-006 (transport mutual exclusion rationale)
- clap derive docs: https://docs.rs/clap/latest/clap/_derive/index.html
- Sibling beads: 6.7.2 stdio transport, 6.7.3 HTTP+SSE transport
Labels: cli, mcp, phase-6
issue.title: 6.7.4: Transport mutual exclusion enforcement at CLI parse (ADR-006)

issue.description:
## Scope

Three independent detectors that contribute to document-level metadata flags:

1. **JavaScript presence detection** — sets `contains_javascript: bool`. Scans:
   - Catalog /OpenAction: if value is a JavaScript action dict (/S /JavaScript), flag=true
   - Catalog /AA (Additional Actions): any value with /S /JavaScript -> flag=true
   - Page-level /AA dicts: any /S /JavaScript -> flag=true
   - AcroForm field /AA dicts: any /S /JavaScript -> flag=true
   - Annotation /A or /AA dicts: any /S /JavaScript -> flag=true
   - JavaScript is NEVER EXECUTED; only its presence is flagged

2. **XFA detection** — sets `contains_xfa: bool`. Checks for /AcroForm /XFA key presence; if present and non-null, flag=true. XFA is an XML-based form spec that is not parsed.

3. **Conformance detection** — sets `conformance: Option<String>` (e.g. "PDF/A-1b", "PDF/A-2u"). Parse the /Metadata stream (if present) as XMP XML using `quick-xml`; extract `pdfaid:part` and `pdfaid:conformance` namespace elements; combine as `PDF/A-{part}{conformance}`.

## Implementation guidance

- Public API:
  - `detect_javascript(catalog: &Catalog, pages: &[PageDict], acroform: &Option<PdfDict>, resolver: &XrefResolver) -> bool`
  - `detect_xfa(acroform: &Option<PdfDict>) -> bool`
  - `detect_conformance(metadata_stream: Option<&[u8]>) -> Option<String>`
- Use `quick-xml = "0.36"` (already in plan's Dependency Matrix); MOVE `quick-xml` from `ocr` feature to `default` (per plan note line 1120)
- JS detection walk: a single recursive walker that descends into /AA, /A, /OpenAction dicts looking for `/S Name("JavaScript")` or `/S Name("JS")` (alternate spec spelling)
- Annotation list per page is in PageDict.annots; resolve each annotation, check its /A and /AA
- XMP parsing: quick-xml's `Reader` with namespace_resolve enabled; pdfaid namespace URI is `http://www.aiim.org/pdfa/ns/id/`
- XMP example payload:
  ```xml
  <rdf:Description xmlns:pdfaid="http://www.aiim.org/pdfa/ns/id/" pdfaid:part="1" pdfaid:conformance="B">
  ```
  -> conformance = "PDF/A-1B" (uppercase the conformance letter per convention)
- /Metadata stream is itself a stream object; decompress via Phase 1.5, then feed to quick-xml

## Critical considerations

- JS detection cost: one walk of the document tree per page (plus annotations, plus AcroForm fields); total < 100 ms for 1000-page PDF
- /AA can be on document, page, annotation, AND form field — all four locations must be checked
- /A on annotations vs /AA: /A is the primary action; /AA is the additional actions (mouse-enter, mouse-leave, etc.); both may have /S /JavaScript
- The PDF spec allows both `/S /JavaScript` and `/S /JS`; check both names
- XMP /Metadata stream is a Type-1 (regular) stream; use Phase 1.5 StreamDecoder normally
- XMP parsing failures (malformed XML): emit STRUCT_INVALID_XMP, return conformance=None; do not panic
- pdfaid:part is the major version: 1, 2, 3, 4; pdfaid:conformance is the level: B (Basic), U (Unicode), A (Accessibility). Concatenate: "PDF/A-{part}{conformance}"
- Other PDF/X variants (PDF/X-1a, PDF/X-3, PDF/X-4) use the pdfxid namespace; conformance string is just "PDF/X-{part}" — detect this too as a stretch goal (out of scope for THIS bead unless trivial)
- The quick-xml feature flag move is critical: conformance detection runs for ALL documents (not just OCR), so quick-xml must be in default. This change is in pdftract-core/Cargo.toml

## Acceptance criteria

- JS test: document with /OpenAction = /S /JavaScript -> contains_javascript = true
- JS test: document with NO JS anywhere -> contains_javascript = false
- JS test: annotation /A /S /JavaScript -> contains_javascript = true (walks annotations)
- XFA test: /AcroForm /XFA present -> contains_xfa = true
- XFA test: /AcroForm without /XFA -> contains_xfa = false
- Conformance test: XMP with pdfaid:part="1" pdfaid:conformance="B" -> "PDF/A-1B"
- Conformance test: no /Metadata stream -> conformance = None
- Conformance test: malformed XMP -> STRUCT_INVALID_XMP; conformance = None; no panic
- quick-xml is in default features (verify via `cargo tree --features default`)
- INV-8 maintained

## References

- Plan section: Phase 1.4 line 1118-1120 (JS / XFA / conformance detection; quick-xml feature gate move)
- Dependency Matrix: quick-xml (moved to default feature)
- PDF spec 12.6 (Actions); 14.3.2 (Metadata Streams)
- INV-8

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement page-break emission in the Markdown sink + --md-no-page-breaks CLI flag. By default, a horizontal rule (---) is emitted between consecutive pages; --md-no-page-breaks suppresses the rule (producing continuous flowing text suitable for LLM ingestion).

Module: crates/pdftract-cli/src/cli.rs (flag) + crates/pdftract-core/src/output/markdown.rs (rule emission).

## Why this matters

LLM ingestion is a major use case: Markdown without page breaks is the ideal input format for instruction-tuned models (page breaks add noise; chunking systems prefer continuous text). For human-readable output (audit, review), page breaks are useful for navigation. The default-on + opt-out matches the more-common human-consumption case.

## Implementation guidance

- CLI flag (clap derive):
  ```rust
  #[arg(long, help = \"Suppress page-break horizontal rules between pages\")]
  pub md_no_page_breaks: bool,
  ```
- Markdown emission:
  - Between consecutive pages, emit \"---\\n\\n\" (horizontal rule + blank line)
  - When --md-no-page-breaks is set, omit
- Place the rule AFTER the last block of one page and BEFORE the first block of the next; not at the very start or end of the document

## Critical considerations

- The horizontal rule in CommonMark: 3+ dashes on a line by themselves, surrounded by blank lines. Format: \"\\n---\\n\\n\"
- For documents with --md-anchors enabled, the per-page anchor comment is independent of the page-break rule
- Don't emit rule for single-page documents (no \"between pages\")
- The rule is suppressed even on the first page if --md-no-page-breaks is set (defensive)

## Acceptance criteria

- Default behavior: 5-page PDF → Markdown has 4 horizontal rules between pages
- --md-no-page-breaks: same PDF → no horizontal rules
- Single-page PDF: no horizontal rules regardless of flag
- Rule format: \"\\n---\\n\\n\" (3 dashes, blank lines before/after)
- Renderer test: passes through GitHub Markdown preview as horizontal rules

## Scope

CLI integration for remote source features (cross-cuts Phase 6.1):

1. **--pages RANGE flag** — comma-separated, 1-based page ranges:
   - Examples: 1-5, 1,3,7, 12-, 1-5,7,12-
   - -N (open start) means 1..N inclusive; N- (open end) means N..page_count
   - Out-of-range emits PAGE_OUT_OF_RANGE; skipped
   - Default: all pages
   - Applies in ALL transport modes and ALL output formats

2. **--header HEADER:VALUE repeatable flag** — custom HTTP headers
3. **URL credential parsing** — https://user:pass@host/path

## Implementation guidance

- Use clap derive macros with ArgAction::Append for repeatable headers
- Page range parser: split by ',', parse each range, return SORTED DEDUP 0-based indices
- 1-based to 0-based conversion
- Emit PAGE_OUT_OF_RANGE for indices >= page_count
- URL credential parsing via url = "2" crate; extract user/pass, reconstruct URL without them
- Custom headers passed through to HttpRangeSource

## Critical considerations

- --pages flag is cross-cut to Phase 6.1; consistent behavior across extract, grep, hash
- Page range parser MUST handle whitespace: "1-5, 7" == "1-5,7"
- Invalid syntax (`5-3`, `abc`, `1.5`): USAGE error + exit 1
- URL credentials visible in shell history; warn users; --header preferred
- Custom header parsing: missing colon emits USAGE error
- ureq basic auth: automatically sets `Authorization: Basic <base64>` from URL credentials

- `pdftract extract --pages 1-5 local.pdf` extracts pages 1-5
- `pdftract extract --pages 12- local.pdf` extracts pages 12..page_count

- `pdftract extract --header 'Authorization: Bearer T' --header 'X-Custom: v' https://...` passes both
- `pdftract extract https://user:pass@host/file.pdf` extracts via basic auth; credentials stripped from logs
- Works with both extract and grep

## Scope

Author profiles/builtin/legal_filing.yaml per the Phase 7.10 YAML schema, plus at least 5 PDF fixtures at tests/fixtures/profiles/legal_filing/ each with a sibling expected-output.json, plus tests/profiles/test_legal_filing.rs that asserts exact-match of metadata.profile_fields.

## Why this matters

The legal_filing profile ships in v1.0.0 as one of the nine built-ins (line 3047). Legal filings (motions, briefs, court orders, dockets) are a high-value document type for legal-tech tools; extracting case_number, court, parties, filing_date, docket_entries correctly enables case-management and citation workflows.

## Implementation guidance

- File: profiles/builtin/legal_filing.yaml
  - name: legal_filing
  - description: "Court filings: motions, briefs, orders, docket entries"
  - priority: 40
  - match: all: [any: [text_contains: ['UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT', 'IN THE COURT OF', 'IN THE MATTER OF', 'Case No.', 'Civil Action No.', 'Plaintiff', 'Defendant', 'Petitioner', 'Respondent', 'COMPLAINT', 'MOTION TO', 'ORDER GRANTING', 'OPINION'], heading_matches: '^(COMPLAINT|MOTION|ORDER|OPINION|BRIEF)'], structural.page_count: {min: 1, max: 500}]
  - extraction: reading_order: xy_cut; readability_threshold: 0.5; include_headers_footers: true (page numbers and citations are load-bearing in legal docs)
  - fields: case_number (near: ['Case No.', 'Civil Action No.', 'Docket No.', 'Cause No.'], regex: '[\w-]+:?\s*\d+[\w-]*'), court (region: top_quarter; pick: largest_font), parties (near: ['Plaintiff', 'Defendant', 'Petitioner', 'Respondent', 'v.'], multi-capture for plaintiff + defendant), filing_date (near: ['Filed', 'Date Filed', 'Dated'], parse: date), docket_entries (region: full; structured list extraction for docket-style documents)
- Fixtures: 5 filings covering: federal complaint, state motion, appellate brief, court order, docket sheet

## Critical considerations

- Court name extraction via 'pick: largest_font' often fails because the court letterhead is graphical, not text; the README must document the failure mode
- case_number regex must handle multiple formats: 1:24-cv-00123 (federal), 2024-CV-12345 (state), 24-1234 (appellate); use a broad capture and let consumers parse
- parties extraction is the hardest field -- some filings have "JOHN DOE, Plaintiff, v. JANE DOE, Defendant" and others have multi-paragraph party blocks; the v1.0 extractor captures the verbatim block and lets downstream parsing decompose
- docket_entries is BEST-EFFORT and only meaningful for docket-sheet documents -- other filing types have no docket entries; the field is empty in that case
- citations (legal opinions cite other cases) are out of scope for the v1.0 profile; downstream tools handle citation extraction (e.g. EyeCite)
- Fixtures MUST be from public sources (SEC EDGAR for SEC-related filings; CourtListener for federal cases; state court public dockets); PROVENANCE entries cite the case captions
- Privacy: filings often contain PII (sealed cases excluded); pick public-case filings only

## Acceptance criteria

- profiles/builtin/legal_filing.yaml validates
- 5+ public-domain fixtures with expected outputs
- tests/profiles/test_legal_filing.rs passes
- Per-field accuracy: >= 90% on the 5-fixture corpus (parties and docket_entries relaxed to >= 80%)

## References

- Plan: lines 2890-3058, 3047 (legal_filing field set); depends on Provenance + Per-profile READMEs

## Scope

Bring docs/research/glyph-recognition-and-unicode-recovery.md to v1.0 final-pass: document the full methodology for the four-level Unicode recovery cascade (encoding, ToUnicode CMap, AGL lookup, glyph-shape perceptual-hash database) plus the bundled shape-to-Unicode database design that backs Level 4 recognition.

## Why this matters

This note is the canonical algorithm reference for one of the hardest problems in PDF extraction (Phase 2.2 + Phase 2.4 + Phase 2.5). Lines 1355 and 1418 in the plan explicitly cite this note as the authority. Without a coherent algorithm description, reviewers cannot validate the implementation and downstream contributors cannot reproduce the per-document recovery decisions.

## Implementation guidance

- File to update: docs/research/glyph-recognition-and-unicode-recovery.md (already exists, currently 112 lines)
- Required content sections:
  - Level 1: PDF-declared encoding tables (WinAnsiEncoding, MacRomanEncoding, MacExpertEncoding, StandardEncoding) -- happy path
  - Level 2: /ToUnicode CMap (when font supplies one) -- second-most-common path
  - Level 3: AGL (Adobe Glyph List) lookup for /Differences entries with glyph names
  - Level 4: Glyph-shape perceptual-hash recognition (rasterize glyph to 32x32 greyscale via fontdue or Type 3 content stream renderer; pHash; look up in bundled shape-to-Unicode database)
  - Bundled database design: schema, size budget, license/provenance, curation pipeline (cross-reference OQ-02 line 495)
  - Confidence scoring: each level emits a confidence in [0,1]; final cascade picks the highest-confidence non-empty result
- Cite Phase 2.2 (font recognition coordinator) and Phase 2.4 (Type 3 charstring renderer) entry points
- Cite Phase 2.5 (shape database bundling) for the build artifact

## Critical considerations

- Database file licensing must be free of unicode license entanglements (likely use the Adobe Glyph List + Unicode CLDR data) -- document the source per file
- Perceptual-hash collisions on visually-similar glyphs (e.g. l vs I vs |, O vs 0) need an explicit tie-break rule (font context: if BaseFont is monospaced and the previous span resolved to digits, prefer 0)
- Confidence floor for Level 4: if pHash distance > T, downgrade to U+FFFD with a SHAPE_AMBIGUOUS diagnostic
- Reproducibility: same glyph shape MUST always hash to the same bucket and yield the same Unicode value (no float nondeterminism, no random seeds)

## Acceptance criteria

- docs/research/glyph-recognition-and-unicode-recovery.md updated with all four cascade levels documented in algorithm form
- Bundled shape-to-Unicode database design specified: file format, size budget, curation/regeneration process
- pHash collision tie-break rules documented
- Confidence scoring formula documented
- Cross-references to Phase 2.2, 2.4, 2.5 and OQ-02 are present
- File grows to approx 300+ lines

## References

- Plan: lines 1355, 1418, OQ-02 (line 495); Phase 2.2, 2.4, 2.5

issue.description:
## Scope

Stand up the top-level Cargo workspace at the repo root with three member crates: `pdftract-core` (library), `pdftract-cli` (binary), `pdftract-py` (PyO3 binding). Members live under `crates/`. The workspace exists explicitly so the three crates share a single `Cargo.lock`, MSRV declaration, license metadata, and dependency resolution graph; this is the precondition for every other release engineering bead.

## Why this matters

The release pipeline assumes one workspace produces one consistent dependency tree. Without a workspace the three crates would each carry their own Cargo.lock and could drift apart on transitive versions — making reproducible builds impossible and breaking the per-tag artifact set guarantee.

## Implementation guidance

- Repo root `Cargo.toml` declares `[workspace]` with `members = ["crates/pdftract-core", "crates/pdftract-cli", "crates/pdftract-py"]` and `resolver = "2"`
- Use `[workspace.package]` for shared metadata: `version`, `edition = "2021"`, `rust-version = "1.78"`, `license = "MIT OR Apache-2.0"`, `repository = "https://github.com/jedarden/pdftract"`, `authors`, `homepage`, `documentation`
- Each member's `Cargo.toml` consumes `package = { workspace = true }` plus a per-member `name`
- Place `[workspace.dependencies]` for shared external deps (serde, anyhow, thiserror, tracing) so the three crates pin one common version
- pdftract-cli has `[[bin]] name = "pdftract"` and `default-run = "pdftract"`
- pdftract-py uses `pyo3` with `extension-module` feature; its `Cargo.toml` declares `crate-type = ["cdylib"]`
- A `.cargo/config.toml` at repo root pins useful build aliases (`alias.bench-ci = "bench --features benchmark"` etc.) so Argo templates can call them consistently

## Critical considerations

- Workspace MUST NOT include a top-level binary or library at the root — only the `[workspace]` table; this avoids the rare-but-painful publish failure where Cargo treats the root as a hidden member
- The workspace `resolver = "2"` is mandatory because `pdftract-py` is a cdylib with different feature requirements than the bin
- `pdftract-core` is `publish = true`; `pdftract-cli` is `publish = true`; `pdftract-py` is `publish = false` (Python wheels go to PyPI, not crates.io)
- The workspace MUST be created before any binary-build, cargo-lock, MSRV, license-deny, or binstall-metadata bead can land

## Acceptance criteria

- `cargo metadata --format-version 1` from repo root lists exactly three workspace members
- `cargo build --workspace --locked` succeeds on a clean clone
- `cargo build --workspace --locked --release` produces `target/release/pdftract` and a `pdftract-core` rlib
- Adding a fourth member crate (e.g. `pdftract-bench`) requires only one edit to the root `Cargo.toml`
- All three crate `Cargo.toml`s reference workspace-wide `version` / `edition` / `rust-version` via `workspace = true`

## References

- Plan section: Release Engineering and Distribution / Artifact Taxonomy, lines 3343-3367
- Sibling crate layout: pdftract-libpdftract is added as a fourth member when the C-FFI SDK bead lands (covered under SDK Architecture epic)
- Cargo Book: workspaces (https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/workspaces.html)

issue.description:
## Scope

Maintain a per-page `xobject_execution_stack: Vec<ObjectId>` tracking the currently-executing form XObjects (push on Do entry, pop on Do exit). Before each Do entry: (1) if the target XObject's ObjectId is already in the stack, emit `STRUCT_XOBJECT_CYCLE` diagnostic and refuse the Do (return without executing); (2) if stack length >= 20, emit `STRUCT_XOBJECT_DEPTH_EXCEEDED` diagnostic and refuse the Do.

## Why this matters

Malicious PDFs use form-XObject cycles to OOM the parser (each cycle invocation doubles the work; an A->B->A->B... loop bounded only by stack growth crashes any parser without cycle detection). Even non-malicious PDFs occasionally have accidental cycles from sloppy edit history.

## Implementation guidance

- Storage: `Vec<u32>` on the page executor, `xobject_execution_stack`. Empty at page start.
- Push: before invoking nested execution, append the form XObject's object number.
- Pop: after nested execution returns (whether normally or due to a diagnostic), remove the top element.
- Cycle check: `contains()` over the Vec — O(depth) lookup; with depth bounded at 20, total cost is constant.
- Depth check: `len() >= 20` -> refuse.
- Diagnostics: each unique cycle/depth event emitted ONCE per page (HashSet of "already-warned" object ids); a second occurrence of the same cycle/depth is silent.
- Stack must be popped on ALL exit paths (panic-safe via RAII guard struct or explicit early-return cleanup).

## Critical considerations

- INV: cycle key is the OBJECT NUMBER, not a content hash or generic identity. Two different objects with identical content are NOT a cycle.
- Same object reachable via DIFFERENT paths is the same cycle. (A->B and A->C->B both push B onto the stack at point B's entry; if B->A then it's a cycle.)
- A->B->A is detected at B's invocation of A (A is already in the stack from the original outer call).
- The depth limit is INCLUSIVE: at depth 20 you may invoke ONE more level (level 21 then refused at the start of level 21).
- Resource cycles (a form referencing itself in /Resources) are separate from execution cycles — not handled here.

## Acceptance criteria

- A->B->A cycle: B's invocation of A emits STRUCT_XOBJECT_CYCLE; A is NOT re-executed; extraction continues.
- Linear A->B->C->D...->T (20 deep): all 20 execute; the 21st level would be refused with STRUCT_XOBJECT_DEPTH_EXCEEDED.
- Same form invoked twice in sequence (NOT nested): second invocation succeeds (no cycle, no overlap in stack).
- A diamond: form A invokes both B and C, B and C both invoke D — no cycle; D executes twice.
- Stack always properly popped after each invocation (verify post-page state).

## References

- Plan section: Phase 3.3 Cycle detection paragraph (line 1569)
issue.title: Cycle detection + 20-level depth limit for form XObject recursion

## Scope

Author the inspector frontend as a single-page vanilla web app: index.html + style.css + app.js + any required assets. Compile into the binary via include_bytes! macros and serve from the / and /static/<asset> routes (7.9.2). Total stripped+gzipped bundle size < 80 KB. No JavaScript framework; no CDN; no external font dependency. CI gate: build script computes gzipped size; PR fails if > 80 KB.

## Why this matters

The < 80 KB bundle target is a binary-size discipline that pays for itself: keeps the pdftract binary slim (Inspector adds ~80 KB to the binary), eliminates external dependencies (no CDN means no network, no privacy leak, no version-skew), and runs offline. Vanilla DOM + minimal CSS is sufficient for the inspector's needs - frameworks (React, Vue, Svelte) would explode the bundle by an order of magnitude.

## Implementation guidance

- Source layout: crates/pdftract-cli/src/inspect/frontend/
  - index.html
  - style.css
  - app.js
  - (any future small assets)
- index.html structure: <html><head> with style.css link, JS module preload <body> with left sidebar (page thumbnails), top toolbar (search input, Prev/Next, overlay toggles), main canvas (SVG render container), right panel (JSON tree of current page)
- style.css: ~5 KB; CSS-only overlay toggling via data attributes on <html>; tooltip via :hover pseudo-class on span outlines
- app.js: vanilla JS modules; fetch() for API calls; URL fragment parsing for #page=N; keyboard event handlers (left/right/space/slash/1-8); localStorage for overlay toggle persistence; <120 KB unminified, target < 50 KB minified+gzipped
- Build: include_bytes!("frontend/index.html") etc. in the Rust source
- Build-time minification: use simple Rust build.rs script to minify-on-build (or commit pre-minified versions); gzip via flate2 at compile time so served bytes are pre-compressed
- CI gate: compute size = sum of gzipped(bundle bytes); assert < 80 KB; emit number in build log
- Overlay toggles persist via localStorage with keys like "pdftract-inspector-layer-spans"
- Keyboard shortcuts: ArrowLeft/ArrowRight = prev/next page, '/' = focus search, '1'-'8' = toggle layer N
- Tooltip content: text, font, confidence, bbox, block ref, MCID, reading idx (all from /api/page/{i})

## Critical considerations

- Bundle size budget < 80 KB stripped+gzipped is HARD: no framework, no icon font, no images other than tiny SVG icons inline
- Browser support: latest Chrome / Firefox / Safari only (no IE, no Edge legacy); use ES modules, modern DOM, Fetch API freely
- Frontend is offline-capable (no CDN); inspector runs without network
- localStorage keys namespaced to "pdftract-inspector-*" so other apps on same origin don't collide
- Accessibility: tab through overlay toggles; ARIA labels on form inputs; high contrast colors for confidence heatmap
- No analytics, no telemetry - this is a debug tool that should never phone home
- CSS-only overlay toggling: data attribute on html (e.g. <html data-layers="spans,blocks,reading_order">); CSS rules .layer-spans { display: none; } html[data-layers~="spans"] .layer-spans { display: block; }

## Acceptance criteria

- Bundle stripped+gzipped size < 80 KB (CI-gated)
- index.html loads in current Chrome, Firefox, Safari (headless smoke tests)
- 8 layer toggles work via CSS only (no JS re-render)
- localStorage persists toggle state across reload
- Keyboard shortcuts 1-8 + arrow keys + '/' work
- URL fragment #page=14 jumps to page 14
- Frontend works offline (no CDN URLs)

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement pdftract.extract_text(path, **kwargs) -> str as a PyO3 function. Returns the plain-text extraction directly as a PyString (no intermediate dict).

Module: crates/pdftract-py/src/extract_text.rs.

## Why this matters

extract_text is the cheap fast path for RAG ingest pipelines that just want the text body; they don't need spans, fonts, or bboxes. Returning a bare str avoids the cost of serializing the full Document to JSON and re-parsing in Python.

## Implementation guidance

- Signature:
  ```rust
  #[pyfunction]
  #[pyo3(signature = (path, **kwargs))]
  pub fn extract_text(py: Python<'_>, path: &str, kwargs: Option<&PyDict>) -> PyResult<String> {
      let opts = parse_kwargs(kwargs)?;
      let text = py.allow_threads(|| pdftract_core::extract_text(path, &opts))?;
      Ok(text)
  }
  ```
- kwargs subset: ocr, ocr_language, pages, password, include_invisible
- GIL release during extraction
- Returns String (PyO3 auto-converts to PyString)

## Critical considerations

- The default text-extraction behavior matches pdftract extract --text on the same input (consistency across CLI + PyO3)
- ExtractionOptions used here is the same struct as for extract; only the format selection differs
- For very large extractions (10 MB+ text), consider returning bytes to avoid Python string allocation overhead; for now, String is simpler and sufficient

## Acceptance criteria

- pdftract.extract_text(\"file.pdf\") returns a str
- The returned text matches pdftract extract --text on the same input (byte-identical)
- pdftract.extract_text(\"file.pdf\", pages=\"1-5\") returns only the first 5 pages

issue.description:
## Scope

Parse the /AcroForm /XFA stream (or array of named streams) and walk the XFA data model to extract <field> element values. Supports two stream layouts: (a) single XDP stream, (b) array of alternating (Name, Stream) entries where stream names ["preamble", "config", "template", "datasets", "form", "postamble"] are concatenated in declared order. Emit Vec<(String full_name, String value)>.

## Why this matters

XFA-only PDFs (US 1040 tax forms, many state and federal forms, healthcare intake) are stubbornly common despite Adobe deprecating XFA. Without XFA parsing, these documents return empty form_fields despite visibly filled data. quick-xml is the right Rust XML choice: streaming, zero-copy, sub-100 KB binary impact.

## Implementation guidance

- Crates: quick-xml = "0.31"
- Locate /AcroForm /XFA:
  - If Stream: this is the full XDP - parse directly
  - If Array: iterate pairs (Name, Stream); concatenate stream contents in array order. Some PDFs include only a subset of the named streams - skip missing ones
- Decode the resulting XML bytes; XFA uses UTF-8 by default
- Use quick-xml Reader with namespace tracking; XFA namespaces: xfa, xdc, xdp, xfdf - register prefixes
- Walk the XDP tree to <xfa:datasets><xfa:data> root; descendant <field> elements (or arbitrary element name in the data partition) hold values as text content
- Field full name: tag path joined with "." (e.g. "form1.section1.firstName")
- Walk <xfa:template> separately to capture field definitions (caption, ui type) - merge with data values by name for richer metadata
- Emit (full_name, value) pairs

## Critical considerations

- Stream order matters - the array form has explicit order in the array; do not reorder
- XFA encryption stubs (xfa:encrypt) exist; skip silently
- Some XFA streams use FlateDecode filter - apply via Phase 1 stream decoder before XML parse
- quick-xml namespace API requires explicit feature flag - enable "encoding" and "namespace" features
- Very large XFA streams (1+ MB on government forms) - use buffered reader; avoid loading entire DOM
- XFA <field> elements in <template> have UI hints (text, checkbox, ddlist) - map to FormFieldValue kinds where possible
- Empty elements (filled but blank) -> value: Some("")
- Malformed XML must NOT crash the whole extraction - emit diagnostic and return partial result

## Acceptance criteria

- Critical test (from plan): XFA-only form - all field values extracted from XFA XML
- Unit tests: single stream, array stream with all 6 names, array stream with 2 names, FlateDecode-compressed stream, malformed XML (diagnostic + partial)
- Public xfa::extract_fields(stream_or_array: &PdfObject) -> Vec<(String, String)>
- quick-xml feature flags: encoding + namespace enabled

## References

- Plan section: 7.4 lines 2616-2619 (XFA)
- XFA 3.3 spec (Adobe)
- 7.4.1 (parallel AcroForm walk)
- 7.4.4 (combiner)
- Phase 1 stream decoder (FlateDecode for compressed XFA)
issue.title: 7.4.3: XFA stream parser (quick-xml + concatenation + data model walk)

issue.description:
## Scope

Build a compile-time `phf::Map<&'static str, char>` covering Adobe Glyph List for New Fonts (AGLFN, ~770 entries) and full AGL 1.4 (~4400 entries). Exposes `pub fn unicode_for_glyph_name(name: &str) -> Option<char>` and a multi-codepoint variant `pub fn unicode_for_glyph_name_multi(name: &str) -> Option<&'static [char]>` for ligature names (e.g. `fi` -> `[f, i]`).

## Why this matters

AGL is the canonical map from PostScript glyph names to Unicode. It is the load-bearing component of Level 2 — every Type1/TrueType font with a named encoding hits this lookup. Compile-time phf::Map gives O(1) lookup with zero runtime allocation.

## Implementation guidance

- Source: download AGL 1.4 (`aglfn.txt` and `glyphlist.txt`) from Adobe's public corpus; commit the JSON-rendered version to `crates/pdftract-core/build/agl.json`.
- `build.rs` uses `phf_codegen` to emit two static maps:
  - `pub static AGL: phf::Map<&'static str, char>` for single-codepoint names.
  - `pub static AGL_MULTI: phf::Map<&'static str, &'static [char]>` for multi-codepoint (ligature) names.
- Friendly-name handling: AGL allows uniXXXX, uXXXXXX, and `<glyphname>.<variant>` patterns. Implement a fallback parser in `unicode_for_glyph_name` BEFORE the phf::Map lookup that handles these algorithmic patterns (no phf entry needed).
- Variant stripping: `H.sc` (small-caps H), `A.alt` (alternate) — strip everything from the first `.` onward and retry the lookup.

## Critical considerations

- INV: phf::Map for AGL must be const-built; build.rs cannot reach into the crate's own deps. Use phf_codegen::Map::build().
- Some AGL entries map to multi-char Unicode strings (ff, ffi, ffl, fi, fl, longs_t, etc.) — those go in AGL_MULTI.
- The patterns `uniXXXX` (4 hex digits) and `uXXXXXX` (up to 6 hex digits) are ALGORITHMIC, not in AGL — do not add 65535 entries to the phf::Map for them.
- Binary footprint target: ~250 KB combined for both maps. Verify via `cargo bloat --release --crates`.

## Acceptance criteria

- `unicode_for_glyph_name("quoteright") == Some('\u{2019}')`.
- `unicode_for_glyph_name("uni20AC") == Some('\u{20AC}')` (Euro, algorithmic).
- `unicode_for_glyph_name("u1F600") == Some('\u{1F600}')` (emoji, algorithmic 6-digit).
- `unicode_for_glyph_name_multi("fi") == Some(&['f', 'i'])`.
- `unicode_for_glyph_name("A.sc") == Some('A')` (variant stripped).
- Unknown name returns None (no panic).
- Binary footprint < 250 KB for both maps.

## References

- Plan section: Phase 2.2 Level 2 (line 1339)
- AGL 1.4 spec (adobe-type-tools/agl-aglfn on GitHub)
issue.title: Adobe Glyph List + AGLFN compile-time phf::Map

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the region-level confidence policy that decides per-region whether to keep assisted-OCR output (mean confidence > 0.7), accept it as-is (between 0.3 and 0.7), or fall back to pure unaided OCR (mean confidence < 0.3). Also configures PSM_SPARSE_TEXT (mode 11) when invoking Tesseract from the BrokenVector path.

## Why this matters

A page may have one region where the text layer is correctly positioned and another where it's misaligned. Per-word validation alone over-rejects words in the misaligned region (capping at 0.4). The region-level policy detects the misalignment and falls back to unaided OCR for those words, recovering accuracy lost to the over-cap.

## Implementation guidance

- Region grouping: use Phase 4.2 line-formation candidates (cluster spans by baseline)
- For each candidate region (line):
  - Compute mean of confidence across all assisted-OCR words in the region
  - mean > 0.7 -> keep as confidence_source = "ocr-assisted"
  - mean < 0.3 -> rerun Tesseract on that region's image crop WITHOUT validation filter; emit as confidence_source = "ocr-fallback"
  - 0.3 <= mean <= 0.7 -> keep as-is
- PSM_SPARSE_TEXT wiring: extend TessOpts in 5.4.1 to carry PageSegMode; BrokenVector path passes PageSegMode::SparseText
- The rerun step (mean < 0.3 case) reuses the cell image already in memory; no re-render needed

## Critical considerations

- Don't re-preprocess for the fallback rerun (5.3 work is wasted otherwise)
- Region grouping uses Phase 4.2 line-formation logic; if 4.2 is not deterministic, neither is this; verify
- PSM_SPARSE_TEXT (11) finds text in arbitrary positions without requiring a dominant text block — appropriate for BrokenVector where text may be fragmented
- confidence_source = "ocr-fallback" is a NEW value that needs 6.1 JSON Schema enum entry
- The 0.7 / 0.3 thresholds are constants ASSISTED_OCR_KEEP_THRESH / ASSISTED_OCR_FALLBACK_THRESH; document tuning

## Acceptance criteria

- Misaligned-text-layer fixture: regions with mean conf < 0.3 trigger fallback; output WER == blind-OCR WER on those regions
- Correctly-aligned fixture: all regions mean conf > 0.7; no fallback triggered
- PSM_SPARSE_TEXT verified via trace on BrokenVector page
- confidence_source values present in 6.1 Schema enum

## References

- Plan section: Phase 5.5 step 5 (line 1919)
- Phase 5.4 PSM modes
- INV-7 confidence_source
issue.title: 5.5.3: Region-level confidence policy (>0.7 keep, <0.3 fallback to pure OCR) + PSM_SPARSE_TEXT wiring

issue.description:
## Scope

Define the unified diagnostic system used across all of pdftract-core:

- `Diagnostic` struct: `{ code: DiagCode, byte_offset: Option<u64>, object_ref: Option<ObjRef>, message: Cow<'static, str> }`
- `DiagCode` enum: enumerates EVERY diagnostic code used by Phases 1-7. Variants follow naming conventions:
  - STRUCT_* — PDF structure errors (parser/object/document layer)
  - STREAM_* — stream-decoder errors
  - XREF_* — xref resolution errors
  - ENCRYPTION_* — encryption-related errors
  - OCR_* — OCR pipeline errors (Phase 5)
  - REMOTE_* — remote-source errors (Phase 1.8)
  - PAGE_* — page-level errors
  - FONT_* — font pipeline errors
- A `///` doc comment per variant explains WHEN the diagnostic is emitted, with examples
- A static catalog DIAGNOSTIC_CATALOG: &[DiagInfo] enumerates all variants with severity, recoverable flag, suggested user action
- Helper macro: emit!(diagnostics, code, byte_offset?, object_ref?, message)

## Implementation guidance

- Use Cow<'static, str> for message so static messages don't allocate
- Severity: Error (extraction may be incomplete), Warning (continues with workaround), Info (XREF_REPAIRED)
- Recoverable: Y means parsing continues; N means document unusable
- Use enum DiagCode with repr(u16) for compact storage
- Module location: `crates/pdftract-core/src/diagnostics.rs`
- CI lint: every new variant must have a `///` doc comment

## Critical considerations

- Naming convention enforcement enables external tools to filter by code prefix
- Catalog referenced by `pdftract --explain-diagnostic STRUCT_MISSING_KEY` (Phase 6 CLI helper)
- byte_offset may be None for non-byte-offset contexts; object_ref may be None for pre-object failures
- Catalog is INFORMATIONAL only at runtime; severity for downstream consumers
- INV-8 enforcement: clippy + proptest catch panics that bypass this system
- Diagnostic struct size 24-32 bytes (profiling shows large parse failures emit hundreds)
- Macro hides Optionality: `emit!(diagnostics, STRUCT_INVALID_NAME, offset=42)` should work without explicit None

## Acceptance criteria

- crates/pdftract-core/src/diagnostics.rs exists with Diagnostic + DiagCode + DIAGNOSTIC_CATALOG
- All Phase 1.1-1.5 child beads have been audited and use the unified DiagCode
- Every DiagCode variant has `///` doc comment + catalog entry
- emit! macro works ergonomically
- `pdftract --list-diagnostics` outputs the catalog (placeholder behind feature flag)
- Diagnostic struct size 24-32 bytes (static_assertions verified)
- INV-8 maintained

## References

- Plan section: Phase 1.6 (error recovery); Diagnostic Code Catalog section
- INV-8
- Phase 0.4 (clippy enforces doc comments)
issue.title: Define unified Diagnostic types + diagnostic code catalog with naming-convention enforcement

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement classify_figure(page) that returns synthetic Block instances with kind=Figure for each image XObject region on the page where text overlaps < 50%. Walks page_image_list (Phase 3.5 inline + Phase 3.3 Do images); creates Block { lines: [], bbox: image_bbox, kind: Figure }.

Module: crates/pdftract-core/src/layout/figure.rs.

## Why this matters

Figures are 2nd-most-common block type after paragraphs; critical for academic paper extraction, technical doc rendering, and figure-citation pipelines. Without figure detection, image regions appear as gaps in the output instead of identifiable blocks.

## Implementation guidance

- Iterate page_image_list (combined from Phase 3.5 inline images + Phase 3.3 Do operator XObject placements)
- For each image bbox:
  - Compute text-glyph overlap: union of all glyph bboxes intersecting the image bbox / image bbox area
  - If overlap < 0.5 (50%): create Block { kind: Figure, lines: [], bbox: image_bbox }
- Insert resulting Figure blocks into page.blocks sorted by bbox top y
- Block.lines is empty Vec (figures have no text lines)
- Don't merge adjacent Figure blocks (each image is its own block); a future enhancement could group multi-panel figures

## Critical considerations

- The 50% text-overlap threshold is calibrated: < 50% means the image is mostly visual content; >= 50% means it's a text-on-image overlay (e.g. screenshot of text) and shouldn't be flagged as Figure
- Inline images (Phase 3.5) have small bboxes; Do-placed XObjects (Phase 3.3) can be page-spanning. Both treated uniformly
- This is a per-image classifier; Phase 5.2 hybrid composer may further refine for partially-textual images
- Block.bbox is the image's bbox in PDF user-space coordinates

## Acceptance criteria

- PDF with 5 figures (images, no text overlay) → 5 Figure blocks in output
- PDF with 1 image fully covered by text (screenshot with text annotation) → no Figure block (text overlap >= 50%)
- Block insertion preserves top-y sort order
- Block.lines is empty Vec
- Test corpus: scientific paper with embedded figures → all detected

## Scope

Parse `/OCProperties` from the catalog and produce an `OcProperties` struct that downstream Phase 3 content stream processing consults when entering `/OC /OCGRef` BDC blocks.

`OcProperties` struct:
- `groups: HashMap<ObjRef, OcGroup>` — every OCG object referenced from /OCGs

OcGroup struct:
- `name: String` — /Name (human-readable)
- `intent: Vec<String>` — /Intent (View, Design, etc.)
- `usage: PdfDict` — /Usage (informational)

## Implementation guidance

- Public API: `parse_oc_properties(resolver: &XrefResolver, oc_props_ref: Option<ObjRef>) -> OcProperties`
- If oc_props_ref is None: return `OcProperties { present: false, ... }`; downstream code treats all content as visible
- Otherwise:
  1. Resolve oc_props_ref to a dict
  2. /OCGs is an array of ObjRefs to OCG dicts; iterate, resolve each, build `OcGroup` for each
  3. /D is the default configuration dict (REQUIRED per spec). It has:
     - /BaseState (Name): `ON` or `OFF`; default `ON`
     - /ON: array of OCG refs that are ON by default (overrides BaseState for these)
     - /OFF: array of OCG refs that are OFF by default (overrides BaseState for these)
  4. For each OCG: visibility = OFF if in /OFF list; ON if in /ON list; BaseState otherwise
- BaseState enum: `On`, `Off`, `Unchanged` (the latter is rare; treat as `On`)

## Critical considerations

- Critical test from plan EC-16: OCG with default OFF state. The fixture has /OCProperties /D /BaseState /OFF (or /D /OFF [ ... OCG ...]). Phase 3 content stream processing must suppress glyphs inside /OC /OCGRef BDC blocks whose referenced OCG is OFF
- Phase 3 implements the SUPPRESSION; this bead only computes the DEFAULT VISIBILITY MAP
- Full OCG toggle support (programmatic state changes via /Configs alternates) is DEFERRED to Phase 7 per plan; this bead handles only the default config (/D)
- Multiple /Configs alternates: /OCProperties /Configs is an array of configuration dicts; only /D is used in this bead
- /OCProperties dict missing: ocg_present = false; default to all-ON behavior (Phase 3 ignores any /OC tags as if OCGs don't exist)
- An OCG referenced via /OC /OCGRef in a BDC block but NOT in the /OCGs array: emit STRUCT_UNKNOWN_OCG, treat as visible (don't suppress)
- /OCMD (Optional Content Membership Dict) is a higher-level construct (multiple OCGs combined via Boolean policy: /AllOn, /AnyOn, /AllOff, /AnyOff); handle minimally in this bead — record the policy and the referenced OCGs; defer evaluation to Phase 3 too
- An OCG's /Intent of `/View` is the rendering intent; if /Design only, it's metadata-only and not rendered. Phase 3 may use this to suppress non-View OCGs
- Performance: a document with 1000 OCGs (unusual but legal) builds a 1000-entry HashMap in <1 ms

## Acceptance criteria

- EC-16 fixture: OCG with default OFF state — `default_visibility[ocg_ref] == false`
- Fixture with /BaseState OFF + /ON [ocg1 ocg2]: ocg1, ocg2 are ON; all others (in /OCGs) are OFF
- Fixture with no /OCProperties: present = false; downstream treats all content as visible
- Fixture with /OCMD combining 3 OCGs via /AllOn: policy preserved; evaluation deferred to Phase 3
- proptest: random PdfObject as /OCProperties never panics
- INV-8 maintained

## References

- Plan section: Phase 1.4 line 1116 (OCG handling, BaseState, /ON, /OFF, /OCMD)
- EC-16 (OCG with default OFF state)
- PDF spec 8.11 (Optional Content)
- Phase 3 (consumes the visibility map)
- Phase 7 (full OCG toggle support — deferred)

issue.description:
## Scope

Build a `cargo xtask gen-shape-db` subcommand that walks a directory of source font files (TrueType / OpenType), rasterizes every mapped glyph at 32x32 via fontdue, computes pHash for each, and writes the result as `build/glyph-shapes.json` with entries `{ phash_hex, char (escaped), source_font (informational), frequency_rank }`.

## Why this matters

The shape DB is the authoritative training corpus for L4 recognition. Without a reproducible offline pipeline, the DB is a mystery binary blob no one can update. Cargo xtask is the standard Rust pattern for "build-supporting tools that ship in the repo but never appear in the published crate".

## Implementation guidance

- Create `xtask/` workspace member with `cargo xtask gen-shape-db --fonts <dir> --output build/glyph-shapes.json`.
- Walk the font directory; for each .ttf/.otf, load via fontdue, enumerate the cmap (`face.glyph_count()` + reverse lookup), filter to glyphs with a known Unicode codepoint.
- Rasterize each glyph at fontdue's natural size scaled to fit 32x32 (centered, padded with zeros). Convert to grayscale.
- Compute pHash via the sibling pHash bead.
- Look up Unicode frequency rank from a separate `frequency.json` (sourced from Wikipedia/Project Gutenberg corpus frequency lists for Latin, Greek, Cyrillic, plus zero rank for symbols).
- Deduplicate by (phash, char): if two source fonts produce the same hash for the same char, keep one; if different chars produce the same hash, keep the higher-frequency char and log the collision.
- Output JSON sorted by phash ascending.

## Critical considerations

- Source fonts MUST be open-licensed: Google Fonts (Apache 2.0 / OFL) and SIL OFL fonts. Document license terms; commit license texts to `build/font-licenses/`.
- Sizing: the 32x32 bitmap must be CENTERED with consistent baseline alignment, otherwise pHash drift across glyphs of same char in different fonts is large. Use ttf-parser to get the glyph's bbox and FontMetrics for ascent/descent normalization.
- Run xtask in CI as a pre-merge check to detect glyph-shape regressions when the input corpus changes.
- Target: ~5000 entries covering Latin (basic + extended), Greek, Cyrillic, common symbols (math, arrows, punctuation), Latin diacritics.

## Acceptance criteria

- `cargo xtask gen-shape-db --fonts <dir>` produces a valid JSON file with the expected schema.
- The output is byte-identical when re-run on the same input (deterministic).
- Running with Liberation Sans, DejaVu, Source Code Pro, and Noto Sans produces ~5000 entries.
- License attribution and source font list documented in build/font-licenses/README.
- Round-trip: rasterize a glyph from a DIFFERENT font, lookup -> match the expected char with Hamming distance <= 8.

## References

- Plan section: Phase 2.5 Source paragraph (line 1428)

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the image_coverage_fraction signal evaluator. Computes the union image coverage of the page; > 0.85 -> Scanned with strength 0.85.

## Why this matters

Pages with most of their area covered by images (whether or not they have text overlays) are predominantly scanned content. Used as a fallback when the more-definitive text_operator_presence signal doesn't fire.

## Implementation guidance

- Signature:
  ```rust
  pub fn image_coverage_fraction(ctx: &PageContext) -> Option<Signal>
  ```
- Compute total image coverage as union of image_xobject_areas (NOT sum — overlapping images shouldn't double-count)
- Union algorithm: sort by x0; sweep computing union per scan; OR use the Klee's algorithm for rectangle union (~O(N log N))
- For simplicity in the first impl: sum / page_area, clamped to 1.0; document the over-counting risk in code comments and revisit if accuracy demands
- If fraction > 0.85 → Some(Signal { strength: 0.85, vote: Scanned })

## Critical considerations

- Union vs sum: 5 overlapping copies of one image = sum of 5x area but union is 1x area; the simple sum overestimates Scanned strength on legitimately multi-overlay pages
- Clamp to [0,1] to avoid > 1.0 fractions on overlapping images (defensive)
- page_area_pt2 from PageContext (computed once at page load)

## Acceptance criteria

- Page with one image covering 90% area → Some(Signal { 0.85, Scanned })
- Page with multiple small images totaling 50% → None (below threshold)
- Page with no images → None
- Coverage clamped to 1.0 on overlapping images

## References

- Plan section: Phase 5.1.2
- Coordinator: pdftract-22p (parent)
Labels: classifier, phase-5, signal
