issue.description:
## Scope

Author and validate two sample reverse-proxy configuration files in docs/operations/:

- docs/operations/serve-nginx-example.conf — nginx config: auth_basic + proxy_pass to localhost:8080, allowlisted paths, header filtering
- docs/operations/serve-traefik-example.yaml — Traefik dynamic config: BasicAuth middleware + service backend pointing at pdftract serve

Both configs are tested by parsing them with their respective tools as a CI gate.

## Why this matters

Sample configs are the bridge between the no-auth posture (sibling bead) and a production deployment. Operators copy-paste from docs/operations/ rather than writing reverse-proxy configs from scratch; bad samples (or missing samples) push operators to either skip the proxy step (insecure) or invent their own potentially-misconfigured proxies. Providing canonical examples removes that risk.

## Implementation guidance

### nginx config (docs/operations/serve-nginx-example.conf)

```nginx
upstream pdftract_backend {
    server 127.0.0.1:8080;
    keepalive 32;
}

server {
    listen 443 ssl;
    server_name pdftract.example.com;

    ssl_certificate     /etc/ssl/certs/pdftract.crt;
    ssl_certificate_key /etc/ssl/private/pdftract.key;

    client_max_body_size 256m;
    proxy_read_timeout 300s;

    auth_basic           \"pdftract\";
    auth_basic_user_file /etc/nginx/htpasswd-pdftract;

    location /extract {
        proxy_pass http://pdftract_backend;
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
        proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
    }

    location /health {
        proxy_pass http://pdftract_backend;
        auth_basic off;  # monitoring should not need credentials
    }

    # Deny everything else
    location / { return 404; }
}
```

### Traefik config (docs/operations/serve-traefik-example.yaml)

```yaml
http:
  routers:
    pdftract:
      rule: \"Host(`pdftract.example.com`)\"
      service: pdftract-backend
      middlewares:
        - pdftract-auth
        - pdftract-limit
      tls:
        certResolver: letsencrypt

  services:
    pdftract-backend:
      loadBalancer:
        servers:
          - url: \"http://127.0.0.1:8080\"

  middlewares:
    pdftract-auth:
      basicAuth:
        usersFile: \"/etc/traefik/htpasswd-pdftract\"
    pdftract-limit:
      buffering:
        maxRequestBodyBytes: 268435456  # 256 MB
        memRequestBodyBytes: 16777216
```

### Validation

- CI step: nginx -t -c docs/operations/serve-nginx-example.conf → exit 0
- CI step: yq eval . docs/operations/serve-traefik-example.yaml → exit 0 (YAML well-formed)
- Optional: traefik --configFile=docs/operations/serve-traefik-example.yaml --check (if traefik CLI available)

## Critical considerations

- Sample configs reference example.com hostnames and example paths; consumers must adapt — document this with comments in the config files
- The htpasswd file generation steps are documented separately (one-liner with htpasswd CLI); not part of these configs
- /health endpoint is auth-exempt in both examples (monitoring scrape should not need credentials; matches the Phase 6.4 convention)
- Deny-everything-else rule in nginx (return 404) prevents path-based exploration; Traefik routes by Host rule which naturally restricts
- The sample configs MUST be in the secret-protection allowlist (already covered in config per parent's mention)
- Add a docs/operations/README.md or a top-of-file comment in each sample explaining the trust model: \"This config assumes pdftract serve is bound to 127.0.0.1; nginx/Traefik provides TLS termination and authentication.\"

## Acceptance criteria

- docs/operations/serve-nginx-example.conf exists and parses cleanly with nginx -t
- docs/operations/serve-traefik-example.yaml exists and parses as valid YAML
- Both files include a top-comment explaining the deployment model and the no-auth pdftract assumption
- CI step in Argo WorkflowTemplate validates both files on every PR touching them
- Documentation prose elsewhere (docs/user-docs/) cross-references these examples

## References

- Coordinator: pdftract-1i366 (parent)

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the FlateDecode filter (the most common PDF filter, used by ~95% of streams):

1. Zlib-decompress raw bytes via `flate2::read::ZlibDecoder`
2. If /DecodeParms has /Predictor != 1, apply the post-inflate predictor:
   - TIFF predictor 2: delta from previous column, per channel
   - PNG predictors 10-15: per-row predictor byte (10=None, 11=Sub, 12=Up, 13=Average, 14=Paeth, 15=Optimum-per-row)
3. Return the unpredicted pixel data

DecodeParms keys (per PDF spec 7.4.4):
- /Predictor (int, default 1 = no predictor)
- /Columns (int, default 1) — columns per row
- /Colors (int, default 1) — color channels per pixel
- /BitsPerComponent (int, default 8) — bits per channel

Bytes per row = ceil(columns * colors * bits_per_component / 8)
For PNG predictor: +1 byte per row (the predictor selector)

## Implementation guidance

- Use `flate2 = "1"` crate (in plan's Dependency Matrix)
- ZlibDecoder construction: `ZlibDecoder::new(&[u8])` -> Read; read all to Vec<u8>
- Predictor application: separate function `apply_predictor(decoded: &[u8], params: &DecodeParms) -> Vec<u8>`
- TIFF predictor 2: for each row, for each column index j > 0: output[j] = input[j] + output[j-1] (per channel, wrapping at byte boundary). Simple delta encoding
- PNG predictors: each row is `<selector_byte> <columns * colors * bits/8 bytes>`. After applying:
  - 10 (None): copy as-is, discard selector
  - 11 (Sub): output[j] = input[j] + output[j - bpp] (where bpp = bytes-per-pixel)
  - 12 (Up): output[j] = input[j] + prev_row_output[j]
  - 13 (Average): output[j] = input[j] + (prev_row_output[j] + output[j - bpp]) / 2 (using integer division)
  - 14 (Paeth): paeth predictor — output[j] = input[j] + paeth(output[j-bpp], prev_row_output[j], prev_row_output[j-bpp])
  - 15 (Optimum): the selector byte itself selects one of 10-14 PER ROW — multiplexer
- Edge case: row 0 has no previous row; treat prev_row as all zeros
- Edge case: column 0 has no previous column; treat as zero
- bpp = ceil(colors * bits_per_component / 8); for 8-bit RGB, bpp=3

## Critical considerations

- Critical test from plan: FlateDecode with PNG predictor 15 (per-row) where all six predictor types (10/11/12/13/14/15 — selectors 0/1/2/3/4 inside a row) appear in one stream; all decoded correctly
- The /Predictor=15 (Optimum) selector applies PER-ROW; do not confuse with selector applying per-pixel
- Predictor params /Columns / /Colors / /BitsPerComponent are REQUIRED for predictors 2 and 10-15; missing emits STRUCT_INVALID_FILTER_PARAMS, defaults applied (predictor disabled)
- Truncated zlib stream (mid-stream EOF): catch the zlib error, return bytes decoded so far + STREAM_DECODE_ERROR diagnostic. flate2's read API returns Result with io::Error on truncation
- Output buffer pre-sizing: estimate via /Length1 if present (rare for streams; common for fonts) or grow naturally
- Performance: FlateDecode is the hot path; profile to ensure throughput >= 400 MB/sec on modern hardware (flate2 with zlib backend can hit this)
- The 2 GB bomb limit (from the orchestrator bead) is checked here: every 64 KB read from ZlibDecoder, increment doc_decompress_counter and check; truncate if exceeded
- /Predictor=2 (TIFF) is rare in PDFs but legal; the math is simpler than PNG (no selector byte per row, just plain delta)

## Acceptance criteria

- Critical test passes: PNG predictor 15 fixture with all 6 selector types decoded byte-perfectly
- Simple FlateDecode (no predictor): byte-perfect round-trip with reference zlib output
- TIFF predictor 2: 8-bit RGB delta-decoded correctly
- PNG predictor 14 (Paeth) on 8-bit RGBA: correct output (verify against libpng reference)
- Truncated stream test: STREAM_DECODE_ERROR + partial bytes
- Bomb limit test: 3 GB-expanding input returns ~2 GB + STREAM_BOMB
- Performance: 100 MB FlateDecode completes in < 250 ms on Hetzner EX44 baseline
- proptest: random byte sequences fed to FlateDecode never panic
- INV-8 maintained

## References

- Plan section: Phase 1.5 line 1141 (FlateDecode predictors); line 1159 (critical test for PNG predictor 15)
- PDF spec 7.4.4 (LZWDecode and FlateDecode Filters); Annex H (Optional Filters)
- PNG spec (predictor filters)
- TIFF 6.0 (Predictor 2)
- Dependency Matrix: flate2
issue.title: Implement FlateDecode with TIFF predictor 2 + PNG predictors 10-15 (per-row predictor 15)

## Scope

- `pages_ref: ObjRef` from `/Pages`

## Implementation guidance

- Public API: `parse_catalog(resolver: &XrefResolver, root_ref: ObjRef) -> Result<Catalog>`
- Use Phase 1.2 `resolver.resolve(root_ref)` to get the catalog PdfObject; expect Dict
- Extract each named entry via `dict.get("Pages")` etc.; if missing required key (/Pages), emit STRUCT_MISSING_KEY and return empty Catalog (no pages)
- /MarkInfo dict has /Marked (boolean), /UserProperties (bool), /Suspects (bool)
- /PageLabels is a number tree; parse via a generic `parse_number_tree<V>(node: &PdfObject) -> Vec<(i64, V)>` helper (delegate to a sibling bead if needed, but since PageLabels is simple, in-line it here)
- PageLabel entries: each value is a dict with /S (style: D / R / r / A / a), /P (prefix string), /St (start integer); convert each label to a String (e.g. "iv" for roman-lowercase index 4 starting at 1)

## Critical considerations

- Critical test from plan: PageLabels number tree — pages with roman-numeral labels followed by arabic labels. Example: pages 0..2 labeled "i", "ii", "iii"; pages 3..end labeled "1", "2", "3", ...
- Number tree (per spec 7.9.7): nodes can be /Kids (internal) or /Nums (leaf). Recursively walk; flatten to sorted Vec<(i64, V)>
- Number tree leaf /Nums is an array of alternating `[key value key value ...]`
- /MarkInfo missing: `is_tagged: false` (not a tagged PDF)
- /Metadata missing: conformance detection skipped; `conformance: null`
- /Root itself missing from trailer (extremely rare, only in severely corrupt files): emit STRUCT_MISSING_KEY; return empty Catalog; the document will have zero pages downstream
- /Pages is the only REQUIRED catalog entry; everything else is optional
- /Names tree is parsed by individual consumers (e.g. JavaScript bead may walk it for /JavaScript subtree); this bead just stores the ObjRef

## Acceptance criteria

- Critical test passes: PageLabels tree with mixed styles parses correctly; per-page labels accessible
- A tagged PDF (`/MarkInfo /Marked true`) sets `mark_info.is_tagged = true`
- A document with no /Outlines: `outlines_ref = None` (not an error)
- A document with /Version 2.0 in catalog: `version: Some("2.0")` (overrides header)
- A document with no /Root in trailer: STRUCT_MISSING_KEY diagnostic; empty Catalog returned
- proptest: random PdfObject as /Root content never panics parse_catalog
- INV-8 maintained

## References

- Plan section: Phase 1.4 line 1111 (document catalog from /Root); line 1129 (PageLabels)
- PDF spec 7.7.2 (Document Catalog)
- PDF spec 7.9.7 (Number Trees)
- INV-8

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the per-span text assembly logic invoked by the merger: append each glyph's codepoint to `span.text`; handle multi-codepoint glyphs (ligature expansion already done by Phase 2) by appending all codepoints in order; handle is_word_boundary glyphs by injecting " " into the PREVIOUS span before starting the new one (per the (a) implementation choice in Phase 4.1 plan note).

## Why this matters

Span text is what gets serialized to JSON and projected to plain-text output. Errors here are immediately visible to end users: missing spaces between words, broken ligatures, RTL text appearing backwards. The "boundary appended to previous span" choice ensures plain-text output round-trips correctly with simple join.

## Implementation guidance

- merge_glyphs_to_spans calls `assemble_text(span, glyph)` for each glyph appended to current span:
  - `span.text.push(glyph.codepoint)` — simple case.
  - Multi-codepoint glyphs (rare; ligature expansion in Phase 2.2): the Phase 2 resolver already emits multiple Glyph structs sharing one bbox for a ligature; per-glyph append works correctly.
- When a span break is triggered by is_word_boundary on the current glyph:
  - Before flushing the current_span, append " " to current_span.text.
  - Then flush; start new span with the boundary glyph (without leading space).
- RTL handling: spans containing primarily RTL characters (Arabic, Hebrew) are emitted in VISUAL ORDER as they appear in the content stream; Phase 4.2 line formation later applies bidi reordering for output. Span-internal text is left untouched.

## Critical considerations

- INV: span text is contiguous UTF-8; do not insert NUL or control chars.
- Soft hyphen (U+00AD) is preserved here; Phase 4.7 strips it.
- ZWJ/ZWNJ (U+200D / U+200C) are preserved here; Phase 4.7 normalizes them based on script.
- U+FFFD is preserved here; Phase 4.7 may repair via ligature/mojibake detection.
- Word boundary appended to PREVIOUS span: if there's no previous span (first glyph of page is a boundary glyph — odd but possible), skip the space injection.
- A multi-codepoint span output from one ligature glyph: glyph emits 2 chars; assemble_text appends both; bbox is the ligature's shared bbox.

## Acceptance criteria

- 5 glyphs "Hello" -> span.text == "Hello".
- 5 glyphs "Hello" + boundary + 5 glyphs "World" -> span1.text == "Hello ", span2.text == "World".
- Ligature glyph emitting (f, i) as 2 glyphs with shared bbox: span.text == "fi" (assuming same font/color/size).
- RTL Arabic span: text in source byte order (Phase 4.2 reorders at line level).
- Boundary at start of page: no space injection; first span starts cleanly.

## References

- Plan section: Phase 4.1 word-boundary implementation choice (line 1619, 1657)
issue.title: Span text assembly (word boundary handling + ligature preservation + RTL handling)

issue.description:
## Scope

Define the abstraction over PDF byte sources and implement the two local-file variants:

```rust
pub trait PdfSource: Read + Seek + Send + Sync {
    fn len(&self) -> u64;
    fn read_range(&self, offset: u64, length: usize) -> io::Result<Bytes>;
    fn prefetch(&self, offset: u64, length: usize) { let _ = (offset, length); }
}
```

Implementations:
1. **MmapSource**: memory-mapped local file via memmap2; madvise(MADV_SEQUENTIAL) on content streams
2. **FileSource**: plain Read+Seek over File; fallback when mmap fails (FUSE mounts, /proc, named pipes)

The trait is the API surface that Phase 1.1-1.5 consume; instead of taking `&[u8]`, they take `&dyn PdfSource`. This is a refactor that touches every parser module's signature.

## Implementation guidance

- bytes = "1" crate for zero-copy slice type
- memmap2 = "0.9" crate
- Bytes type allows zero-copy slicing: MmapSource's read_range returns Bytes::copy_from_slice(&mmap[offset..])
- prefetch is no-op for local files (OS page cache); HttpRangeSource overrides
- Send + Sync bounds critical: rayon page-parallelism requires concurrent reads
- MmapSource: hold Mmap alive for lifetime of source
- FileSource: wrap File in Mutex<File> because Seek requires &mut self but trait takes &self; alternatively use pread/pread64 (POSIX) or ReadFile with offset (Windows)
- Phase 1.1-1.5 signature refactor:
  - Step 1: Define PdfSource trait
  - Step 2: Implement MmapSource + FileSource
  - Step 3: Add adapter `Lexer::from_source(source, range)` alongside existing `Lexer::new(bytes)`
  - Step 4: Migrate callers one by one
  - Step 5: Deprecate `Lexer::new(bytes)` in favor of `Lexer::from_source`

## Critical considerations

- PdfSource trait must be Send+Sync (rayon page-parallelism)
- mmap failure modes: FUSE mounts, /proc files, named pipes — detect and fall back to FileSource
- mmap is unsafe: underlying file MIGHT be modified by another process; document as known limitation (single-writer expected)
- madvise(MADV_SEQUENTIAL) per-region; apply ONLY to content stream regions
- Bytes is reference-counted; cloning cheap; read_range returns Bytes so StreamDecoder doesn't have to copy
- Performance: MmapSource read_range ~1 ns + memcpy throughput (10-20 GB/sec); bottleneck is consumer
- Lexer/ObjectParser refactor non-trivial; introduce incrementally

## Acceptance criteria

- PdfSource trait defined and exported from `pdftract_core::source`
- MmapSource opens any local file; read_range returns correct bytes for arbitrary (offset, length)
- FileSource fallback when mmap fails: synthetic test with /proc file
- Lexer/ObjectParser refactor compiles; existing tests still pass
- prefetch is no-op for local sources
- Performance: MmapSource read_range of 1 MB completes < 100 microseconds
- INV-8 maintained

## References

- Plan section: Phase 1.8 lines 1227-1239
- Dependency Matrix: bytes, memmap2 (default features)
- Phase 1.1-1.5 refactor target
- INV-8
issue.title: Define PdfSource trait + MmapSource + FileSource implementations

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the map_confidence_source(unicode_source: UnicodeSource, corrected_in_4_7: bool) -> ConfidenceSource function that collapses the 6 internal UnicodeSource variants down to the 3 schema-exposed ConfidenceSource variants. Includes the Phase 4.7 correction override (corrections downgrade Native -> Heuristic).

## Why this matters

UnicodeSource is the internal high-fidelity provenance signal (which mechanism resolved each glyph's Unicode); ConfidenceSource is the simplified consumer-facing categorization. The mapping function is the one place the projection happens; getting it wrong silently miscategorizes thousands of spans in a typical document.

## Implementation guidance

- Function signature:
  ```rust
  pub fn map_confidence_source(unicode_source: UnicodeSource, corrected_in_4_7: bool) -> ConfidenceSource
  ```
- Mapping table:
  ```
  | UnicodeSource           | corrected_in_4_7 | ConfidenceSource |
  |-------------------------|------------------|------------------|
  | ToUnicode               | false            | Native           |
  | ToUnicode               | true             | Heuristic        |
  | Agl                     | false            | Native           |
  | Agl                     | true             | Heuristic        |
  | Fingerprint             | false            | Native           |
  | Fingerprint             | true             | Heuristic        |
  | ShapeMatch              | (any)            | Heuristic        |
  | Unknown                 | (any)            | Heuristic        |
  | Ocr                     | (any)            | Ocr              |
  ```
- Implementation:
  ```rust
  pub fn map_confidence_source(s: UnicodeSource, corrected: bool) -> ConfidenceSource {
      match s {
          UnicodeSource::Ocr => ConfidenceSource::Ocr,
          UnicodeSource::ShapeMatch | UnicodeSource::Unknown => ConfidenceSource::Heuristic,
          UnicodeSource::ToUnicode | UnicodeSource::Agl | UnicodeSource::Fingerprint => {
              if corrected { ConfidenceSource::Heuristic } else { ConfidenceSource::Native }
          }
      }
  }
  ```

## Critical considerations

- The corrected_in_4_7 override is the subtle bit: a Phase 4.7-corrected Unicode is no longer the original resolution, so it downgrades from Native to Heuristic regardless of the original source
- OCR is never affected by corrected_in_4_7 (corrections apply to vector text, not raster)
- Exhaustive match on UnicodeSource variants; adding a new UnicodeSource variant requires a match-arm update (compiler-enforced)
- The mapping is one-way; there's no reverse function (multiple UnicodeSource variants map to the same ConfidenceSource)

## Acceptance criteria

- Unit test for each (UnicodeSource, corrected) combination produces the documented ConfidenceSource
- ToUnicode + corrected=true → Heuristic (override applies)
- Ocr + corrected=true → Ocr (override does NOT apply to OCR)
- Exhaustive match: adding a hypothetical UnicodeSource::Fallback to the enum causes a compiler error in this function until a match arm is added
- INV-9 mapping table documented in code comments

## References

- Plan section: Phase 4 UnicodeSource → ConfidenceSource mapping
- INV-9 stable taxonomy
- Phase 4.7 correction phase (source of the corrected_in_4_7 flag)
- Coordinator: pdftract-1f8we (parent)
- Sibling: ConfidenceSource enum
Labels: classifier, mapping, phase-4
issue.title: UnicodeSource -> ConfidenceSource mapping function (6 internal -> 3 schema variants)

## Scope

Implement consistent error JSON response shape: {"error":"CODE","message":"..."} for all 4xx and 5xx responses. Includes custom RequestBodyLimit rejection handler converting tower-http's default text/plain 413 response into a JSON body. Status-code mapping: 400 bad request, 413 payload too large, 422 extraction error, 500 internal.

## Why this matters

API consumers need a single error-parsing strategy. Mixing text/plain (default tower-http) and application/json (handler errors) breaks generic client logic. The custom rejection handler is specifically called out in the plan (line 2130) because tower-http's default is text/plain.

## Implementation guidance

- Define an ApiError struct: { error: String, message: String, hint: Option<String> }
- IntoResponse impl: (StatusCode, Json(ApiError)) tuple; Content-Type application/json
- RequestBodyLimit custom rejection: register via Router::layer(RequestBodyLimitLayer::new(N * 1024 * 1024)) + Router::layer(HandleErrorLayer::new(rejection_handler))
- rejection_handler signature: (request: Request<Body>, response: Response) -> Response; convert default 413 text to JSON
- Mapping from internal errors to status codes:
  - multipart parse error -> 400, code BAD_REQUEST
  - missing required field -> 400, code MISSING_FIELD
  - non-PDF file upload -> 400, code NOT_A_PDF
  - body > limit -> 413, code REQUEST_TOO_LARGE
  - extraction error (encrypted, corrupt) -> 422, code from Diagnostic
  - panic / unexpected -> 500, code INTERNAL
- All error responses include hint field when actionable

## Critical considerations

- The 413 JSON body MUST be {"error":"REQUEST_TOO_LARGE","message":"Request body exceeds the configured limit"} per plan critical test (line 2145)
- Status codes are NOT negotiable post-1.0 (clients depend on them)
- 422 (Unprocessable Entity) for extraction-failed-but-request-was-valid; 400 for malformed-request
- 500 includes a tracing-tag for ops to correlate with logs
- DO NOT leak internal error details in 500 messages; keep generic ("Internal error during extraction")

## Acceptance criteria

- File over size limit -> 413 with custom JSON body (critical test)
- Encrypted PDF -> 422 with code "ENCRYPTED" and a helpful hint
- Corrupt PDF -> 422 with code "CORRUPT_PDF"
- Missing "file" multipart field -> 400 with code "MISSING_FIELD"
- All 4xx/5xx responses Content-Type: application/json

## References

- Plan section: Phase 6.4 error responses (lines 2121-2130) + critical tests (line 2145)
issue.title: 6.4.4: Error JSON body shape + custom RequestBodyLimit rejection handler

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the page-to-raster pipeline that produces a Tesseract-ready GrayImage for every Scanned page and for the image-heavy cells of every Hybrid page. Two-tier rendering architecture: direct image compositing (default, no extra deps, > 90% of scanned PDFs) and pdfium-render via the full-render feature for complex geometry. Includes DPI selection logic (300/400/200 for body/fine/JBIG2), Hybrid cell routing, and the bbox-overlap merge rule (vector wins where overlap > 50%) needed in 4.x assembly.

## Why this matters

This sub-phase determines the binary-size headroom for the OCR-enabled image, which is gated at 120 MB. Going to pdfium-render by default would blow the budget (~140 MB). Direct compositing keeps the standard pdftract:ocr image lean; pdfium-render is opt-in via pdftract:full. It also determines OCR accuracy: wrong DPI = bad recognition, wrong compositing = missed content.

## Implementation guidance

- Two-tier architecture in pdftract-ocr::render module
- Default (no full-render feature): direct compositing path collects image XObjects from Phase 1.5 stream decoder, decodes each, composites onto blank canvas per CTM (cm/Do operators), output as image::GrayImage
- full-render path: pdfium-render renders page; entry point lives behind cfg(feature = "full_render"); runtime ExtractionOptions.full_render gate
- DPI selection logic: parse font_size signal from Phase 4 spans; > 8pt body -> 300, smaller -> 400; JBIG2 image filter -> 200 (already binary)
- Hybrid page handling: render only the cells in PageClassification::hybrid_cells set; emit per-cell GrayImage with (cell_index, image) tuples
- Bbox merge rule (called from 4.x text assembly): given a vector-span bbox and an OCR-span bbox, compute IoU; if > 0.5, prefer vector span

## Critical considerations

- Binary-size CI gate (120 MB for pdftract:ocr) MUST hold; this is the reason for the two-tier design
- pdfium-render adds ~20 MB native library — tracked against weight target; document if enabled in default Docker image
- Standard image tags: pdftract:latest, pdftract:ocr built with --features ocr,serve only; pdftract:full has --features ocr,serve,full-render (140 MB budget, documented as heavyweight variant)
- CTM math from Phase 1 must already be correct (Q/q stack); compositing reuses it
- JBIG2 OCR requires full-render feature (Phase 1.5 filter notes)
- Hybrid cell rendering must NOT re-decode the entire page per cell; decode once, crop per cell

## Acceptance criteria

- All Phase 5.2 child task beads closed
- Pure-image-XObject scanned PDF fixture renders correctly via direct compositing (visual diff < 1% vs. reference)
- pdfium-render fixture (complex image masks + soft masks) renders correctly with --features full-render
- DPI selection matches plan table for body / fine-print / JBIG2 fixtures
- Hybrid page renders only image-heavy cells; vector-only cells skipped (verified by per-cell trace)
- Bbox merge unit test: vector span IoU 0.6 with OCR span -> vector wins; IoU 0.3 -> both kept
- Binary size CI gate (pdftract:ocr <= 120 MB) passes

## References

- Plan section: Phase 5.2 (lines 1846-1867)
- weight target table (Phase 0)
- INV-11 binary-size budget
- Phase 1.5 filter notes (JBIG2 decoding)

issue.description:
## Scope

Linearized PDFs (PDF 1.2+ Optimized for Web View) have a SPECIAL structure: the first object after the header is a Linearization dictionary, and there are TWO xref tables — one at the beginning (covering only the first-page objects) and one at the end (the complete xref).

The detector:
1. Checks for `/Linearized` dict in the first object of the file (typically at byte offset just after the `%PDF-X.Y\n` header)
2. If found:
   a. Parses the partial xref at the beginning (first-page xref)
   b. Parses the complete xref at the end (full xref)
   c. Merges with FULL XREF TAKING PRECEDENCE for any object number present in both
   d. Parses the `/H` (hint stream offset) entry for page-offset hints (used by Phase 1.8 remote prefetch)
3. The forward-scan fallback is DISABLED for linearized files (it would find the partial leading xref and incorrectly stop)

## Implementation guidance

- Public API: `detect_linearization(source: &PdfSource) -> Option<LinearizationInfo>` + `load_xref_linearized(source: &PdfSource, lin_info: LinearizationInfo) -> XrefSection`
- LinearizationInfo: `{ first_page_xref_offset: u64, full_xref_offset: u64, hint_stream_offset: Option<u64>, page_offset_hints: Vec<u64> }`
- Detection algorithm:
  1. Read the first ~2 KB of the file
  2. Skip the `%PDF-X.Y\n` header (~10 bytes)
  3. Look for `obj` keyword; parse the indirect object at that offset
  4. Check if the parsed dict has `/Linearized` (a number, typically 1.0). If yes, this is the lin-dict
  5. Extract `/L` (total file length), `/H` (hint stream offset+length pair), `/E` (first-page end offset), `/N` (number of pages), `/T` (first-page xref offset)
  6. The `/T` value is the offset of the FIRST-PAGE xref; `startxref` at the END of the file gives the FULL xref
- Merger:
  1. Load first-page xref via traditional/stream strategies starting at `/T`
  2. Load full xref via traditional/stream strategies starting at `startxref` (EOF)
  3. Merge: full xref's entries WIN for any conflict (per plan spec)

## Critical considerations

- KU-7 (acceptance criterion): linearized PDF and its non-linearized equivalent must produce identical fingerprint. The fingerprint excludes xref byte layout (ADR-008), so this works automatically IF the resolved object map is the same — and it IS, because full-xref-priority means we use the same logical map a non-linearized file would have
- Critical test: linearization fixture with 100 pages — first-page xref covers ~10 objects, full xref covers all ~500 objects; the merged map has 500 entries with full-xref values
- The `/H` (hint stream) is OPTIONAL but commonly present; pdftract parses it for Phase 1.8 remote-source prefetch optimization (page offset hints accelerate random-access page loading). Without hints, remote source still works but does more fetches
- The hint stream itself is a flate-decoded stream of byte offsets and lengths per page; parsing is a separate concern (out of scope for this bead — Phase 1.8 has its own bead for hint stream parsing)
- The /Linearized dict's /L (file length) MUST match the actual file size; if not, the file was modified after linearization (incremental update). In that case, the linearization is invalid; fall through to non-linearized path (load /Prev chain from EOF startxref)
- The /Linearized dict's /T (first-page xref offset) MUST point to a valid xref structure; if invalid, fall through to non-linearized path
- Forward scan disabled rule: the resolver's main dispatch checks `is_linearized` before falling through to strategy 4
- Per plan: the hint stream is not required for correctness; only for performance

## Acceptance criteria

- Critical test passes: linearized 100-page fixture — merged xref has the right object count and all objects dereferenceable
- KU-7 acceptance: fingerprint of linearized fixture == fingerprint of qpdf-linearization-removed copy
- A non-linearized file: detect_linearization returns None; full path proceeds via /Prev chain
- A linearized file that was incrementally edited (file size != /L): linearization invalidated, full path used
- A linearized file with no /H: hint_stream_offset is None; remote source still works (slower)
- proptest: random byte sequences as lin-dict never panic
- INV-8 maintained

- ADR-008 (fingerprint excludes xref byte layout)
- Phase 1.8 (remote source uses hint stream for prefetch)

issue.description:
## Scope

Convert HocrWord pixel bboxes (from 5.4.3) back to PDF user-space coordinates, accounting for the 10 px white border added in 5.3.4 and the DPI used at 5.2 render time. Emit a Vec<Span> with confidence_source = "ocr", text = HocrWord.text, bbox in PDF pt, and confidence = x_wconf/100.0.

## Why this matters

Without correct coordinate conversion, OCR-emitted spans land at wrong positions on the page, breaking everything downstream: reading order (4.5), bbox-merge with vector spans (5.2.4), Hybrid page merge, receipts (6.8). The 10px padding is a frequent off-by-N source — must be inverted explicitly.

## Implementation guidance

- Coordinate transform: HOCR pixel space -> input image pixel space -> PDF pt
- Step 1: subtract padding (10 px on each side from 5.3.4) -> pre-pad image pixel coords
- Step 2: scale by 72.0 / dpi -> PDF pt (HOCR origin is top-left, PDF origin is bottom-left so Y must flip)
- Step 3: Y-flip: pdf_y = page_height_pt - hocr_y_pt
- Emit Span { text, bbox, font: None, size: None, color: None, rendering_mode: Fill, confidence, confidence_source: "ocr", lang: opts.ocr_language.first().cloned(), flags: 0 }
- Page rotation: if the page was rotated for rendering, apply inverse rotation to the bbox before emitting

## Critical considerations

- 10 px padding must be subtracted in pixel space (before DPI scale) — not in pt space
- Y-axis flip is the #1 source of OCR bbox bugs; add a sanity test verifying word at top of page has highest PDF Y, not lowest
- DPI must match the DPI used in 5.2 rendering; pass it through, do not recompute
- Bbox precision: store as f32 pt to 0.1 pt resolution; HOCR is integer-pixel so derived pt is exact within 0.1
- Hybrid cell handling: OCR done on cell crop, so HOCR coords are cell-local; offset by cell origin before global PDF conversion

## Acceptance criteria

- Critical test (line 1908): HOCR bbox at (10,10,100,30) at 300 DPI on letter-size page -> PDF bbox approximately at expected pt coords (verify via known fixture)
- Y-flip sanity: top-of-page word has highest PDF Y; bottom-of-page word has lowest
- Hybrid cell test: OCR word in cell (3, 2) gets correct global PDF coords
- 100-page OCR output: all spans have valid bboxes inside the page rect

## References

- Plan section: Phase 5.4 HOCR pixel-to-PDF conversion (line 1899) + critical test (line 1908)
- INV-7 confidence_source

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the all_tr3_with_full_page_image signal evaluator. Maps every text operator having Tr=3 AND a single image XObject covering >= 95% of page area -> BrokenVector with strength 0.99 (definitive).

## Why this matters

This is the classic BrokenVector signature: invisible text (Tr=3) overlaid on a full-page raster scan. PDF/A optimizer tools and many scanner outputs produce this layout. Detecting it as definitive lets the BrokenVector pipeline (Phase 5.5) kick in with full OCR re-extraction.

## Implementation guidance

- Signature:
  ```rust
  pub fn all_tr3_with_full_page_image(ctx: &PageContext) -> Option<Signal>
  ```
- Logic:
  ```rust
  let all_tr3 = ctx.text_op_count > 0 && ctx.tr3_op_count == ctx.text_op_count;
  let full_page_image = ctx.image_xobject_areas.iter().any(|area| area / ctx.page_area_pt2 >= 0.95);
  if all_tr3 && full_page_image {
      return Some(Signal { name: \"all_tr3_with_full_page_image\", strength: 0.99, vote: PageClass::BrokenVector });
  }
  None
  ```

## Critical considerations

- Cite EC-12: Tr=3 + full-page-image is a deterministic BrokenVector signal
- tr3_op_count counts text operators with rendering_mode==3 (invisible)
- Single image >= 95% page area; the iter().any uses 0.95 as the threshold
- All text ops being Tr=3 (not just some) is required; a mix indicates intentional invisible overlay (e.g. searchable PDF) and is BrokenVector, but a mix without full-page image is ambiguous
- strength 0.99 makes this definitively top-rank; short-circuits all other evaluators

## Acceptance criteria

- text_op_count=10, tr3_op_count=10, full_page_image=true → Some(Signal { 0.99, BrokenVector })
- text_op_count=10, tr3_op_count=5 → None (mix of Tr=3 and visible)
- text_op_count=0 → None (no text)
- full_page_image=false → None
- Unit tests

## References

- Plan section: Phase 5.1.2
- EC-12 (Tr=3 + full-page-image)
- Coordinator: pdftract-22p (parent)

issue.close_reason: All acceptance criteria PASS: 16 hex string unit tests + 2 proptests. Implementation verified: odd-length zero padding (\x40 not \x04), embedded whitespace handling, mixed case, invalid char diagnostics, unterminated string handling. See notes/pdftract-2hm4.md for details. Commits: cfb7848 (proptests), 4bd3302 (diagnostic rename), edce55c (keyword lexer fixes).
issue.description:
## Scope

Lex hex string tokens of the form `<...>` from the byte slice. Produces `Token::String(Vec<u8>)` of decoded bytes. Handles:

- Hex digit pairs: `<48656C6C6F>` -> bytes `Hello`
- Embedded whitespace (PDF spec 7.2.2 whitespace) ignored between digits
- Odd-length input: the final unpaired nibble is treated as the HIGH nibble of a final byte with LOW nibble 0. Example: `<4>` -> `\x40` (NOT `\x04`)
- Both lowercase and uppercase hex digits accepted (`<aB>` valid)
- Terminator: `>`
- Distinguish from dict delimiter `<<` and `>>` — see the structural-token lexer bead for how the dispatch table decides

## Implementation guidance

- Entry condition: `<` followed by a NON-`<` byte (a dict opens with `<<`)
- Maintain: `current_nibble: Option<u8>` and `out: Vec<u8>`
- For each byte after the opening `<`:
  - If `>`: terminate. If `current_nibble` is `Some(hi)`, push final byte `(hi << 4)` (the low nibble is implicitly 0)
  - If hex digit: parse to 0..15; if `current_nibble.is_some()`, combine and push; otherwise store
  - If whitespace (per PDF spec 7.2.2): skip
  - Otherwise: emit `STRUCT_INVALID_HEX` diagnostic and skip the byte
- EOF before `>`: emit `STRUCT_UNTERMINATED_STRING` diagnostic, return collected bytes (with the dangling nibble padded as above)

## Critical considerations

- Critical test from plan: `<4>` -> `\x40` (one byte 0x40, NOT `\x04`). The trailing zero nibble is LOW, not HIGH. This is the opposite of intuition and a common bug
- Critical test: `<48656C6C6F>` -> `b"Hello"` (5 bytes)
- Embedded whitespace test: `<48 65 6C\n6C 6F>` -> `b"Hello"`; whitespace is ignored, not part of nibble accumulation
- Mixed case test: `<aB48cD>` -> `\xAB\x48\xCD` (3 bytes)
- Invalid characters test: `<48Z65>` emits `STRUCT_INVALID_HEX` for the `Z` and produces `\x48\x65` (the Z is dropped, not used)
- Unterminated test: `<4865` at EOF -> `\x48\x65\x00` (the final nibble pads to 0x00? No — `\x48\x65` is two complete bytes; if there's a third dangling nibble, e.g. `<48657>`, we'd get `\x48\x65\x70`). At EOF with no `>`, emit `STRUCT_UNTERMINATED_STRING` and pad whatever dangling nibble exists
- The `<` byte itself never appears inside a hex string (no escape); it would terminate the string improperly. If found, emit `STRUCT_INVALID_HEX` and skip

## Acceptance criteria

- All Critical tests pass:
  - `<>` -> `b""`
  - `<4>` -> `b"\x40"` (NOT `\x04`)
  - `<48656C6C6F>` -> `b"Hello"`
  - `<aBcD>` -> `b"\xAB\xCD"`
  - `<48 65>` -> `b"Hello"`-prefix `\x48\x65`, whitespace ignored
  - Unterminated `<48` at EOF -> `\x48` plus `STRUCT_UNTERMINATED_STRING`
- proptest property: random byte sequences starting with `<` (not `<<`) never panic
- proptest property: any decode followed by re-encode (via a sibling encoder) produces input-equivalent bytes (or differs only in case + whitespace)
- INV-8 maintained

## References

- Plan section: Phase 1.1 Lexer, line 1032-1033 (hex strings, odd-length zero padding); line 1046 (critical test for hex string odd length)
- PDF spec 7.3.4.3 (Hexadecimal Strings)
issue.title: Implement PDF hex string lexer with odd-length zero padding

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the indicatif-based progress bar that ticks every 100 ms with the current file + page-within-file information. Guarantee an update every 500 ms even when a single file blocks for a long time (watchdog ticker on a dedicated thread). Show files done / total, throughput in MB/s, ETA. Default on TTY, off non-TTY; --progress forces on, --no-progress forces off.

## Why this matters

The progress bar is the single most important user-experience element of pdftract grep: the difference between "this works" and "this hangs". Users wait at terminals; a stalled bar (even with active work) makes them kill the process. The 500 ms guarantee is the contract; any per-file or per-page operation that takes longer than 500 ms must still produce a tick via the watchdog.

## Implementation guidance

- Crate: indicatif = "0.17"
- Multi-progress: one main bar (overall progress) + one "Current" sub-bar (per-file)
- Main bar template: "Searching: [{wide_bar}] {pos}/{len} files ({percent}%) {bytes_per_sec} ETA {eta}"
- Sub-bar template: "Current: {msg}" where msg = "<path> (page {pages_done}/{pages_total})"
- Initialise on start with files_total, bytes_total (from 7.8.3 producer)
- Consume ProgressEvent::FileStart, FileProgress, FileDone, FileSkipped from worker channel; update bars accordingly
- 100 ms internal ticker (indicatif's enable_steady_tick(100ms)) keeps the spinner alive even when no events arrive
- Watchdog: separate thread that polls last_event_time atomic; if > 500 ms elapsed, force a redraw with the same message (no-op for the user but the terminal cursor confirms liveness)
- TTY detection: is_terminal::is_terminal(stdout()) - if false, no bar even with --progress (CI logs would be polluted otherwise)
- Disable when --quiet, --json (unless --progress-json explicitly set), or --no-progress
- Slow-file warning: separate per-file timer in workers; emits ProgressEvent::SlowFile { path, elapsed_secs } at 30s; sink prints to stderr "WARNING: file <path> still processing after <secs>s" while keeping bar visible
- On done: bar shows final stats: "Searched: 512 files (104 MB) in 18.4s (78 MB/s) - 1287 matches"

## Critical considerations

- Watchdog 500 ms guarantee is the user-experience contract (acceptance criterion)
- indicatif's enable_steady_tick alone is not enough for very long file operations - the watchdog adds explicit liveness
- Bar lines printed to stderr (not stdout) so they don't pollute --json output redirection
- ANSI color disabled when NO_COLOR env var set
- TTY detection on non-TTY: no bar, but ProgressEvents still consumed (sink drains channel; otherwise workers block)
- Multi-progress order: main bar on top, Current sub-bar below; cleared on done

## Acceptance criteria

- Bar updates >= every 500 ms during 1000-file grep
- 5 GB slow file in middle: bar continues ticking; slow-file warning at 30s
- Non-TTY: no bar; workers still process correctly
- --no-progress forces off even on TTY
- Bar goes to stderr; --json output to stdout uncontaminated
- Final summary line printed on done

## References

- Plan section: 7.8 lines 2727-2729 (--progress, --no-progress, --progress-json), 2755-2765 (bar template + ticker), 2776-2777 (slow-file warning), 2792 (acceptance criterion >= 500 ms)
- indicatif crate
- 7.8.4 (ProgressEvent source)
- 7.8.5 (stdout coexistence)
- 7.8.9 (--progress-json alternative)
issue.title: 7.8.8: Progress bar (indicatif) with 100ms ticker + 500ms-guarantee watchdog

issue.close_reason: Implemented pdftract cache subcommand with stats/clear/purge actions, global --cache-dir/--cache-size/--no-cache flags, X-Pdftract-Cache HTTP header, and metadata.cache_status/cache_age_seconds JSON fields. All acceptance criteria verified: cache stats on empty dir returns 0 entries, clear/purge commands work correctly, cache integration in extract and serve modes is functional. Commit e2c1e28.
issue.description:
## Scope

Surface the cache as user-visible CLI and HTTP affordances:

- pdftract cache subcommand with stats / clear / purge actions
- Global flags on all extract-style subcommands: --cache-dir DIR, --cache-size SIZE, --no-cache
- HTTP serve mode adds X-Pdftract-Cache: hit | miss | skipped response header
- JSON output adds metadata.cache_status and metadata.cache_age_seconds

Modules: crates/pdftract-cli/src/cache_cmd.rs (subcommand); CLI flag definitions in cli.rs; HTTP handler integration in serve.rs.

## Why this matters

The cache primitives (siblings 6.9.1-6.9.5) are internal; users need a discoverable interface to enable, configure, inspect, and clean the cache. The pdftract cache subcommand is the operator's dashboard: pdftract cache stats DIR shows hit ratio, size, age distribution; pdftract cache clear DIR is the panic button; pdftract cache purge --older-than 30d is the routine maintenance call.

The X-Pdftract-Cache HTTP header lets reverse-proxy logs and monitoring dashboards visualize cache hit ratio at the network layer without parsing JSON bodies. The metadata.cache_status field in JSON output serves the same purpose for batch/CLI extractions.

## Implementation guidance

### Subcommands

- pdftract cache stats DIR — prints:
  ```
  Entries: 1842
  Total size: 487.3 MiB compressed / 4.1 GiB uncompressed (8.5x ratio)
  Hit ratio (since last clear): 67.3% (12,841 hits / 19,082 total)
  Oldest entry: 14d 3h ago
  Newest entry: 12s ago
  Age histogram: <1h: 12.4%, <1d: 38.1%, <7d: 41.2%, <30d: 7.3%, >30d: 1.0%
  ```
- pdftract cache stats DIR --json — emits JSON shape matching the above as fields
- pdftract cache clear DIR — deletes all entries (NOT index.json or sentinel); prompts for confirmation unless -y
- pdftract cache purge DIR --older-than 30d — deletes entries with last-touched > 30d (parsed by humantime crate, already in deps)
- pdftract cache purge DIR --version \"<1.0.0\" — deletes entries with extraction_version satisfying the version constraint (semver crate, already in deps)

### Global flags on extract-style subcommands

- --cache-dir DIR — enable cache for the call; create DIR if absent; default is unset (no cache unless serve subcommand has it default-on)
- --cache-size SIZE — set the LRU size limit (default 1 GiB); accepts suffixes (1 KiB, 1 MiB, 1 GiB) via the humansize-parsing helper
- --no-cache — disable the cache at this call site even if --cache-dir is set globally (e.g. via env var)

### HTTP serve integration

- X-Pdftract-Cache: hit | miss | skipped response header on /extract, /extract/text, /extract/stream
- \"hit\": served from cache
- \"miss\": ran extraction; populated cache
- \"skipped\": cache not configured for this server OR --no-cache equivalent OR streaming mode (never serves from cache, but populates)

### JSON output integration

- metadata.cache_status: \"hit\" | \"miss\" | \"skipped\" (always present in JSON output when cache is configured)
- metadata.cache_age_seconds: N — present only when cache_status == \"hit\"; integer seconds

## Critical considerations

- --no-cache must completely bypass cache code paths (no key hashing, no fs touches) — zero overhead acceptance criterion
- Cache-stats command uses the index.json metadata where possible; only walks the directory if the index is missing or stale
- Hit ratio tracking: maintained in index.json as cumulative counters since last cache clear; reset on pdftract cache clear
- humantime crate for --older-than parsing: \"30d\", \"7d\", \"1h\" all supported
- pdftract cache purge with no flag deletes nothing and prints a help message
- The pdftract cache subcommand does not require the serve or any other feature beyond cache itself
- Confirmation prompt on clear is interactive (read /dev/tty); -y bypasses; refuse in non-TTY contexts without -y
- X-Pdftract-Cache header is set BEFORE the response body is streamed (Axum: insert into response headers in the handler return)
- For streaming mode (/extract/stream), the header is \"skipped\" — never \"hit\" — but cache IS populated when the stream completes successfully

## Acceptance criteria

- pdftract cache stats /tmp/c on an empty dir → \"Entries: 0\" (plan critical test: \"pdftract cache stats on an empty dir: reports zero entries cleanly\")
- pdftract cache stats /tmp/c on a populated dir → correct entry count + size + ratios
- pdftract cache clear /tmp/c -y → all entries deleted; index.json + sentinel preserved
- pdftract cache purge /tmp/c --older-than 30d → entries older than 30 days deleted; newer preserved
- pdftract extract --cache-dir /tmp/c file.pdf (first run) → metadata.cache_status: \"miss\"; cache populated
- pdftract extract --cache-dir /tmp/c file.pdf (second run, same options) → metadata.cache_status: \"hit\"; metadata.cache_age_seconds present
- pdftract extract --cache-dir /tmp/c --no-cache file.pdf → metadata.cache_status: \"skipped\"; cache not touched
- curl -F file=@x.pdf http://localhost:8080/extract → response header X-Pdftract-Cache present with hit/miss/skipped value
- pdftract --no-cache extract file.pdf (no --cache-dir) → no cache code reached; no fs operations on any cache dir
- --cache-size 4GiB parsed as 4 * 1024^3 bytes; --cache-size 4G also accepted (humansize)
- Plan critical test passes: \"pdftract cache stats on an empty dir: reports zero entries cleanly\"

## References

- Plan section: Phase 6.9 Content-Addressed Cache Layer (lines 2441-2447, 2455-2457)
- Sibling 6.9.4 (LRU limit driven by --cache-size)
- Phase 6.1 JSON schema (metadata.cache_status field added here)
- Phase 6.4 HTTP serve (X-Pdftract-Cache header)
- humantime crate for --older-than parsing
- semver crate for --version constraints
Labels: cache, cli, http, phase-6
issue.title: 6.9.6: pdftract cache subcommand + --cache-dir/--cache-size/--no-cache + X-Pdftract-Cache header

issue.close_reason: Implemented lookup_shape with HAMMING_MAX constant (8), exact match optimization via binary search, and frequency tie-breaking. All 24 shape module tests pass. Commit b30f6d0. Verification note at notes/pdftract-2iur.md
issue.description:
## Scope

Implement `pub fn lookup_shape(phash: u64) -> Option<char>` that linearly scans `SHAPE_TABLE`, computes `(phash ^ entry_hash).count_ones()` for each entry, collects all entries with Hamming distance <= 8, and returns the entry with the SMALLEST distance. Ties broken by Unicode frequency rank (lower rank = more common = wins) via `FREQ_TABLE`. Returns None if no entry within Hamming distance 8.

## Why this matters

The lookup function IS the Level 4 entry point that the resolver state machine calls. Its precision (low Hamming threshold) and recall (frequency tie-break) directly determine the accuracy of L4 recovery. The "<= 8" threshold is the plan-specified maximum-tolerance value where false-positive rate begins to dominate.

## Implementation guidance

- Linear scan: `SHAPE_TABLE.iter().enumerate().for_each(...)` — branchless inner loop, count_ones is a single CPU instruction on x86_64 (POPCNT) and aarch64 (CNT).
- Track best so far: `(min_distance, best_idx)`. On tie, fetch FREQ_TABLE[idx_a].1 vs FREQ_TABLE[idx_b].1 and prefer lower freq rank.
- Threshold constant: `const HAMMING_MAX: u32 = 8;` at module level.
- Optionally, before linear scan, attempt exact match via binary search on SHAPE_TABLE (it's sorted by pHash) — early-exit on distance 0.

## Critical considerations

- INV: result MUST be deterministic — given same SHAPE_TABLE and FREQ_TABLE, lookup_shape(h) returns the same Option<char> across runs.
- Performance: 5000 entries x ~10 ns per iter = 50 us worst case. Acceptable per plan budget. If performance becomes an issue, switch to a multi-table-LSH structure (future work, not v0.1.0).
- count_ones uses the `u64::count_ones()` intrinsic; on platforms without hardware popcount, LLVM lowers to software — still acceptable.
- Empty SHAPE_TABLE -> always returns None (no panic).
- HAMMING_MAX threshold should NOT be configurable at runtime in v0.1.0 (configurability adds API surface for marginal value); document the choice.

## Acceptance criteria

- A pHash matching an entry exactly returns that entry's char.
- A pHash differing by 4 bits from one entry returns that entry's char.
- A pHash differing by 9 bits from every entry returns None.
- Ties broken by frequency rank: if two entries have distance 5 and one is char 'e' (rank 5) vs 'q' (rank 1000), 'e' wins.
- Empty SHAPE_TABLE returns None.
- Benchmark: lookup_shape over 5000 entries < 50 us.

## References

- Plan section: Phase 2.5 Query algorithm (line 1424)
issue.title: Runtime nearest-neighbor scanner with Hamming distance + frequency tie-break

## Scope

Define the PageClass enum with the four variants: Vector, Scanned, Hybrid, BrokenVector. Derives Copy, Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize. issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the rule evaluation engine: given the precomputed feature signals (5.6.3) and a list of profiles (5.6.4 builtins or 7.10 user-loaded), evaluate every profile's predicates, compute per-profile scores, return ClassificationResult { document_type, confidence, reasons, runner_up, runner_up_confidence }.

## Why this matters

This is where the classification decision happens. The engine is small (~50 LOC as planned) but its policy choices (score normalization, reason aggregation, tie-breaking) directly determine accuracy on the 200-doc corpus gate.

## Implementation guidance

- Entry: fn classify(signals: &FeatureSignals, profiles: &[Profile]) -> ClassificationResult
- For each profile:
  - For each predicate, evaluate against signals; if matched, sum predicate.weight; collect a Reason string
  - Profile score = sum_of_matched_weights / sum_of_all_weights (normalized to [0,1])
- Pick profile with highest score; if score >= profile.threshold (default 0.6), set document_type = profile.type
- Otherwise document_type = unknown, confidence = best_score (still report so users can see how close)
- runner_up = second-highest scoring profile
- Reasons: top-K (default 5) matched-predicate descriptions in priority order
- Predicate evaluation dispatch:
  - TextContains: count substring hits across signals.text_pattern_hits; match if >= min_hits
  - StructuralHasTable: signals.table_block_count >= min_count
  - PageCountInRange: signals.page_count in [min, max]
  - etc.

## Critical considerations

- Tie-breaking: when two profiles tie on score, pick the one with the most specific (higher predicate count) profile; secondary tiebreak is alphabetical for determinism
- Reason aggregation: must be reproducible (Vec sorted by predicate.weight desc, then by name)
- regex compilation: lazy_static or once_cell::Lazy per profile; never recompile per document
- Profile loading errors (malformed YAML, invalid regex) must surface as PROFILE_INVALID diagnostic, NOT silently drop the profile

## Acceptance criteria

- Unit tests: synthetic FeatureSignals + a hand-crafted profile -> expected ClassificationResult
- Reason ordering reproducible: same inputs -> same reasons in same order
- Tie-breaking deterministic: synthetic two-way tie -> consistent winner
- Score normalization: a profile with one matched predicate weight 1.0 out of total 10.0 -> score 0.1; not 1.0
- runner_up correctly populated when present, None when only one profile scored > 0

## References

- Plan section: Phase 5.6 classifier design (line 1931)
- INV-13 reproducibility
issue.title: 5.6.2: Classifier engine (evaluate all profiles, pick highest above threshold, emit reasons)

issue.description:
## Scope

Sequential post-processing pass after rayon page assembly. Sliding window of 4 pages; for each block in top 7% OR bottom 7% of any page, compare text against same-position blocks on next 3 pages via strsim Levenshtein at UNICODE CHAR LEVEL. If lev_distance <= 5% of text length AND block appears on >= 3 consecutive pages: classify as Header (top 7%) or Footer (bottom 7%).

## Why this matters

Headers/footers are noise in 95% of extraction use cases. Pdfminer.six does NOT have this — major usability differentiator.

## Implementation guidance

- Crate: strsim::levenshtein (byte-level); use strsim::generic_levenshtein with Vec<char> for char-level.
- Sliding window: pages [i, i+1, i+2, i+3].
- Position window: bbox.top >= 0.93 * page_height (top 7%) OR bbox.bottom <= 0.07 * page_height (bottom 7%).
- Same-position: matching y-range AND column (or full-width).
- Pass runs after all per-page rayon assembly.

## Critical considerations

- INV: char-level Levenshtein (not byte); critical for CJK.
- 5% threshold accommodates page-number differences.
- 7% page-height window: 43pt zone on 612pt page.
- 3+ consecutive required (prevents one-off detection).
- "Sliding window of 4" INCLUDES current page.

## Acceptance criteria

- 10 pages with identical "ACME Corp" in top 7%: all 10 Headers.
- 10 pages "Page 1..10 of 10" in bottom 7%: Footers (lev < 5%).
- 2 pages identical, 8 without: NOT classified.
- Different columns: NOT matched.

## References

- Plan section: Phase 4.4 Sequencing note (line 1703)
issue.title: Header/footer cross-page dedup (strsim Levenshtein, top/bottom 7%, 3+ pages)

## Scope

Coordinator for sub-phase 3.4: track BMC/BDC/EMC marked-content sequences and populate the `mcid: Option<u32>` field on each emitted Glyph with the innermost MCID currently in scope. Also handle Optional Content Group (OCG) /OC tags: glyphs inside an OCG whose default state is OFF are STILL emitted but flagged for downstream filtering.

## Why this matters

Marked content is how tagged PDFs link glyphs to the StructTree (which Phase 7.1 exploits for accurate reading order on accessible PDFs). Without MCID tracking, the link is broken and tagged PDFs fall back to XY-cut heuristics. OCG handling lets us optionally suppress hidden layers (watermarks, comments).

## Children

- BMC / BDC / EMC operator parsers + marked-content stack
- MCID propagation to emit_glyph wrapper (sets Glyph.mcid)
- OCG /OC tag tracking + default-OFF detection via /OCProperties

## Critical considerations

- The marked-content stack is a Vec<MarkedContentFrame { tag: Arc<str>, mcid: Option<u32> }>; the INNERMOST frame's mcid wins for enclosed glyphs.
- BMC has no properties (tag only, no MCID).
- BDC has either a name (referring to /Properties resource) or an inline dict; extract MCID from the /MCID key if present.
- EMC without matching BMC: ignored, no panic.
- OCG /OC tagged content: look up /OCProperties /D /OFF list (default OFF OCGs) at page level; if OCG is OFF, set a flag on the glyph (don't drop — Phase 4.6 filters).

## Acceptance criteria

- All 3 children closed.
- Nested BDC: innermost MCID wins for enclosed glyphs.
- EMC without matching BMC: ignored, no panic.
- MCID 0: valid (zero is a legal MCID).
- OCG default OFF: glyphs inside emitted with `is_hidden` flag (to be added).

## References

- Plan section: Phase 3.4 Marked Content Tracking (lines 1577-1590)

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the PDF-password ingress channels: --password-stdin flag (reads one newline-terminated line from stdin), PDFTRACT_PASSWORD env var, Python password= kwarg, MCP password body field, serve password form field. Reject plain --password VALUE unless PDFTRACT_INSECURE_CLI_PASSWORD=1 is set, in which case emit a stderr warning and mask the value in any internal echo.

## Why this matters

TH-07 (line 878) mandates this exact ingress matrix to prevent password disclosure via the process arg list. ps aux on any multi-user system reveals --password VALUE to every other user; the env var, stdin, and form-field ingress all close this hole. The plan defines the rejection-with-opt-in escape hatch so that legitimate one-off interactive use is not entirely blocked but is loud and intentional.

## Implementation guidance

- Files to modify:
  - pdftract-cli/src/args.rs: add --password-stdin flag (bool); the --password VALUE flag stays as a deprecated alias but its handler checks PDFTRACT_INSECURE_CLI_PASSWORD env first
  - pdftract-cli/src/main.rs (or password.rs module): a resolve_password function with priority order: 1) --password-stdin (read one line from stdin, strip terminator); 2) PDFTRACT_PASSWORD env (Some if non-empty); 3) --password VALUE (only if PDFTRACT_INSECURE_CLI_PASSWORD=1; emit stderr warning if so); 4) None
  - pdftract-py/src/lib.rs: PyO3 password= kwarg wired through to SecretString (depends on the secrecy wrapper bead)
  - pdftract-mcp/src/handlers/extract.rs: password parameter in the request body (not URL); typed as SecretString
  - pdftract-serve/src/routes/extract.rs: multipart form field password; typed as SecretString
- Stderr warning copy when --password VALUE is accepted via PDFTRACT_INSECURE_CLI_PASSWORD=1:
  "WARNING: --password VALUE is insecure (visible via 'ps aux'). Use --password-stdin or PDFTRACT_PASSWORD env var instead."
- Exit code if --password VALUE is supplied without PDFTRACT_INSECURE_CLI_PASSWORD=1: 64 (usage error) with a stderr hint pointing at --password-stdin

## Critical considerations

- The stdin discipline interacts with the input-via-stdin case: if the user runs pdftract extract --password-stdin - and the input PDF is also from stdin, the first line is the password and the rest is the PDF bytes (NOT a separate file descriptor); the documentation MUST be explicit
- If --password-stdin is set and the input is also stdin (-), the PDF read begins AFTER the password line is consumed
- The newline stripping rule: trim a single trailing \n or \r\n; do NOT trim leading/trailing whitespace (passwords can legitimately contain leading/trailing spaces)
- An empty password (a bare newline) is treated as no-password, NOT as a zero-length password (which is a different and rare PDF case); document explicitly
- TH-07 test (separate bead) will assert that spawning extract with --password foo exits 64 unless PDFTRACT_INSECURE_CLI_PASSWORD=1
- The PyO3 password= path needs a fast-path when None is passed (do NOT construct a SecretString of an empty string -- distinguish None from empty)

## Acceptance criteria

- --password-stdin flag implemented in pdftract-cli with correct stdin discipline
- PDFTRACT_PASSWORD env var read when present and --password-stdin not supplied
- --password VALUE rejected with exit 64 unless PDFTRACT_INSECURE_CLI_PASSWORD=1; in opt-in case a stderr warning is emitted
- Python password= kwarg lands in SecretString
- MCP password body field and serve password form field both land in SecretString
- Exit codes match the documented policy
- TH-07 test passes (separate bead)

## References

- Plan: line 878 (TH-07 mitigation), line 902-913 (Secrets Handling: PDF password), line 949 (NEVER log password values)
issue.title: Hardening: --password-stdin + PDFTRACT_PASSWORD env var + reject plain --password VALUE

issue.description:
## Scope

Define the three NDJSON frame types (HeaderFrame, PageFrame, FooterFrame) with serde internal-tag "frame" discriminator. Implement the write_frame(writer, frame) helper that serializes one frame as a single JSON line + newline + flush. Used by the streaming pipeline (6.2.2) and by tests.

## Why this matters

Frame structure is the wire contract: any change here breaks consumers. Centralizing frame definitions in one module avoids drift between writer and parser implementations.

## Implementation guidance

- enum NdjsonFrame { Header(HeaderFrame), Page(PageFrame), Footer(FooterFrame) } with serde tag = "frame", rename_all = lowercase
- HeaderFrame { schema_version: &'static str = "1.0", metadata: DocumentMetadata, outline: Vec<OutlineNode>, total_pages: u32 }
- PageFrame includes ALL Page fields (page_index, page_number, page_label, width, height, rotation, page_type, spans, blocks, annotations, tables); use #[serde(flatten)] from Page
- FooterFrame { extraction_quality, errors, threads, attachments, signatures, form_fields, links } — same Phase 7 placeholder shape as Output (6.1)
- write_frame<W: Write>(writer: &mut W, frame: &NdjsonFrame) -> io::Result<()>:
  serde_json::to_writer(writer, frame) -> writer.write_all(b"\n") -> writer.flush()

## Critical considerations

- The "frame" key is a serde tag; it appears as the first key in output JSON (deterministic ordering)
- PageFrame's flatten of Page must NOT cause field-name collision with the "frame" tag
- write_frame's flush is mandatory for streaming consumers
- Each frame is a single-line JSON object; embedded newlines forbidden in field values (serde_json escapes them)

## Acceptance criteria

- Roundtrip unit test: write a HeaderFrame -> parse -> equal to original
- Frame discriminator order: serialize Page frame -> first key in JSON is "frame":"page"
- Three frames emitted in expected sequence by stream test
- Frame-by-frame writer respects flush after every frame

## References

- Plan section: Phase 6.2 frame sequence (lines 2038-2042)
issue.title: 6.2.1: NDJSON frame types (Header/Page/Footer with internal-tag discriminator) + write_frame helper

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the `jedarden/pdftract` Composer package as a subprocess-based SDK. Spawn the bundled `pdftract` binary via PHP's `proc_open`, parse JSON output via `json_decode`, expose the 9 contract methods on a `Jedarden\\Pdftract\\Client`. Integrate with PSR-3 LoggerInterface for opt-in logging. Publishing requires no token — Packagist auto-discovers from git tags. Repo at `github.com/jedarden/pdftract-php`. Deferred to v1.1+ release wave.

## Why this matters

PHP powers WordPress, Drupal, Magento, Laravel ecosystems — particularly relevant for CMS document-upload workflows. PSR-3 is the Composer-ecosystem standard logger interface; integrating means pdftract logs flow into whatever logger the host app uses (Monolog, custom). The git-tag-based publish (no token) is the simplest of all 10 SDKs.

## Implementation guidance

- Composer package: `jedarden/pdftract`
- Repo: `github.com/jedarden/pdftract-php` (separate repo)
- PHP version floor: 8.2 (current PHP stable)
- File layout (generator-driven; see Tera template scaffolding bead):
  - `composer.json` declaring package name + `require` (psr/log)
  - `src/Client.php` (the main client class)
  - `src/Codegen/Methods.php` (generated)
  - `src/Codegen/Errors.php` (generated; 8 exception classes)
  - `src/Models/Document.php`, `Page.php`, etc. (readonly classes)
  - `tests/ConformanceTest.php` (PHPUnit)
- Method signatures (PHP):
  - `class Client { ... }`
  - `public function extract(string|Stringable $source, array $options = []): Document`
  - `public function extractText(string|Stringable $source, array $options = []): string`
  - `public function extractMarkdown(string|Stringable $source, array $options = []): string`
  - `public function extractStream(string|Stringable $source, array $options = []): Generator<Page>`
  - `public function search(string|Stringable $source, string $pattern, array $options = []): Generator<Match>`
  - `public function getMetadata(string|Stringable $source, array $options = []): Metadata`
  - `public function hash(string|Stringable $source, array $options = []): Fingerprint`
  - `public function classify(string|Stringable $source): Classification`
  - `public function verifyReceipt(string $path, Receipt $receipt): bool`
- Option names use camelCase per PHP-FIG convention: CLI `--ocr-language` becomes `ocrLanguage`
- Errors: `PdftractException` is the base; 8 subclasses mirror the contract
- PSR-3 integration: Client constructor accepts `LoggerInterface $logger = null`; logs subprocess invocations at DEBUG, errors at ERROR
- Generator-based streaming for extract_stream and search

## Publishing

- No Argo workflow file needed for the publish action itself (Packagist auto-discovers from git tags)
- A simple `pdftract-php-publish` workflow at `k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/pdftract-php-publish.yaml` does:
  1. `clone-sdk-repo`: `git clone https://github.com/jedarden/pdftract-php.git --branch main`
  2. `sync-version`: update `composer.json` `version` field (optional; Packagist uses git tags)
  3. `conformance`: `vendor/bin/phpunit tests/ConformanceTest.php` (runs the shared suite; aborts on failure)
  4. `tag-and-push`: `git tag vX.Y.Z && git push origin vX.Y.Z` (Packagist webhook auto-discovers)
  5. `warm-packagist`: `curl -X POST https://packagist.org/api/update-package?username=jedarden&apiToken=...` (optional: explicitly poke Packagist to re-index immediately)
- Container: `php:8.2-cli`

## Critical considerations

- ADR-009: runs on iad-ci; never use GitHub Actions
- Packagist webhook auto-discovery typically indexes a new tag within 60 s; the optional `warm-packagist` step shortens the delay further
- PHP's `proc_open` is more complex than other languages' subprocess APIs (descriptor specifications, manual pipe management); document the resource-cleanup pattern in code comments
- The PSR-3 LoggerInterface is the de-facto standard; do NOT depend on a specific logger implementation (Monolog, etc.)
- Generator-based streaming: each yield returns a parsed Page or Match; the underlying subprocess is killed when the Generator is closed
- v1.1+ deferral means this bead does NOT block v1.0 release; priority is P3

## Acceptance criteria

- The `jedarden/pdftract` Composer package is installable via `composer require jedarden/pdftract`
- All 9 contract methods exposed on `Jedarden\\Pdftract\\Client`
- All 8 exception classes inherit from PdftractException
- `vendor/bin/phpunit` runs the conformance suite and 100% passes
- PSR-3 LoggerInterface integration verified (a Monolog instance receives DEBUG and ERROR entries)
- A tag push triggers Packagist auto-discovery within 60 s

## References

- Plan section: SDK Architecture / The Ten SDKs, line 3479 (PHP subprocess via proc_open + json_decode; PSR-3 logger integration; v1.1+)
- Plan section: SDK Architecture / Per-SDK Release Channels, line 3576 (Packagist auto-discovers from git tag)
- Plan section: SDK Acceptance Criteria, lines 3581-3589
- Sibling: SDK contract, conformance suite, code generator
- PSR-3 LoggerInterface spec

issue.description:
## Scope

Extract interactive form field definitions and current values from PDFs. Two parallel pipelines: (a) AcroForm - walk /Fields recursively, handle Tx / Btn / Ch / Sig types, dot-join nested /Kids names, capture /V (current value), /DV (default), /Ff (flags), /Rect (widget bbox). (b) XFA - if /AcroForm /XFA is present, parse the XFA XML stream(s) via quick-xml, walk the data model, extract <field> values keyed by XFA field name. When both are present, prefer XFA values on overlapping field names. Output: document-level form_fields object/map per docs/schema/v1.0/pdftract.schema.json.

## Why this matters

Forms are a massive PDF use case - government applications, healthcare intake, tax returns, vendor onboarding, expense reports. AcroForm covers 90% of forms; XFA covers a stubborn 10% (tax forms, healthcare) that legacy generators still emit. Without XFA support, users with those documents would see empty field lists despite filled-in data being clearly visible. Field flag extraction (required / read-only / multi-line / radio button group) lets downstream consumers understand the form's semantics, not just its values.

## Implementation guidance

- Crates: quick-xml (1) for XFA parsing; reused Phase 1 parser for AcroForm
- AcroForm walker: shared with 7.3.1 (walk_acroform_fields) - return all fields, not just Sig
- AcroForm field types: Tx (text), Btn (button - subdivided by /Ff bits into pushbutton, radio, checkbox), Ch (choice - subdivided into combo, list), Sig (signature; handled by 7.3 - skip in 7.4 output)
- Btn /V is a Name (selected appearance state, typically /Yes or /Off for checkbox/radio; absent = not selected); compute is_checked = (v == "Yes" or other configured /AS)
- Ch /V is a PdfString (selected option); /Opt is array of [export_value, display_text] tuples
- Tx /V is a PdfString (current text); /DV is default text; multi-line flag from /Ff bit 12
- XFA stream: /AcroForm /XFA can be (a) a single stream object containing the full XDP XML, or (b) an array of alternating Name/Stream pairs (concatenate streams in the order ["preamble", "config", "template", "datasets", "form", "postamble"])
- XFA <datasets> section contains the data model - walk <xfa:data> children to find <field> values keyed by element name
- XFA + AcroForm overlap: if a field name appears in both, XFA value wins (per plan)

## Critical considerations

- Field-name dot-joining: parent.child.grandchild; if a field has no /T, skip the segment (collapse consecutive dots)
- /Ff flag bits (PDF 1.7 12.7.3.1): bit 1 = ReadOnly, bit 2 = Required, bit 3 = NoExport; type-specific bits in 12.7.4.x
- Btn Ff bit 15 = Pushbutton, bit 16 = Radio - distinguish from checkbox
- XFA XML may declare namespaces (xmlns:xfa, xmlns:xdc) - quick-xml with namespace support enabled
- XFA encryption sub-elements may exist; skip silently (no encryption handling in v1)
- AcroForm-only PDFs (no /XFA) are the majority; XFA-only PDFs are rare; hybrid is the contentious case
- form_fields output key is the dot-joined name; value is the extracted current value (string/bool/null per field type)

## Acceptance criteria

- All Phase 7.4 child task beads closed
- Critical test (from plan): PDF with text field, checkbox, and dropdown - all three types extracted with correct values
- Critical test: nested field hierarchy - full dot-separated name constructed correctly
- Critical test: XFA-only form - all field values extracted from XFA XML
- Critical test: hybrid XFA+AcroForm - XFA values preferred
- Output: form_fields: HashMap<String, FormFieldValue> at document level per docs/schema/v1.0/pdftract.schema.json
- Schema includes type-specific field shapes (Tx/Btn/Ch with distinct value types)

## References

- Plan section: 7.4 AcroForm and XFA (lines 2604-2627)
- PDF 1.7 spec 12.7 Interactive Forms; XFA 3.3 spec
- 7.3.1 shared AcroForm walker
- docs/schema/v1.0/pdftract.schema.json
- 7.10 profile structural.has_form_field predicate

issue.description:
## Scope

Wrap the Phase 6.3 PyO3 native binding (`crates/pdftract-py`) with the idiomatic Python ergonomics required by the SDK contract: the 9 contract methods exposed as snake_case Python functions, the 8 native exception classes inheriting from `PdftractError`, an optional asyncio wrapper using `asyncio.to_thread`, and the subprocess fallback path for musl-only environments where the native module fails to load. Land the conformance test runner under `crates/pdftract-py/tests/test_conformance.py`.

## Why this matters

The Phase 6.3 binding is a thin PyO3 wrapper; this bead adds the idiomatic ergonomics, the exception hierarchy, the conformance runner, and the subprocess fallback. Without these, the Python SDK fails the contract (e.g. returns raw dicts instead of typed Document objects; raises generic exceptions instead of the 8-class hierarchy). The Argo publishing pipeline (pdftract-py-ci, separate bead under the Release Engineering epic) already exists; this bead delivers the contract-compliant API surface that pipeline ships.

## Implementation guidance

- API surface (mirrors the SDK contract):
  - `pdftract.extract(source, **options) -> Document`
  - `pdftract.extract_text(source, **options) -> str`
  - `pdftract.extract_markdown(source, **options) -> str`
  - `pdftract.extract_stream(source, **options) -> Iterator[Page]`
  - `pdftract.search(source, pattern, **options) -> Iterator[Match]`
  - `pdftract.get_metadata(source, **options) -> Metadata`
  - `pdftract.hash(source, **options) -> Fingerprint`
  - `pdftract.classify(source) -> Classification`
  - `pdftract.verify_receipt(path, receipt) -> bool`
- Option names use snake_case per the contract: CLI `--ocr-language` becomes Python `ocr_language`
- Exception hierarchy (all inherit from `pdftract.PdftractError`):
  - `CorruptPdfError`, `EncryptionError`, `SourceUnreachableError`, `RemoteFetchInterruptedError`, `TlsError`, `ReceiptVerifyError`, `UnsupportedOperationError`
- Type definitions for Document, Page, Span, Block, Match, Fingerprint, Classification — defined as `@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)` and constructed from the native PyO3 return values
- Asyncio wrapper: `pdftract.asyncio.extract(source, **options)` calls `asyncio.to_thread(pdftract.extract, source, **options)` (opt-in; do NOT make sync methods coroutines)
- Subprocess fallback: if `import pdftract._native` raises `ImportError`, fall back to a subprocess implementation (`subprocess.run([cli_path, "extract", "--json", source])`); document the fallback in README
- Conformance runner: `crates/pdftract-py/tests/test_conformance.py` invokes the suite via the Python API and reports per-case pass/fail
- Package metadata: `pyproject.toml` declares `[project]` with `name = "pdftract"`, `version` synced from binary, `license = "MIT OR Apache-2.0"`, `requires-python = ">=3.11"`

## Critical considerations

- The native PyO3 binding (Phase 6.3) is the implementation; this bead is the ergonomic layer on top
- The subprocess fallback is required because pre-built abi3 wheels do not cover musl-libc Linux; on Alpine the wheel install fails and the fallback path activates automatically
- The asyncio wrapper is OPTIONAL per the contract — sync-first is the primary surface
- Type definitions MUST be class-based, NOT raw dicts; using `TypedDict` is acceptable for v0.X but `@dataclass` is preferred
- The `verify_receipt` method does NOT map to an MCP tool but IS in the SDK contract (per plan line 3500)
- The publish path (PyPI) is already implemented in `pdftract-py-ci` (Release Engineering epic) — this bead does NOT touch that pipeline; it delivers the SDK code the pipeline ships

## Acceptance criteria

- All 9 contract methods exposed on the `pdftract` module
- All 8 exception classes inherit from `pdftract.PdftractError`
- Document, Page, Span, Block, Match, Fingerprint, Classification exposed as language-native types (NOT raw dicts)
- `pdftract.asyncio` module provides asyncio wrappers for the 4 long-running methods (extract, extract_stream, search, hash)
- Subprocess fallback path activates on `ImportError` from the native module
- `tests/test_conformance.py` runs the shared suite and 100% passes
- `pyproject.toml` correctly declares package metadata and entry points

## References

- Plan section: SDK Architecture / Per-SDK Release Channels, line 3568 (pdftract-py-ci handles publishing)
- Plan section: SDK Acceptance Criteria, lines 3581-3589
- Phase 6.3 in the plan (the underlying PyO3 binding)
