issue.description:
## Scope

Author tests/security/TH-10-cache-poison.rs that:
1. Initialises a cache directory with a known random HMAC key
2. Performs a legitimate extraction to populate the cache
3. Writes a forged cache entry under a known fingerprint with a tampered output blob and a wrong HMAC
4. Re-extracts; asserts CACHE_INTEGRITY_FAIL diagnostic emitted; asserts the cache miss path runs and produces the correct output (NOT the forged blob)

## Why this matters

TH-10 (line 881) is the local-FS attacker class -- a malicious co-tenant who writes a poisoned cache entry whose key collides with a legitimate fingerprint. Without the HMAC integrity check, subsequent reads return the attacker-controlled blob. Phase 6.9 cache MUST therefore HMAC-sign every entry; this test verifies the signing AND verifies the reject path produces a correct fallback.

## Implementation guidance

- Test file: tests/security/TH-10-cache-poison.rs
- Setup helpers:
  - tempfile::TempDir for the cache directory
  - pdftract cache init --dir <tmp> generates a random per-cache HMAC key stored in <tmp>/key (mode 0600); this key is per-cache, NOT per-process
  - Run pdftract extract --cache <tmp> sample.pdf to populate the cache with a legitimate entry
- Test steps:
  1. Init cache; populate via legitimate extract; record the entry filename (typically <fingerprint-hex>.json or similar)
  2. Read the legitimate entry; extract the HMAC and the blob; copy aside
  3. Write a forged entry at the same path: same fingerprint key, but with a different output blob (replace a known string in the blob -- e.g. swap "Acme Widgets" for "Pwned Inc") and a WRONG HMAC (random bytes)
  4. Re-extract the same PDF with --cache <tmp>: assert CACHE_INTEGRITY_FAIL diagnostic emitted on stderr or in output.diagnostics; assert extracted blob matches the legitimate blob (not the forged blob); assert exit 0
  5. Verify the cache entry was rewritten with a correct HMAC (the rejected forgery was replaced by the genuine extraction's output during the cache-write path)
  6. Negative case: forge the blob BUT compute the correct HMAC using the known key (this simulates an attacker who somehow got the key); assert the forgery succeeds in this case (it should, because the HMAC verifies); document this as the "key compromise" failure mode and link to the rotation policy

## Critical considerations

- HMAC algorithm MUST be HMAC-SHA-256 (per line 881); per-cache random key generated on cache init (NOT per-process, NOT global, NOT derived from the fingerprint itself)
- Key file MUST be mode 0600 on Unix; document the failure mode if it is world-readable (the test asserts the mode on cache init)
- The HMAC input MUST be fingerprint || extraction_options || output_blob (per line 881) -- otherwise a forged extraction_options would not be detected
- CACHE_INTEGRITY_FAIL is treated as a cache miss (NOT a hard error) so that legitimate extraction proceeds; the diagnostic is INFO/WARN level
- The replacement-on-miss behaviour: when the cache rejects a forged entry, the legitimate extraction's output is written and overwrites the forgery; this self-heals if the attacker writes once then leaves
- A repeated-poisoning attack (attacker keeps re-writing the forgery after the legitimate extraction overwrites it) is acknowledged in the plan but is out of scope for v1.0 -- document the failure mode in the test
- Negative case 6 (correct HMAC with attacker key): the only mitigation is key rotation (out of scope for the test; documented as a known limitation)

## Acceptance criteria

- tests/security/TH-10-cache-poison.rs exists and passes
- Cache init produces a 0600 key file
- Forgery with wrong HMAC: CACHE_INTEGRITY_FAIL diagnostic emitted; legitimate output returned; entry rewritten
- Forgery with correct HMAC (key compromise simulation): forged output returned (documented limitation)
- HMAC input is verified to be fingerprint || extraction_options || output_blob

## References

- Plan: line 881 (TH-10 entry), Phase 6.9 (cache filesystem layout), Diagnostic Code Catalog CACHE_INTEGRITY_FAIL
issue.title: TH-10 test: cache poisoning (forged entry rejected; CACHE_INTEGRITY_FAIL; real extraction re-runs)

issue.description:
## Scope

Given a GridCandidate (from 7.2.1 or 7.2.2) and a Vec<Span>, assign each span to the cell whose bbox contains the span's centroid. Build a Cell::content field as the ordered Vec<Span> within each cell (top-to-bottom, left-to-right). Spans whose centroid falls outside all cells become orphan spans and remain in the surrounding block.

## Why this matters

Centroid containment is the standard cell-assignment rule used by pdfplumber and Tabula. It avoids the common bug where a span on a cell border gets assigned to both cells, producing duplicate text. Per-cell ordering preserves the read order within multi-line cells, which is essential for invoice line-items, financial line entries, and bibliographic citations.

## Implementation guidance

- For each Span in the page text: compute centroid = ((x0+x1)/2, (y0+y1)/2)
- For each Cell c: contains(centroid, c.bbox) returns true iff x0 <= cx < x1 AND y0 <= cy < y1 (half-open interval to avoid boundary double-count)
- If contained: push span into c.content
- If contained by NO cell: span remains as a regular paragraph span in the outer block (orphan)
- Within each cell, sort content by (round(y0/2), x0) - line-then-x ordering with a 2-pt y bucket so spans on the same line don't reorder by tiny y noise
- If a single Span's centroid falls in cell A but its bbox overlaps cell B by > 50%, emit a diagnostic "span_bbox_overlaps_multiple_cells" (does NOT split the span)

## Critical considerations

- Half-open interval [x0, x1) avoids double-assignment when a centroid lands exactly on a shared border
- y-axis convention: PDF origin is bottom-left, but cells are top-down in output - keep one convention internally and document
- Cells touching the grid bbox edges (top row, leftmost column) include their outer boundary - extend bbox by 0.5 pt outward to capture spans flush to the border
- Orphan spans are NOT lost - they go to the surrounding paragraph block (Phase 4.3 path); table extraction is additive, not replacing

## Acceptance criteria

- Every span deterministically assigned to at most one cell or marked orphan
- Critical test (from plan): 5x3 bordered table - all 15 cells have correct text content
- Unit tests: centroid on border, span spanning two cells (diagnostic emitted), orphan span preserved in outer block
- Public Cell { bbox: [f32;4], content: Vec<Span>, row: usize, col: usize, rowspan: u32, colspan: u32 }

## References

- Plan section: 7.2 line 2573 (cell content assignment)
- docs/research/table-structure-reconstruction.md
- 7.2.1 / 7.2.2 (grid input)
- 7.2.5 merged cell detection (rowspan/colspan defaulted to 1 here)
issue.title: 7.2.3: Span-to-cell assignment by centroid containment

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the StandardType -> BlockKind mapping that converts walked StructElem nodes into the BlockKind taxonomy used by Phase 4 output. Includes /Artifact suppression and heading-level extraction (H, H1..H6 -> heading with level).

## Why this matters

Mapping is the lever that controls what tagged content surfaces in output and how. Wrong mapping = broken downstream rendering (e.g. an H2 tagged as paragraph loses Markdown heading anchors). /Artifact is the only mechanism to strip running headers/footers correctly per the tagged-PDF contract.

## Implementation guidance

- Mapping table: P -> Paragraph; H -> Heading{level: 1} (no explicit level, default 1); H1 -> Heading{level: 1}; H2..H6 -> Heading{level: 2..6}; Table -> Table; L -> List; LI -> ListItem; Lbl -> ListLabel; LBody -> ListBody; Figure -> Figure; Caption -> Caption; Code -> Code; BlockQuote -> BlockQuote; TOC, TOCI -> Toc; Formula -> Formula; Reference -> Reference; Note -> Note; Form -> FormFieldStruct; Span, Quote -> inline (no block); Document, Part, Art, Sect, Div, NonStruct, Private -> structural container (descend without emitting block)
- Artifact handling: any StructElem with type "Artifact" plus any MCID inside an Artifact marked-content sequence is suppressed entirely - none of its content reaches output
- Unknown types (after /RoleMap resolution): fall back to Paragraph with a diagnostic in the receipts

## Critical considerations

- "Artifact" is BOTH a structure type AND a marked-content tag - the suppression rule applies in both contexts (consume from 3.4 marked-content tagger)
- Heading level extraction: prefer explicit H1..H6 over plain H; nested H elements DO NOT auto-increment level (spec leaves this to the producer)
- Mapping must NOT inject new BlockKind variants without coordination with INV stable-taxonomy guarantee
- LI inside L: emit a ListItem block whose parent index points to the L block

## Acceptance criteria

- Every Standard structure type has a mapping decision (in-table, suppressed, or structural-container)
- Critical test: H1/H2 -> heading level 1/2 (from plan)
- Critical test: /Artifact MCIDs excluded from output (from plan)
- Unit tests: list nesting, table grouping, span passthrough
- Unknown-type fallback path emits a diagnostic line

## References

- INV stable taxonomy (block kinds)
- 7.1.1 walker (provides typed nodes)
- 3.4 marked-content tagger (Artifact tag at content-stream layer)

issue.description:
## Scope

Build the PyO3 Python extension module pdftract. API surface: pdftract.extract(path, **opts) -> dict, pdftract.extract_text(path, **opts) -> str, pdftract.extract_stream(path, **opts) -> Iterator[dict]. Exception hierarchy: PdftractError, EncryptionError. Release GIL via py.allow_threads() during extraction. Build wheels via maturin for 5 target triples through Argo WorkflowTemplate pdftract-py-ci.

## Why this matters

Python is the largest user base for PDF extraction (data science, document AI, LLM pipelines). A clean PyO3 binding lets pdftract reach that audience without users building Rust toolchain locally. GIL release is non-negotiable: Python apps frequently extract from multi-threaded code (Flask request handlers, async event loops with run_in_executor); a GIL-holding extraction blocks all other Python threads for seconds.

## Implementation guidance

- Crate feature: pyo3 with extension-module feature
- Module: pdftract-py/src/lib.rs (separate crate since it has different deps + maturin build)
- API:
  - extract(path: PyAny, **kwargs) -> PyDict (calls Output -> serde_json::to_string -> json.loads in Python? or build PyDict directly via pythonize)
  - extract_text(path, **kwargs) -> PyString
  - extract_stream(path, **kwargs) -> PyIterator yielding PyDict per page
- Options mapped from Python kwargs to ExtractionOptions: ocr, ocr_language, include_invisible, extract_forms, extract_attachments, readability_threshold, password, max_decompress_gb, full_render
- Exception hierarchy: create_exception!(pdftract, PdftractError, PyException); create_exception!(pdftract, EncryptionError, PdftractError)
- py.allow_threads(|| run_extraction()) wraps every blocking call
- Build via maturin: maturin build --features python; 5 target triples: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, x86_64-apple-darwin, aarch64-apple-darwin, x86_64-pc-windows-gnu
- Argo WorkflowTemplate pdftract-py-ci in jedarden/declarative-config -> k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/

## Critical considerations

- py.allow_threads() is non-negotiable per plan (line 2080); without it, Python multi-threading deadlocks
- pythonize crate converts serde-serializable Rust types into PyDict; use it (not manual PyO3 dict construction; that's brittle)
- Exception hierarchy: EncryptionError MUST inherit from PdftractError so users can catch the parent
- Wheel cross-compilation from Linux runner uses manylinux base + osxcross + windows cross; document in 6.3.4
- maturin produces pep-517 compliant wheels; CI uploads to PyPI on milestone tags
- PyO3 GIL management: extract_stream yields per page; reacquire GIL only when yielding (each page lifts GIL momentarily)

## Acceptance criteria

- All Phase 6.3 child task beads closed
- Critical test 1: pdftract.extract("test.pdf") returns dict with correct metadata.page_count
- Critical test 2: pdftract.extract_text("test.pdf") returns plain-text string

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the `github.com/jedarden/pdftract-go` Go module as a subprocess-based SDK. Spawn the bundled `pdftract` binary via `os/exec`, parse JSON output via `encoding/json.Decoder`, expose the 9 contract methods as Go functions accepting `context.Context` for cancellation. No central registry (Go modules are git-tag-based); pkg.go.dev auto-indexes from the published tag.

## Why this matters

Go is the second-most-common backend language in the Cloud Native ecosystem (after Java); pdftract adoption in Kubernetes-native pipelines (KubeFlow, ArgoCD, Tekton) requires a first-class Go SDK. The git-tag-based publishing model means there is no token-management concern for Go publishing — the publish workflow just creates the git tag.

## Implementation guidance

- Module path: `github.com/jedarden/pdftract-go`
- File layout (generator-driven; see Tera template scaffolding bead):
  - `go.mod` declaring `module github.com/jedarden/pdftract-go` and `go 1.22` minimum
  - `pdftract.go` (re-exports public API)
  - `codegen/methods.go` (generated from Tera template)
  - `codegen/errors.go` (generated; 8 error kinds)
  - `subprocess.go` (the exec + JSON-decode machinery)
  - `stream.go` (channel-based streaming for extract_stream / search)
  - `conformance_test.go` (the conformance runner)
- Method signatures (Go):
  - `Extract(ctx context.Context, source Source, opts *ExtractOptions) (*Document, error)`
  - `ExtractText(ctx context.Context, source Source, opts *ExtractOptions) (string, error)`
  - `ExtractMarkdown(ctx context.Context, source Source, opts *ExtractOptions) (string, error)`
  - `ExtractStream(ctx context.Context, source Source, opts *ExtractOptions) (<-chan PageResult, error)` (channel emits Page or error; closed when stream ends or ctx cancelled)
  - `Search(ctx context.Context, source Source, pattern string, opts *SearchOptions) (<-chan MatchResult, error)`
  - `GetMetadata(ctx context.Context, source Source, opts *ExtractOptions) (*Metadata, error)`
  - `Hash(ctx context.Context, source Source, opts *HashOptions) (*Fingerprint, error)`
  - `Classify(ctx context.Context, source Source) (*Classification, error)`
  - `VerifyReceipt(ctx context.Context, path string, receipt *Receipt) (bool, error)`
- Source type: `type Source interface { ... }` with `PathSource`, `URLSource`, `BytesSource` constructors
- Option names use PascalCase per the contract (Go convention): CLI `--ocr-language` becomes `OCRLanguage` (special acronym handling per Go style guide)
- Errors: define `type ErrKind int` enum with constants `ErrCorruptPDF`, `ErrEncryption`, ..., plus `type PdftractError struct { Kind ErrKind; Message string; ExitCode int }`. Use `errors.Is/As`-compatible matching.
- Context cancellation: passing a cancelled context to any method MUST terminate the subprocess via `cmd.Cancel = func() error { return cmd.Process.Kill() }`

## Critical considerations

- Go modules are git-tag-based — no token, no central registry account; the publish workflow just creates a tag
- pkg.go.dev auto-fetches the module on first request; the first request after publish may take a few minutes to index
- The Source interface is the Go-idiomatic alternative to overloaded signatures; do NOT expose a single `string` argument that conditionally interprets as path or URL
- Streaming via channel: the channel MUST be buffered with a small buffer (16) to avoid producer blocking; the consumer is responsible for ranging until the channel closes
- Cancellation MUST propagate to the subprocess; a leaked subprocess is a correctness bug
- The Go version floor (1.22 currently; bump to 1.23 once it's been GA for 6 months) is documented in the README
- vendor directory NOT committed (modules are reproducible from go.sum)

## Acceptance criteria

- The `github.com/jedarden/pdftract-go` module is buildable with `go build ./...`
- All 9 contract methods exposed with the documented signatures
- All 8 error kinds available via `errors.As` matching
- `go test ./...` runs the conformance runner and 100% passes
- Passing a cancelled context to any method terminates the subprocess and returns ctx.Err()
- pkg.go.dev page renders correctly after publish

## References

- Plan section: SDK Architecture / The Ten SDKs, line 3474 (Go subprocess via os/exec + encoding/json Decoder; context.Context-aware)
- Plan section: SDK Architecture / Per-SDK Release Channels, line 3571
- Plan section: SDK Acceptance Criteria, line 3587 (context.Context for cancellation in Go)
- Sibling: pdftract-go-publish Argo workflow (separate bead)
- Sibling: SDK contract and conformance suite
- Effective Go style guide

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement `compute_glyph_advance(state: &GraphicsState, font: &Font, char_code: u32) -> f64` that returns the per-glyph text-space advance width incorporating Tc (char_spacing), Tw (word_spacing, only when char_code == 0x20 in non-Type0 fonts), and Tz (horiz_scaling). Also implement `compute_device_bbox(state: &GraphicsState, font: &Font, char_code: u32) -> [f32; 4]` that maps the glyph's font-unit bbox to PDF user space via `text_matrix * CTM`.

## Why this matters

Wrong advance = wrong text_matrix update = wrong positions for every subsequent glyph in the same TJ. Wrong bbox = wrong baseline clustering, wrong column detection, wrong reading order. This is the load-bearing arithmetic of Phase 3.

## Implementation guidance

- Advance formula per ISO 32000-1 sec 9.2.4:
  ```
  raw_w = font.advance(char_code) / 1000.0   // PDF units -> text-space
  raw_adv = raw_w * font_size                // text-space (relative to em)
  spacing = char_spacing + (if char_code == 0x20 && font.is_simple() { word_spacing } else { 0.0 })
  advance = (raw_adv + spacing) * (horiz_scaling / 100.0)
  ```
- Note: word_spacing applies ONLY to character code 0x20 (space) in SIMPLE fonts (Type1, TrueType, MMType1) — NOT in Type 0 composite fonts (which use multi-byte codes where 0x20 is just a byte fragment).
- `font.advance(char_code)`: dispatch to font.kind() — Std-14 uses hardcoded widths; Type1/TrueType uses /Widths array indexed by code - FirstChar; Type0 uses CID -> width via descendant CIDFont's /W array.
- Device bbox: glyph's font-unit bbox is `font.glyph_bbox(char_code)` -> scale by font_size/1000 -> apply Ts (text rise) y offset -> apply text_matrix -> apply CTM. Output as axis-aligned (transform all 4 corners, take min/max).
- Performance: glyph advance is called per emitted glyph; cache per (FontId, char_code) -> advance (text-space, before Tc/Tw/Tz which are added at call-time).

## Critical considerations

- INV: text_matrix advance update uses ONLY the advance value — NOT the full bbox. Bbox is computed for output, advance for positioning.
- Font size 0 (degenerate): advance == 0, bbox is a single point at current position. Do NOT panic, do NOT divide-by-zero.
- Horiz_scaling 100 (default): factor is 1.0, can be optimized away. Implement clearly first, optimize later.
- Tw applies to BYTE 0x20 (the space character code), not to the CHARACTER ' ' (Unicode 0x20) — for Type 0 with a Unicode CMap, this distinction matters.
- Bbox in PDF user space is LOWER-LEFT origin per Glyph struct spec (line 1544).

## Acceptance criteria

- 12pt Helvetica with no spacing modifications, glyph 'H' (width 722 units): advance = 722/1000 * 12 = 8.664 text-units.
- Same with `Tc 1 Tw 5 Tz 100` and char_code 0x20 (space, width 278): advance = (278/1000 * 12 + 1 + 5) * 1.0 = 9.336.
- Type0 font with Tw set and 0x20 byte: Tw NOT added (verify the is_simple check).
- Tz 50: advance halved.
- Font size 0: advance = 0, bbox degenerate to point (no panic).

## References

- Plan section: Phase 3.2 per-glyph processing (lines 1521-1526)
- ISO 32000-1 9.2.4
issue.title: Per-glyph advance computation (Tc/Tw/Tz corrections + device-space bbox)

issue.description:
## Scope

Reconstruct PDF article thread chains for multi-column and multi-page reading flows. Read /Catalog /Threads array; each entry is an article thread dict with /F (first bead ref) and /I (thread info dict). Walk the bead chain by following /N (next bead) links from the first bead; detect chain end when /N loops back to first bead (circular list). Each bead has /R (page ref) and /V (rect on the page). Reconstruct ordered Vec<{ page_index, rect }> per thread. Emit document-level /threads array.

## Why this matters

Article threads in tagged-PDF magazines, scientific journals, and newspapers explicitly mark the author's intended reading flow across multi-column and multi-page layouts - sidebars, jumps to continuation pages, callout boxes that should be skipped. Without thread reconstruction, the heuristic reading-order detectors (4.5 XY-cut, docstrum) can scramble these layouts. Threads are also the only way to extract a "the actual article" view from a complex magazine page that mixes ads, callouts, and three concurrent articles.

## Implementation guidance

- Crates: none beyond Phase 1 parser
- /Catalog /Threads: Optional array of indirect refs to thread dicts (absent = no threads, empty array in output)
- Thread dict: { /F: first bead ref, /I: thread info dict }
  - /I optional fields: /Title (PdfString), /Author, /Subject, /Keywords
- Bead dict: { /T: thread ref (back-link), /N: next bead, /V: previous bead OR rect (overloaded), /R: page ref, /P: page ref (preferred newer form), /A: appearance stream ref }
  - Wait - the spec actually has /T (thread back-link), /N (next bead), /V (previous bead), /R (rect on page), /P (page); plan description conflated /V with rect - clarify: /R is the rectangle, /P (or older docs use /Pg) is the page reference. Cross-check PDF 1.7 12.4.3 before implementing.
- Walk: start at thread.F; follow .N links; cycle terminates when bead == thread.F again
- Resolve /P (or older /Pg) bead -> page; convert to 0-indexed page_index by looking up the page in document.pages
- Emit Thread { title, author, subject, keywords, beads: Vec<{ page_index, rect: [f32;4] }> }
- Always emit /threads array (empty when none)

## Critical considerations

- Cycle detection: track visited bead refs; abort walk if a non-first bead is revisited (malformed); emit diagnostic
- Plan text says "circular termination" - the legitimate end-condition is N -> F (back to first); ALSO guard against pathological cycles N -> some middle bead
- /R rect: [x0, y0, x1, y1] in PDF user space of the page; do NOT transform to image space
- /P resolution: walk document /Pages tree to find the page index of the referenced page; cache the ref->index map document-wide for O(1) lookup
- Some PDFs use /Threads in older shape (/B + array of beads inline); tolerate both shapes if encountered
- INV: stable thread shape - title/author/subject can be null; bead list always present even if zero beads

## Acceptance criteria

- All Phase 7.7 child task beads closed
- Critical test (from plan): PDF with two article threads - both reconstructed with correct bead order and page references
- Critical test: thread with no /I info dict -> title, author, subject all null; bead chain still reconstructed
- Critical test: bead /V (rect) correctly converted to PDF user-space coordinates for the referenced page
- Critical test: circular bead chain termination - chain walk stops without infinite loop
- Output: document-level /threads: Vec<Thread> per docs/schema/v1.0/pdftract.schema.json
- Schema validates synthetic thread fixture

## References

- Plan section: 7.7 Article Threads (lines 2677-2696)

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement `ResourceStack` — a stack of resource dictionaries with layered lookup. `lookup_font(name)`, `lookup_color_space(name)`, `lookup_xobject(name)`, `lookup_ext_gstate(name)` each search innermost-first and fall through to outer scopes. Initialized with the page's resolved /Resources dict (Phase 1.4). Push/pop on form XObject Do entry/exit.

## Why this matters

PDF resource scoping is hierarchical: a form XObject's /Resources shadows the page's /Resources for the form's content stream. Without scoping, fonts named `/F1` in a form might accidentally resolve to a page-level `/F1` with different metrics. This is a real bug in some early PDF extractors.

## Implementation guidance

- Storage: `Vec<Arc<ResourceDict>>`. The PAGE-level resources are at index 0; each Do push appends a new dict (or a wrapper representing the merged resources).
- Lookup: walk the stack from `last()` to `first()`, return the first match. None if not found in any scope.
- Merging strategy per spec: a form XObject without /Resources INHERITS from the parent page (NOT from the immediately enclosing form). To support this, push only Some(dict) when the form has /Resources; otherwise, don't push and re-use parent scope.
- ResourceDict: pre-resolve sub-dicts at construction time so lookup is just a hashmap query, not an indirect-ref chase.

## Critical considerations

- INV: lookup_font returns the SAME Arc<Font> regardless of which scope finds it — fonts are loaded once per (document, font-resource-dict-entry).
- Some PDFs put /Resources on the form XObject AS A REFERENCE to the page's resources dict (form has no own resources) — handle gracefully, treat as "no own resources".
- /Resources inheritance through nested forms: form A has resources, form B (nested) has none — B inherits from PAGE (not from A) per spec sec 7.8.3. Document this behavior with a test.
- Wait — re-read spec 7.8.3.3: "If a content stream does not have a Resources entry but is contained within a parent that does, the parent's resources are inherited." Form XObjects nest via Do, NOT via dictionary containment — so the FORM XObject's /Resources is the only resource scope visible to its content stream UNLESS missing, in which case the PAGE's resources are visible. Document this carefully.

## Acceptance criteria

- Page with /Font /F1, form XObject with own /Font /F1 (different font): inner form's Tj /F1 resolves to form's font.
- Page with /Font /F1, form XObject with no /Resources: inner form's Tj /F1 resolves to page's font.
- Page with /Font /F1, form XObject with /Resources but no /Font: Tj /F1 fails (form scope has no font subdict, no fallthrough to page per spec).
- Nested form B inside form A: B without /Resources inherits PAGE's, not A's.
- lookup_xobject and lookup_ext_gstate follow same rules.

## References

- Plan section: Phase 3.3 ResourceStack paragraph (line 1565)
- ISO 32000-1 sec 7.8.3
issue.title: ResourceStack: scope-merging stack with fallback lookup

issue.description:
## Scope

Merge the AcroForm field map (from 7.4.2) and the XFA field map (from 7.4.3) into a single Vec<(String full_name, FormFieldValue)>. On field-name collision, prefer the XFA value over the AcroForm value (per plan). Document the precedence rule visibly so callers know which source won. Emit a diagnostic when a collision occurs so users can audit.

## Why this matters

Hybrid AcroForm + XFA PDFs are intentional design: the XFA holds the authoritative current values, while AcroForm provides the viewer's quick-render annotations. The two often disagree (XFA is updated by the JavaScript runtime; AcroForm may carry stale appearance-state values). XFA-wins precedence is the convention used by Adobe Reader and is what users expect.

## Implementation guidance

- Inputs: acro_fields: Vec<(String, FormFieldValue)>, xfa_fields: Vec<(String, String)>
- Build HashMap<String, (FormFieldValue, Source)> where Source is AcroForm | Xfa | Both
- Insert AcroForm fields first; insert XFA fields second, overwriting and tagging Source = Both for collisions
- XFA values are always strings; convert to FormFieldValue::Text { value: Some(xfa_str), default: None, multiline: false, max_length: None } unless an AcroForm sibling exists that gives type hints; then preserve AcroForm type with XFA value
- Emit diagnostic "form_field_collision" { name, acro_value, xfa_value } per collision
- Return ordered Vec<(String, FormFieldValue)> sorted by full_name

## Critical considerations

- XFA value semantics may not match AcroForm semantics for buttons - if AcroForm says Checkbox and XFA gives "true"/"false" or "1"/"0", convert to Button { selected: bool, ... }
- Empty XFA value MUST overwrite a non-empty AcroForm value (XFA is canonical even when blank)
- Collisions are not errors - they are normal in hybrid PDFs; the diagnostic is informational
- Order in output: alphabetical by full_name (deterministic for downstream diff tooling)
- Source: Both is preserved in a separate diagnostic; not in the final output value

## Acceptance criteria

- Critical test (from plan): hybrid XFA+AcroForm - XFA values preferred
- Unit tests: 3 AcroForm + 2 XFA no overlap, 3 AcroForm + 2 XFA both overlapping, XFA boolean -> Checkbox conversion, empty XFA wins over non-empty AcroForm
- Diagnostics emitted on every collision
- Sort order deterministic
- Public form_field::combine(acro, xfa) -> Vec<(String, FormFieldValue)>

## References

- Plan section: 7.4 line 2619 (XFA wins)
- 7.4.2 (AcroForm input)
- 7.4.3 (XFA input)
- 7.4.5 (consumer for JSON output)

## Scope

Author tests/security/TH-04-js-presence.rs that loads tests/fixtures/security/embedded-js.pdf -- a PDF with JavaScript embedded in /AA (additional actions), /OpenAction, and /JS entries -- and asserts that pdftract NEVER executes the JavaScript but flags its presence with a JAVASCRIPT_PRESENT info-level diagnostic and surfaces it as metadata.javascript_actions[] in the JSON output.

## Why this matters

TH-04 (line 875) addresses the attack class of PDFs that try to run JavaScript on open (a vector Adobe Acrobat historically honoured and that has been the source of many CVEs). pdftract MUST never execute embedded JS, but it MUST surface its presence so downstream consumers (security tools, compliance scanners) know to flag the document for review.

## Implementation guidance

- Test file: tests/security/TH-04-js-presence.rs
- Fixture: tests/fixtures/security/embedded-js.pdf
  - Contains a /Catalog with /OpenAction -> /JS containing app.alert("pwn")
  - Contains a /Page with /AA -> /O (open action) -> /JS containing a second alert
  - Contains a separate /Page with /Annot (form field) /A /JS containing a third snippet
  - Total of 3 distinct JavaScript actions across the document
  - Generated via a build script (qpdf or pdfrw)
  - PROVENANCE.md entry: synthetic, public-domain
- Test cases:
  1. Extract the fixture; assert exit 0 (success); assert output contains exactly 3 entries in metadata.javascript_actions[]
  2. Each entry has fields: location ("catalog.openaction", "page.0.aa.O", "page.1.annot.0.A"), code_excerpt (first 200 chars of the JS, NOT the alert call which would actually execute if we ran it)
  3. Assert JAVASCRIPT_PRESENT diagnostic emitted at info level
  4. Assert no process called eval / no v8/JS engine spawned (verify via strace or by absence of any JS engine in dependencies via cargo tree)
- Independent assertion: cargo tree --features=default | grep -i -E '(deno|v8|quickjs|boa)' returns nothing

## Critical considerations

- The fixture MUST be safe to extract -- the test runs the JS code path; if pdftract ever shipped with a JS engine, the test would actually run the JS (worst case: app.alert is harmless, but a malicious fixture could exfiltrate)
- The code_excerpt MUST be truncated and HTML/JSON-escaped if the JSON output renders it -- the test verifies the raw bytes do not break the JSON output
- /AA, /OpenAction, /JS, /JavaScript actions on form fields, and FDF JavaScript imports are the four canonical entry points; the fixture covers at least three
- The diagnostic is INFO level, not WARN or ERROR -- the PDF is well-formed and the presence of JS is not itself an error; consumers decide policy
- A negative test: extract a fixture without any JS; assert metadata.javascript_actions is absent or empty array
- The "no JS engine in deps" check is the strongest assertion -- if a future contributor adds boa or deno_core for some reason, the test fails immediately

## Acceptance criteria

- tests/security/TH-04-js-presence.rs exists and passes
- Fixture tests/fixtures/security/embedded-js.pdf committed with 3 distinct JS actions
- metadata.javascript_actions[] populated with 3 entries
- JAVASCRIPT_PRESENT diagnostic emitted
- cargo tree assertion passes (no JS engine present)
- Negative test (no-JS PDF) also asserted

## References

- Plan: line 875 (TH-04 entry), Phase 1.2 (object parser must see /AA, /OpenAction, /JS entries), Diagnostic Code Catalog JAVASCRIPT_PRESENT

## Scope

Generate the canonical JSON Schema at docs/schema/v1.0/pdftract.schema.json from the Rust output types in pdftract-core and check it in. Add a schemafied migration tool that lives alongside the schema files and applies known v1.0 to v1.x transformations to recorded JSON outputs.

This file is the contract that consumers depend on; any drift between the Rust structs and the schema is a release-blocker. The schema-version migration tool supports the additive-evolution rules in plan lines 3659-ish (additive fields land within v1.x; breaking changes bump to v2.0 with a migration step).

## Implementation guidance

- Source: pdftract-core public output types (concrete serde-derived structs, NOT serde_json::Value per Anti-Patterns line 986)
- Generator crate or build script: schemars (preferred) or a custom JsonSchema derive walker; outputs JSON Schema 2020-12 dialect
- Path: docs/schema/v1.0/pdftract.schema.json (checked in; regenerated via just / xtask command, NOT auto-regenerated on every build)
- Migration tooling: crates/pdftract-schema-migrate/ (or xtask migrate-schema) that takes (schema-version, json) and applies registered transformations

- broken_vector MUST be in the page_type enum (line 1836) -- forgetting this breaks INV-11
- Schema lives at v1.0; future-additive changes (e.g. new metadata fields) land at v1.x but DO NOT bump the file path -- the v1.0 directory remains the v1 schema family per the additive-evolution rules
- A v2.0 schema would land at docs/schema/v2.0/pdftract.schema.json alongside, never replacing v1.0
- Migration tool MUST be deterministic and reproducible (no timestamps, no UUIDs in output) -- consumers may use it in CI

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the `quality-matrix` DAG branch in `pdftract-ci`. Five parallel quality gate steps, any one failing blocks PR merge:

1. **clippy** — `cargo clippy --all-targets --features default,serve,decrypt -- -D warnings` plus library-only lint pass with `-D clippy::unwrap_used -D clippy::expect_used` (INV-8 enforcement)
2. **cargo audit** — `cargo audit --deny warnings --ignore unmaintained` on `Cargo.lock`; >= medium severity advisory blocks the run; an `audit.toml` maintains the allow-list of intentionally-ignored advisories with justifications
3. **cargo deny** — `cargo deny check licenses bans sources advisories` with `deny.toml` enforcing the license allowlist (MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD-3-Clause, MPL-2.0, ISC; deny GPL and AGPL transitively) and the dependency ban list
4. **MSRV check** — `cargo build --features default` against `rust:1.78-slim` (current MSRV); fails if the crate accidentally requires a newer Rust feature
5. **cargo bloat budget** — `cargo bloat --release --features default --crates --target x86_64-unknown-linux-musl -n 50`; binary size must be <= 4 MB stripped; output published as an artifact `bloat-report.json`

## Why this matters

These gates implement Tier 1 hard gates from the plan's Quality Targets section. Without them, regressions to binary size (R2 risk), license contamination, security advisories, MSRV drift, and `unwrap()`/`expect()` use inside `pdftract-core` would slip past code review.

## Implementation guidance

- Clippy: use the same `pdftract-test-glibc:1.78` image from Phase 0.3 (clippy is fastest there because it has full dep tree compiled)
- audit: install `cargo-audit` once into `pdftract-test-glibc` image; run `cargo audit fetch` then `cargo audit`
- deny: install `cargo-deny`; deny.toml lives at repo root; reference `https://embarkstudios.github.io/cargo-deny/` defaults
- MSRV check: pin to `rust:1.78-slim` Docker tag; allow override via `pdftract-ci` workflow parameter `msrv` (default `1.78`)
- cargo bloat: install once into `pdftract-test-glibc`; output JSON via `--message-format=json` then a small post-processor to assert <= 4_194_304 bytes (`4 * 1024 * 1024`)
- Add a `cargo bloat --features remote --crates` second invocation (no gate, info only) to track ureq's contribution and feed PB-5 (the alt-feature escape hatch)
- `audit.toml` allow-list entries MUST include: advisory ID, reason, "ignore until" date (default 90 days), reviewer GitHub handle

## Critical considerations

- The 4 MB binary budget is gated only for `x86_64-unknown-linux-musl` — other triples are larger by nature (Windows PE overhead, macOS Mach-O metadata) and their measurements are informational
- The clippy `-D clippy::unwrap_used -D clippy::expect_used` lint applies ONLY to library code (`crates/pdftract-core/src/`); test code, examples, and `crates/pdftract-cli/` retain the permissive defaults
- INV-8 lint enforcement is restated in this bead because the Phase 0.3 nextest leg does not run clippy
- `cargo audit` may emit advisories on transitive deps we cannot upgrade in lockstep; `audit.toml` allow-list with a documented expiry is the escape hatch
- cargo deny's license check must reject GPL-3.0 (e.g. accidental pull of a GPL-licensed crate via dev-dep)
- If `cargo bloat` exceeds 4 MB, the first-line response is documented in PB-2: switch wordlist to Bloom filter behind the `wordlist-bloom` feature

## Acceptance criteria

- All five quality steps appear in the WorkflowTemplate DAG as `quality-matrix`
- A green PR run shows all five passing within 8 min combined wall-clock
- A deliberate `unwrap()` added inside `crates/pdftract-core/src/lib.rs` causes the clippy gate to fail
- A deliberate advisory-vulnerable dep (e.g. an old `time` crate version) causes the audit gate to fail
- A deliberate GPL-licensed dep causes the deny gate to fail
- A deliberate use of `Rust 1.79+` feature causes the MSRV gate to fail
- `bloat-report.json` is published every run and inspectable from the Argo UI

## References

- Plan section: Phase 0, line 1007 (clippy, bloat, audit, deny, MSRV)
- INV-8 (no panic at public boundary)
- R2 (binary size risk), PB-2 (Bloom filter escape hatch)
- ADR-002 (wordlist storage)

issue.description:
## Scope

Given candidate column gaps, partition the page into candidate columns (regions between consecutive gaps + before-first + after-last). For each candidate, count UNIQUE LINES whose first span's x0 falls within the column's x-range. Promote with line_count >= 3. Returns Vec<Column { x_range, line_count }>.

## Why this matters

False columns from sparse gaps (e.g., a single wide image surrounded by narrow text strips) would otherwise produce nonsensical 5-column detections. The 3-line minimum is the calibrated confidence floor.

## Implementation guidance

- Compute candidate columns: pairs (gap_i.hi, gap_i+1.lo) for consecutive gaps; (0, gap_0.lo) before-first; (gap_last.hi, page_width) after-last.
- For each candidate, walk line list, get line's first span (post-within-line-sort), check if span.bbox[0] in candidate range.
- Count UNIQUE lines per column.
- Filter: line_count >= 3 -> confirmed.
- No gaps detected -> entire page is one column.

## Critical considerations

- INV: 3-line minimum from plan; lowering increases false positives.
- Lines whose first span is in a GAP region remain unassigned (column = None).
- "First span" = leftmost post-sort.

## Acceptance criteria

- 2-column page with 30 lines each: both confirmed.
- 2-column page with 30 lines + 2 lines: only 30-line column confirmed.
- Single column: 1 candidate -> confirmed.
- Empty page: 0 confirmed.

## References

- Plan section: Phase 4.3 (line 1681)

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement step 2 (contrast normalization via histogram stretch to [0,255]) and the image-source dispatch logic that selects the binarization algorithm per page based on PDF filter chain (DCTDecode -> Sauvola; FlateDecode digital -> Otsu; JBIG2Decode -> skip).

## Why this matters

Histogram stretch fixes the input range for downstream binarization. Without it, washed-out scans (low contrast) produce thresholds that lose detail in either highlights or shadows. The image-source dispatch is the policy that picks the right algorithm for the right input — Sauvola is slower but adapts to local lighting; Otsu is faster but assumes a globally consistent illumination.

## Implementation guidance

- Histogram stretch: compute min/max gray values, ignoring extremes (1st/99th percentile to be robust to outliers); linearly map [min, max] -> [0, 255]; skip for JBIG2
- Image-source dispatch reads ImageSource enum (set by 5.3 coordinator from Phase 1.5 filter inventory):
  - PhysicalScan -> Sauvola binarization (step 5.3.3)
  - DigitalOrigin -> Otsu binarization (step 5.3.3)
  - Jbig2 -> skip contrast, skip binarization, skip denoising
- Provide ImageSource detector function: detect_image_source(page: &PageContext) -> ImageSource using Phase 1.5 filter info

## Critical considerations

- Percentile clip (1/99) matters: pure min/max stretch amplifies any single black or white pixel into anchors

- Mixed pages MAY emit IMG_SOURCE_MIXED diagnostic for debuggability

- JBIG2 fixture: histogram stretch skipped (input == output bit-identical for binarization step)

## Scope

Implement the JBIG2Decode passthrough filter. Records the /JBIG2Globals reference (shared symbol dict) for downstream consumers. Emits OCR_JBIG2_UNSUPPORTED diagnostic when the full-render feature is NOT compiled (per EC-11).

Module: crates/pdftract-core/src/decoder/jbig2.rs.

## Why this matters

JBIG2 is the dominant compression for scanned bitonal images (legal documents, archival scans). pdftract-core never decodes JBIG2 itself (the format is too complex; pdfium-render handles it via the full-render feature). Without the passthrough + diagnostic, JBIG2-only PDFs fail silently or with a confusing error.

## Implementation guidance

- JBIG2 has a complex segment format; do NOT validate beyond passthrough (don't try to parse segment headers in pdftract-core)
- Check if full-render feature is enabled (cfg!(feature = \"full-render\"))
- If NOT: emit OCR_JBIG2_UNSUPPORTED diagnostic (per EC-11); still pass through bytes for downstream consumer
- /JBIG2Globals: a reference to a globally-shared symbol dictionary; record the ObjRef on the StreamMeta struct
- The OCR pipeline (Phase 5.4) reads StreamMeta.jbig2_globals_ref to fetch and prepend globals before sending to pdfium-render
- Module: crates/pdftract-core/src/decoder/jbig2.rs

## Critical considerations

- /JBIG2Globals is an indirect reference (ObjRef), not inline data; resolve via XrefResolver to get the global symbols stream
- Without /JBIG2Globals, the JBIG2 stream is self-contained (file-organization), still decodable
- EC-11 (JBIG2 without full-render) emits the diagnostic once per stream; downstream consumer (Phase 5.4) raises a clearer user-facing error
- Passthrough means the raw bytes are stored as-is in the Image XObject's stream content; consumer is responsible for decoding

## Acceptance criteria

- JBIG2 stream with full-render feature → pass-through, no diagnostic
- JBIG2 stream WITHOUT full-render → OCR_JBIG2_UNSUPPORTED diagnostic; pass-through anyway
- /JBIG2Globals reference recorded on StreamMeta
- Self-contained JBIG2 (no globals): StreamMeta.jbig2_globals_ref is None
- Round-trip test with reference JBIG2 fixture (scanned document)

- PDF spec 7.4.7 JBIG2Decode
- Coordinator: pdftract-57np8 (parent)
- Phase 5.4 OCR pipeline (consumes the passthrough output)

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement detect_encryption(trailer: &PdfDict, resolver: &XrefResolver) -> Option<EncryptionInfo> that parses the trailer's /Encrypt dictionary into a structured EncryptionInfo. Recognizes /Filter (Standard handler), /V (1/2/4/5), /R (2/3/4/5/6), /KeyLength, /O, /U, /CF, /StmF, /StrF, /Perms (V=5) fields.

## Why this matters

Encryption detection is the gate: without correct parsing of /Encrypt, the decryption layer doesn't know which algorithm to use, and encrypted PDFs fail with confusing errors. The detection layer is also the place that emits ENCRYPTION_UNSUPPORTED when a non-Standard filter is encountered (e.g. Adobe Public Key, custom crypt filters).

## Implementation guidance

- Public types:
  ```rust
  pub struct EncryptionInfo {
      pub version: u8,        // V: 1, 2, 4, 5
      pub revision: u8,       // R: 2, 3, 4, 5, 6
      pub key_length: u32,    // bits: 40, 128, 256
      pub owner_hash: Vec<u8>, // /O
      pub user_hash: Vec<u8>,  // /U
      pub perms: u32,          // /P or /Perms
      pub file_id: Vec<u8>,    // first16(/ID[0]) from trailer
      pub crypt_filters: Option<CryptFiltersV4>,  // V=4, V=5
  }

  pub struct CryptFiltersV4 {
      pub stream_filter: String,  // /StmF
      pub string_filter: String,  // /StrF
      pub filters: BTreeMap<String, CryptFilterDef>,  // /CF
  }
  ```
- detect_encryption(trailer, resolver):
  1. Look up /Encrypt in trailer (may be ObjRef or inline dict)
  2. Resolve ObjRef via XrefResolver
  3. Check /Filter == /Standard; else emit ENCRYPTION_UNSUPPORTED and return None
  4. Parse /V, /R, /KeyLength
  5. Parse /O, /U (byte strings, length 32 for R<=4, length 48 for R>=5)
  6. Parse /P (32-bit signed int; perms bitfield)
  7. For V>=4, parse /CF (crypt filter dict), /StmF, /StrF
  8. For V=5, parse /Perms (encrypted permissions bitfield)
  9. Extract /ID[0] from trailer (or empty if missing)
  10. Return Some(EncryptionInfo)
- Module: crates/pdftract-core/src/encryption/detection.rs (feature-gated on decrypt)

## Critical considerations

- Custom /Filter values (not /Standard): emit ENCRYPTION_UNSUPPORTED with the filter name in the diagnostic; return None. Do NOT attempt to decrypt
- /O and /U for R<=4 are exactly 32 bytes; for R>=5 are 48 bytes. Length mismatch emits ENCRYPTION_INVALID_DICT
- /P is a signed i32 but treated as u32 bitfield; widely-used permissions bits documented in PDF spec 7.6.3.2
- /ID[0] missing in trailer: use empty Vec<u8>; some encrypted PDFs lack /ID and rely on V=5 (which doesn't require /ID); detection returns Some, decryption layer handles the case
- CryptFilterDef parsing for V>=4: /CFM (AESV2, AESV3, V2 for RC4), /Length, /AuthEvent
- Detection MUST NOT attempt key derivation or decryption; sibling beads do that

## Acceptance criteria

- detect_encryption on a V=1 R=2 RC4-40 fixture returns EncryptionInfo with version=1, revision=2, key_length=40
- detect_encryption on V=5 R=6 AES-256 fixture returns EncryptionInfo with version=5, revision=6, key_length=256
- detect_encryption on non-/Standard filter PDF returns None + ENCRYPTION_UNSUPPORTED diagnostic
- detect_encryption on PDF with /O length 31 (truncated) returns None + ENCRYPTION_INVALID_DICT
- detect_encryption on PDF with no /Encrypt key in trailer returns None (cleanly)
- Unit tests cover all V/R combinations from the spec

## References

- Plan section: encryption detection
- PDF spec 7.6.1, 7.6.3
- Coordinator: pdftract-1z0qt (parent — encryption bundle)
- Sibling beads: RC4 decryption, AES-128 decryption, AES-256 decryption
Labels: detection, encryption, phase-1

issue.description:
## Goal

For any character code from a content stream, resolve a Unicode scalar value and a confidence score. Deliver pdftract-core::font module.

## Sub-phases

- 2.1 Font Type Detection — classify font from resource dict (Type1, Type1 Standard 14, TrueType, Type0 composite, CIDFontType0/2, Type3, OpenType CFF); strip 6-uppercase-letter subset prefix; CIDToGIDMap handling (Identity or stream)
- 2.2 Encoding Resolution — 4-level fallback chain: Level 1 ToUnicode CMap (confidence 1.0); Level 2 named encoding + AGL (0.9); Level 3 font fingerprint cache (0.85); Level 4 glyph shape recognition via fontdue + pHash (0.7); failure U+FFFD (0.0)
- 2.3 CJK Encoding — predefined CMaps (Identity-H/V, UniJIS-UTF16, UniGB-UTF16, UniCNS-UTF16, UniKS-UTF16); raw byte decoding via encoding_rs (Shift-JIS, GB18030, Big5, EUC-KR); multi-byte code parsing from codespace ranges
- 2.4 Type 3 Font Handling — content-stream-defined glyphs; ToUnicode first, then named encoding, then shape recognition; Type3 metrics via /Widths + /FontMatrix
- 2.5 Glyph Shape Database — compile-time sorted slice of ~5000 pHash to char mappings; rendered offline from open-source fonts; pHash = 8x8 DCT top-left AC coefs thresholded against median

## Rationale

PDF encoding is the second-hardest part of extraction after content stream execution. Many real-world PDFs ship subset fonts without /ToUnicode CMaps, so direct character-code-to-glyph lookup fails. The 4-level fallback chain ensures pdftract recovers Unicode for >90% of glyphs even with no ToUnicode — a CI-gated primary objective. Each level emits a unicode_source tag and a confidence score, giving downstream consumers full visibility.

The font fingerprint cache (Level 3) and glyph shape DB (Level 4) are pdftract accuracy differentiators against pdfminer.six and pypdf — both of which fail silently with U+FFFD when /ToUnicode is missing.

## Critical considerations

- Standard 14 fonts have hardcoded metrics; no font program embedded; AGL lookup always succeeds
- Subset prefix is exactly 6 uppercase letters followed by + (e.g. ABCDEF+Times-Roman) — strip BEFORE lookup
- CIDFontType2 with CIDToGIDMap as stream: decode FlateDecode, interpret as 2-byte big-endian GID array indexed by CID
- AGL 1.4 has ~4400 entries; ships as compile-time phf::Map via phf crate
- Font fingerprint DB target: ~500 KB binary footprint (covers top 200 commercial fonts initially)
- Glyph shape DB target: ~300 KB binary footprint (~5000 entries covering Latin, Greek, Cyrillic, symbols)
- pHash quirk: false-positive rate goes up if Hamming threshold > 8; ties broken by Unicode frequency rank
- CJK codespace ranges define 1- vs 2-byte boundaries — parse CMap to determine these

## Acceptance criteria (this epic closes when)

- All 5 sub-phase beads (2.1-2.5) closed
- pdftract-core::font module compiles and integrates with parser
- Unicode recovery rate >90% on tests/fixtures/encoding/ corpus (CI-gated)
- ToUnicode CMap tests pass: bfchar multi-codepoint (fi ligature), bfrange explicit array, WinAnsi 0x92 to U+2019, MacRoman quotation marks
- CJK fixtures decode (Shift-JIS, GB18030, Big5, EUC-KR)
- Type 3 font with arbitrary names + no ToUnicode triggers shape recognition with confidence 0.7
- Font fingerprint DB binary footprint < 500 KB (cargo bloat verified)

## Blocks

- Phase 3 — requires font pipeline for glyph-to-Unicode resolution

## See also

- Plan section: Phase 2: Font and Encoding Pipeline
- docs/research/glyph-recognition-and-unicode-recovery.md

issue.description:
## Scope

Add a `regression-corpus` step to `pdftract-ci` that runs the freshly-built `x86_64-unknown-linux-musl` binary against the 500-PDF private regression corpus stored in B2 (via ARMOR encrypted S3 proxy). Compares per-document JSON output to the previous-known-good baseline; any per-document Character Error Rate (CER) delta > 0.5% blocks PR merge.

The corpus is canonical: it is the private collection of "real-world" PDFs (academic papers, scanned receipts, government forms, legal contracts) curated to be diverse enough to expose regressions across all extraction modes.

## Why this matters

Tier 3 is one of the three hard gates from the plan's Quality Targets section. CER regression > 0.5% on any single document indicates an extraction quality regression that would be felt by end users.

## Implementation guidance

- Corpus location: B2 bucket `pdftract-regression-corpus/v1/*.pdf` accessed via the ARMOR proxy endpoint (encrypted at rest); the `argo-workflows` namespace has a `b2-readonly` Secret (ESO-synced from OpenBao) holding the read-only ARMOR proxy credentials
- Baseline outputs: stored alongside the corpus under the `baselines/<sha256>.json` prefix; baselines are updated by a separate merge-time job, NOT this PR-time job
- Step image: `pdftract-test-glibc:1.78` from Phase 0.3 (already has `b2` CLI and `aws` CLI preinstalled)
- Step sequence per document:
  1. Download the PDF using `aws s3 cp` against the ARMOR proxy service endpoint inside the cluster
  2. Run `./pdftract-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl extract --json --pages all <pdf>` and capture stdout to `actual.json`
  3. Fetch baseline `baseline.json` from B2 at the matching path
  4. Compute per-document CER via `tools/cer-diff actual.json baseline.json --threshold 0.005` (this is a tiny rust binary built from `crates/pdftract-cer-diff/`)
  5. Emit JSON line `{sha, cer_delta, pass}` to `regression-results.jsonl`
- Parallelism: process 8 documents concurrently via `withSequence:` plus `arguments.parameters.shard-index` / `arguments.parameters.shard-total` (8 shards total)
- Failure: any single document with cer_delta > 0.005 marks the step failed and uploads `regression-results.jsonl` as an artifact for diagnosis

## Critical considerations

- The corpus is encrypted at rest via ARMOR per the project's backup strategy; never download via direct B2 public URL — only via the ARMOR proxy service on the iad-ci cluster
- Baseline mismatch is normal during legitimate quality improvements; the workflow has a parameter `regression-mode: gate|update`; PR runs always use `gate`, the merge-time job uses `update` to refresh baselines
- The 500-document corpus is intentionally diverse: 50 academic papers, 50 government forms, 50 invoices, 50 scanned receipts, 50 legal contracts, 50 multi-column magazines, 50 CJK documents, 50 RTL documents, 50 financial filings, 50 misc. Document distribution justifies the 0.5% threshold (per-doc, not aggregate)
- Cache the regression binary in the cargo-cache PVC so it doesn't redownload from artifact storage each step
- Wall-clock budget: 500 docs / 8 shards = ~63 docs per shard; ~3 s per doc target -> ~3 min per shard. If shards exceed 5 min consistently, shard count goes to 16

## Acceptance criteria

- regression-corpus step runs on every PR
- 500 documents processed in <= 8 min total wall-clock
- A deliberate output-format regression (e.g. truncating glyph runs at 80 chars) trips the gate on >= 1 document
- `regression-results.jsonl` artifact published every run
- A PR that legitimately improves extraction quality can be merged through a documented baseline-refresh workflow (out of scope for THIS bead: requires a follow-up bead in Phase 0.6.1 for the baseline-refresh CronWorkflow)

## References

- Plan section: Phase 0, line 1007 (regression corpus mention); Quality Targets / Tier 3
- Project knowledge: ARMOR encrypted S3 proxy for B2 backups
- Sibling: news-trader uses the same `b2-readonly` Secret + ARMOR proxy pattern

## Scope

Implement the diagnostic emission infrastructure: Severity enum (Info, Warning, Error), Diagnostic struct (code, severity, page_index, message, hint), DiagnosticsCollector for aggregating per-page diagnostics, and the registry of stable error codes used across pdftract (e.g. IMG_SOFTMASK_UNSUPPORTED, BROKENVECTOR_OCR_UNAVAILABLE, OCR_LANGUAGE_UNAVAILABLE, etc.).

## Why this matters

Error entries are part of the schema contract: each diagnostic must have stable code + severity + page_index per the Phase 6.1 critical test (line 2032). A stable error-code registry lets downstream tools react programmatically (e.g. "if I see BROKENVECTOR_OCR_UNAVAILABLE I should install Tesseract").

## Implementation guidance

- Severity: enum { Info, Warning, Error } with serde rename_all = lowercase
- Diagnostic: { code: String (must match /^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]+$/), severity, page_index: Option<u32>, message: String, hint: Option<String> }
- DiagnosticsCollector: thread-safe collector backed by Mutex<Vec<Diagnostic>>; emit(code, ...) helper used throughout codebase
- Error code registry: pdftract-core/src/diagnostics/codes.rs with const-fn constants e.g. pub const IMG_SOFTMASK_UNSUPPORTED: &str = "IMG_SOFTMASK_UNSUPPORTED";
- Initial code set (more added as features land):
  - IMG_SOFTMASK_UNSUPPORTED (5.2.1)
  - IMG_SOURCE_MIXED (5.3.2)
  - IMG_DESKEW_OUT_OF_RANGE (5.3.1)
  - BROKENVECTOR_OCR_UNAVAILABLE (5.1.4)
  - OCR_LANGUAGE_UNAVAILABLE (5.4.2)
  - PROFILE_INVALID (5.6.2)
  - REPAIR_RESCUED_FROM_BACKWARDS_XREF (Phase 1)
- Document each code in docs/integrations/diagnostics-codes.md (allowlisted path)

## Critical considerations

- Code strings MUST be SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE; validate at compile time via const-fn or test
- Diagnostics accumulate across rayon threads; collector must be Send + Sync
- emit() is called from extraction code, NOT from output serialization (separation of concerns)
- Aggregate diagnostics for the whole document end up in Output.errors
- Per-page diagnostics also reachable from page (NOT in the per-page struct in Phase 6.1; they aggregate at document level for simplicity)
- Adding a code is a public-API contract change; document discipline in CONTRIBUTING

## Acceptance criteria

- All initial codes emitted somewhere in 5.x code paths (verified via grep)
- DiagnosticsCollector unit test: emit from 4 threads -> 4 entries in final Vec
- Code registry parses: every constant matches the regex pattern
- Output.errors populated correctly on extraction errors

## References

- Plan section: Phase 6.1 critical test (line 2032)
- All Phase 5 diagnostics emitters
- docs/integrations/diagnostics-codes.md (deliverable)

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement pdftract.extract, pdftract.extract_text, and pdftract.extract_stream PyO3 functions. extract returns a PyDict (via pythonize from Output); extract_text returns a PyString of plain text; extract_stream returns a PyIterator yielding one PyDict per page. All options pass through kwargs to ExtractionOptions.

## Why this matters

This is the public Python API surface. Names, signatures, and return shapes are user-facing forever — getting them wrong here means a v2.0 SDK migration.

## Implementation guidance

- extract(py, path: &str, kwargs: Option<&PyDict>) -> PyResult<PyObject>:
  parse kwargs -> ExtractionOptions; py.allow_threads(|| extract_inner(path, opts)) -> Output; pythonize(py, &output)
- extract_text(py, path, kwargs) -> PyResult<PyString>:
  same options handling; py.allow_threads(|| extract_text_inner(path, opts)) -> String
- extract_stream(py, path, kwargs) -> PyResult<PyObject>:
  returns a custom PyClass StreamIterator with __next__ that drives the NDJSON pipeline incrementally
- StreamIterator: holds a Receiver<PageFrame> backed by a background thread running the streaming pipeline; __next__ blocks (with GIL released) on recv; returns PyDict (or raises StopIteration on end)
- kwargs allowed (any subset): ocr (bool), ocr_language (list[str] or comma-string), include_invisible (bool), extract_forms (bool), extract_attachments (bool), readability_threshold (float), password (str), max_decompress_gb (int), full_render (bool)
- Unknown kwargs: raise PdftractError (strict) — don't silently ignore

## Critical considerations

- pythonize converts serde::Serialize to PyDict — use this rather than hand-rolling
- extract_stream yields only page dicts (frame: "page" equivalent); NOT header / footer (per plan line 2067)
- The Iterator protocol's __next__ must release GIL during blocking recv (py.allow_threads)
- For extract_stream, errors mid-stream get raised as PdftractError on __next__
- StreamIterator drops cleanly when garbage-collected mid-stream (background thread observes drop + cancels)

## Acceptance criteria

- pdftract.extract("test.pdf") returns dict with all 6.1 fields
- pdftract.extract_text("test.pdf") returns multi-page text concatenated with form-feed
- pdftract.extract_stream("test.pdf") yields one dict per page; full iteration returns N dicts for N-page PDF
- Unknown kwarg raises PdftractError with field name

## References

- Plan section: Phase 6.3 API surface (lines 2059-2078)
- pythonize crate

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the pdftract doctor subcommand: validates the runtime environment without performing an extraction. Each check produces an OK/WARN/FAIL result with a human-readable detail string. Output formats: colored human-readable table (default), JSON (--json), or features-only (--features). Exit code 0 if all checks pass (no FAIL), 1 if any FAIL.

This bead is the sub-phase coordinator that aggregates the child task beads:

- pdftract-XX: Check definitions (pdftract version+features+git-sha; tesseract install+langs; leptonica; libtiff; libopenjp2; pdfium-render; network reachability; cache dir; profile path; ulimit; available RAM; system locale; temp dir)
- pdftract-XX: Output formats (human colored table; --json; --features)
- pdftract-XX: Exit code policy (0=all OK/WARN; 1=any FAIL)
- pdftract-XX: Runbook integration (docs/operations/manual-platform-smoke.md references doctor output)

## Why this matters

doctor is the operator's first line of defense against \"why isn't this working?\" — a single command that surfaces every common environmental misconfiguration (missing Tesseract, wrong language pack, no network, low disk, bad locale). Without it, debugging requires multiple round-trips and reading source. With it, a fresh deployment's smoke test is a one-liner.

Critically, doctor is REQUIRED to run on every fresh deployment as the first action; runbooks and CI smoke tests invoke it as the gate. The default exit policy (1 on any FAIL even without --exit-on-fail) makes it usable as a CI gate without needing extra flags.

## Critical considerations

- doctor itself MUST never crash; every check is wrapped in catch_unwind so a panic in one check still produces a usable report
- Feature-gated checks (Tesseract checks only when ocr is compiled; pdfium-render only when full-render is compiled) appear as N/A rows in --json output, omitted from human-readable table
- The default exit policy fails on ANY FAIL (not just when --exit-on-fail is given) per plan section 6.10 line 2528
- All checks run sequentially; the longest check is the network reachability HEAD request (configurable timeout, default 5s); total runtime budget is < 10 s on a normal deployment
- doctor ships in the default-feature binary (no feature flag) so even a minimal pdftract binary can validate its environment

## Acceptance criteria

- All 4 child task beads closed
- A fresh Alpine container with pdftract binary copied in but no Tesseract/Leptonica/libtiff: pdftract doctor exits 1 (no flag needed); table shows three FAIL rows; --json output deserializes correctly
- A fully-provisioned container: pdftract doctor exits 0, all rows OK
- Network unreachable: network reachability row reports WARN (slow) or FAIL (DNS failure); does not crash
- --exit-on-fail flag exits 1 on any FAIL across all rows; exits 0 if only WARNs are present
- --profile-dir pointed at a directory containing a profile with password: key: profile-search-path row reports FAIL with PROFILE_SECRETS_FORBIDDEN reference
- Module under crates/pdftract-cli/src/doctor/ (checks/, output/, runbook.rs)
- No feature flag; doctor ships in default-feature binary

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the `@pdftract/sdk` npm package as a subprocess-based SDK. Spawn the bundled `pdftract` binary via `child_process.spawn`, parse JSON output, expose the 9 contract methods as async functions returning Promises. Use Node.js `Readable` streams for `extract_stream` and `search`. Package as a dual ESM + CJS export so both `import` and `require` syntax work. Repo at `github.com/jedarden/pdftract-node`.

## Why this matters

Node.js is the highest-population JavaScript runtime and the most common SDK target after Python. Dual ESM + CJS coverage means modern bundlers (Vite, esbuild) and older toolchains (Webpack 4) both consume the package cleanly. Subprocess transport sidesteps the N-API / FFI complexity that would otherwise gate Node-version compatibility.

## Implementation guidance

- Package name: `@pdftract/sdk` (scoped npm package); version pinned to binary version
- Repo: `github.com/jedarden/pdftract-node` (separate repo per plan acceptance criteria)
- File layout (generator-driven; see Tera template scaffolding bead):
  - `src/index.ts` (re-exports the 9 methods + error classes)
  - `src/codegen/methods.ts` (generated from Tera template)
  - `src/codegen/errors.ts` (generated; 8 exception classes)
  - `src/ergonomics.ts` (hand-written option-normalization, type-coercion)
  - `src/subprocess.ts` (the spawn + JSON-parse machinery)
  - `src/stream.ts` (Readable wrapper for NDJSON output)
  - `test/conformance.test.ts` (vitest)
  - `tsconfig.json` (target ES2022, module ESNext)
  - `package.json` with dual exports:
    ```json
    {
      "type": "module",
      "main": "./dist/cjs/index.cjs",
      "module": "./dist/esm/index.js",
      "exports": {
        ".": {
          "import": "./dist/esm/index.js",
          "require": "./dist/cjs/index.cjs",
          "types": "./dist/types/index.d.ts"
        }
      }
    }
    ```
- Method signatures (TypeScript):
  - `extract(source: string | URL | Buffer, options?: ExtractOptions): Promise<Document>`
  - `extractText(source: string | URL | Buffer, options?: ExtractOptions): Promise<string>`
  - `extractMarkdown(source: string | URL | Buffer, options?: ExtractOptions): Promise<string>`
  - `extractStream(source: string | URL | Buffer, options?: ExtractOptions): Readable` (emits `Page` objects)
  - `search(source: string | URL | Buffer, pattern: string | RegExp, options?: SearchOptions): Readable` (emits `Match` objects)
  - `getMetadata(source: string | URL | Buffer, options?: ExtractOptions): Promise<Metadata>`
  - `hash(source: string | URL | Buffer, options?: HashOptions): Promise<Fingerprint>`
  - `classify(source: string | URL | Buffer): Promise<Classification>`
  - `verifyReceipt(path: string, receipt: Receipt): Promise<boolean>`
- Option names use camelCase per the contract: CLI `--ocr-language` becomes `ocrLanguage`
- Binary lookup: constructor accepts `binaryPath`; otherwise probes PATH; otherwise downloads via `auto-install` flag (default off)
- Subprocess error handling: on non-zero exit, the SDK reads stderr (which is JSON-formatted by the binary in `--json-errors` mode) and throws the appropriate exception class
- Conformance runner: `test/conformance.test.ts` runs the shared suite via vitest

## Critical considerations

- Dual-package hazard: avoid the ESM/CJS dual-package interop pitfall by NEVER importing across the boundary inside the package itself; each entry point is self-contained
- TypeScript types are FIRST-CLASS (the SDK is the type source; downstream consumers do NOT need @types/pdftract)
- The Buffer source argument: Node.js may pass a Buffer for in-memory PDFs; the SDK writes to a temp file (or stdin) and the binary reads from there
- `Readable` for streaming: the underlying binary emits NDJSON; the SDK consumes line-by-line and emits parsed Page or Match objects as stream items
- The dual ESM/CJS build: use `tsup` or `tsc` + a post-build CJS transform; verify with `node -e "require('@pdftract/sdk').extractText(...)"` AND `node --input-type=module -e "import {extractText} from '@pdftract/sdk'; ..."` both work
- Subprocess spawn cost is ~10-50 ms; for hot-path workloads document the `pdftract serve` HTTP transport as the alternative

## Acceptance criteria

- The `@pdftract/sdk` package builds and publishes a dual ESM + CJS distribution
- All 9 contract methods exported with TypeScript types
- All 8 exception classes inherit from PdftractError
- `test/conformance.test.ts` passes 100% of the suite
- Both `import {extract} from '@pdftract/sdk'` and `const {extract} = require('@pdftract/sdk')` work in their respective module modes
- The package downloads/locates the binary correctly per the contract's binary-resolution rules

## References

- Plan section: SDK Architecture / The Ten SDKs, line 3473 (Node.js subprocess + ESM + CJS dual-package)
- Plan section: SDK Architecture / Per-SDK Release Channels, line 3570
- Plan section: SDK Acceptance Criteria, lines 3581-3590
- Sibling: pdftract-node-publish Argo workflow (separate bead)
- Sibling: SDK contract and conformance suite

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement detect_javascript(catalog, pages, acroform, resolver) -> bool that scans the PDF for any JavaScript action dict and sets contains_javascript flag. JavaScript is NEVER EXECUTED; only its presence is flagged.

## Why this matters

JavaScript in PDFs is a major attack surface (CVE-class issues in Acrobat over the years). Downstream consumers (security scanners, RAG ingestion pipelines, audit tools) need to know whether a PDF contains JS so they can quarantine, sanitize, or escalate review. The detector is non-executing — it never runs the JS, only flags presence.

## Implementation guidance

- Public API: detect_javascript(catalog: &Catalog, pages: &[PageDict], acroform: &Option<PdfDict>, resolver: &XrefResolver) -> bool
- Walk sites (each can trigger flag=true):
  1. Catalog /OpenAction: if value is a dict with /S /JavaScript or /S /JS
  2. Catalog /AA (Additional Actions): any sub-dict with /S /JavaScript
  3. Page-level /AA dicts: walk each page; check /AA sub-dicts
  4. AcroForm field /AA dicts: recursive walk through field tree
  5. Annotation /A or /AA dicts: per page, walk annots
- /JS is the alternate spec spelling of /JavaScript; both must be recognized
- Recursive walker design:
  ```rust
  fn dict_contains_js(dict: &PdfDict, resolver: &XrefResolver) -> bool {
      // Direct /S /JavaScript or /S /JS
      if let Some(s) = dict.get(\"S\") {
          if let PdfObject::Name(n) = s {
              if n == \"JavaScript\" || n == \"JS\" { return true; }
          }
      }
      // Recursive: /Next chained action
      if let Some(next) = dict.get(\"Next\") {
          if let PdfObject::Dict(d) = next { return dict_contains_js(d, resolver); }
      }
      false
  }
  ```

## Critical considerations

- JS detection is a presence-only check; pdftract NEVER executes embedded JavaScript. Document this prominently in code and in the JSON schema description for contains_javascript
- /Next chained actions: an action may chain to another via /Next; the walker recurses through chains
- Cycle protection: a malicious PDF could create a /Next cycle; track visited ObjRefs to bound the walk
- AcroForm field tree is itself recursive (fields can have /Kids); reuse the AcroForm walker from Phase 7.4.1
- The flag is a boolean; do NOT include the JS source code in the output (out of scope)

## Acceptance criteria

- PDF with /OpenAction /S /JavaScript → detect_javascript returns true
- PDF with page /AA /O (open) /S /JS → true
- PDF with form field /AA /K (keystroke) /S /JavaScript → true
- PDF with annotation /A /S /JavaScript → true
- PDF with no JS anywhere → false
- /Next-chained action with JS in the second action → true
- Cyclic /Next → no infinite loop (visited-set bound)

## References

- Plan section: Phase 1 metadata detection
- PDF spec 12.6.4 (Actions)
- Coordinator: pdftract-25br8 (parent — 3 detectors)
- Sibling: XFA detection, conformance detection
Labels: detection, javascript, phase-1, security

issue.description:
## Scope

Pin the Minimum Supported Rust Version (MSRV) for `pdftract-core` and `pdftract-cli` to 1.78 by declaring `rust-version = "1.78"` in each crate (via `[workspace.package]` inheritance). Add a `pdftract-ci` matrix leg that builds with `rust:1.78-slim` and fails the workflow if any source file requires a newer Rust feature.

## Why this matters

Without an MSRV gate the project silently absorbs new-Rust-isms (let-else, async-fn-in-traits, edition-2024 features) and downstream consumers stuck on older toolchains break without warning. The MSRV gate makes Rust-version drift a code-review-time conversation, not a post-release surprise.

## Implementation guidance

- Add `rust-version = "1.78"` under `[workspace.package]` in root `Cargo.toml`; both binary crates inherit via `rust-version.workspace = true`
- `pdftract-py` may have its own MSRV (PyO3 ABI requirements) — declare it explicitly there if it diverges
- Add `msrv-check` step to `pdftract-ci`: container `rust:1.78-slim`, command `cargo build --workspace --features default --locked`
- Wall-clock budget: <= 5 min for the MSRV step (uses the same cargo-cache PVC as the rest of CI)
- Document the bump policy in CONTRIBUTING.md and CHANGELOG.md: MSRV bumps are MINOR-version events with at least one release of warning; never a PATCH bump
- A `clippy::msrv` lint MAY be enabled in `clippy.toml` (`msrv = "1.78"`) to surface MSRV-incompatible APIs at lint time

## Critical considerations

- The MSRV applies to the public crates (`pdftract-core`, `pdftract-cli`); `pdftract-py` MSRV is determined by PyO3 and may be newer
- New direct dependencies whose declared MSRV exceeds 1.78 are rejected at code-review time — the `msrv-check` CI step will catch most automatically but reviewers should also call out manually
- Bumping MSRV requires updating: root `Cargo.toml`, the `rust:` image tag in the Argo template, the README MSRV badge, and a CHANGELOG entry
- `rust:1.78-slim` MUST be available on Docker Hub; if the tag is yanked switch to `rust:1.78.0-slim` (pinned point release)
- This bead is a dependency of any task that touches Cargo features or adds new crates — the MSRV gate guarantees those don't drift

## Acceptance criteria

- `cargo metadata` shows `rust_version: "1.78"` on `pdftract-core` and `pdftract-cli`
- `pdftract-ci` WorkflowTemplate has a `msrv-check` step using container `rust:1.78-slim`
- Deliberate use of a Rust 1.79+ feature (e.g. `core::error::Error` in stable) in pdftract-core causes the MSRV step to fail
- README contains an MSRV badge sourced from `Cargo.toml` (e.g. shields.io endpoint)
- CONTRIBUTING.md documents the MSRV bump policy

## References

- Plan section: Release Engineering / Minimum Supported Rust Version, line 3409-3411
- ADR-009 (Argo-only CI)
- Sibling bead: cargo deny license-check (the same `quality-matrix` DAG)
- Related: pdftract-2rf (Phase 0.4 quality gates already references the 1.78 MSRV target)
issue.title: MSRV pinned to 1.78 — declare rust-version and add rust:1.78-slim CI matrix step

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the StructTree coverage check and the per-page XY-cut fallback rule. For each page, compute coverage = (StructTree-claimed MCIDs) / (extracted glyph MCID count). If /MarkInfo /Suspects is true AND coverage < 0.80 on a given page, that page falls back to XY-cut reading order. Set reading_order_algorithm = "struct_tree" if all pages used StructTree; "xy_cut" if any page fell back; "mixed" not used (must pick one per-document field).

## Why this matters

The /Suspects flag is the producer's own warning that its StructTree may be wrong. Trusting an unreliable StructTree silently corrupts reading order on documents where the author intentionally flagged uncertainty. The 80% threshold is the agreed cutoff: below that, too many glyphs are orphan to trust the tree.

## Implementation guidance

- Read /MarkInfo /Suspects from document catalog (false/missing = trust tree always; true = apply per-page coverage check)
- Coverage formula: claimed = count of MCIDs that resolved to a non-Artifact StructElem via ParentTree (7.1.3); total = count of MCIDs emitted in marked-content sequences on this page (from 3.4)
- Per-page decision: if !suspects || coverage >= 0.80 -> use StructTree for this page's reading order; else -> mark page for XY-cut fallback
- reading_order_algorithm document-level field: "struct_tree" if 0 pages fell back, otherwise "xy_cut" (per plan; a future schema bump could distinguish "mixed")
- Per-page diagnostic emitted when fallback triggers: includes page_index, coverage value, MCID counts

## Critical considerations

- Coverage threshold is hard-coded at 0.80 - any change requires INV review
- Falling back on one page must not contaminate other pages' StructTree ordering
- XY-cut fallback path is the existing Phase 4.5 algorithm; this task only ROUTES to it
- Suspects true + coverage < 0.80 + StructTree empty -> still fall back (no division by zero)

## Acceptance criteria

- Critical test from plan: PDF with Suspects true falls back to XY-cut, reading_order_algorithm = "xy_cut"
- Unit tests: Suspects false + 50% coverage -> no fallback; Suspects true + 95% coverage -> no fallback; Suspects true + 60% coverage -> fallback
- Per-page diagnostic appears in receipts when fallback triggers
- Integration: full pipeline test on tagged-suspects-true.pdf fixture produces expected reading order

## References

- Plan section: 7.1 line 2554 (validation rule)
- INV: reading_order_algorithm enum values
- 7.1.3 (ParentTree provides claimed-MCID count)
- 3.4 marked-content (total MCID count)
- 4.5 XY-cut algorithm (fallback target)
