issue.description:
## Scope

Author the `pdftract-java-publish` WorkflowTemplate. Triggered by milestone tag after `pdftract-build-binaries` completes. Builds the Maven artifact, runs the conformance test, GPG-signs the artifacts with the project key, uploads to Sonatype OSSRH staging, releases the staged repository to Maven Central.

## Why this matters

Maven Central is the canonical Java distribution channel, but publishing requires multi-step staging (upload to OSSRH staging -> close staging repo -> release staging repo to Central) plus GPG-signed artifacts. Without an automated workflow, each release requires 15 minutes of manual Sonatype UI navigation — error-prone and easy to skip. OSSRH publishing has unique gotchas (Sonatype's release-or-drop flow, central sync delays) that need to be encapsulated.

## Implementation guidance

- WorkflowTemplate file: `k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/pdftract-java-publish.yaml` in `jedarden/declarative-config`
- Inputs: tag name; OSSRH creds (username + password) from ESO Secret `ossrh-creds-pdftract`; GPG private key + passphrase from ESO Secret `ossrh-gpg-key` (both synced from OpenBao)
- Steps:
  1. `clone-sdk-repo`: `git clone https://github.com/jedarden/pdftract-java.git --branch main`
  2. `sync-version`: update `pom.xml` version to match the binary tag
  3. `import-gpg-key`: `gpg --batch --import < gpg-private-key.asc` (the key is provided as a file)
  4. `conformance`: `mvn test -Dtest=ConformanceTest` (runs the shared suite; aborts on any failure)
  5. `build-and-sign`: `mvn -B clean deploy -P release -DskipTests` (the maven release profile invokes maven-gpg-plugin to sign artifacts)
  6. `close-and-release-staging`: use `nexus-staging-maven-plugin` to auto-close and auto-release the staging repository (or manually via Sonatype REST API)
- Container: `maven:3.9-eclipse-temurin-17`
- The Maven `release` profile in `pom.xml` configures:
  - maven-gpg-plugin (signs all artifacts)
  - maven-source-plugin (attaches sources jar)
  - maven-javadoc-plugin (attaches javadoc jar)
  - nexus-staging-maven-plugin (OSSRH upload + auto-release)
- Re-runnability: OSSRH rejects duplicate version uploads; a re-run on the same tag fails at the upload step; the workflow treats "version exists" as success and continues
- Pre-release publishes (`vX.Y.Z-rc.N`) go to a SNAPSHOT version: `X.Y.Z-rc.N-SNAPSHOT` on OSSRH; do NOT release-to-Central pre-releases

## Critical considerations

- ADR-009: runs on iad-ci; never use GitHub Actions
- OSSRH credentials: legacy Sonatype creds will sunset 2026 (Sonatype is migrating to publish.jetbrains.com or similar); the workflow MUST be portable to the successor system when announced
- GPG key MUST be exported with passphrase encoded in the ESO Secret; document the key generation runbook in `docs/operations/secrets-rotation.md`
- The OSSRH staging-and-release flow has a 10-minute "central sync" delay after release before the artifact appears on `search.maven.org`; expect a small window of "artifact published but not yet on Central"
- Maven Central is IMMUTABLE — a published version cannot be recalled; a bad publish requires a new patch release
- Javadoc and sources jars are REQUIRED by Maven Central policy; missing them fails the release-to-Central step
- The OSSRH project namespace `com.jedarden` requires DNS verification (TXT record on jedarden.com proving control) — one-time bootstrapping

## Acceptance criteria

- WorkflowTemplate file lands at the documented path in jedarden/declarative-config
- A test run against a fresh tag publishes `com.jedarden:pdftract:X.Y.Z` to Maven Central
- The conformance step aborts publish if any case fails
- The artifact appears on `search.maven.org` within 30 minutes of publish completion
- GPG signatures verify against the published public key
- Re-running the workflow on the same tag is idempotent (duplicate-publish treated as success)
- Pre-release tags publish as SNAPSHOTs (not released to Central)

## References

- Plan section: SDK Architecture / Per-SDK Release Channels, line 3572 (Maven Central via OSSRH)
- Plan section: SDK Acceptance Criteria, line 3584 (24-hour cascade)
- ADR-009 (Argo only)
- Sibling: Java SDK implementation bead
- Sonatype OSSRH guide: https://central.sonatype.org/publish/publish-guide/

issue.description:
## Scope

Discover all signature fields in a PDF by walking the AcroForm /Fields array recursively and filtering to fields whose /FT (field type) is /Sig. Produce a Vec<SigFieldRef> with the absolute (dot-joined) field name, the /V indirect reference (if present), and the field /Rect.

## Why this matters

Discovery is the precondition for metadata extraction (7.3.2) and coverage computation (7.3.3). Recursive /Kids walking is required because nested signature groups (employer-signed + employee-signed) are common in HR documents and contracts. Sharing this walker with 7.4 (form fields) avoids two parallel implementations of the same tree traversal.

## Implementation guidance

- Locate AcroForm via document catalog (/Catalog /AcroForm); absent -> no signatures (empty vec)
- /AcroForm /Fields is an array of indirect references to field dicts
- Walk recursively: each field dict may have /Kids (array of nested field dicts); descend in DFS
- Field type /FT inherits from parent if absent on a child (so a parent with /FT /Sig and a /Kids array of leaves with no /FT means all kids are sig fields)
- Construct full field name by joining /T (partial name) values with "." across the parent chain
- Capture: full_name: String, v_ref: Option<ObjRef>, rect: Option<[f32;4]>, page_index: Option<usize>
- page_index resolved by reverse lookup: find which page's /Annots array contains this field's widget annotation

## Critical considerations

- /Kids may be absent (leaf field) - emit the field directly
- /T may be absent on intermediate parent nodes (rare; emit "" segment, dot-join collapses empties)
- /FT inheritance: walk parent chain to find first /FT entry; only fields with /FT /Sig are signature fields
- page_index resolution: not every signature field has a widget on a page (form-only signatures exist); page_index: None in that case
- The walker is intended for reuse by 7.4 form-field walker - design as `walk_acroform_fields(catalog) -> Vec<FieldRef>` then filter

## Acceptance criteria

- Discovery returns all /FT /Sig fields, including nested ones
- Unit tests: flat 2 sigs, nested 1 sig under parent, no AcroForm, AcroForm with no Fields, kids inheriting /FT from parent
- Public sig::discover(&Document) -> Vec<SigFieldRef>
- Reusable walk_acroform_fields helper available for 7.4

- 7.4 AcroForm field walker (shared)
- PDF 1.7 spec 12.7.4.1 Field Dictionaries

## Scope

Author the `pdftract-github-release` WorkflowTemplate. Runs after `pdftract-build-binaries`, `pdftract-py-ci`, `pdftract-crates-publish`, and `pdftract-docker-build` complete. Collects all release artifacts, computes the aggregate `SHA256SUMS` file, signs it with cosign (producing `SHA256SUMS.sig`), attaches the SLSA L3 provenance file (`multiple.intoto.jsonl`) and the CycloneDX SBOM (`pdftract-vX.Y.Z.cdx.json`), generates release notes via `git-cliff` from Conventional Commits since the previous tag, and creates the GitHub Release with all artifacts attached.

## Why this matters

The GitHub Release is the canonical landing page for a milestone. Users click "Release vX.Y.Z" and expect: archives ready to download, checksums verifiable in one command, attestation/SBOM available for compliance review, and human-readable release notes. This template assembles all of that.

## Implementation guidance

- Inputs: tag name; artifacts from upstream templates (10 archives, 5 wheels + 1 sdist, SLSA file, SBOM file); GitHub PAT from ESO Secret `github-pat-pdftract`
- Steps:
  1. `collect-artifacts`: download all artifacts from upstream Argo runs (use the artifact pointer pattern: workflow outputs link to artifact storage)
  2. `compute-sha256sums`: `sha256sum pdftract-vX.Y.Z-*.{tar.gz,zip} pdftract-X.Y.Z*.whl pdftract-X.Y.Z.tar.gz pdftract-vX.Y.Z.cdx.json > SHA256SUMS`
  3. `sign-sums`: `cosign sign-blob --yes --output-signature SHA256SUMS.sig SHA256SUMS` (keyless, OIDC from iad-ci)
  4. `git-cliff-notes`: container `orhunp/git-cliff:latest`, command `git cliff --tag vX.Y.Z --latest > RELEASE_NOTES.md` (Conventional Commits parsed since the previous tag)
  5. `gh-release-create`: `gh release create vX.Y.Z --clobber --notes-file RELEASE_NOTES.md <all artifact paths>`
- The `--clobber` flag enables re-runnable releases (overwrites if exists)
- Pre-release tags (`vX.Y.Z-rc.N`) MUST be created with `gh release create --prerelease`
- Artifact list attached to the release:
  - 10 binary archives (5 triples × 2 feature variants)
  - 5 Python wheels + 1 sdist
  - `SHA256SUMS`
  - `SHA256SUMS.sig`
  - `multiple.intoto.jsonl` (SLSA L3 provenance)
  - `pdftract-vX.Y.Z.cdx.json` (CycloneDX SBOM)
- The release notes include: feature list (parsed from Conventional Commit `feat:` entries since previous tag), bug fixes (`fix:` entries), breaking changes (any entry with `!` or BREAKING CHANGE footer), and a "Verifying this release" section with the one-line cosign verify-blob command

## Critical considerations

- ADR-009: Argo-only; the GH PAT is the auth mechanism (no GH Actions runners involved)
- The PAT requires `contents: write` scope on the pdftract repo to create releases and upload assets
- `git-cliff` config lives at `cliff.toml` in repo root; it parses Conventional Commits and groups by `feat/fix/perf/docs/chore/breaking`
- The aggregate SHA256SUMS file is the SINGLE source of artifact verification — users run `cosign verify-blob --signature SHA256SUMS.sig SHA256SUMS` once to validate every artifact in one shot
- The template depends on ALL upstream templates completing; a `dependsOn` clause in the cascade workflow enforces this
- Failure mode: if `gh release create` partially uploads (e.g. one asset times out), `--clobber` on retry rebuilds the release from scratch
- The CHANGELOG.md in repo root is updated by a separate pre-tag step (or `git-cliff --output CHANGELOG.md` run as a release-prep PR) — this template only emits release notes for THIS tag, not the cumulative changelog

## Acceptance criteria

- WorkflowTemplate file lands at `k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/pdftract-github-release.yaml` in `jedarden/declarative-config`
- A test run against a fresh tag creates a GitHub Release with all artifacts (10 + 6 + 4 metadata = 20 attachments)
- `cosign verify-blob --signature SHA256SUMS.sig SHA256SUMS` succeeds on a downloaded copy
- The release notes contain a "Verifying this release" section with the canonical verify command
- A re-run against the same tag is idempotent (clobbers cleanly)
- Pre-release tags (`vX.Y.Z-rc.N`) are correctly marked as pre-release

## References

- Plan section: Release Engineering / Argo WorkflowTemplates, line 3393
- Plan section: Artifact Taxonomy, lines 3349-3358 (full artifact set)
- Plan section: Signing and Provenance, lines 3397-3403
- ADR-009 (Argo only)
- git-cliff docs: https://git-cliff.org/

## Scope

Author the `pdftract-docs-build` WorkflowTemplate. Triggered by milestone tag, after `pdftract-crates-publish` completes (so docs.rs links resolve). Builds the user documentation mdBook from `docs/book/` and deploys the rendered HTML to Cloudflare Pages at `pdftract.com`. Pattern matches the existing `website-build` template.

## Why this matters

`pdftract.com` is the public-facing documentation home. It hosts the install guide, the CLI reference, the SDK quickstarts, the JSON schema documentation, and demo links. Auto-deploying on every milestone tag keeps the public docs synchronised with the released binary version.

## Implementation guidance

- Build container: `rust:1.78-slim` (for `mdbook` install) or pre-built `peaceiris/mdbook:latest`
- Install: `cargo install mdbook mdbook-mermaid mdbook-linkcheck --locked` (cached in cargo-cache PVC)
- Build command: `mdbook build docs/book --dest-dir target/book`
- Pre-build link-check step: `mdbook-linkcheck` (fail on broken internal links; warn on external)
- Deploy: `wrangler pages deploy target/book --project-name pdftract --branch main` using token from ESO Secret `cloudflare-pages-token` (synced from OpenBao key `cloudflare-pages-token`)
- mdBook config (`docs/book/book.toml`):
  - Title: "pdftract"
  - Authors: ["Jed Cabanero"]
  - `[output.html.fold]` for collapsible sidebar
  - `[output.html.search]` enabled with `limit-results = 30`
  - `[preprocessor.mermaid]` for embedded diagrams
  - `[output.linkcheck] follow-web-links = true cache-timeout = 86400` (a daily web-link sanity check, non-blocking)
- The mdBook source layout:
  - `docs/book/src/SUMMARY.md` - table of contents
  - `docs/book/src/install.md`, `cli-reference.md`, `sdk/python.md`, ..., `schema.md`, `troubleshooting.md`
  - `docs/book/src/architecture/` - rendered from `docs/notes/` symlinks (post-build copy or build-time include)

## Critical considerations

- ADR-009: this runs on iad-ci; the existing `website-build` template (for jedarden.com) is the proven sibling pattern — copy that structure
- The Cloudflare API token rotation interval is 90 days; OpenBao key `cloudflare-pages-token` is rotated per the `docs/operations/secrets-rotation.md` runbook
- `pdftract.com` DNS must be configured to Cloudflare Pages (not GitHub Pages); the DNS bootstrapping is a one-time setup tracked separately
- The template runs AFTER `pdftract-crates-publish` because the docs link to docs.rs/pdftract-core/X.Y.Z and docs.rs only generates docs after the crate is published
- Re-runnable: re-deploying the same tag overwrites the Cloudflare Pages deployment cleanly
- Linkcheck failures on internal links block the deploy; external link failures emit warnings but allow the deploy (network flakiness should not block a release)

- Re-running against the same tag is idempotent

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement zstd compression for cache entries: encode the DocumentJson into a zstd-compressed byte stream before writing, decode on read. Use the zstd crate (already chosen per plan section 6.9 line 2465). Default compression level is 3 (a good speed/ratio trade-off for JSON); configurable via env var for benchmarking but not via CLI.

Module: crates/pdftract-core/src/cache/compression.rs.

## Why this matters

DocumentJson for a typical 100-page PDF is 500 KB - 5 MB uncompressed; zstd typically achieves 5-10x compression on JSON (lots of repeated keys, structural similarity). Without compression, a 1 GiB LRU cache holds ~200-2000 documents; with zstd, the same cache holds 1000-20000 documents — an order-of-magnitude improvement in cache hit rate.

zstd's decompression speed (~1 GB/s on a single core) means the < 20 ms p99 cache-hit target is comfortable even for 5 MB compressed entries. Compression speed is slower (~500 MB/s at level 3) but happens off the hot path — compression cost is amortized over many subsequent hits.

## Implementation guidance

- Use the zstd crate: zstd = \"0.13\"
- Encoder:
  ```rust
  pub fn encode(data: &[u8]) -> std::io::Result<Vec<u8>> {
      let level = 3; // tuned default per benchmarks
      zstd::encode_all(data, level)
  }
  ```
- Decoder:
  ```rust
  pub fn decode(data: &[u8]) -> std::io::Result<Vec<u8>> {
      zstd::decode_all(data)
  }
  ```
- Streaming variants for very large entries (encode_from_reader, decode_into_writer) to avoid buffering full uncompressed JSON in memory; use the std::io::Read/Write traits
- Frame size check: reject decoded output > 256 MB (the same limit as Phase 6.4 HTTP upload max); this is the bomb-protection invariant — a 1 KB zstd file that decompresses to 10 GB must not crash pdftract
- Compression level constant: CACHE_ZSTD_LEVEL = 3; expose as env var PDFTRACT_CACHE_ZSTD_LEVEL for benchmarking; not surfaced as CLI
- No dictionary training in v1 (could be a future optimization to share a dictionary across all entries; cache schema version 2 territory)
- Magic-byte check on decode: zstd frames start with 0x28 0xB5 0x2F 0xFD; reject inputs that don't match (degraded-disk corruption protection)
- Atomic temp+rename writes (sibling 6.9.5) — compression happens during the write to the temp file; rename is atomic, ensuring readers only see complete frames

## Critical considerations

- zstd decode of a truncated frame produces an error; treat as cache miss and delete the corrupt entry (sibling 6.9.5 multi-process safety covers this)
- Decompression bomb: limit decoded size to 256 MB; abort decode beyond limit. This prevents a malicious or corrupted cache entry from OOM-ing the process
- Compression level 3 is the calibrated default; higher (e.g. 9) gives ~10% better ratio at 3x slower compress. Lower (1) is ~30% worse ratio. 3 is the sweet spot for JSON
- Streaming decode is REQUIRED for the 256 MB output limit to be enforced incrementally; loading 256 MB into a Vec before length-checking defeats the purpose
- zstd's CRC checksum (per-frame) is automatically validated on decode; on checksum failure, return Err and let the caller treat as a cache miss
- Memory: zstd decoder allocates ~128 KB of decode buffer per stream; trivial overhead
- No interaction with the rayon thread pool here; cache reads happen on the request thread (synchronous; fast)
- Test corpus: include a real 5 MB DocumentJson fixture for round-trip and benchmark; the JSON should be representative of a real 100-page extraction

## Acceptance criteria

- Round-trip: encode(decode(bytes)) == bytes for a 5 MB DocumentJson fixture
- Compression ratio: a 5 MB representative DocumentJson compresses to <= 1.5 MB (≥ 3.3x ratio)
- Decode of a truncated 100-byte prefix of a real frame → Err
- Decode of a frame that decompresses to > 256 MB → Err with clear bomb-detection message
- Decode of an empty input → Err (no spurious empty-Vec success)
- Decode of bytes not starting with zstd magic bytes → Err
- Benchmark: encode 1 MB DocumentJson at level 3 in < 5 ms on a typical x86-64 (Apple M-class faster)
- Benchmark: decode 1 MB zstd entry in < 2 ms on a typical x86-64

## References

- Plan section: Phase 6.9 Content-Addressed Cache Layer (lines 2465-2467)
- zstd crate: https://crates.io/crates/zstd
- Decompression-bomb protection (TH-01 analogue from Phase 1 lexer threat tests)
- Sibling 6.9.5 (atomic writes interact with compression at temp-file boundary)
- INV-11 (binary size — zstd adds ~50 KB per plan)
Labels: cache, compression, phase-6, zstd

issue.description:
## Scope

Configure maturin to build Python wheels for 5 target triples: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, x86_64-apple-darwin, aarch64-apple-darwin, x86_64-pc-windows-gnu. Set up the build matrix and toolchain prerequisites; produce wheel files conforming to PEP 491 naming.

Module touches: pdftract-py/pyproject.toml + pdftract-py/Cargo.toml + cross-compilation toolchain docs in docs/operations/.

## Why this matters

A binary Python wheel is the only viable distribution method for a Rust extension. Source distribution requires users to have a Rust toolchain (untenable for data scientists). Cross-compilation from a single Linux runner is the only sane way to produce all 5 wheels in one CI run.

## Implementation guidance

- Build tool: maturin (PEP 517 compliant)
- pyproject.toml [build-system] uses maturin
- [tool.maturin] section configures features, bindings (pyo3), and any per-platform conditional compilation
- Linux x86_64 / aarch64: ghcr.io/rust-cross/manylinux base images (manylinux_2_28 = RHEL 8 compatible glibc)
- macOS x86_64 / aarch64: osxcross toolchain via the cross crate (provides Linux→macOS cross-compilation)
- Windows x86_64: cross with x86_64-pc-windows-gnu target
- Each build invocation: maturin build --release --target <triple> --out wheels/
- Wheel filenames follow PEP 491: pdftract-1.0.0-cp310-cp310-manylinux_2_28_x86_64.whl
- Python version compatibility: cp310 ABI3 (supports CPython 3.10+) — single ABI3 wheel per platform vs. per-cp version

## Critical considerations

- ABI3 vs per-cp: ABI3 wheels (cp310-abi3) work for all CPython 3.10+; reduces wheel count from N versions × 5 platforms to 5 platforms
- manylinux_2_28 is the modern baseline; older manylinux2014 (= RHEL 7) is no longer recommended (RHEL 7 EOL)
- macOS cross-compilation requires Xcode SDK files (must be downloaded separately due to Apple license); osxcross handles the staging
- Windows cross uses MinGW (gnu target) for compatibility; the msvc target requires actual Windows + Visual Studio
- aarch64 macOS targets require explicit toolchain setup; document the cross setup in docs/operations/build-wheels.md
- Reproducibility: cross-compilation produces deterministic wheels (same input → same SHA-256); verify via SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH env var

## Acceptance criteria

- maturin build --release --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu produces a valid manylinux wheel
- Same for aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu (Linux ARM64)
- Same for x86_64-apple-darwin (macOS Intel)
- Same for aarch64-apple-darwin (macOS Apple Silicon)
- Same for x86_64-pc-windows-gnu (Windows 64-bit)
- All 5 wheels follow PEP 491 naming
- All 5 wheels are ABI3 (cp310-abi3)
- Reproducibility: same source + SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH → byte-identical wheels across builds

## References

- Plan section: Phase 6.3.4
- maturin docs: https://www.maturin.rs/
- PEP 491 (Wheel binary package format)
- PEP 600 (manylinux platform tag)
- Coordinator: pdftract-z86x6 (parent — wheel build + Argo + PyPI upload bundle)
Labels: maturin, phase-6, pyo3, wheels

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the `test-matrix` DAG branch in `pdftract-ci`. Two parallel test legs:

1. **musl leg** — `cargo test --features default,serve,decrypt` on `x86_64-unknown-linux-musl` (no OCR). Same cross toolchain as build-matrix leg.
2. **glibc leg** — `cargo test --all-features` on `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` using a standard Debian-based Docker image (e.g. `rust:1.78-slim-bookworm`) with `apt-get install -y tesseract-ocr libleptonica-dev libtesseract-dev` baked in or installed at step startup.

Both legs emit JUnit XML to the workflow's artifact store (named `test-results-musl.xml` and `test-results-glibc.xml`) using `cargo nextest` or `cargo-junit-test`.

## Why this matters

The musl leg validates that the production binary feature set (what ships in the GitHub Release tarball) compiles and tests pass against the static-libc target. The glibc leg gives full coverage of the OCR integration path (tesseract requires `libleptonica` / `libtesseract` system libraries that don't exist on Alpine/musl). Without both, OCR regressions would slip through.

## Implementation guidance

- musl image: same `rustembedded/cross:x86_64-unknown-linux-musl` as Phase 0.2 build-matrix leg
- glibc image: build a custom `pdftract-test-glibc:1.78` (Dockerfile in declarative-config under `k8s/iad-ci/docker/pdftract-test-glibc/`) extending `rust:1.78-slim-bookworm` with `apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends tesseract-ocr=5.* libleptonica-dev libtesseract-dev pkg-config build-essential ca-certificates curl` then `cargo install cargo-nextest --locked` and `cargo install cargo-junit-test --locked`
- Test command (musl): `cross test --release --target x86_64-unknown-linux-musl --features default,serve,decrypt -- --test-threads=4`
- Test command (glibc): `cargo nextest run --all-features --profile ci --no-fail-fast`
- nextest profile `ci` (in `.config/nextest.toml`): JUnit XML output, slow-test timeout 60 s, retry once on failure for known-flaky tests (none currently — list maintained inline)
- Cache test artifact reuse: reuse `cargo-cache` PVC; per-target subfolder
- Add `RUST_BACKTRACE=full` to env vars on both legs so panic backtraces appear in logs

## Critical considerations

- Tesseract package version on Debian Bookworm is 5.x; tests must be tolerant of Tesseract 5 output (newer LSTM model defaults) — fixture confidence values may differ from Tesseract 4.x baselines documented in Phase 5 plan

## Scope

Define the `Span` struct exactly per plan with all 10 fields: text (String), bbox ([f32; 4]), font (Arc<str>), size (f32), color (Option<CssHexColor>), rendering_mode (u8), confidence (f32), confidence_source (ConfidenceSource enum), lang (Option<Arc<str>>), flags (u8 bitmask). Define `CssHexColor` as `String` newtype or `[u8; 7]` for #rrggbb. Define `SpanFlags` as a u8 bitmask with named bit constants.

## Why this matters

Span is the second-most-important struct in the output schema (after Glyph). Every JSON output emits Span; every Markdown output reads Span flags for style tags; every Phase 4 child operates on Vec<Span>. Locking the shape now (with full plan fidelity) prevents downstream churn.

## Implementation guidance

- Struct:
  ```rust
  pub struct Span {
      pub text: String,
      pub bbox: [f32; 4],          // union of member glyph bboxes
      pub font: Arc<str>,
      pub size: f32,
      pub color: Option<CssHexColor>,
      pub rendering_mode: u8,
      pub confidence: f32,         // min glyph confidence
      pub confidence_source: ConfidenceSource,
      pub lang: Option<Arc<str>>,  // populated in Phase 7
      pub flags: u8,               // SpanFlags bitmask
  }
  ```
- `pub struct CssHexColor(pub String)` — newtype to enforce #rrggbb format at construction; constructor validates.
- `pub struct SpanFlags;` with associated `pub const BOLD: u8 = 1 << 0; pub const ITALIC: u8 = 1 << 1; pub const SMALLCAPS: u8 = 1 << 2; pub const SUBSCRIPT: u8 = 1 << 3; pub const SUPERSCRIPT: u8 = 1 << 4;` (bits 5-7 reserved).
- Serde derives for JSON serialization.

## Critical considerations

- INV: text is VALID UTF-8 (Rust String); no U+FFFD unless the underlying glyph was U+FFFD AND the readability correction did not repair it.
- INV: bbox is [x0, y0, x1, y1] PDF user space, lower-left origin, AFTER /Rotate normalization.
- color may be None when the source colorspace was Spot or Other; JSON serializes as null.
- lang is None until Phase 7 fills it from /Lang or detected script.
- flags is initially 0; Phase 4.1 flag detector sets bits.
- Struct size budget: ~80 bytes per Span (Arc str = 16 bytes shared, String avg 32, bbox 16, scalars 16). Acceptable for a Vec<Span> ~1000 entries per page.

## Acceptance criteria

- Span constructible with all fields.
- Span Clone is cheap (Arc<str> shared, only String text + Color + Lang allocate).
- Serde JSON serialization round-trips.
- SpanFlags constants distinct and combinable (BOLD | ITALIC == 3).
- CssHexColor::new("#ff0000") -> Ok; CssHexColor::new("red") -> Err.

## References

- Plan section: Phase 4.1 Span struct (lines 1622-1635), ConfidenceSource mapping (lines 1638-1646)

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the OutOfOrderBuffer<Page>: a thread-safe page-ordering buffer that accepts pages completed out of order by rayon and emits them in page_index order. Backed by a BinaryHeap protected by Mutex + Condvar. Window size of 8 entries; when full and the next-expected page hasn't arrived, the producer blocks on the Condvar.

## Why this matters

This is the integration point between rayon's out-of-order parallelism and NDJSON's strict-order output contract. Without this buffer, every page would have to complete in order — defeating Phase 4 parallelism. With it, throughput stays nearly identical to non-streaming mode.

## Implementation guidance

- Module: pdftract-core/src/output/ndjson/buffer.rs
- struct OutOfOrderBuffer { inner: Mutex<Inner>, not_full: Condvar, not_empty: Condvar }
- Inner { heap: BinaryHeap<Reverse<(u32, Page)>>, next_expected: u32, total_pages: u32 }
- push(page): lock; if heap.len() >= 8 -> wait on not_full; heap.push((page.page_index, page)); notify_one(not_empty)
- pop_next_in_order() -> Option<Page>: lock; while heap.is_empty() OR heap.peek().0 != next_expected: wait on not_empty (or return None if all pages received and heap empty); pop; next_expected += 1; notify_one(not_full)
- finish() called by producer after all pages submitted; flips a flag so pop_next_in_order returns None when heap empty + flag set
- Producer threads (rayon workers) call push; output thread calls pop_next_in_order in a loop

## Critical considerations

- Window size 8 is constant NDJSON_OUT_OF_ORDER_WINDOW_PAGES; chosen larger than typical rayon pool (4-8 threads) so output thread is never the bottleneck on balanced workloads
- Pathological case: one very slow page + 7 fast pages around it -> buffer fills, fast pages pile up, eventually backpressure (push blocks) until slow page completes
- Use of BinaryHeap with Reverse pulls smallest page_index first (min-heap)
- Condvar wakeup must always recheck condition (spurious wakeup safety)
- The buffer is single-output-thread; serializing emission to stdout is the consumer's job (in 6.2.3)

## Acceptance criteria

- Unit test: push pages 3, 1, 4, 1, 5, 9, 2, 6 -> pop_next_in_order in 1..=9 order
- Backpressure test: fill buffer with 8 pages all > 0 starting from page 1 -> 9th push blocks until pop_next_in_order pulls page 1
- Concurrency stress test: 8 rayon workers + 1 output thread; 1000 pages -> all 1000 emitted in order
- finish() test: producer finished, heap drained -> pop_next_in_order returns None

## References

- Plan section: Phase 6.2 out-of-order buffer (line 2041)
- INV-13 reproducibility (out-of-order rayon but ordered output)
issue.title: 6.2.2: OutOfOrderBuffer (8-page heap with Condvar backpressure for rayon-to-stream ordering)

issue.description:
## Scope

Extract URI hyperlinks and page annotation objects. Per page, walk /Annots. Collect Link annotations (/Subtype /Link): /A /S /URI -> external URL; /Dest -> internal destination. Both URI and internal links populate the document-level /links array with page_index + rect + (uri | dest). Collect other annotation subtypes (Highlight, Stamp, FreeText, Note, Squiggly, StrikeOut, Underline): record /Subtype, /Rect, /Contents (comment), /T (author), /M (modification date), /C (color). These populate the page-level /annotations array.

## Why this matters

Hyperlinks are the most-asked-for feature for academic-paper extraction (citation DOI/URL extraction). Annotations carry reviewer comments, redlines, and stamps essential for legal/regulatory document workflows. Highlight annotations are how 7.8 grep --highlight emits its results. Splitting links (document-level) from annotations (page-level) follows reader-tool conventions and minimises payload duplication for documents with many cross-page links.

## Implementation guidance

- Crates: none beyond Phase 1 parser
- For each page, iterate /Annots array (Optional, default empty)
- For each annotation, read /Subtype as Name
- Branch on subtype:
  - Link -> extract action /A (if /S /URI -> URL String) or /Dest (Name or Array - internal destination); append to document.links
  - Highlight, Stamp, FreeText, Note (== Text), Squiggly, StrikeOut, Underline, Caret, Ink, Polygon, PolyLine, Line, Circle, Square, FileAttachment, Sound, Movie, Screen, Widget, PrinterMark, TrapNet, Watermark, 3D, Redact -> extract common annotation fields; append to page.annotations
  - Widget -> skip (handled by 7.4 form fields)
  - Popup -> skip (companion annotation to others)
- Common fields per annotation: /Subtype, /Rect ([x0,y0,x1,y1]), /Contents (PdfString -> String), /T (author, PdfString), /M (date, PdfString -> ISO 8601), /C (color array [r,g,b] or [c,m,y,k] or [gray]), /CA (opacity)
- For non-link annotations, also extract /F (annotation flags), /NM (name/id), /Subj (subject)
- For Highlight annotations specifically, also extract /QuadPoints (array of 8*N floats defining N quadrilaterals) - useful for grep cross-checking

## Critical considerations

- /Dest may be a Name (named destination - resolve via /Catalog /Names /Dests name tree) or an Array (explicit destination [page_ref, /XYZ, x, y, zoom])
- Named destination resolution: walk /Catalog /Dests dict OR /Catalog /Names /Dests name tree; output as the original Name string when resolution unavailable
- URI may be Latin-1 in /URI (legacy) or UTF-8; decode permissively
- /M date format reuses 7.3.2 PDF-date-to-ISO-8601 parser
- /C color: 1 element = grayscale, 3 = RGB, 4 = CMYK; always emit as [f32; 3..4] array
- /Contents may contain newlines (multi-line review comments) - preserve them in the String
- Annotations on encrypted forms: still iterable as long as page-level encryption is recoverable
- INV: stable taxonomy of annotation subtypes - new types append, no rename
- The Widget subtype is intentionally routed away from 7.6 to 7.4 (avoids dup with form widgets)

## Acceptance criteria

- All Phase 7.6 child task beads closed
- Critical test (from plan): PDF with 5 URI hyperlinks - all 5 in document-level links with correct URLs
- Critical test: Link with named destination /Dest /SectionTwo - emitted as internal link with dest: "SectionTwo"
- Critical test: page with Highlight and Note - both in page-level annotations with correct subtypes
- Critical test: annotation with no /Contents - contents: null (not empty string)
- Output: document-level /links: Vec<Link>; page-level /annotations: Vec<Annotation>
- Schema includes both shapes; round-trip tests pass

- Plan section: 7.6 Hyperlinks and Annotations (lines 2653-2675)
- PDF 1.7 spec 12.5 Annotations
- docs/schema/v1.0/pdftract.schema.json
- 7.3.2 date parser (reused)

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the `com.jedarden:pdftract` Maven artifact as a subprocess-based SDK. Spawn the bundled `pdftract` binary via `ProcessBuilder`, parse JSON output via Jackson, expose the 9 contract methods on an `AutoCloseable Pdftract` client. Bundle Kotlin extension functions in the same artifact so Kotlin users get idiomatic syntactic sugar. Repo at `github.com/jedarden/pdftract-java`.

## Why this matters

Java + Kotlin together cover Android (Kotlin-first), Spring Boot (Java-first), and Confluent/Kafka stream-processing (Java-first) — the three largest JVM ecosystems. The AutoCloseable client matches the JDK Optional<T>/Stream<T> ergonomics; Kotlin extensions on top means a single artifact serves both communities without dependency on Kotlin runtime for Java consumers.

## Implementation guidance

- Maven coordinates: `com.jedarden:pdftract:X.Y.Z`
- Repo: `github.com/jedarden/pdftract-java` (separate repo)
- File layout (generator-driven; see Tera template scaffolding bead):
  - `pom.xml` (Maven build; java 17 minimum; Jackson 2.x dep)
  - `src/main/java/.../Pdftract.java` (the main client class; AutoCloseable)
  - `src/main/java/.../codegen/Methods.java` (generated)
  - `src/main/java/.../codegen/Errors.java` (generated; 8 exception classes)
  - `src/main/java/.../Document.java`, `Page.java`, etc. (type-bearing records)
  - `src/main/kotlin/.../PdftractKt.kt` (Kotlin extension functions)
  - `src/test/java/.../ConformanceTest.java` (JUnit 5)
- Method signatures (Java):
  - `class Pdftract implements AutoCloseable { ... }`
  - `Document extract(Source source, ExtractOptions options) throws PdftractException`
  - `String extractText(...) throws PdftractException`
  - `String extractMarkdown(...) throws PdftractException`
  - `Stream<Page> extractStream(...) throws PdftractException`
  - `Stream<Match> search(Source source, String pattern, SearchOptions options) throws PdftractException`
  - `Metadata getMetadata(...) throws PdftractException`
  - `Fingerprint hash(...) throws PdftractException`
  - `Classification classify(Source source) throws PdftractException`
  - `boolean verifyReceipt(Path path, Receipt receipt) throws PdftractException`
  - Plus `CompletableFuture<T> ...Async(...)` variants as OPTIONAL futures
- Option names use camelCase per the contract (Java convention): CLI `--ocr-language` becomes `ocrLanguage`
- Source type: sealed interface `Source` with `Source.fromPath(Path)`, `Source.fromUrl(URI)`, `Source.fromBytes(byte[])`
- Errors: `class PdftractException extends Exception` is the base; 8 subclasses (`CorruptPdfException`, etc.) mirror the contract
- The AutoCloseable pattern releases any background process pool the client might maintain (a future optimisation uses `pdftract serve` over a Unix socket; for v1.0 each call spawns a fresh subprocess)
- Kotlin extensions:
  ```kotlin
  fun Pdftract.extract(source: Path, init: ExtractOptions.() -> Unit = {}): Document = ...
  inline operator fun Pdftract.invoke(block: Pdftract.() -> Unit) = use { it.block() }
  ```

## Critical considerations

- Java 17 is the floor (most enterprise users have migrated from 11); document this in the README
- Jackson is the JSON parser; ObjectMapper is configured to fail on unknown fields (`FAIL_ON_UNKNOWN_PROPERTIES`) so a new binary field surprises in dev rather than silently ignoring
- AutoCloseable contract: the client SHOULD be created in a try-with-resources block; documented in every README example
- The Kotlin extensions live in the SAME jar (under `src/main/kotlin/`) so Kotlin users do not need a separate Kotlin-specific artifact; this requires the kotlin-stdlib as an OPTIONAL dependency declared in pom.xml
- The Stream<Page> for streaming: the underlying NDJSON output is consumed line-by-line on a background daemon thread; the Stream is lazy and the subprocess is killed when the stream is closed
- Maven Central via OSSRH (Sonatype) staging requires GPG-signed artifacts; the GPG key is stored in OpenBao key `ossrh-gpg-key` (separate from `ossrh-creds-pdftract`)
- The CompletableFuture variants are OPTIONAL per the contract — sync-first is the primary surface

## Acceptance criteria

- The `com.jedarden:pdftract` artifact builds with `mvn package`
- All 9 contract methods exposed with the documented signatures
- All 8 exception classes inherit from PdftractException
- Document, Page, etc. exposed as Java records (or classes)
- Kotlin extensions in the same jar; a Kotlin user can write `pdftract.extract(path) { ocrLanguage = "eng" }`
- `mvn test` runs the conformance runner and 100% passes
- AutoCloseable cleanup verified (no leaked subprocesses)

## References

- Plan section: SDK Architecture / The Ten SDKs, line 3475 (Java subprocess via ProcessBuilder + Jackson; AutoCloseable Pdftract client; Kotlin extensions)
- Plan section: SDK Architecture / Per-SDK Release Channels, line 3572 (Maven Central via OSSRH)
- Plan section: SDK Acceptance Criteria, lines 3581-3589
- Sibling: pdftract-java-publish Argo workflow
- Sibling: SDK contract and conformance suite

## Scope

Implement OCR language-pack management: detection of installed traineddata files, the ExtractionOptions.ocr_language list -> required-packs mapping, missing-pack diagnostics, and the distribution decision documented for each Docker image variant. Resolves Open Question OQ-04 (OCR language pack distribution strategy).

## Why this matters

Without language packs, Tesseract degrades to script-only recognition (poor accuracy). Different languages need different traineddata files; English alone is ~12 MB, full coverage of 100+ languages is ~600 MB. The distribution strategy directly affects Docker image size, cold-start latency, and air-gapped deployment story.

## Implementation guidance

- Pack-detection helper: detect_available_languages(tessdata_path) -> HashSet<String>
- Language-list-to-packs mapping: each language code maps to "<code>.traineddata" plus optional "<code>_fast.traineddata" or "<code>_best.traineddata" variants
- ExtractionOptions.ocr_language default: vec!["eng"]
- Per-page: if requested language not present, emit OCR_LANGUAGE_UNAVAILABLE diagnostic with the missing language code; fall back to eng if available
- Distribution decision (resolve OQ-04 with the team):
  - pdftract:ocr image bundles eng + a curated set of common langs (deu, fra, spa, ita, por, jpn, chi_sim, chi_tra, kor, rus, ara, hin) totaling ~150 MB
  - pdftract:full image bundles all languages
  - Document chosen set in docs/notes/ocr-language-packs.md (allowlisted)
- Provide a doctor check (6.10) verifying eng + any user-specified --lang are present

## Critical considerations

- OQ-04: this bead owns the resolution. Capture decision in docs/notes/ocr-language-packs.md
- Bundling adds to Docker image size; choices have weight-budget impact
- Missing-pack must NEVER cause a hard crash — degrade with diagnostic + fall back to eng
- Pack paths are tessdata-prefix-relative; honor $TESSDATA_PREFIX env var
- Some Tesseract distributions ship multi-language packs (e.g. "script/Latin.traineddata") — document but do NOT support in v1.0

## Acceptance criteria

- detect_available_languages returns the correct set for the pdftract:ocr Docker image
- Missing language: extraction proceeds with eng fallback + OCR_LANGUAGE_UNAVAILABLE diagnostic
- doctor check verifies presence of eng + any --lang values
- docs/notes/ocr-language-packs.md exists and documents the bundle decision
- OQ-04 closed in plan with reference to this bead's resolution

## References

- Plan section: Phase 5.4 language packs (line 1892) + OQ-04
- docs/notes/ocr-language-packs.md (deliverable)
- Phase 6.10 doctor language check

issue.close_reason: Implemented ' (apostrophe) and " (double-quote) text-show operators. Commit: 59a91f8. Verification note: notes/pdftract-332k1.md. All acceptance criteria PASS: ' operator uses leading, " operator sets word_spacing/char_spacing, both emit TEXT_SHOW_OUTSIDE_BT diagnostic when called outside BT/ET, " handles insufficient operands gracefully. 5 new tests added and passing.
issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the two compound text-show operators: `' string` = move to next line then show string (equivalent to `T*` then `Tj`); `" aw ac string` = set word_spacing = aw, char_spacing = ac, then ' (move to next line, then show). Both reduce to Tj after their state mutations and use the same emission path.

## Why this matters

These exist for compactness in legacy/handcrafted PDFs; they show up in PDFs older than InDesign era. Without them, content streams crash or skip text. They are conceptually simple (delegate to T* + Tj) but the operand parsing differs.

## Implementation guidance

- `' string`: pop 1 string. Internally: invoke T* operator (move to next line per current leading); then invoke Tj with the string.
- `" aw ac string`: pop 1 string + 2 numbers. Internally: set state.word_spacing = aw, state.char_spacing = ac; then invoke ' (T* then Tj).
- Both operators implicitly require BT context (since T* requires it); emit TEXT_SHOW_OUTSIDE_BT if not in text object.
- INV: " mutates word_spacing/char_spacing PERMANENTLY (until next Tw/Tc); it's not a per-operation override.
- Operand types: aw and ac are numeric (Real or Integer); string is a PDF string. Validate types; emit diagnostics on mismatch.

## Critical considerations

- Leading must be set BEFORE ' or " (typically via TD or TL) — if leading == 0, T* is a vertical no-op; ' still shows the string but at the same line. Emit TSTAR_ZERO_LEADING diagnostic from within '.
- " with zero leading is the same edge case.
- These operators are SHARED with the same word boundary, advance, and emission code as Tj — reuse the Tj implementation function; do not duplicate.

## Acceptance criteria

- `'(Hello)` after setting leading 12: produces 5 glyphs, text_matrix translated by (0, -12) before the H.
- `"5 1 (World)`: sets word_spacing 5, char_spacing 1, then T* + Tj producing 5 glyphs with the new spacings in effect.
- `'` outside BT/ET: TEXT_SHOW_OUTSIDE_BT diagnostic, no glyphs.
- `"` with non-numeric aw/ac: TJ_INVALID_ELEMENT diagnostic, falls back to Tj with original spacings.

## References

- Plan section: Phase 3.2 Text-showing operators table (lines 1514-1519)
issue.title: ' (apostrophe) and " (double-quote) text-show operators

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the PageClassifier engine that wires signal evaluators + Hybrid evaluator together, applies the short-circuit rule, resolves conflicting signals into a final PageClass and confidence, and exports a single entry point pdftract_ocr::classify_page(&PageContext) -> PageClassification used by the extraction pipeline.

## Why this matters

This is where ordered signals become a decision. The pipeline is intentionally simple but every choice (signal order, conflict resolution, default page class) is load-bearing for correctness. Concentrating the policy here keeps the classifier auditable.

## Implementation guidance

- Pipeline:
  1. Run Hybrid evaluator first; if it triggers, return immediately (Hybrid takes precedence over Scanned/Vector splits)
  2. Walk signal evaluators in declared order (5.1.2); accumulate votes
  3. Apply short-circuit: as soon as any signal has strength > 0.95, return that class with that strength as confidence
  4. After all signals run with no short-circuit: tally votes weighted by strength; pick the highest-weight class
  5. If no signal voted, default to Vector with confidence 0.5
- Confidence formula: when short-circuited, take the triggering signal's strength; when tallied, take weighted_winner_strength / sum_of_weights (so it stays in [0,1])
- Special case: no text + no images -> classify as Blank pseudo-class (not in PageClass; emitted as page_type=blank by the mapping in 5.1.1)
- Special case: only images, no text -> figure_only (mapped via has_text=false has_images=true)

## Critical considerations

- Hybrid MUST be evaluated first; otherwise a hybrid page with image_coverage > 0.85 short-circuits to Scanned and the hybrid_cells set never gets populated
- Default to Vector (not BrokenVector) when signals are silent — prefer fast path over OCR
- Confidence must be reproducible: deterministic iteration order over signal evaluators (Vec, not HashMap)
- The classifier is side-effect-free: it never logs or panics; failures propagate via Result if input is malformed

## Acceptance criteria

- All four critical-test fixtures classified correctly (Vector, Scanned, BrokenVector, Hybrid) with expected confidence ranges
- Edge cases: blank page -> Blank pseudo; image-only page -> Vector but page_type=figure_only via mapping
- Determinism: classifier output reproducible across runs (CI checks 50 PDFs twice for byte-identical JSON)
- Micro-benchmark: classify_page p99 < 5 ms on a 50-fixture suite

## References

- Plan section: Phase 5.1 critical tests (lines 1840-1844)
- INV-9 stable taxonomy

issue.description:
## Scope

Add two test legs that exercise pdftract via property-based and fuzzing inputs:

1. **Per-PR property tests** — `cargo nextest run --features proptest -- proptest`. proptest cases for lexer, object parser, xref resolver, stream decoder, CMap parser. Budget: 1 CPU-hour per parser module per PR (configured via PROPTEST_CASES env var; ~10,000 cases per module by default).
2. **Nightly fuzz job** — separate Argo CronWorkflow (NOT a step in `pdftract-ci`) running `cargo fuzz run` against five fuzz targets (`lexer`, `object_parser`, `xref`, `stream_decoder`, `cmap_parser`) for 24 CPU-hours each, seeded from `tests/fixtures/malformed/`. New crashes or hangs are filed as `STRUCT_*` diagnostic regressions and posted to the issue tracker via the `argo-workflows-issue-reporter` sidecar.

## Why this matters

PDF grammar is notoriously irregular and real-world PDFs frequently violate the spec. proptest exposes parser invariants that hand-written tests miss (e.g. INV-8 -- no panic at public boundary -- holds for ANY input, not just curated fixtures). Fuzzing covers the malformed-PDF tail; cargo-fuzz's libFuzzer driver is the most effective tool for exposing parser crashes.

## Implementation guidance

- Use `proptest` 1.x with a `proptest-regressions/` directory committed to git so any minimal counterexample replays on future PRs
- Property test suites live under `tests/proptest/<module>.rs` and are gated behind `cfg(feature = "proptest")` so they don't slow down `cargo test`
- Add a `Cargo.toml` feature `proptest = ["dep:proptest"]`
- For nightly fuzzing, use `cargo fuzz` (uses libFuzzer; requires nightly toolchain — use `rust-nightly:latest` Docker image)
- Fuzz targets live under `fuzz/fuzz_targets/<name>.rs`; seed corpus at `fuzz/corpus/<name>/`
- Run via CronWorkflow `pdftract-nightly-fuzz` scheduled at `0 4 * * *` UTC; 24-hour wall budget split across 5 targets (~4.8 hours each)
- Crash artifacts uploaded to the workflow's artifact store as `crashes-<target>.tar.gz`
- A crash file recovered from fuzzing must be added to `tests/fixtures/malformed/` (size <= 100 KB) and a corresponding bd-bead created with reproducer attached

## Critical considerations

- proptest's default seed is non-deterministic — set `PROPTEST_SEED=$(date +%s%N | sha256sum | head -c 16)` per PR and log it so failures can be replayed locally
- proptest discoveries must NOT block PR merge if they reveal a long-standing issue (use `ignore = true` on the failing property + create a follow-up bead); only NEW regressions (cases that worked on the previous commit) block merge
- Fuzz harnesses must be `cfg(fuzzing)` gated and not contribute to default-feature binary size (R2)
- libFuzzer requires sanitizers; `RUSTFLAGS="-Zsanitizer=address"` must be set in the fuzz job container only — sanitizer-instrumented code is NOT shipped
- Cycle detection in object parser (INV-8) is a frequent fuzz finding: seed the corpus with a "self-referencing object" minimal PDF (EC-08) to encourage early discovery
- Decompression bomb fuzz (EC-10): seed corpus with `STREAM_BOMB` minimal repro to ensure 2 GB limit holds under random predictor inputs

## Acceptance criteria

- `proptest` runs on every PR; >= 10,000 cases per parser module exhausted within 1 CPU-hour
- proptest-regressions/ is committed and replayed on every run
- Nightly fuzz CronWorkflow runs successfully for a full 24 hours without infrastructure failure
- New fuzz crashes auto-file a bead (via the issue-reporter sidecar) with the minimal repro attached
- A deliberate panic added to the lexer is caught by proptest within the budget

## References

- Plan section: Phase 0, line 1007 (proptest, cargo-fuzz)
- INV-8 (no panic at public boundary -- the property tests' core invariant)
- EC-08 (circular references), EC-10 (decompression bomb), EC-07 (corrupt xref)
- Sibling templates: needle uses cargo-fuzz in a CronWorkflow — copy the pattern
issue.title: Phase 0.5: Property tests and nightly fuzz job

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement detect_xfa(acroform: &Option<PdfDict>) -> bool. Checks for /AcroForm /XFA key presence; if present and non-null, sets contains_xfa flag.

## Why this matters

XFA (XML Forms Architecture) is an Adobe-specific PDF form spec that pdftract does NOT parse (the XML payload is structurally different from AcroForm). The flag tells downstream consumers \"this PDF has XFA content that is not extracted\"; without it, users see empty form fields and assume the PDF has no forms (it does — they're XFA-only).

## Implementation guidance

- Public API: detect_xfa(acroform: &Option<PdfDict>) -> bool
- Implementation:
  ```rust
  pub fn detect_xfa(acroform: &Option<PdfDict>) -> bool {
      acroform
          .as_ref()
          .and_then(|af| af.get(\"XFA\"))
          .map(|xfa| !matches!(xfa, PdfObject::Null))
          .unwrap_or(false)
      }
  }
  ```
- /XFA value may be either a stream or an array of name/stream pairs (\"packet form\"); both indicate XFA presence

## Critical considerations

- pdftract does NOT extract XFA form fields; that's a Phase 7.4 (AcroForm + XFA combiner) responsibility — this bead is detection only
- /XFA == /Null (explicit null) is treated as absence (false)
- The detector is a one-liner; sibling bead Phase 7.4 has the full XFA stream parser
- Document in code that XFA detection is non-parsing; the XML content is not validated

## Acceptance criteria

- PDF with AcroForm /XFA stream → true
- PDF with AcroForm /XFA [name, stream, name, stream, ...] (packet form) → true
- PDF with AcroForm but no /XFA key → false
- PDF with AcroForm /XFA null → false
- PDF with no AcroForm → false

## References

- Plan section: Phase 1 metadata detection
- PDF spec 12.7 (AcroForm + XFA)
- Coordinator: pdftract-25br8 (parent)
- Sibling: JS detection, conformance detection
- Phase 7.4 (XFA parser; consumes this flag's presence as a routing hint)
Labels: detection, phase-1, xfa
issue.title: XFA detection (AcroForm /XFA key presence)

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the per-region Hybrid evaluator that detects mixed-content pages by 8x8 grid decomposition. Reports Hybrid when both vector cells and scanned cells exceed 15% (>= 10 of 64 each); also returns the set of image-heavy cell indexes for downstream OCR-only-on-cells routing in 5.2.

## Why this matters

Most real-world scanned PDFs are not purely scanned: title pages, signature pages, and mixed business documents have a text header over a scanned form. Without per-region detection, the classifier picks one side and gets the other wrong. Hybrid output also feeds 5.2 image extraction: only the image-heavy cells need OCR; vector cells already have extracted text from Phase 3.

## Implementation guidance

- Grid dimensions: 8 rows x 8 cols = 64 cells, indexed (row, col) with row=0 at page top
- For each cell, compute: text_op_count_in_cell, image_coverage_fraction_in_cell, char_validity_rate_in_cell
- Cell -> CellClass mapping:
  - vector if text_op_count > 0 AND char_validity > 0.6
  - scanned if image_coverage > 0.80 AND text_op_count == 0
  - mixed otherwise (counts as neither)
- Hybrid trigger: vector_cell_count >= 10 AND scanned_cell_count >= 10
- Output: PageClassification { class: Hybrid, confidence: f32 derived from min(vector_cells, scanned_cells)/64, hybrid_cells: Some(BTreeSet of scanned cell indexes) }
- Reuse the per-page char-validity infrastructure from 4.7; just bucket counts by cell

## Critical considerations

- Page rotation MUST be applied before gridding (cell (0,0) is top-left in the rendered orientation, not the raw PDF MediaBox orientation)
- Empty cells (no text, no images) are classified as mixed, not scanned
- Hybrid detection is the only path that returns a non-None hybrid_cells set; other classes leave it None
- Determinism: BTreeSet (not HashSet) for hybrid_cells so serialized output is stable

## Acceptance criteria

- Critical test: hybrid page fixture with text header (top 2 rows) + scanned body (bottom 6 rows) -> Hybrid with hybrid_cells containing rows 2-7 only
- Unit test: page that is 9 vector cells + 9 scanned cells (just under threshold) -> NOT Hybrid (falls through to next signal)
- Determinism: classify twice -> hybrid_cells serializes byte-identically
- Cells correctly exposed for 5.2 OCR routing

## References

- Plan section: Phase 5.1 Hybrid detection (line 1838)
- Phase 5.2 Hybrid page handling (line 1863) consumes hybrid_cells
issue.title: 5.1.3: Hybrid grid-cell evaluator (8x8 decomposition + >=15% rule)

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement AcroForm /Tx (text field) value extraction. Read /V as a PdfString and decode to String. Surface multi-line flag from /Ff bit 12, max-length from /MaxLen. Output a FormFieldValue::Text variant.

Module: crates/pdftract-core/src/acroform/value_text.rs.

## Why this matters

Text fields are the most common AcroForm field type (name/address/notes fields). Without correct PdfString decoding (which honors PDFDocEncoding or UTF-16BE BOM prefix), text with non-ASCII characters (accented Latin, Cyrillic, CJK) extracts as garbage. The multi-line flag is essential for distinguishing single-line input vs textarea content.

## Implementation guidance

- Output variant:
  ```rust
  FormFieldValue::Text {
      value: Option<String>,
      default: Option<String>,
      multiline: bool,
      max_length: Option<u32>,
  }
  ```
- /V (current value): PdfString -> String via Phase 1 PdfString decoder
- /DV (default value): PdfString -> String (optional)
- /Ff bit 12 (1<<12 = 0x1000) → multiline flag
- /MaxLen: i32 → Option<u32> (None if absent or negative)
- PdfString decoding handles both PDFDocEncoding (legacy 8-bit) and UTF-16BE BOM-prefixed forms

## Critical considerations

- /V may be missing on unfilled fields → value: None
- Multi-line text may contain \\r or \\r\\n line endings; preserve them in the String (Python and JS consumers can normalize)
- Empty /V (PdfString of length 0) → value: Some(\"\")
- Field /FT may be /Tx with a /V that's a Name (rare, but seen with /Off-style placeholders); treat as Some(name) for safety
- PdfString decoder is in Phase 1; re-use without modification

## Acceptance criteria

- Text field with /V (My Name) → FormFieldValue::Text { value: Some(\"My Name\"), ... }
- Text field with UTF-16BE BOM-prefixed /V → correct Unicode decode
- Text field with /Ff multiline bit set → multiline: true
- Text field with /MaxLen 50 → max_length: Some(50)
- Empty /V → value: Some(\"\")
- Missing /V → value: None

## References

- Plan section: Phase 7.4.2 (Tx variant)
- PDF spec 12.7.4 (Text fields)
- Coordinator: pdftract-5t92 (parent — Tx/Btn/Ch bundle)
- Phase 1 PdfString decoder
Labels: acroform, phase-7

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the JPXDecode (JPEG 2000) passthrough filter. Validates the JP2 box magic at the start (12 bytes). Emits OCR_JPX_UNSUPPORTED diagnostic when full-render OR system libopenjp2 is unavailable (per EC-12). Pass-through.

Module: crates/pdftract-core/src/decoder/jpx.rs.

## Why this matters

JPEG 2000 appears in higher-quality scanned PDFs and some color-accurate workflows. pdftract-core does not decode it (requires libopenjp2 from the OS); the passthrough preserves bytes for downstream consumers and surfaces a clear diagnostic when the runtime environment can't decode it.

## Implementation guidance

- Validate first 12 bytes match JP2 box magic: 00 00 00 0C 6A 50 20 20 0D 0A 87 0A
- If magic doesn't match → STREAM_INVALID_JPX diagnostic; pass-through anyway
- Check feature gates: cfg!(feature = \"full-render\") AND runtime detection of libopenjp2 (via pkg-config or dynamic load)
- If neither available → emit OCR_JPX_UNSUPPORTED diagnostic (per EC-12)
- Pass-through raw bytes unchanged
- Module: crates/pdftract-core/src/decoder/jpx.rs

## Critical considerations

- The JP2 magic check is a quick validity sanity-check; do NOT decode the structure
- libopenjp2 runtime detection: same approach as Phase 6.10 doctor (pkg-config --exists libopenjp2 OR ldconfig -p | grep libopenjp2)
- Pass-through means the bytes go into Image XObject stream content; downstream consumer decodes
- Some JPEG 2000 PDFs use raw J2K codestream (no JP2 wrapper); magic check fails but data is still valid — emit warning + pass-through; consumer's decoder handles both wrappings

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the pdftract verify-receipt FILE.pdf RECEIPT.json subcommand and the underlying verifier protocol. Given a Receipt and the original PDF, the verifier reproduces the extraction at the receipt's page_index and checks: (1) PDF fingerprint matches, (2) at least one span on the page has bbox overlap >= 90% IoU with the receipt bbox, (3) that span's NFC-normalized SHA-256 equals the receipt's content_hash. Exit codes encode the failure mode: 0 success, 10 fingerprint mismatch, 11 bbox mismatch, 12 content mismatch.

Module: crates/pdftract-cli/src/verify_receipt.rs + crates/pdftract-core/src/receipts/verifier.rs (the protocol logic, reusable from PyO3 bindings later).

## Why this matters

The verify-receipt subcommand is what makes receipts trustworthy: pdftract receipts are independently auditable because the verifier protocol is well-defined, deterministic, and runnable by any party with the source PDF — without trusting pdftract beyond the determinism guarantee. An auditor or compliance pipeline can verify thousands of receipts in a batch with parallel CLI invocations.

The 90% IoU threshold is the calibrated cutoff: PDF re-extraction can shift bbox coordinates by 0-2 points due to floating-point round-tripping through different code paths (e.g. CTM application order); 90% is large enough to be robust against this noise but small enough to detect deliberate bbox tampering.

## Verifier protocol

1. Parse RECEIPT.json (or accept inline JSON via --inline FLAG, or stdin if path is \"-\")
2. Compute Phase 1.7 fingerprint of FILE.pdf — must equal receipt.pdf_fingerprint (exact string match) — else exit 10
3. Run pdftract extract on FILE.pdf with the same extraction_version as in the receipt (warn if version differs — extraction_version in the receipt drives a feature-flag-compatibility check; if pdftract binary's version < receipt extraction_version, ABORT with a clear error)
4. Iterate spans on page receipt.page_index
5. For each span, compute IoU(span.bbox, receipt.bbox) = intersection_area / union_area
6. If max(IoU) < 0.9 → exit 11
7. Take the span with max IoU; compute SHA-256 of NFC(span.text)
8. If sha256 != receipt.content_hash → exit 12
9. Else exit 0

## Implementation guidance

- CLI:
  - pdftract verify-receipt FILE.pdf RECEIPT.json — both args required positional
  - pdftract verify-receipt FILE.pdf - — reads receipt JSON from stdin
  - Flags: --json (machine-readable result on stdout); --quiet (suppress human output, just exit code); --inline JSON (literal receipt as flag value)
- Exit codes:
  - 0: receipt verifies
  - 10: pdf_fingerprint mismatch
  - 11: bbox mismatch (no span on page meets 90% IoU)
  - 12: content_hash mismatch (best-IoU span's text differs)
  - 1: extraction failed (PDF unreadable, encrypted without password, etc.)
  - 2: CLI parse error (clap default)
- IoU computation:
  ```rust
  fn iou(a: [f64; 4], b: [f64; 4]) -> f64 {
      let x0 = a[0].max(b[0]); let y0 = a[1].max(b[1]);
      let x1 = a[2].min(b[2]); let y1 = a[3].min(b[3]);
      if x1 <= x0 || y1 <= y0 { return 0.0; }
      let inter = (x1 - x0) * (y1 - y0);
      let area_a = (a[2] - a[0]) * (a[3] - a[1]);
      let area_b = (b[2] - b[0]) * (b[3] - b[1]);
      inter / (area_a + area_b - inter)
  }
  ```
- Human-readable output:
  ```
  Receipt verified: pdftract-v1:a7f3... page 14 bbox [220, 412, 412, 432]
  Best-match span IoU: 0.987, content_hash: sha256:9b21...
  ```
- JSON output (--json):
  ```json
  {\"status\":\"ok\"|\"fingerprint_mismatch\"|\"bbox_mismatch\"|\"content_mismatch\",
   \"pdf_fingerprint\":\"...\",
   \"page_index\":14,
   \"best_iou\":0.987,
   \"expected_content_hash\":\"sha256:...\",
   \"actual_content_hash\":\"sha256:...\"}
  ```

## Critical considerations

- NFC normalization of the actual extracted text is mandatory before hashing — must match the producer-side normalization (sibling 6.8.1). Use unicode-normalization::UnicodeNormalization::nfc
- The verifier MUST use the same extraction_version as the receipt — if the binary's version differs in MAJOR or MINOR, abort with a clear error directing the user to install the matching version. Patch version differences are allowed (compatible by semver).
- Don't compare floating-point bboxes with == anywhere; the IoU is the only legitimate comparison
- 90% IoU threshold is the calibrated cutoff (plan section 6.8 line 2388); make it a named constant IOU_VERIFICATION_THRESHOLD = 0.9 for clarity
- For receipts with svg_clip present, the verifier does NOT validate the SVG — only the fingerprint/bbox/content. SVG validity is a separate concern (the producer is trusted to emit valid SVG; a tampered SVG doesn't invalidate the underlying span match)
- Encrypted PDFs: prompt for password or accept via --password FLAG; otherwise exit 1 with a clear error
- Receipt JSON with missing required fields → exit 2 with a clap-style error explaining which field is missing
- The verifier can read either the bare Receipt JSON (just the receipt object) OR a full DocumentJson and a --span-id FLAG (deferred; not in this bead)
- Multiple receipts in a batch: future enhancement; this bead implements single-receipt verification only

## Acceptance criteria

- pdftract verify-receipt valid.pdf valid_receipt.json → exit 0; stdout shows \"Receipt verified\"
- pdftract verify-receipt tampered.pdf valid_receipt_for_orig.pdf → exit 10 (fingerprint mismatch) with stderr explaining
- pdftract verify-receipt valid.pdf shifted_bbox_receipt.json (bbox shifted by 100 points) → exit 11
- pdftract verify-receipt valid.pdf wrong_content_receipt.json → exit 12
- pdftract verify-receipt --json valid.pdf valid_receipt.json → exit 0; stdout is single-line JSON with status: \"ok\"
- pdftract verify-receipt - valid.pdf reads from stdin (test with a here-doc)
- 100 receipts verified in batch (via shell loop) total time <= 100 × single-PDF extraction time (proves no quadratic blowup)
- Receipt with extraction_version newer than current binary → exit 1 with clear error
- Plan critical test passes: \"Round-trip: extract with --receipts=lite → verify-receipt against same PDF → success\"
- Plan critical test passes: \"Tamper detection: edit one glyph in the PDF → receipts in that region fail verification; others still pass\"

## References

- Plan section: Phase 6.8 Visual Citation Receipts (lines 2386-2390)
- Sibling 6.8.1 (Receipt struct + lite serialization)
- Phase 1.7 fingerprint (fingerprint computation)
- INV-3 (deterministic Unicode resolution — verifier relies on)
- INV-6 (byte-identical re-extraction — verifier relies on)
- unicode-normalization crate
Labels: cli, phase-6, receipts, verify

## Scope

Bring docs/research/watermark-and-background-separation.md to v1.0 final-pass: document the detection heuristics that mark a span/block as a watermark (rotation, transparency, position, repetition across pages, font signals) and the separation rules that exclude watermarks from default text output while preserving them as kind: watermark blocks.

## Why this matters

Watermarks corrupt reading order and search relevance if mixed into the primary text stream (every page that says CONFIDENTIAL or DRAFT in the centre gets that string injected into the body). Line 1752 in the plan explicitly cites this note as the watermark-detection authority and ties it to a behavioural change: prior to Phase 7, watermarks are not excluded from --text output; after Phase 7, kind: watermark blocks are emitted but kept out of --text. The current 198-line draft sets up the framework.

## Implementation guidance

- File to update: docs/research/watermark-and-background-separation.md (already exists, currently 198 lines)
- Required content sections:
  - Signal: rotation -- spans with rotation in [30deg, 60deg] U [-60deg, -30deg] are watermark-candidate
  - Signal: transparency -- spans with alpha < 0.3 (from graphics state) are watermark-candidate
  - Signal: position -- spans centred on the page with bbox covering > 30% of the page area are watermark-candidate
  - Signal: cross-page repetition -- if the same text + font + similar position appears on >= 3 pages of a multi-page document, it is highly likely a watermark
  - Signal: font signals -- light-grey color, very large font size (> 36pt), bold sans-serif fonts commonly used for watermarks
  - Combination rule: score each signal in [0,1]; sum; threshold at 0.6 to mark as watermark
  - Block emission: emit a watermark block with kind: watermark, content: text, signals: { rotation, alpha, area_fraction, repetition_count, font_signal }
  - --text mode behaviour: pre-Phase-7 default emits watermarks; Phase 7 default excludes; --include-watermarks flag overrides
- Algorithm pseudo-code
- Validation methodology: labelled corpus of watermarked PDFs (CONFIDENTIAL, DRAFT, Approved, custom brand watermarks)

## Critical considerations

- False positive risk: stamps (Approved, Paid) that ARE intentional content vs decorative watermarks -- the distinction is fuzzy; default to including stamps as kind: watermark but document the failure mode
- Background image watermarks (a rasterized logo behind the page text) are NOT covered by this note (they are image-stream territory, Phase 5 page classification)
- The signal scoring weights should be tunable but ship with empirically-validated defaults
- Phase 7.10 form profile may want to override watermark exclusion (e.g. a form watermark may be a legally significant date stamp)
- Reading-order interaction: if a watermark is detected mid-page, do not split a paragraph at its position -- watermarks are removed from the span stream before paragraph assembly

## Acceptance criteria

- docs/research/watermark-and-background-separation.md updated with all signals documented and a scoring formula
- Pseudo-code listing for the combined scorer
- --text mode behaviour (pre vs post Phase 7) documented explicitly
- Edge cases (stamps vs watermarks, raster background watermarks) documented
- File grows to approx 350+ lines

## References

- Plan: line 1752 (watermark exclusion reference), Phase 7 watermark detection, Phase 4 paragraph assembly (reading-order interaction)

issue.description:
## Scope

Construct the cache key for a (PDF, extraction_options) pair. The key is a tuple (fingerprint, opts_hash) where fingerprint is the Phase 1.7 PDF fingerprint and opts_hash is the SHA-256 of the canonical JSON serialization of ExtractionOptions (sorted keys, normalized booleans, defaulted unspecified fields, including extraction_version).

Module: crates/pdftract-core/src/cache/key.rs.

## Why this matters

The cache key MUST be deterministic for the same logical extraction request: two callers with semantically identical options must produce the same opts_hash so they share a cache slot. Canonical JSON (RFC 8785 JCS or a simplified hand-rolled equivalent) is the standard tool for this. Default-filling unspecified fields ensures that ExtractionOptions { ocr: None, ... } and ExtractionOptions { ocr: Some(false), ... } produce the same hash (otherwise the cache would silently produce duplicate entries for the same logical request).

Including extraction_version in the canonicalization makes the cache key version-pinned: an upgraded pdftract binary computes a different opts_hash for the same options, ensuring a clean miss on the upgrade (no risk of serving stale entries with a different output schema).

## Implementation guidance

- Canonical JSON algorithm (simplified JCS):
  1. Take the ExtractionOptions struct
  2. Apply ::default() to fill all Option<T>::None fields with their explicit defaults
  3. Serialize via serde_json with a custom serializer that:
     - Sorts object keys lexicographically (BTreeMap or post-serialize sort)
     - Always emits booleans as true/false (not 1/0)
     - Always emits floats with the minimum decimal representation (e.g. 0.5 not 0.50000000000)
     - Excludes any internal-only fields (e.g. profile path, which is a transient setting; mark with #[serde(skip)])
  4. Add a top-level extraction_version field with the literal pdftract version string
  5. SHA-256 the resulting bytes
- Output as hex string (no \"sha256:\" prefix — that prefix is the format convention for content_hash in Phase 6.8 receipts but not used for cache keys)
- Key constructor:
  ```rust
  pub struct CacheKey { pub fingerprint: String, pub opts_hash: String }
  impl CacheKey {
      pub fn new(fingerprint: &str, options: &ExtractionOptions) -> Self {
          let canonical = canonical_options_json(options, env!(\"CARGO_PKG_VERSION\"));
          let hash = sha2::Sha256::digest(canonical.as_bytes());
          Self { fingerprint: fingerprint.to_string(), opts_hash: hex::encode(hash) }
      }
  }
  ```
- Include a unit-tested invariant: two ExtractionOptions structs that are field-by-field equal (after default-filling) MUST produce the same opts_hash regardless of serialization order

## Critical considerations

- Default-filling is mandatory; otherwise None-fields and Some(default)-fields hash differently
- Float serialization must be canonical: serde_json's default float repr is usually canonical for typical values, but edge cases (e.g. 0.1 vs 0.10000000000000001) must be handled. Use ryu (already a transitive dep) for canonical float formatting if needed
- Profile path (when --profile is used) should NOT be in the hash — what matters is the resolved options after profile application, not the profile filename. Apply the profile, then hash the resolved options
- extraction_version is the literal CARGO_PKG_VERSION string. Pre-release suffixes (e.g. \"1.0.0-rc.1\") are included and treated as version-distinct from \"1.0.0\"
- Sensitive fields (passwords) — do NOT include the password value in the hash. Either skip the field entirely OR hash a stable token like sha256(\"password-set\") OR sha256(\"password-unset\"). Including the literal password would leak it via the cache directory entries (visible to anyone with read access)
- For the password field, use a stable-but-non-leaky encoding: e.g. include \"password_set\": bool but not the value. This means two extractions with different passwords but the same fingerprint would share a cache slot — acceptable because if extraction succeeds with either password, the result is identical
- Verify the algorithm matches across releases: cache entries should remain valid across patch upgrades; canonical-JSON's algorithmic stability is the gate
- Test: serialize the same logical options in 2 different orders, hash both → assert equal

## Acceptance criteria

- CacheKey::new for two ExtractionOptions instances with identical effective values (one with explicit defaults, one with None) → opts_hash equal
- Toggling --ocr from false to true → opts_hash differs
- Toggling --receipts from off to lite → opts_hash differs
- Changing --password but everything else equal → opts_hash equal (password not in hash)
- Different pdftract version (compiled in test fixture) → opts_hash differs
- Sorted-key canonical: serialize { z: 1, a: 2 } and { a: 2, z: 1 } via canonical-JSON → byte-identical
- Float canonical: 0.5 and 0.500 → byte-identical serialization
- Documented invariant: same logical request → same key

## References

- Plan section: Phase 6.9 Content-Addressed Cache Layer (lines 2435-2438)
- RFC 8785 (JSON Canonicalization Scheme): https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8785
- Phase 1.7 fingerprint (other half of the key)
- Sibling 6.9.1 (entry_path consumes (fingerprint, opts_hash))
- Sibling 6.9.6 (--no-cache bypasses key construction entirely)
Labels: cache, hash, key, phase-6

docs.rs is the canonical Rust API reference; broken docs.rs builds are a documentation outage that silently degrades the user experience. Examples in /examples/ are discoverable via cargo (cargo run --example extract) and via docs.rs sidebar, making the API self-explanatory.

## Implementation guidance

### docs.rs config in Cargo.toml

```toml
[package.metadata.docs.rs]
all-features = true
rustdoc-args = [\"--cfg\", \"docsrs\"]
```

- all-features = true ensures docs.rs renders feature-gated items
- rustdoc-args = [\"--cfg\", \"docsrs\"] enables doc(cfg(...)) annotations
- targets = [\"x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu\"] is sufficient (docs.rs default; other targets are skipped by default)

### Examples directory

- crates/pdftract-core/examples/ with one file per contract method:
  - extract.rs: cargo run --example extract -- file.pdf → prints full DocumentJson
  - extract_text.rs: cargo run --example extract_text -- file.pdf → prints plain text

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the Sauvola adaptive thresholding step via leptonica-plumbing's pixSauvolaBinarize. Window size 15x15 (default); k parameter 0.34 (default). Used for PhysicalScan source (from the 5.3.2 image-source dispatch).

Module: crates/pdftract-core/src/ocr/preprocessing/sauvola.rs.

## Why this matters

Sauvola is the gold-standard adaptive thresholding for scanned documents: it computes a local threshold based on a sliding window mean and standard deviation, adapting to local lighting changes. Without it, OCR on scans with uneven lighting (one corner darker than another) produces dropped text in the dark regions.

## Implementation guidance

- Crate: leptonica-plumbing (FFI to libleptonica; provides pixSauvolaBinarize)
- Signature:
  ```rust
  pub fn sauvola_binarize(image: &GrayImage, window_size: u32, k: f32) -> GrayImage
  ```
- Default params: window_size=15, k=0.34 (calibrated for document scans per Sauvola paper)
- Document any deviation from defaults in code comments + ADR if changed
- Output: binary image (0 = white, 255 = black) as GrayImage
- Skip rule: image source is JBIG2 → no-op (already binary; dispatcher decides)

## Critical considerations

- libleptonica is a system dep (apt install libleptonica-dev); already in the Docker image (Phase 0.3 sibling)
- Window size 15x15: smaller window adapts to finer features but introduces noise; larger window misses local lighting changes. 15 is the document-OCR sweet spot
- k parameter 0.34: lower k binarizes more aggressively (more black pixels); higher k more conservatively. Calibrated against Tesseract WER on document scans
- Output is binary (only 0 and 255 values); intermediate gray values would indicate a bug
- Performance: Sauvola is O(N) with sliding-window optimization; 8 MP image in < 500 ms

## Acceptance criteria

- Sauvola on a 1080p scanned page produces a clean binary image
- Output pixel values are exactly 0 or 255 (no gray)
- Sauvola handles uneven lighting (dark corner) without losing text
- Window=15, k=0.34 defaults documented
- Benchmark: 1080p binarized in < 500ms

## References

- Plan section: Phase 5.3.3
- Sauvola paper: Sauvola & Pietikäinen (2000) Adaptive document image binarization
- leptonica-plumbing crate
- Coordinator: pdftract-4lwe (parent — Sauvola/Otsu/median bundle)
- Sibling: Otsu, median-filter denoise
Labels: binarization, phase-5, preprocessing

issue.description:
## Scope

Wire libtesseract into pdftract-ocr. Configure TessBaseAPI per thread (thread_local!), select PSM_AUTO, request HOCR output, parse the HOCR XML to extract per-word bbox + x_wconf, convert HOCR pixel coordinates back to PDF user-space, emit Vec<Span> with confidence_source = "ocr". Includes language-pack loading (default eng; configurable via ExtractionOptions.ocr_language).

## Why this matters

Tesseract is the recognition engine for everything in Phase 5. Correctness here drives the primary CI-gated objective (WER < 3% on clean 300-DPI scans). Initialization cost of Tesseract is substantial (~50 ms per init); thread_local! amortizes across pages on each rayon worker. HOCR is the only Tesseract output format that gives per-word bbox + confidence, both of which are mandatory schema fields for OCR spans.

## Implementation guidance

- Crate: tesseract (version 0.14, wraps libtesseract FFI), quick-xml for HOCR parsing
- Module: pdftract-ocr/src/tesseract.rs
- Pipeline entry: fn run_tesseract(image: &GrayImage, dpi: u32, opts: &TessOpts) -> Result<Vec<Span>>
- TessOpts: { languages: Vec<String>, psm: PageSegMode, tessdata_path: Option<PathBuf> }
- Default config: languages = ["eng"], psm = PSM_AUTO (mode 3), HOCR output
- thread_local! { static TESS: RefCell<Option<TessBaseAPI>> }; lazy init on first use per thread
- Reinitialize when ocr_language changes (cache last-used config; reinit only on diff)
- HOCR parsing: walk for ocrx_word spans; parse title attribute for "bbox x0 y0 x1 y1; x_wconf NNN"
- Coordinate conversion: HOCR pixels -> input image pixels (offset by 10px padding from 5.3.4) -> PDF pt via DPI
- Each parsed word -> one Span { text, bbox, confidence: x_wconf/100.0, confidence_source: "ocr", ... }

## Critical considerations

- WER < 3% on clean 300-DPI scans is CI-gated and is the primary Phase 5 objective
- Tesseract init is per-thread (thread_local!) because TessBaseAPI is not Send; rayon workers each init once
