issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the CLI option parsing + validation for multi-output: --json PATH, --md PATH, --text PATH (each repeatable disallowed), --ndjson (exclusive with all others), --format json,markdown,text + -o BASE for auto-naming. Validate at parse time: at-most-one "-", no duplicate format flags, no --ndjson combined with others. Build the sink list from validated config.

## Why this matters

CLI parsing is the user's first interface with multi-output. Bad errors here ("--json a --json b" silently accepted, only one written) corrupt user trust. Validation MUST happen at parse time so users see errors before extraction starts.

## Implementation guidance

- Use clap with custom validators
- Define a OutputSpec { format: Format, dest: Destination } where Destination = File(PathBuf) | Stdout
- After parsing, build Vec<OutputSpec> and validate:
  1. Count format occurrences; reject if any format > 1
  2. Count Destination::Stdout; reject if > 1 (different formats can BOTH point to files; only ONE can be stdout)
  3. If Format::Ndjson in list AND len > 1: reject ("--ndjson cannot be combined with other formats")
- --format json,markdown,text + -o BASE expansion:
  - For each requested format, derive filename: BASE + appropriate extension
  - Extensions: .json, .md, .txt, .ndjson
- CLI error messages: clear, point to the offending flag
- Default (no output flags): single JSON to stdout

## Critical considerations

- Empty Vec<OutputSpec> after parsing -> default JSON to stdout
- "-" parsing: PathBuf::from("-") detected as Stdout
- --format parsing accepts comma-separated names (json, markdown, text, ndjson)
- -o BASE without --format: error (ambiguous)
- --format without -o: write to stdout for each format? Only one can go to stdout — so multi-format --format requires -o (or one format being stdout)

## Acceptance criteria

- --json a.json --md b.md -> 2 OutputSpecs built
- --json a.json --json b.json -> CLI error "duplicate format"
- --ndjson --md b.md -> CLI error "--ndjson cannot be combined" (critical test line 2284)
- --md - --json out.json -> 2 specs, MD=Stdout, JSON=File
- --md - --json - -> CLI error "at most one stdout"
- --format json,md -o out -> 2 specs, out.json + out.md

## References

- Plan section: Phase 6.6 CLI design + validation rules (lines 2221-2247)

## Scope

Filter at SPAN level removing invisible text (rendering_mode == 3 via PDF Tr 3) from output unless include_invisible. Operates inside block-text join (not block-level).

## Why this matters

Invisible text is COMMONLY used in scanned PDFs as searchable text layer overlaid on the scan. Including it by default DOUBLES extracted text. Excluding by default is correct UX; flag re-enables for forensic use.

## Implementation guidance

- Inside block-text join: skip span if !options.include_invisible && span.rendering_mode == 3 (also include_hidden_layers + glyph hidden flag).
- Whole-block exclusion: if ALL spans filtered, block produces empty text — do NOT emit \n\n.

## Critical considerations

- INV: SPAN-level filter, not block.
- Tr 0-2 visible; Tr 3 invisible; Tr 4-7 invisible variants — treat same as 3.
- Mixed-visibility block: keep visible, drop invisible.
- Span aggregation rule for is_hidden: "any glyph hidden -> span hidden".

## Acceptance criteria

- rendering_mode 3 + include_invisible false: excluded.
- Same with include_invisible true: included.
- Mixed block: visible emitted.
- All-invisible block: no spurious \n\n.
- Tr=4: treated same as Tr=3.

## References

- Plan section: Phase 4.6 (line 1751)

## Scope

Define the PageClassification struct that wraps a PageClass with its confidence and optional hybrid-cell metadata. Lives in crates/pdftract-core/src/page_class.rs alongside the enum.

## Why this matters

Every page-routing decision needs not just the class but the classifier's confidence (for the 0.7/0.3 thresholds in Phase 5.5 escalation policy) and, for Hybrid pages, the set of image-heavy cells (for the Phase 5.2 partial-rasterization optimization). Bundling these into one struct keeps the per-page metadata coherent and serializable.

## Implementation guidance

- Struct:
  ```rust
  #[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
  pub struct PageClassification {
      pub class: PageClass,
      pub confidence: f32,
      #[serde(skip_serializing_if = \"Option::is_none\")]
      pub hybrid_cells: Option<BTreeSet<(u8, u8)>>,
  }
  ```
- Constructor with debug_assert on confidence range:
  ```rust
  impl PageClassification {
      pub fn new(class: PageClass, confidence: f32, hybrid_cells: Option<BTreeSet<(u8, u8)>>) -> Self {
          debug_assert!(0.0 <= confidence && confidence <= 1.0);
          Self { class, confidence, hybrid_cells }
      }
  }
  ```
- BTreeSet (not HashSet) so iteration order is deterministic for JSON output stability
- hybrid_cells is Some only when class == Hybrid; document this invariant

## Critical considerations

- confidence is f32 in [0.0, 1.0]; debug_assert in constructor catches bugs in dev; production code that passes out-of-range silently clamps (avoid panic in release builds — INV-8)
- BTreeSet<(u8, u8)> with row, col indexes; u8 is sufficient because the 8x8 grid in Phase 5.1 has indexes 0..=7
- Roundtrip test: serialize -> deserialize PageClassification == original (with and without hybrid_cells)
- The class != Hybrid && hybrid_cells.is_some() case is allowed by the type system but is a bug; lint via a custom Debug or a validator method

- Unit test: hybrid_cells: None is omitted from JSON output via skip_serializing_if
- Unit test: debug_assert fires on confidence = 1.5 in dev build

## Scope

Add the `pdftract hash` subcommand to the CLI (in `crates/pdftract-cli/src/main.rs`):

- Invocation: `pdftract hash FILE.pdf` or `pdftract hash https://example.com/file.pdf` (remote source via Phase 1.8)
- Output: `pdftract-v1:<64-hex>\n` to stdout
- Flags: --password, --header (repeatable), --pages (ignored for hash since fingerprint is whole-document)

Exit codes (per plan's Section 1.7 CLI spec):
- 0: success
- 2: corrupt file
- 3: encrypted file and no password supplied
- 4: path or URL cannot be read
- 5: network failure mid-extraction (remote URLs only)
- 6: TLS handshake failure

## Implementation guidance

- Use clap = "4" for argument parsing
- Subcommand structure: `pdftract <command>` where hash is one of [extract, hash, grep, verify-receipt, ...]
- Reuse Document-opening logic from extract: build PdfSource, run Phase 1.4 Document::open, call Phase 1.7 compute_fingerprint
- Exit code mapping in single helper: `map_error_to_exit_code(err: &PdftractError) -> i32`
- Print human-readable error to stderr; exit code via std::process::exit

## Critical considerations

- Hash subcommand MUST be fast (no extraction overhead beyond what's needed for fingerprinting). Avoid Phase 2 (font pipeline) or Phase 3 (content stream extraction) if at all possible
- However, fingerprint algorithm DOES need decoded content streams (Phase 1.5) and resolved resource dicts (Phase 1.4). So "fast" = "stop after Phase 1"
- For remote URLs: use HttpRangeSource from Phase 1.8. With Range support, hash may download only xref + content stream bytes
- Exit code 3 vs 4: "file exists but needs password" vs "file doesn't exist or unreachable"
- TLS handshake failure (exit 6) includes certificate chain reason in stderr
- Subcommand emits diagnostics to stderr (one per line, JSON format) if --verbose; default is quiet
- INV-9 (MCP stdio rule): hash subcommand is NOT in MCP mode; can write to stdout

## Acceptance criteria

- `pdftract hash <local-pdf>` prints `pdftract-v1:<hex>\n` to stdout, exit 0
- `pdftract hash <non-existent>` exit 4, stderr "file not found"
- `pdftract hash <encrypted-pdf>` exit 3, stderr "password required"
- `pdftract hash --password test <encrypted-pdf>` exit 0 if correct, 3 if wrong
- `pdftract hash https://localhost/test.pdf` works for remote URLs
- `pdftract hash https://nonexistent.invalid/` exit 4
- `pdftract hash https://expired-cert.example/` exit 6 with TLS reason
- Performance: hash of local 100-page PDF in < 200 ms

issue.description:
## Scope

Enforce the NEVER-log policy across the entire codebase: no credential values, no auth headers, no PDF bytes, no extracted text content at any log level. Implement compile-time and CI-time checks to catch violations.

## Why this matters

The log-policy enforcement is what makes the audit log itself safe to retain and ship to a SIEM — a leak from the log file would mirror leaks from the PDFs themselves. Without enforcement, a future contributor could log a request body for debugging, inadvertently shipping credentials to wherever the log goes. The policy must be enforced mechanically (lint/grep) because manual review misses things.

## Implementation guidance

- SecretString wrapper for sensitive values: passwords, bearer tokens, audit-log lines that carry user-supplied data
  - Display impl prints REDACTED; Debug impl prints REDACTED
  - Internal value accessible only via ::expose_secret() method
- Audit codebase for log/println/eprintln/tracing call sites:
  - Any log call with a variable name suggesting a credential (case-insensitive substring) is flagged
  - Any log call with body, content, text, data is warned; reviewer judgment whether it is content or metadata
- HTTP middleware: strip Authorization / Cookie / Proxy-Authorization headers from any request/response logging
- Stack-trace redaction: panic hook redacts SecretString values in backtraces (they should never appear, but defense-in-depth)
- CI gate: a grep-based script (or a custom clippy lint) scans the codebase; runs in the supply-chain workflow alongside cargo deny
- The audit log writer (sibling bead) explicitly excludes diagnostics message text (only diagnostic codes are logged) — message text could leak content
- Tests: a fuzz-test that supplies credentials and asserts they never appear in any captured log output

## Critical considerations

- secrecy crate provides SecretString with the right Display/Debug semantics; use it consistently
- The CI gate is heuristic; false positives are tolerated (reviewer manually verifies); false negatives are catastrophic (real leaks)
- log::trace! is sometimes useful for debug; gate at compile-time (not log-level) so trace! lines are removed from release binaries
- Add a CONTRIBUTING.md section explicitly listing forbidden log-content patterns
- For audit-log lines carrying user-supplied data (e.g. a URL with a query param), pre-sanitize to remove known sensitive patterns; document the sanitization in the audit-log schema

## Acceptance criteria

- secrecy crate added; SecretString used for credentials everywhere
- Grep-based CI gate runs on every PR; flags new log calls with sensitive variable names
- Fuzz-test confirms no credential values appear in captured log output (10,000 random inputs)
- Authorization / Cookie / Proxy-Authorization headers stripped from any request logging
- Panic hook redacts SecretString contents in backtraces
- CONTRIBUTING.md has a forbidden-log-content section

## References

- Plan section: Phase 6 audit logging policy (lines 931-964)
- secrecy crate: https://crates.io/crates/secrecy
- TH-08 (audit-logging test)
- Coordinator: pdftract-4em4l (parent)
- Sibling: audit-log FILE flag

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the --receipts FLAG on pdftract extract (and all other extract-style subcommands) accepting one of \"off\" | \"lite\" | \"svg\" with default \"off\". Thread the ExtractionOptions.receipts field through the extraction pipeline so the Phase 3+ span/block builders consult it and call the Receipt::lite (sibling 6.8.1) or Receipt::svg (siblings 6.8.2/6.8.3) constructors accordingly.

Module touches: crates/pdftract-cli/src/cli.rs (flag definition); crates/pdftract-core/src/options.rs (ExtractionOptions); crates/pdftract-core/src/extract.rs or wherever the per-span builder lives.

## Why this matters

Without this wiring, the receipt struct exists in isolation (sibling 6.8.1) but is never populated; the SVG generator (sibling 6.8.2) is never invoked; the verifier (sibling 6.8.4) has nothing to verify. This bead is the integration glue that makes the feature reachable from the CLI and the PyO3 bindings and the HTTP serve mode and the MCP tools.

The threading is mechanical but touches every entry point: CLI, PyO3, HTTP /extract handler, MCP extract / extract_text / extract_markdown tools. Centralizing the receipts-mode plumbing on ExtractionOptions means the per-span receipt generation happens in exactly one place (the span builder) regardless of how extraction was invoked.

## Implementation guidance

- ExtractionOptions struct addition:
  ```rust
  pub enum ReceiptsMode { Off, Lite, Svg }
  pub struct ExtractionOptions {
      // ... existing fields
      pub receipts: ReceiptsMode,
  }
  impl Default for ReceiptsMode { fn default() -> Self { ReceiptsMode::Off } }
  ```
- CLI flag:
  ```rust
  #[arg(long, value_name = \"MODE\", value_parser = [\"off\", \"lite\", \"svg\"], default_value = \"off\")]
  pub receipts: String,
  ```
- Map the CLI string to the enum in the CLI-to-options conversion
- Span builder integration: after a Span is constructed with its bbox and text, if options.receipts != Off, construct a Receipt and attach to the span:
  ```rust
  let receipt = match options.receipts {
      ReceiptsMode::Off => None,
      ReceiptsMode::Lite => Some(Receipt::lite(&pdf_fingerprint, page_index, bbox, &text, ...)),
      ReceiptsMode::Svg => Some(Receipt::svg(&pdf_fingerprint, page_index, bbox, &text, &glyph_list, &font_resolver, ...)),
  };
  span.receipt = receipt;
  ```
- Same logic for blocks (block-level receipts cover the union bbox of all spans in the block; text is concatenated span text)
- HTTP serve form-field: receipts=lite|svg|off as a multipart form field
- PyO3: receipts kwarg on extract() with str type
- MCP extract tool: receipts arg in inputSchema (already defined in sibling 6.7.5)
- CLI validation: when --receipts=svg but the receipts feature is not compiled OR (for OCR cases) full-render is not compiled, emit a clear error early — do NOT silently degrade to lite

## Critical considerations

- The default is \"off\"; users opt-in. Receipts add 10-25% to extraction time (plan acceptance criterion), so making them default-on would regress baseline benchmarks
- The mode is per-extraction (not per-span); changing the mode requires a new extract call
- When --receipts=svg and the receipts or full-render feature is NOT compiled, CLI exits 2 with a clear error: \"--receipts=svg requires the 'receipts' feature\" (or full-render for OCR cases — defer the runtime check to the SVG generator)
- Receipts on blocks vs spans: emit at both levels by default; block-level receipts cover the union bbox. Optional --receipts-level=span|block|both deferred to a future iteration (this bead does \"both\" by default).
- The receipt: null placeholder in the JSON schema when --receipts=off must be EXPLICITLY null (or absent via skip_serializing_if), so downstream consumers see a stable shape (plan line 2410)
- Threading through the parallel extraction pipeline: receipts construction happens INSIDE the per-page rayon scope (the page's glyph list and font resolver are local to the page); no cross-page contention
- pdf_fingerprint is computed once at the start of extraction and threaded into the span builder via the per-extraction context (avoid recomputing per-span)

## Acceptance criteria

- pdftract extract --receipts=lite file.pdf → JSON output's spans have non-null receipt fields with the lite shape (no svg_clip)
- pdftract extract --receipts=svg file.pdf → JSON output's spans have receipt fields including svg_clip
- pdftract extract --receipts=off file.pdf → JSON output's spans have receipt: null (or absent)
- pdftract extract file.pdf (no --receipts) → same as --receipts=off
- pdftract extract --receipts=bogus file.pdf → CLI parse error from clap value_parser
- ExtractionOptions struct serializes the receipts field for HTTP/MCP transport
- HTTP /extract with multipart form field receipts=lite produces receipts in the JSON response
- PyO3 extract(path, receipts=\"lite\") works
- MCP tools/call extract with {\"receipts\":\"lite\"} works (matches sibling 6.7.5's inputSchema)
- Block-level receipts are present alongside span-level when --receipts != off
- Plan acceptance criterion: receipt generation adds <= 10% to extraction time for lite, <= 25% for svg (assert in benchmark CI gate)

## References

- Plan section: Phase 6.8 Visual Citation Receipts (lines 2355, 2406)
- Sibling 6.8.1 (Receipt struct constructor used here)
- Sibling 6.8.2/6.8.3 (SVG generator + OCR fallback called from this wiring)
- Phase 6.1 JSON schema (the receipt field is added to SpanJson and BlockJson)
- Phase 6.3 PyO3 bindings (receipts kwarg threading)
- Phase 6.4 HTTP serve (multipart form field)
- Sibling 6.7.5 MCP tools (extract tool's receipts arg)

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement user-editable YAML document profiles that drive document classification (extending Phase 5.6) and apply type-specific extraction tuning. A profile has: name, description, priority, match (boolean DSL combining text_contains / structural / heading_matches / has_currency_pattern / has_signature_field predicates with all/any/none combinators), extraction (overrides for reading_order / table_detection / readability_threshold / include_invisible / include_headers_footers / force_ocr / min_block_chars), and fields (per-profile structured-field extraction DSL with regex / near / region / pick / parse operators). 9 built-in profiles ship in the binary (invoice, receipt, contract, scientific_paper, slide_deck, form, bank_statement, legal_filing, book_chapter). pdftract profiles subcommand family (list, show, export, install, validate). --auto and --profile flags on extract. XDG config path. --profile-hot-reload for serve.

## Why this matters

Profiles transform pdftract from a general-purpose extractor into a tunable extraction PLATFORM. Different document types have radically different layout patterns (invoices left-to-right line-by-line, scientific papers two-column with abstract on top, slide decks one-block-per-page). One-size-fits-all extraction averages out these patterns to mediocre quality on each. Profiles let pdftract apply type-specialised heuristics + extract structured fields (invoice total, vendor, customer, line items) WITHOUT requiring users to write Rust code. YAML editability + built-in profiles + XDG config + hot-reload give a clean operational story: ship safe defaults, let users override per-deployment, let operators iterate live during serve.

## Implementation guidance

- Feature flag: profiles (adds serde_yaml ~200 KB); auto-pulls regex from grep feature OR enables standalone
- Crates: serde_yaml = "0.9", regex (reuse from grep), notify = "6" (for --profile-hot-reload inotify; fallback to polling on platforms without inotify)
- Profile YAML schema (see plan example lines 2896-2943); deserialize to a Profile struct
- Profile loader: walks the search path (lowest priority first; later wins on name collision):
  1. Built-in profiles compiled into binary via include_str!
  2. /etc/pdftract/profiles/*.yaml (system-wide)
  3. $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/pdftract/profiles/*.yaml (defaults to ~/.config/pdftract/profiles/)
  4. --profile-dir DIR (CLI flag, repeatable; takes everything in DIR)
- Match DSL evaluator: boolean tree with all/any/none combinators + 11 predicate kinds; evaluates against a DocumentSignals snapshot
- Extraction tuning: when a profile matches, its `extraction` block overrides specific ExtractionOptions fields
- Field DSL evaluator: each field has localizers (near, region, pick) + extractor (regex, parse); evaluates against extracted spans
- 9 built-in profiles in profiles/builtin/ source dir; each with >= 5 fixtures + regression test in tests/fixtures/profiles/<name>/
- pdftract profiles subcommand: list (show all), show (dump YAML), export (copy built-in to stdout), install (copy to ~/.config/pdftract/profiles/), validate (syntax + schema check, no extraction)
- pdftract extract --auto: evaluate all profiles; pick highest-priority match with confidence >= 0.6
- pdftract extract --profile NAME|PATH: force-apply a named profile or YAML file
- pdftract serve --profile-dir DIR --profile-hot-reload: re-read DIR on every request (inotify-watched; polling fallback)
- Output: when a profile applies, /metadata.profile_name, /metadata.profile_version, /metadata.profile_fields populated
- PROFILE_SECRETS_FORBIDDEN: profile YAML loader rejects top-level keys "secrets", "secret", "token", "tokens", "key", "keys", "password", "passwd", "credentials", "credential"

## Critical considerations

- Built-in profiles via include_str! - zero deploy step, always available
- User profiles via XDG + --profile-dir - opt-in customisation
- Profile resolution: priority field is the user-controllable sort key; on tie, last-loaded wins (load order: built-in -> /etc -> XDG -> --profile-dir)
- Hot-reload disabled by default (file I/O on every request wasteful for stable deployments); inotify when enabled
- Match DSL is intentionally boolean+predicate; no Turing completeness (security; no arbitrary code exec via YAML)
- Field DSL evaluates in document order; first hit per field wins (deterministic)
- Profile validation accepts unknown extraction keys with warning (forward compat) but unknown match predicates are errors
- 9 built-in profiles each ship with >= 5 fixture documents + regression test (acceptance criterion)
- profile_fields output uses field names as keys; null when extractor finds no candidate
- INV: stable taxonomy of match predicates + extraction keys + field DSL operators - new ones append, no rename

## Acceptance criteria

- All Phase 7.10 child task beads closed
- Critical test (from plan): Acrobat sample invoice classified as invoice with confidence > 0.8; fields extracted >= 90% accuracy across 50-invoice fixture
- Critical test: custom profile with priority 100 matching every doc overrides built-ins
- Critical test: malformed regex profile rejected by validate with line-numbered error
- Critical test: profile_fields.total: null when not found (no error)
- Critical test: hot-reload picks up new YAML in DIR on next request
- Critical test: user profile shadowing built-in shown in list with "(overrides built-in)" annotation
- Acceptance: built-in invoice profile >= 90% field accuracy on 50-invoice fixture corpus
- Acceptance: field extraction adds < 5% to per-document time
- 9 built-in profiles ship; each with >= 5 fixtures + regression test
- Built-in profile YAML compiled in via include_str!; user profiles loaded from XDG / --profile-dir

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the document-wide LRU object cache. Mutex<LruCache<ObjRef, Arc<PdfObject>>> with capacity 4096. Caches successful indirect-object resolutions; cache hits skip the re-parse work.

Module: crates/pdftract-core/src/parser/object/cache.rs.

## Why this matters

PDF objects are referenced many times during extraction (e.g., the same Font object referenced from every page using it). Without caching, each reference triggers a full re-parse of the indirect object, multiplying parse cost. The 4096-entry LRU is sized for typical documents (10-100 pages × 40 objects/page); the LRU eviction handles the long-tail of huge documents.

## Implementation guidance

- Crate: lru = \"0.12\" (already in plan's Dependency Matrix)
- Cache:
  ```rust
  use std::sync::Mutex;
  use lru::LruCache;
  use std::num::NonZeroUsize;

  pub struct ObjectCache {
      inner: Mutex<LruCache<ObjRef, Arc<PdfObject>>>,
  }
  impl ObjectCache {
      pub fn new() -> Self {
          Self { inner: Mutex::new(LruCache::new(NonZeroUsize::new(4096).unwrap())) }
      }
      pub fn get(&self, key: &ObjRef) -> Option<Arc<PdfObject>>;
      pub fn insert(&self, key: ObjRef, value: Arc<PdfObject>);
  }
  ```
- Used by the resolve(ref) function in the cycle-detection sibling: on resolution success, insert into cache; on subsequent resolve(ref), check cache first
- Mutex<LruCache> is correct: PDF document parsing is single-threaded per document; rayon parallelism happens at PAGE-level (Phase 3), not during object resolution
- For per-page parallel resolution in Phase 3, each page may have its own cache instance OR share a Mutex'd cache (latency budget acceptable)

## Critical considerations

- Cache size 4096: a typical 100-page PDF has 4000-40000 indirect objects; 4096 captures the hot working set without OOM on huge PDFs
- Cache hit ratio target: > 80% on typical PDFs (verified in benchmark fixture)
- Mutex contention: parsing is mostly single-threaded; the Mutex is essentially free except in Phase 3 page-parallel mode
- Arc<PdfObject> is cheap to clone (refcount increment); cached values are returned by Arc::clone without deep copy
- Eviction on capacity overflow: LRU's standard behavior; no notification to caller (transparent)
- Cache MUST NOT cache failed resolutions (errors, cycles); only successful ones (Some(Arc<PdfObject>))

## Acceptance criteria

- Cache get on miss returns None
- Cache insert + get returns Some(Arc<PdfObject>)
- Cache eviction at capacity 4096 works (LRU semantics)
- Hit ratio > 80% on test fixture (100-page PDF with 5000 objects, 25000 references)
- Concurrent get from 8 threads: no race conditions (Mutex serializes)
- Cache survives process lifetime (cleared on Drop)

## References

- Plan section: Phase 1.2 LRU cache
- lru crate: https://crates.io/crates/lru
- Coordinator: pdftract-4ij2 (parent)
- Sibling: per-thread cycle detection
Labels: cache, parser, phase-1
issue.title: LRU object cache (Mutex<LruCache<ObjRef, Arc<PdfObject>>>, 4096 entries)

issue.description:
## Scope

Bring docs/notes/sdk-invocation.md to v1.0 final-pass: document the subprocess invocation contract that every language SDK follows (argv layout, stdin/stdout/stderr discipline, exit code taxonomy, env-var pass-through, --progress-json schema, --capture-diagnostics archive shape).

## Why this matters

The subprocess contract is the wire protocol every SDK relies on. Mismatched expectations (e.g. an SDK that fails to set --json on the binary, or that does not consume stderr) produce subtle bugs that are very hard to debug from the SDK side. The current 1100-line draft is comprehensive but must be aligned to the secrets-handling policy (TH-07: --password VALUE rejected without env opt-in), the audit-logging policy, and the new --auto / --profile flow.

## Implementation guidance

- File to update: docs/notes/sdk-invocation.md (already exists, currently 1100 lines)
- Required content sections and corrections:
  - argv layout: subcommand + flags + positional args; document the canonical form an SDK SHOULD construct
  - stdin discipline: --password-stdin reads one line; remote sources read PDF bytes from stdin if path is -
  - stdout discipline: extraction output is the ONLY thing on stdout in --json or --text mode; --progress-json events go to stderr (or a side channel)
  - stderr discipline: log lines, progress events, diagnostics
  - Exit code taxonomy: 0 success; 64 usage error; 65 data error (malformed PDF); 66 password missing/wrong; 67 cannot open input; 70 internal error; 73 cannot create output; 74 IO error; 75 temp-failure (retry); 77 permission denied; 78 config error (TH-03 mcp-no-auth lands here)
  - Env-var pass-through: PDFTRACT_PASSWORD, PDFTRACT_MCP_TOKEN, PDFTRACT_INSECURE_CLI_PASSWORD, PDFTRACT_INSECURE_CLI_TOKEN, RUST_LOG, NO_COLOR, XDG_CONFIG_HOME (for profiles)
  - --progress-json event schema: ndjson with event-typed lines (open, page_started, page_completed, ocr_started, ocr_completed, profile_matched, password_received, error)
  - --capture-diagnostics archive: zip / tar layout, contained files (sanitized PDF or fingerprint reference; stderr capture; runtime config snapshot with secrets redacted)
  - SDK examples: Rust process::Command, Python subprocess.run, Node child_process.spawn

## Critical considerations

- TH-07: SDKs MUST construct password ingress via env or stdin, never via plain --password VALUE -- the note must call this out and provide working example code for each language
- Diagnostic capture archive MUST scrub secrets: password values, bearer tokens, full extracted text -- the archive is intended to be shared with maintainers; leaking content would be a TH-08 violation
- The --progress-json password_received event MUST NOT carry the password value (line 911 in plan)
- Exit code 78 is reserved for config errors and is the exit code that mcp --bind without --auth-token returns (TH-03 line 874)
- stdout discipline is critical: SDKs that mix log lines into stdout break JSON parsing for consumers; the binary MUST keep stdout clean

## Acceptance criteria

- docs/notes/sdk-invocation.md updated with the secrets-handling and exit-code-78 corrections
- argv / stdin / stdout / stderr discipline sections present with explicit rules
- Exit code taxonomy complete with TH-NN references where applicable
- --progress-json event schema documented per event type
- --capture-diagnostics archive layout documented with scrubbing rules
- Rust, Python, Node example invocations present and verified to work against the binary

## References

- Plan: lines 833 (per-threat tests), 874 (TH-03 exit 78), 878 (TH-07 password CLI policy), 907 (--password-stdin etc), 911-913 (password redaction in progress-json), 921 (token in SecretString)

issue.description:
## Scope

Detect merged cells (rowspan, colspan) in tables by examining which interior grid edges are present vs. missing. When the interior edge between two adjacent grid cells is absent (no path segment runs along the expected grid line), infer that the cells are merged. Emit colspan or rowspan integers on the surviving cell; suppress the absorbed cell from the output.

## Why this matters

Merged header cells are universal in real-world tables: "Q1 2025" spanning Jan/Feb/Mar columns; "Total" spanning Subtotal/Tax/Net rows; financial reports with multi-level column groupings. Without merge detection, the merged cell's text appears once and the absorbed cells are empty - downstream tools render this as a misaligned table.

## Implementation guidance

- Input: GridCandidate with row_ys + col_xs + segments (from 7.2.1; 7.2.2 borderless has no segments => merged detection skipped)
- For each interior cell (not edge), enumerate the four interior edges that should bound it:
  - top: horizontal segment from (col_xs[i], row_ys[j]) to (col_xs[i+1], row_ys[j])
  - bottom: horizontal segment from (col_xs[i], row_ys[j+1]) to (col_xs[i+1], row_ys[j+1])
  - left: vertical segment from (col_xs[i], row_ys[j]) to (col_xs[i], row_ys[j+1])
  - right: vertical segment from (col_xs[i+1], row_ys[j]) to (col_xs[i+1], row_ys[j+1])
- An edge is "present" if at least 80% of its expected length is covered by clustered segments from 7.2.1
- Missing right edge between cells (i, j) and (i+1, j) -> colspan extension: the cell at (i, j) absorbs (i+1, j); set cell.colspan += 1; mark (i+1, j) as absorbed
- Missing bottom edge between cells (i, j) and (i, j+1) -> rowspan extension: cell at (i, j) absorbs (i, j+1); cell.rowspan += 1
- Iterate until no more merges can be applied (transitive: a cell can absorb multiple neighbours)
- Absorbed cells are flagged with absorbed: true and excluded from the final Vec<Cell>

## Critical considerations

- Edge-presence threshold (80%) tolerates broken/dashed rules typical in PDFs exported from spreadsheets
- Borderless tables (7.2.2) have no segments to infer from - merged-cell detection is a NO-OP; emit a diagnostic instead
- Diagonal merges (rowspan > 1 AND colspan > 1) are valid; algorithm handles via iterative absorption
- Default rowspan/colspan = 1 when no merge inferred
- The cell that survives (top-left of the merged region) keeps its bbox EXPANDED to cover the absorbed cells

## Acceptance criteria

- Critical test (from plan): merged header cell spanning 3 columns - colspan=3 in output
- Unit tests: pure rowspan, pure colspan, diagonal merge (rowspan=2, colspan=2), borderless table NO-OP with diagnostic
- Public Cell.rowspan: u32, Cell.colspan: u32 defaulted to 1
- Absorbed cells excluded from final Vec<Cell>
- Bbox of merged cell covers all absorbed cells geometrically

## References

- Plan section: 7.2 line 2575 (merged cell detection)
- 7.2.1 (segments source)
- 7.2.3 (cell list to mutate)
- docs/research/table-structure-reconstruction.md
issue.title: 7.2.5: Merged cell detection via missing interior edges (rowspan/colspan)

issue.description:
## Scope

The Lexer is the lowest layer of the parser stack: it consumes the raw byte slice from a `PdfSource` (Phase 1.8) and produces a stream of PDF tokens. All higher-level parsers (object parser, xref resolver, content stream processor in Phase 3) call into it. It is hand-written (no `nom` dependency) because PDF's tokenization grammar is simple enough — operators, delimiters, and a handful of literal types — that a state-machine lexer is both smaller and more debuggable than a parser combinator.

This bead is the sub-phase coordinator that aggregates the child task beads:

- pdftract-XX: Whitespace + comment + token-boundary infrastructure (foundational; required by all literal lexers)
- pdftract-XX: Numeric literal lexer (integer + real)
- pdftract-XX: PDF string literal lexer with octal escapes and balanced parens
- pdftract-XX: PDF hex string lexer with odd-length padding
- pdftract-XX: PDF name object lexer with #XX hex expansion + NUL/length rules
- pdftract-XX: Structural token lexer (arrays, dicts, stream/endstream, obj/endobj/R)
- pdftract-XX: Token enum + Lexer struct + position tracking + diagnostic emission
- pdftract-XX: Lexer property test corpus + proptest harness

## Why this matters

The Lexer's correctness underpins everything downstream. A bug that misinterprets a single PDF string with an unusual escape sequence cascades through the object parser into the document model, ultimately producing wrong glyph counts or wrong font selection in Phase 3. The full plan's Critical tests for Section 1.1 are non-negotiable; they exercise the well-known historical gotchas (balanced parens, octal escapes at end-of-string, odd-length hex strings, name `#XX` with `#20` -> space and `#00` -> rejected, name length limit 127 bytes).

The Lexer also establishes the convention for diagnostic emission that the rest of the parser inherits: `STRUCT_INVALID_NAME` (name too long), `STRUCT_INVALID_HEX` (odd hex digits without padding allowance documented elsewhere), `STRUCT_INVALID_OCTAL` (octal escape with non-octal digits). Each diagnostic carries position info so the user can locate the issue.

## Critical considerations

- Whitespace per PDF spec section 7.2.2 is exactly six bytes: 0x00, 0x09, 0x0A, 0x0C, 0x0D, 0x20. Do NOT use Rust's `char::is_whitespace`; it admits Unicode whitespace which is wrong here
- Comments (`%` to end-of-line) are discarded but their bytes still advance position counters so later byte-offset references (xref) remain correct
- The `stream` keyword has a hard rule: it MUST be followed by exactly one of `\n` or `\r\n` (NOT lone `\r`). The lexer emits a `STRUCT_INVALID_STREAM_HEADER` diagnostic if violated
- Name objects are limited to 127 bytes per PDF spec 7.3.5; this length is measured on the RAW bytes in the file, BEFORE `#XX` hex escape expansion. Truncate at 127 bytes and emit `STRUCT_INVALID_NAME`. This subtle pre-vs-post-expansion distinction is one of the most-missed edge cases
- Hex strings of odd length pad with a trailing zero nibble: `<4>` -> `\x40` (not `\x04`). This is the opposite of intuition
- Octal escapes inside string literals are 1-3 digits and consume greedily: `(abc\101)` -> `abcA` (octal 101 = decimal 65 = ASCII A). `(abc\10A)` -> `abc\x08A` (only 2 octal digits because A is not octal)
- The line-continuation escape `\<newline>` in literal strings emits NO character; the bytes following the backslash are consumed but produce nothing
- A whitespace-only file MUST produce an empty token stream and not panic — this is the EC-01 (Empty PDF) edge case for the lexer layer
- For UTF-16 string detection (used by Phase 1.4 outline title parsing): the lexer does NOT decode; it returns raw bytes (PdfString = Vec<u8>). UTF-16BE BOM detection (FE FF prefix) happens at the consumer layer

## Acceptance criteria

- All Critical tests from plan Section 1.1 pass (cited in child beads)
- Lexer is panic-free on any input (INV-8) — verified by per-PR proptest fuzz with >= 10,000 cases per parser module
- Lexer is `no_std`-compatible (no allocation outside `Vec<u8>` for string tokens) — important for future embedded use cases
- All 8 child beads closed
- Diagnostic codes `STRUCT_INVALID_NAME`, `STRUCT_INVALID_HEX`, `STRUCT_INVALID_OCTAL`, `STRUCT_INVALID_STREAM_HEADER` defined and emitted with byte-offset position info
- Module under `crates/pdftract-core/src/parser/lexer/`

## References

- Plan section: Phase 1.1 Lexer, lines 1024-1052
- EC-01 (Empty PDF) for whitespace-only file handling
- INV-8 (no panic in pdftract-core)
- Critical tests cited in child beads

issue.description:
## Scope

Coordinator for sub-phase 2.2: implement the 4-level Unicode fallback chain that resolves any character code from a content stream to a `(char, UnicodeSource, confidence)` triple. The chain is: (L1) ToUnicode CMap -> confidence 1.0; (L2) named encoding + Adobe Glyph List -> 0.9; (L3) font fingerprint cache -> 0.85; (L4) glyph shape recognition via pHash DB -> 0.7; failure -> U+FFFD, 0.0 with `GLYPH_UNMAPPED` diagnostic. Each level emits a `unicode_source` tag for downstream visibility.

## Why this matters

This is the single most important component for accuracy parity with pdfminer/pypdf and the single biggest differentiator pdftract has over them. Many production PDFs ship subset fonts without `/ToUnicode` CMaps; the L3+L4 cascade recovers Unicode where competitors silently emit U+FFFD. The >90% Unicode recovery CI gate enforced by Phase 0 lives here.

## Children

- ToUnicode CMap parser (Level 1)
- Named encodings table (WinAnsi, MacRoman, MacExpert, Standard, Symbol, ZapfDingbats)
- Encoding /Differences overlay handler
- Adobe Glyph List + AGLFN compile-time phf::Map
- Font fingerprint cache (Level 3) and build-time DB pipeline
- Resolver state machine that drives all 4 levels and emits diagnostics

(Level 4 shape recognition is implemented in Phase 2.5 and consumed here.)

## Critical considerations

- INV: each result must carry a confidence in {1.0, 0.9, 0.85, 0.7, 0.0}; no in-between values.
- L1 success short-circuits ALL later levels — never re-resolve.
- L1 returning U+FFFD or empty string MUST fall through (not treated as success).
- Multi-codepoint targets (e.g. `fi` ligature -> `fi`) require returning a slice of chars, not a single char. Plumb this through the Glyph struct.
- Cache hit rate matters: same character code in same font is the common case — cache per `(font_arc_id, char_code)`.

## Acceptance criteria

- All children closed and unit-tested.
- Integration test: full chain returns expected source for each fixture in `tests/fixtures/encoding/`.
- Unicode recovery rate > 90% on the encoding corpus (CI-gated; same metric reported by Phase 0.5 acceptance script).
- `GLYPH_UNMAPPED` diagnostic emitted exactly once per (font, char_code) miss, not once per occurrence.

## References

- Plan section: Phase 2.2 Encoding Resolution (lines 1318-1370)
- docs/research/glyph-recognition-and-unicode-recovery.md

issue.description:
## Scope

Provide the 6 named-encoding character-code-to-glyph-name lookup tables required by Level 2 of the encoding fallback chain: `WinAnsiEncoding`, `MacRomanEncoding`, `MacExpertEncoding`, `StandardEncoding`, `SymbolEncoding`, `ZapfDingbatsEncoding`. Each is a `&'static [Option<&'static str>; 256]` indexed by character code, returning the glyph name (or None for unmapped slots).

## Why this matters

These tables are the bridge between character codes (what the content stream emits) and glyph names (which AGL maps to Unicode). They are baked into the binary so there is no runtime data file. WinAnsiEncoding code 0x92 -> U+2019 (right single quotation mark, mapped via glyph name `quoteright`) is the canonical test that all PDF extractors must pass — pdfminer, pypdf, mupdf all do.

## Implementation guidance

- Source: ISO 32000-1 Annex D.1-D.6 tables. Commit the 6 tables as `crates/pdftract-core/build/named-encodings.json` then emit via build.rs into static arrays.
- Layout: `pub static WIN_ANSI: [Option<&'static str>; 256] = [...]`. Slot 0x20 = `Some("space")`, 0x92 = `Some("quoteright")`.
- Provide a public enum `pub enum NamedEncoding { WinAnsi, MacRoman, MacExpert, Standard, Symbol, ZapfDingbats }` and a method `fn table(&self) -> &'static [Option<&'static str>; 256]`.
- Provide `fn from_name(s: &str) -> Option<NamedEncoding>` for `/Encoding` dispatch.

## Critical considerations

- StandardEncoding is the IMPLICIT default when a Type1 font has no `/Encoding` entry — make sure the from_name fallback handles missing entries.
- SymbolEncoding maps to Symbol-font glyph names (alpha, beta, etc.) NOT Greek Unicode codepoints; AGL handles the Symbol -> Unicode mapping separately.
- ZapfDingbatsEncoding glyph names start with `a` followed by ZapfDingbats glyph numbers (a1..a202); AGL has these.
- WinAnsi has the famous Windows-1252 punctuation range at 0x80-0x9F that StandardEncoding does NOT have.

## Acceptance criteria

- All 6 tables compile into static arrays with binary footprint < 30 KB (verify cargo bloat).
- `WIN_ANSI[0x92] == Some("quoteright")`.
- `MAC_ROMAN[0xD2] == Some("quotedblleft")` and `MAC_ROMAN[0xD3] == Some("quotedblright")`.
- `STANDARD[0x20] == Some("space")`.
- `NamedEncoding::from_name("WinAnsiEncoding") == Some(NamedEncoding::WinAnsi)`.

## References

- Plan section: Phase 2.2 Level 2 (lines 1333-1341)
- ISO 32000-1 Annex D
- Critical test: WinAnsi 0x92 -> U+2019; MacRoman 0xD2/0xD3 (lines 1366-1367)

issue.description:
## Scope

Add comprehensive rustdoc to every public item of pdftract-core. Crate-level //! doc with a worked extract example. Module-level //! doc with overview + cross-references. Item-level /// doc with type signature explanation + at least one worked example for 80% of public items. CI gate: cargo doc --no-deps -D missing-docs MUST pass green for pdftract-core; cargo doc with examples is the canonical reference users land on via docs.rs.

## Why this matters

docs.rs is the canonical Rust API reference, auto-published from rustdoc. The only way to ship a great API reference is to write great rustdoc on the source — there's no separate documentation site for the API surface. The 80% worked-example threshold is the industry norm for well-documented libraries (serde, tokio): users want copyable examples, not just signature docs.

Setting -D missing-docs prevents drift: any new public item without doc fails CI, so the API surface is always documented before merging.

## Implementation guidance

- Crate-level //! at pdftract-core/src/lib.rs:
  - Brief overview (3-5 sentences)
  - Worked extract example with full imports, error handling, output usage
  - Feature flags table (default, ocr, full-render, serve, mcp, cache, receipts, remote, decrypt, profiles)
  - Cross-reference to JSON schema URL
- Module-level //! at each pub mod:
  - Overview of what the module exports + relationship to other modules
  - Stability promises (which types are part of the stable API; which are unstable/internal)
- Item-level /// per pub fn / pub struct / pub enum / pub trait:
  - One-line summary
  - Parameter explanation (for non-obvious args)
  - Return value semantics (especially error variants)
  - At least one ```rust no_run worked example for 80% of public items
  - Cross-references to related items via [`Type`] markdown link syntax
- Feature-gated items: gate doc with #[cfg_attr(docsrs, doc(cfg(feature = \"X\")))] so docs.rs shows feature requirements
- Set #[deny(missing_docs)] at crate root once the initial pass is complete
- CI step: cargo doc --no-deps --all-features 2>&1 | grep -q 'warning:' && exit 1 || exit 0 (fail on any warning)
- docs.rs metadata in Cargo.toml: [package.metadata.docs.rs] all-features = true to ensure docs.rs renders all features

## Critical considerations

- 80% worked-example threshold is measured by a script counting pub items vs. example-containing doc comments; output a coverage report
- Examples MUST compile (rustdoc test runs ```rust blocks); use no_run for examples that need fixtures, ignore for examples that need network
- Cross-reference syntax: [`Type`] resolves to the type in scope; [`super::Type`] for parent module; [`crate::Type`] for absolute path
- Don't document private items; missing_docs lint is pub-only
- Type aliases (pub type X = Y) need doc; trait impls don't (impl-block-level doc inherits from trait)
- The cargo doc CI gate runs on every PR; warnings count as failures (forces clean docs)

## Acceptance criteria

- cargo doc --no-deps --all-features completes without warnings
- 80%+ of public items have at least one worked example (script-measured)
- docs.rs successfully renders the docs after publish (verify on a test release)
- All [`Type`] cross-references resolve (rustdoc lints these)

issue.description:
## Scope

Parse the begincodespacerange / endcodespacerange PostScript blocks in a CMap to extract the legal byte-width boundaries. Output: CodespaceRanges struct with SmallVec<[CodespaceRange; 8]> entries.

Module: crates/pdftract-core/src/cmap/codespace.rs.

## Why this matters

The codespace ranges are the SPEC-MANDATED way the PDF tells the reader where 1-byte codes stop and N-byte codes start. Most predefined CMaps (Identity-H/V, UTF-16 variants) use 1-byte ASCII + 2-byte CJK; the parser is the gate that lets the tokenizer (sibling) walk multi-byte content streams correctly.

## Implementation guidance

- Struct:
  ```rust
  pub struct CodespaceRange {
      pub lo: [u8; 4],
      pub hi: [u8; 4],
      pub width: u8,  // 1, 2, 3, or 4 bytes
  }
  pub struct CodespaceRanges {
      pub ranges: SmallVec<[CodespaceRange; 8]>,
  }
  ```
- PostScript syntax to parse:
  ```
  N begincodespacerange
    <lo1> <hi1>
    <lo2> <hi2>
    ...
  endcodespacerange
  ```
- Each entry is two hex strings of equal byte width (1, 2, 3, or 4 bytes after hex decode)
- Examples:
  - <00> <7F> → 1-byte range covering 0x00..=0x7F
  - <8000> <FFFF> → 2-byte range
  - <8140> <FEFE> → JIS lead/trail 2-byte pattern
- Tokenizer (PostScript-style): split on whitespace; recognize keywords begincodespacerange / endcodespacerange / dict; collect hex-string pairs
- Width inference: width = (hex_string.len() - 2) / 2 (subtract < and > delimiters; each byte is 2 hex chars)
- Width validation: lo.len() == hi.len(); both 1, 2, 3, or 4 bytes
- Diagnostic on malformed range: CMAP_INVALID_CODESPACE; skip the bad entry; continue

## Critical considerations

- Hex string parsing: <C0> not <c0>? Spec says case-insensitive; accept both
- Empty codespace (no begincodespacerange block) defaults to single-byte 0x00-0xFF (defensive); document
- Width-mismatch lo/hi (e.g. <00> <FFFF>) → CMAP_INVALID_CODESPACE; skip
- The CMap PostScript parser is hand-written (not a full PostScript interpreter); only recognizes the relevant keywords. Out-of-scope ops (e.g. dict definitions, name lookups) are tokenized but ignored
- Other CMap blocks (begincidrange, beginbfchar) are sibling concerns (different bead); this bead focuses on codespace ranges only

## Acceptance criteria

- Parse <00> <7F> → 1 range, width=1
- Parse <00> <7F> <8000> <FFFF> in one begincodespacerange block → 2 ranges
- Width inference: 2-char hex → width=1; 4-char hex → width=2
- Case-insensitive hex (<C0> and <c0> equivalent)
- Malformed range (mismatched lo/hi width) → diagnostic + skipped; subsequent ranges still parsed
- Empty CMap → empty ranges (defensive default applied elsewhere)
- Round-trip with Identity-H CMap fixture

## References

- Plan section: Phase 3 CMap parsing
- PDF spec 9.7.5 (CMap)
- ISO 32000-1 9.10.3.1 (Codespace ranges)
- Coordinator: pdftract-19oy (parent — parser + tokenizer)
- Sibling: multi-byte tokenizer (consumes CodespaceRanges)
Labels: cmap, parser, phase-3

issue.description:
## Scope

Expand the user-supplied PATH list into a stream of concrete file work items. For directory paths, walk via walkdir filtering to *.pdf (case-insensitive extension). For single-file paths, push directly. For https:// URLs (when remote feature is enabled), resolve via Phase 1 remote source. Emit a streaming Vec/Iterator<FileWorkItem { path: PathOrUrl, size_hint: Option<u64> }> consumed by the worker pool.

## Why this matters

walkdir is the right abstraction: streaming, handles symlinks, respects max-depth. Filtering at expansion time (vs. at worker time) means workers don't waste cycles opening .txt or .docx files. Remote URL support lets grep operate on cloud-hosted PDFs (B2, S3 web prefixes) without local downloads via the existing Phase 1 remote source pipeline.

## Implementation guidance

- Crate: walkdir = "2"
- For each PATH:
  - if str starts with "http://" or "https://": treat as URL (requires remote feature compiled in; else error)
  - if path is file: push FileWorkItem { path, size_hint: metadata.len() Some }
  - if path is dir: walkdir::WalkDir::new(path).follow_links(false).into_iter()
    - filter_entry: skip if entry.path().extension() != "pdf" (case-insensitive)
    - for each remaining entry, push FileWorkItem { path, size_hint: metadata.len() Some }
- Skip hidden directories (starting with .) by default - users can pass --hidden later if requested (not in v1)
- Skip non-PDF files silently (per acceptance criterion); diagnostic only on encrypted PDFs or parse failures
- Total bytes_total = sum of size_hint; passed to progress bar for ETA
- FileWorkItem channel: bounded MPMC (crossbeam-channel) with capacity = 4 * num_threads to avoid OOM on huge folders
- Stream production: separate producer thread feeds work items into the channel; workers pull

## Critical considerations

- Symlink loops would hang walkdir; follow_links(false) is the safe default
- Case-insensitive extension match: ".pdf" / ".PDF" / ".Pdf" all accepted
- Hidden directory skip: skip both starts-with-dot and Windows hidden-attribute directories (Windows: cross-platform compile path skips the second check)
- Path > 4096 chars: skip with diagnostic (PathBuf can hold but downstream parsers may fail)
- Encrypted PDFs are skipped in worker (not expander); expander still emits the FileWorkItem
- Remote URL feature gate: when remote feature not compiled, https:// PATH emits a clap-time error before traversal starts

## Acceptance criteria

- walkdir filters non-PDF files silently
- Single-file paths produce one FileWorkItem
- Mixed dir+file PATH list works
- https:// URL produces FileWorkItem when remote feature on; clap error when off
- Symlink loop does not hang
- bytes_total accurate sum
- Public produce_work_items(args: &GrepArgs) -> impl Iterator<Item = FileWorkItem>

## References

- Phase 1 remote source (https:// URL fetch)
- walkdir crate
- 7.8.1 (GrepArgs source)

issue.description:
## Scope

Add SLSA Level 3 build provenance generation to the release pipeline. Each release produces a `multiple.intoto.jsonl` file that names the source commit, the builder identity (the iad-ci cluster's OIDC issuer), the exact command line, and the materials consumed (source tarball hash, dependency lockfile hash). The slsa-github-generator project is GitHub-Actions-bound; we adapt the same in-toto attestation format for Argo with custom builder identity claims.

## Why this matters

SLSA L3 is the canonical supply-chain assurance bar for OSS distributions. Downstream consumers (enterprise security teams, Fortune-500 vendor reviews, vetting tools like Scorecard, Sigstore policy controllers) require this attestation to admit pdftract into approved-software lists. Without it, pdftract is shut out of compliance-gated environments.

## Implementation guidance

- The `multiple.intoto.jsonl` is an in-toto attestation in the SLSA Provenance v0.2 (or v1.0) statement format
- One statement per release; subjects are every artifact in the SHA256SUMS file (all 10 archives, 5 wheels + 1 sdist, SBOM)
- The predicate names:
  - `buildType: "https://argoproj.io/argo-workflows@v1"`
  - `builder.id: "https://iad-ci-oidc.ardenone.com/argo-workflows/pdftract-release-cascade"`
  - `invocation.parameters: {tag: "vX.Y.Z", commit: "<sha>"}`
  - `materials: [{uri: "git+https://github.com/jedarden/pdftract@<sha>", digest: {sha1: "<sha>"}}, {uri: "Cargo.lock", digest: {sha256: "<hash>"}}]`
- Generate via a dedicated Argo step that uses `slsa-framework/slsa-verifier` or a hand-rolled equivalent (the slsa-github-generator project is GHA-only; we replicate the predicate format)
- The signed in-toto bundle is attached to the GitHub Release as `multiple.intoto.jsonl`
- Discoverable via `cosign verify-attestation --type slsaprovenance ghcr.io/jedarden/pdftract:X.Y.Z` for the Docker images (the attestation is attached to the image as an OCI artifact in the same `cosign attest` step)
- For binary release artifacts, the in-toto bundle lives in the GitHub Release; verification: `slsa-verifier verify-artifact pdftract-vX.Y.Z-<triple>.tar.gz --provenance-path multiple.intoto.jsonl --source-uri github.com/jedarden/pdftract --source-tag vX.Y.Z`

## Critical considerations

- ADR-009: slsa-github-generator does NOT run on Argo natively; we replicate its predicate format. The level-3 evidence requirements are: (1) the build runs in an isolated builder we control (iad-ci pods), (2) the builder produces non-forgeable provenance (signed via cosign keyless using the cluster OIDC issuer), (3) the builder's provenance is generated INSIDE the build environment with no human intervention

Proptests verify no-panic on random bytes and valid round-trips. INV-8 maintained (no unwrap/expect/panic). See notes/pdftract-3gq3.md for verification details.
issue.description:
## Scope

Lex literal strings of the form `(...)` from the byte slice. Produces `Token::String(Vec<u8>)` of decoded bytes. Handles:

- Escape sequences: `\n` (LF), `\r` (CR), `\t` (TAB), `\b` (BS), `\f` (FF), `\\` (backslash), `\(` (left paren), `\)` (right paren)
- Octal escapes: `\ddd` where d is octal 0-7, consumes 1-3 digits greedily; out-of-range octals (e.g. `\999`) treated as the longest valid prefix + remaining digits as literal text
- Line continuation: `\<newline>` (`\\\n`, `\\\r`, `\\\r\n`) emits NO character; the bytes are consumed but produce nothing
- Nested balanced parens: `(foo (bar) baz)` -> bytes `foo (bar) baz`. The lexer tracks paren depth; only the matching outer `)` terminates the string

## Implementation guidance

- State machine: enter at byte AFTER the opening `(`; maintain `depth: usize = 1`
- On `(` (unescaped): `depth += 1`; emit as literal byte 0x28
- On `)` (unescaped): `depth -= 1`; if `depth == 0`, terminate; otherwise emit as literal byte 0x29
- On `\\`: read next byte; dispatch on `\n`/`\r`/`\t`/`\b`/`\f`/`\\`/`\(`/`\)`/digit/newline
- Octal: after backslash, if next byte is `0-7`, consume up to 3 octal digits, compute value `(d1*64 + d2*8 + d3)`, push as one byte. The value MAY exceed 255 (e.g. `\401` = decimal 257); truncate via `(value & 0xFF)` per spec footnote and emit `STRUCT_INVALID_OCTAL` if `value > 255`
- Line continuation: backslash followed by `\n`, `\r`, or `\r\n` -- consume and emit nothing
- Unknown escape (e.g. `\q`): emit the escaped byte literally (i.e. `q`), no diagnostic (PDF spec 7.3.4.2 explicitly permits this)
- EOF before matching `)`: emit `STRUCT_UNTERMINATED_STRING` diagnostic, return `Token::String` of bytes collected so far

## Critical considerations

- Critical test from plan: `(foo (bar) baz)` -> bytes `foo (bar) baz` (with the spaces and inner parens preserved). Verify paren-depth bookkeeping doesn't double-count
- Critical test: `(abc\101)` -> bytes `abcA` (octal 101 = 65 = ASCII A)
- Critical test: octal escape consumes UP TO 3 digits — `(abc\1019)` is `abcA9`, not `ab(invalid octal 1019)`; the lexer must NOT greedily consume non-octal digits as part of the octal escape
- Critical test: `(abc\10A)` -> bytes `abc\x08A` (only 2 octal digits consumed because `A` is not octal)
- Critical test: line continuation `(abc\<LF>def)` -> bytes `abcdef`. Verify both `\r`, `\n`, and `\r\n` variants work
- Per spec 7.3.4.2: bare `\r` inside string is converted to `\n` (line ending normalization). Implementations vary; pdftract should NORMALIZE (spec-compliant) but emit no diagnostic
- Out-of-range octals: spec says high-order overflow is silently truncated; emit `STRUCT_INVALID_OCTAL` diagnostic as a courtesy but do not fail
- Strings can be very long (multi-MB content streams are sometimes wrapped in strings); use `Vec::with_capacity(64)` initially and grow naturally

## Acceptance criteria

- All Critical tests pass:
  - `(foo (bar) baz)` -> `b"foo (bar) baz"`
  - `(abc\101)` -> `b"abcA"`
  - `(abc\10A)` -> `b"abc\x08A"`
  - `(abc\<LF>def)` -> `b"abcdef"`
  - `(unterminated` -> partial bytes + `STRUCT_UNTERMINATED_STRING` diagnostic
- proptest property: random byte sequences starting with `(` never panic
- proptest property: any valid `(...)` round-trips through the lexer to produce a non-empty `Token::String`
- INV-8 maintained

## References

- Plan section: Phase 1.1 Lexer, line 1032 (string literals with escapes); line 1045 (critical tests for balanced parens, octal at end of string)
- PDF spec 7.3.4.2 (Literal Strings)
- INV-8
issue.title: Implement PDF string literal lexer with octal escapes and balanced parens

issue.description:
## Scope

Demonstrate end-to-end CI health by:

1. Implementing the workflow `exitHandler` that posts run summary to the PR (via the `argo-workflows-pr-status` operator already running on iad-ci)
2. Adding a `setup` step at the front of the DAG that uploads a workflow-metadata artifact (commit SHA, ref, parameter values, container image digests for each step) so failures are reproducible
3. Running a final green-run smoke test against a sample PR to demonstrate every step is reachable and reports correctly

## Why this matters

Phase 0 closes only when a green CI run on a sample PR demonstrates all the steps (build, test, clippy, bloat, audit, deny, MSRV, regression corpus, Tier 4 benchmarks) execute and report results. Observability glue is what surfaces this state to the developer reviewing the PR. Without it, the workflow can succeed silently and developers wouldn't know which step covered what.

## Implementation guidance

- exitHandler template name: `report-status`
- exitHandler payload: JSON `{commit_sha, ref, workflow_phase, started_at, duration_seconds, step_outcomes: {step_name: phase}, artifacts: [name]}` posted to `https://argo-pr-status.argo-workflows.svc.cluster.local/v1/report`
- The pr-status operator is already deployed in iad-ci and consumes this format; it transforms the payload into a GitHub Check Run on the PR's commit
- setup step: an `init-container` style preamble that captures `git rev-parse HEAD`, `git remote get-url origin`, and the workflow.parameters dump, writing them to `workflow-metadata.json`
- The smoke-test PR is on a throwaway branch `pdftract-ci-smoke-<date>`; the PR's commit message identifies it as a smoke test so reviewers don't try to merge it

## Critical considerations

- The pr-status operator runs as a NodePort service inside the iad-ci cluster; the exitHandler MUST hit the cluster-local DNS, not a public URL (the public URL would route through Tailscale and add 200+ ms latency per report)
- Step outcomes for parallel matrices (build-matrix, quality-matrix, test-matrix, bench-matrix) must expand into per-item outcomes so the PR check shows e.g. "build-matrix:x86_64-unknown-linux-musl" and "build-matrix:aarch64-apple-darwin" separately. Single-row aggregation is too coarse for debugging
- The smoke-test PR must NOT be auto-merged; remember to mark it with `do-not-merge` label after demonstrating the green run
- Workflow-metadata artifact size is small (<1 KB); include a `pdftract-ci-template-sha` field with the YAML's commit SHA so it's clear which template version ran each workflow
- Provide a dashboard link in the exitHandler payload pointing to the Argo UI workflow view: `https://argo-ci.ardenone.com/workflows/argo-workflows/{{workflow.name}}` — clickable from the PR check page

## Acceptance criteria

- exitHandler posts to pr-status operator on every workflow completion (success or failure)
- A sample PR receives 1 GitHub Check per step (or per matrix item) showing pass/fail
- `workflow-metadata.json` artifact is uploaded by every workflow and inspectable from the Argo UI
- A deliberate failure in (e.g.) the clippy step surfaces as a failing GitHub Check with the step name visible in the PR's check list
- The smoke-test PR demonstrates a fully green run — all 9 prior Phase 0 beads' steps appear in the Argo UI as Succeeded

## References

- Plan section: Phase 0, line 1013 (Phase 0 must be complete before Phase 1 code review)
- Argo UI: `https://argo-ci.ardenone.com`
- iad-ci sibling operator: `argo-workflows-pr-status` (already deployed)

issue.description:
## Scope

Apply the 50 MB decoded-size cap: if attachment content > 50 * 1024 * 1024 bytes, emit metadata only with data: null and truncated: true. Otherwise, base64-encode the content using the standard RFC 4648 alphabet (with padding, no line breaks) into the data field. Wire the resulting Vec<Attachment> to the document-level /attachments JSON path. Update docs/schema/v1.0/pdftract.schema.json to declare data with contentEncoding: base64.

## Why this matters

The 50 MB cap defends against pathological PDFs that pack hundreds of megabytes of attachments and would otherwise produce gigabyte-scale JSON output. Standard base64 with padding ensures round-trip correctness (PyO3, Python's base64.b64decode, all sinks). The schema's contentEncoding declaration tells JSON Schema validators (and downstream code-gen tooling) that data is base64-encoded bytes, not arbitrary text.

## Implementation guidance

- Crate: base64 = "0.22" with standard alphabet config
- Hard-coded threshold const ATTACHMENT_MAX_DECODED_BYTES: usize = 50 * 1024 * 1024
- For each AttachmentBuilder { content: Vec<u8>, ... }:
  - if content.len() > 50 MB: emit Attachment { name, description, mime_type, size: Some(content.len() as u64), created, modified, checksum_md5, data: None, truncated: true }
  - else: encode content via base64::engine::general_purpose::STANDARD.encode(&content) -> String; emit data: Some(b64), truncated: false
- size is always populated (whether truncated or not)
- Output: /attachments: Vec<Attachment> at document root; always emit array (empty when none)
- Schema: attachment.data: { type: ["string", "null"], contentEncoding: "base64" }; attachment.truncated: { type: "boolean" }; attachment.size: { type: ["integer", "null"], minimum: 0 }
- Schema round-trip test: synthetic attachment with 10-byte content; base64 -> validate -> decode -> bytes equal
- CLI --text mode: do NOT include attachments per plan; only JSON/PyO3/MCP sinks include them
- PyO3: Attachment.data is bytes (PyO3 auto-decodes base64 string)

## Critical considerations

- Standard base64 alphabet uses '+' and '/' (NOT urlsafe variants) - this matches RFC 4648 §4
- Padding is REQUIRED ('=' chars) - omitting padding breaks Python base64.b64decode strict mode
- No line breaks in the base64 string - JSON does not require them and they bloat output
- truncated: true forces data: null even if content was zero-byte (preserve the truncation flag's meaning)
- size on truncated attachments is the ORIGINAL decoded size (so users know what was skipped)
- The 50 MB threshold is at the implementation level; not user-configurable in v1 (future ExtractionOptions.attachment_max_bytes)

## Acceptance criteria

- All other 7.5.x sub-tasks closed; this depends on them
- Critical test (from plan): attachment > 50 MB -> truncated: true, data: null, metadata present
- Round-trip test: small attachment -> base64 -> decode -> bytes equal
- Schema test: docs/schema/v1.0/pdftract.schema.json validates attachment with contentEncoding: base64
- /attachments array always emitted (empty when no attachments)
- CLI --text mode excludes attachments; JSON sink includes them
- PyO3 Attachment.data is bytes

## References

- Plan section: 7.5 line 2640 (50 MB size limit + base64 alphabet + JSON Schema contentEncoding + PyO3 bytes conversion + CLI --text exclusion)
- docs/schema/v1.0/pdftract.schema.json
- 7.5.1, 7.5.2 (input pipeline)
- INV: stable taxonomy + always-emit-array
- Phase 6.1 JSON sink, 6.3 PyO3 binding, 6.5 text sink
issue.title: 7.5.3: 50 MB size limit + base64 encoding + attachments JSON schema

## Scope

Wire the JSON Schema validator into the test suite + CI. Loads docs/schema/v1.0/pdftract.schema.json, runs an extraction on each fixture in tests/fixtures/, validates the output JSON against the schema. Fails CI on schema-validation errors. A schema without a validator is documentation. The validator catches regressions: any code change that emits a field not in the schema, or omits a required one, fails CI. Without it, drift accumulates and downstream clients break.

Created AttachmentBuilder struct with name, description, mime_type, size, created, modified, checksum_md5, content, and truncated fields. Added extract_one() function that resolves Filespec, extracts metadata (/UF preferred over /F, /Desc optional, /Subtype from stream dict), parses PDF dates to ISO 8601, hex-encodes MD5 checksums, and decodes stream data through Phase 1 filter pipeline with 50 MB size limit enforcement. Unit tests pass for string decoding (UTF-16BE BOM, PDFDocEncoding), date parsing, and filename extraction. Verification note: notes/pdftract-3lir.md. Commit: bd91f7d.
issue.description:
## Scope

For each FilespecRef from 7.5.1, resolve the /Filespec dict and extract: /F (system-independent filename), /UF (Unicode filename, prefer when present), /Desc (description), /EF /F (embedded file stream ref). Decode the stream via Phase 1 filters. Extract from stream dict: /Subtype (MIME type), /Params /Size, /Params /CreationDate, /Params /ModDate, /Params /CheckSum (binary MD5 -> hex). Emit AttachmentBuilder { name, description, mime_type, size, created, modified, checksum_md5, content: Vec<u8> }.

## Why this matters

Filename, MIME, and dates are what users see; the decoded content is what their pipelines consume. Hex-encoding the MD5 makes the checksum human-comparable; raw binary in JSON is awkward. /UF over /F is essential for international filenames (Cyrillic, CJK, accented Latin).

## Implementation guidance

- /Filespec /F: PdfString in PDFDocEncoding (legacy ASCII filename)
- /Filespec /UF: PdfString in UTF-16BE BOM-prefixed or UTF-8 (preferred when present)
- /Filespec /Desc: PdfString -> String (Optional)
- /Filespec /EF: dict with /F (or /UF / /DOS / /Mac / /Unix variants) - the embedded file stream
- Resolve /EF /F -> Stream object; apply all stream filters via Phase 1 decoder; result is Vec<u8>
- Stream dict /Subtype: PdfName -> String, e.g. "application/pdf", "image/png", "text/xml"
- Stream dict /Params (a dict): /Size (int, original byte size before any filters), /CreationDate (PdfString date), /ModDate (PdfString date), /CheckSum (PdfString binary - 16-byte MD5 raw)
- Hex-encode /CheckSum as 32-char lowercase: "01ab..."
- Date parsing: reuse 7.3.2 PDF-date-to-ISO-8601 parser
- Filename precedence: /UF if present, else /F
- If /Desc absent, description = None (not "")

## Critical considerations

- Decoded content may exceed available memory on very large attachments - read into Vec<u8> with size pre-check; abort to data: null + truncated: true at 50 MB (handled in 7.5.3)
- /Subtype absent: emit mime_type: None; do NOT guess from filename extension
- /CheckSum may have a different format (16-byte SHA1 in legacy PDFs); document that we only hex-encode the raw bytes and trust the caller's known format
- Stream filter pipeline includes FlateDecode, LZWDecode, ASCII85Decode, ASCIIHexDecode, RunLengthDecode, CCITTFaxDecode (rare for attachments), DCTDecode (rare)
- Encrypted stream that fails to decrypt: emit diagnostic, content empty, mime_type still surfaced from metadata
- /F vs /UF: /F may not be valid UTF-8; decode as PDFDocEncoding then convert

## Acceptance criteria

3. **proptest harness** in `tests/proptest/document_model.rs`:
   - prop_doc_never_panics: arbitrary PDF byte sequences fed to Document::open never panic
   - prop_encryption_roundtrip: encrypted documents with known password produce the same Document as their unencrypted equivalents (modulo metadata)
   - prop_inheritance_consistent: synthetic /Pages trees with varying depth always produce the right per-page MediaBox

## Why this matters

The document model integrates xref, object parser, ObjStm, stream decoder (for /Metadata XMP), AND encryption — so its test corpus exercises Phase 1.1-1.5 end-to-end. Without the corpus, regressions in any of those layers may not surface until much later in development.

## Implementation guidance

- Fixture generation tools: qpdf (for encryption, linearization), Adobe Acrobat (for tagged PDFs with bookmarks), exiftool (for XMP metadata injection)
- The encrypted fixtures need ACTUAL known plaintext content; use a 1-page hello-world PDF as the base, then encrypt with the appropriate algorithm

- The encrypted fixtures' passwords are NOT secret (they're test fixtures); document this clearly in a README under fixtures/

- The ocg_default_off fixture is essential for Phase 3 verification — Phase 3 reads the OcProperties map produced by this bead's code
- The inheritance fixtures (grandparent + missing) verify the page tree walker's accumulation; without these, regressions silently break content extraction on EVERY page that relies on inherited MediaBox
- Performance: full document open of a 100-page PDF should complete within 200 ms (mmap + parse + flatten); large encrypted files may take longer due to per-stream decryption
- proptest: arbitrary bytes fed to Document::open MUST produce either a Document or a structured Err; never a panic. This is the keystone INV-8 test

## Scope

Implement hover tooltips in the inspector frontend. Hovering any span surfaces a tooltip box within 50 ms showing text/font/confidence/bbox/block ref/MCID/reading-idx. Implemented in app.js with a single shared tooltip div, CSS positioning.

Tooltips are the moment-to-moment debugging interaction; hovering answers \"what does pdftract think THIS glyph is?\" in one mouse motion. Without tooltips, users must click into the JSON tree (slower) or read source.

## Implementation guidance

- HTML: single <div id=\"tooltip\"> in the inspector page; initially hidden (display: none)

    - Populate tooltip body with formatted HTML

  - On mouseleave: hide
- 50 ms appearance target: no debouncing; immediate; CSS transition-duration 0; tooltip display: block on mouseenter
- Tooltip auto-repositions if cursor near viewport edge (avoid clipping)

issue.close_reason: Implemented StreamDecoder trait, filter pipeline orchestrator, and max_decompress_bytes bomb limit. Commit 2ee67e5. All acceptance criteria PASS: single/array filter handling, /DecodeParms pairing, filter array ordering [/ASCII85Decode /FlateDecode], abbreviation normalization, 2 GB bomb limit with STREAM_BOMB diagnostic, unknown filter passthrough with STRUCT_UNKNOWN_FILTER, INV-8 maintained. 183 tests pass. Verification note at notes/pdftract-3nnqy.md
issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the orchestration layer for stream decoding:

- `StreamDecoder` trait: `decode(&self, input: &[u8], params: Option<&PdfDict>) -> Result<Vec<u8>, FilterError>`
- Per-filter implementations register via a static table keyed by filter name (`/FlateDecode` -> FlateDecoder, etc.)
- `decode_stream(stream: &PdfStream, source: &dyn PdfSource, opts: &ExtractionOptions, doc_decompress_counter: &mut u64) -> Vec<u8>`:
  1. Reads raw bytes from source at stream.offset of length stream.len_hint (or scans for endstream if hint is None)
  2. Resolves /Filter (single name or array) and /DecodeParms (single dict or array)
  3. Iterates filters in order, calling each filter's decode()
  4. Tracks cumulative output bytes against opts.max_decompress_bytes (default 2 GB)
  5. If limit exceeded: STREAM_BOMB diagnostic, return partial bytes
- ExtractionOptions struct: add `max_decompress_bytes: u64` field (default 2 * 1024_u64.pow(3) = 2 GB)

## Implementation guidance

- Filter dispatch: `static FILTER_TABLE: phf::Map<&'static str, fn() -> Box<dyn StreamDecoder>>` for compile-time lookup (use `phf` crate)
- Alternative: simple `match` on filter name; either is fine. `match` is simpler and faster
- /Filter forms:
  - Name: `/Filter /FlateDecode` -> single filter
  - Array: `/Filter [/ASCII85Decode /FlateDecode]` -> multiple filters in order
  - Missing: stream is raw (no filters); return bytes as-is
- /DecodeParms parallel structure: name -> single dict; array -> array of dicts (or nulls for filters with no params)
- Filter abbreviations per PDF spec 7.4.2 Table 6: /A85 = /ASCII85Decode, /AHx = /ASCIIHexDecode, /CCF = /CCITTFaxDecode, /Fl = /FlateDecode, /LZW = /LZWDecode, /RL = /RunLengthDecode, /DCT = /DCTDecode. Normalize abbreviations to full names at dispatch time
- doc_decompress_counter: a `&mut u64` passed through every decode; each filter's output adds to it; when total > opts.max_decompress_bytes, decoding stops mid-stream with STREAM_BOMB diagnostic
- Per-stream check ALSO required: each individual stream's output must not exceed max_decompress_bytes (otherwise a single 3 GB stream would bypass the per-doc check)

## Critical considerations

- Critical test from plan: filter array [/ASCII85Decode /FlateDecode] — apply ASCII85 first then Flate on its output
- The /DecodeParms array-of-dicts has the same length as the /Filter array; mismatched length emits STRUCT_INVALID_FILTER_PARAMS and uses defaults for missing entries
- Stream length: stream.len_hint is the /Length value from the dict; if None (because /Length was an indirect ref or missing), scan for `endstream` keyword starting at stream.offset
- The endstream-scan fallback is expensive (potentially scanning megabytes); cache the result on PdfStream
- The bomb limit applies BEFORE filter output is materialized: i.e. the FlateDecode wrapper reads decoded bytes incrementally and checks the counter every 64 KB chunk; on exceeded, it truncates and returns partial bytes
- INV-8: any error inside a filter (corrupt data, EOF mid-stream) returns Ok(partial_bytes) + diagnostic, NOT Err — Err is only for "couldn't even start decoding" (e.g. unknown filter)
- Unknown filter: STRUCT_UNKNOWN_FILTER, return raw bytes (passthrough); downstream consumers may still extract usable content
- The filter pipeline must be deterministic: same input + same params -> byte-identical output (for INV-3 fingerprint stability)

## Acceptance criteria

- decode_stream() handles single-filter and array-filter cases
- /DecodeParms array correctly paired with /Filter array
- Critical test: [/ASCII85Decode /FlateDecode] applies filters in correct order
- Filter abbreviations normalized: /A85 routes to ASCII85Decode
- 2 GB bomb limit: a fixture with FlateDecode bomb (small input expanding to 3 GB) returns ~2 GB + STREAM_BOMB diagnostic, completes within 5 sec
- Unknown filter: STRUCT_UNKNOWN_FILTER, raw bytes returned
- INV-8 maintained

## References

- Plan section: Phase 1.5 line 1152 (filter pipeline); line 1154 (decompression limit)
- EC-10 (FlateDecode bomb)
- INV-8
- INV-3 (deterministic decoding for fingerprint stability)
issue.title: Implement StreamDecoder trait, filter pipeline orchestrator, and max_decompress_bytes bomb limit
