## Scope

Implement the borderless table detector for pages without ruling lines. Examine span x0 positions across the page; if 3+ lines share identical x0 values (within 2 pt tolerance) for multiple column groups, and 3+ rows are aligned, treat as a candidate table. Output Vec<GridCandidate> in the same shape as 7.2.1.

## Why this matters

Borderless tables are common in modern document design: scientific papers, slide decks exported to PDF, board reports. Without this detector, these tables emit as ragged paragraphs and lose all column structure. Pdftract's positioning vs. competitors depends on getting borderless detection right - pdfplumber and pdfminer score poorly here.

## Implementation guidance

- Run only when 7.2.1 returned no GridCandidate covering a region (line-based wins)
- Collect span x0 positions for all text on a page; bucket by x0 (tolerance 2.0 pt)
- A bucket is a "column candidate" if it has 3+ spans on different y positions
- A row candidate is a y position where >= 2 column candidates have spans
- Confirm table: 3+ row candidates AND 3+ column candidates, all within a contiguous y range with no vertical gap > 100 pt
- Construct GridCandidate { bbox, row_ys, col_xs, segments: vec![] } with empty segments (no rules detected)
- Reject candidates where row spans suggest single-column paragraph reflow (test: if any column candidate's spans are all on consecutive lines without aligned neighbours in any other column candidate, reject that column)

## Critical considerations

- Threshold is intentionally conservative (3+ rows AND 3+ aligned x0 groups) to avoid false positives on left-aligned text
- Hyperlinks/inline-styled spans get their OWN x0 position (per-span) - do not pre-merge spans into lines before the alignment check
- Vertical gap rule (> 100 pt = end of table) prevents merging two separate tables that share x0 alignment
- Borderless detection runs after line-based; if line-based grid covers a region, do not re-detect there
- Output bbox is the convex hull of the contributing spans, NOT page-wide

## Acceptance criteria

- Critical test (from plan): borderless two-column table detected via alignment heuristic
- Unit tests: paragraph rejected; one-row pseudo-table rejected; 3-row 3-column borderless table accepted; vertical-gap test
- Public TableDetector::detect_borderless(&PageContext) -> Vec<GridCandidate>
- Performance: < 10 ms on 5000-span page

## References

- Plan section: 7.2 line 2572 (borderless detection)
- docs/research/table-structure-reconstruction.md
- 7.2.1 line-based detection (skipped regions)
- 7.2.3 cell content assignment (consumer)
issue.title: 7.2.2: Borderless table detection (x0-aligned span heuristic)

issue.close_reason: Implemented bead chain walker with cycle detection + page/rect resolution. All 28 tests pass. See commit 3ac4721 and notes/pdftract-3o9fu.md.
issue.description:
## Scope

For each ThreadHeader from 7.7.1, walk the bead chain starting at /F. Follow /N (next bead) links; terminate when /N points back to the first bead (legitimate circular end). Detect malformed chains (cycles that don't return to first) and abort with diagnostic. For each bead, extract /P (page ref) and /R (rect on page); convert page ref to 0-indexed page_index via a precomputed ref->index map. Emit Vec<Bead { page_index, rect }> ordered along the chain.

## Why this matters

Chain walking is the only way to follow article flow across multi-column and multi-page layouts. The cycle-detection contract (legitimate end vs. malformed loop) prevents pathological PDFs from causing infinite loops. The page-ref-to-index lookup is the bridge between PDF's indirect-ref world and pdftract's 0-indexed page output model.

## Implementation guidance

- Precompute page_ref_to_index: HashMap<ObjRef, usize> from document.pages once, reuse for all threads
- For each ThreadHeader.first_bead_ref:
  - current = first_bead_ref
  - visited: HashSet<ObjRef> = {first_bead_ref}
  - loop:
    - resolve current; extract /P (page ref), /R (rect [f32;4])
    - page_index = page_ref_to_index.get(P)?; if None -> diagnostic + skip bead
    - rect: validate 4 floats; if shape invalid -> diagnostic + skip
    - push Bead { page_index, rect }
    - next = current.get(/N)
    - if next == first_bead_ref -> end (legitimate circular)
    - if next in visited -> diagnostic "malformed_bead_cycle" + break
    - if next absent -> diagnostic "missing_next_bead" + break
    - visited.insert(next); current = next
- Maximum iterations cap: 10000 beads per thread as a safety net (real-world threads have < 1000)
- Output: Vec<Bead> in chain order; combined with ThreadHeader -> Thread { header_fields, beads }
- Some legacy PDFs use /Pg instead of /P for the page reference; tolerate both

## Critical considerations

- Cycle detection is required (critical test in plan)
- The "circular termination" is the legitimate end condition - not a bug
- Iteration cap of 10000 prevents both real and pathological infinite walks
- /R rect is in PDF user space, ORIGIN BOTTOM-LEFT - do not flip y to image space
- Page ref may point to a page outside the document range (corrupt PDF) - emit diagnostic + skip
- Some beads have a /T back-link to the thread - useful for validation; not required to walk

## Acceptance criteria

- Critical test (from plan): two article threads - both reconstructed with correct bead order and page references
- Critical test: bead /R rect correctly resolved to PDF user-space coordinates for the referenced page
- Critical test: circular bead chain termination - walk stops without infinite loop
- Unit tests: pathological cycle (diagnostic), missing /N (diagnostic), missing /P (skip bead), /Pg fallback
- Public threads::walk_beads(ThreadHeader, &Document) -> Vec<Bead>
- Iteration cap honoured (synthetic 20000-bead test passes with diagnostic)

## References

- Plan section: 7.7 lines 2684-2685 (chain walk + termination)
- PDF 1.7 spec 12.4.3 Articles (bead dict)
- 7.7.1 (ThreadHeader input)
- 7.7.3 (output JSON consumer)
issue.title: 7.7.2: Bead chain walker with cycle detection + page/rect resolution

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement pdftract inspect FILE.pdf [--port PORT] [--bind ADDR] [--no-open] - a self-contained web UI that renders each page as inline SVG with extracted spans, blocks, columns, and reading-order arrows overlaid. 8 toggleable overlay layers (spans, blocks, columns, reading order, confidence heatmap, OCR regions, MCID, anchors). Hover tooltips on each span. Search filter, keyboard navigation, comparison mode --compare. Frontend bundle compiled into binary via include_bytes!, < 80 KB stripped+gzipped. Separate subcommand from serve (per requirement). Default --port 7676 --bind 127.0.0.1 (loopback); non-loopback bind requires --auth-token. axum HTTP server. SVG rendering via glyph outlines from ttf-parser - no rasterization, no pdfium dep in default features.

## Why this matters

The inspector is the trust-and-debugging tool that separates serious from toy extractors. When pdftract produces a confidence value or a column boundary, the user must be able to SEE why - the inspector is that "why" surfaced as overlays. Inspector is critical for diagnosing edge cases ("this scientific paper's reading order is wrong"), validating tagged-PDF claims ("did the StructTree actually drive ordering?"), and onboarding new users who need to build mental models. Self-contained binary (frontend bundled) means inspect runs in one command on any machine with the binary - no install steps, no separate web server.

## Implementation guidance

- Feature flag: inspect (depends on serve); when off, subcommand returns "feature not compiled in"
- Crates: reuses axum + tokio from serve; ttf-parser already in Phase 2; new dep: none (frontend bundled via include_bytes!)
- Subcommand: pdftract inspect FILE.pdf [--port PORT] [--bind ADDR] [--no-open] [--auth-token TOKEN] [--compare OTHER.pdf]
- Launch behavior:
  1. Run full Phase 1-6 extraction on FILE.pdf
  2. Cache result in memory (no disk artifacts)
  3. Start axum on --bind :--port
  4. Open default browser to http://<bind>:<port>/ (suppressed by --no-open)
- HTTP endpoints:
  - GET / -> served HTML page (bundled)
  - GET /static/<asset> -> bundled CSS/JS (include_bytes!)
  - GET /api/document -> document metadata JSON
  - GET /api/page/<i> -> page JSON (spans, blocks, columns, reading_order, ...)
  - GET /api/page/<i>/svg -> SVG render of page i
  - GET /api/page/<i>/thumbnail -> small SVG for sidebar
  - GET /api/raster/<i>.png -> base64 PNG for Scanned pages (no vector outlines)
  - GET /api/search?q=... -> matching spans (lightweight; client also does in-browser search)
- Frontend: vanilla HTML + CSS + JS (no framework); bundle stripped+gzipped < 80 KB
- Page render: server-side SVG construction from extraction result; glyph paths via ttf-parser; vector paths from content stream operators (m/l/re)
- Overlay layers: SVG groups with class names; toggled via CSS display none (no re-render)
- Hover tooltips: client-side; hover any span -> show metadata box (text, font, confidence, bbox, block ref, MCID, reading idx)
- Search: top-bar input filters spans by text substring; matched spans get bright outline; Enter cycles
- Keyboard: left/right page nav; / focus search; 1-8 toggle overlay layers
- URL fragment: #page=N for shareable page links
- Comparison mode (--compare OTHER.pdf): also load OTHER.pdf; render both side-by-side; useful for diffing extraction-algorithm changes

## Critical considerations

- Inspector is a separate subcommand, NOT a serve-mode feature - per user requirement
- Loopback default (127.0.0.1); non-loopback bind requires --auth-token per Phase 6.7 MCP HTTP-mode contract
- SVG rendering via ttf-parser glyph outlines - no rasterization, no pdfium - keeps binary slim
- Scanned pages: source raster image embedded as base64 PNG in SVG
- Frontend bundle < 80 KB stripped+gzipped - hard target; check in CI via wc -c on the gzipped bundle
- 8 overlay layers must toggle independently via CSS only (no re-render)
- localStorage persists overlay state across reloads
- --no-open suppresses xdg-open/open/cmd /c start - needed for CI/headless smoke tests
- Inspector is single-document-per-process (cache one document in memory); for multi-doc use serve
- All endpoints use bearer auth when --auth-token set; loopback bind = auth optional

## Acceptance criteria

- All Phase 7.9 child task beads closed
- Critical test (from plan): launch on sample PDF, GET / returns 200 with valid HTML
- Critical test: all eight layer toggles produce DOM changes (verified via headless-browser test)
- Critical test: keyboard shortcuts trigger bound actions
- Critical test: search filter narrows visible spans correctly
- Critical test: --no-open prevents OS browser launcher
- Critical test: scanned PDF - raster background embedded as base64 PNG; OCR confidence overlays render
- 100-page PDF opens and renders first page within 2 seconds
- Hover tooltip appears within 50 ms of mouse enter
- Frontend bundle < 80 KB stripped+gzipped
- Works in current Chrome, Firefox, Safari (verified via headless-browser smoke tests in CI)
- Binary size budget: ocr,serve,inspect features <= 12.5 MB

issue.description:
## Scope

Coordinator for sub-phase 2.1: load and classify a PDF font from its resource dictionary, normalize subtype handling (Type1, Type1 Standard 14, TrueType, Type0 composite, CIDFontType0/2, Type3, OpenType CFF), strip the 6-uppercase-letter subset prefix from the BaseFont name, and resolve `/CIDToGIDMap` (Identity name OR FlateDecode'd 2-byte big-endian GID stream). Delivers a `Font` value usable by every later step in Phase 2 (encoding resolution, CJK, Type 3, shape DB) and Phase 3 (content stream execution).

## Why this matters

Every glyph processed downstream needs (a) a font object with correct metrics and (b) a glyph-id lookup function. Misclassifying a CIDFontType2 as TrueType, or forgetting to strip a subset prefix, breaks Standard-14 metric lookups and AGL fallbacks for the rest of the pipeline. This sub-phase is the entry point of the font module and must be rock-solid before encoding resolution can be implemented.

## Children

- Font subtype classifier and BaseFont prefix stripper
- Standard 14 font registry (hardcoded metrics)
- Embedded font program loader (ttf-parser / owned_ttf_parser wiring)
- Type 0 composite font + descendant CIDFont loader
- CIDToGIDMap resolver (Identity name and stream form)

## Critical considerations

- The 6-uppercase-letter prefix is EXACTLY 6 capital ASCII letters followed by `+` (regex `^[A-Z]{6}\+`). Strip before any Standard-14 lookup; preserve original on the Font struct for diagnostics.
- CIDFontType2 with `/CIDToGIDMap` as a stream: array length is `2 * (max_cid + 1)` bytes, BIG-ENDIAN u16. Index by CID.
- OpenType CFF fonts live in `/FontFile3` with subtype `/OpenType`; metrics via ttf-parser's CFF support. Do not assume hhea/hmtx layout for these.
- Type 3 font program lives in `/CharProcs` (not a stream); deferred to Phase 2.4 children.
- Standard 14 fonts may have NO `/FontFile*` entry at all; do not error on missing font program for these.

## Acceptance criteria

- All children closed; classifier returns one of {Type1, Type1Std14, TrueType, Type0, CIDFontType0, CIDFontType2, Type3, OpenTypeCFF}.
- Subset prefix `ABCDEF+Times-Roman` strips to `Times-Roman` for Std-14 lookup.
- CIDFontType2 with `/CIDToGIDMap /Identity`: GID == CID.
- CIDFontType2 with stream CIDToGIDMap: 2-byte big-endian decode verified against a fixture.
- Module unit tests in `crates/pdftract-core/src/font/` pass; no unwrap/expect on resource dict access.

## References

- Plan section: Phase 2.1 Font Type Detection (lines 1290-1316)
- ADR: subset prefix handling and CIDToGIDMap decoding

issue.description:
## Scope

For each non-Link annotation routed by 7.6.1, build an Annotation struct with subtype-specific extras. Subtypes in scope: Highlight, Stamp, FreeText, Text (called Note in plan), Squiggly, StrikeOut, Underline, Caret, Ink, Polygon, PolyLine, Line, Circle, Square, FileAttachment, Sound, Movie, Screen, PrinterMark, TrapNet, Watermark, 3D, Redact. Output: page-level Vec<Annotation>.

## Why this matters

Annotations carry the human commentary, redlines, and stamps that drive legal-review, regulatory-filing, and academic-peer-review workflows. Extracting them with structured fields (subtype, rect, author, modified, comment text, color) lets downstream tools build searchable annotation indexes, render review-comment sidebars, or replay redlines onto re-rendered output.

## Implementation guidance

- Annotation struct: subtype, rect, contents (comment text), author, modified (ISO 8601), color (Vec<f32>), opacity, flags, name_id, subject + subtype-specific fields
- Highlight / Squiggly / StrikeOut / Underline: also extract /QuadPoints (8*N floats, N quads); quads field as Vec<[f32;8]>
- Stamp: also extract /Name (icon name, e.g. "Approved", "Confidential", "Draft"); name field as Option<String>
- FreeText: also extract /DA (default appearance string) - the styling for the free-text box; da: Option<String>
- Text (sticky note): also extract /Open (bool, whether note is open by default), /State, /StateModel
- Ink: also extract /InkList (array of stroke point arrays); strokes: Vec<Vec<[f32;2]>>
- Line: /L (4 floats: [x1, y1, x2, y2]); line_endpoints: Option<[f32;4]>
- Polygon / PolyLine: /Vertices (Vec<f32> as pairs); vertices: Vec<[f32;2]>
- FileAttachment: /FS (Filespec ref) - cross-reference with 7.5 attachments output
- Skip Widget, Popup at this point (already filtered in 7.6.1)
- All optional sub-fields default to None when absent
- Preserve original /Subtype name as-is in subtype field (do not normalise to lowercase; keep "Highlight" exactly)

## Critical considerations

- INV: subtype taxonomy includes the full set above + "Other" for unknown - new types append, no rename
- /QuadPoints: PDF spec defines as (x1,y1, x2,y2, x3,y3, x4,y4) per quad, with vertices in reading-order; do not reorder
- Color array length varies by color space (1, 3, or 4); preserve length
- /Contents may be very long for FreeText (paragraph-length notes); no truncation
- /F annotation flags include Invisible, Hidden, Print, NoZoom, NoRotate, NoView, ReadOnly, Locked, ToggleNoView, LockedContents - emit as u32 for caller to interpret
- Subtypes not enumerated above (rare in practice) emit with subtype = original name and no subtype-specific extras; emit diagnostic "unhandled_annotation_subtype"

## Acceptance criteria

- Critical test (from plan): page with Highlight and Note - both in page-level annotations with correct subtypes
- Critical test: annotation with no /Contents -> contents: None (null in JSON)
- Unit tests: Highlight with QuadPoints, Stamp with /Name "Approved", FreeText with /DA, Ink with multiple strokes
- Public extract_annotation(AnnotationCommon, dict) -> Annotation
- INV: subtype taxonomy stable

## References

- Plan section: 7.6 lines 2663-2665 (non-link annotation subtypes)
- PDF 1.7 spec 12.5 Annotations (per-subtype subsections)
- 7.6.1 (dispatcher input)
- 7.5 (FileAttachment cross-reference)
- 7.6.4 (output JSON consumer)

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the per-word validation filter that pairs each Tesseract word output with the nearest vector glyph bbox center from 5.5.1. If the center-to-center distance is < 5 pt, accept the word with its OCR confidence. If >= 5 pt, cap confidence at 0.4 (low confidence; OCR is text but the position hints disagree). Outputs a Vec<Span> with confidence_source = "ocr-assisted".

## Why this matters

This filter is the BrokenVector path's accuracy lever. It allows pdftract to trust OCR text where positions agree with the vector layer's hints (good text-layer-position-aligned cases) while down-weighting OCR text where positions disagree (misalignment indicates either OCR-of-OCR garbage or hallucinated text). Without the filter, assisted-OCR would be equivalent to blind OCR.

## Implementation guidance

- Input: Vec<HocrWord> (from 5.4.3, converted to PDF coords via 5.4.4) + Vec<Glyph> (position-hints from 5.5.1)
- Build a KD-tree of vector glyph bbox centers for O(log N) nearest-neighbor lookup (use kiddo or hand-roll for small N)
- For each Tesseract word:
  - Compute word center = midpoint of bbox
  - Query KD-tree for nearest vector glyph center
  - distance < 5.0 pt -> Span { ..., confidence: word.x_wconf/100.0, confidence_source: "ocr-assisted" }
  - distance >= 5.0 pt -> Span { ..., confidence: min(word.x_wconf/100.0, 0.4), confidence_source: "ocr-assisted" }
- The 5pt threshold is a constant ASSISTED_OCR_DISTANCE_PT in module scope; document its tuning fixtures
- Return Vec<Span> in HOCR document order

## Critical considerations

- KD-tree only needed if N (glyph count) > ~100; below that, linear scan is faster
- 5 pt is approximately one space-character width at 12 pt; smaller risks rejecting legitimate matches, larger risks accepting misaligned
- Confidence cap at 0.4 is exactly below the 0.5 threshold used elsewhere; this ensures bbox-merge (5.2.4) will NOT prefer assisted-OCR over a legitimate vector span
- The validation filter is per-word; aggregation to regions for the 0.7/0.3 confidence-region logic happens in 5.5.3

## Acceptance criteria

- Unit test: vector glyph at (100, 200); Tesseract word at (102, 201) -> accepted full conf; word at (110, 210) (distance > 5 pt) -> cap at 0.4
- Critical-fixture test: PDF/A with correctly positioned invisible text layer -> all Tesseract words accepted full conf; WER < blind-OCR
- Reproducibility: same inputs -> identical Span outputs

## References

- Plan section: Phase 5.5 pipeline step 3 (line 1917)
- Phase 5.2.4 bbox-merge IoU > 0.5 + confidence-floor interaction
issue.title: 5.5.2: Validation filter (nearest-vector-glyph match within 5pt, confidence cap at 0.4)

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement inline-link emission in the Markdown sink. Spans whose bbox falls under a Phase 7.6 link annotation rect get wrapped as [anchor text](URL). The anchor text is the span's text; the URL is from the link annotation's /A /URI or /Dest resolved to a URL fragment.

Module: crates/pdftract-core/src/output/markdown/links.rs.

## Why this matters

Inline links preserve clickable navigation from the source PDF; without them, URLs are bare text or invisible (broken). Scholarly papers and reports rely heavily on inline links for citations and references.

## Implementation guidance

- During Markdown emission per page:
  - For each link annotation (from Phase 7.6) intersecting any span on this page:
    - Find spans whose bbox center falls within the link rect
    - Concatenate their text as the anchor text
    - URL: if /A /URI present, use the URL; if /Dest, render as #page-N anchor (internal)
    - Replace the spans' inline emission with [anchor text](URL)
- Edge cases:
  - Multiple spans in one link rect: concatenate texts; emit one inline link
  - Span partially overlaps link rect: include if center in rect; else skip
  - Link rect with no spans inside: skip (no anchor text)
- Escape inline link characters: [ → \\[, ] → \\] in anchor text

## Critical considerations

- Internal links (/Dest to a page) → emit #page-N anchor; requires the Markdown sink to also emit per-page anchors (sibling --md-anchors or page-break heading IDs)
- External URLs need percent-encoding for parens or whitespace (URL-encode the URL component)
- The Markdown formatter must NOT emit the anchor span as bare text AND as a link; the inline-link mode is mutually exclusive with bare-span emission for those spans
- Order matters: process links before paragraph emission so the spans are pre-tagged

## Acceptance criteria

- PDF with 10 external URL links → Markdown has 10 [text](URL) inline links
- PDF with internal links → emits [text](#page-N) anchors
- Multiple spans in one link rect → concatenated anchor text
- URL with special chars → percent-encoded
- Renderer test: emitted Markdown renders correctly in GitHub preview

## References

- Plan section: Phase 6.5.5
- Phase 7.6 link annotations
- Coordinator: pdftract-5o3zv (parent)
Labels: markdown, phase-6

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the function `classify_font(font_dict: &Dictionary) -> FontKind` that reads `/Subtype`, `/BaseFont`, and (for Type0) descendant CIDFont subtype, returning a `FontKind` enum: `{Type1, Type1Std14, TrueType, Type0, CIDFontType0, CIDFontType2, Type3, OpenTypeCFF}`. Includes a sibling helper `strip_subset_prefix(name: &str) -> &str` that removes a leading 6-uppercase-letter `+` prefix.

## Why this matters

Every Phase 2 codepath branches on FontKind. Std-14 classification gates the hardcoded metric table; Type0/CID classification gates the descendant CIDFont chase; OpenType CFF requires a different ttf-parser entrypoint than TrueType. Getting this wrong cascades into wrong metrics and wrong glyph lookups for the whole document.

## Implementation guidance

- Distinguishing Type1Std14: after stripping subset prefix, compare against the 14 canonical names (Times-Roman, Times-Bold, Times-Italic, Times-BoldItalic, Helvetica, Helvetica-Bold, Helvetica-Oblique, Helvetica-BoldOblique, Courier, Courier-Bold, Courier-Oblique, Courier-BoldOblique, Symbol, ZapfDingbats).
- Distinguishing OpenTypeCFF vs TrueType: look at `/FontFile3` with `/Subtype /OpenType` (CFF) vs `/FontFile2` (TrueType). For Type0 descendants, check both descendant CIDFont's `/Subtype` (CIDFontType0 vs CIDFontType2) AND the FontDescriptor's FontFile3 subtype.
- `strip_subset_prefix`: regex-free implementation — verify chars 0..6 are ASCII uppercase, char 6 is `+`, return `&name[7..]`. Otherwise return input unchanged.

## Critical considerations

- Subset prefix is EXACTLY 6 chars + `+`. Five-letter prefixes or lowercase letters are NOT subset prefixes.
- Some PDFs have BaseFont without subset prefix even for embedded subsets; classifier must not depend on prefix presence.
- For Type0 fonts, BaseFont may differ from the descendant CIDFont's BaseFont. Both should be preserved on the Font struct.

## Acceptance criteria

- Unit tests for all 8 FontKind branches.
- `strip_subset_prefix("ABCDEF+Times-Roman") == "Times-Roman"`.
- `strip_subset_prefix("ABCD+Foo") == "ABCD+Foo"` (too short, no strip).
- `strip_subset_prefix("abcdef+Foo") == "abcdef+Foo"` (lowercase, no strip).
- Std-14 detection ignores subset prefix.

## References

- Plan section: Phase 2.1 (lines 1290-1307)
- Plan table: Font types and loading strategy
issue.title: Font subtype classifier and BaseFont prefix stripper

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the LZWDecode filter. LZW is the older (PDF 1.2+) compression scheme; rare in modern PDFs but still present in legacy documents and some scanner outputs. Uses the `lzw` crate (in plan's Dependency Matrix).

/DecodeParms keys (per PDF spec 7.4.4):
- /EarlyChange (int, default 1) — 1 = increase code size BEFORE the code that would exceed current size (the "early change" variant, used by Adobe); 0 = increase code size AFTER (the original GIF variant)
- /Predictor, /Columns, /Colors, /BitsPerComponent — same semantics as FlateDecode (predictors 2, 10-15)

## Implementation guidance

- Use `lzw = "0.10"` crate
- The `lzw` crate has `LsbReader` / `MsbReader`; PDF uses MSB order. Construct `MsbReader::new(reader, min_code_size: 8)`
- /EarlyChange handling:
  - lzw crate API needs careful inspection: it may default to early-change behavior; verify and add a wrapper for late-change if needed
  - If lzw crate does not natively support /EarlyChange = 0, implement late-change wrapper by maintaining the code dictionary externally and signaling code-size increase one step later
- After LZW decode, apply the same predictor as FlateDecode (delegate to the shared `apply_predictor()` function from the FlateDecode bead)
- The decoded output is fed back into the orchestrator's doc_decompress_counter for bomb limit checking

## Critical considerations

- Critical test from plan: LZWDecode with EarlyChange=0 must match known reference output. Use a fixture stream generated by qpdf with --object-streams=disable --decode-level=all to extract a known LZW-encoded stream
- The lzw crate's exact API may have changed across versions; pin to a specific version and document the interface
- LZW code clearing: the special code 256 (CLEAR_CODE) resets the dictionary; 257 is END_OF_STREAM. The lzw crate handles both internally
- LZW initial code size is 8 bits (codes 0-255 = literals); after 256 entries, grows to 9, 10, 11, 12 bits as the dictionary fills (max 12 bits = 4096 entries; clear on overflow)
- Many PDFs use LZW with the wrong EarlyChange setting (the spec's default is 1, but some PDFs use 0 without declaring it). Heuristic: if decoding fails at byte N with EarlyChange=1, retry with EarlyChange=0; if that succeeds, emit STRUCT_INVALID_FILTER_PARAMS warning. Out of scope for THIS bead — default to declared EarlyChange value and emit STREAM_DECODE_ERROR on failure
- Truncated LZW stream: same recovery as FlateDecode — partial bytes + STREAM_DECODE_ERROR
- Performance: LZW is slower than Flate (~10x slower); rare enough that throughput is not critical

## Acceptance criteria

- Critical test passes: LZWDecode fixture with /EarlyChange 0 decoded byte-perfectly against qpdf reference
- LZWDecode without /DecodeParms (defaults): EarlyChange = 1, no predictor
- LZWDecode + /Predictor 12 (PNG Up): decoded correctly, predictor applied
- Truncated LZW stream: STREAM_DECODE_ERROR + partial bytes
- Bomb limit honored
- proptest: random byte sequences fed to LZWDecode never panic
- INV-8 maintained

## References

- Plan section: Phase 1.5 line 1142 (LZWDecode + EarlyChange + same predictor support)
- PDF spec 7.4.4 (LZWDecode parameters)
- Dependency Matrix: lzw
issue.title: Implement LZWDecode with /EarlyChange parameter (default 1, late 0) + same predictor support as FlateDecode

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the deskew step using leptonica-plumbing's pixDeskew (Hough line transform). Detects dominant text angle on a grayscale input; if detected angle >= 0.3 deg, rotates the image by the negative of that angle. Otherwise skip.

## Why this matters

Physical scans are rarely perfectly aligned. A 1-2 degree skew (common from cheap scanners or auto-document feeders) substantially degrades Tesseract WER. Deskewing first means subsequent steps (binarization, denoising) all operate on aligned text, improving their accuracy too.

## Implementation guidance

- Crate: leptonica-plumbing
- Convert GrayImage into leptonica Pix; call pixDeskew with default search params
- Read out the detected angle; if abs(angle) < 0.3 deg, return input unchanged
- Otherwise rotate via pixRotate (or leave leptonica's rotate-in-place); convert back to GrayImage
- pixDeskew clamps to a search range (typically +/- 15 deg); inputs outside this range are reported as "no skew found" and the function returns input unchanged
- Performance: pixDeskew should be < 100 ms per 8.5x11 page at 300 DPI

## Critical considerations

- pixDeskew accepts grayscale input — DO NOT pre-binarize for skew detection (per plan)
- Always preserve the original aspect ratio and total pixel count; rotation should pad with white, not crop
- The detected angle must be recorded in extraction_quality.deskew_angle_deg (per-page) for debugging
- Determinism: pixDeskew is deterministic for same input; document this so future contributors don't add randomness
- Memory: leptonica Pix conversion to/from image::GrayImage is via raw pixel buffer; ensure no leak (use leptonica's pixDestroy on drop)

## Acceptance criteria

- 2-deg synthetic skewed fixture: deskewed within 0.1 deg of upright (critical test)
- 0.2-deg skewed fixture: untouched (skip branch verified)
- 20-deg skewed fixture (outside search range): leaves input untouched, emits IMG_DESKEW_OUT_OF_RANGE diagnostic
- WER on standard deskew fixture: deskew + OCR < deskew-disabled + OCR

## References

- Plan section: Phase 5.3 step 1 deskew (line 1874)
- leptonica pixDeskew docs
issue.title: 5.3.1: Deskew via leptonica pixDeskew (Hough transform; skip if < 0.3 deg)

issue.description:
## Scope

Author docs/notes/release-signing.md as the OQ-10 resolution: document the v1.0.0 stance on signed binaries -- whether macOS releases are code-signed (Developer ID + notarized), Windows binaries are Authenticode-signed, and Linux releases are GPG-signed -- with the implementation cost and CI-complexity rationale for each decision.

## Why this matters

OQ-10 line 503 explicitly mandates this note: Release lead; documented in docs/notes/release-signing.md. Signing decisions are load-bearing for several reasons:
- macOS Gatekeeper now refuses unsigned binaries by default (downloaded binary will be quarantined and users need to right-click-Open to bypass)
- Windows SmartScreen treats unsigned binaries with suspicion (warning popup on first run)
- Linux distributions and package managers prefer GPG-signed artifacts for the trust chain
- Each adds CI complexity (key management, secrets exposure, signing infrastructure)

The supply-chain table line 895 already commits to SLSA Level 2 attestations via provenance.intoto.jsonl -- this note completes the binary-signing companion decision.

## Implementation guidance

- File to create: docs/notes/release-signing.md
- Required content sections:
  - Background: code-signing vs attestation -- they answer different questions (code-signing: who built this; attestation: how was this built)
  - SLSA Level 2: provenance.intoto.jsonl generated by the Argo runner, included in every GitHub Release (already committed per line 895)
  - macOS: Developer ID cert from Apple ($99/yr per account) + notarization (free but requires API key); CI cost: secrets stored in OpenBao, signing step in pdftract-cargo-build for the darwin triples; consequences if NOT signed: Gatekeeper quarantine, end-user friction
  - Windows: Authenticode cert ($200-400/yr depending on provider, EV cert ~$1000/yr); CI cost: secrets, signing step; alternative: cert-via-azure-trustedsigning (cheaper, requires Azure tenancy); consequences if NOT signed: SmartScreen warning
  - Linux: GPG signing of release tarballs and the cargo registry; sign with a maintainer-controlled GPG key whose public part is checked into the repo; consequences if NOT signed: no major UX impact but trust chain weaker
  - v1.0.0 recommendation (decision rationale, not a plan-blocking commitment without sign-off): GPG sign Linux artifacts; macOS deferred to v1.1 unless someone funds the Apple Developer Program; Windows deferred to v1.1 unless someone funds an Authenticode cert
  - Rotation policy: cert renewal cadence; key compromise procedure (rotate, re-sign, publish new fingerprints)

## Critical considerations

- Funding question: Apple + Windows cert costs are non-trivial; the recommendation must be honest about what is and is not affordable at v1.0.0
- macOS notarization happens AFTER signing and is a separate Apple-API step; document the failure mode (notarization rejection -> binary is signed but still Gatekeeper-blocked)
- GPG key MUST be maintainer-owned, NOT a CI-only key; if the only copy of the private key lives in OpenBao and OpenBao is compromised, the trust chain is permanently broken
- Authenticode signing in CI is complex because the cert is exportable as a .pfx but loading it into the runner requires Windows tooling (signtool) -- since iad-ci is Linux-only per ADR-009, this would require osslsigncode or a cross-platform Authenticode tool
- The note interacts with KU-12 (manual platform smoke test): the smoke test runner needs to verify signature post-install, not just functionality

## Acceptance criteria

- docs/notes/release-signing.md exists with the four sections above
- The v1.0.0 stance is stated clearly with rationale
- The cost / complexity / consequence trade-off is documented for each platform
- Rotation and key-management policy documented
- Cross-references to OQ-10, SLSA Level 2 attestation (line 895), and KU-12 (line 590)

## References

- Plan: line 503 (OQ-10 owner + doc location), line 895 (SLSA Level 2 + signing per-platform), line 590 (KU-12 smoke test interaction)

issue.description:
## Scope

Detect tables in extracted PDF content and reconstruct cell structure. Two detection pipelines: (a) line-based via horizontal+vertical path segments from content-stream operators (m/l/S, re/S, re/f), and (b) borderless via x0-aligned spans (3+ rows confirm). Assign span content to cells by centroid containment. Detect header rows via bold font or StructTree TH. Detect merged cells via missing interior edges. Emit a Block with kind: "table" plus a parallel table object in page output containing rows and cells per the schema.

## Why this matters

Tables are the single highest-value structured-data extraction target in PDFs - financial reports, invoices, scientific papers, regulatory filings, bank statements. Plain text dumps destroy tabular structure; correct table reconstruction makes PDFs usable as data sources without manual cleanup. This is the deciding feature for analyst, finance, and data-engineering users. The combination of line-based + borderless coverage handles the great majority of real-world tables; merged-cell detection raises pdftract above competitors that emit ragged grids on header spans.

## Implementation guidance

- Crates: none (geometry is pure arithmetic; reuse content-stream parser from Phase 3)
- Line-based pipeline: collect path segments emitted by content-stream operators - m (moveto) + l (lineto) + S (stroke), re (rectangle) + S (stroke), re + f (fill); cluster collinear segments (epsilon = 1.0 pt); find intersection points; build grid from intersections
- Borderless pipeline: examine span x0 positions on each page; if 3+ lines share x0 (within 2 pt) across 3+ groups, treat as candidate columns; require 3+ rows to confirm; reject if any cell would span > 100 pt of vertical empty space
- Cell content assignment: for each cell bbox, collect spans whose centroid (geometric center) falls within the bbox; preserve span order within cell (top-to-bottom, then left-to-right)
- Header detection: first row is header if (a) all cells have bold-flagged fonts (PDF font Flags bit 19 OR PostScript name contains "Bold") OR (b) StructTree marks the row as TH
- Merged cell detection: when an interior edge is absent (no path segment runs along the expected grid line) infer rowspan or colspan from geometry; emit `colspan` / `rowspan` integers on the cell

## Critical considerations

- Document the full algorithm in docs/research/table-structure-reconstruction.md (plan reference)
- Line detection must NOT include glyph paths (Type 3 font outlines, decorative rules in figures) - filter to graphics-state stroke operators only; ignore paths inside text objects
- Borderless heuristic threshold (3+ rows AND 3+ aligned x0 groups) is intentionally conservative to avoid false positives on left-aligned paragraphs
- Centroid containment, not edge intersection - prevents double-assignment when spans straddle thin cell borders
- Header detection bold heuristic: respect font Flags bit 19 (FixedPitch=1, Serif=2, Symbolic=4, Script=8, NonSymbolic=32, Italic=64, AllCap=131072, SmallCap=262144, ForceBold=262144) - bold is implied by ForceBold flag OR by "Bold" in BaseFont
- Merged cell rowspan/colspan: ALWAYS integers >= 1; default 1 when unmerged
- Two-page tables: detect and flag (output has `continued: true` on first half, `continued_from_prev: true` on second); full cross-page reconstruction deferred to non-streaming mode

## Acceptance criteria

- All Phase 7.2 child task beads closed
- Critical test from plan: 5x3 bordered table - all 15 cells extracted with correct text
- Critical test: merged header cell spanning 3 columns - colspan=3 in output
- Critical test: borderless two-column table - detected via alignment heuristic
- Critical test: table spanning two pages - detected and flagged (continued: true)
- table object in page output matches docs/schema/v1.0/pdftract.schema.json table shape
- Public TableDetector::detect(&PageContext) -> Vec<Table> entry point
- Documentation: docs/research/table-structure-reconstruction.md with diagrams

## References

- Plan section: 7.2 Table Detection (lines 2566-2585)
- docs/research/table-structure-reconstruction.md (algorithm reference)
- Phase 3 content-stream operators (path segment source)
- Phase 4.3 span/block model (consumer of table blocks)
- Phase 7.1 StructTree TH detection (header source)
- Phase 7.10 profile structural.has_table predicate

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement `merge_glyphs_to_spans(glyphs: &[Glyph]) -> Vec<Span>` that walks the per-page glyph list and groups consecutive glyphs into spans. A new span begins when any of the 5 triggers fires on the current glyph: (1) font_name != prev font_name; (2) `(font_size - prev_font_size).abs() > 0.5`; (3) rendering_mode != prev rendering_mode; (4) RGB-normalized fill_color != prev color; (5) is_word_boundary == true.

## Why this matters

The merger is the bridge from low-level glyph stream to high-level span sequence. Every Phase 4.2/4.3/4.4/4.7 child consumes its output. The 5-trigger set is calibrated against pdfminer/pypdf behavior: aggressive enough to preserve style boundaries, lenient enough to keep words intact.

## Implementation guidance

- Iterate glyphs; maintain `current_span: Option<Span>` and `prev_glyph: Option<&Glyph>`.
- For each glyph:
  - If current_span is None OR any trigger fires: finalize current_span (push to result), start new Span seeded from current glyph.
  - Else: append glyph.codepoint to current_span.text, extend bbox to union, update confidence to min.
- RGB normalization: `Color::DeviceGray(v) -> (v,v,v)`; `Color::DeviceCMYK(...)` -> formula; `Color::DeviceRGB(rgb)` -> as-is; Spot/Other are compared by-variant (Spot(name_a, _) == Spot(name_b, _) iff name_a == name_b).
- Word boundary handling: when triggered by is_word_boundary=true, choose between:
  - (a) Append " " to PREVIOUS span text (still flush previous; new span starts WITHOUT leading space).
  - (b) Emit a 1-char " " span (font/size from prev glyph), then new span.
  Plan allows either; v0.1.0 picks (a) for cleaner JSON output and easier round-trip. Document and test.

## Critical considerations

- INV: text round-trips for plain-text output — joining all span texts in reading order produces the same plain text as the document.
- font_size delta: USE 0.5pt threshold; smaller deltas (e.g., 0.3pt) DO NOT trigger break.
- fill_color comparison: spot colors compared by-name AND by-tint exactly (no float fudge — they're string IDs).
- is_word_boundary glyph is the FIRST glyph of the new span (after the boundary marker takes effect).
- Empty glyph list: returns empty Vec<Span> (no error).
- INV: confidence is the MINIMUM of all member glyphs' confidence; confidence_source is mapped from the WORST glyph (lowest confidence) source.

## Acceptance criteria

- Input "Hello World" (5 glyphs, space-boundary, 5 glyphs): output 2 spans "Hello " and "World" (option a) OR 3 spans "Hello", " ", "World" (option b).
- Input "He" (regular) + "lo" (bold) at same font/color: 2 spans, font_name changes.
- Input with font_size 12pt vs 12.2pt: 1 span (delta < 0.5pt).
- Input with DeviceGray(0.5) then DeviceRGB([0.5,0.5,0.5]): 1 span (RGB-normalized same).
- Input with Spot("PANTONE", 1.0) vs DeviceRGB([1,0,0]) with same hex: 2 spans (Spot != Device).

## References

- Plan section: Phase 4.1 (lines 1612-1620, 1657)
issue.title: 5-trigger break detector + glyph-to-span merger

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the page classification subsystem that decides Vector | Scanned | Hybrid | BrokenVector for every page before any expensive extraction work begins. Outputs a PageClass enum value with confidence: f32 in [0.0, 1.0] plus a per-page page_type JSON string that downstream sinks emit. This coordinator owns the design and integration of all signal evaluators plus the Hybrid grid-cell evaluator plus the PageClass-to-page_type mapping table that flows into 6.1 JSON output.

## Why this matters

Page classification is the entry point of Phase 5: every later sub-phase routes off this decision. Vector pages skip OCR entirely (large wins for vector-heavy docs); Scanned pages go through the full image-extract -> preprocess -> Tesseract pipeline; BrokenVector pages take the special assisted-OCR path (5.5); Hybrid pages require both vector extraction and per-cell OCR. Misclassification at this stage cascades into wrong-mode extraction and either WER spikes (false negatives) or wasted CPU (false positives). It is also a Phase 6.1 deliverable: every value the classifier emits must appear in docs/schema/v1.0/pdftract.schema.json, including broken_vector as a valid page_type.

## Implementation guidance

- Signal evaluators run in declared order with short-circuit when confidence > 0.95
- Signals: text-operator presence, Tr=3 invisible+full-page-image, image coverage fraction (>0.85), character validity rate (<0.4 or >0.85), character density ratio (<0.03)
- Hybrid evaluator: divide page into 8x8 grid cells; cells with text-ops and validity above threshold = vector; cells with image coverage and no text = scanned; >= 10 of 64 cells of each kind => Hybrid
- PageClass internal enum -> page_type JSON string mapping: Vector -> text, Scanned -> scanned, Hybrid -> mixed, BrokenVector pre-OCR -> broken_vector, BrokenVector post-OCR-success -> scanned, no-text-no-image -> blank, image-only -> figure_only
- Inputs come from Phase 1 content-stream operator inventory + Phase 4.7 readability scoring
- Provide a single PageClassifier::classify(&PageContext) -> PageClassification entry point

## Critical considerations

- broken_vector MUST be a valid page_type output value in 6.1 schema (INV-9 stable taxonomy)
- Hybrid path requires Phase 3 to run first to capture vector text; OCR is added afterward only on image-heavy cells
- Char validity rate signal depends on Phase 4.7 wordlist scoring being available
- BrokenVector escalation criterion (readability < 0.5 on Vector class) is set by 4.7, not by classifier directly
- Confidence values must be reproducible: same input -> same confidence number (no float nondeterminism from rayon ordering)
- Page classification runs before Tesseract init, so its cost must stay well under 5ms/page on typical pages

## Acceptance criteria

- All Phase 5.1 child task beads closed
- PageClass enum + PageClassification struct in pdftract-ocr (or shared types crate)
- Critical tests pass: pure-text PDF -> all Vector with confidence > 0.95; scanned single-page PDF -> Scanned; PDF/A with invisible text layer -> BrokenVector; hybrid page -> Hybrid with correct region split
- page_type JSON string mapping table implemented and consumed by 6.1 schema
- Classifier is reproducible (CI: classify same PDF twice -> identical output bytes)
- Classification overhead < 5 ms/page on typical inputs (CI-gated micro-benchmark)

## References

- Plan section: Phase 5.1 Page Classification (lines 1807-1845)
- INV-9 stable taxonomy (page_type enum values)
- Phase 6.1 schema deliverable (broken_vector must appear in JSON Schema)
- Phase 7.10 profile selection depends on page_type semantics

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement pdftract.extract(path, **kwargs) -> dict as a PyO3 function. Parses kwargs into ExtractionOptions, releases GIL during the blocking extraction, and pythonizes the resulting Output struct to a Python dict.

Module: crates/pdftract-py/src/extract.rs.

## Why this matters

The full-extract entry point is the most common SDK call: users invoke it for one-shot Document conversion. Naming, kwargs surface, and return shape are user-facing forever — getting them wrong here forces a v2.0 SDK migration.

## Implementation guidance

- Signature:
  ```rust
  #[pyfunction]
  #[pyo3(signature = (path, **kwargs))]
  pub fn extract(py: Python<'_>, path: &str, kwargs: Option<&PyDict>) -> PyResult<PyObject> {
      let opts = parse_kwargs(kwargs)?;
      let output = py.allow_threads(|| pdftract_core::extract(path, &opts))?;
      pythonize::pythonize(py, &output).map_err(PyErr::from)
  }
  ```
- kwargs allowed: ocr (bool), ocr_language (list[str] or comma-string), include_invisible (bool), extract_forms (bool), extract_attachments (bool), readability_threshold (float), password (str), max_decompress_gb (int), full_render (bool), receipts (str), cache_dir (str), pages (str), formats (list[str])
- Unknown kwargs raise PdftractError (strict, no silent ignore)
- pythonize crate converts serde::Serialize types to PyDict automatically
- py.allow_threads release GIL during the Rust extraction (allows other Python threads to run)

## Critical considerations

- Kwarg parsing: use a strict allowlist; unknown kwargs are user typos and silently-ignored typos cause hard-to-diagnose bugs
- pythonize::pythonize converts nested serde structures to nested PyDict/PyList; the resulting object is a normal dict (not a custom PyClass)
- Errors from pdftract_core map to Python exceptions via the sibling bead (PdftractError hierarchy)
- The path argument accepts local paths and https:// URLs; same dispatch as the CLI
- pythonize has some performance overhead for large outputs; for very large docs, the streaming variant (sibling) is preferred

## Acceptance criteria

- pdftract.extract(\"file.pdf\") returns a dict
- pdftract.extract(\"file.pdf\", ocr=True, ocr_language=[\"eng\"]) returns a dict with OCR text
- pdftract.extract(\"file.pdf\", bogus_kwarg=1) raises PdftractError
- The returned dict's shape matches docs/schema/v1.0/pdftract.schema.json
- GIL is released during extraction (test with 4 concurrent threads each extracting different PDFs)

## References

- Plan section: Phase 6.3.1
- Coordinator: pdftract-2uk9z (parent — 3 entry points bundle)
- Sibling: extract_text entry point, extract_stream entry point
- Sibling pdftract-4ewgr (PdftractError hierarchy)
Labels: phase-6, pyo3

issue.description:
## Scope

Author tests/security/TH-07-ps-leak.rs that spawns pdftract extract --password foo path.pdf with PDFTRACT_INSECURE_CLI_PASSWORD NOT set and asserts the process exits 64 (usage error) with a stderr hint pointing at --password-stdin or PDFTRACT_PASSWORD env. Additionally verifies that when PDFTRACT_INSECURE_CLI_PASSWORD=1 is set the extraction proceeds but a stderr warning naming ps aux is emitted, and that the password value never appears in any captured log buffer.

## Why this matters

TH-07 (line 878) is the operator-misconfig protection against password disclosure via the process arg list. On any multi-user host, ps aux reveals --password VALUE to every other user; the env var, stdin, and form-field ingress all close this hole. The exit-64 contract is what wrappers and shell scripts rely on to fail-fast when a user inadvertently uses the insecure form.

## Implementation guidance

- Test file: tests/security/TH-07-ps-leak.rs
- Test cases:
  1. Spawn pdftract extract --password foo path.pdf with no env opt-in; assert exit 64 within 1 second; assert stderr contains "--password-stdin" and "PDFTRACT_PASSWORD"; assert stderr contains "insecure" (matching the warning copy)
  2. Spawn pdftract extract --password foo path.pdf with PDFTRACT_INSECURE_CLI_PASSWORD=1; assert process either extracts successfully (depending on password correctness against the fixture) or exits with a password-error code (66) but NOT 64; assert stderr contains "WARNING" and "ps aux"
  3. Spawn pdftract extract --password-stdin path.pdf with the password supplied via stdin; assert success (depending on fixture)
  4. Spawn pdftract extract path.pdf with PDFTRACT_PASSWORD=foo env; assert success (depending on fixture)
  5. ps-audit assertion: during the case-2 run, read /proc/<pid>/cmdline; assert it CONTAINS the password (this is the leak we are protecting against; verifying it leaks under the opt-in is the WHOLE POINT of requiring opt-in)
  6. Conversely, during case-3 and case-4 runs: read /proc/<pid>/cmdline; assert it does NOT contain "foo"
- Fixture: tests/fixtures/security/password-protected.pdf with a known correct password (e.g. "secret123" -- choose something unmistakable)

## Critical considerations

- Case 5 is the strongest test: it positively verifies that --password VALUE DOES leak in argv (which is exactly why we reject it by default)
- Cases 3-4 are the positive paths and verify the ingress channels actually work
- The test MUST be timing-tolerant: spawn the child, poll /proc/<pid>/cmdline before the process exits; use a short-lived test fixture so the process lingers long enough
- The fixture password ("secret123" or similar) MUST NOT appear in any log line at any verbosity -- this is the TH-08 overlap; TH-08 has its own test but TH-07 should cross-check at the most-common verbosity (RUST_LOG=pdftract=debug)
- On Windows the /proc path is unavailable; gate case 5/6 on cfg(target_os = "linux") and add a Windows-specific equivalent via WMI Win32_Process if feasible (otherwise #[ignore] on Windows)
- The stderr warning copy needs to be stable so the test can grep for substrings; pick "WARNING: --password VALUE is insecure (visible via 'ps aux')..."

## Acceptance criteria

- tests/security/TH-07-ps-leak.rs exists and passes
- Case 1 (default rejection) passes
- Case 2 (opt-in proceed with warning) passes
- Cases 3-4 (positive ingress channels) pass
- Case 5 (positive leak verification under opt-in) passes on Linux
- Case 6 (no leak under correct channels) passes on Linux
- Fixture tests/fixtures/security/password-protected.pdf committed with documented password

## References

- Plan: line 878 (TH-07 entry); depends on pdftract-2ka7 (--password-stdin + PDFTRACT_PASSWORD hardening)

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement a registry of the 9 named CMaps PDF readers MUST support without an embedded CMap stream: `Identity-H`, `Identity-V`, `UniJIS-UTF16-H`, `UniJIS-UTF16-V`, `UniGB-UTF16-H`, `UniGB-UTF16-V`, `UniCNS-UTF16-H`, `UniCNS-UTF16-V`, `UniKS-UTF16-H`, `UniKS-UTF16-V`. When a Type 0 font's `/Encoding` is a Name matching one of these, the registry returns a `PredefinedCMap` capable of decoding bytes -> CIDs and (for UTF16 variants) CIDs -> Unicode codepoints.

## Why this matters

These names are LITERALLY identifiers — the PDF does not ship the CMap data; the reader must already know them. Without this registry every Type 0 font with a predefined Encoding hits an "unknown CMap" error and falls back to U+FFFD.

## Implementation guidance

- Identity-H / Identity-V: zero-data CMaps. The `decode_bytes` function reads 2-byte big-endian codes as CIDs directly; the `cid_to_unicode` function is None (caller must use ToUnicode).
- UTF16 CMaps: bundle as compile-time `phf::Map<u16, char>` or `phf::Map<u16, &'static [char]>` keyed by CID. Source: build the maps offline from Adobe's public CMap resources (the `Adobe-Japan1-UCS2`, `Adobe-GB1-UCS2`, `Adobe-CNS1-UCS2`, `Adobe-Korea1-UCS2` files).
- Build artifact: `crates/pdftract-core/build/predefined-cmaps/{adobe-japan1, adobe-gb1, adobe-cns1, adobe-korea1}.json`.
- V (vertical) and H (horizontal) variants share the same CID->Unicode mapping; the H/V distinction only affects glyph rendering, not text extraction. Document and unify.
- The codespace ranges for these CMaps are well-known constants (e.g., Adobe-Japan1 is 1-byte 0x00-0x7F + 2-byte 0x81-0x9F lead, 0xE0-0xFC lead). Bake them in.

## Critical considerations

- Binary footprint target: ~1.2 MB combined for all 4 Adobe-N UCS2 maps. This is a chunky allocation — gate behind feature `cjk` (default off) per Phase 0 binary budget; document the cargo bloat number.
- INV: Identity-H/V passthrough does NOT consult any UTF16 map; downstream ToUnicode is mandatory for those.
- The maps have multi-codepoint targets (Japanese ligatures, Hangul syllables decomposed to jamo); use `&'static [char]` value type.
- Some CIDs in Adobe-Japan1 are unassigned — None on lookup is normal, not an error.

## Acceptance criteria

- All 10 names (5 base * 2 H/V) resolve via `from_name(s: &str) -> Option<PredefinedCMap>`.
- Identity-H decodes `[0x00, 0x41]` to CID 65.
- UniJIS-UTF16-H decodes `[0x82, 0xA0]` then maps CID -> Japanese hiragana A (U+3042).
- Vertical (V) variant returns identical CID->Unicode as Horizontal (H).
- Unknown name returns None (no panic, no allocation).
- Feature flag `cjk` controls the 1.2 MB UCS2 map inclusion.

## References

- Plan section: Phase 2.3 (lines 1375-1380)
- Adobe CMap resources (Adobe-Japan1-UCS2.cmap and siblings)

Added ProgressEvent types, worker_run() function, span extraction, fingerprint computation, encrypted PDF handling, and --invert-match support. Fixed encryption module compilation issues. issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the per-file worker function: parse one FileWorkItem into a Vec<Span> via Phase 1 (lexer/object/xref) + Phase 3 (content stream + text operators) + Phase 4 span builder (skipping Phase 4.5 reading-order detection because grep doesn't need ordering). For each span, apply the Matcher (from 7.8.2) and emit Match records to the sink channel. Honor --ocr flag by also OCRing Scanned pages (Phase 5). Skip encrypted PDFs without credentials with a single diagnostic. Skip --invert-match span emission when no matches found (per -v semantics).

## Why this matters

Skipping reading-order detection is the central performance win: it cuts per-file CPU by ~30-40% on typical pages while losing nothing - grep doesn't care about reading order, just span-level match presence. Single-pass parsing means no intermediate text dump to disk and no double-parsing for cache reasons. OCR is opt-in because it's slow; non-OCR mode is the throughput target.

## Implementation guidance

- Inputs: FileWorkItem, Arc<Matcher>, Arc<GrepArgs>, sink: Sender<MatchEvent>, progress: Sender<ProgressEvent>
- Open file via Phase 1 parser; encrypted -> emit ProgressEvent::FileSkipped + diagnostic; return
- For each page, run content stream pass (Phase 3 graphics state + text operators) to produce raw Vec<Span>
  - Span has: text, bbox [f32;4], page_index, confidence f32, font, font_size
- Skip Phase 4.5 reading-order detection (not needed for grep)
- For each span, apply Matcher.find_iter(span.text):
  - For each match: emit MatchEvent { path, page_index, bbox: span.bbox, match_text: span.text[start..end], span_text: span.text.clone(), span_confidence: span.confidence, pdf_fingerprint: cached_fp, crosses_spans: false }
- If --ocr: for pages classified as Scanned (Phase 5.1), run OCR (Phase 5.4) and produce OCR'd spans with confidence from Tesseract; matcher applied identically
- If --invert-match: emit a MatchEvent for spans with ZERO matches (synthetic record); skip spans WITH matches
- crosses_spans: false (cross-span matching is a separate concern; for v1, treat each span as independent)
- After all pages processed, emit ProgressEvent::FileDone { path, matches: total_match_count, duration_ms }
- Per-page progress: emit ProgressEvent::FileProgress { path, pages_done, pages_total } every page (cheap, throttled by sink consumer)

## Critical considerations

- Phase 4.5 SKIPPED on purpose; reading-order is wasteful for grep
- OCR mode (--ocr) typically 10-50x slower than vector grep; user understands the trade-off
- Encrypted-file diagnostic format: "<path>: encrypted (skipped)" to stderr only; not in stdout, not in JSON
- Per-file timing for slow-file warning: capture instant::now() at start; consumer compares against 30s threshold
- pdf_fingerprint: compute once per file from Phase 1; reuse for every match
- Empty PDFs (no pages): emit FileDone with matches: 0; no error
- The worker should NEVER hang: bounded channel + per-page progress ensures sink can detect stuck workers (and the watchdog ticker covers absolute silence)

## Acceptance criteria

- Worker correctness: synthetic 5-page PDF with "INVOICE" on page 3 produces one match
- OCR mode (--ocr): scanned PDF fixture produces matches in OCR'd text
- Encrypted PDF emits single diagnostic + zero matches; FileDone still fired
- --invert-match produces non-match records (one per zero-match span)
- Per-page FileProgress events emitted
- pdf_fingerprint identical across multiple matches in same file
- Public worker_run(item: FileWorkItem, matcher: Arc<Matcher>, args: Arc<GrepArgs>, sink, progress)

## References

- Plan section: 7.8 lines 2700 (single-pass), 2723 (--ocr), 2742 (JSON shape), 2745 (crosses_spans), 2794-2795 (encryption + non-PDF)
- Phase 1 parser; Phase 3 content streams; Phase 4 span builder (skip 4.5)
- Phase 5.1 page classification + 5.4 Tesseract (OCR mode)
- 7.8.2 Matcher
- 7.8.3 FileWorkItem
- 7.8.5 default text output, 7.8.6 JSON-Lines output (sink consumers)
issue.title: 7.8.4: Single-pass per-file parse pipeline (Phase 1 + 3 + spans only; no reading order)

issue.description:
## Scope

Define the `GraphicsState` struct with all 13 fields per the plan (ctm, text_matrix, text_line_matrix, font: Option<Arc<Font>>, font_size, char_spacing, word_spacing, horiz_scaling, leading, text_rise, text_rendering_mode, fill_color, stroke_color). Define the `Color` enum with all 5 variants. Provide `GraphicsState::initial()` returning a state with identity CTM, no font, all spacings 0, horiz_scaling 100, fill/stroke black.

## Why this matters

The struct shape is the contract that the rest of Phase 3 builds on. Getting the field types (Arc<Font> not &Font for lifetime sanity; f64 for matrices to avoid float drift over deep CTM chains; Color enum not Vec<f32> for type safety) right NOW prevents downstream churn.

## Implementation guidance

- Matrices: `Matrix3x3 = [[f64; 3]; 3]` row-major. NOT external nalgebra/glam — hand-roll the 6 ops needed (multiply, identity, scale, translate, rotate, invert). Document the indexing convention in a comment.
- `Color` enum:
  ```rust
  pub enum Color {
      DeviceGray(f32),
      DeviceRGB([f32; 3]),
      DeviceCMYK([f32; 4]),
      Spot(Arc<str>, f32),
      Other,
  }
  ```
- `GraphicsState::initial()`: CTM identity, text_matrix identity (will be reset on BT), font_size 0.0 (must be Tf'd before use), char_spacing/word_spacing/leading/text_rise 0.0, horiz_scaling 100.0, text_rendering_mode 0, fill/stroke `Color::DeviceGray(0.0)` (black per PDF spec).
- Provide `Color::to_css_hex(&self) -> Option<String>` for output serialization: DeviceGray(v) -> "#rrggbb" via v→(v,v,v); DeviceRGB -> "#rrggbb"; DeviceCMYK via standard formula; Spot/Other -> None.

## Critical considerations

- INV: matrices are f64 to absorb the cumulative error of nested CTM chains in deep form XObjects.
- INV: GraphicsState is Clone (cheap thanks to Arc<Font>) so q/Q can snapshot it.
- font is Option because content streams may use color/CTM operators before any Tf — getting None means the stream is malformed for text purposes, NOT a crash.
- Color::Spot holds Arc<str> not &str so it can outlive parse-time borrows.
- DeviceCMYK -> RGB conversion: `R = (1-C)*(1-K), G = (1-M)*(1-K), B = (1-Y)*(1-K)` (naive but acceptable for text color visualization).

## Acceptance criteria

- `GraphicsState::initial()` returns state with ctm == identity, font_size == 0.0, fill_color == DeviceGray(0.0).
- Clone produces a deep-equal value (Arc cloned cheaply).
- `Color::DeviceRGB([1.0, 0.0, 0.0]).to_css_hex() == Some("#ff0000".into())`.
- `Color::Spot("PANTONE".into(), 0.5).to_css_hex() == None`.
- Matrix multiply test: identity * identity == identity within 1e-10.

## References

- Plan section: Phase 3.1 State struct fields (lines 1444-1460), Color type (lines 1463-1471), CSS hex rules (line 1473)
issue.title: GraphicsState struct + Color enum + matrix initialization

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement AcroForm /Ch (choice) value extraction. Surface combo box vs list box via /Ff bit 18 (Combo). Multi-select via /Ff bit 22 (MultiSelect). Parse the /Opt array (full enumeration of choices, each with export value and display text). Surface the selected option value(s).

Module: crates/pdftract-core/src/acroform/value_choice.rs.

## Why this matters

Choice fields (dropdowns and list boxes) carry both the selected value AND the full set of options. Surfacing options enables downstream consumers (form-filling agents, RAG-on-forms) to know the valid value set. Without /Opt parsing, consumers see only the selected value with no context.

## Implementation guidance

- Output variant:
  ```rust
  FormFieldValue::Choice {
      kind: ChoiceKind,  // Combo | List
      selected: Option<String>,
      default: Option<String>,
      options: Vec<(String, String)>,  // (export_value, display_text)
      multi_select: bool,
  }
  pub enum ChoiceKind { Combo, List }
  ```
- /Ff bit 18 (1<<17 = 0x20000) → Combo (else List)
- /Ff bit 22 (1<<21 = 0x200000) → MultiSelect
- /V (selected value):
  - Single-select: PdfString (or Name for Combo)
  - Multi-select: Array of PdfStrings
- /Opt (options):
  - Each entry is either a PdfString (export = display = that string) OR an Array [export_value, display_text]
  - Iterate and produce Vec<(String, String)>
- /DV (default value): same format as /V

## Critical considerations

- /Opt entry format dispatch: PdfObject::String(s) → (s.clone(), s.clone()); PdfObject::Array([export, display]) → (export, display)
- Multi-select: /V is an array; produce Some(\",\".join(values)) or change shape to Vec<String>. Current sibling spec uses Option<String> with comma-join for simplicity; document the format
- Combo with editable field: /Ff bit 19 (Edit); user-typed value not in /Opt is valid; the /V is a String not constrained to /Opt
- Empty /Opt is valid (rare): options is empty Vec
- /V missing: selected is None

## Acceptance criteria

- Combo with /Opt [\"a\", \"b\", \"c\"] /V \"b\" → { kind: Combo, selected: Some(\"b\"), options: [(\"a\",\"a\"),(\"b\",\"b\"),(\"c\",\"c\")], multi_select: false }
- Combo with /Opt [[\"v1\",\"Display 1\"]] /V \"v1\" → options: [(\"v1\",\"Display 1\")]
- List with multi-select /V [\"a\",\"b\"] → multi_select: true, selected: Some(\"a,b\")
- Empty /Opt → options: []
- Missing /V → selected: None

## References

- Plan section: Phase 7.4.2 (Ch variant)
- PDF spec 12.7.6 (Choice fields)
- Coordinator: pdftract-5t92 (parent)
- Sibling: Tx, Btn variants
Labels: acroform, phase-7
issue.title: AcroForm Ch (choice) value extraction (Combo + List + /Opt array parsing)

## Scope

Implement the `pdftract` RubyGem as a subprocess-based SDK. Spawn the bundled `pdftract` binary via Ruby's `Open3.popen3`, parse JSON output via `JSON.parse`, expose the 9 contract methods as module functions and class methods on a `Pdftract::Client`. Publish to RubyGems via the `pdftract-ruby-publish` Argo template. Repo at `github.com/jedarden/pdftract-ruby`. Deferred to v1.1+ release wave (lower priority than v1.0 SDKs).

## Why this matters

Ruby's data-engineering use is niche but committed (Rails apps that ingest PDF receipts, government tax-form processors built on Ruby legacy stacks). Honouring the SDK contract across all 10 languages is the design commitment; deferring to v1.1+ acknowledges the maintenance budget reality without dropping the language.

## Implementation guidance

- Gem name: `pdftract` (RubyGems)
- Repo: `github.com/jedarden/pdftract-ruby` (separate repo)
- Ruby version floor: 3.2 (current Ruby stable channel)
- File layout (generator-driven; see Tera template scaffolding bead):
  - `pdftract.gemspec` (gem metadata)
  - `lib/pdftract.rb` (top-level entry; re-exports module functions)
  - `lib/pdftract/client.rb` (the main Client class)
  - `lib/pdftract/codegen/methods.rb` (generated)
  - `lib/pdftract/codegen/errors.rb` (generated; 8 exception classes)
  - `lib/pdftract/models.rb` (Document, Page, Span, etc. as Struct or Data classes)
  - `test/conformance_test.rb` (minitest)
- Method signatures (Ruby):
  - `Pdftract.extract(source, **options) => Pdftract::Document`
  - `Pdftract.extract_text(source, **options) => String`
  - `Pdftract.extract_markdown(source, **options) => String`
  - `Pdftract.extract_stream(source, **options) => Enumerator<Pdftract::Page>`
  - `Pdftract.search(source, pattern, **options) => Enumerator<Pdftract::Match>`
  - `Pdftract.get_metadata(source, **options) => Pdftract::Metadata`
  - `Pdftract.hash(source, **options) => Pdftract::Fingerprint`
  - `Pdftract.classify(source) => Pdftract::Classification`
  - `Pdftract.verify_receipt(path, receipt) => Boolean`
- Option names use snake_case per Ruby convention: CLI `--ocr-language` becomes `ocr_language` (kwarg)
- Errors: `Pdftract::Error` is the base; 8 subclasses (`CorruptPdfError`, `EncryptionError`, etc.)
- Document, Page, etc. as Ruby `Data` classes (immutable; introduced in Ruby 3.2) — modern Ruby idiom

## Publishing (combined with impl bead because v1.1+ release wave is simpler)

- Argo WorkflowTemplate file: `k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/pdftract-ruby-publish.yaml` in `jedarden/declarative-config`
- Inputs: tag name; RubyGems API key from ESO Secret `rubygems-api-key-pdftract` (synced from OpenBao key)
- Steps:
  1. `clone-sdk-repo`: `git clone https://github.com/jedarden/pdftract-ruby.git --branch main`
  2. `sync-version`: update `pdftract.gemspec` `spec.version = "X.Y.Z"`
  3. `bundle-install`: `bundle install`
  4. `conformance`: `bundle exec rake test:conformance` (runs the shared suite; aborts on failure)
  5. `build`: `gem build pdftract.gemspec`
  6. `publish`: `gem push pdftract-X.Y.Z.gem` using the RubyGems API key file at `~/.gem/credentials`
- Container: `ruby:3.2-slim`

## Critical considerations

- ADR-009: runs on iad-ci; never use GitHub Actions
- RubyGems is IMMUTABLE; a published version cannot be recalled (only `gem yank`)
- The `Open3.popen3` block-form must be used carefully to capture both stdout and stderr without deadlocking on large outputs; use `Open3.capture3` for simple synchronous calls
- Enumerator-based streaming is the idiomatic Ruby pattern; the underlying NDJSON output is parsed line-by-line and yielded to the block
- Ruby's GIL means concurrent calls do NOT achieve parallelism; users wanting parallelism should fork or use processes
- v1.1+ deferral means this bead does NOT block v1.0 release; the priority is P3 (backlog-tier)

## Acceptance criteria

- The `pdftract` gem builds with `gem build`
- All 9 contract methods exposed on the Pdftract module
- All 8 exception classes inherit from Pdftract::Error
- `bundle exec rake test:conformance` runs the conformance suite and 100% passes
- The Argo publish workflow successfully pushes to RubyGems
- A re-run after partial failure is idempotent (duplicate-publish treated as success)

## References

- Plan section: SDK Architecture / The Ten SDKs, line 3478 (Ruby subprocess via Open3 + JSON.parse; v1.1+)
- Plan section: SDK Architecture / Per-SDK Release Channels, line 3575
- Plan section: SDK Acceptance Criteria, lines 3581-3589
- Sibling: SDK contract, conformance suite, code generator

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the core `ObjectParser::parse_direct_object()` that consumes the next sequence of tokens from the Lexer and produces a `PdfObject`. Handles every direct object variant:

- `Token::Null` -> `PdfObject::Null`
- `Token::Bool(b)` -> `PdfObject::Bool(b)`
- `Token::Integer(i)` -> `PdfObject::Integer(i)` (special case: if followed by `Integer + IndirectRef`, becomes `PdfObject::Ref(ObjRef{i, gen})`)
- `Token::Real(r)` -> `PdfObject::Real(r)`
- `Token::String(b)` -> `PdfObject::String(b)`
- `Token::Name(b)` -> `PdfObject::Name(intern(b))`
- `Token::ArrayStart` -> recursive parse until `ArrayEnd` -> `PdfObject::Array(...)`
- `Token::DictStart` -> recursive parse until `DictEnd` -> `PdfObject::Dict(...)`, validating alternating Name/Object pairs
- `Token::DictEnd` followed by `Token::Stream` -> `PdfObject::Stream(PdfStream{dict: ..., offset: ..., len_hint: ...})`

## Implementation guidance

- Indirect-reference detection requires 3-token lookahead: when the current token is Integer, peek ahead 2 tokens; if pattern is `Integer Integer R`, consume all 3 and return `PdfObject::Ref`
- Dict parsing: alternate `Name -> Object`. If after a `DictStart` the first token is NOT a Name, emit `STRUCT_INVALID_DICT_KEY` diagnostic, skip to `DictEnd`, return empty dict
- Stream detection: after a complete dict, if the very next token is `Token::Stream`, the dict represents a stream; record `offset = lexer.position()` (which is just past the `stream\n` header), then SKIP the stream body (don't parse it — Phase 1.5 decodes on demand)
- Stream-body skip: read the `/Length` field from the dict (if direct integer, use it; if indirect ref or missing, scan for `endstream` keyword in the bytes — Phase 1.6 error recovery)
- After skipping the body, the next token MUST be `Token::EndStream`; if not, emit `STRUCT_MISSING_KEY` (missing endstream) and try to recover by scanning forward
- Recursion depth limit: dicts and arrays can nest; impose a max depth of 256 to prevent stack overflow on adversarial input; emit `STRUCT_DEPTH_EXCEEDED` at depth > 256 and return PdfNull

## Critical considerations

- Critical test from plan: nested dict `<< /A << /B 1 >> >>` -> outer dict with one key `A` whose value is the inner dict with key `B` -> Integer(1). Verify recursive parse correctness
- Critical test from plan: array of mixed types `[1 true (str) /Name null]` -> Array with 5 elements of the appropriate variants
- The 3-token lookahead for indirect refs is the trickiest part. Use Lexer::peek_token() which is already a peekable in Phase 1.1
- A dict with an odd number of tokens between `<<` and `>>` (missing value) emits `STRUCT_INVALID_DICT_VALUE`; recover by inserting PdfNull for the missing value
- A dict key that is not a Name token (e.g. `<< 1 2 >>`) emits `STRUCT_INVALID_DICT_KEY` and is skipped
- Stream `/Length` may itself be an indirect ref `5 0 R`; this layer records the ref as the len_hint and lets the consumer (Phase 1.5) deref it on demand
- The stream body skip must be VERY careful with EOF: if the file truncates inside a stream, emit `STRUCT_TRUNCATED_STREAM` and create a PdfStream with offset+len_hint pointing past EOF; downstream decoders return empty bytes with `STREAM_DECODE_ERROR`
- Depth limit of 256 is generous (real PDFs rarely exceed 30 levels); the limit exists for adversarial input

## Acceptance criteria

- All listed direct object variants parse to the expected PdfObject
- Critical tests pass:
  - Nested dict 4 levels deep -> correct tree
  - Array of mixed types -> correct ordering of 5 elements
  - `5 0 R` -> PdfObject::Ref(ObjRef{5, 0})
  - Truncated dict at EOF -> partial dict + STRUCT_UNEXPECTED_EOF diagnostic
  - Depth-300 nested dict -> STRUCT_DEPTH_EXCEEDED at depth 256, returns PdfNull at that level
- proptest property: random valid PDF token sequences never panic
- INV-8 maintained

## References

- Plan section: Phase 1.2 lines 1057-1068
- INV-8
- Phase 1.5 (stream decoder consumes the offset and len_hint produced here)
- Phase 1.6 (error recovery for truncated streams)

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement strategy 4 — the forward-scan fallback. When all three previous strategies (traditional, stream, hybrid) fail, the resolver scans the entire file byte-by-byte looking for the indirect-object header pattern `<digits>+ <digits>+ obj\n` and builds an xref map from those discoveries.

This is the last-resort recovery for files where the xref structure is unrecoverable (truncated, severely overwritten, or corrupt to the point of unparseability). It is SLOW (O(file_size)) but correctness-preserving for any object whose `obj` keyword still exists in the file bytes.

## Implementation guidance

- Public API: `forward_scan_xref(source: &PdfSource) -> XrefSection`
- DISABLED FOR REMOTE SOURCES: if source is HttpRangeSource, return empty XrefSection with `STRUCT_REMOTE_NO_FORWARD_SCAN` diagnostic. Forward scan would require fetching the entire file
- DISABLED FOR LINEARIZED FILES: if the linearization detector found a `/Linearized` dict, forward scan must not be used — it would find the partial first-page xref's objects and incorrectly stop. The linearization handler already provides a full-xref fallback for linearized files
- Algorithm:
  1. Iterate file bytes; at each position check if the byte sequence matches the regex `b"^\\d+ \\d+ obj[\\n\\r ]"` (parse N, G, look for `obj` keyword, verify whitespace after)
  2. On a match: record `XrefEntry::InUse { offset, generation }` keyed by `ObjRef { N, G }`; advance past the match
  3. Continue to EOF
  4. Recover the trailer dict by forward-scanning for the `trailer` keyword (also handles `trailer<<` with no space); if found, parse the following dict; otherwise return empty trailer
  5. Emit `XREF_REPAIRED` diagnostic with note "forward scan recovered N objects"

- Optimization: use a SIMD-accelerated byte search (`memchr` crate) to find candidate ` obj` substrings cheaply; then verify the preceding bytes are `\\d+ \\d+ ` to reduce false positives
- Multi-revision handling: in a file with multiple `\trailer` blocks (incremental updates), the forward-scan finds ALL of them; the LAST `trailer` block wins (it's the most recent revision). For each ObjRef, the LAST `obj` occurrence wins (highest byte offset)

## Critical considerations

- Critical test from plan: file truncated after xref — forward scan finds all objects before truncation point
- Critical test from plan: startxref offset off by one — strategies 1-3 fail; forward scan triggered; XREF_REPAIRED diagnostic emitted
- False positive risk: a string literal in a content stream containing literal text like "5 0 obj fake" could be misdetected. Mitigation: scan only OUTSIDE stream bodies. But Phase 1.3's resolver runs BEFORE the object parser, so we don't yet know where streams are. Accept that some false positives may occur; the object parser (Phase 1.2) will reject them when it tries to read at the spurious offset and fails to find a valid object. The resolver emits a warning per spurious entry but does NOT remove it from the map
- Performance budget: forward scan on a 100 MB PDF takes ~1 sec on a fast machine. This is the worst-case path; users with non-corrupt files never hit it
- Memory: build the entry HashMap incrementally; no need to load the whole file in memory thanks to mmap (Phase 1.8 PdfSource)
- The recovered trailer dict may lack `/Root` (catalog ref); Phase 1.4 document model handles missing /Root by emitting STRUCT_MISSING_KEY and returning an empty Document
- Generation number: the forward scan extracts G from the `obj` line; subsequent-revision overrides happen at the /Prev chain merger (not here). For forward scan, the LAST occurrence of `N G obj` in the file wins for that ObjRef

## Acceptance criteria

- Critical test passes: truncated file's recovered objects (those before the truncation point) are all dereferenceable
- Critical test passes: startxref off-by-one triggers forward scan; XREF_REPAIRED emitted
- Forward scan correctly disabled for HttpRangeSource (emits STRUCT_REMOTE_NO_FORWARD_SCAN)
- Forward scan correctly disabled for linearized files
- Performance: 100 MB PDF scan completes in < 5 seconds on a developer machine
- proptest: random byte sequences never panic forward_scan_xref
- INV-8 maintained

## References

- Plan section: Phase 1.3 line 1091 (forward scan); critical test on truncated file + startxref off-by-one
- EC-07 (Corrupt xref)
- Phase 1.8 (PdfSource trait + HttpRangeSource exclusion)
- Dependency Matrix: memchr crate (transitive via std)
