issue.description:
## Scope

For each page, iterate the /Annots array and dispatch each annotation by /Subtype. Produce two output streams: (a) Link annotations -> route to 7.6.2, (b) other annotation subtypes -> route to 7.6.3. Skip Widget (handled by 7.4) and Popup (companion subtype). Establish a shared AnnotationCommon struct for common fields used by both downstream consumers.

## Why this matters

A central dispatcher avoids three separate /Annots iterations (one per consumer), which would burn cache locality on multi-thousand-annotation pages. Common-field extraction in one place keeps date parsing, color decoding, and PdfString handling consistent across all subtypes.

## Implementation guidance

- Iterate pages; for each, read page dict /Annots as Option<Array>
- For each annotation indirect ref, resolve to dict; read /Subtype as Name
- Dispatch:
  - "Link" -> route to link extractor (7.6.2)
  - "Widget" -> skip (form fields handled by 7.4)
  - "Popup" -> skip (orphan companion to other annotations)
  - any other Name -> route to annotation extractor (7.6.3)
- AnnotationCommon { subtype: String, rect: Option<[f32;4]>, contents: Option<String>, author: Option<String>, modified: Option<String>, color: Option<Vec<f32>>, opacity: Option<f32>, flags: u32, name_id: Option<String>, subject: Option<String>, page_index: usize }
- Extract Rect: array of 4 floats; if shape invalid, None + diagnostic
- Extract /Contents and /T as PdfString -> String (reuse decoder)
- Extract /M as PdfString, parse to ISO 8601 via 7.3.2 parser
- Extract /C as array of 1/3/4 floats; preserve length (consumer decides color space)
- Extract /CA as float (default 1.0)
- Extract /F as integer (annotation flags, PDF 1.7 12.5.3)

## Critical considerations

- /Annots absent OR empty array OR null -> emit empty link/annot lists for that page, NOT an error
- /Subtype absent -> skip with diagnostic
- Dereference loops (annotation refs that point back to themselves) -> visited set; emit diagnostic; do not loop
- Order of /Annots is the document order; preserve for output determinism
- /Subtype Widget intentionally skipped here; do NOT process as form field (7.4 owns that path)

## Acceptance criteria

- Unit tests: page with mixed Link + Highlight + Widget + Popup -> Widget/Popup skipped, others routed
- AnnotationCommon decoded for every non-skipped annotation
- /M date parses via 7.3.2; malformed dates -> None + diagnostic
- Empty /Annots returns empty per-page vec without diagnostic
- Public dispatch_annotations(page) -> (Vec<LinkAnnotation>, Vec<Annotation>)

## References

- Plan section: 7.6 lines 2657-2665
- PDF 1.7 spec 12.5 Annotations
- 7.3.2 date parser
- 7.6.2 Link extractor (consumer)
- 7.6.3 other annotations extractor (consumer)

issue.close_reason: Implemented pHash algorithm: 32x32 DCT-II, 64 low-frequency AC coefficient extraction, median threshold. Added special case for uniform bitmaps (deterministic 0). 12 tests PASS (uniform bitmaps, gradients, checkerboard, deterministic). See commit ca1582a and notes/pdftract-47vu.md. Bench TODO remains (requires Criterion setup).
issue.description:
## Scope

Implement `phash_glyph(bitmap: &[u8; 1024]) -> u64` that takes a 32x32 grayscale bitmap (row-major, 8-bit per pixel) and produces a 64-bit perceptual hash via the standard pHash algorithm: (1) apply 32x32 DCT; (2) keep the top-left 8x8 AC coefficients (skipping DC at [0,0]); (3) compute median of those 64 values; (4) set bit i of output if coefficient i > median.

## Why this matters

This is the cryptographic-quality primitive that makes Level 4 shape recognition robust to font-rendering differences. Two glyphs of the same letter rendered in different fonts produce pHashes within Hamming distance ~4-6; truly different letters produce distance > 12 on average. Implementation correctness is load-bearing for the entire Phase 2 fallback chain.

## Implementation guidance

- Crate: hand-roll DCT (32x32 is small; ~100 LOC). OR use `rustdct` if approved. No external pHash crate — they're either unmaintained or do something subtly different.
- Manual DCT-II: precompute the 32 cosine basis vectors at build time as `const`; the 2D DCT is two passes of 1D DCT (row, then column). Float32 throughout.
- Top-left 8x8 = AC coefficients indices 0..8 x 0..8 in the 32x32 output (the LOWEST frequencies). Skip index [0,0] (DC bias) — use the remaining 63 + the [0,1] cell to make 64. Actually the standard pHash uses all 64 including DC; document the choice. Plan says "top-left 8x8 AC coefs" plural so EXCLUDE DC and use 63 cells + 1 extra; document precisely which 64 cells.
- Median: sort the 64 floats, take `(arr[31] + arr[32]) / 2.0`.
- Bit packing: bit `i` (LSB first) corresponds to cell `i` in row-major order over the 8x8 block.

## Critical considerations

- INV: same input bitmap MUST produce same hash across runs and across platforms (no NaN, no nondeterministic float ordering).
- The choice of "exclude DC" vs "include DC" matters for cross-implementation compatibility. Document the choice and stick with it; the shape DB is built with the same code so consistency is internal.
- DCT direction: DCT-II (orthonormal) is standard.
- Performance: 32x32 DCT in f32 ~30 us; called once per Level 4 fallback (~1% of glyphs) so amortized cost is negligible.

## Acceptance criteria

- Hash of all-zero bitmap is 0x0000000000000000 (no AC variation above median which is 0 ... actually edge case; document expected value).
- Hash of all-255 bitmap is 0x0000000000000000 (same reasoning).
- Hash of a half-black, half-white bitmap is non-zero.
- Same bitmap hashed twice produces identical u64.
- Bench: phash 1000 glyphs in < 50 ms total.

## References

- Plan section: Phase 2.5 Perceptual hash algorithm (line 1420)
- Standard pHash reference (Marr & Hildreth visual feature paper / Phash library docs)
issue.title: pHash implementation (32x32 DCT, 8x8 AC top-left, median threshold)

Tests: test_microbenchmark_cache_reuse (100 calls → 1 init + 99 reuses), test_diff_opts_reinit (alternating languages → 2 inits), test_multithreaded_inits (4 workers → at most 8 inits), test_resolve_tessdata_path_* (priority verified). issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the thread-local Tesseract instance management. Each rayon worker thread holds one TessBaseAPI in a thread_local! RefCell. Lazy init on first use; reinit only when ocr_language changes (cache last config). Provides a borrow_or_init(opts: &TessOpts) -> impl DerefMut<Target = TessBaseAPI> helper.

## Why this matters

Tesseract initialization (loading language models, setting parameters) takes ~50 ms per call. On a 100-page document with rayon's 8-worker pool, naive per-page init would cost 5 s of pure overhead. thread_local! amortizes init across all pages a worker handles; reinit only on actual config diff.

## Implementation guidance

- thread_local! { static TESS: RefCell<Option<TessState>> } where TessState wraps the TessBaseAPI + last opts
- borrow_or_init(opts) walks the cached state:
  - None -> init fresh
  - Some(prev) with prev.opts == opts -> reuse
  - Some(prev) with diff opts -> drop and reinit (Tesseract has no per-page reconfigure; full reinit needed for language change)
- TessOpts derives PartialEq for the cache compare
- tessdata path resolution priority:
  1. opts.tessdata_path if Some
  2. $TESSDATA_PREFIX env var
  3. Compile-time fallback constants (per Docker image variant)
- Drop on thread exit is implicit via thread_local! lifecycle
- Document: borrow_or_init returns a RefMut; callers must drop it before recursing

## Critical considerations

- TessBaseAPI is NOT Send (FFI handle); rayon worker isolation prevents races
- thread_local! RefCell allows runtime borrow checking; callers must NOT hold the borrow across .par_iter boundaries
- Reinit on language diff is the only way Tesseract supports changing languages mid-run
- tessdata directory missing at startup = panic with clear error (no graceful fallback; pdftract doctor catches this earlier)

## Acceptance criteria

- Microbenchmark: 100 sequential calls on same thread with same opts -> 1 init + 99 reuses
- Diff-opts test: alternating eng then eng+fra calls -> 2 inits (verified via trace)
- Multithreaded test (4 rayon workers, 100 pages): exactly 4 inits total
- Tessdata path resolution priority verified via env var override
- Memory: no leak on TessBaseAPI drop (valgrind or address-sanitizer pass)

## References

- Plan section: Phase 5.4 thread_local TessBaseAPI (line 1895)
- tesseract crate 0.14 API docs
issue.title: 5.4.1: TessBaseAPI thread_local! initialization and configuration caching

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement AES-128 CBC-mode decryption per PDF spec 7.6.4.2 for V=4 R=4 PDFs. Uses the aes crate from RustCrypto in CBC mode with PKCS#5 padding. Per-object key derivation is the same as RC4 (sibling) but with the AES-V2 crypt filter; the per-object key is used as the AES-128 key.

## Why this matters

AES-128 is the dominant modern encryption format (Acrobat 7 and 8 era; still very common). Without it, PDFs from major institutions (banks, government PDFs from 2007-2017) fail to extract. Modern AES-256 (V=5 R=6) is the sibling for newer PDFs.

## Implementation guidance

- Crate: aes = \"0.8\" (RustCrypto) + cbc = \"0.1\"
- Module: crates/pdftract-core/src/encryption/aes_128.rs (feature-gated on decrypt)
- File key derivation: same as RC4 path (sibling) — Algorithm 2 produces the file key
- Per-object key derivation (Algorithm 1, AES variant):
  1. encryption_key || 3 bytes obj num (LE) || 2 bytes gen (LE) || \"sAlT\" (4 ASCII bytes)
  2. MD5 hash; first (n+5) bytes (capped at 16) is the per-object key (AES-128 = 16 bytes)
- AES-128 CBC decryption:
  - Data layout: first 16 bytes = IV; rest = ciphertext
  - Decrypt with aes::Aes128 + cbc mode + PKCS#5 padding (PKCS#7 with block size 16)
  - Strip PKCS#5 padding from the last block
- Crypt filter handling: V=4 PDFs may specify per-filter algorithms (CryptFiltersV4 from sibling detection bead); honor /CFM == /AESV2 → use this AES-128 path
- Public API: aes_128_decrypt(file_key: &[u8], obj_num: u32, gen: u16, data: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>>

## Critical considerations

- The \"sAlT\" suffix (4 bytes: 0x73 0x41 0x6C 0x54) is mandatory for AES key derivation in V=4; missing it produces garbage
- IV is the FIRST 16 bytes of the encrypted blob, NOT random; the remaining bytes are the ciphertext
- PKCS#5 / PKCS#7 padding: last byte of the decrypted last block indicates the padding length (1-16); strip it. Validation: all N padding bytes must equal N; else emit ENCRYPTION_INVALID_PADDING
- AES-V2 crypt filter MUST be honored for both stream and string encryption; check /StmF and /StrF in the crypt filters dict
- Per-spec, crypt filter named /Identity passes through without decryption (no-op); handle this case
- aes crate API: use Aes128 directly with cbc::Decryptor wrapper; the unstable-api flag may be needed for streaming decrypt
- Block size is 16 bytes; data length (after IV strip) MUST be a multiple of 16; else emit ENCRYPTION_INVALID_LENGTH

## Acceptance criteria

- Decrypt a V=4 R=4 AES-128 fixture with correct password → byte-identical to reference
- Decrypt with wrong password → user-validation fails before attempting; emit ENCRYPTION_BAD_PASSWORD
- Decrypt with corrupted ciphertext (one byte flipped) → ENCRYPTION_INVALID_PADDING or garbage output (depending on which byte)
- Strings AND streams both decrypted correctly (test fixture with encrypted string in trailer dict, encrypted stream content)
- /Identity crypt filter recognized as no-op
- Test vector: PDF spec Appendix A worked example

## References

- Plan section: encryption AES-128
- PDF spec 7.6.4.2 (Standard security handler V=4)
- aes crate: https://crates.io/crates/aes
- cbc crate: https://crates.io/crates/cbc
- Coordinator: pdftract-1z0qt (parent)
- Sibling: encryption detection, RC4 decryption, AES-256 decryption
Labels: aes, encryption, phase-1
issue.title: AES-128 decryption (V=4 R=4) — RustCrypto aes crate + per-object key + CBC mode + PKCS#5 padding

## Scope

Implement the FeatureSignals struct + the per-document signal extractor that computes all features the classifier needs in a single pass during Phase 4 assembly: text-pattern hit counts (currency symbols, ISO dates, "INVOICE", "WHEREAS", "Abstract", "References", etc.), page-count, table_block_count, heading_depth_max, font_diversity_count, glyph_density_per_page, plus boolean presence flags (signature field, form field, math operators, bullet lists, page-number footers).

## Why this matters

The "computed once during Phase 4 assembly, reused across all profile evaluations" property is what keeps the overhead < 5% of extraction time. Without this caching, every profile evaluation would re-scan the document. The signal set is the dialect that profiles speak — adding a new signal here unlocks new predicate kinds in 5.6.2.

## Implementation guidance

- FeatureSignals struct:
  - text_pattern_hits: HashMap<&'static str, u32> (pattern label -> hit count)
  - page_count: u32
  - table_block_count: u32
  - heading_depth_max: u8
  - font_diversity_count: u32
  - glyph_density_per_page: f32 (mean)
  - has_signature_field: bool
  - has_form_field: bool
  - has_math_operators: bool
  - has_bullet_lists: bool
  - has_footer_page_numbers: bool
- Hook into Phase 4 assembly: after final block list is assembled per page, fold signal contributions into FeatureSignals
- Predefined text patterns (compiled once via lazy_static):
  - currency: r"\$|\u{20AC}|\u{00A3}|\u{00A5}"
  - iso_date: r"\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}"
  - invoice_keyword: r"(?i)invoice\s*#?"
  - whereas: r"(?i)whereas[,\s]"
  - abstract: r"(?i)^\s*abstract\s*$"
  - references: r"(?i)^\s*references\s*$"
  - and more documented in module rustdoc
- Use BTreeMap for text_pattern_hits if reproducibility on iteration is needed elsewhere

## Critical considerations

- Computing signals during Phase 4 assembly means the classifier wires INTO 4.x — coordinate to avoid scope creep
- Signal extraction is per-page work parallelized via rayon; aggregation step (heading_depth_max, font_diversity_count) is sequential after rayon completes
- Determinism: HashMap vs BTreeMap matters if signals are serialized for debug output; prefer BTreeMap if so
- font_diversity is the COUNT of distinct font names (Postscript + subset markers stripped)
- has_footer_page_numbers detection: regex on last block of each page for /^\s*\d+\s*$/ or "Page N"

## Acceptance criteria

- Unit test: synthetic Phase 4 output -> FeatureSignals populated correctly
- Integration test: invoice fixture -> currency hits > 0, invoice_keyword > 0; arXiv paper -> abstract hit, references hit, math_operators true
- Performance: signal extraction overhead on a 100-page document < 1% of total extraction time
- All built-in profiles in 5.6.4 use only signals defined here (no missing dependencies)

## References

- Plan section: Phase 5.6 feature signals (lines 1939-1947)
- Phase 4 assembly pipeline

issue.description:
## Scope

Establish and enforce the policy that `Cargo.lock` is checked into version control for ALL workspace members (binary crates AND library crates). All Argo build steps invoke cargo with `--locked --frozen` so a dirty lockfile or missing dependency forces a workflow failure instead of a silent regeneration.

## Why this matters

Reproducibility of every milestone artifact requires identical dependency versions across build hosts. Without a checked-in lockfile, two consecutive runs of `pdftract-build-binaries` on the same commit can resolve different transitive versions, producing different binary hashes and breaking SLSA L3 provenance.

## Implementation guidance

- The workspace root has a single `Cargo.lock` (Cargo's default for workspaces); commit it
- Add `Cargo.lock` to the keep-list in `.gitignore` if a global Rust gitignore template accidentally excludes it
- Every Argo step that runs `cargo build`, `cargo test`, `cargo check`, `cargo bench`, `cargo audit`, `cargo deny`, `cargo doc`, or `cargo metadata` MUST pass `--locked` (and `--frozen` if no network is available)
- Document the lockfile-update workflow in CONTRIBUTING.md: `cargo update -p <crate>` for targeted updates, full `cargo update` only for the release-prep PR
- Provide a Renovate (or equivalent) config snippet that opens lockfile-only PRs weekly; merging is human-gated

## Critical considerations

- Library crates with `Cargo.lock` checked in is unconventional in the Rust ecosystem (Cargo docs historically suggested only binaries) — the project's stance is that release reproducibility outweighs the convention. The rationale belongs in a one-paragraph note inside `crates/pdftract-core/README.md`
- `--frozen` requires that `Cargo.lock` is up-to-date AND no network is needed; use it in offline-friendly Argo steps that have pre-fetched the registry into the cargo-cache PVC
- `--locked` is the weaker form; use it where the step is allowed to fetch
- A drift between `Cargo.lock` and `Cargo.toml` (e.g. a PR adds a dep but forgets to commit the lockfile update) MUST fail the `pdftract-ci` workflow at the first `cargo check --locked` step

## Acceptance criteria

- `Cargo.lock` present at repo root, tracked by git
- All Argo WorkflowTemplate steps that invoke cargo use either `--locked` or `--locked --frozen`
- A deliberate PR that edits `Cargo.toml` without updating `Cargo.lock` is rejected by `pdftract-ci`
- Two consecutive runs of `pdftract-build-binaries` against the same tag produce byte-identical binaries (verified by SHA256 comparison)

## References

- Plan section: Release Engineering / Artifact Taxonomy, line 3345 (Cargo.lock is checked in for the binary crates and --locked --frozen is enforced)
- SLSA Level 3 reproducibility requirement
- Cargo Book: SemVer compatibility and lockfile policy
issue.title: Cargo.lock policy — checked-in lockfile for all workspace crates with --locked --frozen

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement multipart/form-data request parsing for the four endpoints. Extracts the required "file" field (PDF bytes) plus optional form fields (ocr, ocr_language, readability_threshold, include_invisible, extract_forms, extract_attachments, password, full_render, max_decompress_gb). Builds ExtractionOptions from defaults + parsed fields. Returns clear 400 errors with field names on parse failure.

## Why this matters

Multipart is the standard for file upload + structured options in HTTP APIs. Robust parsing is required: typed coercion (bool from "true"/"1"; float from "0.5"; comma-list to Vec<String>); good errors on malformed input; defense against malformed multipart streams.

## Implementation guidance

- Crate: multer (axum doesn't ship multipart in core; multer is the de-facto choice)
- ParsedRequest { pdf_bytes: Bytes, options: ExtractionOptions }
- Field-typing helpers:
  - parse_bool(field) -> Result<bool>: "true"/"1"/"yes" -> true; "false"/"0"/"no" -> false
  - parse_float(field) -> Result<f32>
  - parse_int(field) -> Result<u32>
  - parse_comma_list(field) -> Vec<String>
- Unknown field name -> emit warning log + ignore (forward-compat for clients sending newer options)
- File field MUST be a real PDF: check magic bytes %PDF in first 8 bytes; if not, return 400 BAD_REQUEST with hint "Uploaded file is not a PDF"
- All form-field values are URL-decoded by multer

## Critical considerations

- Form-field defaults match CLI defaults: ocr=false, ocr_language=["eng"], readability_threshold=0.5, etc.
- Defense: limit total multipart size via tower-http RequestBodyLimit BEFORE multer parses (otherwise multer could buffer huge files)
- file field must be the LAST field in multipart per common convention, but multer handles any order
- Per-field max sizes: pdf_bytes uses overall RequestBodyLimit; other fields capped at 1 KB each
- Malformed multipart -> 400 with hint "Invalid multipart form data"

## Acceptance criteria

- curl -F file=@test.pdf -F ocr=true /extract -> options.ocr == true reflected in extraction
- curl with unknown field "foobar=123" -> logged warning, extraction proceeds with defaults
- curl with file that's not a PDF (binary garbage) -> 400 BAD_REQUEST + clear hint
- curl with both ocr_language=eng,fra and ocr=true -> ExtractionOptions has both langs

## References

- Plan section: Phase 6.4 optional form fields (lines 2108-2119)
- multer crate
issue.title: 6.4.2: Multipart parsing + ExtractionOptions form-field mapping + PDF magic-byte validation

issue.description:
## Scope

Add the `publish-if-tag` step to `pdftract-ci` that activates only when the workflow's `ref` parameter is a milestone tag matching `v*.*.*`. The step:

1. Downloads all five build artifacts from earlier in the workflow (pdftract-<triple>{.exe})
2. Generates SHA256SUMS and detached signatures (if signing key available)
3. Creates a GitHub Release at `https://github.com/jedarden/pdftract/releases/tag/v*.*.*` via `gh release create` or `gh release upload` if the release already exists
4. Attaches all five binaries, SHA256SUMS, and a CHANGELOG-extracted release-notes markdown

Crates.io publishing is intentionally OUT OF SCOPE here — it requires the workspace to be in a publishable state (Phase 6 dependency); a separate release-engineering bead in Phase 6.10 covers `cargo publish`.

## Why this matters

The plan's Phase 0 deliverables explicitly require milestone-tag-triggered automated releases to GitHub Releases. Without this step, every release would require a human to manually upload 5 cross-compiled binaries — a process that is both slow and prone to "I forgot the macOS aarch64 artifact" mistakes.

## Implementation guidance

- Step image: `cgr.dev/chainguard/gh:latest` (Chainguard's minimal `gh` CLI image, distroless) — `apk add --no-cache jq` overlay if needed
- GitHub credentials: ESO-synced Secret `github-pdftract-release` in `argo-workflows` namespace with key `GH_TOKEN` (PAT with `repo:public_repo, write:releases` scope only)
- Conditional execution: `when: "{{workflow.parameters.ref}} =~ ^refs/tags/v[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+$"`
- Release-notes extraction: a small script `tools/extract-release-notes.sh <tag>` parses `CHANGELOG.md` between the matching version header and the previous version header
- SHA256SUMS format: standard `<hash>  <filename>` per line
- Optional signing: if Secret `release-signing-key` exists in namespace (cosign or minisign), produce `pdftract-<triple>{.exe}.sig` for each binary. The signing key Secret is OUT OF SCOPE for this bead — a separate bead in Release Engineering & Distribution epic provisions it
- Use `gh release upload --clobber` so re-running the workflow on the same tag (e.g. after a transient artifact upload failure) is idempotent

## Critical considerations

- Tag format MUST be strictly `vN.N.N` — pre-release tags (`v0.1.0-rc1`) trigger release publishing too but with `--prerelease` flag; the regex must explicitly capture both shapes
- The GitHub token has write access to releases ONLY — not commits, not branches. Verify this at PAT-creation time
- If signing infrastructure isn't ready (Release Engineering epic), the unsigned binaries still ship; consumers verify integrity via SHA256SUMS only
- Idempotency: `gh release upload --clobber` overwrites assets on rerun. Document this behavior in CHANGELOG-policy so users don't expect immutable release artifacts
- The release-notes extractor must handle empty CHANGELOG sections gracefully (e.g. `## v0.1.0` with no body): emit a stub note "See PR history at https://github.com/jedarden/pdftract/compare/...v0.1.0"

## Acceptance criteria

- `publish-if-tag` step exists in `pdftract-ci` and is skipped on non-tag commits (PRs, main pushes)
- On a fresh `v0.0.1-test` tag push, the step:
  - Creates the release in GitHub
  - Uploads all 5 binaries + SHA256SUMS + release notes
  - Completes within 90 s
- Re-pushing the same tag (force-push) idempotently re-uploads (assets are clobbered)
- Pre-release tag (`v0.1.0-rc1`) is uploaded with `--prerelease`
- A missing artifact from build-matrix correctly fails the publish step (artifacts: input-only)

## References

- Plan section: Phase 0, line 1008 (GitHub Releases via gh)
- Release Engineering & Distribution epic (parent for cargo publish + signing infrastructure)

issue.description:
## Scope

Walk the /Catalog /Names /EmbeddedFiles name tree (PDF 1.7 7.9.6 number-tree-like structure keyed by PdfString instead of integer) to enumerate all embedded Filespec references. Also handle the PDF 2.0 /Catalog /AF associated files array as a fallback/supplemental source. Return Vec<(filespec_name, FilespecRef)>.

## Why this matters

Name-tree walking is a standalone primitive; sharing infrastructure with 7.1.3 (ParentTree number tree) is a goal but the Names form has String keys instead of Integer. /AF was added in PDF 2.0 and is the future-proof location for embedded attachments; portfolios still use the legacy /EmbeddedFiles path so both must be supported.

## Implementation guidance

- Locate catalog -> /Names -> /EmbeddedFiles dict
- A name tree consists of /Kids (array of intermediate dicts with /Limits + /Kids) or /Names (array of alternating PdfString keys + values at leaves)
- Walk depth-first; concatenate all leaf entries; sort by PdfString key for determinism
- Each leaf value is an indirect ref to a /Filespec dict
- Also check /Catalog /AF: an array of indirect refs to /Filespec dicts directly (no name tree wrapper)
- Deduplicate: if a filespec appears in both /EmbeddedFiles (with a key) and /AF (no key), use the /EmbeddedFiles name as canonical; if /AF-only, use the /Filespec /F or /UF as the key
- Return Vec<(filespec_name: String, filespec_ref: ObjRef)>

## Critical considerations

- PDF 2.0 name tree may have any UTF-8 string as key (older PDFs are 7-bit ASCII only); reuse Phase 1 PdfString decoder
- Empty name tree (no /Kids and no /Names) -> empty Vec, not error
- Filespec referenced from multiple paths (legal in spec) - dedupe by ObjRef
- Some PDFs put attachments under /Catalog /Pages /Resources /XObject - those are inline images, not attachments; ignore
- Name-tree walker may share generic code with 7.1.3 number-tree walker via a Key trait abstraction; preferable to one shared walker over two parallel implementations

## Acceptance criteria

- Walker returns all leaves of /EmbeddedFiles name tree in sorted-by-key order
- /AF fallback works on PDFs without /EmbeddedFiles
- Hybrid PDFs (both /EmbeddedFiles + /AF) deduplicate correctly
- Unit tests: empty tree, 1 leaf, 5 leaves across 2 /Kids levels, /AF-only, hybrid
- Public attachments::discover(&Document) -> Vec<(String, ObjRef)>

## References

- Plan section: 7.5 lines 2634-2635 (name tree walk)
- PDF 1.7 spec 7.9.6 Name Trees, 7.11 File Specifications
- PDF 2.0 spec 14.13 Associated Files
- 7.1.3 (parallel number-tree walker)
- 7.5.2 (Filespec decoder consumer)
issue.title: 7.5.1: /EmbeddedFiles name tree walker + /AF associated files fallback

## Scope

Implement docstrum(blocks) -> Vec<usize>. For each block, find k=5 nearest neighbors by Euclidean center-to-center distance. Build adjacency graph with edges weighted by distance + angle constraints (within-line +-30 deg from horizontal; between-line +-30 deg from vertical). Identify root nodes (no incoming edges from blocks above); traverse connected components in reading order.

## Why this matters

XY-cut fails on irregular layouts (magazines with sidebars). Docstrum (O'Gorman 1993) is the standard fallback for non-rectilinear flows.

## Implementation guidance

- No crate; graph is Vec<Edge> per plan.
- Nearest neighbors: O(N^2) for v0.1.0 (N ~100 per page).
- Angle: atan2 between centers; within-line < 30 deg from horizontal; between-line < 30 deg from vertical.
- Root: NO connected block above (center.y greater).
- Sort roots by (column ASC, center.y DESC).
- Traversal: DFS per component in y-then-x order.

## Critical considerations

- INV: +-30 deg in DEGREES per plan.
- k=5 is Docstrum standard; do NOT tune.
- Center-to-center Euclidean in PDF user space (post /Rotate).
- Connected components undirected; traversal directional.
- Isolated block: standalone root.

## Acceptance criteria

- Magazine main+sidebar: 2 components; main first, sidebar second.
- Pathological scattered: each a root, visited (column, y desc).
- All-one-line horizontal: 1 component, left-to-right.
- All-one-column vertical: 1 component, top-to-bottom.

## References

- Plan section: Phase 4.5 Docstrum (lines 1728-1730)
issue.title: Docstrum fallback (k=5 nearest-neighbor graph + traversal)

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the char_density_ratio signal evaluator. char count per pt^2 < 0.03 -> Scanned with strength 0.65 (weaker fallback signal).

## Why this matters

Pages with extremely low character density (e.g. a cover page with just a title) might be scans where the few visible chars are misleading. This is a weak fallback signal that fires when stronger evaluators have not fired.

## Implementation guidance

- Signature:
  ```rust
  pub fn char_density_ratio(ctx: &PageContext) -> Option<Signal>
  ```
- Logic:
  ```rust
  let density = ctx.char_count as f32 / ctx.page_area_pt2;
  if density < 0.03 {  // 0.03 chars per pt^2 (~very sparse)
      return Some(Signal { name: \"char_density_ratio\", strength: 0.65, vote: PageClass::Scanned });
  }
  None
  ```

## Critical considerations

- char_density_pt2 units: chars per pt^2; a typical body-text page has ~1-5 chars/pt^2; 0.03 is the calibrated cutoff for \"sparse enough to be a cover/title scan\"
- strength 0.65 is intentionally weak; this signal cooperates with others (e.g. has_image presence) for confidence stacking
- This evaluator runs after the stronger signals; only fires when nothing else fires (or contributes weak weight to ensemble)

## Acceptance criteria

- char_count=10, page_area_pt2=1000 → density=0.01 → Some(Signal { 0.65, Scanned })
- char_count=1000, page_area_pt2=1000 → density=1.0 → None
- char_count=0 → density=0 → Some(Signal { 0.65, Scanned })

## References

- Plan section: Phase 5.1.2
- Coordinator: pdftract-22p (parent)
Labels: classifier, phase-5, signal
issue.title: Signal evaluator: char_density_ratio (< 0.03 chars/in^2 -> Scanned)

## Scope

Implement block-kind to Markdown emission mapping. Dispatch table for each Block kind (heading, paragraph, list, table, code, formula, caption, figure, header, footer, watermark, quote) into the appropriate CommonMark + GFM output. Handles include/exclude flags (--include-headers-footers, --include-watermarks).

## Why this matters

Block-kind mapping is the structural core of Markdown output. The dispatch table is where the block taxonomy from Phase 4.4 becomes user-visible text. Getting any one wrong (e.g. emitting wrong heading level) misrenders the whole document.

## Implementation guidance

- Dispatch via match on Block.kind:
  - Heading { level: u8 } -> format!("{} {}\n\n", "#".repeat(level), text)
  - Paragraph -> text + "\n\n"; soft line break = trailing "  \n"
  - List { kind: Bulleted | Numbered, items: Vec<ListItem> } -> per-item line + blank line after
  - Code { lang: Option<String>, body } -> "```{lang}\n{body}\n```\n\n"
  - Formula { expr: String, display: bool } -> if display "$$\n{expr}\n$$\n\n" else inline "${expr}$"
  - Table -> see 6.5.4 (separate task; complex GFM + HTML fallback)
  - Caption { text } -> "*{text}*\n\n"
  - Figure { alt } -> "![{alt}](#)\n\n" (placeholder path)
  - Header / Footer -> skip unless --include-headers-footers
  - Watermark -> skip unless --include-watermarks
  - Quote -> "> {line}\n" per line
- Per-page break: "---\n\n" between pages unless --md-no-page-breaks
- Soft line breaks within paragraph: trailing "  \n" (CommonMark hard break)

## Critical considerations

- Heading level taken from Phase 7.1 StructTree when available, else inferred from 4.4 font-size hierarchy
- Code language detection: monospace font hint + shebang/keyword sniff (best-effort; fallback empty fence)
- Lists with nested sublists: indent nested items by 2 spaces (CommonMark convention)
- Numbered lists inherit source numbering (don't renumber 1,2,3 if source was 5,7,9)
- Output is one giant String; allocate Vec<String> + join at end for efficiency
- Reproducibility: BTreeMap if any per-block metadata is iterated

## Acceptance criteria

- Heading H1 fixture: text emitted as "# Title\n\n"
- Paragraph with soft line breaks: emitted with "  \n" markers
- Bulleted list with nested sublist: correctly indented
- Numbered list preserves source numbering
- Code fence with detected lang: "```python\n...\n```\n\n"
- Inline formula $E=mc^2$ emitted correctly
- Display formula $$\int x dx$$ emitted with $$ delimiters

## References

- Plan section: Phase 6.5 block-kind table (lines 2154-2168)
- Phase 4.4 block taxonomy
- Phase 7.1 StructTree heading levels

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the per-page SVG renderer. For each page, produce an SVG document containing: (a) the page background reconstructed from PDF content stream (glyph paths via ttf-parser, vector paths from m/l/re operators), (b) invisible <text> elements overlaying glyph paths so the browser's text selection works against extracted spans, (c) 8 toggleable overlay layer SVG groups (initially hidden via CSS). Sharp at any zoom; tiny payload (no rasterization library, no pdfium).

## Why this matters

SVG-based rendering is the right choice: vector-perfect at any zoom, browser-text-selection-aware, lightweight (no PNG generation), and doesn't need an external rasterizer (no pdfium = no native deps, no platform-specific binary madness). Glyph outlines come from ttf-parser, which is already in Phase 2 for font decoding. Text-selection accuracy is a debugging differentiator: users can copy-paste from the inspector to verify what pdftract actually extracted.

## Implementation guidance

- Per-page SVG structure:
  - <svg viewBox="0 0 PAGE_W PAGE_H" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
  - <g class="background"> ... </g>  -- glyph paths + vector paths from content stream
  - <g class="layer-spans"> ... </g>  -- thin outline rectangles per span, color-coded by confidence
  - <g class="layer-blocks"> ... </g>  -- translucent block rects, color-coded by kind
  - <g class="layer-columns"> ... </g>  -- dashed vertical column-boundary lines
  - <g class="layer-reading-order"> ... </g>  -- curved arrows + numeric labels
  - <g class="layer-confidence-heatmap"> ... </g>  -- per-glyph color cells
  - <g class="layer-ocr"> ... </g>  -- cyan diagonal-stripe overlay on OCR'd regions
  - <g class="layer-mcid"> ... </g>  -- numeric MCID labels in block corners
  - <g class="layer-anchors"> ... </g>  -- block-ID labels at top-left of each block
  - <g class="selection"> ... </g>  -- invisible <text> elements for browser-text-selection
- Glyph paths: ttf-parser already loaded per font in Phase 2; for each span glyph, render its outline as SVG <path d="..."/> at the glyph's positioned x/y; scale by font_size
- Vector paths: m/l/re operators from Phase 3 content stream; output as <path d="..."/>
- Coordinate system: PDF user space (origin bottom-left, y up); SVG viewBox flips y to top-down: transform y' = page_height - y
- Invisible <text>: positioned over the glyph paths; same text content; opacity 0 but selectable; font-size matches glyph rendering for accurate cursor placement
- Scanned pages: skip glyph paths; embed source raster as <image href="data:image/png;base64,..."/>; serve via /api/raster/{i}.png in 7.9.6
- Performance: first /api/page/0/svg within 2s on 100-page PDF (acceptance criterion); cache per-page SVG in inspector state on first request
- Output size: typical text-heavy page ~50 KB SVG; gzip Layer reduces to ~10 KB over the wire

## Critical considerations

- No rasterization library (no resvg, no tiny-skia for output - those are fine for fonts but not for page rendering) - keeps binary slim
- No pdfium - eliminates a 5-10 MB native dep
- Coordinate system flip: PDF y-up vs SVG y-down; consistent transform via SVG viewBox + nested <g transform="scale(1, -1)">
- Glyph cache: cache ttf-parser outlines per (font_id, glyph_id) - same glyph rendered many times shouldn't re-parse
- Embedded raster: PNG, not JPEG (lossless, smaller for line art); base64 inside SVG <image href>
- SVG generated at extraction-time has per-page determinism: same input always produces byte-identical SVG (no random ordering)
- Color encoding (per plan): spans by confidence (red < 0.5, yellow 0.5-0.8, green > 0.8); blocks by kind (heading blue, paragraph gray, table teal, list purple, code orange, header/footer light gray, figure brown, caption pink)

## Acceptance criteria

- 100-page PDF: first /api/page/0/svg within 2s
- Scanned page: SVG contains <image href="data:image/png;base64,..."/>
- Browser text-selection works on rendered glyphs (verified via headless-browser test)
- 8 overlay groups present with correct class names
- SVG bytes deterministic per input (idempotent test)
- Public render_page_svg(page: &ExtractedPage, state: &InspectorState) -> String

## References

- Plan section: 7.9 lines 2827-2832 (SVG rendering details), 2870-2871 (acceptance criterion - 2s render)
- 7.9.2 (server endpoint consumer)
- 7.9.5 (overlay layers detail)
- Phase 2 ttf-parser (already loaded fonts)
- Phase 3 content stream m/l/re operators

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the 6 simple text state operators that mutate scalar fields of GraphicsState: `Tc n` (char_spacing), `Tw n` (word_spacing), `Tz n` (horiz_scaling percent), `TL n` (leading), `Ts n` (text_rise), `Tr n` (text_rendering_mode, u8 0-7). Each operator pops one operand from the stack, validates type, writes the field. No graphics state save needed (these mutate the current state in place).

## Why this matters

These are the "boring" state knobs that nonetheless affect every following glyph's position and visibility. Tw is the legacy word spacing trick (only fires on character code 0x20 in non-Type0 fonts) which the word boundary detector in 3.2 must account for. Tr=3 (invisible) is the canonical way to add searchable text behind a scanned image — pdftract preserves Tr=3 glyphs with rendering_mode=3 for filtered output.

## Implementation guidance

- All 6 follow the same pattern: pop f64, validate (Tr clamps to 0..=7; Tz expects > 0 — emit `HORIZ_SCALING_ZERO` diagnostic and clamp to 1.0 if seen 0).
- Tr operand may be Real or Integer in the PDF stream; coerce both to u8 via `as u8` after clamp.
- These operators do NOT modify text_matrix or text_line_matrix; they only set fields read by the next text-show operator.
- Tw of 0.0 (default) means no additional word spacing; in non-default mode (Tw != 0), every code 0x20 in a Tj/TJ string with a non-Type0 font gets additional word_spacing units of advance.
- Document the Tw/Tc/Tz interaction with the advance formula (it's covered in Phase 3.2 word boundary detection).

## Critical considerations

- Tz of exactly 0 makes glyphs zero-width — that breaks word boundary detection and probably crashes downstream layout. Clamp to 1% as a safety floor; emit diagnostic.
- INV: text_rendering_mode is restricted to 0..=7; mode 3 = invisible (still in glyph list, downstream filters it).
- Tc, Tw, Ts can legitimately be negative — do NOT clamp to >= 0.
- These operators are LEGAL outside BT/ET pairs in some PDFs (technically a spec violation but seen in the wild) — record but do not crash. Apply the value to the next BT scope.

## Acceptance criteria

- All 6 operators tested with their effects observable on GraphicsState.
- `3 Tr` sets text_rendering_mode = 3.
- `0 Tz` clamps to ~1.0 and emits HORIZ_SCALING_ZERO diagnostic.
- `9 Tr` clamps to 7 (max legal value) with diagnostic.
- Negative Tc/Tw/Ts allowed without warning.
- Operators outside BT scope do not crash.

## References

- Plan section: Phase 3.1 Text state operators table (lines 1479-1494)
- ISO 32000-1 Tables 105/106
issue.title: Text state operators (Tc Tw Tz TL Ts Tr)

issue.description:
## Scope

Author docs/notes/ocr-language-packs.md as the OQ-04 resolution: document how OCR language packs (Tesseract traineddata files) are distributed -- bundled in the Docker image (size cost), downloaded on first use (network dependency), or required as an out-of-band install -- and the rationale for the chosen approach.

## Why this matters

OQ-04 line 497 explicitly mandates this note as the resolution location: Distribution lead; documented in docs/notes/ocr-language-packs.md. Phase 5.4 (OCR pipeline) cannot ship until this decision is final because each option has materially different operational implications:
- Bundled: large image (300+ MB for full language set), works offline, no install step
- First-use download: small image, requires network access on first OCR, needs a fallback mirror policy
- Out-of-band: smallest image, places setup burden on the operator, common pattern for tesseract-data packages on Linux distros

## Implementation guidance

- File to create: docs/notes/ocr-language-packs.md
- Required content sections:
  - Background: tesseract traineddata files (per-language), size per language (typically 2-30 MB), full pack size (~300 MB for the eng + osd + 100 most common langs)
  - Option A: bundle in Docker image; pros (works offline, no install step), cons (large image, slow to pull)
  - Option B: first-use download; pros (small image), cons (requires network, needs HTTPS download from a maintained mirror)
  - Option C: out-of-band install (apt-get install tesseract-ocr-eng); pros (smallest image), cons (operator-driven setup)
  - Recommended approach for each distribution channel:
    - Docker image: ship eng + osd by default; --ocr-langs flag downloads additional langs on first use
    - cargo install binary: tesseract is a runtime dep; user is responsible for tesseract-ocr-eng (and any other lang packs)
    - PyPI wheel: same as cargo install -- traineddata is a runtime dep

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the --audit-log FILE flag on serve / mcp --bind (and other public-listener subcommands) that emits a per-request NDJSON line carrying ts, client_ip, tool, fingerprint, duration_ms, status, and diagnostics fields. Enforce the NEVER-log policy across the codebase: no password values, no bearer tokens, no PDF bytes, no extracted text content, no Cookie/Authorization/Proxy-Authorization headers at any log level. Audit-log lines carry the structural fingerprint, not the file path or URL.

## Why this matters

Lines 931-964 (Audit Logging) define the policy. TH-08 (line 879) tests it. The audit log is the only structured trace of who-did-what against a publicly-exposed pdftract instance; without it, post-incident forensics is impossible. The log-policy enforcement is what makes the log itself safe to retain and ship to a SIEM -- a leak from the log file would mirror leaks from the PDFs themselves.

## Implementation guidance

- Files to create / modify:
  - pdftract-core/src/audit.rs: an AuditLogWriter that wraps a BufWriter<File> behind a Mutex; writes one NDJSON line per request; flushes after each line
  - pdftract-cli/src/args.rs: add --audit-log FILE flag (FILE = - means stdout); accept on serve, mcp, inspect subcommands
  - pdftract-serve/src/middleware/audit.rs: a tower middleware that records request start; on response, computes duration; writes an AuditRecord
  - pdftract-mcp/src/middleware/audit.rs: same for the MCP server
  - pdftract-core/src/fingerprint.rs: structural fingerprint (already used per Phase 1.7); audit log uses pdftract-v1:<hex> form
- AuditRecord schema (serde Serialize):
  - ts: ISO-8601 RFC3339 UTC string (e.g. 2026-05-16T12:34:56Z)
  - client_ip: string (IP only, no port); None for stdio MCP -- in that case the field is absent
  - tool: string (extract / classify / grep / mcp.extract / etc.)
  - fingerprint: string pdftract-v1:<hex> -- NOT the path or URL
  - duration_ms: u64
  - status: u16 (HTTP-style status code; 200 ok, 4xx client error, 5xx server error)
  - diagnostics: Vec<String> -- diagnostic codes emitted during the request (XREF_REPAIRED, STREAM_BOMB, etc.)
- Log-policy enforcement: a custom log filter / macro wrapper that rejects log lines containing known-secret substrings at compile time where possible (a clippy-style lint) and at runtime via a redaction step for any log line containing PDFTRACT_PASSWORD or known-token patterns
- Rotation: pdftract does NOT rotate; operators configure logrotate. Document this verbatim in the runbook output of pdftract serve --help

## Critical considerations

- The audit log MUST be append-only and crash-safe: write one full line atomically (single write() syscall for short lines, fsync optional); a partial line on crash is preferable to a missing line
- Mutex contention on AuditLogWriter: at 100 req/s, the mutex is fine; at 10k req/s, batch the writes into a channel + a single-writer task
- Client IP detection: use the immediate peer address from the HTTP listener; if X-Forwarded-For is configured (operator-controlled), use the leftmost address from X-Forwarded-For; document that --trust-forwarded-for is opt-in to prevent spoofing
- Stdio MCP requests have no client_ip -- the field is absent (NOT empty string) so consumers can distinguish stdio from HTTP-bound
- The fingerprint is computed from the PDF bytes pre-extraction; if the request never gets to extraction (e.g. fails at upload size limit), the fingerprint is N/A and the field is absent
- The log-policy enforcement at runtime SHOULD be implemented as a Logger wrapper that scans the formatted line for known-secret substrings and emits REDACTED; the compile-time approach (clippy lint) catches the easy cases but cannot reason about runtime-formatted strings

## Acceptance criteria

- --audit-log FILE flag implemented on serve, mcp, inspect subcommands
- Per-request NDJSON line written with all documented fields
- Stdio MCP requests OMIT the client_ip field (vs emit empty string)
- Log-policy enforcement: a test fixture extracts a sensitive PDF at RUST_LOG=pdftract=trace and asserts no known-sensitive substring appears in the captured log buffer (this is the TH-08 test, separate bead, but the runtime guard is here)
- rotation policy documented in --help output
- Fingerprint is logged, NOT path/URL
- AuditLogWriter is crash-safe (single-write per line, no partials in normal operation)

## References

- Plan: lines 931-964 (Audit Logging section), 879 (TH-08 test), 949-954 (NEVER-log list), Phase 1.7 (structural fingerprint source)

issue.description:
## Scope

Define the Python exception hierarchy: PdftractError (base; inherits PyException) and EncryptionError (inherits PdftractError). Map Rust extraction errors (Result::Err variants) to the appropriate Python exception type. Set exception attributes (.code, .page_index, .hint) from the originating Diagnostic when applicable.

## Why this matters

Python exception handling is the user's primary error-recovery interface. Without a clean hierarchy, users either catch a generic Exception (defensive overreach) or miss errors entirely. The hint and code attributes let Python code react programmatically (e.g. catch encryption errors but re-raise on corruption).

## Implementation guidance

- create_exception!(pdftract, PdftractError, PyException);
- create_exception!(pdftract, EncryptionError, PdftractError);
- Mapping function: fn map_error(py: Python, err: ExtractionError) -> PyErr
  - ExtractionError::Encrypted -> EncryptionError with a hint string telling the user to supply the secret keyword argument
  - ExtractionError::Corrupt(reason) -> PdftractError with code, message, hint
  - ExtractionError::Io(io_err) -> PdftractError with message of io_err
  - ExtractionError::Diagnostic(diag) -> PdftractError with diag.code, diag.message, diag.hint
- Exception instances have attributes: code (str), page_index (Optional[int]), hint (Optional[str])
- Register both classes in m.add at module init

## Critical considerations

- Critical-test 3+4 from plan: extract on a missing file raises PdftractError; extract on an encrypted file raises EncryptionError
- EncryptionError MUST inherit from PdftractError (so users catching the base also catch encryption)
- Setting attributes on PyErr instances: use PyErr::new + set_attr after construction
- Attribute names match the Rust Diagnostic field names for consistency
- Hint is user-facing; keep concise and actionable

## Acceptance criteria

- Missing-file extraction raises PdftractError; isinstance(e, PdftractError) True
- Encrypted-file extraction raises EncryptionError; isinstance(e, PdftractError) True (inheritance check)
- Exception has .code, .page_index (None for doc-level), .hint attributes accessible from Python
- Module exposes pdftract.PdftractError and pdftract.EncryptionError classes

## References

- Plan section: Phase 6.3 exceptions (lines 2075-2078) + critical tests (lines 2091-2092)

## Scope

Curate the 200-document labeled corpus (50 invoices + 50 scientific papers + 50 contracts + 50 misc) with ground-truth labels, build the corpus-classification harness, wire the >= 90% accuracy CI gate, and emit per-class precision/recall metrics (>= 0.85) plus macro-F1 (>= 0.88) on each run. This is the primary gate for Phase 5.6.

## Why this matters

The 90% accuracy figure is the contract that justifies bundling 5.6 in the default pdftract binary. Without a CI gate, accuracy regressions creep in undetected. The macro-F1 floor catches class-imbalance gaming (e.g. a classifier that just predicts "unknown" 100% of the time scores ~25% accuracy but macro-F1 ~0; both gates close that loophole).

## Implementation guidance

- Corpus location: tests/corpus/classifier/{invoices,papers,contracts,misc}/*.pdf + labels.csv
- labels.csv schema: path,expected_type
- Source PDFs:
  - invoices: a mix of small business invoices (curated public-domain or generated samples), 50 distinct templates
  - papers: arXiv abstracts (CC-BY licensed; pull 50 distinct sample papers)
  - contracts: public-domain contract templates (CC0 / government), 50 distinct templates
  - misc: 50 PDFs spanning forms, slide decks, book chapters, bank statements (each <= ~10 of any one type to keep "misc" diverse)
- Test harness: tests/corpus_classifier.rs walks labels.csv; calls pdftract classify; aggregates confusion matrix
- Emits per-class precision/recall + macro-F1 + overall accuracy
- CI gate: fail if accuracy < 0.90 OR macro-F1 < 0.88 OR any class precision/recall < 0.85
- Corpus must be cached in Argo Workflow volume to avoid re-downloading every CI run

## Critical considerations

- Total corpus size MAY be large (~100-300 MB); store in object storage and download in CI prologue, NOT in git repo
- License diligence: every PDF must be public-domain, CC0, or CC-BY (verify and document in tests/corpus/classifier/LICENSES.md)
- "misc" class is the catch-all; misclassifying an invoice as "misc" hurts invoice recall but not "misc" precision
- Reporting must be human-readable in CI output: confusion matrix + per-class table
- Allow temporary disabling of the gate via env var PDFTRACT_DISABLE_CORPUS_GATE=1 for debugging (but CI MUST fail loudly if set in main)

## Acceptance criteria

- 200 PDFs assembled (50 + 50 + 50 + 50) with verified licenses
- labels.csv complete and matches file structure
- Harness produces correct confusion matrix
- CI gate passes with bundled built-in profiles (5.6.4) at >= 90% accuracy + >= 0.88 macro-F1 + >= 0.85 per-class precision/recall
- Argo WorkflowTemplate caches corpus download (re-download only on miss)

## References

- Plan section: Phase 5.6 acceptance criteria (line 1973) + critical tests (line 1988)
- Phase 0 CI gates infrastructure

## Scope

Build the test corpus and property-test harness for the Object Parser:

1. **Curated fixtures** under `tests/object_parser/fixtures/`:
   - `nested_dict.pdf.in` — `<< /A << /B << /C 1 >> >> >>`
   - `mixed_array.pdf.in` — `[1 true (str) /Name null 3.14 5 0 R]`
   - `indirect_simple.pdf.in` — `1 0 obj null endobj`
   - `indirect_stream.pdf.in` — `1 0 obj << /Length 5 >> stream\nHELLO\nendstream endobj`
   - `objstm_basic.pdf.in` — a minimal ObjStm with N=5 embedded objects
   - `objstm_extends.pdf.in` — ObjStm A with /Extends to ObjStm B; A holds 3 objs, B holds 2
   - `circular_self.pdf.in` — `1 0 obj << /A 1 0 R >> endobj`
   - `circular_three.pdf.in` — A->B->C->A
   - `truncated_dict.pdf.in` — `<< /A 1 ` (no closing `>>`)
   - `deep_nesting.pdf.in` — 300 levels of nested dicts (tests depth limit)

2. **Proptest properties** in `tests/proptest/object_parser.rs`:
   - `prop_parser_never_panics`: arbitrary byte sequences fed to ObjectParser; assert no panic
   - `prop_resolve_terminates`: arbitrary ObjRef sequences resolved; assert termination within 1000 operations
   - `prop_dict_order_preserved`: random insertion sequences -> dict iteration order matches insertion order
   - `prop_cache_consistency`: two identical resolution sequences produce identical PdfObject hashes
   - `prop_inv8_no_panic`: any input -> Vec<Diagnostic> (possibly empty), no panic

3. **Golden output tests**: each fixture has a sibling `.expected.json` showing the parsed PdfObject in a deterministic JSON serialization; `BLESS=1` rewrites them

## Implementation guidance

- proptest budget: 6 properties × ~5000 cases each = ~30,000 cases total; budget ~15 min CPU per PR (within Phase 0.5 budget)
- Fixture format: `.pdf.in` files are NOT complete PDFs — they're indirect-object snippets that the test harness wraps in a minimal xref-less envelope just to give the lexer something to consume
- Golden output: use serde_json with sorted-key serialization (no — actually use IndexMap-preserving serialization since dict order matters; `serde_json` with `preserve_order` feature)
- The `BLESS=1` env var: when set, the test runner WRITES the actual output to the .expected.json file instead of comparing; used to update goldens after intentional changes

## Critical considerations

- Fixture for circular_self.pdf.in: build a minimal envelope with this object as obj 1; the resolver must terminate (cycle detected) without stack overflow. Run the test with `--stack-size 64KB` to verify cycle detection isn't just "stack big enough to absorb the recursion"
- The deep_nesting.pdf.in fixture (300 levels) must trip STRUCT_DEPTH_EXCEEDED at level 256, NOT panic. Verify the diagnostic byte offset points to the 257th `<<`
- ObjStm fixtures require pre-compressed (zlib) bytes; use `tools/build-objstm-fixture` (a small rust helper that takes a list of objects and emits the binary)

- Property prop_cache_consistency is the cache's own INV-8 corollary: cache hit MUST equal cache miss for the same input

- A deliberately-introduced panic in parse_indirect_object is caught by prop_parser_never_panics within 100 cases
- A deliberately-introduced non-determinism in dict insertion order is caught by prop_dict_order_preserved

issue.description:
## Scope

Decode PDF stream data through its filter pipeline. Called lazily when stream content is first accessed (Phase 1.4 records offsets; this layer decompresses on demand).

Nine filters per plan, in priority order:

| Filter | Implementation | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| FlateDecode | flate2 ZlibDecoder | + predictors: TIFF 2, PNG 10-15 (per-row byte selects for 15) |
| LZWDecode | lzw crate | /EarlyChange (1 early default, 0 late); same predictors |
| ASCII85Decode | hand-written | `z` shortcut, partial final group, `~>` terminator |
| ASCIIHexDecode | hand-written | digit pairs, whitespace ignored, `>` terminator |
| RunLengthDecode | hand-written | length byte 0-127 copy N+1; 129-255 repeat; 128 EOD |
| DCTDecode | passthrough | raw JPEG; validate SOI/EOI; log /ColorTransform |
| JBIG2Decode | passthrough | raw JBIG2; OCR_JBIG2_UNSUPPORTED if no full-render |
| JPXDecode | passthrough | raw JPEG 2000; OCR_JPX_UNSUPPORTED if no full-render |
| CCITTFaxDecode | passthrough | raw CCITT; OCR_CCITT_UNSUPPORTED if no libtiff/full-render |
| Crypt | identity only | /Name /Identity handled; custom: ENCRYPTION_UNSUPPORTED |

Filter pipeline: /Filter is a name or array; /DecodeParms aligned or absent; apply in order; mismatched lengths log diagnostic.

Decompression bomb limit: ExtractionOptions.max_decompress_bytes (default 2 GB = 2 * 1024^3 per document). Cumulative document total AND single-stream exceedance triggers STREAM_BOMB and returns partial bytes.

Child beads:
- StreamDecoder trait + filter pipeline orchestrator + 2 GB bomb limit enforcement
- FlateDecode + PNG/TIFF predictors (TIFF 2, PNG 10-15 per-row)
- LZWDecode + /EarlyChange handling
- ASCII85Decode + ASCIIHexDecode + RunLengthDecode (the three hand-written ASCII decoders)
- DCTDecode + JBIG2Decode + JPXDecode + CCITTFaxDecode passthroughs (with SOI/EOI validation + OCR_*_UNSUPPORTED diagnostics)
- Crypt filter (identity only; reject custom)
- Stream decoder test corpus + per-filter regression fixtures

## Why this matters

Every byte of content in a PDF — text drawing operators, font programs, color profiles, images, even xref streams — is wrapped in one or more filters. A bug in the FlateDecode predictor cascade silently corrupts content streams across the entire document. The 2 GB bomb limit is the only thing standing between pdftract and an adversarial decompression DoS.

## Critical considerations

- The PNG predictor (10-15) is per-row: each decompressed row's FIRST byte is the predictor selector for that row (10=None, 11=Sub, 12=Up, 13=Average, 14=Paeth, 15=Optimum-per-row); the selector byte is then DISCARDED from the row data
- TIFF predictor 2: simple delta from previous-column same-channel byte
- Filter pipeline order matters: `/Filter [/ASCII85Decode /FlateDecode]` means decode ASCII85 first (to get bytes), then Flate-decompress those bytes
- /DecodeParms is parallel to /Filter: if /Filter is an array, /DecodeParms is an array of dicts (or nulls), one per filter
- Mismatched array lengths between /Filter and /DecodeParms: use defaults for unspecified; emit STRUCT_INVALID_FILTER_PARAMS
- DCTDecode/JBIG2/JPX/CCITTFax: pdftract-core stores the raw bytes for the OCR pipeline (Phase 5) to consume; it does NOT itself decode raster
- Crypt filter with /Name /Identity is the no-op; ANY other crypt filter (Custom, V2-default) emits ENCRYPTION_UNSUPPORTED
- max_decompress_bytes is per-DOCUMENT cumulative AND per-STREAM cap: a single 3 GB stream triggers STREAM_BOMB; a doc with 5 × 500 MB streams also triggers it at the 5th
- Error recovery: zlib mid-stream errors return the bytes decoded so far + STREAM_DECODE_ERROR diagnostic; never abort the page

## Acceptance criteria

- All 7 child beads closed
- All Critical tests from plan Section 1.5 pass:
  - FlateDecode with PNG predictor 15 (per-row, all six predictor types in one stream): all decoded correctly
  - LZWDecode with EarlyChange=0: matches reference output
  - ASCII85 with `z` shortcut and odd final group
  - Filter array [/ASCII85Decode /FlateDecode]: decoded in order
  - FlateDecode with truncated zlib stream: partial output + STREAM_DECODE_ERROR
  - DCTDecode: raw bytes unchanged; SOI marker present
- 2 GB bomb limit verified by EC-10 fixture
- INV-8 maintained
- Module under `crates/pdftract-core/src/parser/stream/`

## References

- Plan section: Phase 1.5 Stream Decoder, lines 1133-1165
- EC-10 (FlateDecode bomb); EC-11/12/13 (JBIG2/JPX/CCITT unsupported)
- INV-8 (no panic)
- Dependency Matrix: flate2, lzw, image (image for JPX/CCITT decode in OCR path)
- ADR-003 (pdfium-render opt-in via full-render)

## Scope

## Why this matters

The Argo WorkflowTemplate is the CI orchestration: every PR and tag triggers wheel builds; without the template, builds are manual and inconsistent. Parallel 5-triple builds (vs. sequential) reduce CI time from ~30 min to ~10 min.

## Implementation guidance

- File: jedarden/declarative-config/k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/pdftract-py-ci.yaml
- WorkflowTemplate kind with templates section:
  - linux-x86_64: container ghcr.io/rust-cross/manylinux2_28-cross:x86_64; command maturin build --release --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
  - linux-aarch64: same image, --target aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu
  - macos-x86_64: cross + osxcross image; --target x86_64-apple-darwin
  - macos-aarch64: same image, --target aarch64-apple-darwin
  - windows-x86_64: cross + MinGW image; --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu
  - sdist: maturin sdist (source distribution; tooling for users on uncommon platforms)

- ArgoCD app argo-workflows-ns-iad-ci syncs templates from declarative-config to the cluster

## Critical considerations

- Container image versions pinned (no :latest); reproducibility requires deterministic toolchains
- Resource requests per step: 4 CPU + 8 GB RAM (cross-compilation is memory-hungry)

issue.description:
## Scope

Coordinator for sub-phase 3.3: implement the ResourceStack that scopes a content stream's access to fonts/colorspaces/xobjects/etc. plus the `Do` operator that invokes a form XObject as a nested content stream with merged resources, applied `/Matrix`, `/BBox` clipping, cycle detection, and a 20-level stack depth limit.

## Why this matters

Form XObjects are how PDFs deduplicate repeated content (page headers, watermarks, common drawings). Many real PDFs have form XObjects 5-10 levels deep with overlapping resource dictionaries. Without correct resource scoping every nested glyph could use the wrong font. Without cycle detection, a malicious PDF can cause infinite recursion and OOM.

## Children

- ResourceStack: per-page, scope-merging stack of resource dictionaries with fallback lookup
- Do operator: form XObject lookup, /Matrix and /BBox application, nested execution
- Cycle detection: track in-progress XObject object numbers, emit STRUCT_XOBJECT_CYCLE diagnostic on revisit, bound recursion at 20 levels

## Critical considerations

- Resource lookup is a LAYERED search: innermost scope first, fall through to outer scopes if not found. Some PDFs deliberately omit Resources from a form XObject expecting parent inheritance.
- /Matrix is applied via a `cm` operation BEFORE the form's content stream executes; restored after via q/Q semantics.
- /BBox is a clipping rectangle in form coordinates; ignored for text extraction (we don't render); kept for diagnostic clamping if a glyph bbox exceeds /BBox.
- Cycle detection key: form XObject object number (not pointer/hash) — same object reachable via different paths is the same cycle.
- Depth limit 20: emit STRUCT_XOBJECT_DEPTH_EXCEEDED on level 21, refuse the Do, continue execution.

## Acceptance criteria

- All 3 children closed.
- Form XObject with own /Resources /Font: inner font resolves from form scope, not page scope.
- Form XObject with /Matrix [2 0 0 2 0 0]: glyph bboxes inside the form scaled by 2.
- Form XObject cycle (A->B->A): diagnostic emitted; extraction continues.
- 20-level nested forms: succeeds; 21st emits depth diagnostic.
- Form with empty content stream: no crash, no glyphs.

## References

- Plan section: Phase 3.3 Resource Context and Form XObject Recursion (lines 1561-1575)

issue.description:
## Scope

Author tests/security/TH-02-path-traversal.rs that exercises 10 path-traversal payloads against the MCP server. Per INV-10 pdftract mcp MUST NOT accept file-path parameters; this test verifies the absence of any path parameter on any MCP tool. If a future --root DIR mode is introduced, this test ALSO verifies that path canonicalisation rejects paths escaping DIR with a PATH_OUTSIDE_ROOT diagnostic.

## Why this matters

TH-02 (line 873) is the canonical path-traversal class. The primary mitigation is structural (no path parameters in the MCP tool schema -- attackers cannot specify a path), and the secondary mitigation is the canonicalisation guard for the future --root DIR mode. The test belt-and-suspenders both: pre-mitigation tests that the schema rejects paths, and post-introduction tests that the canonicalisation rejects traversal.

## Implementation guidance

- Test file: tests/security/TH-02-path-traversal.rs
- Test cases (Phase 1: while mcp does NOT accept paths):
  1. List tools via MCP; assert that none of the tool schemas has a parameter named path, file, filename, source_path, or similar
  2. Attempt to call any tool with a path parameter injected: assert the server returns a schema-validation error
- Test cases (Phase 2: when --root DIR is introduced; these tests are #[ignore] until the feature lands):
  - 10 path-traversal payloads against tools that DO accept a relative path under --root DIR:
    1. ../../etc/passwd
    2. ../../../etc/passwd
    3. ../../../../etc/passwd
    4. /etc/passwd (absolute outside root)
    5. ./valid/../../../etc/passwd (normalised traversal)
    6. valid/..%2F..%2Fetc%2Fpasswd (URL-encoded)
    7. valid/..\..\..\etc\passwd (Windows separators on Linux)
    8. valid/etc/passwd (no traversal, valid form but reaching outside via /etc symlink in DIR -- requires symlink fixture setup)
    9. /proc/self/environ (special filesystem)
    10. con (Windows reserved name; relevant on Windows build)
  - For each: assert PATH_OUTSIDE_ROOT diagnostic and a 400-equivalent MCP error response
- The test harness: spawn pdftract mcp --stdio in a child process; communicate via stdin/stdout JSON-RPC; assert on response shape

## Critical considerations

- The Phase 1 tests are the load-bearing ones today; the Phase 2 tests document the future contract
- The test for "no path parameter in any tool schema" is the strongest form: it ensures we cannot accidentally add one later without flipping a test
- Canonicalisation rule for --root DIR: use std::fs::canonicalize on both the requested path AND the root; if the requested-path canonical form does not start with the root canonical form, REJECT
- Symlink-race: between canonicalize and open, an attacker could change the symlink target; mitigate by using openat with O_NOFOLLOW or by re-checking after open (TOCTOU)
- Windows path semantics differ: case-insensitivity, alternate data streams, reserved names (CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, COM1-9, LPT1-9); a comprehensive test list would include these
- The fixture setup for symlink-traversal needs careful filesystem teardown (the symlink itself is in a temp dir that is cleaned up after the test)

## Acceptance criteria

- tests/security/TH-02-path-traversal.rs exists; Phase 1 tests pass; Phase 2 tests #[ignore]d but compile
- All Phase 1 tests assert the absence of path parameters across all MCP tools
- The 10 traversal payloads are documented in the test file even if Phase 2 tests are gated
- INV-10 cited as the structural mitigation source

## References

- Plan: line 873 (TH-02 entry), INV-10 (MCP no-path-parameters), Diagnostic Code Catalog PATH_OUTSIDE_ROOT

## Scope

Wire the Vec<Link> from 7.6.2 to the document-level /links JSON path, and Vec<Annotation> from 7.6.3 to per-page /annotations JSON path. Define the serde schema for both (tagged unions where applicable). Always emit both arrays (empty when none). Update docs/schema/v1.0/pdftract.schema.json. Surface links in Markdown sink as a final References section; surface annotations as page-level review-comment lists.

## Why this matters

The dual emission (document-level links + page-level annotations) reflects how readers think about these objects: links are document-wide navigation, annotations are page-specific commentary. Stable JSON shapes let downstream tools build link indexes, annotation viewers, and review-comment exporters without parsing the entire document.

## Implementation guidance

- Output paths: top-level /links: Vec<Link>; per-page /pages[i]/annotations: Vec<Annotation>
- Link serde: { uri: Option<String>, dest: Option<String>, dest_array: Option<DestArray>, page_index: usize, rect: [f32;4] }
- DestArray: serde tagged enum on fit field: { "page_index": int, "fit": "XYZ", "x": f32, "y": f32, "zoom": f32 } | similar for Fit, FitH, FitV, FitR, FitB, FitBH, FitBV
- Annotation serde: serde tag = "subtype" rename_all = "PascalCase"; common fields flattened; subtype-specific fields (quads, name, da, etc.) as optional struct members
- Always emit arrays (empty Vec, not Option<Vec>)
- Schema: add /$defs for Link, DestArray, Annotation; reference from document-root /links and page /annotations
- Schema round-trip test: synthetic link + annotation -> JSON -> validate -> deserialize -> bytes equal
- Markdown sink: emit links as a "## References" section at the end with [page N] markers; emit annotations as bullet lists at end of each page
- PyO3 binding: expose links and annotations as Python lists of dicts

## Critical considerations

- INV: stable taxonomy of annotation subtypes + link target shapes
- Always-emit-array policy: never null at the JSON layer
- DestArray serde with internal tag avoids untagged enum probing on the consumer side
- /links is sorted by (page_index, rect.y0 desc, rect.x0) for deterministic output
- Per-page /annotations sorted by (rect.y0 desc, rect.x0)
- Markdown sink rendering: shorten URLs > 80 chars with "..." ellipsis
- Annotations should NOT be inlined into block text in plain-text sink (annotations are out-of-line commentary by definition)

## Acceptance criteria

- All other 7.6.x sub-tasks closed
- Schema test: annotation-rich PDF fixture extracts and validates against schema
- Round-trip test: explicit-destination link -> JSON -> deserialize -> bytes equal
- Markdown sink emits References section when links non-empty
- Markdown sink emits per-page annotation bullet lists
- PyO3 binding exposes links and annotations as Python lists
- docs/schema/v1.0/pdftract.schema.json updated with both shapes

issue.description:
## Scope

Define the foundational data structures and lexer skeleton:

- `Token` enum with variants: `Bool(bool)`, `Integer(i64)`, `Real(f64)`, `String(Vec<u8>)`, `Name(Vec<u8>)`, `ArrayStart`, `ArrayEnd`, `DictStart`, `DictEnd`, `Stream`, `EndStream`, `Obj`, `EndObj`, `IndirectRef` (R), `Null`, `Eof`
- `Lexer` struct holding `bytes: &'a [u8]`, `pos: usize`, `diagnostics: Vec<Diagnostic>`
- `Diagnostic { code: DiagCode, byte_offset: u64, msg: String }`
- `DiagCode` enum holding all `STRUCT_*` codes used by the lexer family: `INVALID_NAME`, `INVALID_HEX`, `INVALID_OCTAL`, `INVALID_STREAM_HEADER`, `UNEXPECTED_EOF`, `UNTERMINATED_STRING`
- Public methods: `Lexer::new(bytes)`, `Lexer::next_token() -> Option<Token>`, `Lexer::peek_token() -> Option<&Token>`, `Lexer::position() -> u64`, `Lexer::take_diagnostics() -> Vec<Diagnostic>`
- Internal helpers: `consume_whitespace()`, `consume_comment()` (`%` to EOL), `skip_whitespace_and_comments()`, `is_pdf_whitespace(b)`, `is_pdf_delimiter(b)`

## Implementation guidance

- Use a position-only API (no separate `Span` type): start byte offset is implicit from `position()` before `next_token()`; end offset is `position()` after. Saves a Vec<Range> allocation per token
- Whitespace bytes (PDF spec 7.2.2): 0x00, 0x09, 0x0A, 0x0C, 0x0D, 0x20. Encode as a const lookup table `WHITESPACE: [bool; 256]`
- Delimiters: `( ) < > [ ] { } / %` — also a const lookup table
- `next_token()` always advances past leading whitespace + comments before dispatching to a literal-specific lexer based on the next byte
- `peek_token` impl: cache `Option<(Token, usize)>` (token + post-position) so consecutive peeks don't re-lex. Cache invalidated by every `next_token`
- No allocator beyond `Vec<u8>` for string tokens and `Vec<Diagnostic>` for collected diagnostics
- No `unwrap()` / `expect()` anywhere in lib code (INV-8 lint)

## Critical considerations

- Position tracking is byte-level, NOT character-level. PDF is byte-oriented; "character" is a downstream concern in the font pipeline
- Position MUST advance even when consuming comments — `%comment\n` advances `pos` by `len(comment) + 1`
- Diagnostics are accumulated, NOT bubbled as Results — every parse error continues lexing with a sensible recovery (PdfNull-equivalent at the token level: emit `Token::Null` or skip to next delimiter)
- Token enum variants must `derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)` for use in proptest assertions and downstream caching
- Diagnostic emission MUST be cheap: never `format!()` eagerly; use `Cow<'static, str>` so static error messages don't allocate

## Acceptance criteria

- `cargo build --features default` produces `crates/pdftract-core/src/parser/lexer/mod.rs` exporting `Lexer`, `Token`, `Diagnostic`, `DiagCode`
- `Lexer::new(b"")` returns a lexer that `next_token()` produces `Some(Token::Eof)`, then `None`
- `Lexer::new(b"   \t\n\r%comment\n   ")` produces `Some(Token::Eof)` after consuming all whitespace and the comment
- `Lexer::position()` returns the byte offset just past the last-consumed character (used by xref byte-offset references)
- No `unwrap()` / `expect()` in module source (verified by clippy lint in Phase 0.4)
- Token enum implements PartialEq for proptest assertions

## References

- Plan section: Phase 1.1 Lexer, lines 1024-1052
- INV-8 (no panic in pdftract-core)
- Diagnostic code conventions: STRUCT_* prefix
issue.title: Lexer infrastructure — Token enum, Lexer struct, position tracking, diagnostics

## Scope

Author the per-profile README at profiles/builtin/<type>/README.md for each of the nine built-in profiles (invoice, receipt, contract, scientific_paper, slide_deck, form, bank_statement, legal_filing, book_chapter). Each README describes the profile's match criteria summary, the fields it extracts (with example values), and known limitations / failure modes.

## Why this matters

These README files are the user-facing documentation for each profile. A user who runs pdftract profiles show invoice gets the YAML; a user who runs pdftract profiles describe invoice (or reads docs/user-docs/) gets the README. Without these, the YAML is documentation only for the implementor; non-implementor users cannot tell which profile fits their document or which fields they will get.

## Implementation guidance

- Files to create:
  - profiles/builtin/invoice/README.md
  - profiles/builtin/receipt/README.md
  - profiles/builtin/contract/README.md
  - profiles/builtin/scientific_paper/README.md
  - profiles/builtin/slide_deck/README.md
  - profiles/builtin/form/README.md
  - profiles/builtin/bank_statement/README.md
  - profiles/builtin/legal_filing/README.md
  - profiles/builtin/book_chapter/README.md
- Each README structure (consistent across all 9 profiles):
  1. Title and one-line description (matches the profile YAML description field)
  2. Match Criteria Summary: prose description of what makes a document match this profile (text patterns, structural signals, page count expectations)
  3. Extracted Fields: a table with one row per profile_fields key: field_name, type (string/decimal/date/int), description, example_value, source_location_hint
  4. Known Limitations: bullet list of edge cases where the profile underperforms (e.g. invoice: "Multi-currency invoices may extract the wrong total if currency symbol layout is unusual"; scientific_paper: "DOIs in footnotes are not extracted; only first-page DOIs are picked up")
  5. Sample Input Pointer: link to one or more fixtures under tests/fixtures/profiles/<type>/ that exemplify a successful match
  6. Configuration Tips: how a user might want to override the profile via --profile or by exporting and editing
- The README content is generated semi-automatically: a script (xtask doc-profile) emits a skeleton from the profile YAML; the human author fills in Match Criteria Summary, Known Limitations, and Sample Input Pointer

## Critical considerations

- The Extracted Fields table MUST match the actual profile_fields keys in the YAML -- a drift here is a docs failure; consider a CI check that lints the README against the YAML
- The Known Limitations section is the most valuable part for users -- be honest about underperforming edge cases
- The slide_deck profile is a degenerate case (fields: title, presenter, date, slide_titles) -- its README should note that slide-deck PDFs vary enormously and extraction quality depends on the exporter
- The form profile is even more degenerate (no field extractor; only reading_order: line_dominant + form_fields from Phase 7.4) -- README should explain this and point at form_fields
- Each README should be 1-2 pages in markdown -- not a comprehensive design doc, but more than a YAML comment
- Cross-reference docs/research/document-classification-and-zone-labeling.md (already exists) for the broader classifier theory

## Acceptance criteria

- All nine README files exist at the documented paths
- Each follows the consistent 6-section structure
- Extracted Fields tables match the corresponding profile YAML's profile_fields
- Known Limitations is non-empty and document-specific
- Sample Input Pointer links to actual fixtures in tests/fixtures/profiles/<type>/
- xtask doc-profile skeleton generator scripted (so future profile additions get a starting README for free)

## References

- Plan: lines 3037-3047 (built-in profile field sets), 3049 (5 fixtures + regression test per profile), Phase 7.10 acceptance criteria
