issue.description:
## Scope

Add two cross-cutting components to the Object Parser:

1. **Per-thread cycle detection**: a `thread_local!` `RefCell<HashSet<ObjRef>>` tracking object refs currently being resolved. The `resolve(ref) -> Arc<PdfObject>` API:
   - Checks the cache first
   - If miss: inserts `ref` into the resolution set, fetches+parses the indirect object, removes `ref` from the set, inserts into cache, returns
   - If `ref` already in the set: emit `STRUCT_CIRCULAR_REF` and return `Arc::new(PdfObject::Null)` (no cache write — circular refs are not cached)

2. **LRU object cache** via the `lru` crate: `Mutex<LruCache<ObjRef, Arc<PdfObject>>>` with capacity 4096. Caches successful resolutions document-wide.

## Implementation guidance

- `lru = "0.12"` crate (in plan's Dependency Matrix)
- `Mutex<LruCache>` is correct because PDF document parsing is single-threaded per document; rayon parallelism happens at page-LEVEL during content stream processing (Phase 3), not during object resolution
- For inter-document parallelism (multiple PDFs in flight), each Document has its own cache instance; no contention
- Thread-local resolution stack is correct because rayon WILL spawn multiple page-processing tasks concurrently AFTER the document model is built (Phase 1.4); each task gets its own resolution stack
- Cache hit metric: track via a `CacheStats { hits: u64, misses: u64 }` field on Document, exposed for diagnostic purposes
- Cache key is `ObjRef`, not `(ObjRef, GenerationVersion)` — the xref resolver handles generation-version selection (higher gen wins; older versions never reach the resolver)

## Critical considerations

- Critical test from plan: self-referencing object `1 0 obj << /A 1 0 R >> endobj` -> resolving ObjRef{1,0} dereferences `/A`, which is again ObjRef{1,0}; cycle detection catches it, returns PdfNull WITH `STRUCT_CIRCULAR_REF` diagnostic, NO stack overflow
- Critical test: A -> B -> C -> A (3-cycle): same result, cycle caught at the second A
- The cache must NOT cache cycles' PdfNull result — otherwise after the first cycle detection, subsequent legitimate accesses to A would return cached PdfNull
- Mutex on LRU is acceptable because cache ops are O(1) and short; if profiling shows contention (unlikely), upgrade to parking_lot or dashmap later
- Resolution depth limit (separate from cycle detection): impose max recursion depth of 256 to catch pathological non-cyclic deep chains (extremely rare but possible); emit `STRUCT_DEPTH_EXCEEDED`
- Diagnostic emission: STRUCT_CIRCULAR_REF carries the offending ObjRef in its msg field for debuggability

## Acceptance criteria

- Critical test passes: self-cycle returns PdfNull + STRUCT_CIRCULAR_REF, no stack overflow (test in CI with --stack-size 64KB to verify)
- 3-cycle (A->B->C->A) test passes
- After cycle detection, a SEPARATE access to a legitimate object NOT in the cycle succeeds and is cached normally
- Cache stats: after 1000 resolutions of 100 unique objects, hit ratio >= 90%
- LRU eviction: with cache capacity 4096, the 4097th unique resolution evicts the LRU entry (verified with cache.peek_lru())
- proptest property: random ObjRef resolution sequences never panic and always terminate

## References

- Plan section: Phase 1.2 line 1073 (circular reference guard); Critical considerations on parallelism + caching
- EC-08 (Circular object references)
- INV-8
- Dependency Matrix: lru crate
issue.title: Implement per-thread cycle detection + LRU object cache (lru crate, 4096 entries)

Added 13 integration tests covering PDF spec Appendix A, NIST vectors, password validation (R=2/R=3), empty password path, and invalid input rejection. All 34 RC4 tests pass (21 unit + 13 integration). Verification note: notes/pdftract-4isj9.md. Commit: dcb0430.
issue.description:
## Scope

Implement RC4-based PDF decryption per PDF spec 7.6.4 for V=1 R=2 (40-bit) and V=2 R=3 (up to 128-bit) revisions. Uses the rc4 crate from RustCrypto. Derives the per-object file key from the user/owner password + /O + /P + first16(/ID[0]) per the spec's key-derivation algorithm.

## Why this matters

RC4 PDFs are the long tail of legacy encrypted documents (Acrobat 5 and earlier era). They're rare but persistent in archived collections (legal, government records). Without RC4 support, these documents extract as garbage; with it, they extract correctly. AES (siblings) is for modern PDFs.

## Implementation guidance

- Crate: rc4 = \"0.1\" (RustCrypto)
- Module: crates/pdftract-core/src/encryption/rc4.rs (feature-gated on decrypt)
- Key derivation (per PDF spec 7.6.4.3, Algorithm 2):
  1. Pad password to 32 bytes via the standard padding string (28 bytes of specific bytes; spec table 27)
  2. MD5 hash: pad || /O || /P (4 bytes LE) || first16(/ID[0]) || (if R>=4 && metadata-encrypted): 4 bytes 0xFF
  3. If R>=3: iterate MD5 50 times on the first n bytes (n = key_length/8)
  4. The first n bytes of the MD5 output is the encryption key
- Per-object key derivation (Algorithm 1):
  1. Take the encryption key + 3 bytes object number (LE) + 2 bytes generation (LE)
  2. MD5 hash; first (n+5) bytes (capped at 16) is the per-object key
  3. Initialize RC4 with this key; decrypt the object data
- User password validation (Algorithm 4 for R==2 / Algorithm 5 for R==3):
  1. R==2: pad password; RC4-encrypt the 32-byte padding string with the file key; compare with /U
  2. R==3: pad password; MD5(pad || first16(/ID[0])); RC4 19 times with i^step key; compare first 16 bytes with first 16 of /U
- Public API: rc4_decrypt(file_key: &[u8], obj_num: u32, gen: u16, data: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8>
- md5 crate: md-5 = \"0.10\" (RustCrypto) — already a transitive dep typically, but add if not

## Critical considerations

- The 32-byte standard password padding string is in PDF spec Table 27; copy-paste verbatim; do NOT trust online sources (wrong bytes are widespread)
- Endianness: object number is little-endian 3 bytes (NOT 4); generation is little-endian 2 bytes; concatenated with the encryption key
- For R==3, the 50-iteration loop is on the first n bytes (n = key_length/8), not the full 16
- AES-V2 metadata encryption flag (R>=4): if /EncryptMetadata == false, append 4 bytes 0xFF in the key derivation; otherwise omit
- Object stream decryption: object streams (PDF 1.5+) themselves are encrypted with per-stream keys derived using the stream's obj num + gen
- Strings inside the object are decrypted with the same per-object key (not a different one)
- Use rc4::Rc4 type directly; do NOT trust opaque wrappers

## Acceptance criteria

- Decrypt a V=1 R=2 RC4-40 fixture with the correct password → byte-identical to the unencrypted reference
- Decrypt a V=2 R=3 RC4-128 fixture → byte-identical
- Decrypt with wrong password → garbage output; user-password validation function returns false; emit ENCRYPTION_BAD_PASSWORD
- Test vector: PDF spec's Appendix A worked example
- Empty password (\"\") is the most common case; verify the standard-padding-string-only path

## References

- Plan section: encryption RC4
- PDF spec 7.6.4 (Standard security handler)
- rc4 crate: https://crates.io/crates/rc4
- md-5 crate: https://crates.io/crates/md-5
- Coordinator: pdftract-1z0qt (parent)
- Sibling: encryption detection (provides EncryptionInfo)
Labels: encryption, phase-1, rc4
issue.title: RC4 decryption (V=1 R=2 40-bit; V=2 R=3 up to 128-bit) — RustCrypto rc4 crate

issue.description:
## Scope

Define the `Glyph` struct per plan spec (10 fields), implement `emit_glyph(executor, codepoint, source, confidence, char_code)` that pulls font_name/font_size/rendering_mode/fill_color from the current GraphicsState, computes bbox via the advance/bbox bead, consults the word boundary detector for is_word_boundary, sets mcid from the marked-content stack (Phase 3.4 provides this; emit None here for now), and appends to the per-page raw_glyph_list (Vec<Glyph>).

## Why this matters

The Glyph struct is the OUTPUT of Phase 3 and the INPUT to Phase 4. Its field set is a contract — every consumer assumes 10 fields with the precise types in the plan. Changing the shape later requires touching every Phase 4 child and the JSON serializer. Lock it in now.

## Implementation guidance

- Struct (matches plan):
  ```rust
  pub struct Glyph {
      pub codepoint: char,
      pub unicode_source: UnicodeSource,
      pub confidence: f32,
      pub bbox: [f32; 4],         // [x0, y0, x1, y1] PDF user space, lower-left origin
      pub font_name: Arc<str>,
      pub font_size: f32,
      pub rendering_mode: u8,
      pub fill_color: Color,
      pub is_word_boundary: bool,
      pub mcid: Option<u32>,
  }
  ```
- emit_glyph: composes the struct from inputs + state + detector + marked-content stack.
- raw_glyph_list (Vec<Glyph>) lives on the page executor; grows monotonically per page; passed to Phase 4 at end-of-page.
- Reserve capacity: a typical page has ~2000 glyphs; pre-reserve 4096 to avoid reallocation.
- Subscript/superscript flags are NOT set here — Phase 4.1 derives them from text_rise tracked in state.

## Critical considerations

- INV: bbox is in PDF user space (origin LOWER-LEFT, y-axis UP), AFTER /Rotate normalization (which happens at end-of-page in Phase 3.1 normalization bead).
- INV: every Glyph carries a valid Unicode codepoint (U+FFFD on failure, never panics).
- font name is shared via Arc across all glyphs of same font on the page — cheap clone.
- fill color is OWNED (Color enum has small variants; Arc<str> inside Spot is the only heap pointer).
- mcid is filled in by Phase 3.4 marked-content wrapper around emit_glyph; this bead leaves it as None.
- The is_word_boundary flag is consulted by Phase 4.1 to decide span breaks and synthetic spaces — getting it right here is critical.

## Acceptance criteria

- Emitting glyph for codepoint 'A' from 12pt Helvetica with fill black, mode 0: Glyph struct populated correctly.
- raw_glyph_list grows by 1 per call.
- 1000 emit_glyph calls finish in < 1 ms (perf gate, criterion benchmark).
- Glyph struct size <= 64 bytes (verify via std::mem::size_of) — keeps the Vec dense for cache efficiency.
- Cloning a Glyph is cheap.

## References

issue.description:
## Goal

Transform raw Vec<Glyph> into structured blocks in reading order. Per-page Vec<Block> with Vec<Span>. Plain text output mode works.

## Sub-phases

- 4.1 Glyph to Span Merging — group consecutive glyphs into spans; span-break triggers: font_name, font_size (delta > 0.5pt), rendering_mode, fill_color (RGB-normalized), is_word_boundary; Span struct with text, bbox, font, size, color, rendering_mode, confidence, confidence_source, lang, flags bitmask (bold/italic/smallcaps/sub/super)
- 4.2 Line Formation — cluster spans by baseline proximity (within 0.5 * median_font_size); within line sort by x0 (LTR) or x1 desc (RTL via unicode-bidi); direction tag on line struct
- 4.3 Column Detection — histogram of x0 values at 1pt resolution; gaps > 0.03 * page_width with zero coverage = boundary candidates; require >= 3 lines per candidate column to confirm
- 4.4 Block Formation — group lines into blocks (paragraphs, headings, lists, tables, captions, figures, code, headers/footers, watermarks, formulas, quotes); heuristics on vertical gap, indent change, font size change, rendering mode change, column boundary; block kind assignment per heuristics; header/footer cross-page dedup via strsim Levenshtein
- 4.5 Reading Order — XY-cut algorithm (recursive widest-whitespace split) for rectilinear layouts; Docstrum fallback (k=5 nearest-neighbor with adjacency angles +-30 deg) when XY-cut produces >10 small regions; tagged PDFs deferred to Phase 7.1 StructTree
- 4.6 Output Serialization (Plain Text) — projection of block list; paragraphs separated by double-newline; page breaks as form-feed (0x0C); headers/footers/invisible/watermarks excluded by default with --include flags
- 4.7 Text Readability Validation and Correction — per-span composite score (printable Unicode, dict word coverage via 20k phf::Set wordlist, whitespace distribution, ligature integrity, confidence floor); correction pipeline: ligature repair, hyphenation repair, mojibake detection, soft-hyphen removal, word-break normalization; pages < 0.5 readability on Vector class escalated to BrokenVector and routed to Phase 5.5 assisted OCR

## Rationale

Phase 4 is where pdftract earns its accuracy claim. Existing extractors emit raw glyph sequences regardless of readability; pdftract validates every span and repairs unreadable output. The 4.7 readability validation is a primary accuracy differentiator — extracted text can be used directly without downstream cleanup.

Multi-column reading order (>95% correctness CI-gated) requires XY-cut for clean layouts and Docstrum for irregular ones. Most academic papers are XY-cut; magazines/news with sidebars need Docstrum.

The block-kind taxonomy (heading/paragraph/list/table/caption/figure/code/header/footer/watermark/formula/quote) drives Phase 6.5 Markdown output and Phase 7.10 profile field extraction.

## Critical considerations

- Baseline approximation: y0 + (bbox_height * 0.2); exact value requires font descender metrics
- Column gap threshold scaled to page_width to handle landscape vs. portrait
- Header/footer detection is a SEQUENTIAL post-processing pass after rayon assembly (sliding window of 4 pages, Levenshtein <= 5% of text length, top/bottom 7% of page)
- Word boundary in span text: implementation choice (append space to previous span OR create new space span) — must round-trip to correct plain text
- Bold detection: font name contains "Bold" OR FontDescriptor /Flags bit 18 OR /StemV > 120
- Italic: font name contains "Italic"/"Oblique" OR /ItalicAngle != 0
- Subscript: text_rise < -0.1 * font_size; Superscript: text_rise > 0.1 * font_size
- Mojibake detection: sequences characteristic of Latin-1 decoded as UTF-8 (e.g. A-tilde-c-acute for e-acute); re-decode via encoding_rs if score improves
- Soft hyphen U+00AD stripped from output
- Wordlist: 20k English words as compile-time phf::Set; binary size gate < 250 KB via cargo bloat; if exceeded, swap to bloomfilter feature
- Non-English documents (per /Lang or detected): dict-word signal disabled
- BrokenVector escalation requires ocr feature; without it, page emitted with BROKENVECTOR_OCR_UNAVAILABLE diagnostic

## Acceptance criteria

- All 7 sub-phase beads (4.1-4.7) closed
- pdftract-core::layout module compiles
- All fixture PDFs in tests/fixtures/vector/ extract to plain text matching ground truth (CER < 0.5%)
- Reading order correctness > 95% on multi-column fixtures (CI-gated)
- Readability score > 0.85 on clean vector fixtures (CI-gated)
- Header/footer dedup works across 10-page document; classified blocks excluded from --text output
- Ligature repair, hyphenation repair, mojibake repair all demonstrated on fixtures
- BrokenVector escalation routes to Phase 5.5 when ocr feature compiled in

## Blocks

- Phase 5 (OCR integration) — 4.7 escalation feeds back into 5.1 page classification
- Phase 6.1 (JSON output) — needs Block + Span types defined
- Phase 6.5 (Markdown output) — consumes block kind taxonomy

## See also

- Plan section: Phase 4: Text Assembly and Layout
- docs/research/word-boundary-reconstruction.md
- docs/research/watermark-and-background-separation.md

## Scope

Document and enforce the serve-mode security constraints in code and runtime behavior:

- NO built-in auth (deploy behind reverse proxy); document the design decision; print startup banner advertising the no-auth posture
- NO file-path parameters on any endpoint (all PDFs arrive via multipart upload bytes; server never reads from server filesystem on behalf of request)
- max_decompress_gb form field maps to ExtractionOptions.max_decompress_bytes (multiply by 1<<30)
- --max-decompress-gb CLI flag sets server-lifetime default; per-request form field overrides
- --max-upload-mb (default 256 MB) caps request size via tower-http RequestBodyLimit; hard cap at 4 GiB

## Why this matters

Without auth, an unprotected pdftract serve on a public port is an open door for resource exhaustion or extraction-as-a-service abuse. The plan is explicit (line 2138) that auth is out of scope; the contract is \"deploy behind a proxy\". Making the no-auth posture visible at startup time + enforcing the path-parameter-free design eliminates the most common misconfigurations.

## Implementation guidance

- No auth middleware in the axum router; document the design decision in module rustdoc
- Startup banner printed to stdout on serve start:
  ```
  pdftract serve is starting on 0.0.0.0:8080.
  *** NO BUILT-IN AUTH *** — Deploy behind a reverse proxy for production. See docs/operations/serve-* for examples.
  ```
- File-path safety: PDF is always received as multipart upload bytes; never accept a path parameter. Confirm no endpoint accepts a query or path parameter naming a server-local file
- max_decompress_gb form field: parse from multipart; apply to per-request ExtractionOptions
- --max-decompress-gb CLI flag: server lifetime default (used when per-request field is absent)
- --max-upload-mb: default 256; max 4096 (hard cap to prevent integer overflow); tower-http RequestBodyLimit::layer(max_upload_mb * 1024 * 1024)
- Update CLI --help text to call out the security model: \"pdftract serve has no built-in authentication. Deploy behind a reverse proxy (nginx, Traefik, Caddy) for production use.\"

## Critical considerations

- Path-parameter rejection is by design: there is no endpoint that accepts a server-local path; all PDFs come in via multipart. Confirm by route audit
- --max-upload-mb cap-of-cap at 4 GiB: prevents integer overflow when computing the byte limit
- Decompression limit defense against zip-bomb PDFs; surfaced via DECOMPRESSION_LIMIT error code (matches Phase 1.5 lexer convention)
- Startup banner is printed regardless of TTY (logs are observable from systemd journal, k8s logs); use eprintln! (stderr) for serve modes to keep stdout clean

## Acceptance criteria

- Startup banner printed on serve start (visible in test by capturing stderr)
- Attempted GET /extract?path=/etc/passwd returns 404 (no such endpoint accepts query parameters)
- Decompression limit enforced: zip-bomb fixture rejected with HTTP 422 + DECOMPRESSION_LIMIT code in JSON body
- --max-upload-mb=4097 rejected at CLI parse (hard cap exceeded)
- CLI help text mentions the no-auth posture and points to docs/operations/

## References

- Plan section: Phase 6.4 security constraints (lines 2136-2139)
- Security Hardening epic (pdftract-bgj)
- Coordinator: pdftract-1i366 (parent)
Labels: http-serve, phase-6, security

## Scope

Implement Sauvola adaptive thresholding (via leptonica-plumbing) and Otsu global thresholding (via image crate) plus the 3x3 median-filter denoising step. Wired by the 5.3.2 dispatch decision.

## Why this matters

This is where the image becomes binary (black/white) for Tesseract. Wrong choice or wrong parameters here cost WER directly. The 3x3 median filter cleans salt-and-pepper noise typical of physical scans without blurring character edges.

## Implementation guidance

- Sauvola: leptonica-plumbing's pixSauvolaBinarize with window 15x15 and k=0.34 (defaults); document any deviation
- Otsu: image crate's imageproc::contrast::otsu_level + threshold for global threshold
- Median filter: 3x3 kernel, separable not required (3x3 is small enough); use imageproc::filter::median_filter
- Order: contrast normalization (5.3.2) -> binarization -> denoise
- Skip both binarization and denoise for ImageSource::Jbig2 (already binary, already clean)

## Critical considerations

- Sauvola is computationally heavier than Otsu — but correctness on uneven lighting is worth the cost on physical scans
- Sauvola window size MUST be smaller than the dominant character height (otherwise the local mean blurs across characters)
- 3x3 median is appropriate; 5x5 over-blurs (don't be tempted)
- Output of binarization is a GrayImage with only 0 or 255 pixel values; document this contract
- Determinism: Sauvola and Otsu are both deterministic for same input

## Acceptance criteria

- Uneven-lighting fixture (binding-shadow): Sauvola produces clean binary; visually verified (critical test)
- Clean digital-origin grayscale fixture: Otsu produces correct binary
- JBIG2 fixture: both binarization and denoise skipped (output == input)
- 3x3 median removes salt-and-pepper without changing character bbox count
- WER on standard scan fixture: full preprocessing pipeline (incl. Sauvola + median) < raw-input WER

## References

- Plan section: Phase 5.3 steps 3-4 (lines 1876-1877)
- imageproc::contrast::otsu_level
- leptonica pixSauvolaBinarize

issue.description:
## Scope

Build the complete object -> byte-offset map from the file's xref structure. The xref resolver is the bridge between ObjRef and the byte offset where its indirect object lives. Four strategies attempted in order on failure:

1. Traditional xref table (PDF <=1.4 default; still valid in 1.5+)
2. Xref streams (PDF 1.5+)
3. Hybrid files (traditional + xref stream merged)
4. Forward scan fallback (sequential `N G obj` pattern search; emits `XREF_REPAIRED`)

Plus:
- Incremental updates via `/Prev` chain (later revisions override earlier)
- Linearized PDF detection (`/Linearized` dict in first object) with first-page xref + full xref merge
- Forward scan disabled for linearized files (would find the partial leading xref and stop)
- Forward scan disabled for remote sources (would require downloading the entire file — coordinates with Phase 1.8)

Child beads:
- Traditional xref table parser (20-byte fixed-width entries)
- Xref stream parser (PDF 1.5+, /W field widths, FlateDecode body, type 0/1/2 entries)
- Hybrid file merger (traditional table + xref stream priority logic)
- Forward scan fallback (`N G obj` sequential scan, emits XREF_REPAIRED)
- Incremental update chain handler (/Prev recursive load + override semantics)
- Linearized PDF detector + first-page-xref + full-xref merger
- Xref test fixture corpus: well-formed, corrupt, linearized, multi-revision

## Why this matters

The xref table is the random-access index that makes PDFs more than a sequential dump of objects. Without it, every page access requires a forward scan. Real-world PDFs are notoriously fond of xref corruption — `startxref` off by one is the single most common malformation. The 4-strategy fallback is what lets pdftract handle PDFs that other parsers reject.

INV-8 is paramount here: xref parsing must never panic. A truncated file with a corrupt xref must produce SOME object map (possibly empty) plus a diagnostic, never an exception.

## Critical considerations

- The 20-byte traditional xref entry format is rigid: `nnnnnnnnnn ggggg n \n` (10-digit offset, 5-digit generation, n/f flag, CR+LF or SP+LF). Each entry is exactly 20 bytes. Real-world: some producers emit ` \n` instead of `\r\n`; both must work
- Xref stream entries use variable widths from `/W [type_w obj_w gen_w]`: type-0 (free), type-1 (in use, gives byte offset), type-2 (compressed in ObjStm, gives host obj + index)
- Hybrid files (PDF 1.5+): trailer dict has `/XRefStm offset` pointing at a supplementary xref stream; the traditional table is authoritative for objects it covers, the stream fills gaps
- Incremental updates: trailer dict's `/Prev offset` recursively loads earlier xref; LATER revisions OVERRIDE earlier ones for the same object number (last-write-wins). Implement as recursive load with a HashMap<ObjRef, (offset, type)>
- Linearized PDFs: first object after the header is the linearization dict (`/Linearized /L total_len ...`). The first-page xref is small (just the objects needed for page 1); the full xref is at EOF. Merge with full-xref-priority
- Forward scan strategy: byte-by-byte search for `<digit>+ <digit>+ obj\n` pattern. Slow (O(N)) but correctness is everything. Emit `XREF_REPAIRED` diagnostic when triggered so users know corruption was bypassed
- /Prev chain depth limit: 32 revisions max; emit STRUCT_DEPTH_EXCEEDED on deeper chains (adversarial input)
- For remote sources (Phase 1.8), strategies 1-3 fetch tail bytes via Range; strategy 4 (forward scan) is DISABLED because it would require downloading the entire file

## Acceptance criteria

- All 7 child beads closed
- All Critical tests from plan Section 1.3 pass:
  - PDF with /Prev chain of 3 revisions: latest value of each object number wins
  - Type-2 xref entry: object resolved through /ObjStm correctly
  - Hybrid file: traditional entries override stream entries for same object numbers
  - File truncated after xref: forward scan finds all objects before truncation point
  - startxref offset off by one (common real-world corruption): forward scan triggered, XREF_REPAIRED diagnostic emitted
- Linearized fixture: first-page xref + full xref merged; full xref entries override
- All xref resolution paths INV-8 maintained
- Module under `crates/pdftract-core/src/parser/xref/`

## References

- Phase 1.8 (Remote source disables forward scan)
- KU-7 (linearization fingerprint test)

## Scope

Implement xy_cut(blocks, page_width, page_height) -> Vec<usize> returning input block indices in reading order. Algorithm: find widest VERTICAL whitespace gap, split into left+right; recurse on each half; find widest HORIZONTAL gap; recurse top-then-bottom; continue until single column.

## Why this matters

XY-cut is canonical for rectilinear layouts (Nagy & Seth 1984) — works for academic papers, books. The PREFERRED path of reading-order pipeline.

## Implementation guidance

- Recursive function with MAX_DEPTH = 20.
- find_vertical_split: project x-extents, find largest no-coverage gap; if > threshold, split.
- find_horizontal_split: similarly for y-axis.
- Threshold base: column gap from Phase 4.3.
- Tabulate region count + small-region count for Docstrum trigger.
- Leaf: sort y-desc.

## Critical considerations

- INV: prefer vertical split first (columns dominate).
- > 10 regions with < 3 blocks: caller switches to Docstrum.
- Single block / empty: return as-is.

## Acceptance criteria

- 2-column page 5 blocks each: order col0 all, col1 all.
- 3-column: col0, col1, col2.
- Single column: top-to-bottom.
- Full-width heading + 2 cols below: heading first, col0, col1.
- Pathological scattered: returns order, small-region count signals Docstrum.

issue.description:
## Scope

Build the in-memory document model over the xref-resolved object graph. The Document Model is the high-level "what's in this PDF" view that downstream phases (font pipeline, content streams, output) consume. It is the final product of Phase 1: at the end of 1.4, a caller has a fully-typed Document with resolved page tree, inherited resources, decrypted streams (if encrypted), and detected feature flags.

Child beads:
- Document catalog parser (/Root with /Pages, /Outlines, /MarkInfo, /StructTreeRoot, /AcroForm, /Names, /Metadata, /PageLabels, /OCProperties)
- Page tree flattener with inherited attributes (MediaBox, CropBox, BleedBox, TrimBox, ArtBox, Resources, Rotate)
- Resource dictionary inheritance (per-page merged ResourceDict)
- Encryption dictionary detection + RC4/AES-128/AES-256 decryption (decrypt feature, default-on)
- Optional Content Groups (OCG) handling — default visibility from /OCProperties /D
- JavaScript / XFA / conformance detection (XMP via quick-xml)
- Outline traversal (linked-list walk; UTF-16BE BOM detection; destination decoding)
- Test corpus: encrypted (RC4, AES-128, AES-256), tagged, OCG, multi-revision, outline-heavy, missing /MediaBox

## Why this matters

The Document Model is the API surface that Phase 2 (fonts), Phase 3 (content streams), Phase 4 (text assembly), and Phase 5 (OCR) all build on. A bug here propagates to every output. The encryption support is what lets pdftract handle real-world locked PDFs without the user having to pre-decrypt with qpdf. The OCG handling determines whether layered content (e.g. annotations toggled off in a printable view) is extracted.

## Critical considerations

- Page tree inheritance is the trickiest part: page dict overrides parent dict; root /Pages is the ultimate fallback. The walk visits each leaf page dict, accumulating inherited attributes from each ancestor /Pages node
- Resource dict inheritance: per-key last-write-wins at the page level. If a page's /Resources is `<< /Font << /F1 ... >> >>` and the parent's is `<< /Font << /F2 ... >> /XObject << ... >> >>`, the merged result is `<< /Font << /F1 ... /F2 ... >> /XObject << ... >> >>` (page overrides per-key, but per-namespace merges)
- Content stream concatenation: if a page's /Contents is an array of stream refs, ALL streams are decoded and concatenated in order before Phase 3 processing begins. Graphics state is NOT reset between concatenated streams — they are treated as a single logical stream
- Encryption: detect /Encrypt in trailer; identify /Standard handler; extract /V, /R, /KeyLength, /CF, /StmF, /StrF; try empty-string password first, then user-supplied (ExtractionOptions.password). On unknown handler: ENCRYPTION_UNSUPPORTED, abort
- OCG: read /OCProperties /D /BaseState (ON or OFF, default ON); each OCG's membership in /D /ON or /D /OFF lists determines default visibility. During content streams (Phase 3), suppress glyphs inside `/OC /OCGRef` BDC blocks whose group is OFF
- JavaScript detection: scan /OpenAction, /AA (document + page + form field + annotation), record `contains_javascript: true`. Never EXECUTE; just flag
- Conformance: parse /Metadata stream as XMP via quick-xml; extract pdfaid:part and pdfaid:conformance to construct values like PDF/A-1b. quick-xml MUST be moved from `ocr` feature to `default` (per plan note)
- XFA: check for /AcroForm /XFA presence; record `contains_xfa: true`. Do NOT parse XFA (it's an XML-based form spec; out of scope)
- Outline traversal: linked list via /First and /Next pointers; UTF-16BE BOM (FE FF) detection for /Title decoding; /Dest array or /A /GoTo /Dest action-based destinations

## Acceptance criteria

- All 8 child beads closed
- All Critical tests from plan Section 1.4 pass:
  - Page inheriting MediaBox from grandparent /Pages node
  - Page overriding /Resources /Font partially (merged, not replaced)
  - PageLabels number tree: roman-numeral labels followed by arabic labels
  - Encrypted file with empty owner password: decrypts successfully
  - Encrypted file with unknown handler: ENCRYPTION_UNSUPPORTED, no crash
- 3-level outline hierarchy: all levels, titles, page destinations extracted correctly

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement AES-256 decryption per PDF spec 7.6.4.3 (PDF 2.0; ISO 32000-2) for V=5 R=6. The key derivation differs significantly from RC4/AES-128 — it uses SHA-256 + SHA-384 + SHA-512 in a multi-round Argon2-like protocol (called \"Algorithm 8\"). CBC-mode AES-256 decryption with a 16-byte IV prefix.

## Why this matters

AES-256 is the modern standard (Acrobat X / 2010+); all PDFs encrypted by post-2010 Acrobat use V=5 R=6 by default. The key derivation is the most algorithmically distinct from prior PDF encryption (RustCrypto's sha2 crate covers everything but the orchestration is custom). Getting it wrong silently produces decrypted-garbage which is hard to diagnose.

## Implementation guidance

- Crate: aes = \"0.8\", cbc = \"0.1\", sha2 = \"0.10\" (RustCrypto)
- Module: crates/pdftract-core/src/encryption/aes_256.rs (feature-gated on decrypt)
- File key derivation (PDF spec Algorithm 8 + 9):
  1. Compute hash H = SHA-256(password || first 8 bytes of /U || /U || first 8 bytes of /O || /O)
  2. Iterate 64 times with the round-key protocol involving AES-128-CBC + SHA-256/384/512 selection based on the last byte of the previous hash mod 3
  3. After 64+ iterations, the final H is the user/owner key material
  4. To recover the file encryption key, decrypt /UE (or /OE for owner password path) using H as AES-256-CBC key with IV all-zeros and no padding
- Per-object key derivation: V=5 does NOT use per-object key derivation; the file key is used directly for every object (with the IV as the first 16 bytes of the encrypted blob)
- AES-256 CBC decryption: IV (first 16 bytes) + ciphertext + PKCS#5 padding (16-byte block size)
- /Perms decryption: in V=5, the /Perms field is a 16-byte AES-256-ECB encrypted blob containing the permissions bits; decrypt with the file key
- User password validation (Algorithm 11): compute hash with /U's first-8 bytes salt; compare first 32 bytes against /U
- Owner password validation (Algorithm 12): similar but with /O salt + user-hash inclusion
- Public API: aes_256_decrypt(file_key: &[u8], data: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>>

## Critical considerations

- The 64-round key derivation protocol is the most complex PDF crypto; the round selection rule (last_byte % 3 -> SHA-256/384/512) is the easy-to-miss subtlety. PDF spec Algorithm 2.B steps 1-7 must be implemented verbatim
- AES-256-CBC with no-padding for /UE/OE decryption (these are exactly 32 bytes); PKCS#5-padding for general object decryption
- /UE and /OE are 32 bytes each (the AES-256 key encrypted); /Perms is 16 bytes (ECB-encrypted permissions)
- V=5 PDFs MAY use /Identity crypt filter for selected streams (e.g. metadata) — honor per-filter selection
- The first 8 bytes of /U is the user-hash salt; the next 8 bytes is the validation salt; bytes 16-47 are the hash (in /U total is 48 bytes per V=5)
- All hashes are SHA-256 (32-byte output) by default; SHA-384 (48-byte) and SHA-512 (64-byte) are used in the round protocol depending on previous-hash-byte % 3
- /OE is required for owner-password path; if missing, owner password cannot be used

## Acceptance criteria

- Decrypt a V=5 R=6 AES-256 fixture with correct user password → byte-identical to reference
- Decrypt with correct owner password → byte-identical
- Decrypt with wrong password → validation fails; emit ENCRYPTION_BAD_PASSWORD
- /Perms decryption recovers the correct permission bits (compare with reference)
- Test vector: PDF spec Annex A.4 worked example
- Strings and streams both decrypted correctly (test fixture)
- /Identity crypt filter for metadata stream → no-op pass-through

## References

- Plan section: encryption AES-256
- PDF spec 7.6.4.3 (Standard security handler V=5; ISO 32000-2)
- aes crate
- sha2 crate: https://crates.io/crates/sha2
- Coordinator: pdftract-1z0qt (parent)
- Sibling: encryption detection, RC4 decryption, AES-128 decryption
Labels: aes, encryption, phase-1, pdf2

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the pdfium-render rendering path gated behind the full-render Cargo feature. Provides accurate rendering for complex PDFs with overlapping images, image masks, soft masks, blend modes, and other geometry the direct-compositing path cannot handle. Runtime selection via ExtractionOptions.full_render (no-op if feature absent).

## Why this matters

Real-world scanned PDFs include forms with overlay annotations, multi-layer scans with corrections, and documents with translucent overlays. Without full-render, those PDFs OCR poorly. Keeping pdfium-render opt-in is the binary-size compromise: pdftract:ocr stays under 120 MB while pdftract:full ships pdfium for the hard cases.

## Implementation guidance

- Crate: pdfium-render gated under cfg(feature = "full_render")
- Module: pdftract-ocr/src/render/pdfium_path.rs with pub fn render_page_via_pdfium(doc, page_index, dpi) -> Result<GrayImage>
- pdfium initialization is lazy + thread-local (init is expensive); reuse Pdfium instance across pages
- Honor DPI selection from 5.2.3; convert pdfium's RGB output to GrayImage via luminance
- Provide a runtime detection helper pdftract::ocr::has_full_render() -> bool used by serve mode to validate full_render form-field requests
- Compile-time guard: if feature absent, the entire module is excluded and ExtractionOptions.full_render is silently ignored (no panic, log a debug message at most)

## Critical considerations

- pdfium native library is ~20 MB; pdftract:full image budget is ~140 MB, NOT 120 MB
- pdfium runtime must be loadable at startup; doctor command (6.10) checks this
- Pdfium thread-safety: API requires per-thread Pdfium instance; use thread_local!
- pdfium licensing: BSD-style, compatible — confirm in NOTICE
- Soft-mask / blend-mode fixtures that fail in 5.2.1 should render correctly here (regression test)

## Acceptance criteria

- cargo build --features ocr,serve,full-render produces a binary that exposes the path
- cargo build --features ocr,serve (no full-render) does NOT pull in pdfium
- Soft-masked image fixture: pdfium output matches the visual reference (pixel diff < 1%)
- Runtime fallback: ExtractionOptions.full_render = true with feature absent -> direct compositing path used, no panic
- Binary size CI gate: pdftract:full <= 140 MB

## References

- Plan section: Phase 5.2 full-render feature (line 1854)
- Phase 0 Docker image variants table (line 1856)
- Phase 6.10 doctor check for pdfium native lib

issue.description:
## Goal

StructTree exploitation, table detection, AcroForm/XFA, attachments, signatures, hyperlinks, article threads, grep, inspector, configurable profiles. Each sub-task is independent and can be developed in parallel.

## Sub-phases (all independent of each other after Phase 6)

- 7.1 StructTree Exploitation (Tagged PDF) - walk /StructTreeRoot; map element types to block kinds (P/H1-H6/Table/L/LI/Figure/Artifact); /ActualText overrides extracted text; /Alt for figures; /Lang BCP-47; MCID-to-StructElem via ParentTree; reading_order_algorithm = struct_tree; fallback to XY-cut if MarkInfo /Suspects true and coverage < 80%
- 7.2 Table Detection - line-based via horizontal+vertical path segments (m/l/S, re/S, re/f); borderless via x0-aligned spans (3+ rows confirm); cell content assignment by centroid containment; header detection via bold font or StructTree TH; merged cells via missing interior edges
- 7.3 Digital Signature Metadata - AcroForm /Fields with /FT /Sig; extract /T name, /V Sig dict (/Name, /M, /Reason, /Location, /ByteRange, /SubFilter); validation_status = not_checked (no cryptographic validation in v1)
- 7.4 AcroForm and XFA Field Extraction - walk /Fields recursively; Tx/Btn/Ch/Sig types; nested /Kids names dot-joined; XFA streams parsed via quick-xml; XFA values prefer over AcroForm on overlap
- 7.5 Portfolio and Attachment Extraction - /EmbeddedFiles name tree; Filespec dicts; decode EF streams; 50 MB size limit (metadata only beyond); base64-encoded data field
- 7.6 Hyperlink and Annotation Extraction - per-page /Annots; Link annotations (URI or internal /Dest); other annotation subtypes (Highlight, Stamp, FreeText, Note, Squiggly, StrikeOut, Underline) with /Subtype, /Rect, /Contents, /T author, /M date, /C color
- 7.7 Article Thread Chains - /Threads array; /F first bead + /N next chain; circular termination; reconstruct ordered bead list per thread with page_index + rect
- 7.8 pdftract grep - folder search with bbox results and progress observability; ripgrep-style flags; --highlight DIR writes annotated PDFs; --progress + --progress-json; --json output; 50 MB/s throughput gate on 1000-PDF corpus; >= 2x pdfgrep, >= 3x pdftotext+ripgrep
- 7.9 Inspector Mode - pdftract inspect FILE.pdf --port; SVG page rendering (no rasterization); 8 toggleable overlay layers (spans, blocks, columns, reading order, confidence heatmap, OCR regions, MCID, anchors); hover tooltips; keyboard navigation; <80 KB frontend bundle; separate subcommand (not part of serve)
- 7.10 Document Profiles - user-editable YAML with match DSL (text_contains, structural, heading_matches, has_currency_pattern, etc.), extraction tuning (reading_order, table_detection, readability_threshold), field-extraction DSL (regex, near, region, pick, parse); 9 built-in profiles; pdftract profiles list/show/export/install/validate; --auto and --profile flags; XDG config path; --profile-hot-reload for serve

## Rationale

Phase 7 is the differentiation layer: the features that make pdftract better than pdfminer / pypdf / pdfplumber. Tagged-PDF support (7.1) gives authoritative reading order. Table reconstruction (7.2) makes PDFs useful as data sources. Forms (7.4), signatures (7.3), attachments (7.5), hyperlinks (7.6), threads (7.7) cover the full PDF feature surface.

The three brilliant-idea features (7.8 grep, 7.9 inspector, 7.10 profiles) are user-leverage wins:
- 7.8 grep: single-pass search across folders; bbox results enable highlight annotations
- 7.9 inspector: trust + debuggability via overlay-rich web UI
- 7.10 profiles: type-specialized extraction without code; YAML-extensible

All Phase 7 sub-tasks are independent - they can be developed in parallel by separate developers once Phase 6 is complete.

## Critical considerations

- StructTree validation: MarkInfo /Suspects true triggers XY-cut fallback when coverage < 80%
- Table merged-cells via missing interior edges; rowspan/colspan inferred from geometry
- Signatures: pdftract does NOT cryptographically validate (out of scope); validation_status = not_checked
- Attachments > 50 MB get metadata only + truncated: true; base64 with standard alphabet
- grep: must NEVER appear hung - progress bar updates >= every 500ms
- grep: --highlight DIR adds /Highlight annotations (not content stream modification) so original PDF remains intact
- Inspector: SVG rendering uses glyph outlines from ttf-parser (no rasterization, no pdfium dependency in default features)
- Inspector: frontend bundle compiled into binary via include_bytes!; < 80 KB target
- Inspector: separate subcommand (per user requirement) - NOT a serve mode feature
- Profiles: built-in compiled via include_str!; user profiles loaded from XDG config dir or --profile-dir
- Profiles: profile-hot-reload disabled by default (file I/O on every request wasteful); inotify-based
- Profile YAML loader rejects secrets keys at top level (PROFILE_SECRETS_FORBIDDEN)

## Acceptance criteria

- All 10 sub-phase beads (7.1-7.10) closed
- Tagged PDF reading order matches StructTree element order
- Table extraction handles 5x3 bordered + borderless 2-column + merged-header colspan=3
- AcroForm tx/btn/ch + XFA all extract values correctly
- pdftract grep 50 MB/s throughput on 1000-PDF corpus (CI-gated)
- pdftract inspect renders 100-page PDF first page within 2 seconds
- Built-in invoice profile classifies 50-invoice corpus with >= 90% field accuracy
- All 9 built-in profiles ship with >= 5 fixtures each + regression test

## References

- Plan: Phase 7 (lines 2536-3072)
- Depends on: Phase 6 complete (output schema for fields added by Phase 7)
- Built-in profile fixtures: tests/fixtures/profiles/<name>/

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement two signal evaluators that share the char_validity_rate input from Phase 4.7 readability:

- char_validity_rate < 0.4 -> BrokenVector with strength 0.80
- char_validity_rate > 0.85 -> Vector with strength 0.90

## Why this matters

Char validity is the highest-fidelity signal for distinguishing extractable vector text (>0.85) from broken-vector text (<0.4) where most glyphs are gibberish (mis-encoded). Used after the stronger image-presence signals don't fire.

## Implementation guidance

- Signature (two evaluators, but they share input so package together):
  ```rust
  pub fn char_validity_rate(ctx: &PageContext) -> Option<Signal>
  ```
- Logic:
  ```rust
  let rate = ctx.char_validity_rate?; // Option<f32>; None if Phase 4.7 hasn't run
  if rate < 0.4 {
      return Some(Signal { name: \"char_validity_rate_low\", strength: 0.80, vote: PageClass::BrokenVector });
  }
  if rate > 0.85 {
      return Some(Signal { name: \"char_validity_rate_high\", strength: 0.90, vote: PageClass::Vector });
  }
  None
  ```
- Return None for the middle band (0.4..=0.85); other evaluators handle

## Critical considerations

- char_validity_rate MUST be Option (None if Phase 4.7 has not run on the page yet); evaluator returns None in that case
- The 0.4/0.85 thresholds are calibrated against the Phase 5 fixture corpus
- This signal can return either BrokenVector or Vector; the evaluator chain doesn't pre-assume the vote

## Acceptance criteria

- rate = 0.3 → Some(Signal { 0.80, BrokenVector })
- rate = 0.9 → Some(Signal { 0.90, Vector })
- rate = 0.6 → None (middle band)
- rate = None (Phase 4.7 not run) → None
- Unit tests for all branches

## References

- Plan section: Phase 5.1.2
- Phase 4.7 readability (provides char_validity_rate)
- Coordinator: pdftract-22p (parent)

issue.description:
## Scope

When remote server does not support Range requests (or returns 200 for a Range request), fall back to downloading entire file into temp file, then memory-mapping it as MmapSource.

Triggered by:
- Accept-Ranges absent OR `Accept-Ranges: none` in HEAD response
- Range request returns 200 (full file) instead of 206
- After fallback, emit REMOTE_NO_RANGE_SUPPORT diagnostic

## Implementation guidance

- Public API: invoked by HTTP fetch sequence orchestrator when range support missing
- Algorithm:
  1. Create temp file via tempfile::NamedTempFile::new() (`tempfile = "3"` crate)
  2. Stream response body from `ureq::get(url).call()?.into_reader()` to temp via io::copy
  3. Sync to disk
  4. Reopen as MmapSource
  5. Hold NamedTempFile for lifetime of MmapSource (deleted on drop)
- Disk space check: before download, verify Content-Length fits in available space via nix::sys::statvfs; if not, abort with REMOTE_INSUFFICIENT_DISK
- Cleanup: NamedTempFile's Drop deletes; RAII even on panic

## Critical considerations

- Acceptance criterion: server without Range -> fallback, warning, extraction completes
- Disk space pressure: multi-GB PDFs may not fit /tmp; user can override via TMPDIR env var (POSIX, respected by tempfile)
- Temp file naming: tempfile generates random name in /tmp; no URL leakage
- Performance: 100 MB download in ~10 sec on 100 Mbps; unavoidable when Range not supported
- Fallback INVISIBLE to higher layers: Phase 1.3 and 1.4 see normal MmapSource; only difference is REMOTE_NO_RANGE_SUPPORT diagnostic
- gzip-compressed response (Content-Encoding: gzip): ureq auto-decompresses
- For very small files (< 1 MB), fallback path may be faster than Range-based; don't optimize
- INV-8: download failures emit REMOTE_FETCH_INTERRUPTED + empty MmapSource

## Acceptance criteria

- Mock server without Range: fallback triggers; REMOTE_NO_RANGE_SUPPORT emitted; extraction completes
- Mock server returning 200 for Range: same fallback path
- Disk-space-insufficient: REMOTE_INSUFFICIENT_DISK emitted; clean abort
- Temp file deleted on Document drop (verified)
- gzip-compressed response: bytes decoded, document parses
- INV-8 maintained

## References

- Plan section: Phase 1.8 line 1248 (server fallback)
- Dependency Matrix: tempfile (transitive via ureq), ureq

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the 14 environment checks performed by pdftract doctor. Each check is a function returning a CheckResult { status: OK | WARN | FAIL, detail: String }. Checks are feature-gated where appropriate (Tesseract checks only when ocr is compiled; pdfium-render only when full-render is compiled).

Module: crates/pdftract-cli/src/doctor/checks/ with one file per check + a registry that the output layer iterates.

## Why this matters

The checks are the doctor subcommand's core; they encode every \"things that go wrong in deployment\" lesson learned across pdftract's userbase. Each check's OK/WARN/FAIL thresholds are calibrated against actual failure modes (e.g. Tesseract major 3 fails because OCR results are unusable; major 4 warns because some glyphs OCR incorrectly; major 5+ is OK).

## Checks list

| Check | OK | WARN | FAIL |
|---|---|---|---|
| pdftract binary | Version + git-sha + features compiled in listed | — | — |
| tesseract install (ocr feature) | tesseract --version parses; major >= 5 | major == 4 | binary missing or major <= 3 |
| tesseract languages (ocr feature) | required langs (eng default; configurable via --lang) all present | optional langs missing | eng missing |
| leptonica install (transitive Tesseract dep) | pkg-config --modversion lept >= 1.79 | older | not found |
| libtiff (ocr feature) | found via pkg-config | — | not found |
| libopenjp2 (ocr feature) | found | — | not found |
| pdfium native lib (full-render compiled) | runtime detection succeeds, version >= 6555 | older | not found |
| network reachability (remote compiled) | HEAD https://example.com returns 2xx in <= 5 s | 3xx / slow | failure |
| cache directory (--cache-dir passed or cache default-on) | writable, free space >= 1 GiB, layout version current | free space < 1 GiB or layout migration available | not writable or layout incompatible |
| profile search path (profiles compiled) | every YAML parses; no PROFILE_SECRETS_FORBIDDEN | dir empty | parse errors or secret-keys present |
| ulimit -n (Linux/macOS) | >= 1024 | 512 <= n < 1024 | < 512 |
| available RAM (from /proc/meminfo or sysctl) | >= 256 MiB free | 128 MiB <= n < 256 MiB | < 128 MiB |
| system locale | UTF-8 locale active | non-UTF-8 with C fallback | unset |
| temp dir writable ($TMPDIR / /tmp) | writable + free space >= 100 MiB | free space < 100 MiB | not writable |

## Implementation guidance

- Trait:
  ```rust
  pub struct CheckResult { pub name: &'static str, pub status: CheckStatus, pub detail: String }
  pub enum CheckStatus { Ok, Warn, Fail, NotApplicable }
  pub trait Check { fn name(&self) -> &'static str; fn run(&self, ctx: &DoctorCtx) -> CheckResult; }
  ```
- Registry: Vec<Box<dyn Check>> built at startup; conditional cfg! compilation gates feature-specific checks
- DoctorCtx holds: requested languages (--lang), cache_dir (--cache-dir), profile_dir (--profile-dir), feature flags compiled-in (env-from-build)
- pdftract binary check: env!(\"CARGO_PKG_VERSION\") + env!(\"GIT_SHA\") from build.rs + compile-time feature list. Always OK
- tesseract install: spawn tesseract --version; parse \"tesseract 5.3.0\" pattern; capture stderr too (some distros print to stderr)
- tesseract languages: spawn tesseract --list-langs; parse newline-separated list; cross-reference with ctx.required_langs (defaults to [\"eng\"])
- leptonica: spawn pkg-config --modversion lept; parse semver
- libtiff: pkg-config --exists libtiff-4 (exit 0 = found)
- libopenjp2: pkg-config --exists libopenjp2 (exit 0 = found)
- pdfium: load the dynamic library via libloading or pdfium-render's runtime detector; query FPDF_GetVersion (>= 6555 means \"reasonably modern\")
- network reachability: ureq::head(\"https://example.com\").call() with 5s timeout; classify 2xx as OK, 3xx as WARN, anything else as FAIL
- cache directory: std::fs::metadata + nix::sys::statvfs to check writable + free space; read index.json schema version
- profile search path: walk dir; parse each .yaml via serde_yaml; check for forbidden keys (password, token, secret) per the PROFILE_SECRETS_FORBIDDEN rule
- ulimit -n: libc::getrlimit(RLIMIT_NOFILE); Linux + macOS; Windows: N/A
- available RAM: /proc/meminfo parse on Linux; sysctlbyname(\"hw.memsize\") on macOS; GlobalMemoryStatusEx on Windows
- system locale: read LANG / LC_ALL env vars; check for \"UTF-8\" or \"utf8\" substring (case-insensitive)
- temp dir writable: tempfile::Builder::tempfile_in($TMPDIR or /tmp) round-trip + statvfs free space

## Critical considerations

- All checks must catch panics — std::panic::catch_unwind wrapper around each Check::run; on panic, return FAIL with the panic message
- Each check has a max runtime budget; network reachability is the longest at 5 s; everything else < 100 ms
- Don't run extraction or load PDFs in doctor; this is environment-only
- Feature-gated checks: cfg(feature = \"ocr\") on tesseract/leptonica/libtiff/libopenjp2 modules; cfg(feature = \"full-render\") on pdfium check; etc. Not-compiled checks return CheckStatus::NotApplicable
- The required-langs default is [\"eng\"]; --lang fra (passed to doctor) extends required to [\"eng\", \"fra\"]
- Profile-dir secret detection: serde_yaml::Value::as_mapping iteration; deny-list keys = [\"password\", \"token\", \"secret\", \"api_key\"]; case-insensitive match
- Build-time GIT_SHA injection: in build.rs, capture git rev-parse HEAD output and set as env var GIT_SHA; doctor reads via env!(\"GIT_SHA\")
- Compile-time feature list: in build.rs, enumerate cargo features and emit as a comma-separated env var COMPILED_FEATURES; doctor reads via env!(\"COMPILED_FEATURES\")
- pkg-config invocation must work even when pkg-config is not installed (some minimal containers): if pkg-config binary itself is missing, the lept/libtiff/libopenjp2 checks degrade to running ldconfig -p | grep or a similar fallback

## Acceptance criteria

- Each of the 14 checks has a unit test for OK, WARN, and FAIL paths (where applicable) via fixture-based DoctorCtx
- All checks complete in < 6 s total on a normal deployment (network check is the long pole at 5s budget; rest negligible)
- A check that panics is caught and reported as FAIL with the panic message (no process crash)
- Feature-not-compiled checks return NotApplicable; the output layer skips or marks N/A
- pkg-config not installed: leptonica/libtiff/libopenjp2 checks degrade gracefully (FAIL or WARN with clear detail)
- Profile dir with password: secret-detection FAIL with PROFILE_SECRETS_FORBIDDEN string in detail

## References

- Plan section: Phase 6.10 pdftract doctor (lines 2497-2513)
- INV-8 (no panic)
- Phase 5.4 Tesseract (the OCR checks gate)
- Phase 5.7 profiles + PROFILE_SECRETS_FORBIDDEN rule
- Phase 6.9 cache (cache-dir check)
- Phase 1.8 remote source (network reachability check)
Labels: checks, doctor, phase-6

issue.description:
## Scope

Author the `pdftract-libpdftract-build` WorkflowTemplate. Triggered by milestone tag after `pdftract-build-binaries` completes. Cross-compiles `libpdftract` for all 5 target triples, packages each as `libpdftract-vX.Y.Z-<triple>.tar.gz` (containing .so/.dylib/.dll + .h + .pc), attaches them to the GitHub Release, opens an auto-PR against the Homebrew tap with the updated formula, and emits a draft vcpkg port for manual submission.

## Why this matters

The C-FFI binding has the most distribution surfaces of any SDK (5 triples × 3 channels = 15 outputs) and the highest manual-coordination cost (Homebrew formula updates, vcpkg PRs). Automating these in a single workflow keeps release cadence sustainable.

## Implementation guidance

- WorkflowTemplate file: `k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/pdftract-libpdftract-build.yaml` in `jedarden/declarative-config`
- Inputs: tag name; GitHub PAT from ESO Secret `github-pat-pdftract` (for the formula PR)
- Steps:
  1. `build-libpdftract-matrix`: 5-item matrix over target triples; each invokes `cross build --release -p pdftract-libpdftract --target {{item}} --locked --frozen`
  2. `regenerate-header`: cbindgen regenerates `include/pdftract.h` (built once on host, not per target)
  3. `package-per-triple`: each matrix item packages its output as `libpdftract-vX.Y.Z-<triple>.tar.gz` with `lib/`, `include/`, `lib/pkgconfig/`, `LICENSE-*` directories
  4. `upload-to-github-release`: attach all 5 archives to the existing GitHub Release (created by `pdftract-github-release`); MUST run AFTER `pdftract-github-release` so the release exists
  5. `update-homebrew-tap`: clone `jedarden/homebrew-tap`, edit `Formula/pdftract.rb` with new version + SHA256s for each Bottle, commit, push, open PR (auto-merged by maintainer)
  6. `vcpkg-port-draft`: emit `ports/pdftract/portfile.cmake` + `ports/pdftract/vcpkg.json` as Argo artifacts; the maintainer downloads and PR-submits to `microsoft/vcpkg` manually (vcpkg has strict review requirements that block automated submission)
- Container: cross-rs per-target images for build; `homebrew/brew:latest` for formula update; standard Rust container for cbindgen
- The Homebrew formula uses Bottles (precompiled binaries) per platform, sourced from the GitHub Release attachments
- Re-runnability: GitHub asset upload is `--clobber`; Homebrew formula PR creation is idempotent (re-running checks for existing open PR before creating)

## Critical considerations

- ADR-009: runs on iad-ci with the GitHub PAT; never use GitHub Actions
- The Homebrew tap (`jedarden/homebrew-tap`) is preferred over Homebrew Core because Core has strict notability requirements pdftract may not yet meet at v0.X; document the migration to Core when notability criteria are met (post-v1.0 likely)
- vcpkg port submission to `microsoft/vcpkg` requires: passing CI on Windows/Linux/macOS in vcpkg's own CI, a description, a documentation reference, no GPL deps. The auto-generated portfile is a starting point; manual review and edits will be required
- The workflow runs AFTER `pdftract-github-release` so the release exists for asset attachment; enforced via `dependsOn` in `pdftract-release-cascade`
- The 5-build matrix runs in parallel; failure of one triple does NOT block the other four (`continueOn: failed`)
- Bottles for Homebrew require SHA256s of each platform binary; compute during the package-per-triple step and pipe into the formula update step
- The `pdftract.pc.in` pkg-config file is rendered with the install prefix substituted at install-time, not build-time; document this in the README

## Acceptance criteria

- WorkflowTemplate file lands at the documented path in jedarden/declarative-config
- A test run against a fresh tag produces 5 archives uploaded to the GitHub Release
- A Homebrew formula PR opens against `jedarden/homebrew-tap` with the updated version + Bottle SHA256s
- A vcpkg port draft is emitted as an Argo artifact for manual review
- `brew install jedarden/tap/pdftract` works on a clean macOS box after the formula PR is merged
- Re-running the workflow on the same tag is idempotent
- A simulated failure of one triple does NOT block the other four

## References

- Plan section: SDK Architecture / Per-SDK Release Channels, line 3574 (GitHub Release + Homebrew formula PR + vcpkg port)
- Plan section: SDK Acceptance Criteria, line 3584 (24-hour cascade)
- ADR-009 (Argo only)
- Sibling: C-FFI SDK implementation bead
- Homebrew formula docs: https://docs.brew.sh/Formula-Cookbook
- vcpkg port docs: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/vcpkg/get_started/get-started-adding-to-registry
issue.title: Argo WorkflowTemplate: pdftract-libpdftract-build (GitHub Release + Homebrew formula PR + vcpkg port draft)

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the PyPI upload step in the pdftract-py-ci Argo workflow. Runs ONLY on tag pushes (vX.Y.Z); uses twine to upload all 5 wheels + sdist to PyPI; authenticates with PYPI_TOKEN sealed-secret managed by sealed-secrets in iad-ci.

## Why this matters

PyPI is the canonical distribution channel for Python packages; without the upload step, users can't pip install pdftract. Gating on tag-only prevents accidental uploads from PR builds (PyPI rejects re-uploads of the same version; an accidental main-branch upload would block the next real release).

## Implementation guidance

- Argo workflow step (added to sibling pdftract-py-ci WorkflowTemplate):
  - name: pypi-upload
  - depends: collect-artifacts (success)
  - when: parameter $tag matches regex ^v[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+(-rc\\.[0-9]+)?$
  - container: ghcr.io/pypa/twine:latest
  - command: [\"twine\", \"upload\", \"--username\", \"__token__\", \"--password\", \"$(cat /etc/pypi-token/token)\", \"wheels/*.whl\", \"wheels/*.tar.gz\"]
  - volumeMounts: /etc/pypi-token from secret pypi-token
- Sealed-secret pypi-token at jedarden/declarative-config/k8s/iad-ci/sealed-secrets/pypi-token.yaml
- The sealed-secret unseals to a Secret with the PYPI_TOKEN value (an API token from pypi.org with upload-only scope for the pdftract project)
- Pre-release versions (vX.Y.Z-rc.N) upload to PyPI as pre-releases (no special flag needed; PyPI infers from version)
- ALWAYS use trusted publishing (PyPI's OIDC token exchange) where possible; fall back to API token for the launch
- Skip upload on rebuild of an existing version (PyPI rejects; the workflow should detect and skip with a clear message)

## Critical considerations

- PYPI_TOKEN must have upload-only scope (NOT account-wide write) — security-best-practice
- The sealed-secret is managed via the sealed-secrets controller; rotation requires re-sealing and committing
- ALWAYS use --skip-existing on twine upload to avoid mid-batch failures if a previous run uploaded some wheels
- Tag pattern regex: ^v[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+(-rc\\.[0-9]+)?$ — strict semver with optional rc pre-release; document any extension needed (e.g. -beta.N)
- The upload step is the LAST step in the workflow; failure here is recoverable (re-tag or manual re-upload); failure earlier in the pipeline blocks the upload
- PYPI_TOKEN MUST NEVER appear in logs; use --password $(cat) so the token bytes never traverse env vars (which can leak via process listing)
- Document the runbook for token rotation in docs/operations/pypi-token-rotation.md (separate bead — out of scope here)

## Acceptance criteria

- Workflow step runs only on vX.Y.Z tags
- Successful upload puts all 5 wheels + 1 sdist on PyPI under https://pypi.org/project/pdftract/X.Y.Z/
- Re-running the upload (same version) skips existing wheels with twine --skip-existing
- Failed upload (e.g. PyPI rate-limit) does not corrupt the workflow run; manual retry works
- Sealed-secret pypi-token decrypts correctly in iad-ci cluster
- A PR branch (no tag) does NOT trigger upload step

## References

- Plan section: Phase 6.3.4 (PyPI upload)
- PyPI trusted publishers: https://docs.pypi.org/trusted-publishers/
- twine docs: https://twine.readthedocs.io/
- sealed-secrets controller: https://github.com/bitnami-labs/sealed-secrets
- Coordinator: pdftract-z86x6 (parent)
- Sibling: maturin wheel config, Argo WorkflowTemplate
Labels: phase-6, pypi, release

issue.description:
## Scope

Author docs/operations/manual-release.md as the PB-13 fallback release procedure: when the Argo Workflows runner in iad-ci is degraded or unavailable for a prolonged window, the release lead reproduces the milestone release locally and the CHANGELOG + Revision History records the manual release. Resume Argo-driven releases on the next milestone.

## Why this matters

PB-13 (line 567) explicitly mandates this runbook as the R13 mitigation: Manual release procedure (docs/operations/manual-release.md) reproduces the milestone release locally; release lead executes the steps. R13 (line 549) is rated Likelihood L, Impact H -- low probability but catastrophic if pdftract cannot ship a security patch because Argo is down. The runbook is the explicit fallback that makes the H impact survivable.

## Implementation guidance

- File to create: docs/operations/manual-release.md
- Required content sections:
  - Prerequisites:
    - A clean Linux box (preferably the same Hetzner host that runs Argo); not a developer laptop because the build environment matters for reproducibility
    - All five cross-compile toolchains installed (cross or per-triple targets)
    - Access to OpenBao for the same secrets Argo uses (PyPI token, GitHub release token, Cloudflare token for docs, GPG signing key for tarballs)
    - cargo, rustup, maturin, mdBook, jq, gh installed
  - Step-by-step release procedure:
    1. Verify the tag matches the planned version (git describe --exact-match)
    2. Run the full CI suite locally: cargo test --workspace --all-features
    3. Cross-compile binaries for all five triples: ./scripts/build-release.sh (extracted from the Argo template)
    4. Verify each binary works (cargo run --release on Linux; or just check file output for non-Linux)
    5. Generate SHA-256 checksums: shasum -a 256 dist/* > dist/CHECKSUMS.sha256
    6. GPG sign the checksums file
    7. Build the Python wheels: maturin build --release for each triple via cross
    8. Upload wheels to PyPI: maturin upload (token from OpenBao)
    9. Publish to crates.io: cargo publish for pdftract-core then pdftract-cli (token from OpenBao)
    10. Create GitHub Release: gh release create vX.Y.Z dist/* (token from OpenBao)
    11. Build mdBook: mdbook build docs/user-docs/
    12. Deploy docs: wrangler pages publish to pdftract.com (token from OpenBao)
    13. Generate SLSA Level 2 attestation locally (in-toto / cosign) and attach to the GitHub Release
  - Post-release manual-release record:
    - Append a line to CHANGELOG.md indicating manual release with the date, release lead initials, and a one-liner reason (e.g. iad-ci degraded)
    - Open a follow-up bead to restore Argo-driven release on the next milestone
  - Failure modes during manual release:
    - One triple build fails -- can the release proceed with a partial triple set? (No: all five MUST ship -- the SDK matrix depends on it)
    - PyPI upload fails midway -- recovery procedure (test.pypi.org as a smoke; force overwrite is NOT permitted)
    - SLSA attestation fails -- can the release ship without it? (No: SLSA L2 attestation is a Tier 1 deliverable per supply-chain table)

## Critical considerations

- Manual release is by definition lower-trust than Argo-driven release because the build environment is not the canonical CI environment -- the runbook MUST document this caveat in the CHANGELOG record line
- OpenBao secrets MUST be fetched via the same ESO-style read access that Argo uses; do NOT copy them to disk on the developer machine
- The runbook is also a continuity plan: if the release lead is unavailable, someone else MUST be able to execute these steps -- write it for a stranger
- Cross-compilation for macOS without an Apple Developer cert produces unsigned binaries -- the manual release is the WORST time to also be missing signing; document that as a known degraded outcome
- Idempotency: each step MUST be safe to re-run after a transient failure (e.g. PyPI upload retry); document the safe-retry rule per step

## Acceptance criteria

- docs/operations/manual-release.md exists with the three sections above
- Step-by-step procedure complete (all 13 steps)
- Manual release CHANGELOG record template present
- Failure modes documented for the three most likely partial failures
- Runbook is verbatim-executable by a non-author release lead

## References

- Plan: line 549 (R13 risk register), line 567 (PB-13 fallback procedure), line 895 (SLSA L2 attestation tier), Supply Chain Considerations table
issue.title: Runbook: docs/operations/manual-release.md (PB-13 fallback when Argo unavailable)

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the exit code policy for pdftract doctor:

- Exit 0: all checks are OK or WARN (no FAIL); N/A doesn't affect exit
- Exit 1: at least one check is FAIL (regardless of --exit-on-fail per default policy per plan section 6.10 line 2528)
- Exit 2: CLI parse error (clap default)

The --exit-on-fail flag is accepted but does NOT change behavior — the default policy already exits 1 on any FAIL. The flag is retained for explicit CI-script readability (\"yes, I want exit-on-fail\") and forward-compatibility (a future --warn-as-fail or --no-exit-on-fail would invert).

Module touches: crates/pdftract-cli/src/doctor/mod.rs (the orchestrator that runs checks and computes exit).

## Why this matters

Exit codes are the contract between doctor and the CI / orchestration layer. Inconsistent exit codes (e.g. 0 on FAIL because the policy required a flag) make doctor useless as a deployment gate. The default-policy choice (\"exit 1 on any FAIL even without --exit-on-fail\") is per the plan's explicit decision: doctor is meant to be the gate, and operators shouldn't need to know an arcane flag to make it work as a gate.

## Implementation guidance

- After running all checks (sibling 6.10.1) and producing output (sibling 6.10.2), compute:
  ```rust
  let fail_count = results.iter().filter(|r| r.status == CheckStatus::Fail).count();
  let exit_code = if fail_count > 0 { 1 } else { 0 };
  std::process::exit(exit_code);
  ```
- --exit-on-fail flag: parsed by clap; accepted but unused (documented as \"explicit form of the default policy; reserved for future inversion flags\")
- N/A status does NOT affect exit code
- WARN status does NOT affect exit code (calibrated: WARN = \"watch this but don't block deployment\")
- Document the policy in --help output: \"Exit code 0 if no checks FAIL; exit 1 if any check FAILs. WARN does not affect exit code.\"
- Edge case: zero checks run (impossible normally but defensive) → exit 0

## Critical considerations

- Plan section 6.10 line 2520-2521: \"0: all checks pass (no FAIL); 1: at least one FAIL and --exit-on-fail set, OR any FAIL regardless of --exit-on-fail per default policy\"
- The second clause supersedes the first: default policy is exit 1 on any FAIL. The flag is a no-op behaviorally but kept for explicitness
- Don't conflate WARN with FAIL: WARN's exit-policy-irrelevance is the calibrated decision; operators who want WARN-fails-too should compose with shell scripting (e.g. pdftract doctor --json | jq -e '.summary.warn == 0')
- Process exit must happen via std::process::exit (not via Err propagation through main) because clap's exit-on-help/error code must also be 2 for parse errors

## Acceptance criteria

- pdftract doctor on a system with all OK + some WARN → exit 0
- pdftract doctor on a system with at least one FAIL → exit 1
- pdftract doctor --exit-on-fail on a system with at least one FAIL → exit 1 (same as default)
- pdftract doctor --exit-on-fail on a system with only OK/WARN → exit 0 (same as default)
- pdftract doctor --bogus-flag → exit 2 (clap parse error)
- pdftract doctor --help → exit 0 (clap help)
- Plan critical test passes: \"--exit-on-fail flag: exits 1 on any FAIL across all rows; exits 0 if only WARNs are present\"

## References

- Plan section: Phase 6.10 pdftract doctor (lines 2491, 2520-2521, 2528, 2531)
- Sibling 6.10.1 (CheckResult provides status)
- Sibling 6.10.2 (output happens before exit)
- Sibling 6.10.4 (runbook documents the exit code contract)
Labels: cli, doctor, exit-codes, phase-6
issue.title: 6.10.3: Exit code policy (0 = all OK/WARN; 1 = any FAIL) + --exit-on-fail flag

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the page_type_string(class: PageClass, ocr_succeeded: bool, has_text: bool, has_images: bool) -> &'static str helper that emits the canonical page_type string for the 6.1 JSON schema. The mapping must be exact and stable across releases (INV-9).

## Why this matters

The page_type field in the per-page JSON output is the schema's stable categorical signal that downstream consumers (Phase 6.5 Markdown, Phase 7 advanced features, classifiers) match on. Wrong strings break consumers silently; missing strings cause schema validation failures. Locking the mapping in code (with exhaustive case coverage) is the only way to keep this honest as the 5.1 classifier evolves.

## Implementation guidance

- Function signature:
  ```rust
  pub fn page_type_string(class: PageClass, ocr_succeeded: bool, has_text: bool, has_images: bool) -> &'static str
  ```
- Mapping table:
  ```
  | class           | ocr_succeeded | has_text | has_images | page_type        |
  |-----------------|---------------|----------|------------|------------------|
  | Vector          | -             | -        | -          | \"text\"           |
  | Scanned         | -             | -        | -          | \"scanned\"        |
  | Hybrid          | -             | -        | -          | \"mixed\"          |
  | BrokenVector    | false         | -        | -          | \"broken_vector\"  |
  | BrokenVector    | true          | -        | -          | \"scanned\"        |  // post-OCR recovery
  | (any)           | -             | false    | false      | \"blank\"          |  // overrides class
  | (any)           | -             | false    | true       | \"figure_only\"    |  // overrides class
  ```
- Implementation uses match with explicit handling for each case
- has_text/has_images override the class-based mapping ONLY when both indicate non-text-only content (blank or figure_only); otherwise the class-based mapping wins

## Critical considerations

- INV-9 stable taxonomy: page_type strings are FROZEN by the 6.1 schema version. Any change requires a schema_version bump and a downstream migration plan.
- The override rule (blank/figure_only takes precedence over class) is the subtle bit; document with a precedence comment in the code
- Default rename_all = lowercase serde derive does NOT cover this mapping because of the Hybrid→\"mixed\" rename and the BrokenVector split across two strings (depending on ocr_succeeded). Use a hand-written match expression, not serde rename annotations
- broken_vector MUST be exported in the page_type enum string set (6.1 schema validator checks the enum is consistent with this function)
- Add a unit test covering every (class, ocr_succeeded, has_text, has_images) combination — small enough to be exhaustive (4 × 2 × 2 × 2 = 32 cases)

## Acceptance criteria

- Unit test: each combination from the mapping table produces the documented string
- Unit test: Vector + has_text=false + has_images=false → \"blank\" (override applies)
- Unit test: Hybrid + has_text=false + has_images=true → \"figure_only\" (override)
- Unit test: BrokenVector + ocr_succeeded=true → \"scanned\" (post-OCR recovery)
- Schema validator (Phase 6.1.3) checks the page_type enum in the JSON schema matches the strings produced by this function (lint cross-check)
- Module docstring cites INV-9 frozen-set

## References

- Plan section: Phase 5.1.1 (mapping table)
- INV-9 stable taxonomy
- Phase 6.1 JSON schema (consumes these strings)
- Coordinator: pdftract-1ob (parent)
- Sibling: PageClass enum
Labels: classifier, mapping, phase-5, schema

All 6 acceptance criteria PASS: DeviceGray (0.5 g), DeviceRGB (0.5 0.5 0.5 rg), DeviceCMYK (0.1 0.2 0.3 0.4 k), cs+scn (/DeviceRGB cs 1 0 0 scn), Spot color (/Cs1 cs 0.5 /PANTONE scn), Pattern fall-through (no panic). 24 tests added. issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the 6 color-setting operators that touch fill/stroke color state for text. Pairs operate on the same Color but for fill vs stroke (lowercase = fill, uppercase = stroke): `rg/RG` (DeviceRGB), `k/K` (DeviceCMYK), `g/G` (DeviceGray), plus the general `cs/CS` (set color space) + `sc/SC` (set color in current space) + `scn/SCN` (extended set color, includes pattern/spot args). Result: every glyph emitted thereafter carries the correct Color in its `fill_color` field for downstream span-merge and CSS hex conversion.

## Why this matters

Color is one of the span-break triggers in Phase 4.1; if color tracking is wrong, spans collapse incorrectly across color changes (e.g., a highlighted quote merges into the surrounding paragraph). The Spot color path is critical for invoices and forms that use Pantone-style branded colors.

## Implementation guidance

- `g v`: fill = DeviceGray(v). `G v`: stroke = DeviceGray(v).
- `rg r g b`: fill = DeviceRGB([r,g,b]). `RG r g b`: stroke.
- `k c m y k`: fill = DeviceCMYK([c,m,y,k]). `K c m y k`: stroke.
- `cs /Name`: set color space; track current `fill_color_space: ColorSpaceRef` for sc/scn to consume. Common names: DeviceGray, DeviceRGB, DeviceCMYK, /Pattern, /CalRGB, /ICCBased, /Indexed.
- `sc n1 n2 ...`: set color in current space (numeric args). Number of args depends on current cs.
- `scn n1 ... [/PatternName]`: same as sc plus optional final pattern/spot name. For Spot color spaces, the last name is the colorant name and prior args are tint values.
- For colorspaces other than the 3 Device variants (CalRGB, ICCBased, Pattern, Indexed): set Color::Other for now; record colorspace name for diagnostics.

## Critical considerations

- Pattern colorspace: typically NOT relevant for text but can be set. Always falls into Color::Other.
- INV: fill_color and stroke_color are tracked SEPARATELY. Text usually uses fill_color (rendering modes 0, 2, 4, 6); stroke is used in modes 1, 5 (and 4 for both). Phase 4.1 span merge uses fill_color.
- The cs/CS state is part of the graphics state and saved/restored by q/Q.
- Some PDFs use sc/scn with a name argument that is actually a colorant name in a Spot colorspace: extract as `Color::Spot(name, tint)`.
- DeviceN colorspace (multi-colorant): collapse to Color::Other for v0.1.0.

## Acceptance criteria

- `0.5 0.5 0.5 rg` sets fill_color = DeviceRGB([0.5,0.5,0.5]).
- `0.5 g` sets fill_color = DeviceGray(0.5).
- `0.1 0.2 0.3 0.4 k` sets fill_color = DeviceCMYK([0.1,0.2,0.3,0.4]).
- `/DeviceRGB cs 1 0 0 scn` sets fill_color = DeviceRGB([1,0,0]).
- `/Cs1 cs 0.5 /PANTONE scn` (Spot) sets fill_color = Color::Spot("PANTONE", 0.5).
- Pattern colorspace fall-through emits no panic; fill_color = Color::Other.

## References

- Plan section: Phase 3.1 critical test for color operators (line 1506)
- ISO 32000-1 sections 8.6.6, 8.6.8

- combined_failures.pdf is highest-priority; without it, regressions breaking inter-layer error handling go undetected
