Refactored execute_with_do to use gstate.text_matrix. All acceptance criteria PASS. See commit 172cdad and notes/pdftract-4x0y.md for details.
issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the operators that bind a font (`Tf name size`) and re-position text on the page (`Td tx ty`, `TD tx ty`, `Tm a b c d e f`, `T*`). These are the heart of text state — every following Tj/TJ glyph depends on text_matrix and text_line_matrix produced by these. Resolve Tf's name argument against the current page's resource dictionary `/Font` subdictionary via the ResourceStack (Phase 3.3).

## Why this matters

A Tf bug means every glyph after it uses the wrong font (and therefore the wrong glyph metrics, the wrong encoding chain, and ultimately the wrong Unicode). Td/TD/Tm bugs misposition every glyph — column detection fails, baseline clustering fails, reading order fails.

## Implementation guidance

- `Tf name size`: look up the Name in current ResourceStack's font subdict, fetch the resolved `Arc<Font>` (Phase 2 already loaded it), set GraphicsState.font and font_size. Reset the 20-glyph word-boundary recalibration window (Phase 3.2 invariant — Tf RESETS recalibration).
- `Td tx ty`: `text_line_matrix = translate(tx, ty) * text_line_matrix`, then `text_matrix = text_line_matrix.clone()` (per ISO 32000-1 Table 108).
- `TD tx ty`: same as Td PLUS set `leading = -ty`. Often the first operator on a new line; sets up T* for subsequent lines.
- `Tm a b c d e f`: set BOTH `text_matrix` and `text_line_matrix` directly to `[[a,b,0],[c,d,0],[e,f,1]]`. Does NOT reset font or rendering mode.
- `T*`: equivalent to `0 -leading Td`. If leading == 0, T* is a no-op for x but lowers y by 0 — effectively useless; emit `TSTAR_ZERO_LEADING` diagnostic.

## Critical considerations

- INV: `Tm` does NOT accumulate — it OVERWRITES both matrices. A `Tm` after `Td` discards the Td translation.
- INV: After a `Tm`, subsequent `Td` is relative to the NEW text_line_matrix, not to the pre-Tm position (per critical test line 1504).
- Translation order matters: `translate(tx, ty) * text_line_matrix` means tx,ty are in TEXT space (post-existing-matrix); verify against ISO 32000-1 formula and add a regression test.
- Tf with unknown resource name: emit `FONT_RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` diagnostic; set font to None (subsequent text-show ops emit no glyphs); do not abort.
- Tf with font_size <= 0: clamp to 1.0 with diagnostic — zero-size text is undefined behavior in spec but seen in wild.

## Acceptance criteria

- `BT 100 200 Td 50 0 Td ET` ends with text_matrix translation == (150, 200).
- `BT 100 200 Tm 50 0 Td ET` ends with text_matrix translation == (50, 0) relative to Tm origin, NOT (150, 200).
- `TD 0 -12` sets leading to 12 and translates by (0, -12).
- `T*` after `TD 0 -12 ET BT` translates by (0, -12) using saved leading.
- Tf with unknown name does not crash; emits diagnostic.

## References

- Plan section: Phase 3.1 Text state operators (lines 1490-1493)
- Critical tests: Td chain, Tm followed by Td (lines 1503-1504)
issue.title: Font binding (Tf) + text positioning operators (Td TD Tm T*)

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement HTTP-Range-Reads-backed PdfSource:

```rust
pub struct HttpRangeSource {
    client: ureq::Agent,
    url: String,
    headers: Vec<(String, String)>,
    content_length: u64,
    cache: Mutex<LruCache<u64 /* block_index */, Bytes /* 64 KB block */>>,
}
```

Cache: 64 blocks × 64 KB = 4 MB total per document.

## Implementation guidance

- ureq = "0.10" with rustls feature (per ADR-001). No async runtime
- lru = "0.12" for cache
- Block size 64 KB (65,536 bytes). Block index = offset / 65536
- For read_range spanning multiple blocks:
  - Check cache for each block
  - For misses, batch contiguous blocks into single Range request
  - Insert each fetched block into cache
- Single shared Agent for connection pooling
- Headers passed on every request
- Timeouts: connection 10s, read 30s; on timeout emit REMOTE_FETCH_INTERRUPTED

## Critical considerations

- 64 × 64 KB = 4 MB per document; 10 concurrent = 40 MB total memory
- LRU eviction per-document; no cross-document cache reuse
- Range request: `Range: bytes=START-END` (inclusive)
- Response: 206 Partial Content with `Content-Range: bytes START-END/TOTAL`
- If server returns 200 OK (not 206), it ignored the Range header; emit REMOTE_NO_RANGE_SUPPORT, trigger fallback (separate bead); DO NOT cache the 200 response
- Mutex<LruCache> serializes cache access; for read-heavy, consider parking_lot or DashMap later
- Authentication: URL-embedded basic auto-handled by ureq; custom Bearer / API key via --header
- TLS: rustls backend (per ADR-001); certificate validation on by default
- INV-8: network errors return Err but orchestrator catches, emits REMOTE_FETCH_INTERRUPTED; no panic

## Acceptance criteria

- HttpRangeSource::open performs HEAD, records content-length + Accept-Ranges
- read_range(50_000, 200_000) makes right number of Range requests
- Cache hit ratio >= 80% on typical workloads
- Critical test: extract page 5 of 100-page mock PDF; < 100 KB transferred
- Connection drop test: partial bytes + REMOTE_FETCH_INTERRUPTED
- TLS handshake failure: clear stderr message; exit 6 (in CLI integration)
- proptest: random read_range sequences never panic
- INV-8 maintained

## References

- Plan section: Phase 1.8 lines 1239-1248
- ADR-001 (ureq selection)
- Dependency Matrix: ureq (remote feature only)
- INV-8
issue.title: Implement HttpRangeSource with 4 MB LRU page-cache (64 × 64 KB blocks)

issue.description:
## Scope

Add the grep subcommand to the pdftract CLI via clap. Implement all flags from the plan options table: -r/--recursive, -i/--ignore-case, -E/--extended-regexp, -F/--fixed-strings, -w/--word-regexp, -v/--invert-match, -l/--files-with-matches, -c/--count, -j/--threads, --ocr, --json, --highlight DIR, --max-results, --progress, --no-progress, --progress-json, --quiet. PATTERN is positional; PATH... is variadic positional defaulting to ".".

## Why this matters

Flag compatibility with ripgrep is a deliberate choice - users already know ripgrep semantics, the muscle memory transfers, the learning curve disappears. Misalignments here (e.g. -F as opt-in instead of default) would surprise users. The clap structure is the foundation; every other 7.8.x bead consumes the parsed Args struct.

## Implementation guidance

- clap derive macro; struct GrepArgs { recursive: bool, ignore_case: bool, extended_regexp: bool, fixed_strings: bool, word_regexp: bool, invert_match: bool, files_with_matches: bool, count: bool, threads: Option<usize>, ocr: bool, json: bool, highlight: Option<PathBuf>, max_results: Option<usize>, progress: ProgressMode (enum Auto/On/Off), progress_json: bool, quiet: bool, pattern: String, paths: Vec<PathBuf> }
- Default -F (fixed-strings = true); -E flips to regex mode
- -i: case-insensitive (applies to both literal and regex)
- -w: word-boundary check (\b<pattern>\b for regex; pre/post char-class check for literal)
- -v: invert matches (print spans WITHOUT a match)
- -l: only print filenames (count == "any match")
- -c: print count per file (count of matched spans, not match instances)
- -j N: thread count (default num_cpus::get())
- --highlight DIR: validate DIR exists OR can be created (mkdir -p)
- --progress: enum Auto | On | Off (--progress = On, --no-progress = Off, default = Auto = On if TTY else Off)
- --progress-json: implies --progress = Off (the two are alternatives)
- --quiet: suppresses all stdout + progress bar; sets exit code 0 if any match, 1 if no match
- Path defaults: if empty, push ".", implicit -r
- Feature gating: when grep feature is OFF, subcommand still registered but execute prints "feature 'grep' not compiled in" and exits

## Critical considerations

- ripgrep compat: -r default ON when path is dir, OFF when path is single file (preserve ripgrep behavior)
- Default match mode: literal/-F (per plan) - users opting into regex pass -E
- --highlight + --quiet: --quiet still allows --highlight (annotation output independent of stdout)
- --json + --quiet: --quiet wins (no stdout); --json + --progress-json: both valid (stdout JSON-Lines + stderr progress JSON-Lines)
- --max-results: hard cap; sink stops printing AND workers told to stop; clean termination

## Acceptance criteria

- clap parses all flags from the plan table
- Default behavior matches ripgrep (literal by default, -i off, -r implicit on dirs)
- Unit tests: every flag combination from the plan's Critical tests section
- Feature-off path: prints meaningful error
- Path expansion: . recurses by default; single-file PATH does not recurse

## References

- Plan section: 7.8 Options table (lines 2710-2731)
- ripgrep flag semantics (target compatibility)
- clap-derive crate
- 7.8.2 (regex engine consumer)
- 7.8.4 (per-file pipeline consumer)

All 40 hybrid tests PASS. Commit: e96a791. Verification note: notes/pdftract-4y9l.md. issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the Hybrid page handling pipeline: consume PageClassification::hybrid_cells (set of (row,col) tuples from 5.1.3), render only those cells (not the whole page), run OCR per cell, and merge OCR span output with Phase 3 vector spans using the bbox-overlap rule (vector wins where IoU > 0.5).

## Why this matters

Without per-cell routing, Hybrid pages either run OCR over the entire page (waste; overlays the text region with garbage OCR) or skip OCR entirely (miss the scanned region). The bbox merge rule is the precise contract between Phase 3 vector text and Phase 5 OCR text; both can output spans for overlapping regions and the merger must pick correctly.

## Implementation guidance

- Cell rendering: render the full page once at the selected DPI, then crop per cell from the rendered raster (cheaper than re-rendering per cell)
- Cell crop coordinates: cell_w = page_w_px / 8, cell_h = page_h_px / 8; row r, col c -> crop [c*cell_w, r*cell_h, (c+1)*cell_w, (r+1)*cell_h]
- For each cell: run preprocessing (5.3) + Tesseract (5.4) -> Vec<OcrSpan>
- Merge step (separate fn merge_vector_and_ocr_spans(vector: &[Span], ocr: &[Span]) -> Vec<Span>):
  1. For each ocr span O: find any vector span V with IoU(O.bbox, V.bbox) > 0.5
  2. If found: drop O (keep V; vector wins)
  3. If not found: keep O
  4. Return all V + retained O sorted by reading order
- IoU formula: area(A ∩ B) / area(A ∪ B); bboxes are AABB so intersection is a simple rect

## Critical considerations

- Hybrid cells use grid coords from 5.1.3 (BTreeSet for deterministic iteration); preserve order
- IoU > 0.5 is "vector wins" — but if the vector span has lower confidence than 0.5, prefer OCR (avoid promoting bad vector text); refer to 4.7 readability score
- Reading order after merge is recomputed by Phase 4.5 — this task only produces the merged Vec<Span>, not the final ordering
- Cells at page edges may have partial coverage; pad with white if the crop extends beyond the rendered page

## Acceptance criteria

- Hybrid fixture (text header + scanned body): OCR runs only on bottom 6 rows, not on entire page (verified by tracing OCR call count)
- Merge unit tests: IoU 0.6 -> vector kept; IoU 0.3 -> both kept; IoU 0.6 but vector_confidence 0.2 -> OCR kept
- End-to-end Hybrid extraction produces a span list with no duplicate text from overlapping vector + OCR regions
- Performance: Hybrid page processing time < Scanned full-page processing time by at least 30% on the standard fixture

## References

- Plan section: Phase 5.2 Hybrid page handling (line 1863)
- Phase 5.1.3 hybrid_cells output
- Phase 4.5 reading order
- INV-7 confidence_source on every Span
issue.title: 5.2.4: Hybrid page routing (render only image-heavy cells) + vector+OCR bbox merge rule

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement `ObjectParser::parse_indirect_object()` which reads the four-token preamble (`Integer Integer Obj`), parses one direct object, expects `Token::EndObj`, and returns `PdfIndirect { id: ObjRef, obj: PdfObject }`.

## Implementation guidance

- Read 3 tokens: expect `Integer(N)`, `Integer(G)`, `Token::Obj`. If mismatch, emit `STRUCT_INVALID_INDIRECT_HEADER` and try to recover by scanning forward to the next `obj` keyword
- Construct `ObjRef { object: N as u32, generation: G as u16 }`
- Call `parse_direct_object()` for the body
- Expect `Token::EndObj`. If missing, emit `STRUCT_MISSING_KEY` (missing endobj) and recover by scanning forward to the next `endobj`, `obj`, or EOF
- Return `PdfIndirect { id, obj }`

## Critical considerations

- N (object number) > u32::MAX is invalid per spec; clamp to u32::MAX with `STRUCT_INTEGER_OVERFLOW`
- G (generation) > u16::MAX is invalid per spec; clamp to u16::MAX
- The body can be ANY direct object including a Stream — the stream body skip happens inside parse_direct_object(), so endobj appears AFTER endstream
- The Pratt-like recovery on missing endobj is important for EC-07 (corrupt xref where one indirect object is malformed but neighbors are fine)
- Multi-object skip recovery: if scanning for endobj finds `obj` first (i.e. the next indirect object's header), the current indirect object is malformed — abort with PdfNull body and let the caller (xref resolver) continue with the next object
- The lexer's position counter (used by xref) MUST be valid when this function returns — both success and recovery paths must leave position at the byte just past `endobj`

## Acceptance criteria

- Simple test: `1 0 obj null endobj` -> PdfIndirect{ id: ObjRef{1, 0}, obj: PdfObject::Null }
- Stream test: `12 0 obj << /Length 5 >> stream\n12345endstream endobj` -> PdfIndirect with PdfObject::Stream
- Recovery test: `1 0 obj null` (no endobj before next `obj`) -> emit STRUCT_MISSING_KEY, position advances to start of next indirect-object header
- Recovery test: `999999999999 0 obj null endobj` -> ObjRef{u32::MAX, 0} + STRUCT_INTEGER_OVERFLOW
- proptest property: random byte sequences fed to parse_indirect_object never panic

## References

- Plan section: Phase 1.2 line 1071 (indirect object parsing)
- Phase 1.6 (error recovery for missing endobj)
- INV-8

issue.close_reason: Implemented OCR receipt fallback for SVG receipts. Created ocr_fallback.rs module with 150 DPI PNG raster rendering via pdfium-render, integrated with SVG generator via GlyphSource enum, added data-source="ocr" attribute. All 54 receipts tests pass. Verification note at notes/pdftract-4yspv.md. Commit d48c685.
issue.description:
## Scope

When SVG-mode receipt generation encounters glyphs without font outlines available (OCR-sourced glyphs from Phase 5.4, or PDF Type 3 PostScript glyphs not decodable by ttf-parser), fall back to embedding a 150-DPI PNG raster of the bbox region as a base64-encoded <image> element inside the SVG. The SVG root element carries data-source=\"ocr\" so consumers can distinguish vector vs. raster receipts.

Module: crates/pdftract-core/src/receipts/ocr_fallback.rs.

## Why this matters

Without this fallback, SVG-mode receipts on scanned PDFs (the primary OCR use case) would be empty or broken — the most-needed receipts (for OCR-extracted text that an auditor most wants to verify visually) would be the ones that fail. The PNG fallback preserves the round-trip verifier protocol: content_hash is computed from the resolved Unicode regardless of whether glyphs were vector or raster, so the verifier (sibling 6.8.4) works identically on either receipt type.

150 DPI is the sweet spot between file size (lower DPI degrades readability of small text) and audit clarity (higher DPI bloats the SVG inline payload). At 150 DPI, a typical 12pt-text bbox of 200×30 PDF points becomes a 416×62-pixel PNG — about 5-15 KB base64-encoded.

## Implementation guidance

- Trigger condition: any glyph in the receipt's bbox whose Phase 3 GlyphList.source == GlyphSource::OCR OR whose font outline lookup via ttf-parser returns None
- When triggered, the SVG generator (sibling 6.8.2) does NOT emit <path> elements; instead emits:
  ```xml
  <svg viewBox=\"0 0 W H\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/2000/svg\" data-source=\"ocr\">
    <image href=\"data:image/png;base64,...\" x=\"0\" y=\"0\" width=\"W\" height=\"H\"/>
  </svg>
  ```
- Raster source: re-render the bbox region from the source PDF at 150 DPI via pdfium-render (Phase 5.4 dependency, gated behind the full-render feature flag)
- If pdfium-render is not available at build time (default features), fall back to lite-mode receipt for this span (svg_clip remains None) with a stderr WARN: \"SVG receipt for OCR span requires full-render feature; emitting lite-mode receipt instead\"
- PNG encoding via the image crate (already a transitive Phase 5.4 dep); compression level 6 (default); no metadata chunks
- base64 encoding via the base64 crate (already in deps from Phase 6.4 multipart parsing); URL-safe variant NOT required (data: URLs accept standard base64)
- Cropping: the rendered page is at 150 DPI; the bbox coordinates (PDF points) are converted via the same coordinate-transform used in sibling 6.8.2 (origin at top-left of bbox, y-flipped)

## Critical considerations

- The data-source=\"ocr\" attribute on the SVG root is a custom XML attribute; it does not affect rendering but lets downstream consumers (audit dashboards, verifier diagnostics) distinguish vector vs. raster receipts
- content_hash is computed from the resolved Unicode text, NOT from the raster — so a Tesseract miscall in the OCR layer produces a wrong content_hash (the verifier detects this on re-extraction; correctly flagged as code 12)
- Mixed-source spans (some glyphs have outlines, some are OCR-sourced) fall entirely into the OCR-raster path: emit a single PNG covering the whole bbox; do NOT mix <path> and <image> elements (avoids alignment bugs)
- 150 DPI is the default; expose it as a constant (SVG_OCR_RASTER_DPI = 150.0) for future tuning but do not surface as a CLI flag in this bead (deferred)
- pdfium-render rendering is expensive; cache per-page rasters within a single extraction (multiple spans on the same page share the rendered raster, cropped per-bbox)
- The PNG raster preserves the original glyph appearance, so an auditor can read the actual scanned text — useful even when the OCR layer guessed wrong (the receipt's bbox still points at the right region)
- Feature-gating: this module is compiled only when both receipts AND full-render features are enabled; cfg(all(feature = \"receipts\", feature = \"full-render\")) on the module declaration

## Acceptance criteria

- Given a span with Phase 3 GlyphList containing GlyphSource::OCR entries, SVG mode emits an <image> element with base64-encoded PNG and data-source=\"ocr\" on root
- Generated PNG when decoded shows the bbox region of the source PDF at ~150 DPI
- aggregate JSON size for 100 OCR receipts on a scanned 100-page document: <= 1.5 MB
- When full-render feature is NOT compiled, OCR spans degrade to lite-mode receipts with a stderr WARN
- Same-page receipts share the rendered raster (verified by counting pdfium-render calls in a test fixture)
- Mixed-source spans (vector + OCR glyphs in same bbox) → entirely OCR-raster path (asserted in test)
- Plan critical test passes: \"OCR-sourced receipt: SVG contains base64 PNG; data-source=\\\"ocr\\\" attribute present\"

## References

- Plan section: Phase 6.8 Visual Citation Receipts (lines 2399, 2416)
- Phase 3 GlyphList + GlyphSource enum
- Phase 5.4 OCR pipeline (source of OCR glyphs)
- pdfium-render crate (full-render feature, page rasterization)
- image crate (PNG encoder)
- base64 crate (base64 encoding)
- Sibling 6.8.2 (SVG generator that delegates to this module)
- Sibling 6.8.4 (verifier protocol — content_hash is text-derived, raster doesn't affect verification)
Labels: ocr, phase-6, receipts, svg

issue.description:
## Scope

Build the axum router that serves: (a) /  -> bundled HTML page (7.9.3), (b) /static/<asset> -> bundled CSS/JS (7.9.3), (c) /api/document -> document-level JSON metadata, (d) /api/page/<i> -> per-page JSON, (e) /api/page/<i>/svg -> SVG render of page i (7.9.4), (f) /api/page/<i>/thumbnail -> small SVG for sidebar, (g) /api/raster/<i>.png -> base64 PNG for scanned pages, (h) /api/search?q=... -> matching span list. Bearer-token auth on every endpoint when --auth-token set; loopback bind = auth optional.

## Wsy this matters

The HTTP API is the contract between frontend and backend. Stable URL shapes let the frontend (7.9.3) and the API server evolve independently. Server-side SVG rendering puts the heavy work on the backend (where Rust is fast) and keeps the frontend bundle small.

## Implementation guidance

- Crates: axum (already in serve feature), tokio
- Router (Router::new()):
  - .route("/", get(serve_index))
  - .route("/static/<asset>", get(serve_static))
  - .route("/api/document", get(api_document))
  - .route("/api/page/{i}", get(api_page))

issue.description:
## Scope

For each Link annotation routed by 7.6.1, extract the link target. If /A /S is /URI, read /A /URI as the external URL. If /Dest is a Name, resolve via /Catalog /Names /Dests name tree (else emit the raw Name as the dest string). If /Dest is an Array (explicit destination), record the page reference and fit type/coordinates. Emit Link { uri: Option<String>, dest: Option<String>, dest_array: Option<DestArray>, page_index: usize, rect: [f32;4] } onto the document-level links array.

## Why this matters

URI links cover ~80% of useful hyperlink data (DOIs, references, web URLs). Named destinations are how legal/regulatory cross-references work ("see Section 2.3"). Explicit destinations carry the precise viewing parameters (which page + which coordinates the link jumps to) used by tools that need to follow internal links programmatically.

## Implementation guidance

- Inputs: per-page Vec<LinkAnnotation> from 7.6.1; document /Catalog /Names /Dests + /Catalog /Dests for resolution
- /A (action dict): if present and /S is the Name "URI", read /A /URI as PdfString -> String; assign uri
- /Dest variants:
  - Name -> attempt resolution via /Catalog /Dests dict first, then /Catalog /Names /Dests name tree; if resolved to explicit destination array, parse as below; if unresolved, dest: Some(name_as_string), dest_array: None
  - String (PdfString) -> treat as named destination, resolve same way
  - Array (explicit destination) -> [page_ref, fit_name, ...args]; parse to DestArray { page_index, fit: FitType, coords: Vec<f32> }
- FitType enum: XYZ { x, y, zoom } | Fit | FitH { top } | FitV { left } | FitR { left, bottom, right, top } | FitB | FitBH { top } | FitBV { left }
- If both /A /S /URI and /Dest present, prefer /A /S /URI (uri); document precedence
- page_index: from the source page (passed in from 7.6.1)
- rect: from the link annotation's /Rect

## Critical considerations

- URI string may contain percent-encoded UTF-8; do NOT percent-decode (keep as-is for URL parsers downstream)
- /Dest name resolution may chain: dest name -> array containing another name (rare); resolve once, do not recurse to avoid loops
- /Catalog /Names /Dests is a name tree; reuse the 7.5.1 name-tree walker
- /Catalog /Dests is a flat dict (PDF 1.2 legacy) - prefer when present, fall back to /Names /Dests for PDF 1.3+
- Some PDFs use /JavaScript actions; we DO NOT execute them - if /A /S /JavaScript, emit Link with uri: Some("javascript:<truncated>") + diagnostic
- Empty /A and empty /Dest -> emit Link with both None + diagnostic "link_without_target"

## Acceptance criteria

- Critical test (from plan): 5 URI hyperlinks - all appear in document links
- Critical test: Link with named destination /Dest /SectionTwo -> dest: "SectionTwo"
- Unit tests: explicit /Dest array (XYZ fit), /Dest as string-name, /JavaScript action diagnostic, missing target diagnostic
- Public Link { uri, dest, dest_array, page_index, rect } emitted per link
- /Dest resolution falls back gracefully when unresolved

## References

- Plan section: 7.6 lines 2660-2662 (Link extraction)
- PDF 1.7 spec 12.5.6.5 Link Annotations, 12.3.2 Destinations
- 7.5.1 name-tree walker (Dests resolution)

- 7.6.4 (output JSON consumer)

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement per-thread cycle detection in the Object Parser. A thread_local! RefCell<HashSet<ObjRef>> tracks object refs currently being resolved. The resolve(ref) -> Arc<PdfObject> API checks for cycles before recursing; on cycle, emits STRUCT_CIRCULAR_REF and returns Arc::new(PdfObject::Null).

Module: crates/pdftract-core/src/parser/object/cycle.rs.

## Why this matters

PDF objects can legitimately reference each other (e.g., outline trees with /Parent pointers); a circular reference would cause infinite recursion in a naive resolver. The per-thread tracking is the standard pattern for preventing recursion bombs while supporting concurrent per-page parsing in Phase 3.

## Implementation guidance

- thread_local! storage:
  ```rust
  thread_local! {
      static RESOLVING: RefCell<HashSet<ObjRef>> = RefCell::new(HashSet::with_capacity(64));
  }
  ```
- resolve(ref) algorithm:
  1. RESOLVING.with(|set| set.borrow_mut().insert(ref)) → check if already present
  2. If true (cycle detected): emit STRUCT_CIRCULAR_REF; return Arc::new(PdfObject::Null) (no cache write)
  3. If false (new resolution): fetch + parse the indirect object
  4. After completion: RESOLVING.with(|set| set.borrow_mut().remove(&ref))
  5. Insert into LRU cache (sibling bead)
  6. Return
- The Drop guard pattern: use a RAII guard that removes the ref from RESOLVING on Drop (handles panics gracefully — INV-8 caveat)
- HashSet capacity 64: typical PDF resolution depth is < 10; 64 is conservative

## Critical considerations

- thread_local! choice: PDF object resolution may happen in parallel across pages (Phase 3 rayon parallelism); each thread needs its own resolution stack
- Cycle detection MUST NOT cache the failed resolution (caching would persist the failure across resolution attempts; the next attempt should retry)
- STRUCT_CIRCULAR_REF diagnostic carries the cycle's ObjRef; downstream consumers can decode the cycle path
- The fallback PdfObject::Null lets callers continue parsing; downstream consumers handle Null appropriately (e.g., dict.get returns Null which serializes to nothing)
- INV-8 no-panic: even on cycle, no panic; the diagnostic + Null path is the recovery

## Acceptance criteria

- Linear chain A→B→C: resolves correctly (3 inserts + 3 removes)
- Cycle A→B→A: detected; STRUCT_CIRCULAR_REF emitted; Null returned
- Cross-thread: each thread has independent resolution stack (verify with thread::spawn test)
- Drop guard: panic mid-resolution doesn't leave stale entries in RESOLVING (test with panic_hook)
- INV-8: no panic on any input

## References

- Plan section: Phase 1.2 cycle detection
- Coordinator: pdftract-4ij2 (parent — cycle detection + LRU cache)
- Sibling: LRU object cache
Labels: parser, phase-1
issue.title: Per-thread cycle detection (thread_local HashSet<ObjRef>; STRUCT_CIRCULAR_REF diagnostic)

  - match: all: [any: [text_contains: ['Account Statement', 'Statement of Account', 'Opening Balance', 'Closing Balance', 'Beginning Balance', 'Ending Balance', 'Account Number'], heading_matches: '^(Account Statement|Statement Summary)'], structural.has_table: true, structural.page_count: {min: 1, max: 30}, has_currency_pattern: true]

issue.description:
## Scope

Coordinator for sub-phase 4.2: group spans into `Line` structs by baseline proximity. For each span compute baseline = `y0 + (bbox_height * 0.2)` (approximation; exact requires font descender metrics). Cluster spans with baselines within `0.5 * median_font_size` of each other. Within a line, sort spans by x0 ascending (LTR); detect RTL by majority bidi class R/AL of characters and re-sort by x1 descending. Set `direction = "ltr" | "rtl" | "mixed"` on the Line struct.

## Why this matters

Without correct line formation, every Phase 4 downstream step fails: column detection histograms become meaningless if spans are not grouped by horizontal row; block formation cannot tell paragraph boundaries from line breaks; reading order has no notion of "next line". The 0.5 * median_font_size threshold is the calibrated value that handles superscript/subscript (which should NOT form separate lines) without merging unrelated rows.

## Children

- Line struct definition + baseline computation
- Baseline clustering algorithm (within 0.5 * median_font_size)
- Within-line span sorting (LTR x0 asc; RTL x1 desc via unicode-bidi)
- RTL direction detection (majority bidi class on characters)

## Critical considerations

- INV: baseline approximation y0 + bbox_height * 0.2 is the plan formula; exact descender metrics deferred (font.descriptor.descent could improve this but adds complexity).
- median_font_size is computed PER PAGE from all spans; small spans (footnotes) cluster correctly even on heading pages because the median dominates.
- Superscript glyphs at baseline ~5% higher than text baseline: WITHIN the 0.5*median threshold, so they cluster with the main line.
- RTL detection requires unicode-bidi crate's character category lookup; majority threshold per plan is >50% of chars in line are R/AL.
- "mixed" direction (line has both LTR and RTL spans, e.g., Arabic with embedded English): keep ltr/rtl sort; mark direction="mixed" for downstream Phase 4.5 to handle.

## Acceptance criteria

- All 4 children closed.
- Two-column layout: columns NOT merged into one line (the column gap exceeds proximity threshold).
- Superscript span at higher y: clustered with baseline text (not separate line).
- Arabic text: bidi R characters detected, spans sorted right-to-left.
- Mixed Latin+Arabic line: detected as "mixed" direction, sort order is implementation-defined consistent with bidi.

## References

- Plan section: Phase 4.2 Line Formation (lines 1660-1675)

issue.description:
## Scope

The Object Parser consumes the Lexer's token stream and produces the in-memory PDF object model: a tree of typed PdfObject variants. It handles indirect-object wrappers (`N G obj ... endobj`), object streams (`/ObjStm`), and the per-thread cycle-detection stack that prevents `STRUCT_CIRCULAR_REF` from causing stack overflow during dereferencing.

Child beads:
- PdfObject enum + ObjRef type + IndexMap-backed PdfDict definition
- Indirect object parser (`N G obj ... endobj` wrapper)
- Object stream parser (`/ObjStm`): decompress + parse + cache embedded objects
- Cycle detection via per-thread resolution stack + STRUCT_CIRCULAR_REF emission
- Object cache (LRU 4096 entries via lru crate)
- Critical-test fixture corpus + proptest harness

## Why this matters

The Object Parser is the layer at which "bytes" become "structured PDF data". All subsequent phases (xref resolver, document model, content stream processor, font pipeline) work with `PdfObject` values, never raw bytes. Bugs at this layer have catastrophic blast radius — an `IndexMap` insertion-order bug, for instance, would silently change content stream order and corrupt every multi-stream page.

The cycle detection is INV-8-critical: a self-referencing object like `1 0 obj << /A 1 0 R >> endobj` would, naively, dereference into infinite recursion. The per-thread resolution stack catches this and emits STRUCT_CIRCULAR_REF.

## Critical considerations

- `PdfDict` MUST use `IndexMap<Arc<str>, PdfObject>` (NOT `HashMap`) to preserve insertion order — this matters for content-stream-order-sensitive operations downstream
- `PdfString` is `Vec<u8>` of raw bytes BEFORE any encoding interpretation — the encoding decision lives in Phase 1.4 (for outline titles) and Phase 2 (for font-decoded text)
- `PdfStream { dict: PdfDict, offset: u64 }` — the stream content bytes are NOT loaded eagerly; the offset is into the underlying PdfSource (mmap or HttpRangeSource); Phase 1.5 decodes on demand
- `PdfRef(u32, u16)` — 32-bit object number, 16-bit generation number. The xref resolver (Phase 1.3) maps PdfRef -> byte offset
- Object streams (`/ObjStm`): when a PdfObject is a stream with `/Type /ObjStm`, the parser must decompress the stream content ONCE, parse all N embedded objects, and cache them as `Arc<[u8]>` so subsequent dereferences of any embedded object don't re-decompress
- LRU object cache size: 4096 entries per the plan's "Critical considerations" section. Keyed by `ObjRef`, value is `Arc<PdfObject>`. Cache is global (per-document); the `lru` crate provides O(1) get/put
- Per-thread resolution stack: tracks `HashSet<ObjRef>` of currently-being-resolved refs; entering `resolve(ref)` pushes; exiting pops; if `ref` already in set, emit `STRUCT_CIRCULAR_REF` and return `PdfNull`
- Object stream `/Extends` field: an ObjStm can reference a previous ObjStm via `/Extends N G R`. The recursive resolution of these forms a stream-chain — apply cycle detection here too
- A stream's `/Length` may itself be an indirect reference (PdfRef). The parser dereferences `/Length` before delegating to the stream decoder; if the dereferenced /Length is missing or non-integer, emit `STRUCT_MISSING_KEY` and use the byte range from `stream\n` to `endstream` (fallback)

## Acceptance criteria

- All 6 child beads closed
- All Critical tests from plan Section 1.2 pass:
  - Nested dict: `<< /A << /B 1 >> >>` -> correct inner dict
  - Array of mixed types: `[1 true (str) /Name null]`
  - Object stream: decompress, parse all N objects, verify all ObjRefs resolve
  - Self-referencing object (circular): returns PdfNull with diagnostic, no stack overflow
- INV-8 maintained: no panics on any input
- Module under `crates/pdftract-core/src/parser/object/`
- Public API: `ObjectParser::new(lexer)`, `parse_indirect_object() -> Result<PdfIndirect>`, `resolve(ref: ObjRef) -> Arc<PdfObject>`

## References

- Plan section: Phase 1.2 Object Parser, lines 1053-1082
- EC-08 (Circular object references)
- INV-8 (no panic at public boundary)
- ADR-005 (LRU cache pattern)
- Dependency Matrix: indexmap, lru crates

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement Otsu global thresholding via the image crate's imageproc::contrast::otsu_level + threshold functions. Used for DigitalOrigin source (from 5.3.2 image-source dispatch); faster than Sauvola when illumination is globally consistent.

Module: crates/pdftract-core/src/ocr/preprocessing/otsu.rs.

## Why this matters

Otsu is the classic global-threshold algorithm: finds the threshold that maximizes inter-class variance between background and foreground. Optimal when illumination is consistent (digital-origin images, screenshots, born-digital PDFs). Faster than Sauvola because it's a single global threshold, not per-pixel.

## Implementation guidance

- Crate: image + imageproc (already in deps for Phase 5)
- Signature:
  ```rust
  pub fn otsu_binarize(image: &GrayImage) -> GrayImage
  ```
- Algorithm:
  ```rust
  use imageproc::contrast::{otsu_level, threshold};
  let level = otsu_level(image);
  threshold(image, level)
  ```
- Output: binary image (0 or 255)
- O(N) for histogram + O(256) for threshold search; very fast (~30 ms for 1080p)

## Critical considerations

- Otsu assumes a bimodal histogram (foreground + background); fails on tri-modal (e.g. document with watermark) — sticks the threshold between two of the three modes, may misclassify
- For digital-origin images (PDF rendered to raster), Otsu is fine; for scans, Sauvola (sibling) is better
- imageproc's otsu_level returns u8 (the threshold value); imageproc's threshold function binarizes
- No parameters to tune; the algorithm is parameter-free

## Acceptance criteria

- Otsu on a digital-origin (uniform-lit) page produces clean binary
- Output pixels are exactly 0 or 255
- Benchmark: 1080p binarized in < 50ms (faster than Sauvola)
- Fails gracefully on tri-modal histograms (no panic; output is still binary, just suboptimal)

## References

- Plan section: Phase 5.3.3
- Otsu paper: Otsu (1979) A threshold selection method
- image crate, imageproc crate
- Coordinator: pdftract-4lwe (parent)
- Sibling: Sauvola, median-filter denoise
Labels: binarization, phase-5, preprocessing

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement `build_x0_histogram(spans: &[Span], page_width: f32) -> Vec<u32>` that returns a Vec of u32 counts of length `ceil(page_width)`, indexed by x0 (rounded to nearest integer pt). Each span contributes 1 to the bucket at its x0. The histogram is the primary signal for column detection (gap finding sibling consumes this).

## Why this matters

The histogram makes column detection a 1D peak-finding problem rather than a 2D clustering problem. 1pt resolution is per-plan and gives good discrimination at standard PDF page widths (612pt letter, 595pt A4).

## Implementation guidance

- Allocate Vec<u32> of size `page_width.ceil() as usize`; initialized to 0.
- For each span: `idx = span.bbox[0].round() as usize`; clamp to [0, hist.len()-1]; `hist[idx] += 1`.
- Edge case: x0 < 0 or x0 > page_width — clamp with diagnostic.

## Critical considerations

- 1pt resolution: for an 8.5x11 page (612pt wide), 612 buckets — trivial memory.
- Only x0 (LEFT edge) is histogrammed; x1 is irrelevant for column LEFT-edge alignment detection.
- Each span contributes EXACTLY ONE bucket; long spans don't fill multiple buckets.

## Acceptance criteria

- 1 span at x0=100, page_width=612: hist[100] == 1.
- 5 spans at x0=100,100,200,200,300: hist[100]==2, hist[200]==2, hist[300]==1.
- Span at x0=-5: clamped to hist[0], diagnostic.
- Empty spans: returns Vec of zeros.

## References

- Plan section: Phase 4.3 Algorithm (line 1681)
issue.title: x0 histogram builder (1pt resolution over page width)

issue.description: ## Scope Implement inline span styling translation from Phase 4.1 flags bitmask to Markdown inline syntax. Bold (bit 0) -> **text**. Italic (bit 1) -> *text*. Bold+italic -> ***text***. Subscript (bit 3) -> text. Superscript (bit 4) -> text. Smallcaps (bit 2) -> text. Color-only differences: no styling. ## Why this matters Inline span styling preserves visual semantics that affect document comprehension (e.g. italicized terms, mathematical exponents as superscript). Without this layer, Markdown loses formatting differentiation; LLMs reading the output lose key cues (e.g. emphasis). ## Implementation guidance - fn span_to_markdown(span: &Span) -> String - Read span.flags bitmask: - bit 0 (BOLD): wrap in ** - bit 1 (ITALIC): wrap in * - bit 3 (SUBSCRIPT): wrap in - bit 4 (SUPERSCRIPT): wrap in - bit 2 (SMALLCAPS): wrap in - Combinations: bold+italic uses *** (CommonMark shortcut); bold+sub uses **text** etc - Color-only flag differences: do NOT emit any styling (color is not semantically meaningful in Markdown; downstream renderers strip it) - Escape Markdown special chars in text: \, `, *, _, [, ], (, ), #, !, +, -, ., (block-context-sensitive) - Use a single regex or hand-written escaper for special chars ## Critical considerations - Markdown escape rules are context-sensitive: in code blocks NOTHING is escaped; in inline text, `*` `_` `[` etc. must be escaped to prevent unintended formatting - Smallcaps uses HTML span because CommonMark has no smallcaps syntax (plan line 2176) - Combination order matters for nesting: emit **...** not **...** (renderers handle both, but consistency aids diff readability) - Empty spans (whitespace-only) emit unwrapped (no point wrapping whitespace in formatting) - Unicode replacement char U+FFFD passes through as-is (LLM can detect garbled spans) ## Acceptance criteria - Critical test: bold + italic span emitted as ***text*** - Subscript span: 2 in H2O test fixture - Superscript span: th in 4th fixture - Smallcaps: CAPS - Color-only difference: no styling emitted - Special chars escaped: span text "1*2" -> "1\*2" ## References - Plan section: Phase 6.5 inline span styling (lines 2170-2178) - Phase 4.1 flags bitmask

issue.description:
## Goal

Execute PDF content stream operators to produce a raw glyph list with positions. Deliver pdftract-core::content module; raw Vec<Glyph> per page.

## Sub-phases

- 3.1 Graphics State Machine — full state stack: ctm, text_matrix, text_line_matrix, font, font_size, char_spacing, word_spacing, horiz_scaling, leading, text_rise, text_rendering_mode, fill_color, stroke_color; Color enum (DeviceGray/RGB/CMYK/Spot/Other); 14 text state operators; CTM operator cm; q/Q stack with depth limit 64; page /Rotate normalization
- 3.2 Text Operator Processing — Tj, TJ (with kerning), ', double-quote; per-glyph: decode char codes, resolve Unicode via Phase 2, compute glyph advance, compute device-space bbox via text_matrix * CTM, detect word boundaries (adaptive threshold)
- 3.3 Resource Context and Form XObject Recursion — ResourceStack per page; Do operator pushes form XObject scope with merged resources; form /Matrix applied to CTM; /BBox as clipping; cycle detection; stack depth limit 20
- 3.4 Marked Content Tracking — BMC, BDC, EMC operators; track innermost MCID per glyph; OCG /OC tag suppression when default state is OFF
- 3.5 Inline Images — BI/ID/EI sequences; detect and skip without confusing parser; EI must be preceded by whitespace per spec

## Rationale

The content stream interpreter is the PDF execution engine. It converts the operator sequence into a structured glyph list with full position + font + color metadata. Every later phase (layout, OCR, output) consumes this glyph list. Without a correct graphics state machine, multi-column layouts, rotated pages, scaled forms, and nested XObjects all produce wrong results.

The adaptive word boundary detector is critical: TeX-generated PDFs frequently omit space characters and rely on positional gaps. Recalibration scope per-font with 20-glyph bootstrap ensures different fonts on the same page use appropriate thresholds.

Marked content tracking (3.4) enables Phase 7.1 StructTree exploitation: tagged PDFs annotate each glyph with an MCID linking to a structure element.

## Critical considerations

- Per-glyph Unicode resolution calls into Phase 2; cache hits on same char code in same font are common — exploit this
- Word boundary threshold comparison happens in TEXT SPACE, not device space (do NOT apply CTM before comparing)
- 20-glyph recalibration window resets on every Tf operator
- For first 20 glyphs after font switch, use fixed initial threshold of 0.25 * font_size
- TJ negative kerning values mean tighter spacing (no space); large positive (> 0.2 * font_size) injects a synthetic word boundary
- text_matrix is reset to identity on every BT; text_line_matrix tracks the current line origin
- Tr=3 (invisible text) preserved in Glyph list with rendering_mode=3; CLI filters via flag
- Color CSS hex conversion: DeviceGray(v) to DeviceRGB([v,v,v]); DeviceCMYK to approximate RGB; Spot/Other to null
- Form XObject /Matrix multiplies into CTM before nested execution; restore CTM on return
- Cycle detection emits STRUCT_XOBJECT_CYCLE diagnostic; depth limit 20

## Acceptance criteria

- All 5 sub-phase beads (3.1-3.5) closed
- pdftract-core::content module compiles and consumes Phase 1 + Phase 2 outputs
- Per-page Vec<Glyph> produced for all fixture PDFs in tests/fixtures/vector/
- All Phase 3 critical tests pass: q/Q 64-deep, Td chain, TeX-PDF word boundaries, TJ kerning, invisible text, form XObject cycle, marked content nesting, inline images
- Page /Rotate 90/180/270 produces correctly normalized bboxes

## Blocks

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the four "passthrough" image filters. pdftract-core does NOT decode raster image data itself — it stores the raw encoded bytes for the OCR pipeline (Phase 5) to consume. The passthrough wraps each filter with:

1. Format-specific marker validation (DCT: SOI/EOI; JBIG2: segment header; JPX: JP2 box magic; CCITT: minimal validation)
2. Diagnostic emission for missing decoder support (OCR_JBIG2_UNSUPPORTED if no full-render feature; OCR_JPX_UNSUPPORTED; OCR_CCITT_UNSUPPORTED if no libtiff)
3. Recording of relevant metadata (DCT: /ColorTransform value; JBIG2: /JBIG2Globals stream ref)

## Implementation guidance

- DCTDecode (JPEG):
  - Validate the first 2 bytes are 0xFF 0xD8 (SOI = Start Of Image marker); if not, emit STREAM_INVALID_JPEG diagnostic but still pass through
  - Validate the last 2 bytes are 0xFF 0xD9 (EOI = End Of Image marker); some buggy producers omit EOI; emit STREAM_INVALID_JPEG warning but pass through
  - /DecodeParms may have /ColorTransform (0 = none, 1 = YCbCr conversion); record for downstream consumer
  - Pass through raw bytes unchanged
- JBIG2Decode:
  - JBIG2 has a complex segment format; do not validate beyond passthrough
  - Check if `full-render` feature is enabled; if NOT: emit OCR_JBIG2_UNSUPPORTED (per EC-11); still pass through bytes for downstream consumer
  - /JBIG2Globals: a reference to a globally-shared symbol dictionary; record the ref for the OCR pipeline (which uses pdfium-render to decode JBIG2 if full-render is on)
- JPXDecode (JPEG 2000):
  - Validate JP2 box magic at the start (12 bytes: `00 00 00 0C 6A 50 20 20 0D 0A 87 0A`)
  - Without full-render OR system libopenjp2: emit OCR_JPX_UNSUPPORTED (per EC-12); pass through bytes
- CCITTFaxDecode:
  - Without full-render OR system libtiff (via image crate's tiff feature): emit OCR_CCITT_UNSUPPORTED (per EC-13); pass through bytes
  - /DecodeParms commonly has /K (encoding: -1 Group 4, 0 Group 3 1D, > 0 Group 3 2D), /Columns, /Rows, /EncodedByteAlign, /EndOfLine, /BlackIs1; record for downstream

## Critical considerations

- Critical test from plan: DCTDecode passes raw bytes unchanged AND SOI marker present (verify both)
- The OCR_JBIG2_UNSUPPORTED / OCR_JPX_UNSUPPORTED / OCR_CCITT_UNSUPPORTED diagnostics are emitted at PARSE time even though the image may never be needed for OCR; this gives operators visibility that the file CAN'T be OCR'd later. EC-11 / EC-12 / EC-13
- Passthrough means: the bytes go into the document model AS-IS; the Phase 5 OCR pipeline either decodes them (via pdfium-render or image crate) or skips that image region
- DCTDecode is the most common image filter (~80% of PDF images); ensure SOI/EOI validation is fast — these are 2-byte checks at fixed offsets
- /JBIG2Globals stream ref: the actual global symbol dict is a separate stream object; pdftract records the ref so the OCR pipeline can dereference it later
- The OCR pipeline (Phase 5.2) re-reads the dict's /Filter to know what decoder to use; pdftract-core doesn't need to choose a decoder here
- Per ADR-003: pdfium-render is OPT-IN via `full-render` feature; default builds emit the *_UNSUPPORTED diagnostics for JBIG2 / JPX / CCITT
- INV-8: invalid JPEG / JBIG2 / JPX / CCITT data does NOT cause panic; the passthrough preserves any bytes (including malformed ones)
- File size: image streams can be many MB; the bomb limit applies (the orchestrator counts each filter's output bytes); a malicious 3 GB embedded JPEG triggers STREAM_BOMB

## Acceptance criteria

- Critical test passes: DCTDecode fixture with known JPEG — bytes unchanged, SOI marker present
- JPEG without EOI marker: passes through with STREAM_INVALID_JPEG warning
- JBIG2Decode without full-render feature: OCR_JBIG2_UNSUPPORTED diagnostic emitted; bytes still passed through
- JPXDecode without full-render: OCR_JPX_UNSUPPORTED emitted
- CCITTFaxDecode without libtiff feature: OCR_CCITT_UNSUPPORTED emitted
- JP2 box magic check on JPXDecode: detects malformed JPX with STREAM_INVALID_JPX
- proptest: random byte sequences as each filter never panic
- INV-8 maintained

## References

- Plan section: Phase 1.5 lines 1146-1149 (DCT/JBIG2/JPX/CCITT passthroughs + OCR diagnostics); critical test line 1164 (DCT passthrough + SOI marker)
- EC-11, EC-12, EC-13 (unsupported image format diagnostics)
- ADR-003 (pdfium-render opt-in via full-render)
- Phase 5.2 (OCR consumes the raw bytes)
issue.title: Implement DCTDecode / JBIG2Decode / JPXDecode / CCITTFaxDecode passthroughs with SOI/EOI validation + OCR_*_UNSUPPORTED diagnostics

## Scope

Implement the ParentTree resolver that assigns each MCID-tagged marked-content sequence on a page to its owning StructElem. Walks the /StructTreeRoot /ParentTree (a number tree keyed by structParents) and produces a per-page map MCID -> StructElemRef that the block builder consumes.

## Why this matters

Without the ParentTree, the StructTree is just a list of titles with no glyph attachment - blocks cannot be reconstructed because the parser cannot tell which glyphs belong to which StructElem. ParentTree resolution is the only correct way per spec; alternatives (centroid containment) misattribute glyphs on overlap.

## Implementation guidance

- /StructTreeRoot /ParentTree is a number tree (PDF 1.7 7.9.7); keyed by /StructParents (integer on page or annotation object dictionaries)
- For each page, look up its /StructParents key in the number tree; the value is an array of StructElem refs indexed by MCID position (entry i = StructElem owning MCID i)
- Annotations have their own /StructParent (singular) - this resolves to a single StructElem ref (not an array)
- Build the per-page map: HashMap<u32 mcid, Rc<StructElemNode>>
- Some entries may be null (MCID used in content but not claimed by any StructElem) - record as "orphan MCID" and route to coverage calculation in 7.1.4

## Critical considerations

- Number-tree walking requires /Kids/Names/Limits traversal (NOT a flat dict); reuse name-tree walker if shared
- Annotations with /StructParent point INTO the structure tree (an annotation's /Contents become tagged content under that StructElem)
- Malformed ParentTree (off-by-one indexing, missing entries) MUST NOT crash; record diagnostic and treat all MCIDs on that page as orphans
- Cache the resolved map per page so coverage check (7.1.4) and block builder share without re-walking

## Acceptance criteria

- ParentTree walked correctly for both numeric tree shapes (Kids+Limits, leaf Names)
- Per-page map built; orphan MCIDs recorded
- Unit tests: synthetic ParentTree with valid + malformed + missing entries
- Test fixture: tagged PDF with annotation /StructParent linking to body StructElem

## References

- Plan section: 7.1 line 2550 (MCID-to-StructElem mapping)
- PDF 1.7 spec 14.7.4.4 ParentTree
- PDF 1.7 spec 7.9.7 Number Tree
- Phase 3.4 marked-content tagger (MCID source)
- 7.1.4 (coverage check consumer)

## Scope

Author `SECURITY.md` at the repo root. Documents the responsible-disclosure contact (`security@jedarden.com`), the 90-day disclosure window, the supported version policy, the use of GitHub's private vulnerability reporting, the CVE assignment process, and the coordination policy with downstream packagers (Homebrew, distro maintainers if any exist at the time).

## Why this matters

A published vulnerability disclosure process is required by industry norms (OpenSSF Scorecard `vulnerabilities` check, Google's open-source vetting, the U.S. CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog process). Without SECURITY.md, security researchers either file public issues (worst case) or do not report at all (also bad). Aligning to industry-norm 90-day windows means coordinated disclosure with downstream consumers is predictable.

## Implementation guidance

- File location: `/SECURITY.md` at repo root
- Sections (in order):
  1. **Supported Versions** — table:
     | Version | Supported |
     |---|---|
     | latest minor | Yes |
     | previous minor | Yes (security fixes only) |
     | older | No |
  2. **Reporting a Vulnerability**:
     - Email: `security@jedarden.com` (PGP key fingerprint published in the README; key file at `docs/security/pgp-public-key.asc`)
     - Alternative: GitHub Private Vulnerability Reporting (link to the repo's Security tab)
     - Do NOT open a public issue or PR
  3. **Disclosure Window**:
     - Acknowledge receipt within 48 hours
     - Initial triage within 5 business days (confirmed/dispute/need-more-info)
     - Fix and CVE within 90 days of confirmation (extendable by mutual agreement for complex issues)
     - Public disclosure: simultaneous with fix release; embargoed coordination with downstream packagers (Homebrew, distros) for major vulns
  4. **CVE Assignment**:
     - Filed via GitHub Security Advisories (GitHub is a CNA)
     - Researcher credited unless they request anonymity
  5. **Scope** — what counts as a security issue:
     - In scope: code execution from crafted PDF, path traversal, SSRF, MCP auth bypass, signature verification bypass, supply-chain attacks
     - Out of scope: DoS via large valid PDFs (covered by resource limits, not a vuln), missing security headers on the demo site, vulns in dependencies already disclosed upstream
  6. **Safe Harbor** — researchers acting in good faith and following this policy are protected from legal action by the project (no DMCA, no CFAA threats)

## Critical considerations

- The `security@jedarden.com` alias MUST forward to a monitored inbox (24-hour SLA on the acknowledgement); test the alias quarterly
- A PGP key for the security contact MUST be published with a fingerprint in the README; rotate every 2 years; the public key file lives at `docs/security/pgp-public-key.asc`
- The 90-day window aligns with industry norms (Project Zero, ZDI, GitHub Security Lab) — shorter windows discourage researchers; longer windows are seen as obstruction
- Coordinated disclosure with downstream packagers: if a major vuln is fixed and a Homebrew formula exists, ping the formula maintainer 24 hours before public disclosure
- Safe Harbor language is non-trivial; copy the Disclose.io safe-harbor template verbatim and link to the source
- GitHub's CNA scope: GitHub Security Advisories can issue CVEs for vulnerabilities in code hosted on GitHub; this avoids the MITRE backlog

## Acceptance criteria

- `SECURITY.md` exists at repo root with all six sections
- `security@jedarden.com` alias is set up and monitored
- PGP key for the security contact is published at `docs/security/pgp-public-key.asc` and referenced in the README
- GitHub's Community Standards check marks Security Policy as green
- A test report sent to `security@jedarden.com` receives an acknowledgement within 48 hours
- Linked from README, from CONTRIBUTING.md (responsible-disclosure section), and from the security ISSUE_TEMPLATE (which redirects users here)

## References

- Plan section: Release Engineering / Contributor Workflow, line 3433 (SECURITY.md with security@jedarden.com + 90-day disclosure)
- OpenSSF Scorecard `vulnerabilities` check
- Disclose.io safe-harbor template
- GitHub Security Advisories docs

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the default (non-JSON) match-printing sink. Consumes MatchEvent records from worker channel and prints to stdout in the format: "<path>:p<page+1>:[x0,y0,x1,y1]:  <span_text>" with the bbox as comma-separated 1-decimal-place floats. Page index displayed 1-based for user friendliness. Honor -l (files-with-matches only), -c (per-file count only), --max-results, --quiet flags. Sink runs in main thread; workers feed via mpsc channel.

## Why this matters

Default output is what users see 90% of the time; the format must be greppable, parseable, and visually scannable. Path-first format mirrors ripgrep + grep conventions. The bbox is the differentiator vs. other PDF greppers - it lets follow-up tools navigate exactly to the matched location. 1-based page numbers match every PDF viewer in existence.

## Implementation guidance

- Channel: std::sync::mpsc::Receiver<MatchEvent> or crossbeam-channel; one consumer (sink) runs in main thread
- Format string: "{path}:p{page_index_1_based}:[{x0:.1},{y0:.1},{x1:.1},{y1:.1}]:  {span_text}"
- Two-space gap before span_text to make scanning easier
- Path: if running with relative paths, print relative; if absolute, print absolute (preserve user input)
- -l flag: skip printing each match; instead, on FileDone, if file had > 0 matches, print "<path>"; deduplicate across multiple matches in same file using a HashSet<PathBuf>
- -c flag: skip printing each match; on FileDone, print "<path>:{match_count}"; if count == 0, only print when -v is set
- --max-results N: track running total; once N reached, signal workers to stop (via Arc<AtomicBool> shutdown flag); finish gracefully
- --quiet: suppress all stdout; sink still consumes channel to drain workers
- Exit code: 0 if any match printed, 1 if zero matches across all files, 2 on fatal error (per grep convention)
- Print is line-buffered via stdout().lock() for thread safety; flush after each line for streaming behavior
- ANSI color: detect TTY + NO_COLOR env var; if color enabled, highlight match_text in red within span_text (default off for v1; future enhancement)

## Critical considerations

- 1-based page index (p1, not p0) - PDF viewers all use 1-based; aligns with user expectations
- bbox 1-decimal-place floats give precision without verbosity
- -l mode: a file with 100 matches prints once; dedupe critical for file path printing
- -c with 0 matches: only prints when -v flag is set (per grep convention)
- --max-results gracefully stops workers; do not abort mid-page (worker finishes its current page then sees shutdown flag)
- --quiet exit code: 0 for any match, 1 for none, 2 for fatal - same as grep
- First-match latency: sink should print immediately on first MatchEvent receipt (within 100 ms of process start per acceptance criterion)

## Acceptance criteria

- Default output format matches plan exactly
- 1-based page numbers (p1 for first page)
- -l prints unique filenames only
- -c prints counts per file
- --max-results 5 stops after 5 matches; workers stop cleanly
- --quiet suppresses stdout; exit code reflects match presence
- First match printed within 100 ms (verified via integration test)
- Public TextSink::run(rx: Receiver<MatchEvent>, args: &GrepArgs) -> i32 exit_code

## References

- Plan section: 7.8 lines 2733-2737 (default format), 2720-2722 (-l, -c flags), 2726 (--max-results), 2730 (--quiet)
- 7.8.4 (MatchEvent source)
- 7.8.6 (JSON-Lines alternative)
- 7.8.8 (progress bar coexistence)
issue.title: 7.8.5: Default human-readable text output sink (path:p<page>:bbox:span_text)

issue.description:
## Scope

Multi-output emission architecture. Trait OutputSink { open(header), page(page), close(footer) }. Concrete sinks: JsonSink, MarkdownSink, TextSink, NdjsonSink, ReceiptSink (Phase 6.8). Single extraction populates any subset of formats concurrently. Atomic writes (temp + rename). Single-stdout validation. NDJSON mutually exclusive with whole-document formats. HTTP serve mode multipart/mixed for multi-format requests.

## Why this matters

Users routinely want JSON for programs AND Markdown for docs AND plain text for grep. Running extraction three times wastes ~3x CPU. This architecture lets one extraction populate all formats concurrently. Atomic writes guarantee that an interrupted extraction never leaves partial output files behind. The 1.1x performance target (line 2275) keeps multi-output basically free.

## Implementation guidance

- Trait:
  trait OutputSink: Send {
      fn open(&mut self, header: &DocumentHeader) -> io::Result<()>;
      fn page(&mut self, page: &Page) -> io::Result<()>;
      fn close(&mut self, footer: &DocumentFooter) -> io::Result<()>;
  }
- Concrete sinks (6.6.1):
  - JsonSink (whole-doc; buffers pages until close, then emits Output)
  - MarkdownSink (whole-doc; buffers pages, emits MD on close)
  - TextSink (streaming-friendly; emits per page on page())
  - NdjsonSink (streaming; emits frames on each call)
  - ReceiptSink (Phase 6.8; whole-doc with receipt augmentation)
- Pipeline: extraction calls open/page/close on every registered sink
- Atomic writes (6.6.2): open as <path>.tmp.<pid>; rename to <path> on successful close
- CLI design:
  - --json out.json --md out.md --text out.txt  (multiple at once)
  - --md - --json out.json  (one to stdout, one to file)
  - --format json,markdown,text -o out  (auto-naming)
- Validation rules (6.6.3):
  - At most one format may use "-"
  - Repeating same format flag rejected
  - --ndjson mutually exclusive with all other formats
- HTTP serve (6.4) update: new "format" form field accepting comma-separated formats; single-format returns body; multi-format returns multipart/mixed

## Critical considerations

- Memory ceiling: in-memory model held until slowest sink completes; for 500-page doc with 200 spans/page -> ~20 MB peak (acceptable)
- Atomicity: panic mid-extraction leaves NO partial output files (verified by panic-injection fixture)
- Cross-format consistency: all sinks observe same document_fingerprint in headers
- JSON sink output MUST be byte-identical whether emitted alone or alongside MD sink (sink isolation invariant)
- Trait OutputSink is Send (not Sync); sinks own their state

## Acceptance criteria

- All Phase 6.6 child task beads closed
- Single extraction -> 3 simultaneous outputs (JSON + MD + text) completes within 1.1x single-format time
- Cross-format consistency: all sinks see same document_fingerprint
- Atomicity: panic mid-extraction leaves NO partial output files
- --json a.json --md b.md -> both produced, both valid (critical test)
- --md - --json out.json -> MD to stdout, JSON to file
- Same extraction with --json only vs --json --md -> JSON byte-identical
- --ndjson --md b.md rejected at CLI parse time

## References

- Plan section: Phase 6.6 (lines 2217-2284)
- Phase 1.7 document_fingerprint

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the MCP bearer-token ingress channels: --auth-token-file PATH (PATH contains only the token, terminating newline stripped) as the RECOMMENDED path, PDFTRACT_MCP_TOKEN env var as the fallback. Reject plain --auth-token VALUE unless PDFTRACT_INSECURE_CLI_TOKEN=1 is set. Enforce TH-03: pdftract mcp --bind MUST require a token unless the bind address resolves to 127.0.0.1 or ::1; startup aborts with exit code 78 otherwise.

## Why this matters

TH-03 (line 874) is the foundation of the multi-tenant deployment story; without it, any operator who copy-pastes pdftract mcp --bind 0.0.0.0:PORT from a tutorial silently exposes an unauthenticated tool surface to the entire network. Lines 916-921 codify the channel-and-rejection policy. The exit-78 contract is what monitoring relies on to detect a misconfiguration and refuse to mark the pod ready.

## Implementation guidance

- Files to modify:
  - pdftract-cli/src/args.rs (mcp subcommand): add --auth-token-file PATH; the --auth-token VALUE flag stays as a deprecated alias guarded by PDFTRACT_INSECURE_CLI_TOKEN env
  - pdftract-mcp/src/auth.rs: a resolve_token function with priority: 1) --auth-token-file (read file, strip terminating newline); 2) PDFTRACT_MCP_TOKEN env (Some if non-empty); 3) --auth-token VALUE (only if PDFTRACT_INSECURE_CLI_TOKEN=1; stderr warning if so); 4) None
  - pdftract-mcp/src/bind.rs: a check_bind_security function called BEFORE listener creation:
    - parse the bind address
    - if resolved address is in {127.0.0.0/8, ::1/128} AND no token -> ok (loopback exemption)
    - if resolved address is anything else AND no token -> stderr error + exit 78
    - if token is provided -> ok regardless of bind address
- Loopback resolution: parse bind addr; use std::net::SocketAddr::ip().is_loopback() (handles both v4 and v6); for hostnames like "localhost" resolve via std::net::ToSocketAddrs and check ALL resolved addresses are loopback (a hostname that resolves to mixed loopback + non-loopback addresses MUST be treated as non-loopback to fail closed)
- Exit code 78 (config error per sysexits.h EX_CONFIG) with stderr message: "ERROR: pdftract mcp --bind ADDR requires --auth-token-file PATH or PDFTRACT_MCP_TOKEN env (loopback addresses 127.0.0.1 / ::1 exempt). Refusing to bind to ADDR without authentication."
- Inspector token (Phase 7.9) follows the same channels and same enforcement -- treat as a parallel implementation but in pdftract-inspector

## Critical considerations

- Loopback exemption MUST fail closed when in doubt -- a hostname that does not resolve, or resolves to mixed addresses, is NOT exempt
- The check runs BEFORE the listener binds; if the listener bound first the port would still be open during the failure window
- DNS rebinding: a hostname that resolves to loopback at startup but later resolves to non-loopback is out of scope for this check (it is a hostfile / DNS server attack class, not a pdftract attack class)
- The --auth-token-file mode is preferred because the file's mode bits (chmod 0600) prevent other users from reading it; env vars leak via /proc/PID/environ which is readable by the same user
- A token of length < 32 chars is acceptable but a stderr warning is emitted (entropy budget concern); the binary does NOT enforce a minimum length so existing deployments are not broken
- TH-03 test (separate bead) spawns mcp --bind 0.0.0.0:0 with no token; asserts startup failure with exit 78

## Acceptance criteria

- --auth-token-file PATH flag implemented; reads file and strips trailing newline
- PDFTRACT_MCP_TOKEN env var resolved when --auth-token-file absent
- --auth-token VALUE rejected (exit 64) unless PDFTRACT_INSECURE_CLI_TOKEN=1
- mcp --bind ADDR with non-loopback ADDR and no token: aborts with exit 78
- mcp --bind ADDR with loopback ADDR and no token: succeeds
- mcp --bind ADDR with token: succeeds regardless of address
- Inspector token follows the same policy
- TH-03 test passes (separate bead)

## References

- Plan: lines 874 (TH-03 mitigation), 915-921 (Secrets Handling: MCP bearer token), 922-924 (Inspector token same channels)
issue.title: Hardening: PDFTRACT_MCP_TOKEN env var + --auth-token-file flag + TH-03 startup abort enforcement

## Scope

Author the `pdftract-dotnet-publish` WorkflowTemplate. Triggered by milestone tag after `pdftract-build-binaries` completes. Builds the `Pdftract` NuGet package, runs the conformance test, publishes to NuGet.org via the API key.

## Why this matters

Manual NuGet publishing is one command but easy to skip under deadline pressure; the workflow encapsulates conformance gating and credential management. NuGet.org is the canonical .NET distribution channel; no equivalent of Maven Central's staging flow exists — publishing is one-shot.

## Implementation guidance

- WorkflowTemplate file: `k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/pdftract-dotnet-publish.yaml` in `jedarden/declarative-config`
- Inputs: tag name; NuGet API key from ESO Secret `nuget-api-key-pdftract` (synced from OpenBao key `nuget-api-key-pdftract`)
- Steps:
  1. `clone-sdk-repo`: `git clone https://github.com/jedarden/pdftract-dotnet.git --branch main`
  2. `sync-version`: update `Pdftract.csproj` `<Version>X.Y.Z</Version>` to match the binary tag
  3. `restore`: `dotnet restore` (uses package lock for reproducibility)
  4. `build`: `dotnet build --configuration Release --no-restore`
  5. `conformance`: `dotnet test --no-build --filter FullyQualifiedName~ConformanceTests` (runs the shared suite; aborts on any failure)
  6. `pack`: `dotnet pack --configuration Release --no-build --output ./packages`
  7. `publish`: `dotnet nuget push ./packages/*.nupkg --api-key $NUGET_API_KEY --source https://api.nuget.org/v3/index.json --skip-duplicate`
- Container: `mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:8.0`
- Re-runnability: `--skip-duplicate` makes the publish idempotent
- Pre-release publishes (`vX.Y.Z-rc.N`) use the NuGet pre-release version syntax: `<Version>X.Y.Z-rc.N</Version>`; NuGet treats these as pre-release automatically

## Critical considerations

- ADR-009: runs on iad-ci; never use GitHub Actions
- NuGet API key MUST have `Push new packages` permission on the `Pdftract` package id (created on first publish); rotate every 365 days per the secrets rotation runbook
- NuGet.org is IMMUTABLE — a published version cannot be recalled, only unlisted; a bad publish requires a new patch release
- Symbol packages (`.snupkg`) are recommended but optional; if generated (`<IncludeSymbols>true</IncludeSymbols>`), they MUST be pushed alongside the main package
- NuGet's indexing is asynchronous (~5 min); the package may not be visible on nuget.org immediately after publish
- Failure of `pdftract-dotnet-publish` is recoverable by re-running the workflow

## Acceptance criteria

- WorkflowTemplate file lands at the documented path in jedarden/declarative-config
- A test run against a fresh tag publishes `Pdftract@X.Y.Z` to NuGet.org
- The conformance step aborts publish if any case fails
- The package is installable via `dotnet add package Pdftract --version X.Y.Z` within 15 minutes of publish
- A re-run is idempotent (`--skip-duplicate` returns 0)
- Pre-release tags publish with pre-release version suffix

## References

- Plan section: SDK Architecture / Per-SDK Release Channels, line 3573 (NuGet)
- Plan section: SDK Acceptance Criteria, line 3584 (24-hour cascade)
- ADR-009 (Argo only)
- Sibling: .NET SDK implementation bead
- dotnet nuget push docs: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/nuget/reference/cli-reference/dotnet-nuget-push

## Scope

Author docs/user-docs/src/json-schema-reference.md: a rendering of docs/schema/v1.0/pdftract.schema.json as human-readable Markdown. Each top-level type linked to its source plan section. Without it, downstream developers either read the raw schema JSON (cumbersome) or guess from examples. The reference is what RAG-ingest pipeline authors, MCP agent prompt authors, and Python wheel users land on when designing their consumers.

## Implementation guidance

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the --audit-log FILE flag on serve / mcp --bind / inspect subcommands. Emits a per-request NDJSON line with ts, client_ip, tool, fingerprint, duration_ms, status, and diagnostics fields. The AuditLogWriter wraps a BufWriter<File> behind a Mutex; writes one NDJSON line per request; flushes after each line.

Module: crates/pdftract-core/src/audit.rs + crates/pdftract-cli/src/args.rs + crates/pdftract-cli/src/middleware/audit.rs (for both serve and mcp).

## Why this matters

The audit log is the only structured trace of who-did-what against a publicly-exposed pdftract instance; without it, post-incident forensics is impossible. NDJSON makes the log directly consumable by SIEMs (Splunk, Datadog, ELK) without intermediate parsing. The structural fingerprint (vs file path or URL) keeps PII out of the log while preserving the document identity.

## Implementation guidance

- AuditLogWriter:
  ```rust
  pub struct AuditLogWriter {
      writer: Mutex<BufWriter<Box<dyn Write + Send>>>,
  }
  impl AuditLogWriter {
      pub fn open(path: &Path) -> io::Result<Self>;  // FILE = - means stdout
      pub fn write_record(&self, record: &AuditRecord) -> io::Result<()>;
  }
  ```
- AuditRecord schema (serde Serialize):
  - ts: ISO-8601 RFC3339 UTC string (e.g. 2026-05-16T12:34:56Z)
  - client_ip: Option<String> (IP only, no port); None for stdio MCP
  - tool: String (extract / classify / grep / mcp.extract / etc.)
  - fingerprint: Option<String> (pdftract-v1:hex form; None if extraction failed before fingerprint computation)
  - duration_ms: u64
  - status: String (\"ok\" | \"error\")
  - diagnostics: Vec<String> (diagnostic codes only, no messages — message text could leak content)
- CLI flag: --audit-log FILE on serve, mcp, inspect; FILE = - means stdout; absent means no audit log
- Middleware: tower::Layer that wraps every request; records start time; on response computes duration; writes AuditRecord
- The writer is created at startup; passed by Arc into the axum router state

## Critical considerations

- BufWriter + Mutex: lock-per-write; writes are NOT contended in practice (per-request); BufWriter amortizes file I/O cost
- Flush after each line: ensures crash safety (lines committed to disk before next request returns)
- File rotation: NOT in this bead (operators use logrotate externally); document this
- The audit log file is owned by the pdftract process; the operator must ensure the file path is writable
- FILE = - means stdout; useful for systemd/k8s where logs are captured by the runtime
- Stdio MCP mode: audit log writes to stderr (NOT the FILE flag — stdio mode's stdout is JSON-RPC); document this departure

## Acceptance criteria

- pdftract serve --audit-log /var/log/pdftract.ndjson → per-request NDJSON lines appear
- Each line is single-line valid JSON (no embedded newlines in values)
- duration_ms is accurate (verified via a 100ms-sleep fixture)
- client_ip captured from X-Real-IP or X-Forwarded-For header (set by reverse proxy)
- Stdio MCP audit goes to stderr (with --audit-log /dev/stderr or implicitly)
- Concurrent requests: writes don't interleave (Mutex ensures atomic line writes)
- Crash mid-request: log line either fully present or fully absent (BufWriter flushes after each write)

## References

- Plan section: Phase 6 audit logging (lines 931-964)
- Coordinator: pdftract-4em4l (parent — audit-log + policy enforcement bundle)
- Sibling: log-policy enforcement
Labels: audit, phase-6, security

issue.description:
## Scope

Add a Cargo bench target pdftract-grep-1000 that runs grep across the tests/fixtures/grep-corpus/ (1000 PDFs, ~100 MB total). Wall-clock time and throughput are recorded to benches/results/<commit-sha>.json. CI gates the run against (a) pdfgrep: pdftract must be >= 2x faster, (b) pdftotext + ripgrep sequential pipeline: pdftract must be >= 3x faster, (c) pdftract historical results: > 10% regression blocks the PR. CI runner uses --progress-json so Argo logs show continuous file_done heartbeats during the bench.

## Why this matters

The throughput gate is a binding contract. Without CI-enforced benchmarks, refactors quietly slow down the hot path and the 50 MB/s claim erodes. Comparison against external tools (pdfgrep, pdftotext+ripgrep) keeps the marketing claim honest: pdftract is supposed to be faster, and CI proves it on every PR. Argo Workflow logs with --progress-json mean operators see steady file_done events instead of multi-minute silence.

## Implementation guidance

- Bench: criterion benchmark or a custom Cargo bench bin; criterion is preferred for stable variance
- Fixture corpus: tests/fixtures/grep-corpus/ - 1000 small PDFs (~100 KB avg, mix of vector + scanned)
- Build corpus separately; commit a manifest CSV (filename, byte size, expected match count for "the") so the bench validates correctness too
- Workflow:
  - Phase 0 CI step: run pdftract grep "the" tests/fixtures/grep-corpus/ -j 4 --progress-json
  - Capture wall clock + match count
  - Record to benches/results/<commit-sha>.json: { commit, started_at, files_total, bytes_total, duration_ms, matches_total, throughput_mb_s, peak_rss_mb }
  - Compare against last main-branch result; > 10% regression in throughput -> CI fails
- External baselines (run in same CI step on same corpus, same 4-core machine):
  - pdfgrep -r "the" tests/fixtures/grep-corpus/ - time it
  - find tests/fixtures/grep-corpus/ -name '*.pdf' | xargs -I{} pdftotext {} - | rg "the" - time it
  - Compute ratios; pdftract must be >= 2x pdfgrep, >= 3x pdftotext+ripgrep
- Argo Workflow log expectation: a file_done JSON event every 50-100 ms (smooth heartbeat)
- Peak RSS measured via /usr/bin/time -v or rusage from a wrapper

## Critical considerations

- Corpus stability: commit a fixed corpus to git LFS or generate it deterministically from a seed (regenerable script avoids bloat); document the choice
- Determinism: 4-core CI machine; pin rayon thread count to 4; pin OS scheduler (taskset 0-3) for stable throughput
- Variance: criterion provides confidence intervals; require 3 runs per measurement; 10% threshold compares medians
- External baseline absence: if pdfgrep or pdftotext not installed in CI image, skip ratio check with a CI warning (do not fail)
- Memory cap: peak RSS < 200 MB is a separate acceptance criterion; bench captures it
- benches/results/<sha>.json: committed by CI back to a separate results branch (NOT main) to avoid commit-pong on every PR; alternative is GH artifact upload
- Bench corpus should be regeneratable from public domain PDF inputs (e.g. arXiv abstracts) so anyone can rerun

## Acceptance criteria

- Bench target pdftract-grep-1000 exists in Cargo.toml under [[bench]]
- CI step runs bench and records to benches/results/<sha>.json
- 50 MB/s gate enforced; PR fails on miss
- 2x pdfgrep gate enforced; PR fails on miss (warns if pdfgrep absent)
- 3x pdftotext+ripgrep gate enforced; PR fails on miss (warns if either tool absent)
- 10% regression vs. prior main blocks PR
- Argo log shows steady file_done events
- Corpus regeneration script in tests/fixtures/grep-corpus/regenerate.sh

- Phase 0 CI bench infrastructure
- 7.8.4, 7.8.5, 7.8.6, 7.8.9 (system under test)
