issue.description:
## Scope

Walk the document outline (bookmarks) linked list and produce a nested `Outline` tree for inclusion in the document-level JSON output.

Outline struct:
- `title: String` — decoded title text
- `count: i32` — /Count (positive = expanded by default; negative = collapsed; zero = no children)
- `dest_page: Option<u32>` — page index of the destination (0-based)
- `dest_anchor: Option<DestAnchor>` — anchor type and coordinates within the page
- `children: Vec<Outline>` — nested outlines

DestAnchor enum:
- `Xyz { left: Option<f64>, top: Option<f64>, zoom: Option<f64> }`
- `Fit`, `FitH(Option<f64>)`, `FitV(Option<f64>)`, `FitR(left, bottom, right, top)`, `FitB`, `FitBH(Option<f64>)`, `FitBV(Option<f64>)`

## Implementation guidance

- Public API: `parse_outlines(resolver: &XrefResolver, outlines_ref: Option<ObjRef>, pages: &[PageDict]) -> Vec<Outline>`
- If outlines_ref is None: return empty Vec (no outlines in document)
- Otherwise:
  1. Resolve outlines_ref to the outline root dict
  2. Start traversal at /First (first child outline node)
  3. For each node, recursively walk via /First (first child) and /Next (next sibling)
  4. Terminate at null /Next (end of sibling list) or null /First (no children)
- Each outline node dict has:
  - /Title (string) — REQUIRED
  - /Parent (ref to parent outline or root) — sanity check only
  - /First, /Last (ref to first/last child) — for traversal
  - /Next, /Prev (ref to next/prev sibling) — for traversal
  - /Count (integer) — number of visible descendants (positive expanded, negative collapsed)
  - /Dest (array) OR /A (action dict) — destination
- Title decoding:
  - If raw bytes start with `[0xFE, 0xFF]` (UTF-16BE BOM): decode rest as UTF-16BE; convert to UTF-8 String
  - Otherwise: decode as PDFDocEncoding (Latin-1 with named character overrides per spec Table D.2); convert to UTF-8 String
- Destination resolution:
  - `/Dest` is an array `[page_ref /XYZ left top zoom]` etc. — page_ref is an indirect ref to a Page dict; look up its index in `pages` Vec
  - `/A` is an action dict; if /S /GoTo, recurse on /A /D (which is a /Dest-style array)
  - Named destinations: /Dest can be a Name; resolve via catalog /Names /Dests number/name tree (out of scope for THIS bead; handle as TODO and emit STRUCT_UNRESOLVED_DESTINATION)

## Critical considerations

- Critical test from plan: PDF with 3-level bookmark hierarchy — all levels, titles, and page destinations extracted correctly
- UTF-16BE BOM detection: the bytes [0xFE 0xFF] are the BOM; some producers OMIT the BOM but still use UTF-16BE encoding (rare). Detect via heuristic: if every other byte (high byte) is 0x00 in a non-ASCII string, it's UTF-16BE. Fall through to PDFDocEncoding otherwise
- PDFDocEncoding is the spec's character set for "PDF text strings"; it's Latin-1 plus 29 named overrides (e.g. octal 142 = u160 -> Bullet character). Use a static lookup table; see PDF spec Table D.2
- Cycle detection: an outline node's /Next may form a cycle (malformed file); maintain HashSet<ObjRef> of visited nodes; emit STRUCT_CIRCULAR_REF on cycle, stop traversal
- Depth limit: 16 levels of nested outlines (very generous); emit STRUCT_DEPTH_EXCEEDED at deeper nesting
- Destination /Dest array with named first-element (string): looked up via /Names /Dests in catalog. For THIS bead: emit STRUCT_UNRESOLVED_DESTINATION as TODO; proper resolution can be a future enhancement
- /Count = 0 means the outline has no children (rare; usually /First /Last are also null in that case)
- An outline with /A /S /URI (web link instead of internal destination): record as `dest_page: None, dest_anchor: None` and add `link: String` field to the Outline struct? — Out of scope; just emit STRUCT_NON_GOTO_OUTLINE and record an empty destination

## Acceptance criteria

- Critical test passes: 3-level bookmark fixture — all 3 levels visible in output; titles correct (mix of ASCII and UTF-16BE)
- UTF-16BE BOM test: title bytes `[FE, FF, 0x00, 0x48, 0x00, 0x69]` -> "Hi"
- PDFDocEncoding test: title bytes with byte 0x8C (a PDFDocEncoded character) -> correct Unicode (e.g. "S with caron")
- /Count test: outline with /Count -3 (3 descendants, collapsed) -> count = -3 in JSON output
- Destination /XYZ test: outline -> page 5 at (100, 700, 1.5x zoom) -> dest_page=5, dest_anchor=Xyz{Some(100.0), Some(700.0), Some(1.5)}
- Cycle in /Next: STRUCT_CIRCULAR_REF; partial outline returned
- proptest: random outline tree shapes never panic
- INV-8 maintained

## References

- Plan section: Phase 1.4 line 1124 (outline traversal: linked list, UTF-16BE BOM, PDFDocEncoding, /Dest vs /A /GoTo, /Count)
- PDF spec 12.3.3 (Outline Hierarchy)
- PDF spec Annex D.2 (PDFDocEncoding character set)
- INV-8

issue.description:
## Scope

Parse the PDF 1.5+ xref stream — an alternative to the traditional table that supports compression (via FlateDecode) and the new type-2 (compressed-in-ObjStm) entry. An xref stream is itself an indirect-object stream with `/Type /XRef` and specific required keys:

- `/Size` — total object count
- `/W [type_w obj_w gen_w]` — byte widths of each field per entry (e.g. `[1 4 2]` = 1-byte type, 4-byte offset, 2-byte generation)
- `/Index [first_1 count_1 first_2 count_2 ...]` — subsection boundaries (default: `[0 /Size]`)
- `/Root`, `/Info`, etc. — same trailer dict keys as traditional

Entry types after decompression:
- Type 0: free; `obj_w` bytes = object number of next free; `gen_w` bytes = would-be-generation
- Type 1: in use, uncompressed; `obj_w` bytes = byte offset in file; `gen_w` bytes = generation
- Type 2: in use, compressed in ObjStm; `obj_w` bytes = host ObjStm object number; `gen_w` bytes = index within ObjStm (NOT generation; type-2 entries always have generation 0)

## Implementation guidance

- Public API: `parse_xref_stream(source: &PdfSource, stream_obj_offset: u64) -> XrefSection`
- Use Phase 1.2 parse_indirect_object to read the xref-stream object
- Use Phase 1.5 StreamDecoder to decompress the body (always FlateDecode in practice)
- Walk the decompressed body in `(type_w + obj_w + gen_w)`-byte strides
- For each entry, dispatch on type:
  - Type 0 -> `XrefEntry::Free { next_free, generation }`
  - Type 1 -> `XrefEntry::InUse { offset, generation }`
  - Type 2 -> `XrefEntry::Compressed { host_obj_stm: u32, index: u32 }` (generation is always 0)
- Map entries to ObjRefs using `/Index` subsection boundaries
- The trailer dict is the stream object's dict itself (no separate `trailer` keyword)

## Critical considerations

- Critical test from plan: type-2 xref entry must route through ObjStm correctly. After parsing the xref stream, a type-2 entry tells the resolver "object N is at index I in host ObjStm H"; the resolver calls Phase 1.2's ObjStm parser to fetch the actual object
- `/W` widths can be 0 for fields that always have the same value (e.g. `/W [1 4 0]` means generation is always 0). Decoded value defaults to 0 for zero-width fields
- A common field width pattern: `/W [1 3 1]` — fits files <= 16 MB. Larger files use `/W [1 4 2]`. Both must work
- Predictor: xref streams may use FlateDecode WITH a predictor (e.g. PNG Up predictor); Phase 1.5's decoder handles this transparently
- `/Index` default is `[0 /Size]` if absent; do not assume it's always present
- Endianness: multi-byte fields are BIG-ENDIAN per spec (e.g. a 4-byte offset of 0x00000123 = 291 in big-endian, not 305401856 little-endian)
- The xref stream's own indirect object (`N G obj << ... >> stream\n...endstream endobj`) is itself an entry in some xref — typically a type-1 entry in a `/Prev` predecessor. Bootstrap: the very first xref stream is found at `startxref` directly, no /Prev needed
- A malformed entry (e.g. type byte = 5, unknown): emit STRUCT_INVALID_XREF_ENTRY, treat as type 0 (free, ignored)

## Acceptance criteria

- Simple test: xref stream with `/W [1 4 2] /Index [0 6]`, 6 entries decoded correctly
- Type-2 test: a type-2 entry routes through ObjStm and dereferences successfully
- Multi-subsection test: `/Index [0 3 100 2]` produces entries at obj 0,1,2 and 100,101
- Predictor test: xref stream with FlateDecode + PNG Up predictor decoded correctly (Phase 1.5 handles predictor)
- Field-width edge case: `/W [1 4 0]` (generation always 0) parses
- proptest: random byte sequences fed to parse_xref_stream never panic
- INV-8 maintained

## References

- Plan section: Phase 1.3 line 1089 (xref streams)
- PDF spec 7.5.8 (Cross-Reference Streams)
- Phase 1.5 (FlateDecode + predictors)
- Phase 1.2 (ObjStm resolution for type-2 entries)
issue.title: Implement xref stream parser (PDF 1.5+, /W field widths, type 0/1/2 entries)

Every other Phase 6 sub-phase (NDJSON, PyO3, HTTP, Markdown, multi-output, MCP, receipts, cache, doctor) reads from or writes to this schema. Errors here cascade everywhere. issue.close_reason: PDF name object lexer already fully implemented. All 23 name tests pass including critical tests for #20 hex expansion, #00 NUL rejection, 127-byte raw length limit. Verification note at notes/pdftract-5dng.md. Commit 951bf9a.
issue.description:
## Scope

Lex name object tokens of the form `/Name` from the byte slice. Produces `Token::Name(Vec<u8>)` of the decoded name bytes (NOT including the leading `/`). Handles:

- `#XX` hex escapes within names: `/Foo#20Bar` -> `Foo Bar` (the `#20` decodes to space)
- NUL byte rejection: `/Foo#00Bar` is INVALID per spec; emit `STRUCT_INVALID_NAME` and reject (return Token::Name of bytes truncated at the NUL)
- Length limit: names are at most 127 bytes per PDF spec 7.3.5. This length is measured on the RAW bytes in the file (BEFORE `#XX` expansion). If exceeded, truncate at 127 raw bytes and emit `STRUCT_INVALID_NAME`
- Termination: stops at any whitespace or delimiter (`( ) < > [ ] { } / %`)
- Empty name: `/` alone (followed by delimiter or EOF) -> Token::Name(b"") (legal per spec)

## Implementation guidance

- Entry: position immediately AFTER the leading `/`
- Maintain: `raw_consumed: usize` (raw bytes from input), `out: Vec<u8>` (decoded bytes)
- Loop until whitespace, delimiter, or `raw_consumed >= 127`:
  - If byte is `#`: read next 2 bytes as hex; if both valid hex, decode and push; if invalid, emit `STRUCT_INVALID_NAME` and push the `#` as literal
  - Otherwise: push byte as-is to `out`; `raw_consumed += 1`
- Post-loop check: if any byte in `out` is `0x00`, emit `STRUCT_INVALID_NAME` and truncate `out` at the NUL
- If `raw_consumed >= 127`: emit `STRUCT_INVALID_NAME` (length exceeded), truncate `out` at 127 raw bytes

## Critical considerations

- Critical test from plan: `#20` -> space (0x20). Verify hex digits map correctly
- Critical test from plan: `#00` is rejected (NUL in name is invalid per spec); emit diagnostic
- Critical test from plan: name length limit 127 bytes applied to RAW byte count BEFORE `#XX` expansion. A name like `/AAA...AAA#41` (124 A's + `#41`) = 127 raw bytes => valid (the `#41` IS counted as 3 raw bytes, expanding to `A` post-decode -> 125 decoded bytes). A name with 128 raw bytes is truncated AT 127 raw and may end mid-`#XX` sequence; the truncation must NOT leave a half-decoded escape (i.e. if the 127th byte is `#`, truncate to 126 to keep the name well-formed)
- The `#` followed by invalid hex (e.g. `#GZ`) emits `STRUCT_INVALID_NAME` and treats the `#` as literal text. The `G` and `Z` then go on to be processed normally (likely terminating the name if delimiter; not here, so kept as literals)
- Names ARE case-sensitive per PDF spec; do not lowercase
- Spec 7.3.5 says names should be PDFDocEncoded (Latin-1 subset) but in practice any bytes appear. pdftract preserves bytes verbatim and lets the consumer decide. Phase 1.4 outline parser converts to UTF-8 when known to be a textual name
- The empty name `/` alone IS legal per spec; do not emit a diagnostic. Token::Name(b"") is fine

## Acceptance criteria

- All Critical tests pass:
  - `/Foo` -> `Token::Name(b"Foo")`
  - `/Foo#20Bar` -> `Token::Name(b"Foo Bar")` (space inserted)
  - `/Foo#00Bar` -> `Token::Name(b"Foo")` + `STRUCT_INVALID_NAME` diagnostic
  - `/AAA...AAA` (128 A's) -> `Token::Name(b"AAA...AAA")` (127 A's) + `STRUCT_INVALID_NAME`
  - `/` (alone, followed by whitespace) -> `Token::Name(b"")` (no diagnostic)
  - `/#23#23` -> `Token::Name(b"##")` (decodes to two `#` characters)
  - `/Foo#GZ` -> `Token::Name(b"Foo#GZ")` (G/Z are not hex; `#` kept literally) + `STRUCT_INVALID_NAME`
- proptest property: random byte sequences starting with `/` never panic and produce a Token::Name <= 127 raw bytes
- INV-8 maintained

## References

- Plan section: Phase 1.1 Lexer, line 1033 (Name objects, #XX hex escape, NUL rejection, 127-byte length); line 1046-1050 (critical tests for #20 / #00 / name length)
- PDF spec 7.3.5 (Name Objects)
issue.title: Implement PDF name object lexer with #XX hex expansion, NUL rejection, 127-byte length limit

issue.description:
## Scope

Extract embedded files from PDF portfolios and the /EmbeddedFiles name tree. Locate the name tree in /Catalog /Names /EmbeddedFiles; walk its leaves yielding Filespec dictionaries; decode the EF stream; emit an attachments array at document level with filename, description, mime type hint, size, creation/mod dates, checksum, and base64-encoded data. Apply a 50 MB size limit: beyond that, emit metadata only with data: null and truncated: true. Check /Collection in catalog for portfolio navigator metadata (schema + sort fields).

## Why this matters

PDF portfolios (introduced PDF 1.7, used heavily by legal document bundles and Acrobat collections) wrap multiple attached files inside a single PDF; without portfolio extraction, the wrapper is the only thing pdftract sees and the actual content is missed. /EmbeddedFiles also handles XML attachments to invoices (ZUGFeRD, Factur-X) and source files attached to scientific papers. The 50 MB limit prevents accidental gigabyte-base64-blob attacks on the JSON output.

## Implementation guidance

- Crates: none beyond Phase 1 parser + Phase 1 stream decoder
- Locate /EmbeddedFiles via document catalog: /Catalog /Names /EmbeddedFiles (name tree); also fall back to /Catalog /AF (associated files array, PDF 2.0)
- Walk the name tree (PDF 1.7 7.9.6) - same code as 7.1.3 ParentTree number tree walker, but for Names tree (keyed by PdfString, not integer)
- Each leaf is a /Filespec dict (/Type /Filespec optional): extract /F (system-independent filename), /UF (Unicode filename, prefer when present), /Desc (description), /EF (embedded file ref dict)
- /EF /F is the indirect ref to the file stream itself; decode via Phase 1 stream pipeline (apply all filters)
- From the stream dict, extract /Subtype (MIME type hint as Name, e.g. "image/png"), /Params dict containing /Size, /CreationDate, /ModDate, /CheckSum (16-byte MD5)
- Size limit: if decoded_size > 50 * 1024 * 1024, set data: null and truncated: true; ALWAYS emit metadata regardless
- base64 encoding: standard alphabet (RFC 4648), no line breaks, padding NOT omitted (data must be re-decodeable round-trip)
- Portfolio /Collection: if catalog /Collection exists, extract /Schema (field definitions) and /Sort (sort order) for richer portfolio metadata

## Critical considerations

- 50 MB threshold is on DECODED size, not encoded; check after stream decode but before base64
- base64 encoding rules: standard alphabet, padding present - JSON Schema declares contentEncoding: base64 which mandates standard
- Filename precedence: /UF > /F (PDF 1.7 7.11.2); /UF is UTF-8 / UTF-16 capable
- /CheckSum is raw 16-byte MD5 (binary); emit as lowercase hex string in output
- /CreationDate and /ModDate are PDF date format D:YYYYMMDDHHmmSSOHH'mm - parse to ISO 8601 (reuse 7.3.2 parser)
- Portfolio navigator metadata is informational; missing /Collection is normal for plain EmbeddedFiles
- Encrypted streams: skip with diagnostic if encryption is unrecoverable
- PyO3 binding: data is bytes (PyO3 converts from base64 automatically); other sinks emit raw base64 string
- CLI --text mode: attachments NOT included (per plan); only JSON sink emits them

## Acceptance criteria

- All Phase 7.5 child task beads closed
- Critical test (from plan): PDF with 3 embedded files of different MIME types - all extracted with correct filenames and sizes
- Critical test: attachment with no /Desc - description: null (not empty string)
- Critical test: attachment exceeding 50 MB - metadata present, data: null, truncated: true
- Output: attachments: Vec<Attachment> at document level per docs/schema/v1.0/pdftract.schema.json
- JSON Schema attachment.data: { type: string, contentEncoding: base64 } when non-null
- Round-trip test: base64-encoded data decodes back to byte-identical content

## References

- Plan section: 7.5 Portfolio and Attachments (lines 2629-2651)
- docs/schema/v1.0/pdftract.schema.json (attachments shape)
- PDF 1.7 spec 7.11 (File Specifications), 7.9.6 (Name Trees), 12.3.5 (Collections)
- Phase 1 stream decoder (decompression)
- 7.3.2 PDF date parser (reused for CreationDate/ModDate)

## Scope

Frontend interactive features: (a) Hover any span -> tooltip box appears within 50 ms showing text/font/confidence/bbox/block ref/MCID/reading-idx. (b) Click a span -> right-hand JSON-tree panel scrolls to the corresponding node and highlights it. (c) Top-bar search input -> filters spans whose text matches; matched spans get bright outline; Enter cycles through matches.

## Why this matters

These are the moment-to-moment debugging interactions. Hover lookups answer "what does pdftract think THIS glyph is?" in one mouse motion. Clicking jumps to the underlying JSON for full inspection. Search filter narrows down to the spans of interest on a 1000-span page. Without these, the overlays are pretty but not actionable.

## Implementation guidance

- Tooltip: single <div id="tooltip"> in HTML, positioned absolute, initially hidden
  - On mouseenter span (selector .layer-spans rect, .layer-confidence-heatmap rect): read data-* attrs; populate tooltip body; position at cursor + (8, 8); show

- 50 ms acceptance criterion is fast - no setTimeout; CSS transition-duration 0; data already in DOM
- Search filter is in-browser (no /api/search round trip needed) for instant feedback; /api/search exists as backup for very large pages
- JSON tree should be lazy-rendered for huge pages (1000+ spans) - render visible portion only; expand on user demand
- Highlight color on span click: yellow background, 2s linger; CSS class .highlighted with animation
- Search match Enter cycle: store currentMatchIndex; on Enter, increment and scroll into view smoothly
- Escape from search input: clear filter, focus back on canvas

issue.close_reason: Type3 font loader implemented in commit ece0442. All acceptance criteria PASS: FontMatrix scaling (0.001 vs 1.0), missing Widths defaults to all-zero, out-of-range codes return 0. 13 unit tests pass. Verification note in notes/pdftract-5f92.md.
issue.description:
## Scope

Implement `load_type3(font_dict)` returning a `Type3Font` struct populated with: `/CharProcs` (HashMap<Arc<str>, ContentStreamRef> from glyph name to content stream object number), `/FirstChar`, `/LastChar`, `/Widths` array (per-code advance widths in glyph space), `/FontMatrix` 3x3 transform applied during execution, `/Resources` (form XObject / font deps for nested execution), and `/Encoding` for code -> glyph name.

## Why this matters

Type 3 is structurally unlike every other font subtype — there is no font program, no glyph table, no cmap. The "font" is a dictionary of named content streams plus a code-to-name encoding map. Without this loader nothing downstream can render or recognize Type 3 glyphs.

## Implementation guidance

- `/CharProcs`: dictionary of glyph name -> stream object reference. Build a `HashMap<Arc<str>, ObjectId>`; lazy-fetch the stream bytes on first rasterization (cache thereafter).
- `/Widths` length should equal `LastChar - FirstChar + 1`. Validate; on mismatch emit `TYPE3_WIDTHS_LENGTH_MISMATCH` diagnostic and clamp.
- `/FontMatrix`: 6-element array `[a b c d e f]` representing the 2D affine; default `[0.001 0 0 0.001 0 0]` if absent. Store as a `Matrix3x3` for uniform handling with the rest of the graphics state.
- `/Resources`: optional; defaults to the page's resource dictionary if absent. Important for form XObject lookups inside glyph streams.
- `/Encoding`: same handling as for Type 1 (named encoding + Differences). Pass through to the Phase 2.2 resolver chain.

## Critical considerations

- INV: advance width for code C = `Widths[C - FirstChar] * FontMatrix[0]` (assuming standard FontMatrix); apply FontMatrix to scale glyph-space widths to text-space units.
- Glyph stream resolution: a content stream may start with `d0 wx wy` (set width, no painting) or `d1 wx wy llx lly urx ury` (set width + bbox, paint). The PARSED advance from these operators MAY differ from `/Widths`; per spec `/Widths` wins. Do not parse d0/d1 for width.
- A Type 3 font with no `/CharProcs` is malformed but seen in the wild — treat as zero-glyph font, return Type3Font with empty char_procs map; all lookups return None.
- Glyph names in CharProcs may be arbitrary user strings — do not assume they are AGL names.

## Acceptance criteria

- Valid Type 3 font loads with all fields populated.
- `/FontMatrix [0.001 0 0 0.001 0 0]`: advance for code with width 500 -> 0.5 text-units.
- `/FontMatrix [1 0 0 1 0 0]` (the Type 3 default): same width 500 -> 500 text-units (different scale).
- Missing `/Widths` defaults to all-zero with diagnostic.
- Code outside [FirstChar, LastChar] returns advance 0 with no panic.

## References

- Plan section: Phase 2.4 Pipeline + Metrics paragraphs (lines 1402-1408)
- Critical test: /FontMatrix [0.001 0 0 0.001 0 0] scaling (line 1414)
issue.title: Type 3 font loader (/CharProcs, /Widths, /FontMatrix)

issue.description:
## Scope

Coordinator for sub-phase 4.1: group consecutive glyphs into `Span` structs (text, bbox-union, font, size, color, rendering_mode, confidence, confidence_source, lang, flags bitmask). A new span begins when ANY of the 5 triggers fires: font_name change, font_size delta > 0.5pt, rendering_mode change, fill_color change (after RGB normalization, spot colors distinct), or is_word_boundary on current glyph.

## Why this matters

Spans are the granular unit of style and content for everything downstream — line formation reads spans, block formation reads lines of spans, markdown output emits per-span style tags. Wrong span boundaries collapse styled text into single runs (losing bold/italic boundaries) OR explode every glyph into its own span (destroying line layout). The 5-trigger rule is the calibrated middle ground.

## Children

- Span struct definition (10 fields per plan)
- 5-trigger break detector (font_name, font_size, rendering_mode, fill_color, is_word_boundary)
- Span flag detector (bold, italic, smallcaps, subscript, superscript bitmask)
- ConfidenceSource enum + UnicodeSource -> ConfidenceSource mapping
- Span text assembly (word boundary -> space, ligature expansion preserved)

## Critical considerations

- INV: span text is HUMAN-READABLE Unicode (post-ligature-expansion, post-word-boundary-injection); bbox is UNION of all member glyph bboxes (min x0/y0, max x1/y1).
- font_size delta threshold is 0.5pt (per plan), NOT exact equality — small rounding differences in scaled forms otherwise spuriously break spans.
- fill_color comparison is on RGB-NORMALIZED values; DeviceGray(0.5) and DeviceRGB([0.5,0.5,0.5]) are SAME color and DO NOT trigger a break.
- Spot colors are distinct from each other AND from RGB values (even if same final hex) per plan.
- is_word_boundary: implementation choice between (a) append space to previous span's text, OR (b) emit a synthetic 1-char " " span. Plan says either is valid; must round-trip to correct plain text.
- confidence is the MINIMUM glyph confidence within the span (worst-case per span).

## Acceptance criteria

- All 5 children closed.
- Mixed bold/regular run in one text object: span break at font change.
- Color change mid-line: span break.
- Word boundary glyph: produces either (a) trailing space in prev span OR (b) separate space-span.
- Subscript run (text_rise -3pt with font_size 12): SubScript flag set, SuperScript flag NOT set.
- font_size delta of 0.3pt: NO span break (within tolerance).

## References

- Plan section: Phase 4.1 Glyph -> Span Merging (lines 1612-1659)
issue.title: Phase 4.1: Glyph to Span Merging (coordinator)

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement pdftract grep - a ripgrep-style folder regex search across PDFs that returns matches with page_index + bbox in PDF user-space coordinates. Single-pass parsing (no extract-to-disk-then-grep detour). Designed to be fast over folders of hundreds-to-thousands of PDFs without ever appearing hung. Subcommand: pdftract grep [OPTIONS] PATTERN [PATH...]. Flags mirror ripgrep (-r, -i, -E, -F, -w, -v, -l, -c, -j N, --json, --max-results, --quiet). Plus pdftract-specific flags: --highlight DIR (writes annotated PDFs), --progress (TTY default), --progress-json (machine-readable stderr events), --ocr (also OCR scanned pages). 50 MB/s throughput on 1000-PDF corpus, CI-gated; >= 2x pdfgrep, >= 3x pdftotext+ripgrep.

## Why this matters

Grep across folders of PDFs is one of the most common knowledge-work tasks (find every contract that mentions "indemnification", every invoice with "Acme Corp", every filing referencing a docket number). Existing tools force a two-step pipeline (pdftotext + ripgrep) that is slow, drops bbox information, and provides no progress feedback - users stare at silent terminals wondering if the job hung. pdftract grep is THE flagship "brilliant idea" feature: single-pass, bbox-aware, observable, with the option to write back annotated PDFs that highlight every match. The 50 MB/s throughput target and progress-bar contract are non-negotiable user experience requirements.

## Implementation guidance

- Feature flag: grep (gates regex, walkdir, indicatif crates); when off, the grep subcommand returns a "feature not compiled in" error at parse time
- Crates: regex 1.10 (~500 KB), walkdir 2 (~30 KB), indicatif 0.17 (~50 KB) - all gated behind grep
- Subcommand: pdftract grep PATTERN [PATH...]; argparse via clap; PATH defaults to "." with implicit recursion when path is a dir
- Path expansion: walkdir for dirs (extension filter *.pdf); single-file paths processed directly; https:// URLs (when remote feature on) fetched via Phase 1 remote source
- Parallel pipeline: rayon thread pool sized by -j N (default num_cpus); per-file work item: parse + extract spans + apply regex
- Per-file pipeline: Phase 1 parse -> Phase 3 content streams -> Phase 4 span list (DO NOT run reading-order detection - spans are enough for grep)
- Per-span match: apply regex (or literal); for each match, emit Match { path, page_index, bbox, match_text, span_text, span_confidence, pdf_fingerprint, crosses_spans? }
- crosses_spans: true when a regex match crosses span boundaries (rare; after 4.7 readability correction joins spans); union bbox
- Default output format: "path:p<page>:bbox:<text>" human-readable; --json switches to JSON-Lines
- --highlight DIR: for each PDF, after matches collected, append /Highlight annotations to /Annots arrays per page; write to DIR/<name>-highlighted.pdf
- Progress: indicatif bar; ticker at 100 ms; updates >= every 500 ms guaranteed (separate ticker thread keeps spinner alive on slow files)
- --progress-json: per-event JSON-Lines emitted to stderr (start, file_start, file_progress, file_done, done)
- Slow-file warning: per-file timer; if > 30s, emit warning to stderr including path + elapsed; continue processing
- Encrypted PDFs (no password): single per-file diagnostic; not counted as a match
- Non-PDF files in folders silently skipped (no diagnostic spam)
- Bench target: pdftract-grep-1000 in benches/; CI gates throughput >= 50 MB/s, >= 2x pdfgrep, >= 3x pdftotext+ripgrep

## Critical considerations

- MUST NEVER appear hung: progress bar updates >= 500 ms even when individual files are slow; ticker thread keeps spinner alive
- --highlight modifies /Annots only (adds /Highlight annotations) - original content stream untouched so output is a valid PDF readable in Acrobat/Preview/browsers
- Memory cap: peak RSS < 200 MB on 1000-file search (acceptance criterion)
- First-match latency < 100 ms on 1000-file corpus (worker producers; sink prints first match as soon as any worker reports one)
- JSON-Lines = one match per line; stable line termination (\n, never \r\n) for downstream pipes
- pdf_fingerprint: include the Phase 1 fingerprint so callers can dedupe across reruns
- regex defaults to LITERAL (-F is default); -E enables full regex per plan
- Binary size budget: default features rise from 4 MB to 4.6 MB to accommodate grep; documented as approved Weight Targets allocation
- Recommended for pdftract:full Docker image + pdftract-full GitHub Release binary
- Subcommand-level concurrency: file-level rayon parallel; within a file, parsing is serial (Phase 1 not parallel-safe per design)

## Acceptance criteria

- All Phase 7.8 child task beads closed
- CI-gated throughput: >= 50 MB/s on 1000-PDF corpus (4-core CI machine)
- First-match latency: < 100 ms of process start on 1000-PDF corpus
- Memory: peak RSS < 200 MB during 1000-file search
- Annotated output: every JSON match present as /Highlight annotation in --highlight DIR/<name>-highlighted.pdf
- Progress bar updates >= every 500 ms even when files are slow
- Non-PDF files in folders silently skipped
- Encrypted PDFs skipped with one per-file diagnostic; not counted as match
- All ripgrep-style flags work as documented in the plan options table
- --progress-json emits all expected event types in order
- 5 GB PDF middle-of-folder: slow-file warning at 30s; processing continues
- Critical tests from plan all pass

## References

- Plan section: 7.8 pdftract grep (lines 2698-2806)
- Plan Weight Targets table (binary size allocation)
- INV: --highlight non-destructive
- 7.6 annotation extractor (Highlight annotation format reference)
- Phase 0 CI bench infrastructure (pdftract-grep-1000 target)
- Phase 1 remote source (https:// URL support)

Code compiles successfully. Verification note at notes/pdftract-5izq5.md. Commits: 7971a0f.
issue.description:
## Scope

Wire the NDJSON streaming pipeline end-to-end: emit HeaderFrame to BufWriter<io::Stdout> (128 KB buffer), spawn a rayon-fed extraction job, output thread pulls from OutOfOrderBuffer (6.2.2) emitting PageFrames in order, after producer.finish() emit FooterFrame. Also wires the --stream / ExtractionOptions.streaming = true entry point + the header/footer-detection deferred-window logic for streaming mode.

## Why this matters

The pipeline orchestration is where the parts come together. It also owns the streaming-mode contract: NDJSON consumers see frames as soon as pages are ready (low first-byte latency) and the whole document never sits in memory. Header/footer detection's deferred-3-page-window logic is documented here so users know to use non-streaming when exact kind: header/footer is mandatory.

## Implementation guidance

- Module: pdftract-core/src/output/ndjson/pipeline.rs
- Entry: fn extract_streaming<W: Write>(pdf_source, opts, writer: &mut W) -> Result<()>
- BufWriter wraps the writer with 128 KB capacity
- Step 1: parse document metadata; write HeaderFrame
- Step 2: spawn rayon job over pages; each worker computes Page and calls buffer.push
- Step 3: output thread loop: buffer.pop_next_in_order -> write_frame -> repeat until None
- Step 4: after producer.finish() and pop loop exits: aggregate ExtractionQuality + collect Diagnostics -> write FooterFrame
- Header/footer block detection in streaming mode: maintain sliding window of last 4 emitted pages; identify header/footer blocks if matched across window (4.4 logic); for the first 3 pages, emit blocks with kind: paragraph (no retroactive correction)
- CLI: pdftract extract --stream file.pdf

## Critical considerations

- Header/footer in streaming mode is approximate: first 3 pages NOT retroactively corrected (per plan line 2044)
- Document the streaming-mode limitation in CLI help text and JSON Schema description for kind
- Aggregate ExtractionQuality (mean_confidence) computed incrementally as pages stream, NOT held in memory
- Errors emitted by any rayon worker are sent to a Mutex<Vec<Diagnostic>> consumed in footer
- 128 KB BufWriter capacity: large enough that one page (typical ~10 KB) doesn't trigger a flush at every write
- Streaming mode is INCOMPATIBLE with cache (6.9) — disable cache lookup when streaming

## Acceptance criteria

- Critical test: 100-page document via --stream -> exactly 102 newline-delimited JSON objects in correct order
- Memory profile: 100-page streaming extraction holds < 2x peak memory of a 5-page extraction (proves no full-document buffering)
- First-byte latency: time from extract start to first byte of HeaderFrame < 200 ms on a 100-page document
- Streaming mode + cache: cache lookup skipped; cache population still happens (6.9 contract)

## References

- Plan section: Phase 6.2 frame sequence + BufWriter (lines 2038-2046)
- Phase 4.4 header/footer dedup (downstream of streaming)
- Phase 6.9 cache interaction

issue.description:
## Scope

Author tests/security/TH-08-log-audit.rs that runs pdftract extract with RUST_LOG=pdftract=trace over tests/fixtures/security/sensitive.pdf -- a PDF containing known-distinctive strings (a specific password value, a unique passphrase in the body text, a recognizable bearer-style token) -- and asserts that the captured log buffer (stdout + stderr combined) contains NONE of the known-sensitive substrings.

## Why this matters

TH-08 (line 879) is the regression-prevention test for the NEVER-log policy (lines 949-954). Any future contributor who tracing::debug!s an ExtractionOptions or a request body could trivially leak the password to logs; this test catches that the next time CI runs. It is the executable assertion that the secrecy crate wrapping (separate bead) is correctly applied at every call site.

## Implementation guidance

- Test file: tests/security/TH-08-log-audit.rs
- Fixture: tests/fixtures/security/sensitive.pdf
  - Body text contains the unmistakable substring "UNIQUE-MARKER-IN-BODY-TEXT-7f9a"
  - Password-protected (password value: "UNIQUE-PASSWORD-FOR-TH08-7f9a")
  - PROVENANCE.md: synthetic, public-domain
- Test cases:
  1. Run pdftract extract --password-stdin sensitive.pdf with RUST_LOG=pdftract=trace; capture stdout + stderr into a buffer; assert:
     - Buffer does NOT contain "UNIQUE-PASSWORD-FOR-TH08-7f9a"
     - Buffer does NOT contain "UNIQUE-MARKER-IN-BODY-TEXT-7f9a"
     - Buffer DOES contain (because we want trace to actually be on) substrings like "extract" or "page_count" -- to confirm trace IS active
  2. Same as case 1 but with --debug enabled: same assertion (no leak)
  3. Run pdftract mcp --stdio with PDFTRACT_MCP_TOKEN="UNIQUE-TOKEN-FOR-TH08-7f9a" and send an extract request via the stdio channel; capture stderr; assert the token value never appears
  4. Audit-log fixture: run pdftract serve --audit-log /tmp/audit.log and submit a request; assert /tmp/audit.log contains fingerprint and ts fields but NOT the path or the password or extracted text
- The capture mechanism: spawn pdftract as a child process; capture stdout and stderr via pipes; concatenate into one buffer; search

## Critical considerations

- The unique markers must be sufficiently distinctive that an incidental substring match in unrelated log content is extremely unlikely (7-char-suffix-hex is fine)
- The test MUST run at TRACE level (the highest verbosity) -- a leak that only triggers at TRACE is still a leak
- The test buffer search MUST be substring-based, not line-based -- a partial match (the password appearing as part of a longer string) is still a leak
- A regression class to specifically watch for: Debug-printing an ExtractionOptions; tracing::debug!("?opts" syntax that prints the struct); any tracing of HTTP request headers (Authorization or Cookie); any tracing of the raw PDF stream
- The test SHOULD spread its assertion across multiple subcommands (extract / mcp / serve / inspect) -- a leak in only one path is still a leak
- For the audit-log case, the diagnostic-codes field is allowed but extracted text content is forbidden; the test asserts the specific markers are absent

## Acceptance criteria

- tests/security/TH-08-log-audit.rs exists and passes
- Fixture tests/fixtures/security/sensitive.pdf committed with documented unique markers and password
- All 4 test cases pass
- Test runs at TRACE level
- Substring search across stdout + stderr + audit log

## References

- Plan: lines 879 (TH-08 entry), 931-964 (Audit Logging section), 949-954 (NEVER-log list); depends on pdftract-4em4l (audit-log hardening bead)
issue.title: TH-08 test: log audit (RUST_LOG=trace; no sensitive substring leaks)

issue.description:
## Scope

Introduce the secrecy crate as a workspace dependency and wrap every in-memory secret-holding value in secrecy::SecretString (or SecretBox where appropriate): PDF passwords, MCP bearer tokens, inspector tokens, and the password component of HTTP basic-auth on remote fetches. Replace any String typed field that holds a secret with SecretString and remove all Debug derives that would print them.

## Why this matters

A single accidental tracing::debug!("opts: {opts:?}") that prints a struct holding a String password leaks the secret to logs forever. secrecy::SecretString prevents that at the type level by implementing a Debug that prints REDACTED and by forcing explicit .expose_secret() at the call sites that legitimately read the value. Line 921 in the plan explicitly mandates this: "The token value is held in a secrecy::SecretString to prevent accidental Debug print." Without this wrapper TH-08 (log audit) cannot be passed reliably -- any future code path could trivially regress.

## Implementation guidance

- Crate to add: secrecy at the latest stable major version, behind a workspace dependency entry in Cargo.toml (not feature-gated -- always on)
- Types to wrap (rg the workspace for String holding secrets):
  - pdftract-core ExtractionOptions.password (currently Option<String>) -> Option<SecretString>
  - pdftract-mcp authentication state (token field) -> SecretString
  - pdftract-inspector launch state (single-use token) -> SecretString
  - pdftract-remote HTTP fetch URL credential component -> SecretString (urlencoded; stripped from logs)
  - pdftract-serve form-field deserialization for password -> SecretString via a custom serde Deserialize
- Derive policy: structs that hold any SecretString MUST NOT #[derive(Debug)]; provide a manual Debug impl that prints REDACTED for the secret fields and the actual values for non-secret fields
- Helper: a SecretFingerprint wrapper that exposes a SHA-256-based fingerprint for use in audit logs (so the log can correlate without exposing the value)
- Call-site discipline: .expose_secret() is the ONLY legitimate read accessor; rg in CI fails the build if it appears outside of: pdf decryptor, auth header constructor, basic-auth header builder

## Critical considerations

- secrecy::SecretString cannot be serialized via serde by default -- a custom Serialize that yields REDACTED MUST be provided so that ExtractionOptions can still be serialized for diagnostics archives without leaking
- A workspace-wide clippy lint must reject manual Debug derives on structs that hold SecretString (custom lint or a CI grep guard)
- The remote-fetch URL handling is tricky: the URL is conceptually one value but the password component is a secret -- the wrapper SHOULD parse the URL once, separate the password into a SecretString, and keep a sanitized URL representation for logging
- PyO3 binding: Python users pass password= as a Python str -- the PyO3 conversion MUST land directly in SecretString without ever materializing an intermediate Rust String in a Debug-printed struct
- Test: ensure that printing an ExtractionOptions via Debug never leaks the password; add a doctest that asserts this

## Acceptance criteria

- secrecy crate is a workspace dependency
- All listed secret-holding fields are SecretString-wrapped
- No struct holding a SecretString derives Debug; manual Debug impls in place where needed
- Custom clippy lint or CI grep rejects unauthorised .expose_secret() call sites
- Doctest in pdftract-core demonstrates that Debug-print of ExtractionOptions never includes the password value
- TH-08 log audit test (separate bead) passes once this lands

## References

- Plan: line 921 (token in SecretString), Secrets Handling section (lines 897-929), TH-08 (line 879)

## Scope

Implement the --json output sink: one MatchEvent serialised per line to stdout. JSON shape per plan: { path, page_index, bbox, match_text, span_text, span_confidence, pdf_fingerprint, crosses_spans? }. page_index is 0-based in JSON (machine convention; the human format flips to 1-based). Honor -l/-c (still emit JSON shapes: { path } / { path, count }) when those flags are set with --json.

## Why this matters

JSON-Lines is the format that downstream tools want: jq parseable, one row per match, no streaming-JSON-array gotchas. The shape exposes everything pdftract knows about each match (bbox + confidence + fingerprint) so analytics pipelines can dedupe by fingerprint across runs, weight by confidence, or render the bbox directly.

## Implementation guidance

- Crate: serde_json (already in Phase 6.1)
- Per MatchEvent, serialize { path: String, page_index: u32, bbox: [f32; 4], match_text: String, span_text: String, span_confidence: f32, pdf_fingerprint: String, crosses_spans?: bool (omit when false) }
- crosses_spans serde: skip_serializing_if = "is_false"
- Line termination: \n (LF only, never \r\n) per JSON-Lines convention
- Numeric serialization: bbox values with 4 fractional digits (preserve precision; JSON doesn't lose float info but be explicit)
- -l + --json: emit { "path": "..." } per unique file, deduplicate
- -c + --json: emit { "path": "...", "count": N } per file on FileDone
- Path field: same as text sink - relative if user input was relative
- pdf_fingerprint: format "pdftract-v1:<hex>" per Phase 1.7 fingerprint scheme
- Line-buffered writes via stdout().lock() + writeln!; flush after each line
- --json forces --no-progress unless --progress-json explicitly set (avoid mixing progress chars into stdout)

## Critical considerations

- page_index is 0-based in JSON (machine), 1-based in human text output (per design)
- JSON-Lines := one JSON object per line, separated by single \n, no enclosing array
- crosses_spans omitted when false to keep typical line short; clients should default to false
- Schema documentation: add a small spec for the JSON-Lines shape under docs/schema/v1.0/grep-jsonl.schema.json (separate from main extraction schema)
- --quiet + --json: --quiet wins; suppress stdout
- Serialization of NaN / Infinity in span_confidence: serde_json errors by default; replace with null

## Acceptance criteria

- Critical test (from plan): regex match emits one JSON-Lines record per match with all fields present
- crosses_spans omitted when false
- -l + --json emits one record per unique file
- -c + --json emits one record per file with count
- jq-parseable output (integration test pipes through jq -r .path)
- page_index 0-based in JSON
- pdf_fingerprint present and formatted "pdftract-v1:<hex>"

## References

- Plan section: 7.8 line 2724 (--json flag), 2742 (JSON shape sample)
- 7.8.4 (MatchEvent source)
- 7.8.5 (text sink alternative)
- Phase 1.7 fingerprint scheme
- docs/schema/v1.0/grep-jsonl.schema.json (new schema file)

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the `pdftract-swift` Swift Package Manager package as a subprocess-based SDK. Spawn the bundled `pdftract` binary via Foundation's `Process`, parse JSON output via `JSONDecoder`, expose the 9 contract methods as async functions returning `Document`, `Page`, etc. Linux + macOS only (server-side use; explicitly NOT iOS due to Apple's process-spawn restrictions). Publishing is git-tag-based to `github.com/jedarden/pdftract-swift`. Deferred to v1.1+ release wave.

## Why this matters

Server-side Swift is growing in the macOS-native dev community (Vapor framework, Apple's swift-distributed-actors). The iOS exclusion is a known platform limitation — Apple does not permit spawning arbitrary subprocess in App Store apps; users wanting iOS support should call `pdftract serve` over HTTP from the iOS client and let the server-side Swift code handle the subprocess. Honouring the SDK contract across all 10 languages includes Swift; v1.1+ deferral acknowledges the smaller user base.

## Implementation guidance

- Swift package name: `pdftract-swift`
- Repo: `github.com/jedarden/pdftract-swift` (separate repo; SPM is git-tag-based)
- Swift version floor: 5.10 (current stable channel)
- Platforms: `.macOS(.v13)`, `.linux` (iOS NOT supported)
- File layout (generator-driven; see Tera template scaffolding bead):
  - `Package.swift` (SPM manifest)
  - `Sources/Pdftract/Pdftract.swift` (main public API)
  - `Sources/Pdftract/Codegen/Methods.swift` (generated)
  - `Sources/Pdftract/Codegen/Errors.swift` (generated; 8 exception classes)
  - `Sources/Pdftract/Models/Document.swift`, `Page.swift`, etc. (Codable structs)
  - `Tests/PdftractTests/ConformanceTests.swift` (XCTest)
- Method signatures (Swift, async-first):
  - `public struct Pdftract { ... }`
  - `public func extract(source: Source, options: ExtractOptions = .init()) async throws -> Document`
  - `public func extractText(source: Source, options: ExtractOptions = .init()) async throws -> String`
  - `public func extractMarkdown(source: Source, options: ExtractOptions = .init()) async throws -> String`
  - `public func extractStream(source: Source, options: ExtractOptions = .init()) -> AsyncThrowingStream<Page, Error>`
  - `public func search(source: Source, pattern: String, options: SearchOptions = .init()) -> AsyncThrowingStream<Match, Error>`
  - `public func getMetadata(source: Source, options: ExtractOptions = .init()) async throws -> Metadata`
  - `public func hash(source: Source, options: HashOptions = .init()) async throws -> Fingerprint`
  - `public func classify(source: Source) async throws -> Classification`
  - `public func verifyReceipt(path: String, receipt: Receipt) async throws -> Bool`
- Source type: `public enum Source { case path(String); case url(URL); case bytes(Data) }`
- Option names use camelCase per Swift convention: CLI `--ocr-language` becomes `ocrLanguage`
- Errors: `public enum PdftractError: Error` with 8 cases mirroring the contract (Swift's `Error` protocol is the idiomatic root)
- AsyncThrowingStream for streaming: backed by the binary's NDJSON output; canceling the iteration kills the subprocess
- Document, Page, etc. as Codable structs

## Publishing

- Argo WorkflowTemplate file: `k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/pdftract-swift-publish.yaml` in `jedarden/declarative-config`
- Inputs: tag name; GitHub PAT from ESO Secret `github-pat-pdftract`
- Steps:
  1. `clone-sdk-repo`: `git clone https://github.com/jedarden/pdftract-swift.git --branch main`
  2. `sync-version`: update `Package.swift` (SPM does not require explicit version; the git tag IS the version)
  3. `conformance`: `swift test --filter ConformanceTests` (runs the shared suite; aborts on failure)
  4. `tag-and-push`: `git tag X.Y.Z && git push origin X.Y.Z` (SPM tag format is NUMERIC, no `v` prefix)
  5. `warm-spi`: post the tag to Swift Package Index (`https://swiftpackageindex.com/api/...`) to trigger indexing
- Container: `swift:5.10-jammy` (official Swift Linux image)

## Critical considerations

- ADR-009: runs on iad-ci with the GitHub PAT; never use GitHub Actions
- iOS is EXPLICITLY UNSUPPORTED — document in README. iOS users must use `pdftract serve` over HTTP from their Swift code
- SPM tag format does NOT use `v` prefix (NUMERIC only: `1.0.0`, not `v1.0.0`); the publish workflow MUST strip the `v` from the binary tag when creating the SPM tag
- Swift Package Index is the de-facto SPM registry; tagging triggers their auto-indexing
- The `Process` class on Linux requires a different launch-path API than macOS; abstract behind a thin internal helper that detects the OS at runtime
- Foundation on Linux is the swift-corelibs-foundation reimplementation; some Foundation APIs are subtly different from Apple's; test on Linux explicitly
- v1.1+ deferral means this bead does NOT block v1.0 release; priority is P3

## Acceptance criteria

- The `pdftract-swift` package is consumable via SPM (`.package(url: "https://github.com/jedarden/pdftract-swift.git", from: "X.Y.Z")`)
- All 9 contract methods exposed on Pdftract
- All 8 error cases on PdftractError
- `swift test` runs the conformance suite and 100% passes
- iOS is documented as unsupported; macOS and Linux are supported
- A tag push triggers Swift Package Index indexing
- AsyncThrowingStream cancellation terminates the subprocess

## References

- Plan section: SDK Architecture / The Ten SDKs, line 3480 (Swift subprocess via Process + JSONDecoder; Linux + macOS only; v1.1+)
- Plan section: SDK Architecture / Per-SDK Release Channels, line 3577 (git tag on pdftract-swift; SPM is git-tag-based)
- Plan section: SDK Acceptance Criteria, lines 3581-3589
- Sibling: SDK contract, conformance suite, code generator
- Swift Package Manager docs: https://www.swift.org/documentation/package-manager/

issue.description:
## Scope

Author tests/security/TH-03-mcp-no-auth.rs that spawns pdftract mcp --bind 0.0.0.0:0 with NO auth token configured and asserts that startup aborts immediately with exit code 78 and a stderr message naming --auth-token-file as the remediation. The companion case (--bind 127.0.0.1:0 with no token: succeeds) verifies the loopback exemption.

## Why this matters

TH-03 (line 874) is the canonical operator-misconfig protection. Without it, an operator who copy-pastes pdftract mcp --bind 0.0.0.0:PORT from a tutorial silently exposes an authenticated-tool surface to the entire network. The exit-78 contract is what kubelet readiness probes rely on to refuse to mark the pod ready when misconfigured.

## Implementation guidance

- Test file: tests/security/TH-03-mcp-no-auth.rs
- Test cases:
  1. Spawn pdftract mcp --bind 0.0.0.0:0 with no auth env vars set; assert process exits 78 within 5 seconds; assert stderr contains "auth-token" and "loopback"
  2. Spawn pdftract mcp --bind [::]:0 with no auth; same assertion
  3. Spawn pdftract mcp --bind 127.0.0.1:0 with no auth; assert process binds successfully (sleep 1s, then SIGTERM and verify it was running)
  4. Spawn pdftract mcp --bind [::1]:0 with no auth; same as case 3
  5. Spawn pdftract mcp --bind 0.0.0.0:0 with PDFTRACT_MCP_TOKEN=test-token-32-chars-min; assert process binds successfully
  6. Spawn pdftract mcp --bind 0.0.0.0:0 with --auth-token-file pointing at a temp file containing "test-token"; assert successful bind
  7. Spawn pdftract mcp --bind localhost:0 where localhost resolves to ONLY loopback: assert successful bind
  8. Spawn pdftract mcp --bind <hostname-that-resolves-mixed>:0: assert exit 78 (fail-closed when mixed)
- Use std::process::Command::spawn + child.wait_timeout (via wait-timeout crate) or a manual fd poll
- For each spawn, verify the listener never accepted a connection during the failure window by attempting a connect from a parallel thread

## Critical considerations

- The test MUST verify exit 78 specifically (not just non-zero) because exit-78 is what monitoring relies on
- The test MUST verify that no listener accepted connections during the failure window (otherwise the failure is non-atomic and the protection is real-world useless)
- Bind to :0 in the success cases (let the OS pick the port) to avoid port-collision flakiness in CI
- Case 7 (hostname resolving to ONLY loopback) requires either a hostfile or 127.0.0.1 directly; in CI without /etc/hosts control, use the direct loopback literal
- Case 8 is the trickiest: synthesize a hostname that resolves to mixed loopback + non-loopback addresses; on most CI runners this is impossible without /etc/hosts; document and #[ignore] if not feasible in the CI image
- Inspector (Phase 7.9) has parallel test; consider extracting common harness

## Acceptance criteria

- tests/security/TH-03-mcp-no-auth.rs exists and passes
- Cases 1-6 pass in CI
- Case 7 passes when /etc/hosts cooperates; case 8 #[ignore]d with explanation if CI cannot synthesize
- Verified: no listener accepted connections during the failure window
- Exit code 78 specifically asserted
- Stderr message contains "auth-token" and "loopback"

## References

- Plan: line 874 (TH-03 entry); depends on pdftract-59zz (Hardening: PDFTRACT_MCP_TOKEN + --auth-token-file + TH-03 enforcement)

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement a filesystem-backed content-addressed cache for extraction results, keyed by PDF fingerprint (Phase 1.7) + canonical-JSON SHA-256 of extraction options. On cache hit, return the zstd-decompressed cached JSON without re-running extraction (target: < 20 ms p99 on a 100-page PDF). On miss, run extraction and populate the cache for next time. Multi-process safe via atomic writes (temp + rename); no distributed lock.

This bead is the sub-phase coordinator that aggregates the child task beads:

- pdftract-XX: Filesystem layout (cache_dir/fp[0:2]/fp[2:4]/full_fp/opts_hash.json.zst)
- pdftract-XX: Cache key construction (fingerprint + canonical options JSON SHA-256)
- pdftract-XX: zstd compression encode/decode
- pdftract-XX: LRU eviction policy (default 1 GiB; touched-time via O_APPEND sentinel)
- pdftract-XX: Multi-process safety (atomic temp+rename writes; no distributed lock)
- pdftract-XX: pdftract cache subcommand (stats / clear / purge) + --cache-dir / --cache-size / --no-cache flags + X-Pdftract-Cache HTTP header

## Why this matters

Cache hits transform pdftract from a CPU-bound extraction service into a filesystem-bound lookup: 10,000 req/s sustained throughput on commodity SSD vs. 1-100 req/s for fresh extraction. The cache is the difference between pdftract scaling to handle a high-volume RAG ingest pipeline and being the bottleneck. Content-addressed keying (fingerprint + options hash) means the cache automatically invalidates on PDF edits AND on options changes (e.g. switching --ocr on/off) without manual cache busting.

The filesystem-only design avoids external dependencies (no Redis, no PostgreSQL); LRU eviction keeps disk usage bounded; zstd compression keeps the per-entry footprint small (a 100-page JSON typically compresses 5-10x). Multi-process safety is achieved by atomic temp+rename writes and tolerating duplicated work on first-miss races (two processes computing the same key both write; second write wins; no lock).

## Critical considerations

- Cache key MUST include the extraction_version. On binary upgrade, the canonical options JSON's serialization may change subtly (default value additions, field reorderings); including extraction_version in the canonicalization forces a clean cache miss on upgrade
- INV-6 (byte-identical re-extraction) underlies the cache contract: if the cache returns a value that does NOT match a fresh extraction of the same input + same options, the cache is BROKEN and must be invalidated for the entire fingerprint
- NDJSON streaming mode (Phase 6.2) does NOT serve responses from cache (caching defeats streaming's whole point) but DOES populate the cache when streaming completes to a non-error state
- Cache directory must be writable; cache misses on a non-writable cache_dir log a warning and proceed without caching (don't error the extraction)
- LRU touched-time updates use O_APPEND writes to a single sentinel file (no per-entry stat call); aggregator reads the sentinel during eviction sweeps
- Concurrent writers on the same key: both run extraction; both write to distinct temp files; both rename; second rename wins atomically. Wasted work is tolerated to avoid distributed-lock complexity
- HTTP serve mode adds X-Pdftract-Cache: hit | miss | skipped response header (per plan)
- JSON output adds metadata.cache_status: \"hit\" | \"miss\" | \"skipped\" and metadata.cache_age_seconds: N (when status is \"hit\")
- Corrupt entry on disk (truncated, zstd-decode-failure): treated as a miss; entry deleted; extraction re-runs

## Acceptance criteria

- All 6 child task beads closed
- Cache hit on 100-page PDF: result returned in < 20 ms p99 (plan acceptance criterion)
- 1000 concurrent cache hits: throughput > 10,000 req/s on commodity SSD (plan acceptance criterion)
- Cache survives process restart (filesystem-only state)
- --no-cache reverts to baseline extraction with zero overhead (cache code paths skipped entirely)
- Module under crates/pdftract-core/src/cache/ (layout.rs, key.rs, compression.rs, lru.rs, multi_process.rs) plus crates/pdftract-cli/src/cache_cmd.rs for the subcommand
- Feature flag cache (implicitly enabled by serve); adds zstd crate (~50 KB) only when active
- All 6 critical tests from plan section 6.9 pass

## References

- Plan section: Phase 6.9 Content-Addressed Cache Layer (lines 2419-2475)
- INV-6 (byte-identical re-extraction)
- Phase 1.7 fingerprint (used as cache key component)
- zstd crate: https://crates.io/crates/zstd
- Phase 6.4 HTTP serve (X-Pdftract-Cache header integration)
- Phase 6.2 NDJSON streaming (cache-population-but-no-cache-serve interaction)
- Phase 6.1 JSON schema (metadata.cache_status field)
Labels: cache, coordinator, performance, phase-6

## Scope

Produce the final output shape for tables: emit a Block with kind: "table" in the block list (per Phase 4.3 schema) AND a parallel Table object inside the page output's `tables` array per docs/schema/v1.0/pdftract.schema.json. The Table object contains rows (Vec<Row>), each Row contains cells (Vec<Cell>) with bbox, text, colspan, rowspan, is_header_row. Wire two-page-table detection to set continued/continued_from_prev flags.

## Why this matters

Without a stable output shape, downstream sinks (JSON, Markdown, MCP, PyO3) cannot render tables consistently. The dual emission (Block + Table object) lets the block list preserve reading order while the tables array gives random-access by index for tooling that wants rows-and-cells without parsing blocks.

## Implementation guidance

- Block emission: { id: "block_<n>", kind: "table", bbox, page_index, table_index: usize, reading_order_idx } - the table_index is the position in page.tables
- Table object: { id: "table_<n>", bbox: [x0,y0,x1,y1], rows: Vec<Row>, header_rows: u32, detection_method: "line_based" | "borderless", continued: bool, continued_from_prev: bool, page_index }
- Row: { bbox, cells: Vec<Cell>, is_header: bool }
- Cell: { bbox, text: String, spans: Vec<SpanRef>, row: usize, col: usize, rowspan: u32, colspan: u32, is_header_row: bool }
- Two-page table detection: if a GridCandidate on page N ends within 50 pt of page bottom AND a GridCandidate on page N+1 starts within 50 pt of page top with the same column count and similar col_xs (within 5 pt RMSE), set page N .continued = true and page N+1 .continued_from_prev = true
- Update docs/schema/v1.0/pdftract.schema.json to include the table object shape
- Add a test_v_1_0_table_schema_roundtrip test to schema validation suite

- Both pages flagged when continued; full cross-page reconstruction (joining rows) is DEFERRED to non-streaming mode per plan
- text field is the concatenated content of all spans in the cell, joined with " " - keep for downstream simplicity

issue.description:
## Scope

Cross-cutting error recovery for malformed PDF files. Per plan: never panic in library code (INV-8); every parse error continues with a sensible default + structured diagnostic.

The error-recovery layer is NOT a separate module — it's a set of contracts that EACH of Phase 1.1-1.5 must implement consistently. This sub-phase coordinates the consistency review, the cross-cutting diagnostic catalog, and the integration-level adversarial fixtures.

Strategies (per plan):
1. Truncated file at EOF: forward xref scan; any endobj before truncation = valid (delivered by Phase 1.3 forward-scan bead)
2. Corrupt xref entry (bad offset): attempt to parse at listed offset; if first bytes != `N G obj`, skip entry with diagnostic; do NOT remove from xref map (other objects may be valid)
3. Missing required dict key: return PdfNull, emit STRUCT_MISSING_KEY with object number; caller handles null gracefully
4. Integer overflow in object dimensions: clamp to i32::MAX and log; do not panic
5. Circular object reference: detected via per-thread resolution stack; return PdfNull with diagnostic (delivered by Phase 1.2 cycle-detection bead)

Child beads:
- Diagnostic code catalog + unified error/diagnostic types
- Integer overflow clamping helper + STRUCT_INTEGER_OVERFLOW emission audit across Phase 1
- Adversarial test corpus (combined-failure-mode PDFs) + integration assertion harness

## Why this matters

INV-8 (no panic at the public boundary of pdftract-core) is a HARD GATE — Phase 0.4 clippy lint enforces it at compile time. Phase 1.6 ensures the EMITTED diagnostics are consistent, complete, and useful for debugging. Without consistency, users see a mix of "STRUCT_INVALID_FOO" and "STRUCT_FOO_INVALID" diagnostics; the catalog enforces naming and message-template conventions.

The adversarial corpus is the integration-level test that exercises 1.1-1.5 simultaneously: a fixture with truncated file + corrupt xref entry + missing /MediaBox + integer overflow in /BBox + circular ref between two objects should produce a Document with sensible defaults and a Vec of N diagnostics, NOT a panic.

## Critical considerations

- Each Phase 1.1-1.5 child bead already emits its own diagnostics; Phase 1.6 is the AUDIT pass that ensures:
  - All diagnostic codes follow the catalog naming convention (STRUCT_*, STREAM_*, OCR_*, ENCRYPTION_*, REMOTE_*, PAGE_*, XREF_*)
  - Every diagnostic includes byte offset + (where applicable) object reference for debuggability
  - Every emit site has a corresponding test fixture
- The adversarial corpus is integration-level (combines failures across layers); per-layer fixtures live in their respective Phase 1.x test beads
- INV-8 enforcement: combine `cargo clippy -D clippy::unwrap_used -D clippy::expect_used` (Phase 0.4 lint, lib-code only) + `proptest_never_panics` (Phase 1.x property tests) + adversarial corpus integration tests
- Real-world malformations are RARELY single: a file truncated mid-stream often ALSO has a missing endobj, ALSO has integer overflow in /Length. The adversarial fixtures intentionally stack failures
- The diagnostic emit budget: a 100-page document with no malformations emits 0 diagnostics; a heavily-malformed document may emit 1000+; the output schema's `errors[]` array is unbounded but the CLI's default verbosity limits display to the first 100 (with "N more diagnostics omitted" tail)

## Acceptance criteria

- All 3 child beads closed
- All Critical tests from plan Section 1.6 pass:
  - File where 30% of xref entries point to wrong offsets: remaining 70% extracted correctly
  - Missing /MediaBox on every page: default letter size (612×792) used, diagnostic emitted per page
  - Object with endobj missing: parser reads to next N G obj pattern and continues
- INV-8 verified end-to-end: 0 panics across all adversarial fixtures + 10,000 proptest cases per parser module per PR (Phase 0.5)
- Diagnostic catalog documented in `crates/pdftract-core/src/diagnostics.rs` with a `///` doc-comment per variant explaining when it's emitted

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement parsing of the `/Differences` array on a font's `/Encoding` dictionary. The Differences array sparsely overlays glyph-name reassignments on top of a base named encoding. Format: `[n /Name1 /Name2 ... m /OtherName ...]` — a starting integer code followed by a sequence of glyph names assigned to consecutive codes; another integer resets the position.

## Why this matters

Many embedded fonts use the standard encoding indirection trick: declare BaseEncoding = WinAnsi (or omit it) and then override specific slots with custom glyph names via Differences. Without this overlay the encoding chain misses every overridden glyph.

## Implementation guidance

- Input: an `Object::Array` whose elements alternate `Integer` and `Name`. Walk linearly, maintaining a `cursor: u32` initialized from each integer encountered, incrementing after each name.
- Output: `pub struct DifferencesOverlay { entries: Vec<(u32, Arc<str>)> }` — sparse list of `(code, glyph_name)` overrides. Lookup is binary-search-on-code, but the array is usually < 32 entries so linear is fine.
- A combined `FontEncoding { base: Option<NamedEncoding>, differences: DifferencesOverlay }` exposes `glyph_name_for(code)`: differences first, base second.
- Default base when neither `/Encoding/BaseEncoding` nor `/Encoding` is present: StandardEncoding for Type1, the font's built-in encoding for TrueType (often MacRoman or WinAnsi).

## Critical considerations

- Glyph names in Differences may be arbitrary user names not in AGL — Level 2 returns None for those; resolver falls through to L3/L4.
- Multiple Differences blocks (multiple `Integer Names...` runs) in the same array — handle correctly.
- Some PDFs use `/Differences` without `/BaseEncoding` and the base encoding is implicit; document the fallback hierarchy in the bead.
- Integer codes can exceed 255 for single-byte encodings — clamp to u8 range or emit `ENCODING_DIFFERENCE_OUT_OF_RANGE` diagnostic.

## Acceptance criteria

- `[ 39 /quotesingle 96 /grave ]` parses to two entries: code 39 -> quotesingle, code 96 -> grave.
- `[ 39 /a /b /c ]` parses to three entries: 39 -> a, 40 -> b, 41 -> c.
- Lookup of overlaid code returns the override; lookup of non-overlaid code returns the base encoding entry.
- Unknown glyph name in difference returns Some (not None) so the resolver can attempt L3/L4 with the name.

## References

- Plan section: Phase 2.2 Level 2 (lines 1337)
- ISO 32000-1 sec 9.6.6.4

## Scope

Implement the xtask gen-schema binary at xtask/src/bin/gen_schema.rs that derives JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 from the Rust Output / Page / Span / Block / Diagnostic / Outline types via the schemars crate. Emits to docs/schema/v1.0/pdftract.schema.json with stable alphabetical key ordering.

## Why this matters

JSON Schema is the public contract for pdftract's output; downstream consumers (Python wheel users, HTTP API clients, MCP agents, LangChain/LlamaIndex integrations) validate JSON responses against it. Without an auto-generated schema, the contract drifts every time a Rust type changes; with auto-generation, the source of truth is the Rust types and the schema is always in sync.

## Implementation guidance

- xtask binary at xtask/src/bin/gen_schema.rs:
  ```rust
  fn main() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
      let mut schema = schemars::schema_for!(pdftract_core::Output);
      // Set $id, title, description, version
      schema.schema.metadata.as_mut().unwrap().id = Some(\"https://pdftract.com/schema/v1.0/pdftract.schema.json\".into());
      schema.schema.metadata.as_mut().unwrap().title = Some(\"pdftract Output v1.0\".into());
      // Sort keys alphabetically for stable diff
      let value = serde_json::to_value(&schema)?;
      let sorted = sort_keys_recursive(value);
      let pretty = serde_json::to_string_pretty(&sorted)?;
      std::fs::write(\"docs/schema/v1.0/pdftract.schema.json\", pretty)?;
      Ok(())
  }
  ```
- schemars derive on Output, Page, Span, Block, Diagnostic, Outline, OutlineNode, Annotations, Table, FormField, Attachment, Signature, etc. — every type that appears in the JSON output
- Schema includes $schema: https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema; $id: stable URL
- Enum properties (page_type, severity, confidence_source) enumerated explicitly via #[schemars(rename_all)] and explicit enum derive
- Phase 7 placeholder objects use sentinel empty schema (will be populated when Phase 7 lands)

## Critical considerations

- broken_vector MUST appear in page_type enum (5.1 + 6.1 requirement); cross-check after generation
- confidence_source enum: [\"native\", \"heuristic\", \"ocr\"] per sibling pdftract-1f8we
- Stable key ordering: use a recursive sort on the serde_json::Value tree before serialization; alphabetical key order in objects
- schemars version: schemars = \"1\" (stable); some derives require schemars-derive proc-macro
- Output types must derive JsonSchema; this is a cross-crate addition (every public type in pdftract-core's output module)
- The xtask binary is invoked via cargo xtask gen-schema (alias in .cargo/config.toml)
- Output path is committed to the repo (docs/schema/v1.0/pdftract.schema.json) so reviewers see schema diffs in PRs

## Acceptance criteria

- cargo xtask gen-schema regenerates docs/schema/v1.0/pdftract.schema.json
- Generated schema validates against JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 (lint via jsonschema::draft202012::is_valid)
- Generated schema's page_type enum contains broken_vector
- Generated schema's confidence_source enum contains native, heuristic, ocr
- Stable ordering: regenerating twice produces byte-identical output
- All Phase 7 placeholder types appear in $defs with sentinel empty schemas
- Schema $id is the stable URL https://pdftract.com/schema/v1.0/pdftract.schema.json

## References

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement `repair_hyphenation(block: &mut Block) -> u32` that detects, within a single block, lines ending with a hyphen at or near the column right edge (text ends with `-`, span bbox.x1 is within `0.05 * column_width` of column right) AND the next line in the same block starts with a lowercase letter (continuation). Joins: strip the trailing hyphen from line N's last span, prepend its truncated word to the first word of line N+1's first span. Returns count of repairs.

## Why this matters

Hyphenation is how typeset text wraps long words. Without repair, "hyphen-\nation" extracts as two separate strings "hyphen-" and "ation" (or worse, "hyphenation" stays split in dict lookup, lowering readability). Joining recovers the word AND lets dict coverage score it correctly.

## Implementation guidance

- Iterate consecutive line pairs within a block (do NOT join across blocks per plan).
- Check for hyphenation:
  - line[n].last_span.text ends with `-` (also `‐` U+2010 or `‑` U+2011 — non-breaking hyphen).
  - line[n].last_span.bbox[2] >= column_right_x - 0.05 * column_width (hyphen at right edge).
  - line[n+1].first_span.text starts with a LOWERCASE letter (continuation; uppercase = new sentence, not hyphenation).
  - line[n].last_span and line[n+1].first_span are in the same column.
- Repair:
  - Find the last word in line[n].last_span.text (split by whitespace, take last); strip the trailing hyphen.
  - Find the first word in line[n+1].first_span.text.
  - Join the two: `joined_word = stripped_last + first`.
  - Modify line[n].last_span.text: replace the hyphenated word with `joined_word + " "` (preserve trailing space).
  - Modify line[n+1].first_span.text: remove the first word.
  - If line[n+1].first_span becomes empty, remove it (the span); if line becomes empty, remove the line.
- Track repair count; return it (caller sets confidence_source = Heuristic if > 0).

## Critical considerations

- INV: do NOT join across blocks (paragraph boundary kills hyphenation).
- INV: capital-start of next line indicates NOT a continuation (e.g., "President Lincoln-\nMore on the war..."); do NOT join.
- Some legitimate hyphenated compound words (e.g., "self-described") should NOT be joined; but at line-end ambiguity persists. v0.1.0 errs on the side of joining (more common case is wrapping).
- Multi-line hyphenation chains (rare) are handled by iterative pair-wise repair.
- Strip the SOFT hyphen U+00AD too (sibling bead also handles, but here it's specifically the line-end case).
- Modifying span text MAY change bbox; recompute or accept slight drift (text doesn't grow horizontally — already wrapped).

## Acceptance criteria

- Two lines "Long hyphen-" + "ation continues" -> joined to "Long hyphenation continues" in line[n] text; line[n+1] starts at second word.
- Two lines "Long hyphen-" + "More text" (capital start) -> NOT joined.
- "Long-" at column right + next-line "ago" in same column: joined to "Longago".
- Lines in different columns: NOT joined.
- "Long-" not at column right edge (mid-line hyphen): NOT joined.

## References

- Plan section: Phase 4.7 Correction pipeline step 2 (line 1778)
- Critical test: "Hyphenated word spanning line break: joined correctly, hyphen stripped" (line 1791)
issue.title: Hyphenation repair (end-of-line hyphen + next line first word -> joined, hyphen stripped)

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the merge logic for hybrid PDF files. A hybrid file has BOTH:
- A traditional xref table at the location pointed to by `startxref`
- A supplementary xref stream pointed to by `/XRefStm offset` in the trailer dict

Per PDF spec, the traditional table is AUTHORITATIVE for the objects it covers; the stream's type-2 entries (compressed-in-ObjStm) fill gaps NOT covered by the traditional table.

This bead implements the merge: given both an `XrefSection` from the traditional parser and another from the stream parser, produce a single merged map with the correct priority semantics.

## Implementation guidance

- Public API: `merge_hybrid(traditional: XrefSection, stream: XrefSection) -> XrefSection`
- Algorithm:
  1. Start with the traditional section's entries
  2. For each entry in the stream section: if the same ObjRef is NOT in the traditional map, insert it; if it IS in the traditional map (even as type-1), traditional wins
  3. The merged trailer takes the traditional one (it's the authoritative entry point); /XRefStm key is dropped from the merged trailer
- Detect a hybrid file: traditional trailer dict has `/XRefStm <offset>` key. Without this key, the file is purely traditional (no stream involvement)

## Critical considerations

- Critical test from plan: hybrid file — traditional entries override stream entries for same object numbers
- The /XRefStm offset points at a separate indirect-object stream (not a chained /Prev); load it independently via Phase 1.3's xref stream parser
- A hybrid file's stream typically holds ONLY type-2 entries (the compressed-in-ObjStm objects that the traditional table cannot represent); type-1 entries in the stream are redundant
- Edge case: traditional table marks an object as Free, stream marks it as InUse. The plan's spec says traditional wins; the object is FREE per the merged map. Emit STRUCT_HYBRID_CONFLICT diagnostic so the user knows
- Edge case: traditional table is absent from `startxref` location entirely (the offset points to a stream); this is NOT a hybrid — it's a pure xref-stream file; the hybrid handler isn't invoked
- The /XRefStm key cascades through `/Prev`: if revision A has /XRefStm and /Prev pointing to revision B which also has /XRefStm, both streams are merged into their respective traditional tables before the /Prev chain merger combines them
- After the merge, the resulting XrefSection MUST be marked `is_hybrid: true` so the linearization detector (separate bead) knows to skip the linearization-specific path

## Acceptance criteria

- Critical test passes: hybrid fixture with overlapping object numbers — traditional entries win
- Hybrid fixture with stream-only type-2 entries: those entries are added to the merged map
- Free/InUse conflict test: STRUCT_HYBRID_CONFLICT diagnostic emitted
- Non-hybrid trailer (no /XRefStm): merge is not invoked; pure traditional path returned
- proptest: random combinations of traditional and stream sections never panic
- INV-8 maintained

## References

- Plan section: Phase 1.3 line 1090 (hybrid files); critical test on traditional priority
- PDF spec 7.5.8.4 (Hybrid-Reference Files)

issue.description:
## Scope

Author the conformance test runner pattern that every SDK implements. Each SDK ships a `pdftract-sdk-conformance` binary or test target that: loads `tests/sdk-conformance/cases.json`, iterates cases, invokes the SDK's native method with the case's options, compares the result against `expected` with tolerances, reports per-case pass/fail with a machine-readable JSON summary. Publish the summary as an Argo artifact and link it from each SDK's README.

## Why this matters

Without a per-language runner, the suite is unreachable from CI in any language but Rust. The runner is what turns the shared JSON into a per-SDK gating signal; without it, the "100% conformance pass before publish" acceptance criterion cannot be enforced.

## Implementation guidance

- Per-language runner location convention: each SDK has a `tests/conformance/` (or language-equivalent: `pdftract_test_conformance.go`, `ConformanceTests.cs`, etc.) that invokes the suite
- Shared runner skeleton (pseudocode):
  ```
  cases = load_json(SUITE_PATH)
  results = []
  for case in cases:
      if case.feature not in available_features or case.min_schema_version > binary_schema_version:
          results.append({id: case.id, status: "skip"})
          continue
      try:
          actual = sdk.call(case.method, case.fixture, case.options)
          ok = compare_with_tolerances(actual, case.expected, case.tolerances)
          results.append({id: case.id, status: "pass" if ok else "fail", actual: actual, expected: case.expected})
      except Exception as e:
          results.append({id: case.id, status: "error", error: str(e)})
  write_json("conformance-report.json", {sdk: SDK_NAME, results: results})
  exit(0 if all_pass else 1)
  ```
- Per-language runner deliverables (one per SDK):
  - Python: `tests/test_conformance.py` (pytest harness invoking pdftract via the PyO3 binding)
  - Rust: `crates/pdftract-cli/tests/conformance.rs` (cargo test target)
  - Node.js: `test/conformance.test.ts` (vitest)
