## Scope

Add the inspect subcommand to the pdftract CLI: pdftract inspect FILE.pdf [--port PORT] [--bind ADDR] [--no-open] [--auth-token TOKEN] [--compare OTHER.pdf]. Validate inputs, run extraction, start axum, and (unless --no-open) launch the OS browser to the served URL. Default --port 7676, --bind 127.0.0.1. Non-loopback bind requires --auth-token (consistent with Phase 6.7 MCP HTTP-mode rule).

## Why this matters

The subcommand entry point is the user contract. Defaults must be safe (loopback only); non-loopback binds must be auth-gated; --no-open is essential for CI/headless smoke tests; --compare unlocks comparative debugging. Without correct argparse and validation here, every later inspector feature is unreachable.

## Implementation guidance

- struct InspectArgs { file: PathBuf, port: u16 (default 7676), bind: IpAddr (default 127.0.0.1), no_open: bool, auth_token: Option<String>, compare: Option<PathBuf> }
- Validation:
  - bind != 127.0.0.1 && bind != ::1 && auth_token.is_none() -> error "binding to non-loopback address requires --auth-token"
  - file must exist + be readable; otherwise error
  - compare: if present, must exist + be readable
- Run pipeline: invoke Phase 1-6 extraction; cache InspectorState { document_a: ExtractionResult, document_b: Option<ExtractionResult>, auth_token }
- Build axum router (see 7.9.2)
- Start server: axum::Server::bind((bind, port)).serve(router)
- Browser launch: if !no_open, spawn `xdg-open <url>` on Linux, `open <url>` on macOS, `cmd /c start <url>` on Windows; non-blocking; ignore errors (CI environments without browser shouldn't fail)
- Print "Inspector running at http://<bind>:<port>/" to stdout
- Trap Ctrl-C to shut down cleanly

## Critical considerations

- 127.0.0.1 default forces explicit opt-in for network exposure (security: prevents accidental LAN exposure)
- --auth-token enforcement matches Phase 6.7 MCP rule - shared rationale, shared rule
- Browser launcher fallback: if exec fails (no $DISPLAY), print "Open http://... in your browser" instead of crashing
- --compare requires symmetric extraction (run pipeline twice); slightly more memory usage; document
- Extraction errors (corrupted PDF) -> print error + exit 1; do not start server

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement `detect_and_repair_mojibake(span: &mut Span, scorer: impl Fn(&str) -> f32) -> bool` that scans span.text for sequences characteristic of Latin-1 bytes interpreted as UTF-8 (e.g., `Ã©` for `é`, `Ã¨` for `è`, `â€™` for `'`), attempts re-decoding via encoding_rs (treat the bytes as windows-1252 / Latin-1), accepts the re-decoded text IF the scorer reports a higher readability score on the new text.

## Why this matters

Mojibake is the second-most-common encoding-side failure (after broken ToUnicode): PDFs producing UTF-8 text from underlying Latin-1 bytes without re-encoding produce double-encoded UTF-8 that looks like garbage but is recoverable. Without this, ~3% of European-language PDFs extract as gibberish.

## Implementation guidance

- Crate: `encoding_rs` (already approved).
- Detection: heuristic check — does span.text contain at least 2 occurrences of any of these telltale 2-char sequences?
  - `Ã©` `Ã¨` `Ã ` `Ã®` `Ã´` `Ã» Ã¢ Ã§ Ã±` (common French/Spanish chars when Latin-1 decoded as UTF-8)
  - `â€™ â€"  â€œ â€` (smart quotes / em-dash from Windows-1252)
  - `Â` followed by a non-ASCII char (NBSP and similar)
- If detected: take span.text, encode as UTF-8 bytes, then DECODE those bytes as windows-1252 via `encoding_rs::WINDOWS_1252.decode_without_bom_handling(&utf8_bytes)`. The result is the candidate re-decoded text.
- Score both: original span.text and candidate via the `scorer` callback (typically the readability scorer).
- If `candidate_score > original_score + epsilon` (epsilon = 0.05 to avoid noise): replace span.text with candidate; return true.
- Else: leave unchanged; return false.

## Critical considerations

- INV: re-decoding is REVERTED if it doesn't improve readability (false-positive safety).
- The encoding is windows-1252 NOT pure Latin-1 (windows-1252 is what Windows produces and is the most common source of mojibake; encoding_rs's `WINDOWS_1252` covers smart quotes and other Microsoft-isms).
- Re-decoding may be NESTED in pathological cases (triple-encoded); v0.1.0 does ONE re-decode pass per span; document.
- A clean ASCII or pure UTF-8 span: NO Ã/â sequences detected; pass-through (no-op).
- Performance: cheap heuristic check; only the rare detected cases pay the re-decode cost.

## Acceptance criteria

- Span text "café" -> no Ã detected -> no change.
- Span text "cafÃ©" -> detected, re-decoded to "café", score improves -> accept.
- Span text "cafÃ©sandbar" (one Ã, no other indicators) -> may or may not be detected (heuristic threshold).
- Span text "Ã©Ã¨Ã ï¿½" (multiple indicators): detected, re-decoded; if score improves, accept.
- Asian text (no Latin-1 indicators): pass-through unaffected.

## References

- Plan section: Phase 4.7 Correction pipeline step 3 (line 1779)
- Critical test: "Latin-1 mojibake Ã© corrected to é when re-decode raises readability score" (line 1792)
issue.title: Mojibake detection + Latin-1-as-UTF-8 re-decode via encoding_rs

issue.description:
## Scope

Configure cargo-deny's license policy at repo-root deny.toml. The policy permits MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, ISC, Zlib, Unicode-DFS-2016 in default-feature dependencies. GPL/AGPL/LGPL are rejected. Optional features with copyleft deps require an ADR-recorded exception.

## Why this matters

A copyleft dependency creeping into a default-feature transitive chain would force the entire project under GPL (or trigger a license-incompatibility build failure on consumers). cargo-deny is the standard tooling for license-policy enforcement in the Rust ecosystem; integrating it into CI catches violations at PR time before they're merged.

The Unicode-DFS-2016 entry is mandatory: the unicode-ident crate (a near-universal transitive dep) uses it; without the explicit allow, every PR fails on cargo deny check licenses.

## Implementation guidance

- Create deny.toml at repo root:
  ```toml
  [graph]
  targets = [
    \"x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu\",
    \"x86_64-unknown-linux-musl\",
    \"x86_64-apple-darwin\",
    \"aarch64-apple-darwin\",
    \"x86_64-pc-windows-msvc\",
  ]

  [licenses]
  version = 2
  allow = [
    \"MIT\",
    \"Apache-2.0\",
    \"Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception\",
    \"BSD-2-Clause\",
    \"BSD-3-Clause\",
    \"ISC\",
    \"Zlib\",
    \"Unicode-DFS-2016\",
  ]
  confidence-threshold = 0.93
  exceptions = []  # populated only via ADR review

  [licenses.private]
  ignore = false

  [bans]
  multiple-versions = \"warn\"
  wildcards = \"deny\"

  [advisories]
  vulnerability = \"deny\"
  unmaintained = \"warn\"
  yanked = \"deny\"

  [sources]
  unknown-registry = \"deny\"
  unknown-git = \"deny\"
  ```
- CI integration: cargo deny check licenses bans advisories sources in the PR workflow (Argo WorkflowTemplate)
- Document the ADR process for adding to the exceptions list (requires a new ADR file in docs/adr/)

## Critical considerations

- confidence-threshold 0.93: cargo-deny uses fuzzy matching to identify license text; 0.93 catches mostly-correct LICENSE files while rejecting suspicious ones
- The targets list covers all platforms in the release matrix; deps that are platform-specific (e.g. windows-sys) only have their license checked when building for that platform
- Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception is needed because some Rust standard library crates use it
- multiple-versions = \"warn\" (not deny): duplicate versions in the dep tree are a quality concern but not a license concern; downgrade to deny once dep hygiene is good
- yanked = \"deny\" prevents shipping yanked crates (a yanked dep means a known vulnerability or critical bug)
- vulnerability advisories use the RustSec database (https://rustsec.org/); requires cargo-deny update before each CI run

## Acceptance criteria

- deny.toml exists at repo root with the configuration above
- cargo deny check licenses passes on the current dep tree
- cargo deny check bans passes
- cargo deny check advisories passes
- Argo WorkflowTemplate includes a cargo-deny step that fails the build on any violation
- A test PR adding an MPL-licensed transitive dep (e.g. webpki-roots-anchor) → CI fails at cargo-deny step

## References

- Plan section: Phase RE (Release & Versioning)
- cargo-deny docs: https://embarkstudios.github.io/cargo-deny/
- RustSec advisory database
- Coordinator: pdftract-16wv (parent — dual-license bundle)
Labels: cargo-deny, ci, license, phase-re
issue.title: cargo-deny license policy + deny.toml configuration

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the `Tj string` operator: take a single PDF string (decoded byte sequence — may include escapes, octal, balanced parens), tokenize the bytes per the current font's codespace ranges, resolve each character code to Unicode via Phase 2 resolver, emit a `Glyph` for each, and advance text_matrix per the per-glyph advance formula.

## Why this matters

Tj is the SIMPLEST text-show operator and the foundation for the more complex TJ, ', " operators (which all internally reduce to Tj-like emission). Getting Tj right unlocks all four. ~30% of text-show calls in real PDFs are Tj (the rest are TJ for kerned output from professional typesetters).

## Implementation guidance

- Operand: a PDF string object (already byte-decoded by Phase 1 lexer; handles octal `\NNN`, escapes `\n \r \t \b \f \\ \( \)`, line continuations, balanced parens).
- Tokenize bytes into character codes via font's codespace ranges (Phase 2.3 tokenizer for CJK; simple 1-byte tokenizer for non-Type0).
- For each character code:
  1. Resolve `(chars, source, confidence)` via Phase 2 resolver.
  2. For each resolved char (multi-char on ligatures), emit a Glyph.
  3. Compute advance for this code (Phase 3.2 per-glyph advance bead).
  4. Update text_matrix: `text_matrix = translate(advance, 0) * text_matrix`.
- INV: each emitted Glyph carries the CURRENT graphics state's font, font_size, fill_color, rendering_mode, plus the resolved Unicode + source + confidence + computed bbox.

## Critical considerations

- Empty string `()` is a legal no-op; do not advance, do not emit.
- A multi-byte character code (CJK) consumes 2+ bytes but produces 1 advance step — advance is computed AFTER full code is tokenized.
- The Phase 2 resolver may return a multi-char slice (ligature expansion); each char becomes a SEPARATE Glyph with DUPLICATED bbox (same physical glyph, multiple Unicode chars). The first char is marked with is_word_boundary if applicable; subsequent chars share the same bbox.
- Word boundary detection runs BEFORE advance update — compare predicted advance vs actual, inject synthetic boundary if delta exceeds threshold (Phase 3.2 word boundary bead handles this).
- Glyphs with rendering_mode 3 (invisible) are STILL emitted; downstream filters them.

## Acceptance criteria

- `Tj (Hello)` produces 5 glyphs with codepoints H, e, l, l, o.
- `Tj <FB01>` with font ToUnicode mapping FB01 -> "fi" produces 2 glyphs (f, i) sharing one bbox.
- Empty `Tj ()` no-ops.
- `Tj` outside BT/ET emits TEXT_SHOW_OUTSIDE_BT and produces no glyphs.
- `Tj` with font=None (Tf never called) emits TEXT_SHOW_NO_FONT and produces no glyphs.

## References

- Plan section: Phase 3.2 (lines 1512-1527)
- ISO 32000-1 Table 109

issue.description:
## Scope

Set up cbindgen to auto-generate crates/pdftract-libpdftract/include/pdftract.h from the Rust extern \"C\" surface at build time. The header is shipped alongside the libpdftract binary in the release archive so C/C++ consumers can include it without manual translation.

Module: crates/pdftract-libpdftract/build.rs + cbindgen.toml config.

## Why this matters

A hand-maintained .h file drifts from the Rust extern \"C\" surface every time a method signature changes; cbindgen reads the Rust source and emits the canonical .h, eliminating sync bugs. The generated header is the contract between libpdftract and every C/C++ consumer — its correctness is load-bearing for ABI stability.

## Implementation guidance

- cbindgen config at crates/pdftract-libpdftract/cbindgen.toml:
  ```toml
  language = \"C\"
  header = \"/* Copyright 2026 Jed Cabanero. MIT OR Apache-2.0 */\"
  include_guard = \"PDFTRACT_H\"
  no_includes = false
  pragma_once = true
  cpp_compat = true
  documentation = true
  style = \"both\"

  [export]
  prefix = \"pdftract_\"
  ```
- build.rs:
  ```rust
  fn main() {
      let crate_dir = std::env::var(\"CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR\").unwrap();
      let config = cbindgen::Config::from_file(format!(\"{crate_dir}/cbindgen.toml\")).unwrap();
      cbindgen::Builder::new()
          .with_crate(&crate_dir)
          .with_config(config)
          .generate()
          .expect(\"Unable to generate bindings\")
          .write_to_file(format!(\"{crate_dir}/include/pdftract.h\"));
  }
  ```
- Header is committed to the repo (for IDE/tooling discoverability) AND regenerated on build (CI gate asserts the committed file matches the generated one)
- cpp_compat = true emits extern \"C\" { ... } guards so the same header works in C and C++
- pragma_once = true adds #pragma once for modern compilers; include_guard adds #ifndef PDFTRACT_H for older compilers

## Critical considerations

- The header MUST be regenerated whenever the extern \"C\" surface changes; the CI gate diffs committed vs. generated and fails on mismatch (\"run cargo build to regenerate include/pdftract.h\")
- cbindgen's documentation = true picks up Rust doc comments and emits them as Doxygen comments in the .h
- Some Rust types do not translate directly: cbindgen handles repr(C) structs, c-style enums, function pointers; non-FFI types (Vec, String, Box without raw pointer) generate cbindgen errors at build time
- The header is included in the release archive (Phase SDK distribution) at include/pdftract.h
- A separate pdftract.pc pkg-config file is sibling work (or a follow-up bead); not in this bead's scope

## Acceptance criteria

- cargo build -p pdftract-libpdftract regenerates crates/pdftract-libpdftract/include/pdftract.h
- The generated .h compiles cleanly with gcc -xc -c -o /dev/null include/pdftract.h
- The generated .h compiles cleanly with g++ -xc++ -c -o /dev/null include/pdftract.h (cpp_compat verified)
- CI gate: committed include/pdftract.h byte-equal to fresh generation; mismatch fails CI with clear message
- Header contains include guard + pragma once + extern \"C\" guards
- All extern \"C\" functions from sibling bead appear in the header

## References

- Plan section: Phase SDK epic (C/C++ SDK row)
- cbindgen docs: https://github.com/mozilla/cbindgen
- Sibling beads: scaffold (provides the extern \"C\" surface to scan), API surface (defines the functions)
- Coordinator: pdftract-1eaxm (parent)
Labels: cbindgen, cpp, phase-6, sdk

issue.description:
## Scope

Thin wrapper around `encoding_rs` exposing `decode_cjk_bytes(encoding: CjkEncoding, bytes: &[u8]) -> String` for the four major CJK byte encodings used in legacy PDFs. `CjkEncoding` is an enum `{ShiftJis, Gb18030, Big5, EucKr}`. Used by Phase 2.3 fallback path when a font's encoding indicates a raw byte encoding and no CMap/ToUnicode is present.

## Why this matters

Older PDFs (especially scanned-and-converted Asian-language documents) sometimes encode text as raw byte sequences in a non-Unicode encoding rather than via a CMap. encoding_rs is the gold-standard Rust implementation of these encodings (it powers Firefox); reusing it spares us from implementing 4 complex code-page mappings ourselves.

## Implementation guidance

- Crate: `encoding_rs`. Already approved.
- Each encoding has a singleton: `encoding_rs::SHIFT_JIS`, `encoding_rs::GB18030`, `encoding_rs::BIG5`, `encoding_rs::EUC_KR`.
- API: `encoding.decode_without_bom_handling(bytes)` returns `(Cow<str>, bool)` where the bool indicates malformed bytes. Map malformed -> replacement char U+FFFD and emit `CJK_DECODE_MALFORMED` diagnostic with a byte count.
- Public function signature: `pub fn decode_cjk_bytes(enc: CjkEncoding, bytes: &[u8]) -> (String, bool)`.
- Round-trip test: encode "テスト" as Shift-JIS bytes, decode -> get "テスト" back.

## Critical considerations

- Do NOT use `decode_with_bom_handling`; PDF byte streams never have a BOM.
- GB18030 is 1-2-4 byte variable-width; encoding_rs handles this — do not pre-tokenize.
- Big5 has the Big5-HKSCS extension that encoding_rs's `BIG5` encoding handles; document this.
- EUC-KR / KS X 1001: the encoding_rs `EUC_KR` covers KS X 1001 + Unified Hangul.
- These are FALLBACKS — the primary path is predefined CMap + ToUnicode. Document when this fallback fires (raw encoding name or unrecognized CMap name + lead byte in CJK range).

## Acceptance criteria

- All 4 encodings decode known sample byte sequences to expected Unicode strings.
- Malformed input produces U+FFFD chars and the diagnostic, no panic.
- Empty input returns empty string.
- API is `cfg(feature = "cjk")`-gated alongside the predefined CMap registry.

## References

- Plan section: Phase 2.3 (lines 1382-1386)
- encoding_rs Dependency Matrix entry

## Scope

Implement the glibc test leg in pdftract-ci's test-matrix DAG branch. cargo nextest run --all-features on a custom pdftract-test-glibc:1.78 image extending rust:1.78-slim-bookworm with tesseract/leptonica/libtesseract installed. Emits JUnit XML to artifact store.

## Why this matters

The glibc leg gives full coverage of the OCR integration path (tesseract requires libleptonica / libtesseract system libraries that don't exist on Alpine/musl). Without it, OCR regressions slip through to production where users hit them first.

## Implementation guidance

- Custom Docker image pdftract-test-glibc:1.78 (Dockerfile in declarative-config under k8s/iad-ci/docker/pdftract-test-glibc/):
  - Base: rust:1.78-slim-bookworm
  - apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends tesseract-ocr=5.* libleptonica-dev libtesseract-dev pkg-config build-essential ca-certificates curl
  - cargo install cargo-nextest --locked
  - cargo install cargo-junit-test --locked
- Test command: cargo nextest run --all-features --profile ci --no-fail-fast
- nextest profile ci: JUnit XML output, slow-test timeout 60s, retry once on known-flaky
- Output: JUnit XML to artifact store as test-results-glibc.xml
- Parallel-runnable with musl leg

## Critical considerations

- All-features includes ocr, serve, decrypt, full-render, profiles, mcp, cache, receipts, remote
- Image build is a separate concern (handled by Dockerfile in declarative-config; built and pushed by Argo separately)
- Test runtime budget: glibc leg < 15 min on cached deps (longer than musl due to OCR test corpus)
- pdfium-render (full-render feature) requires libpdfium runtime; install via the image (cargo build downloads pdfium binary cache)

## Acceptance criteria

- Step runs on every PR
- glibc test failures block PR merge
- JUnit XML produced
- All OCR-feature tests covered

## References

- Plan section: Phase 0.3
- jedarden/declarative-config/k8s/iad-ci/docker/pdftract-test-glibc/Dockerfile
- Coordinator: pdftract-30n (parent)

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement a rule-based, reproducible, user-extensible document-type classifier. Built-in types: invoice, receipt, contract, scientific_paper, slide_deck, form, bank_statement, legal_filing, book_chapter, unknown. Each profile defines matching predicates (text patterns, structural signals, page-count ranges, font signals). Classifier evaluates every loaded profile against extracted document; selects highest-scoring profile above 0.6 confidence threshold (else unknown). Feature signals computed once during Phase 4 assembly and reused across all profile evaluations.

## Outputs:
- metadata.document_type (string, from the enum)
- metadata.document_type_confidence (f32 in [0,1])
- metadata.document_type_reasons (Vec<String>) explaining why
- runner-up information for the classify CLI subcommand

## Why this matters

5.6 is the bridge to Phase 7.10 profiles. The --auto flag uses 5.6 classification to pick a profile that tunes the extraction (e.g. invoice profile boosts table detection, scientific_paper profile boosts formula detection). The rule-based design is deliberate: reproducibility (no model weights), transparency (reasons exposed in output), user-extensibility (YAML profiles in 7.10), binary size (no ML deps).

## Implementation guidance

- Module: pdftract-core/src/classifier/ (NOT pdftract-ocr; classifier works on Phase 4 output regardless of OCR)
- Profile evaluator architecture (5.6.2): each profile is a list of MatchPredicate { kind, weight, target } where MatchPredicate kind = TextContains | StructuralHasTable | PageCountInRange | FontDiversity | etc.
- Score = sum of (matched predicate.weight) / sum of (all predicate.weight); profile with highest score above 0.6 wins
- Feature-signal cache (5.6.3): compute once per document, reuse across profile evaluations; populated during Phase 4 assembly
- Built-in profile definitions (5.6.4): 9 profile types + matching predicates each
- classify CLI subcommand (5.6.5): print JSON {document_type, confidence, reasons, runner_up, runner_up_confidence}
- Feature flag: classifier engine is in default features (~50 LOC); built-in profile bundle behind profiles feature

## Critical considerations

- 200-document labeled corpus accuracy >= 90% (CI-gated) is the primary 5.6 deliverable
- Per-document classification overhead < 5% of total extraction time
- Reproducibility: same input -> same output bit-for-bit (no HashMap iteration; use BTreeMap or Vec<(K,V)>)
- Without profiles feature: classifier returns unknown / 0.0 / no reasons; document this contract
- Profile YAML schema lives in 7.10 but field names must be locked here (the classifier consumes the YAML output of profile authoring)
- regex crate is the only new dep; already pulled in by grep and profiles features

## Acceptance criteria

- All 5.6 child task beads closed
- 200-doc corpus: classification accuracy >= 90%; per-class precision and recall >= 0.85; macro-F1 >= 0.88 (CI-gated)
- All 6 critical-test fixtures classified correctly: invoice (>0.8 conf), arxiv paper, IRS Form 1040, scanned receipt, novel (book_chapter or unknown)
- pdftract classify CLI returns proper JSON shape
- Reproducibility: classify same PDF twice -> identical JSON
- Overhead < 5% on standard extraction benchmark

## References

- Plan section: Phase 5.6 (lines 1925-1988)
- Phase 7.10 profile schema (consumes classifier output)
- KU-9 (finance subcorpus accuracy)

issue.description:
## Scope

Expose pdftract as a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server so LLM agents (Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, Continue, custom agents using the Anthropic or OpenAI SDKs) can invoke extraction as a tool. Two transports are supported, **mutually exclusive per process**: stdio (local agent host-process integration) and HTTP+SSE (remote service deployment).

This bead is the sub-phase coordinator that aggregates the child task beads:

- pdftract-XX: JSON-RPC 2.0 framing layer (hand-written; shared by stdio + HTTP transports)
- pdftract-XX: stdio transport (Content-Length-headered framing; stdin/stdout; stderr-only logs; INV-9)
- pdftract-XX: HTTP+SSE transport (POST / + GET /sse; axum-based; reuses Phase 6.4 infrastructure)
- pdftract-XX: Transport mutual exclusion enforcement at CLI parse (per ADR-006)
- pdftract-XX: Tool catalog (extract, extract_text, extract_markdown, search, get_metadata, get_table, get_form_fields, get_attachments, hash, classify)
- pdftract-XX: Path-traversal protection via --root DIR with JSON-RPC -32602 rejection on escape
- pdftract-XX: Bearer-token auth required on non-loopback bind (startup abort if missing)

## Why this matters

MCP is the cleanest contract for agents to invoke pdftract: a typed tool catalog with JSON-Schema arg shapes, structured error codes, and per-call observability. Without an MCP server, agents must either (a) shell out to pdftract CLI and parse stdout/stderr (fragile, no streaming) or (b) hit the HTTP serve endpoints directly (works but loses the MCP capability negotiation and the per-tool argument schema that drives agent tool-selection).

The stdio + HTTP split mirrors the MCP spec's two transport types and matches actual deployment patterns: stdio for in-process agent hosts (Claude Desktop, Continue), HTTP+SSE for hosted multi-tenant deployments (corporate Claude Code at scale, vendor MCP marketplaces).

## Critical considerations

- Transports are mutually exclusive per process (ADR-006): stdio mode owns stdout as the JSON-RPC sink, HTTP mode treats stdout as a log channel. Forbidding both at CLI parse time makes the contract unambiguous and prevents stdout-double-ownership bugs.
- INV-9: in stdio mode, stdout is JSON-RPC-only. Every log line, panic backtrace, or stray println goes to stderr. Any violation breaks the JSON-RPC stream and is treated as a P0 bug.
- Bearer-token auth REQUIRED on non-loopback bind. Startup aborts with clear error if --bind 0.0.0.0:... given without --auth-token or PDFTRACT_MCP_TOKEN env var. Loopback (127.0.0.1, ::1) does not require a token.
- --root DIR enables path-traversal protection: all local paths resolved relative to DIR; any resolved path escaping DIR rejected with JSON-RPC error code -32602. Without --root, the working directory is the implicit root (no protection). HTTPS URLs are unaffected by --root.
- Tool catalog returned by tools/list must include argument JSON Schemas so agents can render forms/select arguments. Reuse the Phase 6.1 JSON Schema fragments where possible (DocumentJson for extract response shape, ExtractionOptions for arg shapes).
- Structured logging on every tool invocation: ISO-8601 timestamp, tool name, path (or its SHA-256 hash when --no-log-paths), duration_ms, response_size_bytes, error_code if any. Log level controlled by RUST_LOG and the MCP logging/setLevel request (whichever is more verbose).
- JSON-RPC framing is hand-written (no separate crate dependency); both transports share the same Request/Response/Notification types.

## Acceptance criteria

- All 7 child task beads closed
- Stdio mode responds to tools/list within 50 ms of receiving the request on stdin (acceptance criterion in plan section 6.7)
- Remote mode handles 50 concurrent clients each running extract on different PDFs without errors
- Switching between transports requires only a flag change; no other configuration touched
- Bearer token required when binding to a non-loopback address: startup aborts with a clear error if missing
- Path-traversal attempt with --root /var/data: path=\"../../etc/passwd\" rejected with JSON-RPC -32602
- All Critical tests from plan section 6.7 pass (6 tests cited in child beads)
- Module under crates/pdftract-cli/src/mcp/ (with framing/, stdio.rs, http.rs, tools.rs, root.rs, auth.rs submodules)
- Feature flag mcp (depends on serve); no new direct dependencies — reuses axum, tokio, tower-http from Phase 6.4

## References

- Plan section: Phase 6.7 MCP Server Mode (lines 2286-2349)
- INV-9 (stdio MCP stdout is JSON-RPC only)
- ADR-006 (transport mutual exclusion)
- Phase 6.4 HTTP infrastructure reuse
- MCP spec: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/spec
Labels: api, coordinator, mcp, phase-6

issue.description:
## Scope

Author the 9 built-in profile definitions (invoice, receipt, contract, scientific_paper, slide_deck, form, bank_statement, legal_filing, book_chapter) as YAML files bundled inside the pdftract binary via include_str! and a hand-rolled YAML loader (or rust-embed if approved). Each profile must hit its own positive fixtures and not over-trigger on negative fixtures during the 200-doc CI gate.

## Why this matters

The built-in bundle is the out-of-the-box experience for the classifier. Without good defaults, users would need to hand-author profiles before --auto becomes useful. The 200-doc corpus gate is the contract that the bundle must satisfy.

## Implementation guidance

- File layout: profiles/builtin/{invoice,receipt,contract,scientific_paper,slide_deck,form,bank_statement,legal_filing,book_chapter}.yaml
- Each YAML uses the schema from 5.6.1
- Per-profile predicate suggestions:
  - invoice: text_contains("invoice", "total", "subtotal"), structural.has_table, page_count 1-5
  - receipt: text_contains("$", currency regex), font_diversity 1-2 (single font common on thermal printers), page_count 1
  - contract: text_contains("whereas", "party", "agreement"), heading_depth_at_least 2, page_count 2-50
  - scientific_paper: text_contains("abstract", "references", "et al."), has_math_operators, page_count 4-30
  - slide_deck: aspect_ratio_landscape (NEW signal? if needed, extend 5.6.3), heading on every page, page_count 5-150
  - form: structural.has_form_field, page_count 1-10
  - bank_statement: text_contains("statement", "transaction", currency), structural.has_table, page_count 1-20
  - legal_filing: text_contains("court", "plaintiff", "defendant"), has_footer_page_numbers, page_count >= 1
  - book_chapter: page_count >= 20, heading_depth_at_least 1, font_diversity 1-3
- Profile loader: profiles::load_builtins() -> Vec<Profile>, reads each YAML via include_str! and parses

## Critical considerations

- Profile weights MUST sum to a value that lets a typical positive fixture exceed the 0.6 threshold; tune via iterative fixture matching
- Negative-fixture testing: each profile must NOT classify a randomly-chosen fixture of another type as itself (precision >= 0.85 per class)
- profiles feature gate: when compiled out, builtin profile bundle is excluded from binary; classifier returns unknown
- YAML parsing happens once at process startup; cache the Vec<Profile>

## Acceptance criteria

- All 9 profiles bundled and loadable
- Each profile correctly classifies its own positive fixture (sample of 3+ per type) with confidence > 0.6
- 200-doc corpus: per-class precision and recall >= 0.85; macro-F1 >= 0.88
- profiles feature compiled out: bundle absent from binary (verified via cargo bloat)
- Profile YAML files are < 5 KB each

## References

- Plan section: Phase 5.6 (line 1929) + acceptance criteria (line 1973)
- Phase 7.10 profile authoring (built-ins serve as starter templates)

issue.close_reason: Implemented CIDToGIDMap resolver for CIDFontType2 descendant fonts. Identity form (zero-allocation short-circuit) and stream form (2-byte big-endian GID values) both implemented. All acceptance criteria PASS: Identity lookup returns CID as u16, stream decodes correctly to [0, 5, 10], out-of-range CID returns GID 0 without panic, CIDTOGIDMAP_TRUNCATED diagnostic emitted on odd-byte-count. 29 type0 tests pass. Commit e79e806. Verification note at notes/pdftract-5sh.md.
issue.description:
## Scope

Implement `resolve_cid_to_gid(map_entry: &Object) -> CidToGidMap` for CIDFontType2 descendant fonts. Two valid forms: name `/Identity` (GID == CID, no lookup) and a stream (FlateDecode-decoded, interpreted as a flat array of 2-byte big-endian GIDs indexed by CID). Returns an enum `CidToGidMap::{Identity, Array(Box<[u16]>)}`.

## Why this matters

A wrong GID lookup picks the wrong glyph outline and (if shape recognition is reached) returns the wrong character. The Identity short-circuit must not allocate. The stream form is incredibly common in embedded subsets — every CJK PDF with a TrueType outline has one.

## Implementation guidance

- Identity detection: object is `Object::Name(name)` with `name == "Identity"`. Return `CidToGidMap::Identity` (zero allocation).
- Stream detection: object is a stream (apply Phase 1.3 filter pipeline first to get the decoded bytes).
- Decoded byte array length is `2 * (max_cid + 1)`. Each pair (high, low) forms `(u16::from_be_bytes([high, low])) -> GID`.
- Build `Box<[u16]>` of length `decoded.len() / 2`. For odd-length input emit `CIDTOGIDMAP_TRUNCATED` diagnostic and truncate.
- Lookup: `Identity => cid as u16`; `Array(arr) => arr.get(cid as usize).copied().unwrap_or(0)`. GID 0 is the `.notdef` glyph by convention; do NOT panic.

## Critical considerations

- Many CIDToGIDMap streams have lengths exceeding 200 KB (covering ~65k CIDs); allocate on the heap once, never per-lookup.
- CID values can exceed u16 range theoretically but in practice all CIDs in /W fit in u16; if a CID > arr.len(), return GID 0.
- `/Identity` is a NAME object, not a string `"Identity"`. Match on Object::Name.
- Test fixture: a small synthetic stream `[0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x05, 0x00, 0x0A]` decodes to `[0, 5, 10]` meaning CID 0->GID 0, CID 1->GID 5, CID 2->GID 10.

## Acceptance criteria

- Identity form: lookup of any CID returns same value as u16.
- Stream form: synthetic 3-CID array decodes correctly per above.
- Out-of-range CID returns GID 0 with no panic.
- Diagnostic `CIDTOGIDMAP_TRUNCATED` emitted on odd-byte-count input.

## References

- Plan section: Phase 2.1, "CIDFontType2 with /CIDToGIDMap as a stream" critical test (line 1315)
issue.title: CIDToGIDMap resolver (Identity and stream forms)

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement `strip_soft_hyphens(span: &mut Span) -> u32` that removes ALL occurrences of U+00AD (SOFT HYPHEN) from span.text. The soft hyphen is a FORMATTING HINT indicating where a typesetter MAY break a word for line wrapping; it is NOT content and should not appear in extracted text. Returns count of stripped codepoints.

## Why this matters

Soft hyphens appearing in extracted text break word identification ("automa­tion" doesn't match "automation" in dict lookup, RAG search, anything downstream). Stripping them is universally correct AND simple — there are zero contexts where soft hyphens should be preserved in extracted text.

## Implementation guidance

- Use a single-pass filter: `span.text.retain(|c| c != '\u{00AD}');`.
- Track count: pre-strip char count minus post-strip char count.
- Update span.bbox: leave unchanged (the soft hyphen had zero visual width AND was inside the rendered glyph extent — bbox doesn't need adjustment).
- Apply BEFORE scoring (per Phase 4.7 coordinator).

## Critical considerations

- INV: U+00AD has zero visual width when not at line-break; it's metadata in the source PDF text stream. Some PDF producers emit it inline; some only at line-break points.
- The hyphenation repair sibling bead handles the line-break case (where a soft hyphen MAY have been rendered as a visible hyphen). This bead is the broader cleanup.
- Do NOT strip U+2010 (HYPHEN) or U+2011 (NON-BREAKING HYPHEN) — those are content.
- Performance: single-pass O(n) per span.

## Acceptance criteria

- Span text "automa\u{00AD}tion" -> "automation" (1 stripped).
- Span text "no soft hyphens here" -> unchanged.
- Span text "\u{00AD}\u{00AD}\u{00AD}" -> "" (3 stripped).
- Word containing U+2010 hyphen-minus: NOT stripped.
- Returns correct strip count.

## References

- Plan section: Phase 4.7 Correction pipeline step 4 (line 1780)
issue.title: Soft-hyphen U+00AD removal

issue.description:
## Scope

For each AcroFormField from 7.4.1, normalise the raw /V (and /DV) PDF object into a typed FormFieldValue based on the field's /FT. Tx -> String. Btn -> { Pushbutton (no value), Checkbox/Radio (selected: bool, state_name: String) }. Ch -> { Combo/List (selected: String, options: Vec<(export_value, display_text)>) }. Sig fields are skipped (handled by 7.3).

## Why this matters

Raw PDF objects (Name, String, Array) are not consumer-friendly - downstream sinks need typed values that map cleanly to JSON. Distinguishing pushbutton from checkbox from radio is essential for form replication, automated form-filling tools, and machine-readable extracted data. The /Opt array on Ch fields gives the full enumeration of choices, not just the selected one.

## Implementation guidance

- FormFieldValue enum: Text { value: Option<String>, default: Option<String>, multiline: bool, max_length: Option<u32> } | Button { kind: ButtonKind, selected: bool, state_name: Option<String>, pushbutton: bool, radio: bool } | Choice { kind: ChoiceKind, selected: Option<String>, default: Option<String>, options: Vec<(String, String)>, multi_select: bool } | Signature (skipped - handled by 7.3) | Unknown { field_type: String }
- Tx: /V is PdfString -> String (decode via Phase 1 PdfString decoder); multi-line from /Ff bit 12; max_length from /MaxLen
- Btn:
  - /Ff bit 15 = Pushbutton (no /V); bit 16 = Radio (mutually exclusive within parent)
  - Checkbox: /V is /Yes (selected) or /Off (unselected) or some other configured /AS state
  - Radio: /V is the state name of the selected button (typically the export value from /AP /N dictionary)
  - is_checked = !(value == "Off" or value is absent)
- Ch:
  - /Opt is array; each entry is either a PdfString (display_text = export_value) or a 2-element array [export_value, display_text]
  - /V is selected export value(s); /Ff bit 22 = MultiSelect (then /V is array)
  - /Ff bit 18 = Combo (else List)
- Sig: skip (delegate to 7.3)
- Unknown /FT: emit as Unknown { field_type } for forward compatibility

## Critical considerations

- /V absent on Tx: value: None (not empty string)
- /V on Btn checkbox absent or /Off: selected: false; state_name: Some("Off")
- PdfString decoding: PDFDocEncoding default; UTF-16BE if BOM-prefixed - reuse Phase 1 decoder
- Multi-line value preserves \n and \r within the string
- /Ff is u32; preserve all bits (other consumers may want different bits)
- /MaxLen is u32; absent = no limit

## Acceptance criteria

- Critical test (from plan): text field, checkbox, and dropdown - all three types extracted with correct values
- Unit tests: unselected checkbox, selected radio, multi-select list, combo with /Opt 2-tuple entries, multi-line text
- Public form_field::extract_values(&[AcroFormField]) -> Vec<(String, FormFieldValue)>
- Sig fields are skipped (yields nothing in this pipeline)
- All bits of /Ff preserved for downstream inspection

## References

- Plan section: 7.4 lines 2610-2613 (Tx/Btn/Ch)
- PDF 1.7 spec 12.7.4.2 (Tx), 12.7.4.3 (Btn), 12.7.4.4 (Ch)
- Phase 1 PdfString decoder
- 7.4.1 (input walker)
- 7.4.4 (combiner consumer)
issue.title: 7.4.2: AcroForm value extraction for Tx / Btn / Ch types

issue.description:
## Scope

Walk the /Pages subtree (which is a tree of /Pages nodes containing /Kids of either more /Pages nodes or leaf /Page dicts) and produce a flat `Vec<PageDict>` with all inherited attributes resolved.

PageDict struct:
- `obj_ref: ObjRef` — the page's own indirect reference
- `media_box: [f64; 4]` — REQUIRED; inherited if missing on this page
- `crop_box: Option<[f64; 4]>` — defaults to media_box if absent
- `bleed_box: Option<[f64; 4]>` — defaults to crop_box
- `trim_box: Option<[f64; 4]>` — defaults to crop_box
- `art_box: Option<[f64; 4]>` — defaults to crop_box
- `rotate: i32` — 0/90/180/270; must be a multiple of 90
- `resources_ref: ObjRef` — merged resource dict (built by Phase 1.4 Resource Inheritance bead)
- `contents: Vec<ObjRef>` — list of content stream refs (in order)
- `annots: Vec<ObjRef>` — annotation array
- `actual_text: Option<String>` — from /ActualText if tagged
- `lang: Option<String>` — from /Lang
- `aa: Option<PdfObject>` — page-level additional actions (used by JS detection)

## Implementation guidance

- Public API: `flatten_page_tree(resolver: &XrefResolver, pages_ref: ObjRef) -> Vec<PageDict>`
- Algorithm: recursive walk with inherited-attribute accumulator
  ```
  fn walk(node: &PdfDict, inherited: InheritedAttrs) -> Vec<PageDict> {
      let mut current = inherited.clone();
      // Merge node's own inheritable attrs into current
      if let Some(mb) = node.get("MediaBox") { current.media_box = mb; }
      ...
      if node.get("Type") == Some(Name("Page")) {
          // Leaf: emit PageDict
          vec![PageDict::from(node, current)]
      } else {
          // Internal /Pages node: recurse into /Kids
          node.get("Kids").as_array().flat_map(|k| walk(resolver.resolve(k), current.clone())).collect()
      }
  }
  ```
- Inheritable attributes: MediaBox, CropBox, Resources, Rotate (per PDF spec 7.7.3.4)
- Non-inheritable: BleedBox, TrimBox, ArtBox, Contents, Annots (each leaf must declare its own)
- /Contents normalization: if /Contents is a single ObjRef, wrap in Vec; if it's an Array, take each ref; if a Stream, error (it should be indirect)
- /Rotate must be multiple of 90; if not, emit STRUCT_INVALID_ROTATE, clamp to nearest multiple
- /MediaBox missing AND not inherited: EC-09 — substitute US Letter (612 x 792 points), emit STRUCT_MISSING_KEY

## Critical considerations

- Critical test from plan: page inheriting MediaBox from grandparent /Pages node. Verify the walk correctly accumulates inheritance across 3+ levels
- Critical test EC-09: page with no MediaBox and no inherited MediaBox -> US Letter substituted (612 x 792)
- Cycle detection in page tree: page tree should be a tree (no cycles), but malformed files might have them. Maintain HashSet<ObjRef> of visited nodes; emit STRUCT_CIRCULAR_REF on cycle, prune that subtree
- Depth limit: max 16 levels of /Pages nesting (very generous — real PDFs rarely exceed 5)
- /Kids array can have direct PdfDict embedded instead of indirect ref (rare but legal). Handle both
- The flatten preserves leaf order (left-to-right depth-first walk produces page_index 0, 1, 2...)
- Empty /Pages tree: zero pages; page_count = 0 (EC-01 single-page or zero-page edge case)
- Content stream concatenation per plan: if /Contents is an array of stream refs, ALL streams are decoded and concatenated in order before Phase 3 content-stream processing. Graphics state is NOT reset between concatenated streams — they are treated as a single logical stream. This concatenation is performed by Phase 3, but the PageDict.contents Vec preserves the order

## Acceptance criteria

- Critical test passes: 3-level /Pages tree with MediaBox only on grandparent — all leaf pages inherit correctly
- Critical test passes: page with no MediaBox anywhere — defaults to (0, 0, 612, 792); STRUCT_MISSING_KEY emitted
- A /Pages tree with cycles: cycle detected; partial flattening returned
- /Rotate value 45: STRUCT_INVALID_ROTATE; clamped to 0 (nearest multiple)
- Page count matches the catalog's /Pages /Count (cross-check; emit STRUCT_INVALID_PAGE_COUNT if mismatch)
- proptest: random page-tree shapes never panic
- INV-8 maintained

## References

- Plan section: Phase 1.4 line 1112 (page tree flattening with inheritance + content stream concat)
- EC-09 (Missing /MediaBox)
- PDF spec 7.7.3.4 (Page Tree Inheritance)
- INV-8

issue.description:
## Scope

Extend Phase 3 content-stream processing with a position-hint mode: when invoked with PositionHintMode::Yes, the operator interpreter still computes per-glyph bboxes via the current ToUnicode + CTM logic, but emits each glyph with unicode = U+FFFD (replacement character) and confidence = 0.0. The output is a Vec<Glyph> that is geometrically correct but textually nonsensical, suitable as input for the 5.5.2 validation filter.

## Why this matters

The whole point of the BrokenVector assisted-OCR path is "use the broken text layer's positions as hints without trusting its Unicode". Without a position-hint mode in Phase 3, the only way to get bboxes is to also pull in the broken Unicode and discard it later, which couples 5.5 to 3.x and is brittle. Phase 3 already does CTM tracking; adding a flag to bypass the Unicode lookup is cheap and isolating.

## Implementation guidance

- Add ProcessingMode enum to Phase 3 content-stream processor: { Normal, PositionHint }
- In PositionHint mode:
  - skip ToUnicode CMap lookup (which is one of the more expensive per-glyph operations)
  - emit Glyph { unicode: '\u{FFFD}', confidence: 0.0, bbox, font: None, size: None, color: None, ... }
- The Tj / TJ / ' / " operators all still need to advance the text matrix correctly (positions must be right)
- Hook: pdftract_core::content_stream::process_with_mode(stream, mode) -> Vec<Glyph>
- 5.5 calls this with PositionHint to get the geometry, then 5.5.2 uses that geometry to filter Tesseract output

## Critical considerations

- The position-hint mode MUST advance the text matrix exactly like normal mode (string widths from font metrics matter for positioning even when Unicode is replaced)
- Confidence = 0.0 (not 1.0) so downstream code doesn't accidentally trust the position-hint glyphs as text
- The implementation should NOT touch encoding repair pipelines (Phase 2.x) — encoding is irrelevant when we're discarding Unicode
- Performance: position-hint mode should be FASTER than normal mode (skipped ToUnicode lookup); measure and document

## Acceptance criteria

- Unit test: same input PDF, process_with_mode(stream, Normal) vs (stream, PositionHint) -> bboxes identical, Unicode differs (U+FFFD everywhere in PositionHint)
- Microbench: PositionHint mode >= 10% faster on a 100-glyph fixture
- BrokenVector PDF/A fixture: PositionHint output has correct number of glyphs with valid bboxes inside the page

## References

- Plan section: Phase 5.5 pipeline step 1 (line 1915)
- Phase 3 content stream processor (existing)

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the SVG clip generator for --receipts=svg mode. Given a Receipt's bbox and the corresponding glyph list from Phase 3, produce a self-contained SVG document embedding the glyph outlines (extracted via ttf-parser's outline API). The SVG renders standalone in any browser without external font dependencies; the viewBox is normalized to the bbox so the SVG scales correctly when embedded in dashboards or audit reports.

Module: crates/pdftract-core/src/receipts/svg.rs.

## Why this matters

SVG-mode receipts let the receipt stand alone as visual proof: an auditor can paste the SVG into a document or email and see the actual glyphs from the source PDF, without having the PDF on hand. This is the primary differentiator over text-only citation systems. Lite mode (sibling 6.8.1) requires the verifier to have the source PDF to validate; SVG mode lets the receipt carry its own visual evidence.

ttf-parser is already in the default deps, so SVG mode adds NO new dependencies — only output-generation code. The SVG output is hand-written XML (no svg-rs crate); the markup is small enough that a hand-rolled writer is more efficient and easier to audit.

## Implementation guidance

- Algorithm:
  1. Iterate the glyph list for the page (from Phase 3 GlyphList)
  2. Filter to glyphs whose bbox center falls within the receipt bbox
  3. For each glyph, look up its font face (Phase 3 FontResolver), query ttf_parser::Face::outline_glyph(gid, &mut builder) to get the path
  4. Translate the glyph outline coordinates into the SVG coordinate system (origin at top-left of receipt bbox; y-axis flipped from PDF's bottom-left)
  5. Concatenate the path data into a single <path d=\"...\"/> element per glyph (or a single combined path if all glyphs share fill_color)
  6. Set fill from the glyph's fill_color (Phase 3 GlyphStyle)
  7. Wrap in <svg viewBox=\"0 0 width height\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/2000/svg\">...</svg>
- ttf_parser::OutlineBuilder trait: implement to convert MoveTo/LineTo/QuadTo/CurveTo/Close into SVG path commands (M, L, Q, C, Z)
- Coordinate transform: SVG y = bbox.y1 - pdf_y (flip); SVG x = pdf_x - bbox.x0 (translate to bbox origin)
- viewBox normalization: width = bbox.x1 - bbox.x0; height = bbox.y1 - bbox.y0
- SVG output is escaped XML: glyph counts can be large; use a String buffer and write! macro rather than constructing intermediate structures
- The svg_clip field of the Receipt is populated with the full SVG as a String (suitable for inline embedding in JSON)
- If a glyph has no font outline available (OCR-sourced or font extraction failed), defer to sibling 6.8.3 OCR fallback

## Critical considerations

- ttf-parser's outline_glyph returns None for some glyph indices (CID with no outline, missing glyph); the SVG generator must handle this by falling back to OCR raster (sibling 6.8.3) or skipping the glyph with a comment
- Glyph fill_color comes from Phase 3's GlyphStyle; convert from PDF DeviceRGB/CMYK/Gray to CSS color (e.g. \"rgb(0,0,0)\" or \"#000000\")
- SVG path data uses absolute coordinates (uppercase letters: M, L, Q, C, Z); relative commands work but make round-trip testing harder
- The SVG MUST NOT reference external resources (no <image href=\"...\">, no <use xlink:href=\"...\">) — it must render correctly when embedded in a data: URL
- xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/2000/svg\" is required on the root <svg> element for data: URL rendering to work in browsers
- Coordinate precision: PDF user space is in 1/72-inch units; round path coordinates to 2 decimal places to keep SVG size down without visible loss
- Plan acceptance criterion: pixel-diff < 1% in headless browser between rendered SVG and expected PNG (asserted in the verify-receipt CI test)
- Glyph order in the SVG matters for overlapping glyphs (e.g. composite ligatures); preserve the document order (Phase 3 GlyphList order)
- Some PDF fonts use Type 3 (PostScript) outlines that ttf-parser cannot decode; for these, defer to OCR raster

## Acceptance criteria

- Given a bbox + glyph list with TTF/OTF-outline glyphs, the generated SVG renders identically (pixel diff < 1%) to the same region rendered by a reference PDF renderer (pdfium-render or mupdf-fixture); test in headless Chrome
- Aggregate JSON size for 100 SVG receipts on a 100-page document <= 500 KB (plan acceptance criterion)
- SVG output is valid XML (asserted via quick-xml parse roundtrip in tests)
- SVG output contains no external resource references (no http://, href=, xlink:href= except for xmlns); enforced by a string-scan test
- SVG renders in img src=\"data:image/svg+xml,...\" in Chrome, Firefox, Safari (3-browser headless test in CI)
- For glyphs with no ttf-parser outline, generator falls back to OCR raster (sibling 6.8.3) — no panic, no missing glyphs
- Plan critical test passes: \"SVG clip: render in headless browser; pixel diff vs. expected image < 1%\"
- Coordinate transform unit-tested: a glyph at PDF position (220, 432) with bbox (200, 400, 240, 440) produces SVG path data anchored at (20, 8) (within 0.01 tolerance)

## References

- Plan section: Phase 6.8 Visual Citation Receipts (lines 2380, 2392-2399, 2415)
- ttf-parser outline API: https://docs.rs/ttf-parser/latest/ttf_parser/struct.Face.html#method.outline_glyph
- Phase 3 GlyphList + GlyphStyle (input data structures)
- Phase 1.7 fingerprint (in the Receipt struct, but not used here directly)
- Sibling 6.8.1 (Receipt struct with svg_clip field)
- Sibling 6.8.3 (OCR fallback for glyphs without outlines)
Labels: phase-6, receipts, svg

All acceptance criteria tests present and passing (array_with_integers, dict_with_name_and_integer, hex_string dispatch, bool/null/obj/endobj/R keywords, stream header validation). See notes/pdftract-5upi.md for full verification details. INV-8 maintained via proptest guards.
issue.description:
## Scope

Lex the structural (non-literal) tokens that aren't numeric or string-shaped:

- `[` / `]` -> `Token::ArrayStart` / `Token::ArrayEnd`
- `<<` / `>>` -> `Token::DictStart` / `Token::DictEnd` (must be distinguished from hex string `<...>` — `<<` is dict, `<` followed by anything else is hex)
- Keywords: `true`, `false`, `null`, `obj`, `endobj`, `stream`, `endstream`, `R`, `xref`, `trailer`, `startxref`, `%%EOF`
- The keyword lexer is a final dispatch: if the byte is `a-zA-Z` or a non-delimiter symbol, consume bytes until whitespace/delimiter and match against the keyword table

## Implementation guidance

- Dispatch table in `next_token()` post-whitespace:
  - `[` -> ArrayStart, advance 1
  - `]` -> ArrayEnd, advance 1
  - `<` -> peek next; if `<`, return DictStart and advance 2; otherwise hand off to hex string lexer
  - `>` -> peek next; if `>`, return DictEnd and advance 2; otherwise emit `STRUCT_UNEXPECTED_BYTE` and advance 1
  - `(` -> hand off to literal string lexer
  - `/` -> hand off to name lexer
  - `+`/`-`/`.`/`0-9` -> hand off to numeric lexer
  - `a-z`/`A-Z` (keyword start) -> consume to delimiter/whitespace, match against keyword table:
    - `true` -> Token::Bool(true)
    - `false` -> Token::Bool(false)
    - `null` -> Token::Null
    - `obj` -> Token::Obj
    - `endobj` -> Token::EndObj
    - `stream` -> Token::Stream (PLUS: validate that the next byte sequence is `\n` or `\r\n` -- emit `STRUCT_INVALID_STREAM_HEADER` otherwise)
    - `endstream` -> Token::EndStream
    - `R` -> Token::IndirectRef
    - `xref` / `trailer` / `startxref` / `%%EOF` -> Token::Keyword(&'static str) (xref-resolver consumes these)
    - Any other word -> Token::Keyword(consumed_bytes) — the object parser will reject unknown keywords
- Stream-header validation: the byte AFTER the `stream` keyword MUST be `\n` (0x0A) or `\r\n` (0x0D 0x0A). A lone `\r` is INVALID per PDF spec 7.3.8.1 — emit `STRUCT_INVALID_STREAM_HEADER` and skip whatever line ending is present

## Critical considerations

- The `<` vs `<<` ambiguity is the most common dispatch bug. Be explicit: peek the next byte BEFORE deciding
- Keyword matching is byte-exact (case-sensitive). `True` (capital T) is NOT the bool keyword; it's parsed as a generic Token::Keyword and the object parser will reject it
- The `R` keyword (indirect reference) appears between two integers, e.g. `12 0 R`. The lexer emits 3 tokens: Integer(12), Integer(0), IndirectRef. The object parser combines them
- The `stream` keyword followed by an invalid line ending must NOT skip the stream body; emit the diagnostic and let downstream code recover via /Length or `endstream` scan
- `%%EOF` (PDF end-of-file marker) is a special comment-like token that the xref resolver looks for; treat it as Token::Keyword("%%EOF") rather than as a comment
- The xref keyword may appear as the first byte of the xref table line; the xref resolver dispatches on it
- Unknown keywords (e.g. `foo`) emit Token::Keyword(b"foo"); the object parser checks against valid operator names and emits `STRUCT_UNKNOWN_KEYWORD` if not recognized

## Acceptance criteria

- All Critical tests pass:
  - `[1 2 3]` -> ArrayStart, Integer(1), Integer(2), Integer(3), ArrayEnd, Eof
  - `<< /A 1 >>` -> DictStart, Name(b"A"), Integer(1), DictEnd, Eof
  - `<48>` (hex string, NOT dict) -> Token::String(b"\x48"), Eof — verify `<` followed by non-`<` correctly dispatches to hex lexer
  - `<<<48>>>` -> DictStart, String(b"\x48"), DictEnd? — actually that's `<<` + `<48>` + `>>`. Tricky test
  - `true false null` -> Bool(true), Bool(false), Null, Eof
  - `12 0 obj null endobj` -> Integer(12), Integer(0), Obj, Null, EndObj, Eof
  - `5 0 R` -> Integer(5), Integer(0), IndirectRef, Eof
  - `stream\n...endstream` (where ... is body): Token::Stream, then body bytes consumed by the object parser (NOT by the lexer), then Token::EndStream
  - `stream\rxxx` (lone CR after stream keyword) -> Token::Stream + `STRUCT_INVALID_STREAM_HEADER` diagnostic
  - `True` (case-mismatched keyword) -> Token::Keyword(b"True"), Eof (object parser will reject)
- proptest property: random byte sequences never panic and always produce a finite token stream terminated by Eof
- INV-8 maintained

## References

- Plan section: Phase 1.1 Lexer, lines 1034-1039 (array/dict delimiters, stream/endstream, obj/endobj/R, comments)
- PDF spec 7.3.8.1 (Stream Objects, header line ending)
- PDF spec 7.3.2 (Boolean), 7.3.9 (Null)
issue.title: Implement structural token lexer (arrays, dicts, stream/endstream, obj/endobj/R, bool/null keywords)

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the BrokenVector escalation: after aggregate_page_readability computes the page's readability score, check if (a) page_score < 0.5 AND (b) Phase 5.1 already classified the page as Vector class. If both, escalate by re-classifying to BrokenVector and routing the page to Phase 5.5 assisted OCR (if `ocr` feature is compiled in). Without the OCR feature, emit `BROKENVECTOR_OCR_UNAVAILABLE` diagnostic AND set page_type = "broken_vector" in the output.

## Why this matters

This is the FEEDBACK LOOP that ties extraction quality back to the OCR pipeline. Without it, broken vector extraction silently produces garbage and the user has no clue why. With it, Phase 5.5 re-runs the page through OCR using the partial vector data as positional hints (per docs/research/), recovering text where pure vector extraction failed.

## Implementation guidance

- After aggregate_page_readability:
  ```rust
  if page.extraction_quality.readability < 0.5 && page.page_type == PageType::Vector {
      page.page_type = PageType::BrokenVector;
      #[cfg(feature = "ocr")]
      {
          // Route to Phase 5.5 assisted OCR
          phase_5_5::route_assisted_ocr(page);
      }
      #[cfg(not(feature = "ocr"))]
      {
          emit_diagnostic("BROKENVECTOR_OCR_UNAVAILABLE", page.index);
          // page output uses page_type = broken_vector but no OCR was attempted
      }
  }
  ```
- The Phase 5.5 routing is a function call that takes the page state, runs OCR on the page raster, validates the OCR text against the partial vector glyph positions, and (if successful) replaces the page's spans with the OCR-derived spans tagged ConfidenceSource::Ocr.
- Without ocr feature: the function call is stubbed out via cfg; page emits with page_type = broken_vector and the diagnostic.
- The 0.5 threshold is plan-specified; not configurable in v0.1.0.

## Critical considerations

- INV: escalation only applies to Vector pages (not Raster pages — those already went through OCR in Phase 5.4; not Hybrid pages either).
- INV: ocr feature gating is via #[cfg(feature = "ocr")]; build succeeds without the feature with the diagnostic path active.
- The escalation HAPPENS during Phase 4.7; the actual OCR work is queued for Phase 5.5 execution which may be PARALLELIZED with other pages.
- Re-routing implies re-extracting the SAME page through a different pipeline; the original Vector extraction is discarded (or kept for diagnostics).
- After OCR completes (Phase 5.5), the page's readability is recomputed; if STILL < 0.5, give up (emit diagnostic but keep best-effort output).

## Acceptance criteria

- Vector page with score 0.4: escalated to BrokenVector; OCR invoked if feature on.
- Vector page with score 0.6: NOT escalated.
- Raster page with score 0.4: NOT escalated (already OCR).
- Build without ocr feature on BrokenVector page: BROKENVECTOR_OCR_UNAVAILABLE diagnostic emitted, page_type=broken_vector in output.
- Build with ocr feature: re-extraction via Phase 5.5 happens; page emerges with new readability.

## References

- Plan section: Phase 4.7 Per-page readability + escalation (line 1783)
- Critical test: "Page readability < 0.5 on vector page: page re-classified to BrokenVector, OCR invoked" (line 1793)

issue.description:
## Scope

Bring docs/research/word-boundary-reconstruction.md to v1.0 final-pass: document the adaptive word-boundary algorithm including initial threshold = 0.25 * font_size, the 20-glyph median adjustment, the 1.5x median formula, and the full Tc/Tw/Tz (character-spacing, word-spacing, horizontal-scaling) corrections.

## Why this matters

Word boundary reconstruction is the single most consequential transformation in Phase 4 (text assembly). Wrong boundaries break every downstream operation: paragraph reflow, search indexing, OCR confidence scoring, profile field extraction (which depends on regex matches over reassembled text). Line 1529 in the plan explicitly cites this note as the source of truth for the formula. The current 202-line draft establishes the framework but predates the Tc/Tw/Tz formalization.

## Implementation guidance

- File to update: docs/research/word-boundary-reconstruction.md (already exists, currently 202 lines)
- Required content sections:
  - Background: why naive glyph-spacing thresholds fail (font-specific spacing, kerning, justified text, CJK no-space text)
  - Initial threshold: 0.25 * font_size; rationale and empirical basis
  - Adaptive adjustment: after 20 glyphs, compute median actual inter-glyph gap; set threshold = 1.5 * median
  - Per-glyph corrections:
    - Tc (character-spacing operator) -- additive width modifier
    - Tw (word-spacing operator) -- applied only on SPACE U+0020
    - Tz (horizontal scaling operator) -- multiplicative
  - Pseudo-code: input = ordered glyph list with bboxes + Tc/Tw/Tz from graphics state; output = word boundary positions
  - Edge cases: zero-width joiners, combining marks, CJK no-space text, justified text with extra inter-word gaps, monospaced fonts with wider-than-default spacing
  - Validation methodology: test against ground-truth tokenisations on a labelled corpus

## Critical considerations

- Tz is multiplicative in graphics state, not additive -- documented formula must reflect this
- Tw applies only when the character is U+0020 (SPACE) -- a common bug is applying it to all whitespace
- Adaptive median can be skewed by a few large inter-block gaps -- use median (not mean) and exclude outliers > 4x the median
- CJK: heuristic spacing rules do not apply; word segmentation requires per-language dictionaries (outside Phase 4 scope, documented as a deferred problem)
- Justified text: inter-word gaps inflate -- the adaptive threshold absorbs this naturally but document the failure mode

## Acceptance criteria

- docs/research/word-boundary-reconstruction.md updated with complete Tc/Tw/Tz formula
- Pseudo-code listing present
- Edge cases (ZWJ, combining marks, CJK, justified text, monospaced) called out
- Validation methodology specified with reference to a labelled corpus location
- File grows to approx 350+ lines from the existing 202

## References

- Plan: line 1529 (adaptive threshold + Tc/Tw/Tz reference); Phase 3.1 (graphics state machine) for Tc/Tw/Tz source operators
issue.title: Research note: docs/research/word-boundary-reconstruction.md final-pass with Tc/Tw/Tz formula

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the recursive AcroForm field walker. Starts at /Catalog /AcroForm /Fields, walks each field and its /Kids depth-first, builds the full field name as parent /T values dot-joined, and emits a flat Vec<AcroFormField> with type, name, value, default, flags, rect, page_index. Shared with 7.3.1 (signature discovery uses the same walker, filtered to /FT /Sig).

## Why this matters

The walker is the foundation of both 7.3 and 7.4. Recursive descent is the only correct way to handle nested form fields (radio button groups inside a parent group, repeating subforms in employer/employee section dividers). Dot-joined names are the standardised representation that downstream consumers (JSON, PyO3, profiles 7.10) can dereference as one flat map.

## Implementation guidance

- Entry: catalog.get(b"AcroForm").and_then(|af| af.get(b"Fields")) -> array of indirect refs to field dicts
- For each field dict, capture /T (partial name), /FT (type, inherited from parent if absent), /V (current value), /DV (default value), /Ff (flags), /Rect (widget bbox if leaf)
- Recurse into /Kids; the parent /T is prepended to each child's full name with "."
- Skip empty /T segments (e.g. "" or absent)
- Resolve widget annotation -> page mapping: for each leaf field, search every page's /Annots array for the field's indirect ref; record page_index
- Emit AcroFormField { full_name: String, field_type: AcroFieldType (enum: Tx/Btn/Ch/Sig/Other), value: Option<PdfObject>, default: Option<PdfObject>, flags: u32, rect: Option<[f32;4]>, page_index: Option<usize>, opt: Option<Vec<(String,String)>> for Ch }
- Inheritance: /FT, /V, /DV, /Ff, /DA, /Q all inherit from parent if absent

## Critical considerations

- Cycles in /Kids (malformed) -> detect via visited set; emit diagnostic; do not infinite-loop
- Field-name collisions: PDF spec forbids two leaves with the same full name, but malformed PDFs exist; emit a diagnostic and keep the LAST one (consistent with viewer behavior)
- Inherited /FT: a parent with /FT /Btn and unstamped children means all children are buttons - resolve at emission time
- Widget annotations may have /Parent pointing back to the field - handle both directions
- The walker returns ALL field types, including /Sig; 7.3 filters its consumer to /Sig only

## Acceptance criteria

- Unit tests: flat 3 fields, nested 2 levels deep, /T inheritance, /FT inheritance, name collision diagnostic
- Critical test (from plan): nested field hierarchy - full dot-separated name constructed correctly
- Shared API: walk_acroform_fields(catalog) -> Vec<AcroFormField> usable by 7.3.1
- Cycle detection prevents infinite loops on malformed input
- page_index resolution correct on multi-page forms

## References

- Plan section: 7.4 line 2609 (recursive walk + dot-join)
- PDF 1.7 spec 12.7.3 Field Dictionaries, 12.7.4 Field Types
- 7.3.1 (signature filter consumer)
- 7.4.2 (type-specific value extractor consumer)
issue.title: 7.4.1: AcroForm field walker (recursive /Fields + dot-joined names)

issue.description:
## Scope

Author the `pdftract-crates-publish` WorkflowTemplate. Triggered by milestone tag after `pdftract-build-binaries` green. Publishes `pdftract-core` to crates.io first, polls the crates.io index for propagation, then publishes `pdftract-cli` (which depends on `pdftract-core`). If `pdftract-libpdftract` ships, it is published in the same template after `pdftract-cli`.

## Why this matters

crates.io has a hard ordering requirement: a crate cannot depend on a sibling whose version is not yet visible in the registry index. Without the index-propagation wait, `pdftract-cli` publish would fail with "no matching version" 30 s after `pdftract-core` is published. This template encapsulates the brittle waiting logic so release engineers do not hand-execute it.

## Implementation guidance

- Inputs: tag name (e.g. `v0.3.0`), api token from ESO Secret `crates-io-token-pdftract` (synced from OpenBao key `crates-io-token-pdftract`)
- DAG nodes:
  1. `publish-core`: `cargo publish -p pdftract-core --locked --token $TOKEN`
  2. `wait-index-core`: poll `https://index.crates.io/pd/ft/pdftract-core` until the just-published version appears (5-min timeout, 10 s poll interval)
  3. `publish-cli`: `cargo publish -p pdftract-cli --locked --token $TOKEN`
  4. `wait-index-cli` (optional, only if a downstream step needs to see it indexed)
  5. (optional) `publish-libpdftract`: same pattern, after `publish-cli`
- Container: `rust:1.78-slim` (matches MSRV)
- Use `--dry-run` first on a non-tag manual run for sanity testing; the production workflow runs without `--dry-run`
- crates.io rejects duplicate publishes; a re-run after partial failure is safe — the first crate's publish step will fail with "already uploaded" which the workflow MUST treat as success and continue

## Critical considerations

- ADR-009: no GitHub Actions; crates.io publish runs on iad-ci with the API token from OpenBao -> ESO -> Secret
- The index-propagation wait CANNOT be skipped — crates.io's sparse index has up to 60 s of propagation delay even on green API responses
- The crates.io API token is rotated every 90 days; rotation runbook in `docs/operations/secrets-rotation.md`; ESO auto-resyncs within 60 s
- Partial publish leaves a half-published version recoverable via `cargo yank`; the template documents the `cargo yank --vers X.Y.Z pdftract-core` recovery command
- `pdftract-py` is `publish = false` and is NEVER published to crates.io (it goes to PyPI via `pdftract-py-ci`)
- The template gates `pdftract-cli` strictly on `pdftract-core` index propagation; the workflow MUST not race ahead

## Acceptance criteria

- WorkflowTemplate file lands at `k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/pdftract-crates-publish.yaml` in `jedarden/declarative-config`
- A test run against a fresh tag publishes pdftract-core first, then pdftract-cli, in strict order
- The index-propagation wait succeeds within 5 min on the happy path
- A duplicate-publish retry returns 0 (idempotent)
- A re-run after partial failure recovers without manual intervention beyond `cargo yank` for the half-published version

## References

- Plan section: Release Engineering / Argo WorkflowTemplates, line 3391
- Plan section: Distribution Channels, line 3374
- ADR-009 (no GitHub Actions)
- crates.io index documentation: https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/registry-index.html
- Sibling: pdftract-libpdftract publish bead under the SDK Architecture epic
issue.title: Argo WorkflowTemplate: pdftract-crates-publish (core first, wait for index, then cli)

issue.description:
## Scope

Hand-written JSON-RPC 2.0 implementation shared by the stdio and HTTP+SSE transports of the MCP server. No separate crate dependency: JSON-RPC's wire format is small enough (Request, Response, Notification, ErrorObject) that a hand-rolled module is smaller, easier to audit, and one fewer dep in the supply chain than e.g. jsonrpc-core or jsonrpsee.

Module: crates/pdftract-cli/src/mcp/framing/ with:
- mod.rs: Request, Response, Notification, ErrorObject, BatchMessage enums
- serde_json-backed (re)serialization with strict id-type preservation (number vs. string vs. null)
- Error code constants: -32700 ParseError, -32600 InvalidRequest, -32601 MethodNotFound, -32602 InvalidParams, -32603 InternalError, plus implementation-defined range -32099..-32000 reserved for pdftract-specific errors

## Why this matters

Both transports parse the same JSON-RPC envelope; only the framing differs (Content-Length headers for stdio vs. HTTP request body + SSE event). Centralizing the envelope types means a single audit point for spec conformance (e.g. id field MUST preserve its JSON type; jsonrpc field is the literal string \"2.0\"; method MUST be a string; params are optional but if present must be array or object).

A subtle MCP-spec gotcha: id field MUST be returned in the response with the same JSON type as received. JSON-RPC 2.0 allows id to be number, string, or null; treating them all as Option<i64> silently corrupts string-id clients. The framing module enforces id type preservation via a Value-typed Id variant.

## Implementation guidance

- Define id as enum Id { Number(i64), String(String), Null }; derive Serialize, Deserialize, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash
- Define Request { jsonrpc: \"2.0\" literal validated on deserialize, method: String, params: Option<Value>, id: Option<Id> }
- Define Response { jsonrpc: \"2.0\", result: Option<Value>, error: Option<ErrorObject>, id: Id } — exactly one of result or error is present (mutually exclusive; enforce in serializer with custom Serialize impl or post-construction validator)
- Define Notification { jsonrpc, method, params: Option<Value> } — no id field
- Define ErrorObject { code: i64, message: String, data: Option<Value> }
- Batch support: serde untagged enum BatchMessage::Single(Request) | BatchMessage::Batch(Vec<Request>); responses to batches are batched in the same shape
- Constructor helpers: Response::success(id, result), Response::error(id, ErrorObject), ErrorObject::method_not_found(\"name\"), etc.

## Critical considerations

- jsonrpc field MUST be the literal string \"2.0\" — reject \"1.0\", \"2\", or missing on deserialize with a custom Deserialize that returns a serde error
- id MUST preserve type on the response — never coerce string-id 123 to number-id 123 or vice versa
- Notifications (no id) MUST NOT receive a response, even on error. The transport layer drops the response message when the original request had no id.
- Parse-error responses (-32700) have id: null because the request couldn't be parsed enough to extract its id. All other error responses include the original id.
- Method names like \"rpc.\"-prefixed are reserved by the spec; pdftract tools use unprefixed names (tools/list, tools/call, etc.) per the MCP spec convention with slash-separated namespaces
- Batch with empty array is an invalid request per spec; return a single error response (not a batched response) with code -32600

## Acceptance criteria

- Round-trip test: serialize Request { method: \"tools/list\", params: None, id: Id::Number(1) } → bytes → deserialize → equal Request
- ID preservation test: Id::String(\"abc\") and Id::Number(42) and Id::Null all round-trip with no type change
- Parse-error path: malformed JSON input → Response { error: Some(ErrorObject { code: -32700, ... }), id: Id::Null }
- Method-not-found path: ErrorObject::method_not_found(\"unknown\") produces { code: -32601, message: \"Method not found\", data: Some(\"unknown\") }
- Notification path: Notification has no id field in its serialized output; deserialize of {\"jsonrpc\":\"2.0\",\"method\":\"x\"} yields Notification (not Request with id: None)
- Batch round-trip: BatchMessage::Batch with 3 requests serializes to a 3-element JSON array; deserializes back to the same shape
- Unit tests cover all 6 spec-defined error codes and all 3 id type variants
- jsonrpc field validation: deserialize of {\"jsonrpc\":\"1.0\",\"method\":\"x\",\"id\":1} fails with a clear error

## References

- Plan section: Phase 6.7 MCP Server Mode (lines 2286-2349)
- JSON-RPC 2.0 spec: https://www.jsonrpc.org/specification
- MCP spec: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/spec
- INV-9 (stdout discipline — depends on framing module separating parse errors from transport errors)
Labels: framing, mcp, phase-6, rpc
issue.title: 6.7.1: JSON-RPC 2.0 framing layer (shared by stdio + HTTP)

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement 3x3 median-filter denoising as the post-binarization noise-removal step. Removes salt-and-pepper noise typical of physical scans without blurring character edges. Wired by the 5.3 preprocessing pipeline coordinator.

Module: crates/pdftract-core/src/ocr/preprocessing/denoise.rs.

## Why this matters

Salt-and-pepper noise (single black/white pixels scattered across an otherwise clean image) confuses Tesseract: each noise pixel may be misclassified as a character or fragment. Median filter removes isolated pixels without affecting the edges of legitimate characters (which are surrounded by like-colored neighbors).

## Implementation guidance

- Crate: imageproc (already in deps)
- Signature:
  ```rust
  pub fn median_denoise(image: &GrayImage) -> GrayImage
  ```
- Algorithm:
  ```rust
  use imageproc::filter::median_filter;
  median_filter(image, 1, 1)  // 3x3 = (2*1+1)x(2*1+1)
  ```
- Order in preprocessing pipeline: contrast normalization (5.3.2) → binarization (sibling Sauvola/Otsu) → THIS denoise
- Skip rule: image source is JBIG2 → no-op (already clean; JBIG2 compression is bitonal lossless)
- 3x3 kernel: small enough to preserve character strokes (typical stroke width 3-5 px at 300 DPI); larger kernels (5x5) blur characters

## Critical considerations

- imageproc::filter::median_filter takes radius x and y (1, 1 = 3x3); kernel size is (2r+1)x(2r+1)
- median filter for binary images is fast: O(N) since the median of 9 binary values is a majority vote
- Median is preferred over Gaussian for binary noise: Gaussian smooths character edges (bad for OCR); median preserves them
- The denoise step is OPTIONAL for born-digital images (already clean); the 5.3 dispatcher (sibling 2s0c) skips for JBIG2; could also skip for DigitalOrigin in a future optimization

## Acceptance criteria

- Image with salt-and-pepper noise denoised cleanly (verified visually + WER improvement)
- Character edges preserved (no rounded corners on letterforms)
- Output is binary (matches input binarity)
- Benchmark: 1080p denoised in < 100ms
- JBIG2 input → no-op (passed through unchanged)

## References

- Plan section: Phase 5.3.3
- imageproc::filter::median_filter
- Coordinator: pdftract-4lwe (parent)
- Sibling: Sauvola, Otsu
Labels: denoise, phase-5, preprocessing
issue.title: 5.3.3c: Median-filter denoise (3x3 kernel; imageproc::filter::median_filter)

issue.description:
## Scope

When --progress-json is set, suppress the indicatif bar and instead emit one JSON object per line to stderr for each progress event: start, file_start, file_progress, file_done, done. The schema mirrors the plan's example exactly. Used by Argo Workflows logs and other CI/automation contexts where a TTY bar is useless but progress observability is still required.

## Why this matters

CI runners (Argo Workflows, GitHub Actions, etc.) don't have TTYs but they do log stderr; without --progress-json, a long-running grep produces zero output until done, which looks like a hang. The JSON event stream gives the Argo log a steady heartbeat that automation tools (CI alarms, watchdog scripts) can parse to detect actual stalls. Same observability contract as the TTY bar (>= every 500 ms event when work is happening).

## Implementation guidance

- Schema (events):
  - { event: "start", files_total: u64, bytes_total: u64, started_at: RFC3339 timestamp }
  - { event: "file_start", path: String, size: u64 }
  - { event: "file_progress", path: String, pages_done: u32, pages_total: u32 }
  - { event: "file_done", path: String, matches: u32, duration_ms: u64 }
  - { event: "file_skipped", path: String, reason: String }  (encrypted, parse failure)
  - { event: "slow_file", path: String, elapsed_secs: u64 }
  - { event: "done", files_processed: u64, matches_total: u64, duration_ms: u64 }
- Emit one JSON object per line, line-terminated by \n (LF only)
- All events go to stderr (so they don't conflict with stdout JSON-Lines from --json output)
- --progress-json implies --no-progress (bar off; events are the alternative)
- file_progress throttled to one event per page (or one per 500 ms when many pages process per file - throttle in sink consumer)
- started_at uses chrono::Utc::now().to_rfc3339(); chrono is OK to add (transitive via existing deps in many cases)
- Compatible with the TTY bar's watchdog: a separate atomic ticker for events guarantees the 500 ms heartbeat even when no work-derived event has occurred (synthetic file_progress with same numbers, OR a heartbeat event)

## Critical considerations

- --progress-json mutually exclusive with --progress; both can be passed but --progress-json wins (bar suppressed)
- Schema is stable: events listed above MUST appear with those exact field names (downstream automation parses them)
- Backwards compat for future event additions: schema is open (additional fields allowed); new event types can be added
- file_progress throttling: one event per page is fine for typical 100-page PDFs; for 10000-page PDFs, throttle to >= 100ms between events to avoid flooding stderr
- All event objects MUST validate against a JSON Schema; ship docs/schema/v1.0/grep-progress.schema.json

## Acceptance criteria

- Critical test (from plan): all expected event types emitted in order
- Events emit to stderr; --json stdout output uncontaminated
- 500 ms heartbeat guarantee verified by integration test (artificial slow file)
- started_at RFC3339 format
- docs/schema/v1.0/grep-progress.schema.json validates emitted events
- --progress-json suppresses TTY bar

## References

- Plan section: 7.8 lines 2729 (--progress-json flag), 2766-2775 (event examples), 2785 (CI use case)
- 7.8.4 (ProgressEvent source)
- 7.8.8 (TTY bar alternative)
- docs/schema/v1.0/grep-progress.schema.json (new schema file)
issue.title: 7.8.9: --progress-json machine-readable events to stderr
