issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the text_operator_presence signal evaluator: a pure function over PageContext that returns Signal { name: \"text_operator_presence\", strength, vote: PageClass } based on text-operator count and image-coverage. Maps 0 text ops + has images -> Scanned with strength 0.95.

## Why this matters

This is the strongest single signal for scanned PDFs: a page with image XObjects but ZERO text-drawing operators (Tj, TJ, ', \", T*) is almost certainly a pure scan. The strength 0.95 means this signal short-circuits the evaluator chain when it fires.

## Implementation guidance

- Signature:
  ```rust
  pub fn text_operator_presence(ctx: &PageContext) -> Option<Signal>
  ```
- Logic:
  ```rust
  if ctx.text_op_count == 0 && !ctx.image_xobject_areas.is_empty() {
      return Some(Signal { name: \"text_operator_presence\", strength: 0.95, vote: PageClass::Scanned });
  }
  None
  ```
- Returns None when signal does not fire (allows next evaluator in chain to run)
- Pure function; no side effects; deterministic

## Critical considerations

- Tj, TJ, ', \" all count as text operators; the content stream operator inventory is in PageContext.text_op_count (Phase 1 collects this)
- image_xobject_areas is a Vec of bboxes (parallel to placement records); empty Vec means no images
- A page with 0 text ops AND 0 images is blank; falls through to blank handling elsewhere (this evaluator returns None for blank pages)
- Short-circuit at 0.95: if this signal fires, the classifier's main loop stops here

## Acceptance criteria

- text_op_count=0 + image_xobject_areas=[bbox1] → Some(Signal { strength: 0.95, vote: Scanned })
- text_op_count=10 + images → None (text-bearing page)
- text_op_count=0 + no images → None (blank; handled elsewhere)
- Unit test for each case

## References

- Plan section: Phase 5.1.2
- Coordinator: pdftract-22p (parent — 5 signal evaluators)
- Sibling: 4 other evaluators
Labels: classifier, phase-5, signal
issue.title: Signal evaluator: text_operator_presence (0 text ops + has images -> Scanned)

issue.description:
## Scope

Author tests/fixtures/profiles/PROVENANCE.md as the canonical attribution and licensing manifest for every fixture file across tests/fixtures/profiles/ AND tests/fixtures/classifier/ AND tests/fixtures/security/. Every fixture source MUST be public-domain or open-licensed; no leaked confidential data. A pre-commit hook (or CI test) verifies that every fixture file has a PROVENANCE entry.

## Why this matters

Fixtures with confidential or proprietary content in a public repository would be a public disclosure incident -- comparable to a secrets-in-code leak. The plan is explicit: PROFILE_SECRETS_FORBIDDEN catches profile YAML with secrets; PROVENANCE.md catches PDF fixtures with proprietary content. The licensing audit also protects the project from copyright claims (a fixture pulled from a paywalled journal would expose the project).

## Implementation guidance

- File to create: tests/fixtures/profiles/PROVENANCE.md (one canonical location; covers fixtures across all of tests/fixtures/profiles, classifier, security, malformed)
- Format: a table with one row per fixture file:
  | path | source_url | license | downloaded_date | sha256 | notes |
- License entries MUST be from the approved list: public-domain (PD), CC0-1.0, CC-BY-3.0, CC-BY-4.0, CC-BY-SA-3.0, CC-BY-SA-4.0, US-government (federal documents typically PD), Apache-2.0, MIT (rare for documents); reject GPL/LGPL/AGPL for fixtures (we do not want the GPL viral terms to attach to test data)
- The downloaded_date is the date the file was retrieved; if older than 1 year, a re-verification step should be triggered (the source URL may have changed terms)
- The sha256 is the content hash; if a fixture changes, the sha256 changes and the provenance row must be updated
- Generation script: scripts/check-provenance.sh enumerates every fixture file under tests/fixtures/, looks up each in PROVENANCE.md, asserts a row exists with a matching sha256; fails the build on mismatch
- Per-fixture notes column: any caveats (e.g. "shrunk via qpdf --optimize-images=jpeg-compress to reduce repo size", "redacted personal details by replacing all names with John Doe")

## Critical considerations

- The sha256 is load-bearing -- if a fixture is regenerated and the row is not updated, the script catches it; this prevents accidentally swapping a public-domain fixture with a proprietary one
- For synthetic fixtures (generated by a build script), the provenance row says "synthetic, generated by <script>, public-domain" and lists the script as the source_url
- For partially-derived fixtures (e.g. a public-domain PDF with synthetic redactions applied), the row lists both the original source and the derivation script
- The check-provenance.sh script runs in CI as a Phase 0 gate (analogous to the supply-chain checks)
- Anyone adding a fixture without updating PROVENANCE.md will have their PR fail
- The misc category in the classifier corpus needs PROVENANCE rows even for the most-mundane fixtures (a sample receipt template is still a fixture)
- TH-NN security fixtures (xss-payload.pdf, embedded-js.pdf, sensitive.pdf, bomb-10k-2g.pdf, password-protected.pdf) are all synthetic and need rows pointing at their generation scripts

## Acceptance criteria

- tests/fixtures/profiles/PROVENANCE.md exists with one row per fixture file
- Every fixture file under tests/fixtures/ is enumerated; no orphans
- License column populated for every row; only approved licenses appear
- sha256 column populated; matches the actual file content
- scripts/check-provenance.sh validates the manifest against the filesystem; CI gate green
- Synthetic-fixture rows point at their generation scripts as the source_url

## References

- Plan: line 833 (per-threat fixture mandate), Phase 5.6 corpus acceptance criteria (lines 1973-1988), supply-chain table (line 891 -- parallel checksum policy for build-time data files)
issue.title: Provenance manifest tests/fixtures/profiles/PROVENANCE.md (public-domain / open-license attribution for every fixture)

issue.description:
## Scope

Define the Receipt struct and its lite-mode JSON serialization. Lite-mode receipts contain exactly five fields per span: pdf_fingerprint, page_index, bbox, content_hash, extraction_version. Lite-mode is the cheapest form (~120 bytes per receipt before JSON overhead) and is suitable for attaching to every span in audit logs and RAG citation pipelines.

Module: crates/pdftract-core/src/receipts/lite.rs and the shared Receipt type in crates/pdftract-core/src/receipts/mod.rs.

## Why this matters

The Receipt type is the data model the entire phase rests on; SVG mode (sibling 6.8.2) is an extension that adds the svg_clip field, and the verifier protocol (sibling 6.8.4) consumes the same shape. Getting the field set wrong (e.g. omitting content_hash, or using a non-canonical hash form) forces a breaking schema change later. Lock the schema here and version it via extraction_version.

NFC normalization of the text before hashing is the most easy-to-miss subtlety: macOS HFS+/APFS sometimes round-trips through NFD, and Python's json.dumps on a string read from such a file produces a different content_hash than the same text read from ext4. NFC normalization makes content_hash stable across platforms.

## Implementation guidance

- Define:
  ```rust
  pub struct Receipt {
      pub pdf_fingerprint: String,    // Phase 1.7 fingerprint, prefixed: \"pdftract-v1:...\"
      pub page_index: usize,          // 0-based, matches Phase 6.1 schema
      pub bbox: [f64; 4],             // [x0, y0, x1, y1] in PDF points; copies the parent span's bbox
      pub content_hash: String,       // \"sha256:<hex>\" of NFC-normalized text
      pub extraction_version: String, // semver of pdftract that produced this receipt
      pub svg_clip: Option<String>,   // None in lite mode; Some(svg) in svg mode (sibling 6.8.2)
  }
  ```
- Constructor: Receipt::lite(pdf_fingerprint, page_index, bbox, text, extraction_version) — computes content_hash internally
- content_hash computation:
  ```rust
  use unicode_normalization::UnicodeNormalization;
  let nfc: String = text.nfc().collect();
  let hash = sha2::Sha256::digest(nfc.as_bytes());
  format!(\"sha256:{}\", hex::encode(hash))
  ```
- Use unicode-normalization crate (already a default dep for Phase 3 Unicode resolution)
- extraction_version is env!(\"CARGO_PKG_VERSION\") at compile time
- serde Serialize/Deserialize derive; svg_clip is #[serde(skip_serializing_if = \"Option::is_none\")] so lite-mode output does NOT include the key (saves bytes; cleaner schema)
- Receipt is wired into the SpanJson and BlockJson types from Phase 6.1 as an Option<Receipt> field with #[serde(skip_serializing_if = \"Option::is_none\")]

## Critical considerations

- NFC normalization is mandatory before hashing; do not hash raw bytes or NFD text. unicode-normalization::UnicodeNormalization::nfc() is the canonical impl
- pdf_fingerprint format must match the Phase 1.7 output exactly, including the \"pdftract-v1:\" prefix — the verifier (sibling 6.8.4) compares strings, not parsed structures
- bbox is [x0, y0, x1, y1] in PDF user-space points; same coordinate system as the parent span (NOT page coordinates, NOT clipped to page box)
- extraction_version uses semver; format is the literal CARGO_PKG_VERSION value (e.g. \"1.0.0\", \"1.0.0-rc.1\")
- Adding receipt: null placeholders in the JSON schema when --receipts=off is required so downstream consumers see a stable shape (plan line 2410)
- Receipt size in lite mode is dominated by the two hex strings (fingerprint ~70 bytes including prefix, content_hash 71 bytes including \"sha256:\" prefix); aim for total JSON size ~150-180 bytes per receipt

## Acceptance criteria

- Receipt::lite(...) produces a Receipt with svg_clip == None
- serde_json::to_string on a lite Receipt produces JSON without the svg_clip key (asserted in unit test)
- content_hash for a string round-trips: extract → hash → re-extract → hash → equal
- content_hash for NFC vs NFD forms of the same logical string produces the SAME hash (test with U+00E9 vs U+0065 U+0301)
- content_hash for two textually-different strings differs (sanity test)
- 100 receipts on a 100-page document: aggregate JSON size increase <= 15 KB (plan acceptance criterion)
- Receipt is wired into SpanJson and BlockJson from Phase 6.1 via Option<Receipt> field
- Documentation comments on each field explain the units, base, and format

## References

- Plan section: Phase 6.8 Visual Citation Receipts (lines 2351-2417, especially 2357-2384)
- Phase 1.7 fingerprint format (\"pdftract-v1:...\" prefix)
- Phase 6.1 SpanJson + BlockJson schemas (receipt field is added here)
- unicode-normalization crate: https://crates.io/crates/unicode-normalization
- INV-3 deterministic Unicode resolution
Labels: lite, phase-6, receipts, schema

issue.description:
## Scope

Extract from PDFs hosted in cloud storage without downloading the full file. Cuts bandwidth by 95%+ for partial-page extractions from large documents. Enables `pdftract extract https://...` and `pdftract grep https://...`.

Architecture change to Phase 1: replace the implicit `memmap2`-only I/O assumption with a `PdfSource` trait abstracting random access. Three implementations:
- MmapSource: memory-mapped local file (default; behavior unchanged from original Phase 1 spec)
- FileSource: plain Read+Seek over File (fallback when mmap fails — FUSE mounts, /proc, named pipes)
- HttpRangeSource: HTTP Range: request reader with a bounded LRU page-cache of 64 × 64 KB blocks (4 MB total per document)

Feature flag: `remote` (default OFF; adds ureq ~500 KB). Per ADR-001, ureq chosen over reqwest for binary size: no async runtime, rustls backend, no native TLS dependency.

Child beads:
- PdfSource trait + MmapSource + FileSource implementations
- HttpRangeSource implementation with LRU page-cache
- HTTP fetch sequence (HEAD probe -> tail Range fetch -> page-by-page on-demand)
- Server fallback for non-Range servers (temp-file download + memory-map)
- Authentication (URL-embedded basic, --header flag for custom; SigV4 deferred)
- --pages RANGE CLI flag (cross-cuts 6.1; 1-based comma-separated ranges)
- Linearized PDF hint stream parser + prefetch optimization
- Remote source test corpus (mock HTTP server with various scenarios)

## Why this matters

The remote source adapter is a TIER-1 differentiator: pdftract is the only PDF extractor that can extract specific pages from a remote 500-page PDF with < 5 MB downloaded. Without it, users must download the full file. The PdfSource trait also enables future S3/GCS/Azure-blob sources via the same interface.

## Critical considerations

- Per ADR-001: ureq 0.10 with rustls feature; chosen for binary size budget (R2)
- Per ADR-008: forward-scan xref fallback is DISABLED for remote sources (would require downloading the entire file); wired into Phase 1.3's forward-scan bead
- Per Dependency Matrix: `pdftract:full` Docker image includes `remote`; default-feature binary does NOT
- HTTP fetch sequence:
  1. HEAD request -> record content-length and verify Accept-Ranges: bytes
  2. Initial Range: bytes=-16384 (tail) -> parse startxref, trailer, root xref subsection
  3. As objects are dereferenced, fetch the byte range per page on demand
  4. Resources (fonts, XObjects) fetched lazily and cached for document lifetime
  5. Cross-reference streams (PDF 1.5+) fetched when traditional xref is unavailable
- Server fallback: if Accept-Ranges absent OR Range request returns 200 instead of 206 -> emit REMOTE_NO_RANGE_SUPPORT and fall back to streaming the entire response body into a temp file, then memory-map
- Authentication:
  - HTTPS basic via URL credentials (https://user:pass@host/path)
  - Custom headers via --header repeatable flag
  - S3 (SigV4) DEFERRED to a future `s3` feature
- CLI flag --pages RANGE cross-cuts Phase 6.1: comma-separated 1-based ranges (e.g. 1-5,7,12-); default all; out-of-range emits PAGE_OUT_OF_RANGE

## Acceptance criteria

- All 8 child beads closed
- All Acceptance criteria from plan Section 1.8 pass:
  - 500-page PDF on remote server: extract pages 47-52 only with total downloaded < 5 MB
  - Server without Range: fall back to temp-file download, emit warning, complete
  - Network failure mid-extraction: partial result + REMOTE_FETCH_INTERRUPTED, no panic, exit 5
  - TLS-handshake failure: clear error with cert chain reason; exit 6
- All Critical tests from plan Section 1.8 pass (5 mock-server tests)
- Module under `crates/pdftract-core/src/source/` (mmap.rs, file.rs, http.rs)
- Feature `remote` adds ureq 0.10 + rustls; binary size delta < 500 KB

## References

- Plan section: Phase 1.8 Remote Source Adapter, lines 1221-1279
- ADR-001 (ureq over reqwest)
- ADR-008 (forward-scan disabled for remote)
- Dependency Matrix: ureq 0.10 (remote feature)
- INV-8
- Phase 1.3, Phase 6.1

## Scope

Author docs/operations/manual-platform-smoke.md as the KU-12 quarterly platform smoke-test runbook: the release lead executes this against at least one physical macOS machine and one Windows VM before each milestone tag, and a failure blocks the milestone.

## Why this matters

KU-12 line 590 explicitly mandates this runbook: Manual quarterly smoke-test runbook in docs/operations/manual-platform-smoke.md. ADR-009 (line 482) acknowledges that macOS and Windows binaries are built via cross on Linux but never runtime-tested in CI -- the manual smoke is the compensating control. Without a documented, repeatable runbook, the smoke test is folklore and milestones ship with no real platform verification.

## Implementation guidance

- File to create: docs/operations/manual-platform-smoke.md
- Required content sections:
  - Prerequisites:
    - macOS: at least one physical machine (M-series and Intel both ideal); access via SSH or in-person
    - Windows: a clean VM (recommend a fresh Windows 11 install in VirtualBox/Parallels/HyperV; do NOT reuse a developer machine because dev tooling masks Gatekeeper/SmartScreen behaviour)
    - Test PDFs: pull from tests/fixtures/ -- pick one each of vector, scanned, encrypted, large (1000+ pages), with-attachments, with-OCR
  - Per-platform smoke checklist (step-by-step):
    1. Download the macos / windows binary from the GitHub Release page (the actual user path; do NOT scp the artifact)
    2. Verify the SHA-256 against the published .sha256 file
    3. Run the binary with no args -- check that --help returns sensibly
    4. Run pdftract extract sample.pdf > out.json -- check exit 0
    5. Validate out.json against docs/schema/v1.0/pdftract.schema.json
    6. Run pdftract extract --auto sample-invoice.pdf -- check profile_name field present
    7. Run pdftract mcp --stdio and exchange a list-tools handshake (script provided)
    8. Run pdftract inspect sample.pdf --no-open -- check inspector launches
    9. Run pdftract grep --include='*.pdf' "Invoice" tests/fixtures/profiles/invoice/ -- check matches reported
    10. On macOS: check that Gatekeeper does NOT block the binary (or document the bypass path)
    11. On Windows: check that SmartScreen does NOT block the binary (or document the bypass path)
  - Failure recording template: a markdown table to fill in (date, release tag, platform, step number, observed behaviour, blocking yes/no, follow-up bead ID)
  - Sign-off rules: release lead signs off; a single blocking failure blocks the milestone tag

## Critical considerations

- The runbook MUST be executable verbatim by someone who is NOT the release lead -- this is a continuity plan, not a personal checklist
- macOS Gatekeeper behaviour changes with each major macOS version; the runbook should note the macOS version against which it was last validated
- Windows SmartScreen behaviour changes with each Windows Defender definition update; same caveat
- The 11-step checklist is the v1.0.0 minimum; add steps as features ship (e.g. when Phase 7.9 inspector ships, step 8 becomes required)
- Sign-off MUST be recorded in the CHANGELOG (parallel to the PB-13 manual release procedure record) so that "we shipped without smoke test" is auditable

## Acceptance criteria

- docs/operations/manual-platform-smoke.md exists with the four sections above
- Per-platform step-by-step checklist present with all 11 steps
- Failure recording template present
- Sign-off rules documented
- Cross-references to KU-12, ADR-009, and docs/schema/v1.0/pdftract.schema.json present
- The runbook is verbatim-executable by a non-author

## References

- Plan: line 482 (ADR-009 CI scope), line 590 (KU-12), line 3413-3419 (Cross-Platform Test Limitation section)

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the `bench-matrix` DAG branch in `pdftract-ci` that runs head-to-head benchmarks against three pinned competitor tools:

- `pdfminer.six==20231228`
- `pypdf==4.2.0`
- `pdfplumber==0.11.0`

All four (pdftract + 3 competitors) are timed via `hyperfine --warmup 2 --runs 5` against a fixed `benches/competitors/corpus/` of representative PDFs (~50 documents from the regression corpus: 25 vector PDFs + 25 OCR-required raster PDFs). Results published as an Argo artifact `benchmark-results.json` and as a markdown comment on the PR via the `argo-workflows-pr-commenter` sidecar.

Failure conditions (any one blocks merge):
- Regression > 10% on `pdftract-grep-1000` benchmark vs. previous main-branch baseline
- `pdftract` not >= 10x faster than `pdfminer.six` on any vector PDF (CI-gated; PHASE 0 hard gate)

## Why this matters

Speed is one of pdftract's three differentiators (per Mission). Without competitive benchmarks in CI, performance regressions slip through reviews and the >= 10x-faster-than-pdfminer commitment from the plan's hard gates erodes silently.

## Implementation guidance

- Bench runner image: `python:3.11-slim-bookworm` extended with `apt-get install -y hyperfine` and `pip install -r benches/competitors/requirements.txt` (the three competitors pinned at the versions above)
- requirements.txt is canonical; updates require a deliberate PR with manual baseline refresh
- pdftract binary: use the `x86_64-unknown-linux-musl` artifact produced by Phase 0.2 (NOT a fresh build — production-shaped binary)
- Corpus: `benches/competitors/corpus/` — committed to the repo; ~10 MB total; 50 documents
- Per-tool wrapper script: `benches/competitors/run-<tool>.sh` invokes the tool with equivalent flags (extract-text mode, all pages)
- hyperfine invocation per (tool, doc) pair: `hyperfine --warmup 2 --runs 5 --export-json result.json -- "<wrapper> <doc>"`
- Aggregate results into `benchmark-results.json` with schema `{tool, doc, mean_ms, stddev_ms, min_ms, max_ms}` then compute per-tool geo-mean across all docs
- Baseline: `benches/baselines/main.json` is committed; the PR baseline is `git show main:benches/baselines/main.json`; the regression comparison is `(pr_geomean - base_geomean) / base_geomean`
- Special benchmark `pdftract-grep-1000`: run `pdftract grep "the" benches/corpus/wikipedia-1000.pdf` 5 times; regression > 10% blocks PR

## Critical considerations

- Hyperfine variance on Spot infra can be high; the 5-run sample + geomean across the corpus is the noise-reduction strategy. Per-document p95 deltas are NOT gated individually (too noisy)
- Cold-start vs warm-start: hyperfine's `--warmup 2` discards the first 2 runs to amortize page-cache loading
- Pin Python version (3.11) and competitor versions explicitly; floating versions would invalidate baselines monthly
- Some competitors crash on certain documents (e.g. pypdf on heavily encrypted PDFs); the runner must catch crashes and emit a per-tool/per-doc `crash: true` entry instead of a numeric time; competitor crashes do NOT block the pdftract PR
- 10x-faster gate: per Phase 0 plan, pdftract must be >= 10x faster than pdfminer.six on vector PDFs. The gate is `pdftract_geomean / pdfminer_geomean <= 0.1` across the 25 vector docs in the corpus
- Provide the markdown PR comment via the `argo-workflows-pr-commenter` sidecar (already present on iad-ci); format: a 4-row table per-tool with geo-mean ms + 95% CI

## Acceptance criteria

- `bench-matrix` step appears in the WorkflowTemplate DAG and runs on every PR
- All 4 tools time successfully on >= 90% of the corpus (>= 45/50 docs)
- `benchmark-results.json` artifact published every run
- A PR with a deliberate 50% slowdown to pdftract trips the regression gate
- A PR that makes pdftract <10x faster than pdfminer trips the 10x gate
- PR comment with benchmark table appears within 60 s of run completion

## References

- Plan section: Phase 0, line 1007 (Tier 4 benchmarks)
- Quality Targets, Tier 4 (competitive bench hard gate)
- Mission (speed differentiator)

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement `Do name` operator: look up the named XObject via ResourceStack; if /Subtype is /Form, fetch and decode its content stream, push a fresh graphics state (q), apply the form's /Matrix to CTM, push a new ResourceStack scope (if form has own /Resources), execute the form's content stream recursively, pop the resource scope, pop the graphics state (Q). If /Subtype is /Image, treat as image (no glyphs produced, Phase 5 image extraction handles it).

## Why this matters

Do is the recursion point of the content stream interpreter. Without correct application of /Matrix, scaled/transformed forms produce wrong-positioned glyphs. Without nested execution, content reuse via forms is invisible to the extractor. Skipping image XObjects (the OTHER /Subtype) without confusing the parser is required for any PDF with embedded images.

## Implementation guidance

- Pop the Name from operand stack.
- ResourceStack::lookup_xobject(name) -> Option<Arc<XObject>>. If None, emit XOBJECT_RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND, return.
- Dispatch on /Subtype:
  - `/Form`: invoke nested executor.
  - `/Image`: skip text emission but ALWAYS record an `ImageXObject { bbox: current_ctm * unit_square }` in the page's image list for Phase 4.4 figure-block detection.
  - Other: emit XOBJECT_UNKNOWN_SUBTYPE, skip.
- Form execution sequence (mirrors `q ... cm ... contents ... Q`):
  1. cycle check: if `xobject_id` in current execution stack, emit STRUCT_XOBJECT_CYCLE, return.
  2. depth check: if stack depth >= 20, emit STRUCT_XOBJECT_DEPTH_EXCEEDED, return.
  3. Push xobject_id onto cycle-detection stack.
  4. Save graphics state (q).
  5. Apply /Matrix to CTM (cm).
  6. If form has /Resources: push new ResourceStack scope.
  7. Decode and execute form's content stream (recursive call to executor).
  8. Pop ResourceStack scope (if pushed).
  9. Restore graphics state (Q).
  10. Pop xobject_id from cycle-detection stack.
- /BBox clipping: for v0.1.0, IGNORE (we don't render); record /BBox on the XObject for diagnostics only.

## Critical considerations

- INV: nested execution shares the same per-page state (raw_glyph_list grows from the nested glyphs too; q/Q stack is shared).
- The form's content stream may be a Stream object whose /Length must be honored; reuse Phase 1 stream decoder.
- /Matrix default is [1 0 0 1 0 0] (identity); apply unconditionally.
- Forms can contain Tf operators that re-bind the current font to a form-resource font; this is correct behavior (different fonts in different scopes).
- Image XObject detection: must add to page's image list with bbox in PAGE coordinates (CTM-transformed unit square 0..1, 0..1) so Phase 4.4 can locate figures.

## Acceptance criteria

- Do invoking a form with own /Resources /Font: nested Tj uses form's font.
- Do invoking a form with /Matrix [2 0 0 2 0 0]: nested glyph bboxes 2x larger than form-space coordinates would suggest.
- Do invoking image XObject: no glyphs added; page image list grows by 1 entry with correct bbox.
- Do for unknown XObject name: diagnostic emitted, execution continues.
- Form with empty content stream: no crash, no glyphs.

## References

- Plan section: Phase 3.3 Form XObject execution (line 1567)
issue.title: Do operator: form XObject lookup, /Matrix application, nested execution

issue.description:
## Scope

Author the `pdftract-node-publish` WorkflowTemplate. Triggered by milestone tag after `pdftract-build-binaries` completes. Builds the `@pdftract/sdk` package (dual ESM + CJS), runs the conformance test suite against the bundled binary, publishes to npm.

## Why this matters

Without an automated publish workflow, the Node.js SDK requires manual publishing per milestone — a 5-minute task that gets skipped under deadline pressure and breaks the "SDK ships within 24 hours of binary release" acceptance criterion. The Argo cascade encapsulates the gating (conformance pass) and the auth (npm token from OpenBao).

## Implementation guidance

- WorkflowTemplate file: `k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/pdftract-node-publish.yaml` in `jedarden/declarative-config`
- Inputs: tag name; npm token from ESO Secret `npm-token-pdftract` (synced from OpenBao key `npm-token-pdftract`)
- Steps:
  1. `clone-sdk-repo`: `git clone https://github.com/jedarden/pdftract-node.git --branch main`
  2. `sync-version`: bump `package.json` version to match the binary tag; commit and push the bump (a separate maintenance PR if the SDK is in a separate repo per the plan's "Each SDK lives in its own git repository" requirement)
  3. `install-deps`: `npm ci` (uses package-lock.json for reproducibility)
  4. `build`: `npm run build` (produces dist/esm, dist/cjs, dist/types)
  5. `conformance`: `npm test -- conformance` (runs the shared suite against the bundled binary; aborts on any failure)
  6. `publish`: `npm publish --access public --provenance` (publishes to npm registry; npm OIDC provenance is OPTIONAL since we already have SLSA L3 — but npm provenance is free and complements it)
- Container: `node:22-slim` (LTS); pin to a specific 22.x.y for reproducibility
- Re-runnability: npm rejects duplicate publishes (`Conflict: 409`); the workflow treats a duplicate-publish error as success (idempotent) and continues
- Pre-release publishes (`vX.Y.Z-rc.N`): use `npm publish --tag rc` so `npm install @pdftract/sdk` does not pick up pre-release versions
- The workflow depends on `pdftract-build-binaries` (the binary must exist for the conformance step to invoke); enforced via `dependsOn` in `pdftract-release-cascade`

## Critical considerations

- ADR-009: runs on iad-ci with the npm token from OpenBao -> ESO; never use GitHub Actions
- The npm token MUST have `publish` scope on the `@pdftract` scope; rotate every 90 days per the secrets rotation runbook
- The SDK lives in a SEPARATE git repo (`jedarden/pdftract-node`); the publish workflow clones it, syncs the version, runs build + conformance + publish — but the SOURCE CODE of the SDK lives in that separate repo, NOT in the main pdftract repo
- Alternative: a monorepo layout in the main pdftract repo with the SDK code under `sdks/node/` — the plan explicitly chooses separate repos for independent release cadence (line 3579)
- npm provenance (`--provenance` flag) requires the npm CLI v9.5+; if it fails (unsupported registry), fall back to non-provenance publish but log a warning
- Failure of `pdftract-node-publish` is recoverable by re-running just that workflow (`argo submit --from workflowtemplate/pdftract-node-publish --parameter tag=vX.Y.Z`)

## Acceptance criteria

- WorkflowTemplate file lands at the documented path in jedarden/declarative-config
- A test run against a fresh tag publishes `@pdftract/sdk@X.Y.Z` to npm
- The conformance step aborts publish if any case fails
- A re-run after partial failure is idempotent (npm duplicate-publish treated as success)
- The published package is installable via `npm install @pdftract/sdk@X.Y.Z`
- Pre-release tags publish with `--tag rc` (verifiable: `npm dist-tag ls @pdftract/sdk` shows `rc -> X.Y.Z-rc.N`)

## References

- Plan section: SDK Architecture / Per-SDK Release Channels, line 3570
- Plan section: SDK Acceptance Criteria, line 3584 (24-hour cascade)
- ADR-009 (Argo only)
- Sibling: pdftract-node SDK implementation bead
- npm publish docs: https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v10/commands/npm-publish

## Scope

Coordinator for sub-phase 4.3: identify column boundaries on each page from the histogram of span x0 values. Algorithm: bin x0 coordinates at 1pt resolution into a histogram covering 0..page_width; gaps in the histogram wider than `0.03 * page_width` with zero span coverage are column boundary candidates; require >= 3 lines to start in each candidate column before promoting it to a confirmed column. Apply column labels to every span.

## Why this matters

Column detection gates the XY-cut reading order (Phase 4.5) AND the per-column block formation (Phase 4.4). Without correct columns, two-column academic papers extract with interleaved lines from both columns — the most visible failure mode of pdfminer.six.

## Children

- x0 histogram builder (1pt resolution over page width)
- Gap detection (>= 0.03 * page_width contiguous zero-coverage)
- Column confirmation (>= 3 lines per candidate column)
- Column label assignment to spans + Line.column index

## Critical considerations

- INV: column gap threshold scales with page_width (handles landscape vs portrait correctly).
- 3-line confirmation prevents false columns from accidental gaps.
- Spans on a full-width line (e.g., page-spanning heading) belong to ALL columns or NO column — pick "no column" (column = None / column = -1) so block formation handles them as full-width blocks.
- /Rotate normalized coordinates (Phase 3.1) — page_width is the rotated width.

## Acceptance criteria

- All 4 children closed.
- Three-column academic paper: three distinct columns detected (3 column labels 0, 1, 2).
- Full-width heading above two-column body: heading spans not assigned a column (column = None); body spans within columns 0 and 1.
- Single-column page: no false column splits; all spans get column 0.

## References

- Plan section: Phase 4.3 Column Detection (lines 1677-1688)

issue.description:
## Scope

Modify `emit_glyph` (Phase 3.2 sibling) to consult the marked-content stack and set Glyph.mcid to the INNERMOST frame's mcid (if any). When the stack is empty, mcid is None. When the innermost frame has mcid=None (BMC without MCID), walk OUTWARD looking for the nearest frame with mcid=Some(_) — per spec, MCID inheritance from outer marked content scopes IS implementation-defined; we pick "innermost ANY mcid wins" to be deterministic.

## Why this matters

Phase 7.1 StructTree exploitation joins glyphs to structure elements via the MCID. If the wrong MCID is attached (e.g., outer instead of innermost), structure-based reading order produces wrong block ordering. The plan is explicit: "innermost MCID wins for enclosed glyphs".

## Implementation guidance

- emit_glyph reads `executor.marked_content_stack`. Walk from `last()` to `first()`, return the first `Some(mcid)`.
- Set Glyph.mcid to that Option<u32>.
- Optimization: cache the "current MCID" on the executor and update it on every BMC/BDC push and EMC pop (avoid scanning the stack per emit_glyph). The cache invalidates only on push/pop, which is rare relative to emit_glyph frequency.

## Critical considerations

- INV: plan says "innermost MCID wins" — innermost frame with mcid=Some takes precedence over outer frames. BMC frames (no MCID) are transparent.
- Re-read plan: "innermost MCID wins for enclosed glyphs" — clarify: if BDC /A <</MCID 1>> contains BMC /B contains glyph G, then G.mcid = Some(1) (the innermost MCID, regardless of intervening MCID-less frames).
- A glyph emitted with no marked-content scope active: mcid = None.
- MCID 0 is a VALID mcid value; do not treat it as None.
- The cache update on BMC push: only update if new frame has mcid.is_some() AND replace the saved cache with new value; on EMC pop, recompute by scanning stack downward. (Scanning on pop is rare.)

## Acceptance criteria

- Glyph emitted inside BDC /Span <</MCID 5>>: mcid == Some(5).
- Glyph emitted inside BDC /Outer <</MCID 1>> BDC /Inner <</MCID 2>>: mcid == Some(2) (innermost wins).
- Glyph emitted inside BDC /Outer <</MCID 1>> BMC /Inner: mcid == Some(1) (BMC has no MCID, outer wins).
- Glyph emitted outside any marked-content scope: mcid == None.
- MCID 0 propagates as Some(0), not None.

## References

- Plan section: Phase 3.4 Output paragraph (line 1585)
- Critical test: "Nested BDC: innermost MCID wins" (line 1588)
- Critical test: "MCID 0: valid" (line 1590)

## Scope

Implement the classify CLI subcommand: pdftract classify FILE.pdf [--profiles DIR] -> emits JSON {document_type, confidence, reasons, runner_up, runner_up_confidence}. Runs metadata + Phase 4 lite (just enough signal extraction) then 5.6.2 classifier; does NOT do full extraction. Also wires the --auto flag for pdftract extract that uses 5.6 to pick a profile.

## Why this matters

The CLI exposes the classifier to ops/scripting users without forcing a full extraction. JSON output is the contract for piping into pdftract extract --profile <output>. The --auto flag is what makes 5.6 useful to the average user (no manual --profile choice required).

## Implementation guidance

- Add classify subcommand to clap CLI definition
- Args: path (positional), --profiles DIR (optional, defaults to built-ins), --json (default true), --pretty (pretty-print JSON), --top-k (default 5 for reasons)
- Pipeline:
  1. Load profiles (built-ins + --profiles DIR if specified)
  2. Open PDF, extract metadata + signals only (no full text extraction)
  3. classify(signals, profiles) -> ClassificationResult
  4. Serialize as JSON
- Exit codes: 0 always (even on unknown); use --exit-on-unknown 1 for users who want to gate on classification
- --auto flag for extract subcommand: runs classifier, picks profile, then runs full extract with that profile's options

## Critical considerations

- classify must be fast (< 1s on typical PDFs); skip Phase 5 OCR even on scanned docs (use Phase 1 metadata + heuristics on the first 1-2 pages for the page_count + structural signals)
- For scanned PDFs that need OCR for text-pattern detection: emit document_type=unknown unless --classify-with-ocr is set

- Path traversal: --profiles DIR is opened with canonicalize + check that it doesn't escape current working directory (defense in depth)

## Acceptance criteria

- CLI invocation: pdftract classify invoice.pdf -> JSON with document_type=invoice
- --auto flag on extract subcommand: classifier runs, profile applied, full extraction proceeds
- JSON shape matches plan example exactly
- Performance: classify on a typical 5-page PDF < 200 ms
- Help text documents all flags

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the --root DIR CLI flag for the MCP server: when set at startup, all local-path tool arguments are resolved relative to DIR and any resolved path that escapes DIR is rejected with JSON-RPC error code -32602 (\"Invalid params\"). Without --root, the working directory is the implicit root and no escape protection is applied.

Module: crates/pdftract-cli/src/mcp/root.rs (path resolution + escape check), plus integration in the per-tool dispatch (sibling bead 6.7.5).

## Why this matters

MCP servers running in hosted multi-tenant contexts (Phase 6.7.3 HTTP+SSE mode) MUST NOT let an agent read arbitrary filesystem paths. The --root DIR flag is the minimum bound: any tool's path argument is canonicalized relative to DIR; if the canonical result is not a descendant of DIR, the request fails with -32602 before any file I/O happens. This blocks classic ../../../etc/passwd escapes, symlink-escape attacks (canonicalize follows symlinks), and absolute-path attacks (an absolute path supplied as the argument).

Without --root, the server runs in trust-the-caller mode (suitable for local stdio with a single user); the flag is required posture for any deployment exposed beyond a single trust boundary.

## Implementation guidance

- CLI: add #[arg(long, value_name = \"DIR\")] root: Option<PathBuf> to McpArgs
- At startup, if --root is set, canonicalize the directory once via std::fs::canonicalize and store the result in shared MCP state
- Per-tool dispatch (sibling 6.7.5) calls resolve_path(arg) for every path argument before invoking the underlying pdftract function
- resolve_path logic:
  ```rust
  fn resolve_path(arg: &str, root: Option<&Path>) -> Result<PathBuf, McpError> {
      // https:// URLs bypass the check entirely (HttpRangeSource handles them)
      if arg.starts_with(\"http://\") || arg.starts_with(\"https://\") { return Ok(arg.into()); }
      // If root is None, return the arg as-is (no protection)
      let root = match root { Some(r) => r, None => return Ok(arg.into()) };
      // Resolve arg as a path relative to root
      let candidate = root.join(arg);
      // Canonicalize follows symlinks; this is what makes the check secure
      let canonical = std::fs::canonicalize(&candidate).map_err(|e| McpError::invalid_params(format!(\"path resolution failed: {e}\")))?;
      // Reject if canonical is not a descendant of root
      if !canonical.starts_with(root) {
          return Err(McpError::invalid_params(format!(\"path '{arg}' escapes root '{}'\", root.display())));
      }
      Ok(canonical)
  }
  ```
- HTTPS URLs (per plan section 6.7 line 2325 + 2327) are unaffected by --root — the remote source adapter handles them
- Absolute-path arguments must be rejected when --root is set: arg.starts_with('/') or arg is_absolute() → -32602 with \"absolute paths not permitted under --root\"

## Critical considerations

- canonicalize() requires the path to exist; non-existent files yield IO::NotFound, which should also become -32602 (so the agent gets a structured error rather than a generic IO failure)
- Symlink-escape: a symlink inside --root pointing to /etc/passwd canonicalizes to /etc/passwd, which fails the starts_with(root) check — handled correctly by canonicalize
- TOCTOU race: between resolve_path and the eventual file open, a symlink could be swapped. Mitigation: open the file via the canonical path returned from resolve_path; once canonical is computed, downstream code never re-resolves
- Per-tool error code: -32602 is JSON-RPC's standard \"Invalid params\" — use it for path-escape, not -32603 (Internal Error) or pdftract-specific codes
- Plan section 6.7 line 2346 critical test: \"Path-traversal attempt with --root /var/data: path=\\\"../../etc/passwd\\\" rejected with -32602\"
- Document in the --help output that --root does NOT confine HTTPS URLs (they are handled by the remote source adapter and have their own URL-allowlist mechanism — out of scope here)
- --root must be a directory; if a file path is given, startup aborts with a clear error
- root path must be canonicalized at startup (not stored as the raw user input) so the starts_with check operates on canonical forms throughout

## Acceptance criteria

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the DCTDecode (JPEG) passthrough filter. pdftract-core does NOT decode JPEG raster data itself; the filter validates SOI/EOI markers, records /ColorTransform metadata for downstream consumers (OCR pipeline, full-render mode), and passes through the raw bytes unchanged.

Module: crates/pdftract-core/src/decoder/dct.rs.

## Why this matters

DCTDecode is the dominant image-encoding filter in modern PDFs (95%+ of embedded photos). Without the passthrough, image XObjects fail to materialize and the page composer can't produce hybrid raster+vector output. Passthrough avoids pulling in a JPEG decoder dep (libjpeg-turbo is ~200 KB binary cost) for the common no-OCR no-rendering case.

## Implementation guidance

- Validate first 2 bytes are 0xFF 0xD8 (SOI = Start Of Image marker); if not, emit STREAM_INVALID_JPEG diagnostic but still pass through
- Validate last 2 bytes are 0xFF 0xD9 (EOI = End Of Image marker); some buggy producers omit EOI; emit STREAM_INVALID_JPEG warning but pass through
- /DecodeParms may have /ColorTransform (0 = none, 1 = YCbCr conversion); parse and record on the StreamMeta struct
- Pass through raw bytes unchanged
- Module: crates/pdftract-core/src/decoder/dct.rs

## Critical considerations

- DCTDecode raw bytes are valid JPEG; consumers (Phase 5.4 OCR rasterizer, full-render mode) feed them to libjpeg-turbo / image crate
- Some PDFs use DCTDecode with /DecodeParms /JPEGTables (interchangeable global tables); for now, log STREAM_JPEG_TABLES_UNSUPPORTED if present (rare in practice)
- /ColorTransform default in /DecodeParms is 1 (YCbCr) for 3-channel images; record as default if absent
- The validation is best-effort; do NOT fail the extraction on a malformed JPEG; emit diagnostic and pass through

## Acceptance criteria

- Valid JPEG (SOI + EOI) → pass-through bytes; no diagnostic
- Missing SOI → STREAM_INVALID_JPEG diagnostic; pass-through anyway
- Missing EOI → STREAM_INVALID_JPEG warning; pass-through
- /ColorTransform 0 → recorded on StreamMeta; downstream consumer can read
- Round-trip test with reference JPEG fixture

## References

- Plan section: Phase 1.5 passthrough filters
- PDF spec 7.4.8 DCTDecode
- Coordinator: pdftract-57np8 (parent — 4 passthrough filters)
- Sibling: JBIG2/JPX/CCITT passthroughs

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the BrokenVector-path OCR pipeline. For pages classified as BrokenVector (5.1) or escalated by 4.7 readability < 0.5, run Phase 3 in position-hint mode (collect vector glyph bboxes, treat all Unicode as U+FFFD), run Tesseract in PSM_SPARSE_TEXT mode, validate every Tesseract word against the nearest vector glyph bbox center (within 5pt), accept with OCR confidence or cap at 0.4. Fallback to pure unaided OCR if confidence falls under 0.3 across a region.

## Why this matters

PDF/A documents with invisible OCR text layers frequently have garbage in that layer (OCR-of-OCR, copy-paste artifacts, encoding bugs). Naive extraction emits the broken text; blind OCR replaces it but loses positional cues. Assisted OCR uses the broken layer's positions as a hint while re-running Tesseract, producing strictly better WER than blind OCR on misaligned-text-layer fixtures. This is a primary pdftract differentiator.

## Why subtle

5.5 is subtle because three failure modes exist and the policy must handle each: (a) text layer is correctly positioned but garbage Unicode -> reuse positions, accept OCR Unicode; (b) text layer is misaligned (positions wrong) -> validation rejects misaligned words, fall back to pure OCR confidence; (c) text layer is partially correct -> mix per-word. The validation filter is the differentiator vs simple "OCR over BrokenVector".

## Implementation guidance

- Module: pdftract-ocr/src/assisted.rs
- Pipeline:
  1. Phase 3 position-hint mode: collect glyph bboxes; emit unicode=U+FFFD for every glyph
  2. Run 5.2 image render -> 5.3 preprocess -> 5.4 Tesseract WITH psm = PSM_SPARSE_TEXT (mode 11)
  3. Parse HOCR words (5.4.3); convert coords to PDF (5.4.4)
  4. For each Tesseract word: find nearest vector glyph bbox center; if center distance < 5 pt -> accept with OCR conf; else cap conf at 0.4
  5. If OCR conf > 0.7 in a region -> use OCR text; if OCR conf < 0.3 -> re-run without validation filter (pure OCR fallback)
- Region grouping for the conf-threshold logic: use Phase 4.2 line-formation to define regions
- Output: Vec<Span> with confidence_source = "ocr-assisted" or "ocr-fallback"

## Critical considerations

- PSM_SPARSE_TEXT (mode 11) is mandatory for BrokenVector pages — text may be fragmented or partially occluded
- 5pt distance threshold for validation is a hand-tuned constant; document the rationale + the fixtures it was tuned against
- Confidence cap at 0.4 prevents misaligned OCR from being preferred by 5.2.4 bbox-merge over a legitimate vector span
- Fallback to pure OCR must NOT re-render or re-preprocess; reuse the prior Tesseract output, just remove the validation filter
- BrokenVector escalation requires ocr feature; without it, page emitted with BROKENVECTOR_OCR_UNAVAILABLE diagnostic (handled in 5.1.4)
- confidence_source values "ocr-assisted" and "ocr-fallback" are NEW and need to be allow-listed in 6.1 JSON Schema enum

## Acceptance criteria

- All 5.5 child task beads closed
- Critical test 1: PDF/A with correct invisible text layer positions: assisted OCR WER < blind OCR WER
- Critical test 2: PDF/A with incorrect text layer positions: validation filter rejects misaligned; fallback applies; WER comparable to blind OCR (not worse)
- confidence_source = "ocr-assisted" / "ocr-fallback" present in 6.1 JSON Schema enum
- BROKENVECTOR_OCR_UNAVAILABLE diagnostic emitted when ocr feature compiled out + page is BrokenVector

## References

- Plan section: Phase 5.5 (lines 1910-1923)
- Phase 4.7 BrokenVector escalation
- Phase 5.2.4 bbox-merge interaction
- INV-7 confidence_source taxonomy

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement AcroForm /Btn (button) value extraction. Distinguish pushbutton, checkbox, and radio button via /Ff bits 15 (Pushbutton) and 16 (Radio). For checkbox/radio, surface selected state and the associated state name (/Yes, /Off, or custom appearance state).

Module: crates/pdftract-core/src/acroform/value_button.rs.

## Why this matters

Distinguishing pushbutton (no value) from checkbox (binary state) from radio (one-of-N) is essential for form replication, automated form-filling tools, and machine-readable extracted data. Without the distinction, all three appear identical in JSON output, breaking downstream consumers that need to know whether the user can click or toggle.

## Implementation guidance

- Output variant:
  ```rust
  FormFieldValue::Button {
      kind: ButtonKind,  // Pushbutton | Checkbox | Radio
      selected: bool,
      state_name: Option<String>,
      pushbutton: bool,
      radio: bool,
  }
  pub enum ButtonKind { Pushbutton, Checkbox, Radio }
  ```
- /Ff bit 15 (1<<15 = 0x8000) → Pushbutton
- /Ff bit 16 (1<<16 = 0x10000) → Radio
- Default (neither bit set): Checkbox
- Pushbutton: no /V; output { kind: Pushbutton, selected: false, ... }
- Checkbox: /V is /Yes (selected) or /Off (unselected) or some other configured /AS state
  - selected = (/V != /Off && /V.is_some())
  - state_name = the actual Name (e.g. \"Yes\", \"On\", \"Off\")
- Radio: /V is the selected option's state name; siblings (radio buttons in same group) all share the parent field but each has its own /AP appearance dict
  - selected = (this radio button's /AS == parent's /V)
  - state_name = this button's /AS state

## Critical considerations

- /Ff is a 32-bit integer; bits are 1-indexed in the PDF spec; bit 15 means 1 << 14 (0-indexed = bit 14 = value 0x4000)... actually re-check: PDF spec uses 1-indexed bits but the value is shifted from bit 0. So bit 15 = position 14 = value 0x4000? Verify in PDF spec 12.7.5 Table 222
- Some PDFs use custom appearance state names (e.g. /Selected instead of /Yes); the state_name field preserves the actual name for downstream consumers
- Radio button parent /Kids array holds the individual radio widgets; iterate /Kids to determine which one matches /V
- Pushbutton has /Ff /Pushbutton set; /V is typically absent or /Null
- Checkbox /Ff has bit 15 clear AND bit 16 clear; the default value of /V is /Off

## Acceptance criteria

- Pushbutton field → FormFieldValue::Button { kind: Pushbutton, selected: false, ... }
- Selected checkbox (/V == /Yes) → { kind: Checkbox, selected: true, state_name: Some(\"Yes\") }
- Unselected checkbox (/V == /Off) → { kind: Checkbox, selected: false, state_name: Some(\"Off\") }
- Radio button group with /V == \"OptionA\" → button with /AS == OptionA reports selected: true; others false
- Custom state name (/V == /Selected) → state_name: Some(\"Selected\"), selected: true

## References

- Plan section: Phase 7.4.2 (Btn variant)
- PDF spec 12.7.5 (Button fields)
- Coordinator: pdftract-5t92 (parent)
- Sibling: Tx, Ch variants
Labels: acroform, phase-7
issue.title: AcroForm Btn (button) value extraction (Pushbutton + Checkbox + Radio variants)

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the CCITTFaxDecode (Group 3/4 fax) passthrough filter. Records /DecodeParms (/K, /Columns, /Rows, /EncodedByteAlign, /EndOfLine, /BlackIs1) on StreamMeta. Emits OCR_CCITT_UNSUPPORTED diagnostic when full-render or libtiff is unavailable (per EC-13).

Module: crates/pdftract-core/src/decoder/ccitt.rs.

## Why this matters

CCITT Group 3/4 is the dominant compression for scanned legal documents and faxed PDFs. pdftract-core does not decode CCITT (requires libtiff via image crate's tiff feature); the passthrough preserves bytes for downstream consumers.

## Implementation guidance

- Pass-through raw bytes unchanged
- /DecodeParms parsing:
  - /K (encoding: -1 = Group 4, 0 = Group 3 1D, > 0 = Group 3 2D)
  - /Columns (image width in pixels)
  - /Rows (image height in pixels; optional)
  - /EncodedByteAlign (bool, default false; whether each line is byte-aligned)
  - /EndOfLine (bool, default false; whether EOL markers are present)
  - /BlackIs1 (bool, default false; whether 1 bit means black or white)
- Record all parsed params on StreamMeta.ccitt_params
- Check feature gates: cfg!(feature = \"full-render\") AND libtiff availability (via image crate)
- If unavailable → emit OCR_CCITT_UNSUPPORTED diagnostic (per EC-13)
- Module: crates/pdftract-core/src/decoder/ccitt.rs

## Critical considerations

- CCITT has no magic bytes; can't validate at the stream level (the params determine the format)
- /K parameter is critical for downstream decoder; defaults vary by tool (Group 4 is most common modern usage; Group 3 1D is legacy)
- /BlackIs1 inversion: some PDFs invert the bit-meaning; downstream decoder must respect this param
- /Columns is REQUIRED; absent /Columns → STREAM_INVALID_CCITT diagnostic
- Pass-through bytes go to Image XObject stream content; consumer decodes via libtiff

## Acceptance criteria

- CCITT stream with full-render + libtiff → pass-through, no diagnostic
- CCITT stream WITHOUT full-render → OCR_CCITT_UNSUPPORTED diagnostic
- /K=-1 /Columns=2480 /BlackIs1=true → all 3 params recorded on StreamMeta
- Missing /Columns → STREAM_INVALID_CCITT diagnostic
- Round-trip test with reference CCITT fixture

## References

- Plan section: Phase 1.5 passthrough filters; EC-13
- PDF spec 7.4.6 CCITTFaxDecode
- Coordinator: pdftract-57np8 (parent)
Labels: ccitt, decoder, phase-1

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the stdio transport of the MCP server: read JSON-RPC messages from stdin, frame them by Content-Length headers, dispatch to the tool handlers, and write responses back to stdout. All log output is routed to stderr; stdout is treated as a JSON-RPC-only sink (INV-9).

Module: crates/pdftract-cli/src/mcp/stdio.rs.

Subcommand surface: pdftract mcp --stdio (or bare pdftract mcp with no transport flag, which defaults to stdio).

## Why this matters

stdio is the dominant local-agent transport: Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Continue, and Cursor all spawn MCP servers as child processes and communicate over the child's stdio. Getting the framing wrong (e.g. emitting an extra newline, mistakenly writing a log line to stdout) breaks every downstream agent — silently in some cases, since the agent typically times out rather than reporting the malformed frame.

INV-9 (stdio mode stdout is JSON-RPC-only) is the system-wide invariant for this: it must be enforced at every code path that could touch stdout. The transport sets a global panic hook that writes to stderr, removes any println!/eprintln! macros in the call stack, and uses an explicit BufWriter<Stdout> as the only legitimate stdout consumer.

## Implementation guidance

- MCP wire format uses LSP-style Content-Length-headered messages over stdio:
  ```
  Content-Length: 123\\r\\n
  \\r\\n
  {\"jsonrpc\":\"2.0\",...}
  ```
- Reader loop:
  1. Read headers line-by-line until empty line; parse Content-Length
  2. Read exactly Content-Length bytes from stdin
  3. Parse as JSON via the Phase 6.7.1 framing module
  4. Dispatch to handler; on success, frame and write response to stdout
- Writer always uses a single BufWriter<Stdout> protected by a Mutex; never touches stdout from any other code path
- Log routing: set log/tracing subscriber writer to io::stderr at MCP startup; verify no println! call sites in the dispatch path (cargo-deny lint or grep gate in CI)
- EOF on stdin → graceful shutdown: stop accepting new requests, drain any in-flight handlers, exit 0
- Parse error on a request → respond with Response { error: ErrorObject { code: -32700 }, id: Id::Null } and continue reading
- Concurrency: stdio is single-client by spec; handlers may be sync or async, but the read loop is sequential
- Process must exit cleanly on stdin close, on SIGTERM (graceful drain), and on SIGINT (immediate)

## Critical considerations

- INV-9 enforcement: any stray println! to stdout breaks the JSON-RPC stream. Set up a panic hook at MCP startup that writes panic info to stderr (never stdout); audit dispatch path for println!; use cargo-deny or grep gate in CI
- Content-Length must be byte length, not character count; messages with multi-byte UTF-8 require correct byte counting
- Header line terminator is \\r\\n per LSP spec; some clients accept \\n but pdftract emits \\r\\n strictly
- Single-byte read at a time on stdin is too slow for batched messages; use BufReader<Stdin> with a buffer >= 64 KiB
- Backpressure: stdin reads naturally backpressure (single-client by spec); no explicit flow control needed
- On unexpected EOF mid-message (Content-Length: 100 but only 50 bytes received before EOF), exit with diagnostic; do not block forever
- stderr logs must include a startup banner indicating MCP stdio mode is active, with version and feature flags — agents grep for this

## Acceptance criteria

- Piping '{\"jsonrpc\":\"2.0\",\"id\":1,\"method\":\"tools/list\"}' with proper Content-Length headers to a fresh pdftract mcp --stdio invocation produces the expected tools/list response on stdout within 50 ms (critical test from plan section 6.7)
- EOF on stdin → process exits 0 within 100 ms
- Malformed JSON request → -32700 ParseError response with id: null; subsequent valid requests still work
- No println! / no log line ever appears on stdout (test by capturing stdout in a roundtrip test and asserting every byte is part of a JSON-RPC frame)
- Panic in a handler → panic message goes to stderr; process exits non-zero; no partial JSON on stdout
- Process exits 0 on SIGTERM after draining in-flight requests; exits non-zero on SIGINT immediately

## References

- Plan section: Phase 6.7 MCP Server Mode (lines 2286-2349, especially 2292-2296)
- INV-9 (stdio mode stdout is JSON-RPC only)
- MCP spec: stdio transport: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/spec/transports#stdio
- LSP framing reference: https://microsoft.github.io/language-server-protocol/specifications/lsp/3.17/specification/#headerPart
- Phase 6.7.1 framing module dependency
Labels: mcp, phase-6, stdio, transport
issue.title: 6.7.2: stdio transport (Content-Length framing + stderr-only logs + INV-9)

issue.description:
## Scope

Author the `pdftract-docker-build` WorkflowTemplate. Triggered by milestone tag. Builds 3 multi-arch Docker images (`latest`, `ocr`, `full`) for amd64 + arm64, pushes them to ghcr.io/jedarden/pdftract, and signs each multi-arch manifest list with cosign keyless signatures using the iad-ci cluster OIDC issuer.

## Why this matters

GHCR is the recommended distribution channel for users who do not have a Rust toolchain. The 3 image variants correspond to the 3 feature axes (default = baseline, ocr = with Tesseract pre-installed, full = all-features); users pull whichever matches their workload. Cosign signatures provide supply-chain assurance against image-substitution attacks.

## Implementation guidance

- 3 image variants: `latest` (default features), `ocr` (default + OCR feature, includes Tesseract binary + tessdata-fast English), `full` (all features)
- 2 architectures: linux/amd64, linux/arm64
- Use `buildx` with the docker-container driver and the QEMU emulator setup step
- Push tags per the Artifact Taxonomy table:
  - `ghcr.io/jedarden/pdftract:X.Y.Z`, `:latest` (default features)
  - `ghcr.io/jedarden/pdftract:ocr-X.Y.Z`, `:ocr` (ocr variant)
  - `ghcr.io/jedarden/pdftract:full-X.Y.Z`, `:full` (full variant)
- Push order: version-tagged first, then floating tag last
- Each multi-arch manifest list signed via `cosign sign --yes ghcr.io/jedarden/pdftract:X.Y.Z@sha256:...` (and similarly for each variant)
- Use the iad-ci cluster's OIDC issuer for keyless signing (no key material on disk)
- The Dockerfile (in the pdftract repo) supports build-arg `FEATURES=default|ocr|full` to select the cargo feature set
- The base image is `gcr.io/distroless/cc-debian12` for default and `debian:bookworm-slim` for the ocr variant (Tesseract has glibc dependencies that distroless does not satisfy)
- Both LICENSE files copied to `/usr/share/doc/pdftract/` in every image

## Critical considerations

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement NDJSON streaming output mode. Three-frame structure: header (metadata + outline + total_pages), per-page frames in page_index order with 8-page out-of-order buffer + Condvar for backpressure, footer (extraction_quality + errors + Phase 7 placeholders). Wrapped in BufWriter<io::Stdout> with 128 KB buffer. Header/footer detection limited in streaming mode (deferred 3-page window).

## Why this matters

NDJSON streaming is the right output mode for very large PDFs and for consumers that process pages incrementally (LLM agents, log pipelines). Without streaming, a 5000-page document blocks until completion. The 8-page out-of-order buffer is the rayon-friendliness lever: rayon completes pages out of order; without buffering, the output thread would block waiting for the next-in-order page, defeating parallelism.

## Implementation guidance

- Crate: serde_json (existing); std::io::BufWriter; std::sync::{Mutex, Condvar}
- Frame types via internal-tagged serde enum:
  - HeaderFrame { frame: "header", schema_version: "1.0", metadata, outline, total_pages }
  - PageFrame { frame: "page", ...all Page fields }
  - FooterFrame { frame: "footer", extraction_quality, errors, threads, attachments, signatures, form_fields, links }
- BufWriter<io::Stdout> with 128 KB buffer; flush after each frame
- Out-of-order buffer: BinaryHeap<(Reverse<u32>, Page)> protected by Mutex
- Output thread: loop: while top.page_index == next_expected: pop + emit + increment expected; else wait on Condvar
- When buffer holds 8 pages and next-expected hasn't arrived: producer thread blocks on Condvar; this is backpressure (8 chosen larger than typical rayon pool of 4-8 threads)
- Header/footer block detection: only label as kind: header/footer if observed in trailing 4-page window; first 3 pages get kind: paragraph (NOT retroactively corrected; document this in module rustdoc)

## Critical considerations

- BufWriter flush after every frame is required for streaming consumers; do NOT defer
- newline as frame separator; never use other delimiters
- Output stream is always stdout; serve mode uses chunked HTTP response with same framing
- INV-13 reproducibility: out-of-order buffer preserves page_index order on output, so byte-output is reproducible across runs despite rayon variability
- Each frame is a complete valid JSON object on a single line (no embedded newlines)
- 8-page window is a constant NDJSON_OUT_OF_ORDER_WINDOW; document the tuning rationale
- Backpressure via Condvar ensures the output thread is never the bottleneck on balanced workloads

## Acceptance criteria

- All Phase 6.2 child task beads closed
- Critical test: 100-page document outputs exactly 102 newline-delimited JSON objects (header + 100 pages in order + footer)
- Out-of-order completion test: synthetic rayon-jitter -> pages emitted in correct page_index order
- Frame-by-frame consumer reads each line as valid JSON (verified by Python json.loads in test)

## References

- Plan section: Phase 6.2 (lines 2034-2052)
- INV-13 reproducibility

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement atomic file writes (temp + rename) and panic-safe cleanup. All file-backed sinks open output as <path>.tmp.<pid>.<rand>; rename to <path> only on successful close(). If extraction panics mid-write, the temp file is removed on Drop (via RAII guard).

## Why this matters

Without atomic writes, an interrupted extraction (Ctrl+C, panic, OOM) leaves a half-written output file. Users can't tell partial from complete; downstream pipelines consume garbage. Atomicity is the only way to deliver the "panic mid-extraction leaves NO partial output files" acceptance criterion (line 2277).

## Implementation guidance

- AtomicFileWriter struct:
  - Constructor: AtomicFileWriter::create(path) -> Result<Self>
  - Open <path>.tmp.<pid>.<rand-suffix> for write
  - Public method commit(self) -> Result<()>: close + rename to <path>
  - Drop impl: if not committed, remove temp file
- File-backed sinks wrap their Box<dyn Write> in AtomicFileWriter
- For stdout sinks (path == "-"), no temp file needed; pass through to io::stdout()
- Random suffix: 6-char alphanumeric (e.g. via rand crate)
- Rename uses std::fs::rename (atomic on POSIX; on Windows uses MoveFileExW with REPLACE_EXISTING)

## Critical considerations

- Drop runs on panic; cleanup MUST handle "remove failed" gracefully (log warning, don't double-panic)
- Rename is atomic on same filesystem; if target is on different mount, falls back to copy+delete (NOT atomic). Document and warn if detected
- Temp file in same directory as target (cross-filesystem rename risk addressed)
- For NdjsonSink streaming to stdout: atomic doesn't apply (stdout is unidirectional); document as such
- For multi-sink: all sinks must commit successfully or NONE commit (transactional). On any commit failure, all temp files are cleaned up via Drop

## Acceptance criteria

- Critical test (line 2282): inject panic mid-extraction -> no partial output files on disk; only temp files (which are removed on Drop)
- Successful extraction: temp file renamed to target; target exists with full content
- Concurrent extractions to different paths: no collision (random suffix)
- Drop cleanup: forcibly killed process (kill -9) -> next process invocation can clean up orphaned temp files via doctor check (6.10)

## References

- Plan section: Phase 6.6 atomic writes (line 2247) + critical test (line 2282)
issue.title: 6.6.2: AtomicFileWriter (temp + rename) + Drop cleanup + panic safety

## Scope

Build integration-test infrastructure for remote source adapter:

1. **Mock HTTP server** (wiremock or mockito crate):
   - Serves PDFs with Range support

2. **Critical test scenarios** under tests/remote/integration.rs:
   - Extract page 5 of 100-page PDF via mock with Range: < 100 KB transferred

issue.description:
## Scope

For non-Std-14 Type1, TrueType, and OpenType CFF fonts, locate the font program stream (`/FontFile`, `/FontFile2`, or `/FontFile3`) on the FontDescriptor, decode filters, and wrap it in an `owned_ttf_parser::OwnedFace` (TrueType / OpenType) or a Type 1 parser (Type1). Expose unified `glyph_id_for(char)` / `advance(gid)` / `bbox(gid)` methods.

## Why this matters

The embedded font program is the authoritative source of glyph metrics and `cmap` mappings. ttf-parser's owned variant is required because the font Face borrows from the byte buffer — without `OwnedFace`, we can't store the Face in an `Arc<Font>` without lifetime soup.

## Implementation guidance

- Crates: `ttf-parser`, `owned_ttf_parser`. Both already approved in the Dependency Matrix.
- For TrueType (`/FontFile2`): `OwnedFace::from_vec(decoded_bytes, 0)`.
- For OpenType CFF (`/FontFile3` with `/Subtype /OpenType`): same constructor; ttf-parser handles CFF when the `opentype-layout` feature is on.
- For Type1 (`/FontFile`): the font program is a tokenized PostScript stream with an encrypted CharStrings dict. Use a minimal Type1 parser — only need glyph names list and Widths from FontDescriptor; do NOT parse CharStrings. Document this limitation.
- Expose `pub struct EmbeddedFont { face: OwnedFace, ... }` and a trait that the Font wrapper consumes.

## Critical considerations

- Many embedded fonts are SUBSETS — glyph_id_for unmapped chars must return None, not panic.
- Filter decoding for font streams: usually FlateDecode; sometimes none. Reuse Phase 1.3 stream decoder.
- ttf-parser returns advances in units-per-em; caller must divide by units_per_em * font_size.
- Some fonts have a corrupt or zero-length `cmap` — return a Font where glyph_id_for always returns None and rely on Phase 2.2 fallback chain.

## Acceptance criteria

- Successfully load a TrueType font from a fixture PDF; verify glyph_id_for('A') matches Face cmap.
- OpenType CFF font loaded; advance for known glyph matches reference value.
- Type1 font program: gracefully wrap with limited capability; do not crash on missing CharStrings parser.
- Corrupt font program: return a Font with no glyph_id_for hits; emit `FONT_PARSE_FAILED` diagnostic, do not abort.

## References

- Plan section: Phase 2.1, Crates section (line 1309)
- Dependency Matrix entries for ttf-parser and owned_ttf_parser

issue.description:
## Scope

For each discovered SigFieldRef (from 7.3.1), resolve its /V indirect reference and extract structured metadata: signer /Name, /M (signing date, parsed to ISO 8601), /Reason, /Location, /SubFilter (signature format), /ByteRange (computed coverage fraction). Emit a Signature struct per signature.

## Why this matters

This is the headline output of 7.3 - everything compliance and legal teams want is in these fields. The PDF date format requires explicit parsing (no chrono dep needed); coverage_fraction reveals incomplete signatures that only cover part of the file (a common red-flag in tampered docs).

## Implementation guidance

- For each SigFieldRef with v_ref Some, resolve the indirect reference; treat None as unsigned (emit Signature with value: null)
- Extract /Name (signer name) as PdfString -> UTF-8 String; default ""
- Extract /M (signing date) as PdfString in format D:YYYYMMDDHHmmSSOHH'mm
  - Hand-parse: strip leading D:; parse year, month, day, hour, minute, second; parse timezone offset (O is + or - or Z); emit RFC 3339 ISO 8601 string "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS+HH:MM"
  - Tolerate truncated dates (date only, no time, no tz) - fill defaults: 00 time, Z tz
- Extract /Reason (PdfString -> String); optional
- Extract /Location (PdfString -> String); optional
- Extract /SubFilter (Name) -> String, e.g. "adbe.pkcs7.detached"
- Extract /ByteRange as array of 4 integers; if shape invalid, set null + diagnostic
- Compute coverage_fraction: needs file size (passed in from parser context); coverage = (br[1] + br[3]) / file_size
- validation_status: "not_checked" - hard-coded per plan

## Critical considerations

- Date parsing must not crash on any input; fall back to null + diagnostic
- /Name may use PDFDocEncoding or UTF-16BE BOM-prefixed - reuse Phase 1 PdfString decoder
- /ByteRange != 4 elements -> coverage_fraction: null
- /SubFilter is a Name (not String) - read as Name token in PDF parser
- Future-proofing: keep validation_status as String, not bool, so future v2 can add "valid"/"invalid" without breaking schema

## Acceptance criteria

- Critical test (from plan): PDF with two signature fields - both extracted with correct signer names and dates
- Critical test: unsigned signature field - emitted with value: null
- Critical test: /ByteRange coverage fraction computed correctly
- Unit tests: malformed date string (returns null + diagnostic), missing /Name (returns ""), missing /ByteRange (returns null coverage)
- Output: Signature { field_name, signer_name, signing_date: Option<ISO8601>, reason, location, sub_filter, byte_range, coverage_fraction, validation_status: "not_checked", value: Option<{...}> }

issue.description:
## Scope

Define the OutputSink trait + implement the five concrete sinks: JsonSink (whole-doc buffered), MarkdownSink (whole-doc buffered), TextSink (per-page emission), NdjsonSink (per-frame emission), and ReceiptSink stub (Phase 6.8 fills in). All sinks accept a Box<dyn Write> destination at construction.

## Why this matters

The trait + sinks are the architectural backbone of multi-output. Per-format emission logic lives behind a single uniform interface; the extraction pipeline drives sinks without knowing their type. Adding a new format = add a new sink, not change the pipeline.

## Implementation guidance

- trait OutputSink: Send {
      fn open(&mut self, header: &DocumentHeader) -> io::Result<()>;
      fn page(&mut self, page: &Page) -> io::Result<()>;
      fn close(&mut self, footer: &DocumentFooter) -> io::Result<()>;
      fn name(&self) -> &'static str;  // for error messages
  }
- DocumentHeader = { schema_version, metadata, outline }
- DocumentFooter = { extraction_quality, errors, threads, attachments, signatures, form_fields, links }
- JsonSink { writer: Box<dyn Write>, pages: Vec<Page>, header: Option<DocumentHeader> }: buffer pages; on close, serialize Output as a single JSON document
- MarkdownSink { writer: Box<dyn Write>, pages: Vec<Page>, header: Option<DocumentHeader> }: buffer pages; on close, emit Markdown
- TextSink { writer: Box<dyn Write> }: on page(), write text + form-feed; no buffering
- NdjsonSink { writer: BufWriter<Box<dyn Write>> }: on open(), write HeaderFrame; on page(), write PageFrame; on close(), write FooterFrame
- ReceiptSink: Phase 6.8 owns; expose minimal stub interface here

## Critical considerations

- Box<dyn Write> + Send: the writer must be Send for sinks to live across threads
- TextSink emits per page (streaming-friendly) but JsonSink/MarkdownSink buffer (whole-doc emission)
- NdjsonSink already exists from 6.2.3; wrap that logic in the OutputSink trait
- name() is for error reporting: "JsonSink failed to write: ..."
- DocumentHeader and DocumentFooter are subset structs of Output; share serde derives

- TextSink emits exactly 3 form-feed-separated page contents

## Scope

Implement cluster_spans_into_lines(spans, median_font_size) -> Vec<Line>. Two spans same line if |baseline_a - baseline_b| <= 0.5 * median_font_size. Algorithm: sort spans by baseline; sweep; spans within threshold form cluster; close on first baseline beyond threshold; emit Line per cluster.

## Why this matters

Clustering tolerance is critical: too tight = superscripts wrong line; too loose = two-column rows merge. 0.5 * median_font_size validated on test corpus.

## Implementation guidance

- median_font_size: median of all spans' font_size on page (O(n log n) sort or quickselect O(n)).
- compute_baseline for each span (sibling).
- Sort by baseline ASC.
- Sweep: cluster_max_baseline; if new baseline - cluster_max_baseline <= 0.5 * median_font_size, append; else close + open new.
- Emit Line per cluster.

## Critical considerations

- INV: threshold = 0.5 * median_font_size; do NOT hardcode.
- median_font_size from ALL spans (incl. headings).
- Two-column at same y: cluster into one Line; Phase 4.4 block formation splits per column.
- Empty input: empty Vec.

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the parser for PDF 1.5+ object streams (`/Type /ObjStm`). When the document model dereferences an object whose location in the xref table is `type-2` (compressed in an ObjStm), this parser:

1. Looks up the host ObjStm by its ObjRef
2. Decompresses the ObjStm's stream content ONCE (via Phase 1.5 FlateDecode)
3. Reads the ObjStm header: `/N` (number of embedded objects), `/First` (byte offset to first embedded object)
4. Parses the prefix line of N integer pairs: `obj_number_1 offset_1 obj_number_2 offset_2 ... obj_number_N offset_N`
5. For each embedded object at `/First + offset_k`, parses ONE direct object (no `obj` / `endobj` wrapper around embedded objects)
6. Caches the decoded `Vec<(u32, PdfObject)>` keyed by the host ObjStm's ObjRef as `Arc<Vec<(u32, PdfObject)>>` for fast subsequent lookups
7. Handles `/Extends N G R`: if present, the current ObjStm extends another ObjStm (chain); recursively load the parent ObjStm too (with cycle detection)

## Implementation guidance

- ObjStm cache: `HashMap<ObjRef, Arc<Vec<(u32, PdfObject)>>>` per-document
- Cycle detection on `/Extends`: maintain `HashSet<ObjRef>` of in-progress ObjStms; if `/Extends` resolves to an in-progress ObjStm, emit `STRUCT_CIRCULAR_REF` and stop the chain
- Stream content access: use `Phase 1.5 StreamDecoder::decode(stream, source)` to get `Vec<u8>` of decompressed bytes
- Header parsing: split the first `/First` bytes of the decompressed content by whitespace, parse pairs of integers. The header MUST contain exactly N pairs; if mismatch, emit `STRUCT_INVALID_OBJSTM` and use as many valid pairs as can be parsed
- Embedded object parse: create a fresh Lexer over the decompressed-content-bytes starting at `/First + offset_k`, call `parse_direct_object()`. Embedded objects have NO `obj`/`endobj` wrapper per spec
- Embedded objects MUST NOT themselves be Streams (spec disallows nested streams). If parsed as a Stream, emit `STRUCT_INVALID_OBJSTM` and use PdfNull

## Critical considerations

- Critical test from plan: object stream decompresses, parses all N objects, all ObjRefs resolve correctly
- The `/N` and `/First` dict entries are REQUIRED on ObjStm; missing emit `STRUCT_MISSING_KEY` and return empty Vec (no objects extractable)
- ObjStm's `/Filter` is typically `/FlateDecode`; other filters allowed but rare. Use Phase 1.5's filter pipeline transparently
- Decompression bomb: an ObjStm could decompress to many GB; the 2 GB per-document limit (Phase 1.5 max_decompress_bytes) applies here. If exceeded, emit `STREAM_BOMB` and stop processing remaining embedded objects
- Caching by Arc<Vec<...>>: enables concurrent reads from multiple threads (rayon page-level parallelism per plan's "Critical considerations")
- The xref resolver (Phase 1.3) calls into this parser for type-2 entries — the API surface must accept `(host_objstm_ref, embedded_index)` and return `&PdfObject`
- Extends chain depth: limit to 16 to prevent adversarial deep chains; emit `STRUCT_DEPTH_EXCEEDED`
- Generation number rule: embedded objects in an ObjStm ALWAYS have generation 0 (per spec); do not allow non-zero generation in type-2 xref entries

issue.description:
## Scope

Extract digital signature field metadata from PDFs. Walk AcroForm /Fields looking for Sig-type fields (/FT /Sig); for each, extract /T (field name), /V (signature dict) with /Name (signer), /M (signing date ISO 8601), /Reason, /Location, /ByteRange (byte ranges signed), /SubFilter (signature format identifier). Emit a signatures array at document level. Set validation_status: "not_checked" for every signature; pdftract does NOT perform cryptographic validation in v1.

## Why this matters

Signature metadata answers "who signed this?" and "when?" without cryptographic verification. This is what compliance, legal-discovery, and document-management workflows actually consume - the cryptographic chain validation requires CA root trust stores, OCSP/CRL infrastructure, timestamp authority verification, and is firmly out of scope for v1. Pdftract exposing structured metadata (with explicit validation_status = not_checked) is more honest than returning an opaque "verified" or "not verified" boolean that no one can audit.

## Implementation guidance

- Crates: none beyond Phase 1 parser
- Walk catalog -> /AcroForm -> /Fields recursively (fields may nest in /Kids); flatten to a list
- For each field where /FT is the name "Sig": this is a signature field
- /V (signature dict) may be absent (unsigned field) - emit with value: null
- /SubFilter common values: adbe.pkcs7.detached, adbe.pkcs7.sha1, adbe.x509.rsa.sha1, ETSI.CAdES.detached, ETSI.RFC3161 (timestamp)
- /ByteRange is an array [start1, len1, start2, len2] giving the two byte ranges covered by the signature (everything except the signature blob itself); compute coverage = (len1+len2) / file_size
- /M (date) is in PDF date format D:YYYYMMDDHHmmSSOHH'mm - parse to ISO 8601 (chrono optional; can hand-parse to avoid dep)
- validation_status enum: "not_checked", future values "valid", "invalid", "indeterminate" - set "not_checked" universally

## Critical considerations

- Pdftract MUST NOT silently appear to validate signatures - the validation_status: "not_checked" is required and tests confirm it
- /ByteRange null or malformed -> coverage_fraction: null with diagnostic; do not crash
- /M missing or unparseable -> signing_date: null with diagnostic; do not crash
- Signature fields without /V (placeholder for future signing) MUST still be enumerated - the field's existence is meaningful even when unsigned
- AcroForm walking is shared with 7.4 (form fields) - design the walker once, reuse
- Out-of-scope: certificate chain extraction, OCSP queries, timestamp validation - explicitly NOT in v1

## Acceptance criteria

- All Phase 7.3 child task beads closed
- Critical test (from plan): PDF with two signature fields - both extracted with correct signer names and dates
- Critical test: signature field with no /V (unsigned) - extracted with value: null
- Critical test: /ByteRange coverage correctly computed as fraction of file bytes signed
- Output: document-level signatures: Vec<Signature> per docs/schema/v1.0/pdftract.schema.json
- validation_status: "not_checked" on every signature; integration test asserts this

## References

- Plan section: 7.3 Digital Signature Metadata (lines 2587-2602)

- Phase 7.4 AcroForm walker (shared infrastructure)
- docs/schema/v1.0/pdftract.schema.json (signatures shape)
