issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the histogram-stretch contrast normalization step in the OCR preprocessing pipeline. Computes min/max gray values from the input image (ignoring outliers via 1st/99th percentile), linearly maps the [min, max] range to [0, 255], and skips entirely for JBIG2 sources (already binary).

Module: crates/pdftract-core/src/ocr/preprocessing/contrast.rs.

## Why this matters

Without contrast normalization, washed-out scans (low dynamic range) produce binarization thresholds that lose detail in either highlights or shadows — the downstream Sauvola/Otsu binarizer can't compensate. Histogram stretch normalizes the input range so the binarizer operates on a consistent [0, 255] grayscale.

The 1st/99th percentile robustness handles inputs with a few hot pixels or black artifacts that would otherwise dominate the min/max calculation.

## Implementation guidance

- Function signature:
  ```rust
  pub fn histogram_stretch(image: &mut GrayImage) -> Result<(), PreprocError>
  ```
- Algorithm:
  1. Compute histogram (256 bins for u8 gray)
  2. Find p01 = value at the 1st percentile (cumulative count >= 1% of total pixels)
  3. Find p99 = value at the 99th percentile
  4. For each pixel: new_value = ((old - p01) * 255) / (p99 - p01); clamp to [0, 255]
- Skip rule: image source is JBIG2 → return Ok(()) without modification
- In-place mutation for performance (avoid double allocation)
- Use image crate's GrayImage type (already in deps for Phase 5.4)

## Critical considerations

- 1st/99th percentile robustness: an image with one all-black pixel and one all-white pixel would normalize to no-op without percentile robustness; this approach handles that
- Numerator (old - p01) * 255 can overflow u16; cast to i32 for the arithmetic
- Division by zero risk: if p99 == p01 (uniform image), no stretching is possible; return early
- Performance: 8 MP image (large scan) processed in < 50 ms on a typical CPU

## Acceptance criteria

- Image with [50, 200] range → stretched to [0, 255]
- Image with hot pixels at 0 and 255 → percentile robustness handles correctly
- Uniform image (single gray value) → no panic; return early with no-op
- JBIG2 image → no-op (skipped)
- Benchmark: 1080p grayscale processed in < 30 ms

## References

- Plan section: Phase 5.3.2
- image crate: https://crates.io/crates/image
- Coordinator: pdftract-2s0c (parent — contrast + image-source dispatch bundle)
- Sibling: image-source dispatch
Labels: image, phase-5, preprocessing
issue.title: 5.3.2a: Contrast normalization (histogram stretch [min, max] -> [0, 255]; 1st/99th percentile robust)

issue.description:
## Scope

Define the foundational data types of the object model in `crates/pdftract-core/src/parser/object/types.rs`:

- `ObjRef { object: u32, generation: u16 }` — Copy, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd; Display as `"<obj> <gen> R"`
- `PdfObject` enum: `Null`, `Bool(bool)`, `Integer(i64)`, `Real(f64)`, `String(Vec<u8>)`, `Name(Arc<str>)`, `Array(Vec<PdfObject>)`, `Dict(PdfDict)`, `Ref(ObjRef)`, `Stream(PdfStream)`, `Indirect(Box<PdfIndirect>)`
- `PdfDict` type alias: `IndexMap<Arc<str>, PdfObject>` — preserves insertion order
- `PdfStream { dict: PdfDict, offset: u64, len_hint: Option<u64> }`
- `PdfIndirect { id: ObjRef, obj: PdfObject }`
- Helper methods on PdfObject: `as_int() -> Option<i64>`, `as_real() -> Option<f64>`, `as_name() -> Option<&str>`, `as_dict() -> Option<&PdfDict>`, `as_stream() -> Option<&PdfStream>`, `as_array() -> Option<&[PdfObject]>`, `as_string() -> Option<&[u8]>`, `as_ref() -> Option<ObjRef>`, `is_null() -> bool`
- Name interning: a thread-local `Arc<str>` interner so that `/Length`, `/Type`, `/Filter`, `/Font` etc. share a single allocation across thousands of dict instances

## Implementation guidance

- Use `indexmap = "2"` crate (already in plan's Dependency Matrix)
- `Arc<str>` interner: `thread_local! { static INTERNER: RefCell<HashSet<Arc<str>>> = ... }`; `intern(s: &str) -> Arc<str>` lookups-or-inserts; tested size cap ~10k entries (no eviction needed — PDF name vocabulary is bounded)
- `PdfObject::Real` uses `f64`; `PartialEq` on PdfObject must handle NaN: `Real(NaN) != Real(NaN)` per IEEE-754 (use `f64::total_cmp` if total ordering is needed elsewhere)
- `PdfObject::Indirect` is Box-allocated because it's rare (only at top of each indirect-object statement) and keeps the enum size small (24 bytes target on 64-bit)
- Document-comment each variant with the PDF spec section it represents (7.3.2 Bool, 7.3.3 Numeric, etc.)
- Define a `PdfNull = PdfObject::Null` const (or use the variant directly) for the cycle-detection fallback and missing-key fallback

## Critical considerations

- `PdfDict`'s `IndexMap` MUST preserve insertion order across all serialization paths (the JSON output schema relies on dict order for some receipt-replay scenarios per Phase 6.8)
- The PdfObject enum size is performance-critical: each page's resource dict may have hundreds of PdfObjects; trimming variant size from 32 to 24 bytes via Box-on-rare-variant is worth it
- `Arc<str>` for names enables cheap clones during dict-iteration; without interning, each `/Type` key would allocate fresh `Box<str>` per dict
- `PdfStream::len_hint` is the optional `/Length` value if it's a direct (not indirect) integer; the stream decoder uses it as the read size. If `None`, the decoder scans for `endstream`
- Floats: PDF reals are `f64`-precision-equivalent; CTM matrix products and clip-region math (Phase 3) use `f64` throughout. Do not downcast to `f32`
- ObjRef ordering: sort by `(object, generation)` for deterministic dict iteration in fingerprint computation (Phase 1.7)

## Acceptance criteria

- `cargo build --features default` produces `crates/pdftract-core/src/parser/object/types.rs` exporting all the listed types
- `std::mem::size_of::<PdfObject>() <= 32` bytes on x86_64 (unit test asserts this)
- `PdfDict` instances preserve insertion order (round-trip test: insert keys in known order, iterate, assert same order)
- Name interner deduplicates: two `intern("Length")` calls return Arcs with `Arc::ptr_eq`
- All helper methods (as_int, as_real, ...) return Some for the expected variant and None for others
- `PdfObject::Indirect`-via-Box keeps enum size below 32 bytes

## References

- Plan section: Phase 1.2 line 1058-1068 (PdfObject types)
- Dependency Matrix: indexmap
- Phase 1.7 (fingerprint requires deterministic dict order)
- Phase 6.8 (receipts may rely on dict order for JSON byte-identity)
issue.title: Define PdfObject enum, ObjRef, IndexMap-backed PdfDict, Arc<str> name interning

## Scope

Implement the line-based table detector. Collect all horizontal and vertical path segments emitted by content-stream operators (m/l/S for moveto+lineto+stroke, re/S for rectangle stroke, re/f for rectangle fill outline). Cluster collinear segments within epsilon 1.0 pt. Find intersection points of horizontal vs. vertical clusters. Build a candidate grid from the intersections. Output a Vec<GridCandidate> for each page.

## Why this matters

Bordered tables (financial reports, invoices, scientific papers, regulatory filings) constitute the majority of tables that downstream users actually want. Line-based detection is the most reliable signal - if ruling lines are present, the table is unambiguously delimited. Without this, all tables would fall through to borderless heuristics, which have higher false-positive rates and cannot recover thin or single-line dividers.

## Implementation guidance

- Source of segments: Phase 3 graphics-state path operators (m/l/c/v/y/re), terminated by stroke (S/s) or fill (f/F/B/B*); collect only horizontal (|dy| < epsilon) and vertical (|dx| < epsilon) strokes
- Filter out path segments that occur INSIDE text objects (BT..ET) - those are glyph outlines from Type 3 fonts, not table rules
- Cluster collinear segments: two horizontal segments are collinear if |y1 - y2| < 1.0; merge their x ranges into a longer segment when ranges overlap (or are within 2 pt gap)
- Intersection finder: for each horizontal segment H, intersect with each vertical segment V; intersection exists if V.x falls within H.x range AND H.y falls within V.y range (within epsilon)
- Grid construction: sort distinct horizontal y values (row boundaries) and distinct vertical x values (column boundaries); a cell is (rowi, coli) bounded by (xi, yj, xi+1, yj+1)
- Output GridCandidate { bbox: [x0,y0,x1,y1], row_ys: Vec<f32>, col_xs: Vec<f32>, segments: Vec<Segment> }

## Critical considerations

- Filled rectangles (re/f) without stroke contribute their outline as four virtual segments (top, right, bottom, left) - common pattern for filled header rows
- Dashed/dotted strokes still count - check the line dash pattern only if matching ground-truth visual rules later
- Very long horizontal lines spanning the page width that are NOT part of a table (e.g. section dividers) - filter by checking for at least one perpendicular intersection
- Performance: page-level segment count can be 1000+ on dense table pages; cluster step is O(n log n) via spatial bucketing, not O(n^2)

## Acceptance criteria

- Detector emits GridCandidate for every closed grid of >= 4 cells
- Critical test (from plan): 5x3 bordered table - returns one GridCandidate with row_ys.len()==6, col_xs.len()==4
- Unit tests: single rectangle, nested rectangles, mixed text+rules, glyph-path noise rejected
- Public TableDetector::detect_line_based(&PageContext) -> Vec<GridCandidate>
- Benchmark: < 5 ms on 1000-segment page

## References

- Plan section: 7.2 line 2571 (line-based detection)
- docs/research/table-structure-reconstruction.md
- Phase 3 path operator inventory
- 7.2.2 borderless detection (alternative pipeline)
- 7.2.3 cell content assignment (consumer)

issue.description:
## Scope

Configure cosign keyless signing throughout the release pipeline. Sign `SHA256SUMS` blob with `cosign sign-blob` (producing `SHA256SUMS.sig`); sign each Docker multi-arch manifest list with `cosign sign --yes`; attach SLSA provenance with `cosign attest`. All signatures use the iad-ci cluster's OIDC issuer (no key material on disk). Register the issuer with the Sigstore root of trust.

## Why this matters

Keyless signing eliminates the lifetime-key custody problem: there is no private key to leak. The signature is verifiable forever via the Sigstore transparency log (Rekor), which records the workflow's OIDC identity at sign time. This is the modern Sigstore best practice and matches the OpenSSF Scorecard "signed releases" check.

## Implementation guidance

- Install cosign in the Argo workflow container: pre-built `chainguard/cosign:latest` image
- The OIDC issuer URL for iad-ci must be registered with Sigstore Fulcio; one-time bootstrapping: open a PR against `sigstore/fulcio` policy to allow the iad-ci issuer (or use a self-hosted Fulcio for fully air-gapped use, deferred to v1.1+)
- The issuer subject claim used at sign-time is the Argo workflow's ServiceAccount token; it identifies the workflow that produced the signature
- Sign blob command: `cosign sign-blob --yes --output-signature SHA256SUMS.sig --bundle SHA256SUMS.bundle SHA256SUMS`
- Sign image command: `cosign sign --yes ghcr.io/jedarden/pdftract:X.Y.Z@sha256:...`
- Attest provenance: `cosign attest --predicate provenance.json --type slsaprovenance --yes ghcr.io/jedarden/pdftract:X.Y.Z@sha256:...`
- Verification commands (documented in the README "Verifying releases" section):
  - Blob: `cosign verify-blob --certificate-identity-regexp 'argo-workflows/pdftract-' --certificate-oidc-issuer 'https://iad-ci-oidc.ardenone.com/' --signature SHA256SUMS.sig SHA256SUMS`
  - Image: `cosign verify --certificate-identity-regexp 'argo-workflows/pdftract-' --certificate-oidc-issuer 'https://iad-ci-oidc.ardenone.com/' ghcr.io/jedarden/pdftract:X.Y.Z`

## Critical considerations

- ADR-009: NO GitHub OIDC; the signer identity is the iad-ci OIDC issuer
- The `cosign verify --certificate-identity-regexp` value MUST match the actual identity asserted in the cluster OIDC token — this is the most common verification failure mode
- The Sigstore Rekor transparency log entry is immutable and public; signing happens online (the Argo workflow MUST be able to reach the Rekor and Fulcio endpoints)
- Air-gapped verification is possible via the `.bundle` file (a self-contained verification bundle including the cert chain and Rekor inclusion proof)
- Rekor write costs are negligible but require outbound connectivity; in the rare cluster-isolation event the cosign step is the failure point
- Key rotation is a NON-CONCERN with keyless signing (there is no key to rotate)
- The `iad-ci-oidc.ardenone.com` URL is the placeholder; the actual issuer URL must be set in the WorkflowTemplate's environment

## Acceptance criteria

- cosign installed in every Argo template that signs anything (release workflows + docker-build workflow)
- The iad-ci OIDC issuer is registered with Sigstore (one-time)
- `SHA256SUMS.sig` produced by every release and attached to the GitHub Release
- Every Docker image (3 variants × 2 arches under 3 multi-arch lists) is signed
- SLSA provenance is attached to each image via `cosign attest`
- A test run of `cosign verify-blob --signature SHA256SUMS.sig ...` succeeds against the documented identity
- A test run of `cosign verify ghcr.io/jedarden/pdftract:X.Y.Z` succeeds
- The README "Verifying releases" section documents the exact verification commands

## References

- Plan section: Release Engineering / Signing and Provenance, lines 3397-3403
- Plan section: Artifact Taxonomy, line 3352 (SHA256SUMS.sig), line 3358 (Docker image signing)
- ADR-009 (no GH OIDC)
- Sigstore docs: https://docs.sigstore.dev/cosign/overview/
- OpenSSF Scorecard signed-releases check
issue.title: cosign keyless signing using iad-ci OIDC issuer (for SHA256SUMS.sig and Docker images)

## Scope

Implement `classify_code(block, font_descriptors, column_baseline_x0) -> bool` returning true when ALL spans use monospace font AND block.bbox[0] >= column_baseline_x0 + 2 * em_width. Sets block.kind = Code. Runs as post-processing.

## Why this matters

Code blocks are standard markdown elements (triple-backtick); without detection they extract as malformed paragraphs (each line a new paragraph from indent).

## Implementation guidance

- 2-pass: 5-trigger detector first, then upgrade-to-Code pass.
- Monospace: font.descriptor.flags bit 0 (FixedPitch) OR font.name contains "Mono"/"Courier"/"Code"/"Fixed"/"Console" (case-insensitive).
- All-spans-monospace requirement.
- column_baseline_x0 = median x0 of non-Code paragraph blocks in column.
- em_width = font_size.

## Critical considerations

- INV: code detection AFTER block formation; does NOT alter boundaries.
- Mixed-font code (syntax highlight): same font_name with different colors -> still classify.
- Indent threshold may miss flush-left code; add TODO.
- FixedPitch flag is bit 0 not bit 1 — verify ISO 32000-1 Table 123.

## Acceptance criteria

- All-Courier, indented 24pt, font_size 12pt (2em=24): Code.
- All-monospace, not indented: NOT Code.
- Mixed serif+monospace: NOT Code.
- One serif span at end: NOT Code.
- FixedPitch flag set, no "Mono" in name: STILL Code.

## Scope

Generate a CycloneDX Software Bill of Materials for every release. The SBOM (`pdftract-vX.Y.Z.cdx.json`) enumerates every direct and transitive dependency with version, license, and supplier metadata; covers both the binary Rust crates AND the Python wheel. Attached to the GitHub Release and to each Docker image (via `cosign attest --type cyclonedx`).

## Why this matters

CycloneDX is the OSCAL-aligned, U.S.-government-preferred SBOM format (per EO 14028 and NTIA minimum elements). Enterprise procurement teams require an SBOM for any third-party software entering the org. Without one, pdftract is excluded from the same compliance pipelines that SLSA L3 unblocks.

## Implementation guidance

- Install `cargo-cyclonedx` in the Argo release container: `cargo install cargo-cyclonedx --locked`
- Generate command: `cargo cyclonedx --format json --top-level --override-filename pdftract-vX.Y.Z.cdx.json`
- The `--top-level` flag emits one SBOM for the entire workspace (covers pdftract-core, pdftract-cli, pdftract-py)
- For the Python wheel, the maturin build embeds the same Rust deps; no separate Python-package SBOM needed for v0.X. Add `cyclonedx-bom` for Python deps (pip dependencies) in v1.1+ if maturin pulls additional Python packages — currently it does not
- For each Docker image, attach the SBOM via `cosign attest --predicate pdftract-vX.Y.Z.cdx.json --type cyclonedx --yes ghcr.io/jedarden/pdftract:X.Y.Z@sha256:...`
- The SBOM is also included in the SHA256SUMS aggregate file (subject to the same cosign verify-blob umbrella)
- Discoverable post-release: `cosign download attestation --predicate-type https://cyclonedx.org/bom/v1.5 ghcr.io/jedarden/pdftract:X.Y.Z`

## Critical considerations

- The CycloneDX schema version is pinned to 1.5 (current as of v0.1.0); upgrade to 1.6+ is a release-engineering MINOR bump documented in the CHANGELOG
- The SBOM MUST include every transitive dependency (cargo-cyclonedx default behaviour); manually pruning is unsafe
- License field on each component is populated from `cargo metadata` — a dep with missing license metadata appears as `null` in the SBOM and is a license-policy concern (see cargo deny license-check bead)
- The SBOM is regenerated on every release; do not check it into git (it would create churn on every commit)
- For v1.1+ consider also emitting the SPDX 2.3 format alongside CycloneDX (some downstreams require SPDX)
- Vulnerability scanners (Trivy, Grype, Snyk) all consume CycloneDX directly — once published, a downstream user can `grype sbom:./pdftract-vX.Y.Z.cdx.json` to surface known CVEs

## Acceptance criteria

- The `pdftract-github-release` workflow includes a `generate-sbom` step that emits `pdftract-vX.Y.Z.cdx.json`
- The SBOM is attached to the GitHub Release as an asset
- The SBOM is attached to each Docker image via `cosign attest --type cyclonedx`
- The SBOM is included in the SHA256SUMS aggregate
- `cyclonedx-cli validate --input-file pdftract-vX.Y.Z.cdx.json` passes schema validation
- A test run of `grype sbom:./pdftract-vX.Y.Z.cdx.json` produces an interpretable vulnerability report

## References

- Plan section: Release Engineering / Artifact Taxonomy, line 3354 (CycloneDX SBOM)
- Plan section: Signing and Provenance (SBOM is signed alongside other artifacts)
- CycloneDX spec: https://cyclonedx.org/specification/overview/
- EO 14028 SBOM requirements
- cargo-cyclonedx: https://github.com/CycloneDX/cyclonedx-rust-cargo
issue.title: CycloneDX SBOM generation via cargo cyclonedx (pdftract-vX.Y.Z.cdx.json)

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement orchestration layer connecting HttpRangeSource to Phase 1.3 xref resolver and Phase 1.4 document model:

1. **HEAD probe**: HEAD request to URL; record Content-Length, Accept-Ranges, Content-Type
2. **Initial tail fetch**: `Range: bytes=-16384` — parse startxref, trailer, root xref subsection
3. **Xref parsing**: Phase 1.3 strategies 1, 2, 3 (traditional / stream / hybrid); strategy 4 (forward scan) DISABLED for remote
4. **Page object dereferencing on demand**: as document model dereferences each page's /Contents, HttpRangeSource fetches relevant byte range
5. **Resource lazy load**: fonts and XObjects fetched on first reference, cached for document lifetime
6. **Xref stream fetch (PDF 1.5+)**: when traditional xref unavailable, fetch via same Range mechanism

## Implementation guidance

- Public API: `open_remote(url: &str, opts: &RemoteOpts) -> Document` (same shape as Document::open(path))
- Internally:
  ```rust
  let source = HttpRangeSource::open(url, opts)?;
  let (xref, trailer) = resolve_xref(&source)?;
  let doc = Document::build(&source, xref, trailer)?;
  ```
- 16 KB tail size generous; can reduce to 4 KB but 16 KB typically captures xref-stream object too
- Forward-scan disable: `is_remote: bool` flag on XrefResolver; when true, strategy 4 returns empty XrefSection + STRUCT_REMOTE_NO_FORWARD_SCAN
- Page object dereferencing: when Phase 1.4 resolves page's /Contents, HttpRangeSource fetches bytes for specific stream
- Prefetch optimization: for linearized files with hint streams, prefetch next page's content stream while current is processed
- Connection reuse: ureq Agent maintains connection pool; HTTP/1.1 keep-alive

## Critical considerations

- Acceptance criterion: 500-page PDF on remote server -> extract pages 47-52 only with total downloaded < 5 MB
- 16 KB tail might miss xref (very rarely); if startxref points BEFORE tail offset, fetch larger tail progressively (32, 64, ..., 1024 KB)
- HEAD failure modes: 405 (Method Not Allowed) -> fall back to GET with Range: bytes=0-0; no Content-Length -> REMOTE_NO_CONTENT_LENGTH; 403/401 -> exit 4
- Per-page fetch granularity: /Contents may be array; fetch each (or batch contiguous)
- Performance: 500-page extraction with --pages 47-52 in < 3 sec
- TLS: rustls handles certificate validation; clear error on TLS failure (exit 6)

## Acceptance criteria

- open_remote(url) returns Document with correct page count
- Critical test: 500-page mock PDF, pages 47-52 extracted, < 5 MB transferred
- HEAD failure modes (405, no Content-Length, 401) handled gracefully
- xref forward-scan disabled for remote (verify via mock server)
- Page-by-page on-demand fetch verified: page 5 only triggers ~3 Range requests
- Performance: mock-server extraction of 5 pages from 500-page in < 3 sec
- INV-8 maintained

## References

- Plan section: Phase 1.8 lines 1241-1247
- Phase 1.3 (xref with forward-scan disable)
- Phase 1.4 (document model on-demand)
- INV-8
issue.title: Implement HTTP fetch sequence: HEAD probe -> tail Range fetch -> page-by-page on-demand

issue.description:
## Scope

Build a compile-time `phf::Set<&'static str>` of the 20,000 most common English words for the dict-coverage signal in readability scoring. Source: a public-domain English frequency list (e.g., COCA top 20k, or Wikipedia title corpus filtered to 20k). Embed via build.rs as `crates/pdftract-core/src/layout/wordlist.rs`. CI gate: `cargo bloat --release --crates | grep pdftract_wordlist` must report <= 250 KB; if exceeded, swap implementation to `bloomfilter::Bloom<&str>` (~25 KB).

## Why this matters

The wordlist IS the dict-coverage signal. Without it, the 30% weight in readability scoring goes to a meaningless 0. With it, readability correctly flags gibberish output from broken extraction. 20k words covers ~95% of English text corpus tokens (Zipf's law).

## Implementation guidance

- Source artifact: `crates/pdftract-core/build/wordlist-en-20k.txt` — one lowercase word per line, sourced from COCA frequency list (public) or similar.
- Validation: every word is lowercase, length 1-30 chars, ASCII (no Unicode in v0.1.0 wordlist; English wordlist).
- `build.rs`: read the txt, `phf_codegen::Set::build()` each entry, emit `pub static EN_WORDLIST_20K: phf::Set<&'static str> = ...;`.
- API: `pub fn is_english_word(s: &str) -> bool { EN_WORDLIST_20K.contains(s.to_lowercase().as_str()) }`.
- Caller (dict_coverage signal) lowercases input before lookup.
- Bench: `cargo bench` for is_english_word; assert < 100 ns per call (benchmark sub-bead).

## Critical considerations

- INV: phf::Set lookup is O(1); 20k entries adds ~200 KB compiled (typical phf overhead).
- Binary size gate enforced by CI: `cargo bloat --release --crates --filter pdftract_core | grep wordlist` reports allocation; fail build if > 250 KB.
- Fallback if gate exceeds: switch to bloomfilter (approximate set membership, ~25 KB at 0.1% FPR for 20k items, acceptable for a scoring signal).
- Wordlist is ENGLISH ONLY (v0.1.0); non-English documents bypass dict signal (set to 1.0). Document this; multilingual wordlist planned for future.
- Word forms: include common inflections (plurals -s, verb -ed/-ing) in the 20k. COCA list includes lemma plus top inflections.
- Plural/possessive handling: caller should strip trailing `'s` and `s` before lookup if doing fuzzy matching; v0.1.0 does exact lookup only.

## Acceptance criteria

- `is_english_word("the")` -> true.
- `is_english_word("THE")` -> true (case-insensitive via lowercase).
- `is_english_word("xyzqwerty")` -> false.
- Bench: < 100 ns per lookup over 1000 random words.
- Binary size: phf::Set + table within 250 KB (cargo bloat verified).
- CI gate FAILS the build if 250 KB exceeded; SUCCEEDS at 240 KB.

## References

- Plan section: Phase 4.7 Word list (line 1787)
- Critical test: "20,000-word phf::Set lookup: < 100 ns per word" (line 1795)
issue.title: Wordlist build (20k EN compile-time phf::Set + binary-size CI gate < 250 KB)

issue.description:
## Scope

Land the two license files at repo root and configure all workspace crates to declare \"MIT OR Apache-2.0\" via workspace-package inheritance. Also wire license-file shipping into every distributable artifact (binary archives, Python wheels, Docker images).

## Why this matters

Dual MIT OR Apache-2.0 licensing is the Rust ecosystem norm and the maximally-permissive combination accepted by downstream package managers (Homebrew, NixOS, Debian, RHEL). A missing or wrong license declaration is grounds for crates.io publish failure; a missing license file in a binary archive is a license violation when the binary is redistributed.

## Implementation guidance

- LICENSE-MIT: copy MIT License text with \"Copyright (c) 2026 Jed Cabanero\"
- LICENSE-APACHE: copy Apache License 2.0 text verbatim (no per-author placeholder)
- In root Cargo.toml [workspace.package]:
  ```toml
  license = \"MIT OR Apache-2.0\"
  authors = [\"Jed Cabanero <me@jedcabanero.com>\"]
  ```
- Every crate's [package] section uses license.workspace = true to inherit
- Each binary archive (per Artifact Taxonomy table from Phase RE) ships both LICENSE-MIT + LICENSE-APACHE alongside the binary
- Python wheel: pyproject.toml [tool.maturin] section configures license-files; both files end up in dist-info/
- Docker image: COPY LICENSE-MIT LICENSE-APACHE /usr/share/doc/pdftract/ in Dockerfile

## Critical considerations

- Apache-2.0 NOTICE file is OPTIONAL for the project itself; document in CONTRIBUTING.md that downstream redistributors MAY add one
- The cargo deny license policy (sibling bead) cross-references this declaration; ensure the declared license is in the policy's allow list
- crates.io validates the license field at publish time; the string \"MIT OR Apache-2.0\" is SPDX-compatible and accepted
- Binary archives that omit the license files violate Apache-2.0's redistribution clause (section 4(a)); CI gate verifies presence in every archive

## Acceptance criteria

- Repo root has LICENSE-MIT and LICENSE-APACHE files
- LICENSE-MIT contains \"Copyright (c) 2026 Jed Cabanero\"
- LICENSE-APACHE matches https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0.txt verbatim
- cargo metadata --format-version 1 | jq -r '.packages[].license' shows \"MIT OR Apache-2.0\" for every workspace crate
- Build a binary archive (cargo dist build or equivalent); assert both license files are at the top level of the archive
- Build a Python wheel via maturin; unzip and assert both license files in {name}-{version}.dist-info/

## References

- Plan section: Phase RE (Release & Versioning)
- SPDX license identifiers: https://spdx.org/licenses/
- Coordinator: pdftract-16wv (parent — dual-license bundle)
Labels: docs, license, phase-re

issue.description:
## Scope

After BI/ID/EI parsing, record the inline image as an `ImageXObject` entry in the page's image list (same list populated by Do operator's /Subtype /Image branch). Bbox is computed from the current CTM applied to the unit square (0,0)-(1,1) — inline images, like form XObjects, occupy the unit square in their own coordinate system before CTM application.

## Why this matters

Phase 4.4 block formation classifies blocks as `figure` when they contain only image XObjects and no text glyphs. Without recording inline images, those figure blocks would be misclassified as empty paragraphs or omitted entirely.

## Implementation guidance

- After EI consumed and image bytes captured, compute bbox:
  - Unit square corners in image space: (0,0), (1,0), (0,1), (1,1).
  - Transform each by current CTM to get device-space points.
  - Take axis-aligned min/max.
- Create `ImageXObject { bbox: [f32; 4], source: ImageSource::Inline, header: InlineImageHeader, bytes_ref: ImageBytesRef }`.
  - `source` distinguishes inline vs Do-referenced form.
  - bytes_ref: for v0.1.0 a Vec<u8> of the decoded bytes (post-filter) OR raw bytes if we don't decode here (Phase 5.2 handles image extraction proper).
- Append to executor.page_image_list (Vec<ImageXObject>); same Vec as populated by Do /Image branch.
- Phase 5.2 image extraction will read this list and route to OCR/figure output.

## Critical considerations

- INV: page_image_list grows monotonically per page; Phase 4 reads it after content stream completes.
- For v0.1.0, do NOT decode the inline image bytes here — store raw + filter chain; Phase 5.2 decodes if/when needed for OCR.
- Bbox computation uses POST-/Rotate normalization (Phase 3.1 normalization happens AFTER content stream; image bboxes are normalized in the same pass over the image list).
- Some inline images use /ImageMask true — these are 1-bit masks, not pictorial content; flag in InlineImageHeader for Phase 5.2 to skip raster extraction.
- ImageXObject struct must be shared between inline and Do-Image paths so Phase 4.4 figure detection is uniform.

## Acceptance criteria

- Inline image with no CTM modification: bbox == [0,0,1,1] in PDF user space.
- Inline image with `100 0 0 50 200 300 cm` before BI: bbox == [200,300,300,350] (CTM is scale 100x50 + translate 200,300).
- Page with 3 inline images: page_image_list has 3 entries with correct bboxes.
- Image mask (/ImageMask true): recorded but flagged as mask.
- /Rotate 90 normalization correctly transforms image bbox.

## References

- Plan section: Phase 3.5 (line 1596) + Phase 4.4 figure-block detection (line 1705)
issue.title: Inline image -> ImageXObject record in page image list

## Scope

Implement the default-feature image rendering path: walk a page's content stream, collect every image XObject reference (Do operator), retrieve each via Phase 1.5 stream decoder, place each onto a blank canvas using its CTM at Do time, and return the composited image::GrayImage for the page. Handles the 90%+ case of scanned PDFs where the scan is a single full-page image (or a small set of large images).

## Why this matters

This is the keystone of the binary-size strategy. Direct compositing has zero external dependencies (uses image crate from default deps). Every scanned PDF that this path handles is one less pdftract:full Docker image users need.

## Implementation guidance

- Crate: image (default ocr feature)
- Walk the content stream operator list (Phase 3 output)
- Build CTM stack (q/Q + cm operators); at each Do, snapshot current CTM and pair with XObject ref
- Retrieve each image XObject from Phase 1.5; convert to GrayImage (luminance conversion from RGB if needed)
- Compute pixel placement: image_bbox_pdf_pt = CTM * unit_square; pixel_bbox = image_bbox_pdf_pt * dpi/72.0
- Composite each placed image onto a white-background canvas at the page-rendered-size resolution
- Render order = stream order (later draws over earlier)

## Critical considerations

- Page rotation must be applied to the canvas size and to placement
- Negative-determinant CTMs (flip) must be honored — Y-axis flip is common in PDFs
- Image XObjects with /Matrix on the XObject form itself must compose with the placement CTM (rare but exists)
- Soft-masked images (/SMask) ARE NOT supported in this path; emit IMG_SOFTMASK_UNSUPPORTED diagnostic + skip the mask; full-render handles them properly
- Inline images (BI/ID/EI) are also image XObjects in disguise; treat them the same way

## Acceptance criteria

- Single full-page-scan fixture: composited GrayImage visually matches the source image (pixel diff < 0.5% allowing for resampling)
- Multi-image-tile fixture (e.g. four-up scanned page): all four images placed correctly
- Rotated page (90, 180, 270): output orientation matches the rendered page
- Soft-masked-image fixture: emits diagnostic + skips mask without crashing
- Integration test compares direct-compositing output to pdfium-render output on a simple fixture (must agree within tolerance)

## References

- Plan section: Phase 5.2 default rendering (line 1852)
- Phase 1.5 stream decoder
- Phase 3 content stream operators
issue.title: 5.2.1: Direct compositing path (image XObject collection + CTM placement)

The pdftract checkpoint is durable but legacy-shaped. .beads/config.json records UUID 7bd9e664-1757-1a91-1165-d64e8d0e75e4, while the current pointer, restored database, event origins, and provenance receipts carry an empty store UUID. bead 0.2.6 therefore refuses a fresh-clone restore with Unverified restore source: pointer store_uuid is empty, and its compatibility importer rejects the old events as having invalid origin identity. Recovery currently requires the historical bead 0.1.3 importer.

## Scope

Migrate the checkpoint to the current verified identity/event format without losing or rewriting semantic issue history. Use an explicitly reviewed bead-rs migration path; do not delete and reinitialize the live queue, use bf/br recovery commands, or hand-edit issue/event JSON.

- config.json, the live workspace row, current.json, and all newly published checkpoint manifests carry one non-empty, consistent workspace UUID.
- Every event has a valid origin_store_uuid, positive origin_event_sequence, and valid event hash under the current schema.
- Provenance receipts have valid non-empty source/target identities and hashes, or are migrated with an explicitly documented compatibility rule.
- All 2,595 issues present at audit generation gen-ba4d57b93c10f3a5223223c2050fd4e7, including the stabilization beads and 2,535 dependency edges, survive byte-for-byte at the semantic field level.
- In a fresh clone with the current supported bead binary, bead restore against the named current generation succeeds without an older binary or manual database surgery.
- bead doctor passes database, schema, dependency graph, checkpoint freshness, and backup-generation integrity checks.
- A verification note records before/after generation IDs, record counts, root hashes, migration command/version, and fresh-clone proof.

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement `detect_span_flags(span: &Span, font: &Font, text_rise: f32) -> u8` that returns a SpanFlags bitmask combining the 5 flag bits: BOLD, ITALIC, SMALLCAPS, SUBSCRIPT, SUPERSCRIPT. Detection uses font name string matching, FontDescriptor /Flags bit checks, /StemV/ItalicAngle metrics, and the glyph's text_rise relative to font_size.

## Why this matters

Style detection drives Markdown output emoji (** for bold, _ for italic, etc.) and structured JSON for downstream consumers. Without flag detection, every formatted document extracts as plain unformatted text. Pdfminer.six misses bold/italic about 30% of the time; pdftract's multi-signal approach catches >95%.

## Implementation guidance

- BOLD detection (set bit 0 if ANY of):
  - font.name contains "Bold" (case-sensitive substring match — covers "Bold", "BoldItalic", "Bd").
  - font.descriptor.flags has bit 18 (the SerifBold or ForceBold flag — re-verify against ISO 32000-1 sec 9.8.2 Table 123).
  - font.descriptor.stem_v > 120 (StemV is the dominant stem thickness; > 120 thousandths-of-em is bold by convention).
- ITALIC detection (set bit 1 if ANY of):
  - font.name contains "Italic" or "Oblique".
  - font.descriptor.italic_angle != 0.0 (non-zero italic angle is by definition italic).
- SMALLCAPS detection (set bit 2 if ANY of):
  - font.name contains "SC" or "SmallCaps".
  - font.descriptor.flags has bit 3 set (SmallCap flag).
- SUBSCRIPT detection (set bit 3 if text_rise < -0.1 * font_size).
- SUPERSCRIPT detection (set bit 4 if text_rise > 0.1 * font_size).
- Sub and super are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE — text_rise is one value per span (use span-level rise, computed from first member glyph).

## Critical considerations

- INV: BOLD and ITALIC can BOTH be set (BoldItalic is common).
- SmallCaps and Bold/Italic can coexist (rare but legal).
- text_rise threshold of 0.1 * font_size matches plan; smaller offsets (e.g., 0.05 * font_size) are NOT sub/superscript (could be baseline jitter).
- Span-level text_rise: the span is built from glyphs that all share the same Ts (subscript triggers a span break only via rendering_mode or color change, not Ts itself — wait, Ts doesn't trigger a break per plan). So a span's text_rise is uniform — use first glyph's text_rise.
- Wait — re-read plan: the 5 triggers do NOT include text_rise. So a span CAN span a Ts change. In practice, subscript spans usually have a font_size change too (smaller font for subscript), which DOES trigger a break. Document this edge case.
- Some fonts use ".sc" suffix in name for small caps (e.g., "TimesNewRoman.sc"); add this pattern.

## Acceptance criteria

- "Times-Bold" font: BOLD set.
- "Helvetica-Italic" font: ITALIC set.
- "Times-BoldItalic" font: BOLD | ITALIC set.
- text_rise -2pt with font_size 12pt: SUBSCRIPT set (rise/size = -0.167 < -0.1).
- text_rise +1.5pt with font_size 12pt: SUPERSCRIPT set.
- text_rise -0.5pt with font_size 12pt: NEITHER (rise/size = -0.042, within threshold).
- font.descriptor.flags bit 18 set: BOLD set (even without "Bold" in name).
- /StemV 150 (no "Bold" in name, no flags bit): BOLD set.

## References

- Plan section: Phase 4.1 Flag detection (lines 1648-1653)
- Plan critical test: "Subscript with Ts -3: SuperScript flag NOT set, Subscript flag set" (line 1658)
issue.title: Span flag detector (bold/italic/smallcaps/sub/super bitmask)

All acceptance criteria PASS: Type0+CIDFontType2 loads, widths [10 [500 600]] resolve correctly, range form [100 200 800] works, missing CID falls back to DW, CIDFontType0 uses ttf-parser CFF entrypoint. 23/23 unit tests pass. issue.description:
## Scope

Implement `load_type0(font_dict)` that follows `/DescendantFonts` (always a 1-element array) to the CIDFont dictionary, classifies the descendant as CIDFontType0 or CIDFontType2, reads `/DW` (default width), parses `/W` array (per-CID widths, two formats: `[c [w1 w2 ...]]` and `[cfirst clast w]`), and produces a `Type0Font` value containing both the parent and descendant. Skips the encoding pipeline (deferred to 2.3 CJK), but provides the metric/glyph-program access required by the encoding pipeline and content stream executor.

## Why this matters

Type 0 composite fonts are the only font kind that uses multi-byte character codes. Without correctly walking parent -> descendant -> font program, no CJK extraction is possible. The W array parsing is non-trivial because it intermixes two distinct shapes.

## Implementation guidance

- `/DW` default width is in 1/1000 of text units, default 1000 if absent.
- `/W` array parsing: scan token-by-token; on encountering an integer followed by `[`, switch to per-CID mode and consume widths until `]`; on encountering integer followed by integer followed by integer, that is `cfirst clast w` range mode.
- Build `widths: BTreeMap<u32, u16>` for sparse storage; CIDs can be arbitrary (e.g., 50000+).
- For CIDFontType2, also load the CIDToGIDMap (see sibling bead).
- Cache the descendant Face/font program in an `Arc` so the parent Type0Font wraps it cheaply.

## Critical considerations

- The descendant CIDFont's `/Subtype` is `CIDFontType0` (CFF) or `CIDFontType2` (TrueType/OpenType-TT). Pick the right ttf-parser entrypoint.
- `/W` parsing edge case: empty `[]` arrays inside per-CID form are legal but pointless; ignore.
- `/CIDSystemInfo` is mostly informational; record for diagnostics but do not gate behavior on it.
- The parent Type0 font's `/Encoding` field is the CMap that maps bytes -> CIDs; load it via Phase 2.3 CJK code, not here.

## Acceptance criteria

- A Type0 font with CIDFontType2 descendant loads; widths from a `[10 [500 600]]` example resolve as CID 10 -> 500, CID 11 -> 600.
- Range form `[100 200 800]` resolves: CIDs 100..=200 all -> 800.
- Missing CID falls back to DW.
- CIDFontType0 (CFF) descendant: ttf-parser CFF entrypoint used; advance lookups work.

## References

- Plan section: Phase 2.1 (lines 1300-1305)
- ISO 32000-1 sec 9.7.4 (CIDFonts) for /W syntax
issue.title: Type 0 composite font + descendant CIDFont loader

issue.description:
## Scope

Build the per-page merged `ResourceDict` for every page during page tree flattening. The merge walks from root /Pages downward, accumulating each ancestor's /Resources entries into the descendant's view. Per-key last-write-wins at the PAGE level — but per-namespace MERGE (Font dict from grandparent + Font dict from page = combined Font dict).

ResourceDict struct:
- `fonts: IndexMap<Arc<str>, ObjRef>` — /Font namespace
- `xobjects: IndexMap<Arc<str>, ObjRef>` — /XObject namespace
- `ext_gstates: IndexMap<Arc<str>, ObjRef>` — /ExtGState namespace
- `color_spaces: IndexMap<Arc<str>, PdfObject>` — /ColorSpace namespace (may be ref OR direct array)
- `shadings: IndexMap<Arc<str>, ObjRef>` — /Shading namespace
- `patterns: IndexMap<Arc<str>, ObjRef>` — /Pattern namespace
- `properties: IndexMap<Arc<str>, ObjRef>` — /Properties namespace (used for marked content OCG refs)
- `proc_set: Vec<Arc<str>>` — /ProcSet (deprecated; informational only)

## Implementation guidance

- Public API: `merge_resources(ancestor: &ResourceDict, child: &PdfDict) -> ResourceDict`
- Called once per leaf page during flatten_page_tree walk; ancestor is the rolled-up parent ResourceDict, child is the page's own /Resources dict
- Algorithm per namespace (Font, XObject, ...):
  ```
  for (key, value) in child.font_namespace {
      merged.fonts.insert(key, value); // last-write-wins per-key
  }
  // ancestor's keys remain unless overridden
  ```
- All ObjRefs in each namespace are KEPT AS REFS, not resolved here. Phase 2 (fonts) and Phase 3 (XObjects) resolve them as needed
- ColorSpace can be inline (an array) or indirect; preserve PdfObject as-is
- /Resources missing on a page: inherit the parent's ResourceDict (no merge needed)
- /Resources missing on the root: use an empty ResourceDict (some PDFs use only document-level inheritance)

## Critical considerations

- Critical test from plan: page overriding /Resources /Font partially — merged, not replaced. Example: ancestor has `<< /Font << /F1 /F2 >> /XObject << /Im1 >> >>`; page has `<< /Font << /F3 >> >>`. Merged: `<< /Font << /F1 /F2 /F3 >> /XObject << /Im1 >> >>` (F3 added to font namespace; XObject inherited)
- /Font namespace's /F1 key on the page OVERRIDES /F1 on the ancestor (last-write-wins per-key)
- The whole-namespace replacement behavior would be WRONG: if a page declares `/Font << /F3 >>`, the F1/F2 from ancestor must still be available because content streams may reference them
- Per-page caching: once a page's merged ResourceDict is built, cache it in the PageDict; subsequent resolution doesn't re-walk
- Memory: each PageDict carries its own ResourceDict; for a 1000-page PDF with shared fonts, this is up to 1000 × 200 bytes = 200 KB — acceptable
- /ProcSet is deprecated in PDF 1.7+; do not enforce; just preserve
- /Resources values can be EITHER indirect refs OR direct dicts; the IndexMap holds ObjRef so direct dicts need to be put-in-cache-and-referenced. Simpler: hold `PdfObject` for ColorSpace (since inline arrays are common); hold `ObjRef` for the rest (since they're nearly always indirect)

## Acceptance criteria

- Critical test passes: 3-level resource inheritance test — leaf page sees merged fonts from all 3 levels
- Per-key override test: page's /F1 wins over ancestor's /F1
- /Resources missing on page: inherits parent's; verify Arc<ResourceDict> is the SAME instance (Arc::ptr_eq) for memory efficiency when no merge needed
- ColorSpace inline-array test: ancestor has `<< /ColorSpace << /CS1 [/CalRGB << ... >>] >> >>`; the inline array is preserved in the merged dict
- Empty root /Resources: empty ResourceDict propagates to all leaf pages
- INV-8 maintained

## References

- Plan section: Phase 1.4 line 1113 (resource dict inheritance)
- PDF spec 7.7.3.3 (Resource Dictionary)
- INV-8
issue.title: Implement per-page Resource dictionary inheritance (Font, XObject, ExtGState, ColorSpace, Shading, Pattern, Properties)

## Scope

Author profiles/builtin/contract.yaml per the Phase 7.10 YAML schema, plus at least 5 PDF fixtures at tests/fixtures/profiles/contract/ each with a sibling expected-output.json, plus tests/profiles/test_contract.rs that asserts exact-match of metadata.profile_fields.

## Why this matters

The contract profile ships in v1.0.0 as one of the nine built-ins (line 3041). Contracts are the highest-value document type for legal-tech and corporate compliance; extracting parties, effective_date, term, governing_law, and signatures correctly enables downstream contract-management workflows.

## Implementation guidance

- File: profiles/builtin/contract.yaml
  - name: contract
  - description: "Legal contracts and agreements with parties, effective date, term, and signatures"
  - priority: 20
  - match: all: [any: [text_contains: ['AGREEMENT', 'CONTRACT', 'WHEREAS', 'NOW THEREFORE', 'In witness whereof'], heading_matches: '^(Agreement|Contract|Memorandum of Understanding)'], structural.page_count: {min: 2, max: 200}]; none: [text_contains: ['Invoice #', 'Receipt']]
  - extraction: reading_order: xy_cut; readability_threshold: 0.5; include_headers_footers: false
  - fields: parties (near: ['between', 'party of the first part', 'BY AND BETWEEN'], pick: nearest_below), effective_date (near: ['Effective Date', 'Date of Agreement', 'as of'], parse: date), term (near: ['Term', 'Initial Term', 'expires on', 'shall remain in effect'], regex pattern), governing_law (near: ['Governing Law', 'governed by the laws of'], pick: nearest_right), signatures (region: bottom_quarter; has_signature_field: true detection)
- Fixtures: 5 contracts covering: NDA (1-2 pages), employment contract (5-10 pages), MSA (20+ pages), simple service agreement, real-estate purchase
- Expected outputs: 5 expected-output.json

## Critical considerations

- Contracts often have multi-page tables of definitions, witness blocks, and exhibits -- the field extraction should focus on the first 3 pages for most fields; this is a tunable that may need per-fixture adjustment
- parties extraction is the hardest field -- legal language varies wildly (between X and Y; among A, B, and C; party of the first part); the regex / near hint set must be broad
- signatures detection depends on Phase 7.3 (signature field detection); if Phase 7.3 not yet shipped, fall back to text-based heuristics (e.g. presence of "/s/" or "Signature:" line)
- Fixtures should include at least one bilingual contract (English + Spanish or English + French) to stress the matcher
- Term field has structurally rich representations: "5 years from Effective Date", "expires 2031-12-31", "shall continue until terminated"; the regex should capture the verbatim text and let downstream parsing handle it
- Contracts with embedded scanned signature images are EC-class edge cases; document as a known limitation

## Acceptance criteria

- profiles/builtin/contract.yaml validates
- 5+ fixtures with expected outputs
- tests/profiles/test_contract.rs passes
- Per-field accuracy: >= 90%

## References

- Plan: lines 2890-3058, 3041 (contract field set); depends on Provenance + Per-profile READMEs

Clones `github.com/jedarden/pdftract-go`, syncs the module version, runs the conformance test, creates a git tag matching the binary version, pushes it. pkg.go.dev auto-indexes within minutes.

## Why this matters

Go modules have no centralised registry; publishing is "create a git tag". This workflow encapsulates the gating (conformance must pass) and the credential management (GitHub PAT to push the tag). Without it, the Go SDK requires manual tag-pushing — easy to miss under deadline pressure.

## Implementation guidance

- WorkflowTemplate file: `k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/pdftract-go-publish.yaml` in `jedarden/declarative-config`
- Inputs: tag name; GitHub PAT from ESO Secret `github-pat-pdftract`
- Steps:
  1. `clone-sdk-repo`: `git clone https://github.com/jedarden/pdftract-go.git --branch main`
  2. `sync-version`: ensure module version metadata (if any) matches the binary tag
  3. `regenerate`: optionally re-run `pdftract sdk codegen --lang go --out .` if a generator change has landed since last publish (idempotent)
  4. `conformance`: `go test -run Conformance ./...` (runs the shared suite against the bundled binary; aborts on any failure)
  5. `tag-and-push`: `git tag v$VERSION && git push origin v$VERSION`
  6. `warm-pkg-go-dev`: `curl https://proxy.golang.org/github.com/jedarden/pdftract-go/@v/v$VERSION.info` (triggers pkg.go.dev indexing)
- Container: `golang:1.22-bookworm`
- Re-runnability: a re-run after a partial failure will detect the existing tag and skip the push step (idempotent)
- The workflow depends on `pdftract-build-binaries` (the binary must exist for the conformance step)

## Critical considerations

- ADR-009: runs on iad-ci with the GitHub PAT from OpenBao -> ESO; never use GitHub Actions
- The GitHub PAT needs `repo:write` scope on `jedarden/pdftract-go` (not on `jedarden/pdftract`)
- pkg.go.dev indexing is asynchronous; the warm-up curl typically triggers indexing within 60 s but the page may take up to 24 hours to fully reflect
- Module proxy caching is permanent — a published version CANNOT be recalled or modified; a bad publish requires a new patch release
- The git-tag-based publish is the canonical Go convention; do NOT also publish to a private registry or vendor any files
- Failure of `pdftract-go-publish` is recoverable by re-running the workflow (the existing tag is harmless)

## Acceptance criteria

- WorkflowTemplate file lands at the documented path in jedarden/declarative-config
- A test run against a fresh tag creates a `v$VERSION` tag on `github.com/jedarden/pdftract-go`
- The conformance step aborts publish if any case fails
- `go get github.com/jedarden/pdftract-go@v$VERSION` resolves correctly within a few minutes after publish
- pkg.go.dev page renders within 24 hours
- A re-run is idempotent (existing tag handled gracefully)

## References

- Plan section: SDK Architecture / Per-SDK Release Channels, line 3571 (git tag on pdftract-go; pkg.go.dev auto-indexes)
- Plan section: SDK Acceptance Criteria, line 3584 (24-hour cascade)
- ADR-009 (Argo only)
- Sibling: Go SDK implementation bead
- Go modules reference: https://go.dev/ref/mod
issue.title: Argo WorkflowTemplate: pdftract-go-publish (git-tag pdftract-go repo; pkg.go.dev auto-indexes)

## Scope

Implement the four endpoints: POST /extract (JSON), POST /extract/text (text/plain), POST /extract/stream (NDJSON), GET /health. Each endpoint handler parses multipart, builds ExtractionOptions, calls extraction via spawn_blocking, returns appropriate Content-Type. Health endpoint immediate-return.

## Why this matters

The endpoints ARE the contract. Names, methods, response shapes are immutable post-1.0. Status-code semantics (400/413/422/500) determine how middleware (e.g. load balancers, retry policies) handle pdftract.

## Implementation guidance

- Crate: axum 0.7+
- Router::new()
  .route("/extract", post(handle_extract))
  .route("/extract/text", post(handle_extract_text))
  .route("/extract/stream", post(handle_extract_stream))
  .route("/health", get(handle_health))
- handle_extract:
  1. Parse multipart -> pdf_bytes + options
  2. tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || extract_inner(pdf_bytes, options)) -> Output
  3. Return Json(Output) -> 200 OK, Content-Type application/json
- handle_extract_text: same shape but returns String + Content-Type text/plain
- handle_extract_stream:
  1. Parse multipart
  2. Spawn rayon producer + Receiver<PageFrame>
  3. Return Body::from_stream(ReceiverStream::new(rx).map(|f| serde_json::to_vec(&f).map(|v| {v.push(b'\n'); v}))) with Content-Type application/x-ndjson
- handle_health: GET; immediate JSON {"status":"ok","version":env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")}
- All endpoints listed in /openapi or behind /docs (deferred)

## Critical considerations

- Streaming endpoint must NOT block per-page on rayon completion; output is async stream
- Health endpoint MUST respond in < 10 ms even during load
- multipart "file" field name is required; missing -> 400
- Optional form fields (ocr, ocr_language, etc.) default to ExtractionOptions defaults
- Error responses use Json({"error": code, "message": msg}) for all 4xx + 5xx
- spawn_blocking pool is separate from async executor; extraction never blocks tokio reactor

## Acceptance criteria

- curl -F file=@test.pdf /extract -> 200 JSON valid against schema
- curl /health -> 200 immediately
- curl -F file=@empty.pdf /extract -> 422 with error code
- curl with missing "file" multipart field -> 400 with error code
- Streaming endpoint: curl response is NDJSON; consumer can newline-parse incrementally

## References

- Plan section: Phase 6.4 endpoints (lines 2099-2106)
issue.title: 6.4.1: Four endpoints (POST /extract, /extract/text, /extract/stream, GET /health)

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the security controls enumerated by the Threat Model (lines 831-967) and back every Per-Threat Security Matrix row (TH-01 through TH-10) with an executable test fixture under tests/security/. Ship the secrets-handling policy (secrecy::SecretString wrappers, --password-stdin, PDFTRACT_PASSWORD env, PDFTRACT_MCP_TOKEN env, --auth-token-file, PROFILE_SECRETS_FORBIDDEN loader rejection), the audit-logging subsystem (--audit-log FILE with fingerprinted client_ip + tool + duration + status emission and structured log policy enforcement), and the supply-chain guards (Cargo.lock pin for binary crates, cargo audit + cargo deny CI gates, build/CHECKSUMS.sha256 enforcement on build-time data files).

## Why this matters

The plan treats this section as load-bearing because pdftract is exposed to attacker-controlled input on every extraction surface (lexer, stream decoders, font parsers, content stream interpreter, remote fetcher, MCP/serve listeners, profile loader, cache, inspector frontend, CI runners). Threat IDs TH-01 through TH-10 are NOT aspirational — the plan declares each MUST have at least one corresponding test fixture and that new threats SHALL be added before mitigating code merges (line 833). This epic operationalizes that requirement. The mitigations also gate v1.0.0: failures here would block release at the Tier 1 hard-gate level the same way an accuracy regression would.

## Implementation guidance

- TH-NN tests live at tests/security/TH-NN-<short-name>.rs and use fixtures under tests/fixtures/security/ and tests/fixtures/malformed/
- secrecy::SecretString wraps PDF password, MCP bearer token, inspector token, HTTP basic-auth password — prevents accidental Debug print
- Password ingress: --password-stdin (one line from stdin), PDFTRACT_PASSWORD env, Python password= kwarg, MCP password body field, serve password form field. Plain --password VALUE REJECTED unless PDFTRACT_INSECURE_CLI_PASSWORD=1 set
- MCP token ingress: --auth-token-file PATH (recommended), PDFTRACT_MCP_TOKEN env. Plain --auth-token VALUE REJECTED unless PDFTRACT_INSECURE_CLI_TOKEN=1 set
- Profile loader rejects YAML with top-level password/token/secret/api_key with PROFILE_SECRETS_FORBIDDEN diagnostic
- Audit log: --audit-log FILE (or -) writes newline-delimited JSON with ts/client_ip/tool/fingerprint/duration_ms/status/diagnostics fields; fingerprint instead of path
- Logging policy: NEVER log PDF bytes, password values, bearer tokens, extracted text content, profile-with-secrets contents, Cookie/Authorization/Proxy-Authorization headers at ANY level
- Cargo.lock checked in for pdftract-cli and pdftract-py (binary crates); gitignored for pdftract-core library crate
- cargo audit + cargo deny CI gates: severity >= medium blocks merge for audit; deny enforces license allowlist + banned-crate list (openssl-sys, native-tls, git2, libgit2-sys forbidden; rustls + ring >= 0.17.5 + rustls >= 0.23 required)
- build/font-fingerprints.json and build/glyph-shapes.json SHA-256 checksums in build/CHECKSUMS.sha256; build.rs verifies on every build

## Critical considerations

- TH-03: mcp --bind requires --auth-token unless bind resolves to 127.0.0.1/::1; startup MUST abort with exit code 78 otherwise
- TH-05: URL schemes restricted to https://; localhost/RFC1918/IPv6 ULA/link-local/loopback refused unless --allow-private-networks; refusal emits URL_PRIVATE_NETWORK
- TH-09: Inspector frontend SHALL never use innerHTML/outerHTML with extraction output; CSP default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' on every inspector response
- TH-10: Each cache entry stores HMAC-SHA-256 over fingerprint || extraction_options || output_blob with a per-cache random key created on cache init; reads verify HMAC and treat mismatch as miss with CACHE_INTEGRITY_FAIL
- INV-10: MCP MUST NOT accept file-path parameters (path traversal pre-mitigation via design)
- Hardening implementation beads MUST land before the TH-NN tests that exercise them (dependency wiring matters)
- secrets-allowlist already broad; new TH-NN content may still need additional allowlist entries (see .beads/config.yaml)
- Quarterly cargo vendor snapshot mirrors to ardenone/declarative-config under build-mirrors/pdftract/<quarter>/ for incident recovery; not in normal build path

## Acceptance criteria

- All TH-01 through TH-10 tests exist, pass, and are gated in CI (Phase 0 quality gates)
- secrecy crate wraps every secret type; cargo geiger or equivalent shows no Debug derive on secret-holding structs
- --password-stdin, --auth-token-file, PDFTRACT_PASSWORD, PDFTRACT_MCP_TOKEN all functional; insecure plain CLI variants emit warning + require env opt-in
- Profile loader rejects YAML with credential keys with PROFILE_SECRETS_FORBIDDEN diagnostic
- --audit-log FILE emits one NDJSON line per request matching the documented schema (ts/client_ip/tool/fingerprint/duration_ms/status/diagnostics)
- TH-08 log audit test: extract a sensitive fixture at RUST_LOG=pdftract=trace, assert no known-sensitive substring appears in captured log buffer
- Cargo.lock checked in for binary crates; cargo audit + cargo deny green in Phase 0 CI; build/CHECKSUMS.sha256 enforced by build.rs

## References

- Plan sections: lines 831-833 (intro + per-threat test requirement), 835-844 (attacker profiles), 847-864 (attack surfaces + impact classes), 866-881 (Per-Threat Security Matrix TH-01 through TH-10), 883-896 (Supply Chain Considerations), 897-929 (Secrets Handling), 931-964 (Audit Logging), 949-954 (NEVER-log list), INV-10 (no MCP path parameters)
issue.title: Security Hardening (Threat Model controls TH-01 through TH-10, supply chain, secrets policy, audit logging)

## Scope

Build the test corpus that verifies the fingerprint algorithm's reproducibility and content-sensitivity properties:

1. **Fixture pairs** under `tests/fingerprint/fixtures/`:
   - acrobat_resave/ — same source saved twice by Acrobat (different /CreationDate, /ID, xref byte layout); fingerprints must match
   - pdftk_resave/ — same source through pdftk; fingerprints match the original
   - qpdf_resave/ — same source through qpdf; fingerprints match
   - linearization_toggle/ — pair: unlinearized.pdf and `qpdf --linearize` output; fingerprints must match (KU-7)
   - metadata_only/ — pair: original and copy with /Title, /Producer, /CreationDate, /Author changed; fingerprints must match (ADR-008)
   - content_edit_one_glyph/ — pair: original 100-page and copy with one glyph removed; fingerprints MUST DIFFER
   - content_edit_one_paragraph/ — pair: copy with one paragraph re-typed; fingerprints MUST DIFFER
   - byte_identical/ — same file twice; fingerprints must match (sanity)

2. **Reproducibility test**: invoke compute_fingerprint() 100 times on acrobat_resave/v1.pdf, assert all 100 outputs byte-identical (INV-3)

3. **Cross-platform test** (CI-integrated): same fixtures across linux-gnu / linux-musl / aarch64-linux-musl; fingerprints must match (verifies banker's rounding implementations agree)

## Why this matters

Critical tests for Phase 1.7 are non-negotiable; this corpus is the CI gate. Without linearization-toggle test, KU-7 slips; without metadata-only test, ADR-008 silently violated; without content-edit test, algorithm could degrade to "constant hash".

## Implementation guidance

- Use base PDFs from regression corpus (e.g. Tornado Cash whitepaper, TPC-DS spec)
- For Acrobat re-save: simulate via `qpdf --object-streams=preserve --normalize-content=y`
- For metadata edits: use exiftool with -Title=... -Producer=... etc.
- For content edits: use Python with pikepdf or qpdf --qdf mode; record diff in sidecar EDIT.md
- .expected.txt per fixture pair: single line MATCH or DIFFER
- Reproducibility test: 100 invocations in tests/fingerprint/repro_test.rs

## Critical considerations

- Critical test from plan: Acrobat+pdftk side-by-side same fingerprint
- KU-7: linearization toggle, both produce same fingerprint despite different byte layouts
- Content-sensitivity: removing single glyph changes fingerprint
- Cross-platform reproducibility: banker's rounding well-specified; verify via CI
- Fixture provenance: public-domain or MIT-licensed; document in fixtures/README.md
- Performance per fixture pair: < 200 ms each side; total corpus < 5 sec
- A regression where algorithm becomes deterministic-but-not-stable across platforms caught by cross-platform CI

## Acceptance criteria

- All 8 fixture pairs exist with sibling .expected.txt files
- `cargo test -p pdftract-core -- fingerprint` passes
- 100-invocation repro test passes (INV-3)
- Cross-platform CI (Phase 0.2 targets) confirms identical fingerprints across linux-gnu, linux-musl, aarch64-linux-musl
- Deliberate regression (e.g. including /Producer in hash) caught by metadata_only test
- Deliberate regression (e.g. HashMap instead of BTreeMap for resource dict) caught by repro test
- All Critical tests from plan Section 1.7 pass

## References

- INV-3, INV-13, KU-7
- ADR-008
- Phase 0.2, 0.3 (cross-platform build/test)

## Scope

Author the GitHub issue and PR templates under `.github/`. Five issue templates (bug, feature request, performance regression, documentation, security advisory) plus one PR template. The bug template MUST require `pdftract doctor` output. The security template MUST redirect to SECURITY.md (do not allow public security issues to be filed).

## Why this matters

Well-structured templates reduce maintainer triage burden by 50%+ and improve reproducibility of user-reported issues. The security-template redirect prevents accidental public disclosure of vulnerabilities. The PR template enforces the linked-issue + scope-statement + test-plan requirements documented in CONTRIBUTING.md.

## Implementation guidance

- File locations:
  - `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml` - disables blank issues; lists contact links (Discussions for questions, SECURITY.md for vulns)
  - `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.md` - fields: pdftract version (`pdftract --version`), OS + arch, install method (cargo install / cargo binstall / docker / pip / brew), expected behaviour, actual behaviour, reproduction steps, `pdftract doctor` output (REQUIRED), minimal PDF reproducer (or note "cannot share"), error message
  - `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/feature_request.md` - fields: use case, proposed API surface, alternatives considered, willing to implement
  - `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/performance_regression.md` - fields: pdftract version (last known good + current), benchmark or measurement methodology, hardware spec, observed regression magnitude, profile attached (perf, flamegraph), suspected commit
  - `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/documentation.md` - fields: page URL, suggested correction
  - `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/security.md` - single field: a callout that redirects to SECURITY.md ("If you have discovered a security vulnerability, do NOT file a public issue. Please report via the process in SECURITY.md.") plus a confirmation checkbox before allowing submit
  - `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` - fields: linked issue (`Closes #N`), scope statement (which Phase / which Acceptance Scenario), test plan, manual-test evidence (if applicable), performance impact (if hot path touched), checklist (DCO sign-off, conventional commit, CHANGELOG entry if user-visible, docs updated if API surface changed)
- Use YAML frontmatter to set labels: bug template auto-applies `bug` label; perf regression auto-applies `performance` + `regression`; etc.
- The PR template includes a checklist that requires the contributor to confirm local validation per CONTRIBUTING.md

## Critical considerations

- Required fields use the YAML form syntax (GitHub Issue Forms), not the older Markdown template syntax - Issue Forms allow `required: true` enforcement at the form level
- The `pdftract doctor` requirement in the bug template MUST be marked `required: true` - without doctor output, 80% of "won't reproduce" issues stem from environment-mismatch
- The security template redirect MUST be a top-of-form callout, not buried; consider making the security template a config.yml "contact link" instead of an issue template form so users CANNOT file it as a public issue at all (preferred)
- Avoid creating a template per third-party integration - these become stale; one bug template handles all bugs
- The PR template DCO sign-off checklist item refers to `git commit --signoff`; a hook on the repo can enforce this automatically (deferred to v1.1+)

## Acceptance criteria

- All five issue templates and the PR template land at the documented paths
- Filing a new issue via GitHub UI shows the four user-facing templates (bug, feature, perf, docs) plus a security contact link
- Filing a bug forces a `pdftract doctor` output entry (UI blocks submission if missing)
- Filing a security advisory through the UI redirects to SECURITY.md (the user cannot create a public security issue)
- The PR template renders correctly on new PRs and includes the linked-issue + scope-statement + test-plan + checklist sections
- GitHub Community Standards check marks "Issue templates" and "Pull request template" as green

## References

- Plan section: Release Engineering / Contributor Workflow, line 3431 (PR template) and line 3437 (.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/)
- GitHub Issue Forms documentation
- Sibling: CONTRIBUTING.md (the PR template enforces what CONTRIBUTING describes)
- Sibling: SECURITY.md (the security template redirects there)

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement `group_lines_into_blocks(lines, column_widths) -> Vec<Block>` that sweeps lines top-down and breaks blocks when ANY of 5 ordered triggers fires: (1) vertical gap > 1.5 * line_height; (2) first-line x0 differs from subsequent by > 0.03 * column_width; (3) median font_size delta > 1pt; (4) rendering_mode change; (5) column boundary (MANDATORY).

## Why this matters

Calibrated balance between over-segmentation and under-segmentation. Plan-specified thresholds.

## Implementation guidance

- Sort lines by (column ASC NaN-last, baseline DESC) — process column-by-column top-down.
- Sweep: maintain current_block; for each line check triggers in order.
- Vertical gap: prev_baseline - current_baseline > 1.5 * median_line_height_in_block.
- Indent change: |line.bbox[0] - block_avg_x0| > 0.03 * column_width.
- Font size change: |line.median_font_size - block_median_font_size| > 1.0.
- Rendering mode change: line.rendering_mode != block.rendering_mode.
- Column change: MANDATORY.

## Critical considerations

- INV: column change is MANDATORY (no exceptions).
- Indent change is a SIGNAL — per plan, treat as paragraph indent (new block above).
- line_height computed from BLOCK median, not page median.

## Acceptance criteria

- 5 lines equal spacing/font: 1 block.
- 5 lines, 30pt gap, 5 more: 2 blocks.
- Heading 18pt above 12pt body: 2 blocks.
- Two-column: lines in col 0 separate from col 1.
- Indented first line (>9pt offset, 300pt column_width): NEW BLOCK starts.

## References

- Plan section: Phase 4.4 Heuristics (lines 1694-1699)
issue.title: Line-to-block heuristic detector (5 break triggers in order)

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the HTTP+SSE transport of the MCP server: clients POST JSON-RPC requests to / and consume server-initiated events over GET /sse. Built on axum + tokio, reusing the Phase 6.4 dependency footprint (no new direct crates).

Module: crates/pdftract-cli/src/mcp/http.rs.

Subcommand surface: pdftract mcp --bind ADDR (or pdftract mcp --bind 127.0.0.1:8080).

## Why this matters

HTTP+SSE is the MCP transport for hosted multi-tenant deployments: a single pdftract process behind a reverse proxy serves many concurrent agent clients. Reusing axum/tokio from Phase 6.4 keeps the binary surface and dependency tree shared with the existing pdftract serve mode; the only delta is the routing table and the per-connection SSE event stream.

The HTTP+SSE pattern (POST for client→server requests, SSE GET for server→client notifications) is per the MCP spec and matches how most existing MCP servers (FastMCP, the reference Anthropic implementations) wire up the transport.

## Implementation guidance

- Routes:
  - POST /: body is a JSON-RPC Request (or Batch); response body is the corresponding Response (or Batch). Content-Type: application/json
  - GET /sse: opens a server-sent-events stream; server sends Notification messages as `data: {jsonrpc:2.0,method:notifications/...}\\n\\n` chunks. Long-lived connection; keepalive ping every 30 s.
  - GET /health: 200 OK with `{\"status\":\"ok\",\"version\":\"...\"}` (matches Phase 6.4 shape)
- Reuse axum, tokio, tower-http from Phase 6.4 — no new direct deps
- Per-request handlers run inside spawn_blocking when they invoke extraction (Phase 6.4 pattern); pure-tokio for lightweight calls (tools/list, hash, etc.)
- SSE keepalive: server pushes a comment line `: keepalive\\n\\n` every 30 s on idle channels so reverse proxies do not time the connection out
- Multiple concurrent clients: SSE channel per client; use tokio::sync::broadcast for fan-out of server-initiated notifications
- POST / supports both single Request and batched [Request, Request, ...] per JSON-RPC 2.0; response shape matches the request shape (single vs. batched)
- Response Content-Type for POST / is always application/json (never text/event-stream); SSE is GET-only

## Critical considerations

- HTTP+SSE mode treats stdout as a log channel (opposite of stdio mode) — this is why ADR-006 forbids running both modes in one process. Stdout discipline is reversed but well-defined.
- Backpressure on /sse: if a client cannot keep up, drop notifications for that client rather than blocking the producer; log the drop at WARN
- Request body limit: same 256 MB default as Phase 6.4 serve mode (configurable via --max-upload-mb); custom JSON rejection body on 413
- Concurrency budget: each in-flight extraction holds one spawn_blocking slot (rayon pool from Phase 6.4); upstream rate-limiting must be done by the reverse proxy or via tower-http RateLimitLayer
- 50-concurrent-clients acceptance test (plan line 2335): all 50 must succeed without errors; use connection-keepalive between requests
- Reuses bearer-token auth from sibling bead 6.7.7 — every endpoint except /health checks Authorization: Bearer ... when --auth-token is set or when binding to non-loopback (mandatory)
- Tools/call with extract on a 100-page PDF can take seconds to minutes; client must keep the POST connection open. SSE notifications can advertise progress (notifications/progress per MCP spec) — emit one notification per 10 pages processed.
- Path-traversal protection applies to local-path arguments (the --root flag from sibling bead 6.7.6); HTTPS URLs are unaffected

## Acceptance criteria

- POST / with JSON-RPC tools/list returns the tool catalog (Content-Type: application/json)
- GET /sse opens a long-lived event stream; keepalive comment lines arrive every 30 s
- 50 concurrent clients each calling tools/call extract on distinct PDFs all succeed without 5xx errors (plan section 6.7 acceptance criterion)
- GET /health returns 200 with version info even during heavy load
- POST / with batched [Request, Request] returns a [Response, Response] array
- POST / over the size limit → 413 with custom JSON body shape
- Bearer-token auth: omitting Authorization header on non-loopback bind → 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer header

## References

- Plan section: Phase 6.7 MCP Server Mode (lines 2298-2303)
- Phase 6.4 HTTP serve infrastructure (reused dependencies, spawn_blocking pattern)
- MCP spec: HTTP+SSE transport: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/spec/transports#http-with-sse
- ADR-006 (transport mutual exclusion)
- Sibling beads: 6.7.1 framing, 6.7.7 bearer-token auth, 6.7.6 --root path-traversal protection
Labels: api, http, mcp, phase-6, transport
issue.title: 6.7.3: HTTP+SSE transport (POST / + GET /sse via axum)

issue.close_reason: Implemented WordBoundaryDetector with bootstrap (0.25×font_size) and adaptive (1.5×median) thresholds. Added WordBoundaryManager for per-font tracking. TextState struct for Tc/Tw/Tz tracking. 27 tests passing. Verification note at notes/pdftract-h2s0z.md. Commit a79260b.
issue.description:
## Scope

Implement a per-font adaptive word boundary detector that determines, for each newly-emitted glyph, whether to set `is_word_boundary = true` based on the EXTRA text-space gap between the expected next glyph position (from previous glyph's advance) and the actual next glyph position (from the new glyph's text-matrix translation). The detector uses a FIXED initial threshold `0.25 * font_size` for the first 20 glyphs after a font switch, then recalibrates to `1.5 * median_actual_gap` for subsequent glyphs.

## Why this matters

THE differentiator on TeX-generated PDFs. LaTeX traditionally emits text WITHOUT explicit space characters — words are separated only by positional gaps. Pdfminer.six fails utterly on these (single run-on word per line). The 20-glyph bootstrap + 1.5x median is the algorithm from `docs/research/word-boundary-reconstruction.md` proven to handle TeX, InDesign, and arbitrary letter spacings.

## Implementation guidance

- State per font: `pub struct WordBoundaryDetector { font_id: FontId, sample_count: u32, samples: Vec<f64> (capacity 20), threshold: f64 }`. Live as a HashMap<FontId, Detector> on the page executor.
- INV: comparison is in TEXT SPACE (per plan implementation req (a)) — use text-space gap, NOT device-space.
- For each glyph emitted by Tj/TJ:
  1. Compute `expected_gap = 0` (back-to-back chars share advance, no gap expected at the same baseline).
  2. Compute `actual_gap` = current text_matrix x-translation minus previous text_matrix x-translation minus previous glyph's advance.
  3. If `actual_gap > threshold`, set `is_word_boundary = true` on this glyph; emit a synthetic space conceptually (Phase 4.1 will materialize it as text).
  4. Append `actual_gap` to samples; sample_count += 1.
  5. If sample_count > 20 AND sample_count % 5 == 0 (recalibrate every 5 samples after bootstrap): compute median of last 20 samples, set threshold = 1.5 * median.
- Reset detector on Tf operator (font switch) — per plan implementation req (b).
- Reset detector on BT — per Phase 3.1 lifecycle (text matrices reset; no continuity).

## Critical considerations

- INV: bootstrap threshold = 0.25 * font_size; THIS IS FIXED, not configurable.
- INV: recalibration formula = 1.5 * median; samples window = 20.
- TJ-injected boundaries (from the large-positive-kern path) bypass the detector — they're set directly by the TJ implementation. The detector handles INTRA-string gaps.
- Negative gap (overlapping glyphs, kerning < 0): never a word boundary. Detector ignores negative samples.
- Vertical writing modes (Type0 fonts with vertical CMap variant) flip x and y axes; detector handles only horizontal mode in v0.1.0.
- Performance: detector is called per emitted glyph; samples Vec grows bounded; median computation on 20 elements is O(n log n) = trivial.

## Acceptance criteria

- Initial 20 glyphs after Tf: any gap > 0.25 * font_size triggers boundary.
- Gap exactly at threshold: NOT a boundary (strictly greater than).
- 21st glyph onward: threshold is 1.5x the median of last 20 actual gaps.
- Tf switch: new font starts fresh with bootstrap threshold.
- BT inside same font: bootstrap resets.
- A "TeX-style" PDF (no explicit spaces, only positional gaps between words ~0.3 * font_size and within-word gaps ~0.05 * font_size): correct boundaries injected.

## References

- Plan section: Phase 3.2 Word boundary threshold (lines 1529-1535)
- docs/research/word-boundary-reconstruction.md
- INV: comparison in text space (req a)
issue.title: Adaptive word boundary detector (20-glyph recalibration per font)

issue.description:
## Scope

Coordinator for sub-phase 2.3: handle multi-byte character sets for Type 0 composite fonts. Delivers (1) the 9 predefined CMap entries (Identity-H/V, UniJIS-UTF16-H/V, UniGB-UTF16-H/V, UniCNS-UTF16-H/V, UniKS-UTF16-H/V), (2) raw byte decoding for Shift-JIS / GB18030 / Big5 / EUC-KR via encoding_rs, and (3) codespace-range-driven multi-byte tokenizer that knows where 1-byte codes end and 2-byte codes begin in a content stream byte sequence.

## Why this matters

Without CJK support pdftract cannot extract from Japanese, Chinese, or Korean PDFs at all — the entire content stream is parsed as 1-byte codes producing garbage Unicode. Predefined CMaps are how publishers identify standard encodings without embedding the full CMap stream, so the registry of recognized names is mandatory.

## Children

- Predefined CMap registry (Identity-H/V + 8 UTF16 CMaps)
- encoding_rs adapter for Shift-JIS / GB18030 / Big5 / EUC-KR raw byte decode
- Codespace range parser + multi-byte content-stream tokenizer

## Critical considerations

- Identity-H/V are passthrough: CID == character code. They are used by EVERY Type 0 font with an embedded ToUnicode CMap (which then handles CID -> Unicode).
- UTF16 CMaps are only used when no `/ToUnicode` is present and the font relies on the predefined mapping.
- Codespace ranges define the byte-width boundaries; 0x00-0x7F is often single-byte even in a 2-byte CMap (the so-called "lead byte range" tells the tokenizer when to expect a continuation byte).
- A SINGLE TJ string can contain mixed 1-byte and 2-byte codes — the tokenizer must peek at the lead byte to decide.

## Acceptance criteria

- All 3 children closed.
- An Identity-H Type 0 font with a ToUnicode CMap extracts text correctly via passthrough.
- A Type 0 font with `/Encoding /UniJIS-UTF16-H` and no ToUnicode extracts Japanese text via the predefined CMap.
- A content stream with mixed `0x41 0x82 0xA0 0x42` (ASCII A, JIS hiragana, ASCII B) tokenizes into 3 codes [0x41, 0x82A0, 0x42] given a codespace specifying 0x00-0x7F single-byte and 0x81-0xFE leading.
- All 4 encoding_rs adapters decode known JIS / GB / Big5 / EUC-KR byte sequences correctly.

## References

- Plan section: Phase 2.3 CJK Encoding (lines 1371-1396)
- Critical tests: Identity-H passthrough, 6879 JIS chars, two-byte boundary, mixed codes
