issue.description:
## Scope

Implement the /Catalog /AF (Associated Files) array walker. /AF was added in PDF 2.0 as the future-proof location for embedded attachments; legacy portfolios still use /EmbeddedFiles (sibling), but new PDFs increasingly use /AF.

Module: crates/pdftract-core/src/attachment/associated_files.rs.

## Why this matters

PDF 2.0 (ISO 32000-2) standardized /AF as the canonical embedded-file location, with /Relationship metadata indicating the file's role (e.g., \"Source\", \"Data\"). Without /AF support, PDF 2.0 attachments are invisible to extraction.

## Implementation guidance

- Locate /Catalog /AF (absent → empty Vec)
- /AF is an array of Filespec indirect references; iterate and return Vec<(Option<String>, ObjRef)> where String is the optional /Relationship metadata
- For each Filespec ref:
  - Resolve the Filespec dict
  - Extract /F or /UF for the name (UF preferred; same logic as sibling 7.5.2)
  - Extract /AFRelationship if present (e.g., \"Source\", \"Data\", \"Alternative\", \"Supplement\", \"EncryptedPayload\", \"Unspecified\")
  - Construct return entry: (Some(relationship_string) if AFRelationship else None, filespec_ref)
- Merge with /EmbeddedFiles results (sibling) at the caller level; deduplicate by filespec ObjRef

## Critical considerations

- /AF is per-Catalog (document-level); /AF can also appear per-page or per-annotation (out of scope for this bead; this is document-level only)
- /Relationship enum has fixed values per ISO 32000-2; don't validate, just pass through
- The merge with /EmbeddedFiles: if the same Filespec appears in both, prefer /AF (it has additional metadata); deduplicate by ObjRef
- PDF 1.7 documents that lack /AF still work via /EmbeddedFiles fallback

## Acceptance criteria

- PDF 2.0 with /AF [filespec1, filespec2] → returns 2 entries
- PDF 1.7 with no /AF → empty Vec
- PDF with both /AF and /EmbeddedFiles: combined list with dedup
- /AFRelationship preserved on output
- Test fixture: PDF 2.0 with /AF containing 3 attachments + /Relationship strings

## References

- Plan section: Phase 7.5.1
- PDF spec ISO 32000-2 14.13 (Associated Files)
- Coordinator: pdftract-4bgp (parent)
- Sibling: /EmbeddedFiles name tree walker
Labels: attachment, phase-7

issue.description:
## Scope

Implement bearer-token authentication for the MCP HTTP+SSE transport. When the --bind address is non-loopback (not 127.0.0.1, ::1, or any loopback range), a bearer token MUST be configured via --auth-token VALUE flag or PDFTRACT_MCP_TOKEN environment variable. Startup aborts with a clear error if missing. Every authenticated endpoint checks the Authorization: Bearer ... header and returns 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer on missing or invalid tokens.

Module: crates/pdftract-cli/src/mcp/auth.rs.

## Why this matters

The MCP HTTP+SSE transport exposes pdftract as a network service; without auth, any process that can reach the bind address can invoke tools, including extract on filesystem paths (subject to --root protection from sibling 6.7.6). Bearer-token auth is the minimum credential layer; the network operator is responsible for TLS termination (typically at a reverse proxy per the Phase 6.4 pattern).

The startup-abort on non-loopback without a token is a tripwire: it prevents the most common misconfiguration where an operator binds to 0.0.0.0 in development and forgets to add auth before deploying. Aborting at process startup (not first request) makes the misconfiguration immediately visible.

## Implementation guidance

- CLI: --auth-token VALUE on McpArgs; also accept PDFTRACT_MCP_TOKEN env var (CLI flag takes precedence if both set)
- Startup logic in the HTTP transport (sibling 6.7.3):
  ```rust
  fn validate_auth_config(bind: SocketAddr, token: Option<&str>) -> Result<(), String> {
      let is_loopback = bind.ip().is_loopback();
      if !is_loopback && token.is_none() {
          return Err(format!(
              \"--bind {bind} requires --auth-token (or PDFTRACT_MCP_TOKEN env var) because it is not a loopback address. \\\n             For loopback-only access, bind to 127.0.0.1 or ::1.\"
          ));
      }
      Ok(())
  }
  ```
- Loopback detection: SocketAddr::ip().is_loopback() covers 127.0.0.0/8 and ::1; do NOT use any heuristics on the string form
- IPv6 loopback ::1 must be detected correctly
- Middleware: tower::Layer that intercepts every request; checks Authorization: Bearer <token> against the configured token in constant time (subtle::ConstantTimeEq from the subtle crate); rejects with 401 + WWW-Authenticate: Bearer on mismatch
- /health endpoint is auth-exempt (matches Phase 6.4 convention: monitoring scrape should not need credentials)
- The token value itself is read from env var or CLI; do not log the token value in stderr (only its SHA-256 prefix to confirm config without leaking)

## Critical considerations

- Constant-time comparison is mandatory; ==/eq for token comparison leaks timing information (the bytes that match prefix). Use subtle::ConstantTimeEq or hand-rolled XOR-accumulate
- WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm=\"pdftract\" on 401 lets clients (curl, agent HTTP clients) auto-handle the auth flow
- Multiple tokens are NOT supported in this bead; a single token per process. Multi-tenant deployments use one process per tenant or a reverse-proxy auth layer with header injection
- Token rotation: requires process restart. Document this in the --help text
- Loopback binding to 127.0.0.1 still allows local processes from any UID to connect on most Linux systems; --auth-token is recommended even for loopback in shared-host environments (warn in --help)
- 0.0.0.0 binding without --auth-token must fail at startup with a clear stderr message and exit code 2 (not 1, to distinguish from runtime errors); the message must include the actual --bind value and the fix
- The token is per-process; restarting pdftract with a different token invalidates all existing tokens (matches the simpler-is-better deployment story)

## Acceptance criteria

- pdftract mcp --bind 0.0.0.0:8080 (no token) → startup aborts with exit code 2 and a clear stderr message naming the --bind value and the fix
- pdftract mcp --bind 0.0.0.0:8080 --auth-token secret123 → starts successfully; requests without Authorization header → 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer header
- pdftract mcp --bind 0.0.0.0:8080 with PDFTRACT_MCP_TOKEN=secret123 env var (no --auth-token flag) → starts successfully
- pdftract mcp --bind 0.0.0.0:8080 with BOTH env var and --auth-token flag → --auth-token wins; log line at INFO indicates which source provided the token
- pdftract mcp --bind 127.0.0.1:8080 (no token) → starts successfully (loopback exemption)
- pdftract mcp --bind [::1]:8080 (no token) → starts successfully (IPv6 loopback exemption)
- Valid Authorization: Bearer secret123 → request succeeds
- Invalid token → 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer header
- /health endpoint is auth-exempt: GET /health returns 200 without any Authorization header
- Token comparison is constant-time (verified via timing-attack test in CI)
- Plan critical test passes: \"Bearer token required: --bind 0.0.0.0:8080 without token aborts startup; with token, valid requests succeed and missing tokens get 401\"

## References

- Plan section: Phase 6.7 MCP Server Mode (lines 2302, 2337, 2347)
- subtle crate for constant-time comparison: https://docs.rs/subtle
- RFC 6750 (Bearer Token Usage): https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6750
- Sibling bead 6.7.3 (HTTP+SSE transport — this auth wraps every endpoint)
- Phase 6.4 (HTTP serve has no built-in auth; MCP differs because of the higher trust-boundary expectation)
Labels: auth, mcp, phase-6, security

## Scope

Generate docs/schema/v1.0/pdftract.schema.json from the Rust output types in pdftract-core via schemars; check it in. This is the canonical INV-11 contract that consumers depend on.

Module: xtask/src/bin/gen_schema.rs (sibling pdftract-5nv9h is the parent; this bead is the orthogonal initial-generation work).

NOTE: This bead's scope overlaps with sibling pdftract-5nv9h (xtask gen-schema binary); coordinate to avoid duplication. The orthogonal split: this bead covers the FIRST generation + checked-in schema; sibling 5nv9h covers the xtask binary itself + the CI gate.

## Why this matters

INV-11 mandates that JSON output validates against docs/schema/v1.0/pdftract.schema.json for every page in every fixture, gated in Tier 2 CI. Without the initial schema check-in, downstream consumers have no contract.

## Implementation guidance
